hooks.doc:
`AddAttributeTooltipsEvent`: the lines that follow a stack's attribute lines
(`ItemStack.addAttributeTooltips`), after the modifiers the stack shows and
`gather_skipped_attribute_tooltips` left in. Push lines to `lines`, each with a colour as
`rgba` packs it (`u32::MAX` keeps the text's own); they land beside the attribute lines
without finding where those end. `shown` is whether the stack's
`minecraft:tooltip_display` shows the attribute modifiers (`shouldShow`); the hook is
asked either way. `player` and `player_entity_id` are the local player's,
`None` for the recipe book's search text, which has none and drops the colours, and for a stack
nested in another's tooltip (a crossbow's loaded projectile); `advanced`
(F3+H) and `creative` (a creative tab's own slot) are the tooltip's `TooltipFlag`. Asked
each frame the tooltip shows, only while a mod listens. Client-side.
A component deeper than 512 nodes refuses capture or the whole writeback;
no event field is applied if any Text field fails conversion.

Register client asset reload listeners before a reload stages its
assets (NeoForge's `AddClientReloadListenersEvent`, the client's
counterpart of `add_server_reload_listeners`): the first load
on the loader thread, then every later reload — the player
changed resource packs, F3+T was pressed, or a server sent its packs.
The listener's `prepare` then reads the merged asset view with
resource-pack overrides resolved, and its returned apply publishes the
parsed state, all applies after all prepares, before
`client_resources_reloaded`. A listener that returns an error
aborts the reload and keeps every listener's previous assets.
Client-side, in Reloading nested in Setup initially and World later.
Later registration is on the render thread, prepare on the loader,
and apply on the owning game thread; completion restores the entering
phase. Startup's empty Host grants no extra access.

Add discoverable resource or data packs before a repository selects its
packs (`AddPackFindersEvent`). The builder reports the repository's pack
type. Runs at startup and whenever that repository is rediscovered; no
world state is available during startup registration.

Extra geometry in chunk section meshes (NeoForge's `AddSectionGeometryEvent`):
`register(renderer)` adds the mod's own `SectionGeometry`, which the mesher asks to add its
quads every time it meshes a section, on its worker threads. The quads are part of that
section's mesh: they follow its rebuilds, are never drawn twice, and go when it unloads.
Asked once at start on the client, before resources load.

Register server data reload listeners after packs are selected. The
host gives registry access at registration, as
`AddServerReloadListenersEvent.getRegistryAccess` does. Runs every data
load on the owning server thread in Reloading: only registry facts,
settings and mod-list reads are available through this Host. World
handles, services and transactions panic naming the phase. Existing
data-load callbacks retain their DataLoadContext; no setup event is added.

The optional contribution of the neighbour `event.state` at `event.pos`
(`IBlockExtension.getAdjacentBlockPathType`). `event.path_type` is that
neighbour's own classified type, not the node's type. The readonly host
reads the owning level. `Some` immediately becomes the node's type and
ends the scan, even if equal to its current type; `None` keeps that
neighbour's fluid and vanilla fallback, never suppressing it. Neighbours
are visited x, then y, then z, each from -1 to 1, excluding the node's
own column. No mob is supplied. These answers run after static
classification; per-search evaluator caches remain.
Diverges from upstream: new hook.

`Block.affectNeighborsAfterRemoval` for a mod's block: an authoritative server removed the
block `state` from `pos` (`moved`: a piston pushed it) and has run its template class's own
updates. Push onto `updates` the neighbour updates it wants, in order: `OutputSignal`
(`updateNeighbourForOutputSignal`), `Neighbours` (`updateNeighborsAt`) and
`NeighboursExcept(direction)` (`updateNeighborsAtExceptFromFacing`); the level runs each
at once, as the block's own override would. Answered from inside the level's write: it
reads, and cannot write blocks or spawn entities.

neoforge: none (vanilla Block.affectNeighborsAfterRemoval; NeoForge adds no event or extension for it)

hooks.doc:
A tree's `alter_ground` decorator (`AlterGroundDecorator.place`, the
podzol under a big spruce) is about to turn the ground around
`positions`: the lowest of its trunk or roots (`logs` if it has no roots,
`logs` and `roots` when they start level, else `roots`); only those at
the first one's Y are placed around. `logs`, `leaves` and `roots` are the
decorator context's lists, each sorted by Y. Set `provider` to your own
`GroundProvider::Mod` to choose the ground; to change it only where you
like, wrap the provider you found and ask it for the rest, since several
mods may each wrap the one before. Once per decorated tree, before any
ground is placed; the hook itself draws nothing. Server-side, on the
worldgen worker threads (and on the server thread when a sapling grows),
with the server's worldgen `context`: no `Host`, no writes.

`BlockState.getAnalogOutputSignal`: the signal a comparator reads from
the block `state` at `pos`, `face` the side that touches the comparator
(or the conductor in front of it). `output` holds vanilla's answer:
change it when the block is yours (0 to 15; anything else is clamped).
Asked only for blocks `has_analog_output` answered for, from
inside the level's update: don't change the world here. When the
answer changes without the block's state changing, call
`level.update_neighbors(host, pos, state, NeighbourUpdate::OutputSignal)`; a change of
state through
`native_set_block` or `native_set_block_property` (neighbour updates
on) tells the comparators itself, as vanilla's `Level.setBlock` does.
Authoritative servers only.

neoforge: none (vanilla BlockBehaviour.getAnalogOutputSignal; NeoForge adds no event or extension for it)

hooks.doc:
The player `tamer` (UUID) and `tamer_entity_id` is about to tame the
mob `entity` of `kind` (`AnimalTameEvent`): its taming roll succeeded
(a wolf's bone, a cat's fish, a parrot's seeds or a nautilus's food;
a horse, donkey, mule or llama the player rides). Set `cancel` for the
attempt to fail instead, as a failed roll does: smoke for a pet, and
a horse bucks its rider off. Before `entity_tame`. Server-side.

A player took an anvil's result at `pos` and the levels, inputs and anvil wear are done (`AnvilCraftEvent.Post`); a broken anvil is already air. `craft` holds the inputs and the result as they were before. Not called when `anvil_craft_pre` cancelled.

A player took an anvil's result at `pos` (`AnvilCraftEvent.Pre`), before the levels are charged, the inputs used up and the anvil worn. `craft` holds the inputs and the result as they were before. Set `cancel` to refuse the take: the result stays in its slot and the inputs, levels, inventory and cursor are as before the click.

An anvil at `pos` took damage, changing its block from `from` to `to`.
`to` is air when the anvil broke. Server-side.

An anvil at `pos` made vanilla's result with a left input, for
`player` (UUID) and `player_entity_id` (`AnvilUpdateEvent`, after
`AnvilMenu.createResult`), whenever an input or the name changed:
`update` holds the inputs (the right one may be empty, for a rename),
the rename text and vanilla's result, and its `output`, `xp_cost`
and `material_cost` start at vanilla's for the mods to change; set
`cancel` for no result. The signed XP cost is preserved; a cost of
zero or less prevents taking the output, not a level refund. Negative
material costs are clamped to zero. Both sides: the server's menu,
and a server's client menu with the local player.

`MobEffect.applyEffectTick`: the content mod's resolved `EffectKey` `effect` acts on
`entity` in `dimension` (`minecraft:overworld`). Clear `keep` and the
effect ends now, before it counts down. `entity` is a mob's
`Entity.getId`, None for a player (`host.players().acting_player()` says who).
It runs inside the entity's tick: a mob's world borrows the game
there, so the game is read-only, and it does not hold the ticking
mobs, nor the player's effects. `holder` identifies the holder; Host
reads of a mob holder are unavailable while it is ticking. Queued
changes apply after the hook; clearing `keep` ends the effect.
Server-side.

neoforge: none (vanilla MobEffect.applyEffectTick; NeoForge adds no event or extension for it)

hooks.doc:
NeoForge's `IItemExtension.applyEnchantments`: the enchanting table applies
`enchantments`, the list it chose for the clicked row as (id, level), to `stack`, the
item in its input slot (`EnchantmentMenu.clickMenuButton`). `result` arrives with
vanilla's result: a book becomes an enchanted book with the same count and components,
then each level is added as `ItemStack.enchant` adds it, keeping the higher one.
Replace or change it, and the input slot holds it; `player_enchant_item`, the
`enchanted_item` trigger and `enchant_item` then see it. The levels and lapis paid stay
as without the part. The result goes through the stack boundary: an unknown item,
invalid damage or an oversized count is refused, and so is a count other than the
input's, since the table holds one input; a refused result keeps vanilla's. Only the
`ItemPart`s attached to `stack`'s item are asked, on the server, with a read-only
`Host`. Loot, trades and spawn gear (`EnchantmentHelper.enchantItem`) don't ask. The
contract beyond the method's name and parameters is Horizon's reading, not checked
against NeoForge's.

Apply a registered pose (`HumanoidModel.ArmPose`'s transformer).
Asked only for a selected registered pose, once per model and arm during
humanoid extraction, in vanilla's physical-arm application order. Suppressed
poses do not call the transformer. `humanoid` contains the selected poses
after `get_arm_pose` answers. `right_arm` identifies the physical arm, not the hand.
Write absolute pitch, yaw and roll in radians into `angles`; initially all
components are non-finite, meaning preserve the base model angle. Each
non-finite component is ignored. The ordinary swing and species animations
still run afterward. Native and wasm mods receive the same value contract.

Armor is about to take durability damage from a hit (NeoForge's
`ArmorHurtEvent`, vanilla's `LivingEntity.doHurtEquipment`): once per
hit, for the pieces that would wear, and first for the helmet alone when a
falling block hits a player (`hurtHelmet`). `entity` is the wearer's entity id,
`player` its UUID (None for a mob), `kind` its type and `source` the hit's
damage type (`causing` and `direct` are 0: the hit does not carry them here). Each entry has
its `slot`, the `stack`, the `damage` vanilla worked out and a
`new_damage` a mod may change (0 for none; Unbreaking is applied
after). Canceling means no armor damage. A server player's `feet`,
`legs`, `chest` and `head`; a mob's `body` (a horse's armor).
Server-side.

A player takes an item from an armor stand or puts one on it
(`ArmorStand.interact`, after the stand's disabled-slot checks and
`swapItem`'s take/put locks, before anything moves): `stand_id` is the
stand's `Entity.getId` and `slot` the one the click reached
(`mainhand`, `offhand`, `feet`, `legs`, `chest` or `head`). Set
`cancel` and nothing changes: neither the stand nor the player's hand,
and the click is spent. The player's state is swapped in for the call;
`player` is the UUID the helpers take. Not told of a click that changes
nothing (an empty hand on an empty slot). Not covered, other ways a
stand's equipment moves: breaking or blasting the stand (its items
drop), a dispenser putting armour on one, a mod's own changes.
Server-side, for every player of the world.

NeoForge's `ArrowLooseEvent`: the player releases a bow `stack` with
`has_ammo` and `charge` ticks held. Change `charge` or set `canceled`
to prevent the shot; negative charge also prevents it. Unlike
`living_entity_use_item_stop`, this does not skip the whole item
release; `entity_shoot_bow` reports a spawned arrow afterward
with read-only force. Fires on the Game running the bow release, including
LAN guests; a remote client's own release path is not covered. Crossbows
are not covered; `arrow_nock` is the bow's start.

A player is about to nock `bow` with `hand` (`BowItem.use`, NeoForge's
`ArrowNockEvent`): `has_ammo` is whether `getProjectile` found ammunition
or the player is in creative. Set `cancel` to fail the use.

A player attacks the entity `entity` (`Entity.getId`) of type `kind`
(`minecraft:item_frame`, `minecraft:cow`, `minecraft:player`) standing
at `pos` in the level `dimension` (a `&str`): `ServerGamePacketListenerImpl.handleInteract`'s attack, once
in reach, where `Player.attack` starts. The swing has not begun, so the
attacking player's attack strength is still the charge the blow uses
(vanilla reads it at the start of `Player.attack`; the swing resets it
afterwards). Set `canceled` and the blow does nothing (no damage, no
knockback, the frame keeps its item). Server-side, for every player of
the world (`host.players().acting_player()` says who).

Two animals bred and a baby is about to be made (NeoForge's
`BabyEntitySpawnEvent`, vanilla's `Animal.spawnChildFromBreeding`):
`parent` and `partner` are entity ids, `player` and `player_entity_id`
the UUID and entity id of the player who fed them into love
(`getCausedByPlayer`, None when none), `kind` the baby's type (a horse
and a donkey have a mule). NeoForge's `setChild` (another baby)
needs a handle to a mob not yet in the world, which this hook does not expose. Set `cancel` for no baby: the
parents still rest and lose their love (their ages were already set
to 6000), but there is no baby, no experience, no `animals_bred`
statistic, no advancement and no heart particles. Not fired for
turtles, frogs and sniffers (an egg, no baby) or armadillos' own paths.
Villagers do not post this animal-only event, matching NeoForge's
documented `Animal.spawnChildFromBreeding` posting site; a rejected
villager join instead leaves the child's bed free. On the server.

A model whose `loader` a mod registered (`register_model_loaders`) is baked: push its
quads to `quads` for a loader your mod owns. `config` is the model's JSON object converted
to a `Tag`, and `model` names the model. It is asked once per model on each resource load,
on the resource loader, never per frame.

neoforge: none (vanilla UnbakedGeometry.bake of a loader ModelEvent.RegisterLoaders registers; NeoForge adds no event for it)

hooks.doc:
The colour the block `state` at `pos` gives the beam of the beacon at `beacon_pos`
(`IBlockExtension.getBeaconColorMultiplier`), asked as the beacon builds its beam sections
one block at a time. `color` starts at the block's own answer: the beacon's white and a
stained glass block's or pane's dye colour, empty for the rest. Set `Some(rgb)` to tint
the beam as stained glass does (a colour unlike the section below starts a new section
mixed half and half with it), or `None` to let the beam pass untinted, or stop at an
opaque block other than bedrock, as vanilla does. The beam takes the red, green and blue
channels; alpha is ignored. Asked on both sides, since a client builds the beam it draws
from the blocks it has, with the level read-only: register the mod on both and answer
the same on each. With no part attached to the state, the game checks the hook
subscription and the block key before any event conversion, so the cost is one table
lookup per block above a beacon. Diverges from upstream: new hook.

A beacon at `pos` activated or deactivated after its beam was checked.
`active` says whether it now has a complete pyramid. Server-side.

On an authoritative server, a bell at `pos` is about to ring. Set
`cancel` to stop the ring and its raider reveal.

neoforge: none (NeoForge has no such event; Bukkit's BellRingEvent)

hooks.doc:
Change the colours of `biome` (`minecraft:plains`) on this client: the
grass, foliage (leaves, vines), dry foliage (leaf litter) and water
tints, 0xRRGGBB, as its biome file and the colormaps set them. Asked
for every biome when a mod calls `native_refresh_biome_colors`, which
rebuilds the terrain with them; a season mod answers from its season
and calls that when the season turns. The dark forest's modifier
still applies to the grass set here; the swamp's noise colours
replace it.

neoforge: none (NeoForge adds ColorResolvers with RegisterColorHandlersEvent.ColorResolvers; it does not retint a biome's own colours)

hooks.doc:
A server guest's block-breaking animation changed to `progress` at
`pos` (0 through 9).

On an authoritative server, fire is about to burn the block at `pos`
away. Set `cancel` to keep that block.

neoforge: none (NeoForge has no such event; Bukkit's BlockBurnEvent)

hooks.doc:
An authoritative server committed a changed state through `Level.setBlock`.
The world contains `new`; block side effects and neighbour updates follow.

neoforge: none (NeoForge has no set-block event; IBlockExtension.onBlockStateChange is the block part hook on_block_state_change, at the end of the write)

hooks.doc: A block finished cooking `item` into `result` at `pos`.

A server player stopped digging `pos` before the block broke, after
the server cleared the dig and sent the block back to the client.
The player's state is not swapped in.

neoforge: none (NeoForge has no such event; Bukkit's BlockDamageAbortEvent)

hooks.doc:
A dispenser equipped `item` on the first eligible `target` in front
of its block at `pos`. `target` is `player`, `mob` or `armor_stand`.
The equip, item consumption, sound and game event have completed.
Server-side.

NeoForge's `BlockDropsEvent`: a block `state` broke at `pos` and `Block.dropResources` has built the item entities `drops` it will spawn, but nothing is in the world yet. `breaker` is the breaking player's UUID (none for a break the level makes: a piston, water, a neighbour update, `/setblock destroy`) and `tool` the stack they used (none when no tool). `breaker_entity` is the entity that broke the block (NeoForge's `getBreaker()`): the player, or the mob whose own break of this block is running (a ravager's, a wither's). It is none when no entity broke it: a piston, water, a neighbour update, `/setblock destroy` and explosions. `block_entity` is the block's block entity (NeoForge's `getBlockEntity()`), none for a block without one and for explosions (their blocks are already gone). For a player's break the removal has already taken the block entity out of the world, so its saved data, read before the removal (its `CustomName` too), is held through the event: `level.block_entity_data(entity)` reads it, and the handle is stale (reads refuse) once the event ends, also if a listener panics. `drops` is the list `Block.popResource` built: each stack with the position, motion and pickup delay its item entity will have, drawn before the event as vanilla draws them, so the level random's order does not depend on whether a mod listens. Edit the list (take out, change or add drops; empty stacks don't spawn) or `experience`, the points `spawnAfterBreak` would award at the block's centre (ores, sculk, spawners; silk touch has already zeroed it, as NeoForge's description says, "the true value, after enchantments"). Set `cancel` and nothing spawns: no drops, no experience, and none of `spawnAfterBreak`'s other effects (an infested block's silverfish); a bee nest's bees are `playerDestroy`'s, not `spawnAfterBreak`'s, and still come out. With the `block_drops` rule off the list and the experience are emptied after the event. It fires on the player's break, a mob's block break that drops loot, explosions and every level-side `Block.dropResources` (a piston breaking a block, water washing one away, a removed support). Player, explosion and mob block loot passes through `loot_drops` first; level-side breaks are not asked `loot_drops`. Explosion events run after the blast has removed its blocks and merged their loot, before any items spawn, with no breaker or tool and zero initial experience. Each block's event owns only its share of a merged stack, at that entity's prepared position and velocity; cancellation cannot remove another block's share. Unchanged shares rejoin the original merged entity, while edited or added entities spawn exactly as returned. Even a block with no loot gets an event (TNT that primes instead does not). Neither registration nor a no-op listener changes the merge or the level random's draws. It does not fire for dispensers or a block's own loot-table drop through another path. It runs inside the level's write, so the level host reads blocks and draws the level's random in vanilla's order and writes nothing. Authoritative servers only. Replaces `block_exp`, whose catalog row named no NeoForge event (`none`) and fired only on the level-side path: the amount is `experience` here. Diverges from upstream: `block_exp` is removed into this hook.

Initial saved data for a declared block entity (`EntityBlock.newBlockEntity`),
fired inside the write that creates it (`LevelChunk.setBlockState`), on
a server and on a client of one. `state` is the actual placed state for a
block declared through `stateful_block_entity`; its properties are available
through the Host's state registry. The declaration owns the type id. No
answer creates no entity for a state-aware factory; other declared types
start with an empty compound. The level is read-only, as `newBlockEntity`
gets no level.

neoforge: none (vanilla EntityBlock.newBlockEntity; NeoForge adds no event or extension for it)

hooks.doc:
A client tick of this client's copy of the mod block entity at `pos`
(`ClientLevel.tickBlockEntities`), when its `id` is yours and its
block's state ticks on the client (`block_entity_client_ticks`):
once per client tick while the level runs, in vanilla's ticker order
among the others, whether or not the copy is drawn. `block_entity` is
its handle, `state` its block's state and `entity` its data, read only,
as the frame's handling of the server's packets merged it before the
frame's ticks (`block_entity_update_tag`). Start, stop and fade
its sounds and add its particles here. Never called on a server, and
never again for a copy removed or whose chunk unloaded.

neoforge: none (vanilla BlockEntityTicker from EntityBlock.getTicker with the client level; NeoForge adds no event)

hooks.doc:
Whether block `block`'s block entity ticks on the client
(`EntityBlock.getTicker` asked with the client level): set `ticks` when
it is yours, and `block_entity_client_tick` runs for it once per
client tick. Asked once for each mod block, for all of its states,
the first time a client level ticks with a part that has a client tick.
Set `ticks` to true to make it tick, and never clear a value an earlier mod or mixin set.

neoforge: none (vanilla EntityBlock.getTicker with the client level; NeoForge adds no event or extension for it)

hooks.doc:
The synchronized `tag` has been merged into this client's block entity.
`source` distinguishes chunk data from a later update packet. Empty chunk
compounds send no notice; empty update-packet compounds do. Absent tags
send no notice. Called once for each accepted tag,
only for a matching mod block entity that the client created.
Reads through `entity` already see the merged data. This notice cannot
change the received tag. Missing tags and vanilla block entities call nothing.
Related NeoForge receive paths `IBlockEntityExtension.onDataPacket` and
`handleUpdateTag` perform loading; they are not counterparts of this notice,
which runs after the merge.

neoforge: none (post-merge notice; IBlockEntityExtension.onDataPacket and handleUpdateTag are related loading paths, not counterparts)

hooks.doc:
The mod block entity `entity` has been added to its level, with saved
data already applied, before its first tick (`IBlockEntityExtension.onLoad`).
Fires once for each instance on both logical sides, including placement.
A chunk loaded again creates new instances and calls this hook again.
Read saved data through the attached handle and the supplied `HostSide`.

Where the mod block entity at `pos` draws, for culling
(NeoForge's `getRenderBoundingBox`): `bounds` is min x, y, z then max
x, y, z, in blocks from the block's lower north-west corner. It starts
as the block with a block of margin around it; widen it when your
`block_entity_submit` draws further (a tall shaft, a beam), or
set an infinite value for one never culled. Asked once a frame for each
within its view distance (`block_entity_view_distance`) whose chunk is drawn.

Draw the mod block entity at `pos`, of block `block`
(`mymod:machine`), on this client: once a frame while it is in view
(vanilla's `BlockEntityRenderer.submit`: within its view distance, 64 blocks unless
`block_entity_view_distance` says otherwise, its chunk
faded in, and its bounds, `block_entity_render_bounding_box`,
in the frustum), when its `id` is yours. `state` is the block's state
(`blockEntity.getBlockState()`: read its `facing` with
`native_block_state_property`), `entity` holds what the server sent
(`block_entity_update_tag`). Add geometry with
`native_draw_quad`, `native_draw_cube`, `native_draw_block` and
`native_draw_item` under `draw`'s pose stack, which starts at the
block's lower north-west corner, in blocks; `draw` also has the partial
tick, the game time and the block's light.

A server tick of the block entity at `pos`, in vanilla's order among
the others (`Level.tickBlockEntities`), when its `id` is yours: read
and change its saved compound `nbt`, its item slots `items` (keep
their count: as many as its container has, none without one) and the
data slots its menu shows (`data`). It is out of the world during the
call (the block entity at `pos` reads as a `Mod` with an empty id, and
a save leaves it out); if the call removes or replaces it, `entity` is
dropped. Clients, the window's own in single player included, get
what `block_entity_update_tag` gives when its chunk is sent or
its block changes.
Each Part starts with `Changed` and sees the preceding accepted payload.
`*event.reply = BlockEntityTickReply::Unchanged` discards only this Part's
payload edits: no reply snapshot is encoded, decoded or applied. Earlier
Parts' `Changed` edits survive later `Unchanged` replies.
If all Parts answer `Unchanged`, ticking alone does not dirty the chunk,
advance its revision or notify containers/comparators. The original
placeholder must still exist; independent Host writes keep their own effects,
including accepted item writes, while aborted Host transactions stay aborted.
The default `Changed` retains full checked write-back.

neoforge: none (vanilla BlockEntityTicker; NeoForge adds no event or extension for it)

hooks.doc:
Whether block `block`'s block entity ticks (`EntityBlock.getTicker`):
set `ticks` when it is yours. Asked for each of the block's states
when a world opens.
Set `ticks` to true to make it tick, and never clear a value an earlier mod or mixin set.

neoforge: none (vanilla EntityBlock.getTicker; NeoForge adds no event or extension for it)

hooks.doc:
Extend existing types' valid blocks (NeoForge `BlockEntityTypeAddBlocksEvent`).
Fired after content declarations, before worlds load. `types` contains every
registered type. Append `(type, block)` pairs to `additions`; this never changes
the block's factory or ticker. Filter `types` to implement predicate selection.
Use `event.modify(kind, blocks)` for a direct addition, or
`event.modify_matching(predicate, blocks)` for all matching registered keys.
Duplicate additions are harmless; unknown keys or incompatible classes fail startup.
Existing sign-template memberships remain valid without a listener.
Blocks must share the common vanilla superclass of the type's existing blocks.

What clients get of the block entity at `pos` when its `id` is
yours (`BlockEntity.getUpdateTag`): set `tag` to it, read from
`entity` alone. Asked on the server whenever a chunk holding it is
sent and whenever its block changes, on the server thread or, for a
saved chunk sent past the view distance (`lan::far`), another one; a client's copy of the block
entity (made by `block_entity` there) merges it into its `nbt`.
Leave it unset to send no tag of yours. A block change puts the one-shot fields of
`ModBlockEntityView::set_client_update_fields` over it, and sends them alone when it is unset.

neoforge: none (vanilla BlockEntity.getUpdateTag; NeoForge adds no event or extension for it); IBlockEntityExtension.handleUpdateTag is the client half

hooks.doc:
How far from the camera the mod block entity of block `block` draws, in blocks
(vanilla's `BlockEntityRenderer.getViewDistance`): 64 unless a part answers. Set
`distance` for your own block: further for something seen from afar (a beacon-like
beam, a large display), nearer for small detail. It is asked once for each mod block,
the first time this client draws block entities, and kept: never per frame. A value
that isn't finite and above 0 is ignored. Beyond NeoForge: the renderer's own method,
no event.

neoforge: none (vanilla BlockEntityRenderer.getViewDistance; NeoForge adds no event or extension for it)

hooks.doc:
A block at `pos` is about to fade from `from` to `to` because of
melting or coral death. Set `cancel` to keep it. Server-side.
A dispenser at `pos` failed to dispense `item`. Server-side.

Precipitation is about to form ice or place or thicken snow at `pos`.
`from` and `to` are block state IDs. Set `cancel` to keep the old state.
Server-side.

A sapling, azalea, mushroom or fungus at `pos` is about to grow into the
configured `feature`, `None` when vanilla has none to place (a lone dark
oak sapling). Set `cancel`, or `feature` to `None`, to keep the block;
set `feature` to another key to grow that one. Server-side.
Mods can use `level.random()` to access the growth random source.

Before an eligible targeted block's selection outline is built.
Cancel skips only the default block highlight, after normal HUD and game-mode gates.

On an authoritative server, fire is about to be placed at `pos` by
flint and steel, a fire charge, lava, lightning or fire spread. Set
`player` is the acting server player when there is one. Set `cancel` to
leave the position unchanged.

neoforge: none (NeoForge has no such event; Bukkit's BlockIgniteEvent)

hooks.doc: The jump factor of a block state this part is attached to (`Block.getJumpFactor`, which `Entity.getBlockJumpFactor` reads for the player, the cube, the panda, the rabbit and every other living jumper) is being read; vanilla's values are 0.5 for honey and 1.0 for the rest. A part may change `factor` (`event.factor`). The entity reads the block at its feet and, when that gives 1.0, the block below it, so a changed factor takes part in that choice exactly as the block's own would. It runs for each read, on both sides and on the client's replayed ticks, so register the mod on both and keep the listener a pure function of its inputs. It is given the loop `context` of the side that ticks the entity, and takes no `Host`. NeoForge's counterpart `Block.getJumpFactor()` is a method of the block, with no bus event, so this is a part method only; a mod reacting to its own blocks uses this part. Diverges from upstream: new hook.

neoforge: none (vanilla Block.getJumpFactor; NeoForge adds no event or extension for it)

hooks.doc:
A guest's block inventory lock check at `pos`. `locked` is the
vanilla result and may be changed. The guest's state is not swapped in.

The optional classification of `event.state` at `event.pos`
(`IBlockExtension.getBlockPathType`). Asked before every vanilla rule,
including air and `is_pathfindable`. `Some` replaces the whole static
classification; `None` declines to vanilla. The readonly host reads the
owning level, so the same state may answer differently at different positions.
No mob is supplied: engine callers in NeoForge pass null. The server's
4096-slot positional cache stores the final static classification, including
Open, until a matching block-updated notification or slot collision. It
survives time, reload and chunk lifetime. Ordinary writes clear only on
actual change with UPDATE_CLIENTS and full status at least BLOCK_TICKING;
direct block-entity notifications clear even unchanged state. Neighbour
and mob-specific adjustments run afterwards, outside that cache.
Diverges from upstream: new hook.

A sculk sensor or shrieker received a vibration for `event` at `pos`.
Set `cancel` to suppress its response. Server-side.

Hides a block state from the mesher: set `event.hidden` and the state draws nothing, as if its blocks were air. Its neighbours' faces toward it show, it no longer hides what is behind it, and its fluid layer and block entity are not drawn; light, collision and the server are untouched. The answer depends on the state alone and is resolved at mesh time, never per frame: the game asks once for every state when the client joins a world, and again for every state each time a mod calls `ClientHost::refresh_render_visibility` (a toggle, an ore scanner). Attach the part to vanilla blocks with `block_part_tag`. With no mod answering, the mesher pays nothing.

Draw a block overlay a mod said it draws itself (`custom_draw` in
`extract_block_screen_effect`), before vanilla's overlay of that kind, once a frame each.
A canceled overlay is asked too. Set `replace_vanilla` to leave vanilla's overlay out.
`effect`, `state` and `pos` are the extract event's; `partial_tick` is the world's and
`hide_gui` says the HUD is hidden. Every mod is asked about every such overlay, so a mod
ignores those it did not claim. Client-side.

A dispenser sheared `entity` of kind `kind` at the block in front of
its own block at `pos`, after the shearing effects. Server-side.

The redstone signal the block `state` at `pos` gives on its `face`, the
side that touches the block reading it: `BlockState.getDirectSignal`
when `direct` (what passes through a block it touches, as a lever's
does), else `getSignal`. `signal` holds vanilla's answer: change it when
the block is yours (0 to 15; anything else is clamped). Asked very often,
from inside the level's update, so answer from your own state: check the
block first, and don't read or change the world here. When the answer
changes, and once the block is placed, call
`level.update_neighbors(host, pos, state, NeighbourUpdate::Neighbours)`. Authoritative
servers only.

neoforge: none (vanilla BlockBehaviour.getSignal and getDirectSignal; NeoForge adds no event or extension for it)

hooks.doc: The speed factor of a block state this part is attached to (`Block.getSpeedFactor`, which `Entity.getBlockSpeedFactor` reads for the player, mobs, boats and minecarts where vanilla reads it) is being read; vanilla's values are 0.4 for honey and soul sand and 1.0 for the rest. A part may change `factor` (`event.factor`). The entity reads the block at its feet and, when that is not water or a bubble column and gives 1.0, the block below it, so a changed factor takes part in that choice exactly as the block's own would. It runs for each read, on both sides and on the client's replayed ticks, so register the mod on both and keep the listener a pure function of its inputs. It is given the loop `context` of the side that ticks the entity, and takes no `Host`. NeoForge's counterpart `Block.getSpeedFactor()` is a method of the block, with no bus event, so this is a part method only; a mod reacting to its own blocks uses this part. Diverges from upstream: new hook.

neoforge: none (vanilla Block.getSpeedFactor; NeoForge adds no event or extension for it)

hooks.doc:
On an authoritative server, a fluid flows or fire spreads from `from`
into `to` (`kind` is `fluid` or `fire`): `FlowingFluid.spreadTo`, and
`FireBlock.tick` setting fire to `to` or burning it (`checkBurnOut`).
Set `canceled` to leave the block at `to` as it is. Fluids ask on
every flow: answer fast.

neoforge: none (BlockEvent.FluidPlaceBlockEvent covers only fluids making stone and the like, not flow or fire spread)

hooks.doc:
`Block.stepOn` for a mod block, on its authoritative server level.
No self: the simulation owns the entity during this callback.

neoforge: none (vanilla Block.stepOn; NeoForge adds no event or extension for it)

hooks.doc:
Blocks this mod adds, declared in code rather than one file each
(NeoForge's `DeferredRegister.Blocks` drained by `RegisterEvent`):
push a `mod_api::Block` per block, the same declaration
a content mod's `data/<id>/horizon/block/<path>.json` holds (a
vanilla `template`, `properties`, `state_properties`, `shapes`...),
with its id in a namespace owned by your mod's manifest. It has a block
item, as a file's does, unless `item` is false (`Block::with_item(false)`).
They join the content mods' blocks: the one whose
id is that namespace when it is on (your models, textures, loot and
recipes are its files), else one of their own, with the template's
look. Ids, saves and the check that a joining client has the same
blocks are the files' (docs/modding/src/how-to/content-mods.md). Asked once at start, on every
side, before any resource loads: push the same ones every time, from
nothing but your code. Unowned namespaces refuse registration, naming the mod
and namespace. Each mod receives its own declaration batch. Declarations
that don't pass the other files' checks
are logged and that namespace's are left out.

`BonemealEvent`: bone meal from `stack` used on the block `state` at
`pos` (`BoneMealItem.growCrop`), by `player` or, when it is `None`, by
a dispenser or a villager. `valid_bonemeal_target` is the block's
`isValidBonemealTarget`. Cancel skips vanilla's growth, the block's
own bone meal Parts and the meal's use: `growCrop` then answers
`successful` (`setSuccessful`), which is `false` unless a mod sets it.
Fired on both sides; changes to `stack` stay. Set it to None to consume
the whole stack; a nonempty result is validated before any write-back.

An entity bounced off a block state this part is attached to (`Block.bounceOn`), after falling `event.fall_distance` blocks. It fires only when the entity bounced, just before vanilla sets its movement. `event.movement` is the movement the bounce leaves it (`x`, `y`, `z`): change it to change what the entity keeps. It runs inside the entity's move, on the level random host: it reads blocks and draws the level's random in vanilla's order, but writes nothing. Players and mobs bounce here; dropped items and the other entities do not.

neoforge: none (vanilla Block.bounceOn; IBlockExtension.getBounceRestitution only returns a factor)

hooks.doc:
An entity landed on a block state this part is attached to and asks its restitution
(`IBlockExtension.getBounceRestitution`, which `Entity.getBlockBounciness` asks of the block
an entity lands on): the factor its vertical speed is multiplied by when it hits the block
from above. Set `factor` (`event.factor`) to change it; it starts at the block's own value,
1.0 for slime, 0.75 for a bed or a shelf mushroom and zero for the rest. `event.entity` and
`event.kind` are the entity that landed and its type, and `event.pos` is the block it
reads (`Entity.getOnPosLegacy`). The entity takes the larger of the factor and its own
bounciness and, unless it is a living one, multiplies it by 0.8 as vanilla does, so 0.5
bounces an entity half as high as slime. A sneaking player, a block tagged
`#minecraft:suppresses_bounce` and a fall too slow to matter still do not bounce, and
`bounce_on` still hears the bounce afterwards. A non-finite answer is ignored.

Asked for the player and the mobs on both sides, so a client predicts its own bounce with
the answer: register the mod on both and answer the same on each. The level host reads
the entity's level (match `LevelSide` for its side) and cannot write; the question can be
asked more than once for one tick: a client predicting its own move and a server
replaying a client's tick ask again. The answer must be a pure function of the host
and the event: no random draws, no part state that changes per call, and no counting
calls. The same inputs must give the same factor.
Dropped items keep their own slime rule. With no part attached to the state, the
owning game checks the hook subscription and prepared API block key before any event
conversion, so the cost is one table lookup. Diverges from upstream: new hook.

A player breaks the block `state` at `pos`, once the game allowed it
(the held item can break blocks, the debug stick didn't take the
click): where `ServerPlayerGameMode.destroyBlock` starts. Set
`canceled` to keep the block: nothing is destroyed or dropped, and a
guest sees it back. Set `exp_to_drop` to `Some(amount)` to replace
the experience sample later, after item drops are prepared;
`None` keeps sampling. A subscribed block part's `exp_drop` answer is
supplied as this event's initial amount. `block_drops` sees and may change that
amount afterwards; cancellation or disabled block drops suppresses it.
Server-side, for every player of the world (the
helpers read the acting one). Diverges from upstream: renamed from
`destroy_block`, to NeoForge's `BreakBlockEvent`.

A brewing stand finished brewing at `pos`, after its bottle contents
were changed. Server-side.
A brewing stand at `pos` consumed `fuel` and gained brewing fuel. Server-side.
A brewing stand at `pos` began brewing `ingredient`, after fuel and the timer were set. Server-side.

A server broadcast line is about to be logged and sent. Change `line`
or set `cancel` to drop it.

neoforge: none (NeoForge has no such event; Bukkit's BroadcastMessageEvent)

hooks.doc:
A server player empties a bucket at `pos` (`fluid`: `minecraft:water`,
`minecraft:lava`, `minecraft:powder_snow`; a fish or axolotl bucket
empties `minecraft:water`): where `BucketItem.use` has found the block
the fluid goes into and the player may build there, right before it is
placed. Set `cancel` and nothing is poured and the bucket stays full.
The player's state is swapped in, so `PlayerRef::tell` answers them. Only
for guests of a server. `fill_bucket` hears this click too (and
the filling one) without the player and the fluid. Not heard: a
dispenser, a cauldron, and a fluid a block places itself.

neoforge: none (vanilla BucketItem.emptyContents; NeoForge has no matching event)

hooks.doc:
The stacks a mod adds to the creative tab `tab` (`minecraft:ingredients`, or another mod's
`<mod id>:<name>`) while the tabs' contents are built (NeoForge's
`BuildCreativeModeTabContentsEvent`, during vanilla's `CreativeModeTabs.buildAllTabContents`):
push each stack to `items`, in order (`accept`). They come after the tab's own items and
those of the mods before, and join the end of the search tab. A stack the tab or the search
tab already lists (the same item and components) is not listed twice there, and an empty
stack is left out. `has_permissions` is the build's `hasPermissions`: whether the operator
items tab is allowed (the player can use game master blocks and the Operator Items Tab
option is on). Asked for every item tab, the operator items tab and the mods' tabs among
them, not for the search, saved toolbars or survival inventory tabs. Asked when the tabs
are built: the first time the creative inventory opens after the game's resources load,
and again whenever `has_permissions` changes. Client-side.

The mouse sensitivity and cinematic camera option a grabbed player's
mouse turn reads this frame (`MouseHandler.turnPlayer`). Change either
for this turn only; the options are unchanged. Client-side. This shapes how far the
mouse turns the view; `ClientHost::set_local_rotation` sets the view directly, and the
two meet in the same angles the tick's move packet sends.

Final scaled third-person camera distance, before visual-shape collision clipping.
`entity` includes its living scale/distance and optional mount scale/distance.
Only finite requests in 0..=1024 blocks replace the vanilla distance.

The camera this frame is drawn from, `partial` ticks past the last tick, after vanilla
placed it (`Camera.update`): its position, and its yaw and pitch in degrees. Set them to
draw the world from anywhere: a cinematic or replay camera. Only the picture, the sound's
listener and the billboards facing the camera follow it; the player, where they aim, the
first-person hand and which chunks load stay the player's. Values that aren't finite keep
vanilla's. Not called on the title screen's panorama.
`camera_roll`, asked right after, rolls it.

The roll of the camera this frame is drawn from, in degrees about its view direction,
asked right after `camera_pose` with the same `partial`. It starts at 0 each frame and is
kept within a turn. It turns the drawn camera, a front view's too: at +90 the world's up
is at the screen's left, as `Camera.setRotation`'s roll and NeoForge's
`ViewportEvent.ComputeCameraAngles` turn it. The picture, the frustum, the billboards facing the camera, `Camera.view`
and `project` follow it; the first-person hand, the HUD and where the player aims don't.
Distortion Effects doesn't scale it, unlike `camera_shake`. A value that isn't finite is
0. Not called on the title screen's panorama.

The camera shake native mods ask for in this frame, `partial` ticks
past the last tick (0 to 1): add your pitch, yaw and roll in degrees
and your offset in blocks, along the camera's right, up and back, to
`shake`, so several mods' shakes add up. Read while playing only;
Horizon scales the sum by Distortion Effects and bounds it
(`native_shake_matrix`).

Camera submersion fog type (`Camera.getFluidInCamera`), checked before fog and camera
fluid effects are set up. Allows native mods (such as Freecam) to clear underwater,
lava or powder snow submersion by setting `fog_type` to `FogType::Atmospheric`.

`key.togglePerspective` (F5) is cycling the window's camera type (`Minecraft.handleKeybinds`
calling `Options.setCameraType(getCameraType().cycle())`): `previous` is the type it leaves,
and `next` comes in as vanilla's next one (first person, third person behind, third person
in front, then first person again); set `next` to another, to skip a type or keep one.
Once a press, before the type changes; the post effect of the camera entity follows the
answer as it follows vanilla's. `camera_type` and `set_camera_type` read and set the type
at any other moment. Client-side. Beyond NeoForge: there is no counterpart. Diverges from
upstream: new hook.

neoforge: none (NeoForge has no camera type event)

hooks.doc: An item was placed on a campfire at `pos` and began cooking.

On an authoritative server, whether the block `state` at `pos` lets the fence, wall, or
iron bars or pane `connector` beside it connect to it
(`IBlockExtension.canBeConnectedTo`): the block being connected to answers, not the
connecting one. `kind` names the connector's vanilla rule, `direction` points from the
block toward the connector and `face_solid` is whether the block's face toward it is
sturdy. Asked once the connector's vanilla rule answered, each time the connector is
placed or settles its shape toward the block. `Some(true)` connects, `Some(false)`
refuses and `None` keeps vanilla's rule. The connector's own `connects_to` is asked
after, starting from this answer, and has the last word. A panicking part is contained
and vanilla's answer is used. The level is read-only. With no part attached to the
state, the cost is one table lookup. Diverges from upstream: new hook.

Whether `fluid` at `fluid_pos` waters the farmland this part is attached to, the block
`state` at `pos` (`IBlockExtension.canBeHydrated`): set `hydrates` to `Some(true)` or
`Some(false)`, or leave it `None` for vanilla's rule, a fluid in `#minecraft:water`.
`FarmlandBlock.randomTick` scans the 9×2×9 box from `pos` (x and z from −4 to 4, y 0 and 1)
and asks only where the fluid is not empty, in x, then y, then z order; the first position
that hydrates ends the scan, and the farmland goes to moisture 7. Rain on the block above,
moisture changes and drying out are unchanged. The farmland decides which fluids water it.
Asked on an authoritative server; the level is read-only. With no part attached to the
farmland, the scan is vanilla's. Diverges from upstream: new hook.

`CanContinueSleepingEvent`: a sleeping living entity's check that it may go on
sleeping, run each tick for a server player the dead and health checks would not
already wake, and for a sleeping villager or wandering trader. `entity` is its UUID,
`name` a player's name (empty for a mob) and `kind` its type (`minecraft:player`).
`problem` is what vanilla found (`getProblem`): `NotPossibleHere` when the bed at `pos`
is gone, `NotPossibleNow` when a player's bed rule no longer lets them sleep (daytime),
none when nothing is wrong. `may_continue` starts empty, meaning `problem.is_none()` (`mayContinueSleeping`);
set it `Some(true)` to keep them asleep, `Some(false)` to wake them. The player's state is not swapped in
on a guest tick.

On an authoritative server, whether the block `state` at `pos`, destroyed by
`explosion`, drops (`IBlockExtension.canDropFromExplosion`), asked where
`BlockBehaviour.onExplosionHit` asks `Block.dropFromExplosion`. `Some(false)` skips
what the drop runs: the block's `spawnAfterBreak` (an infested block's silverfish, an
ore's experience) and its loot; `Some(true)` runs them, even for TNT; `None` keeps
vanilla's answer, where only TNT drops nothing. The block is removed either way, and a
TNT still primes (`TntBlock.wasExploded` is not part of the answer). A panicking part
is contained and vanilla's answer is used. The level is read-only. With no part
attached to the state, the cost is one table lookup. Diverges from upstream: new hook.

`Player.canEat` for `stack`, from `Consumable.canConsume` when eating
starts and block interaction eligibility for cake and candle cake.
For cake, `stack` is the held stack (None for an empty hand), and
`can_always_eat` is false. `vanilla_can_eat` is vanilla's answer (creative,
`can_always_eat`, or hungry). Answer `Some(false)` to refuse the food,
`Some(true)` to let a full player eat; `can_eat` left `None` keeps
`vanilla_can_eat`. Both sides (the client starts eating as the
server does), so answer from the stack and the player alone.

neoforge: none (vanilla Player.canEat; NeoForge adds no event or extension for it)

hooks.doc:
On an authoritative server, whether `entity` may destroy the block `state` at `pos`
(`IBlockExtension.canEntityDestroy`), asked where vanilla asks its per-block rule: the
wither's block break (`WitherBoss.canDestroy`: not `#wither_immune`), a dangerous
wither skull's blast (the entity is the skull, readable during the blast; only a block
it may destroy has its resistance capped at 0.8), the dragon's `checkWalls` (a
`#dragon_transparent` block is skipped before the part is asked, and a
`#dragon_immune` block stays even on a yes), a zombie's door breaking (asked as the
goal starts) and the turtle-egg `RemoveBlockGoal`'s target choice. `Some(true)` makes a
block vanilla spares destroyable for that entity, `Some(false)` spares one it would
break (the dragon is then in a wall), and `None` keeps vanilla's rule. The griefing
gate (`entity_mob_griefing`) runs first, so with griefing off nothing breaks whatever
the part says, and `living_destroy_block` can still keep a block the part allowed (the
egg goal's target choice fires no such event). Ravager: griefing event only. A
panicking part is contained and vanilla's rule is used. Asked every tick for each
block in the dragon's head, neck and body: answer fast, from the inputs. The host is
read-only. With no part attached to the state, the cost is one table lookup. Diverges
from upstream: new hook.

NeoForge's `IItemExtension.canEquip`: may `stack` go into the equipment
slot `slot` of the living entity `entity`, of type `kind`
(`minecraft:player`)? `slot` is an `EquipmentSlot` name: `head`,
`chest`, `legs`, `feet`, `mainhand` or `offhand`, and `body` or
`saddle` from a dispenser. `can_equip` arrives holding the data answer,
as `LivingEntity.isEquippableInSlot` and `Equippable.canBeEquippedBy`
read the stack's own `equippable` component (a stack's override
replaces the item's): yes when it names that slot and its
`allowed_entities` is absent or lists the entity type (an empty list
allows none); with no component, removed or never there, yes for
`mainhand` only. Set it either way. Asked where vanilla asks: the
armour slots of a player's inventory menu (`ArmorSlot.mayPlace`, which a
shift-click into one reaches too), a dispenser equipping what stands in
front of it (`EquipmentDispenseItemBehavior`, one entity at a time) and
a mob picking an item up off the ground (`Mob.equipItemIfPossible`). It
decides whether the stack fits the slot, not what the slot holds,
whether the entity may wear one at all (`canUseSlot`) or the dispenser's
own rules for the entity. Only the `ItemPart`s attached to `stack`'s
item are asked, on both sides, as the client's menu predicts the slot.
`host` is read-only: read `entity` through it (its position, its
equipment) to answer from its state when asked. The stack is converted
once and lent to each slot and entity a native menu click, dispense or pickup
asks about. Each decision prepares one owned copy per participating wasm guest
instance and lends it by token to every candidate. Mutable access invalidates
the source revision; replacing or removing it changes its identity. Stale
preparation and stale apply preconditions refuse without asking again. Pickup
scope is one mob's attempt. Missing prepared exports refuse at load or part
registration. A stale or missing target refuses wherever a part is asked;
the no-listener data path performs no conversion or entity lookup.
Target type, position, health, maximum health, alive/living status and physical
equipment are retained outside traversal; other Host reads can allocate.

NeoForge's `IItemExtension.canFitInsideContainerItems`: may `stack` go inside an item
that holds items? `fits` arrives with vanilla's answer
(`Item.canFitInsideContainerItems`): every stack fits except a shulker box. Set it
`true` or `false`. It is asked, on both sides, wherever that rule is:
- a shulker box's slots (`ShulkerBoxSlot.mayPlace`), in its menu and a guest's;
- a bundle (`BundleContents.canItemBeInBundle`): a click that puts the stack in a
  bundle, and the `/item` bundle contents;
- the item slots a mod gives an item (`item_container`) and its bundle slots.

A hopper filling a shulker box doesn't ask: vanilla tests the block there, not this.
A `true` for a shulker box lets shulker boxes nest. That is the mod's choice, and the
NBT readers' depth limit still bounds it. Only the `ItemPart`s attached to `stack`'s
item are asked. It is given the loop `context` of the side that runs the menu or the
insert and takes no `Host`, so answer from the stack and `context` alone, and fast:
a click may ask it for each slot it checks. With no part on the stack's item the cost
is one table lookup, and the stack isn't converted. The contract beyond the method's
name and parameters is Horizon's reading, not checked against NeoForge's. Diverges
from upstream: new hook.

NeoForge's `IItemExtension.canGrindstoneRepair`: does the grindstone repair `stack` as
it repairs a damageable item? `can_repair` arrives with vanilla's answer, whether the
stack is damageable (`ItemStack.isDamageableItem`); set it `true` or `false`. It is
asked at two places, on both sides (the server's menus and the client's own result):
- `GrindstoneMenu.mergeItems`, for the top stack when both inputs are single stacks of
  the same item. `true` takes the repair branch: one item, the enchantments of both
  merged, then all but the curses removed. Durability is merged only when the result
  has durability, as vanilla checks it again on the copy. `false` takes the other
  branch: two matching stacks of an item that stacks give two, and anything else
  gives nothing.
- The input slots' `mayPlace` (damageable or enchanted): a granted stack can be placed.
  This site is Horizon's reading.

A single enchanted input is never asked: that branch merges nothing. Only the
`ItemPart`s attached to `stack`'s item are asked. It is given the loop `context` of the
side that runs the menu and takes no `Host`, so answer from the stack and `context`
alone, and fast. With no part on the stack's item the cost is one table lookup, and
the stack isn't converted. The contract beyond the method's name and parameters is
Horizon's reading, not checked against NeoForge's. Diverges from upstream: new hook.

Whether the player `player`'s tool harvests the block `state` at `pos`
(`IBlockExtension.canHarvestBlock`, what `Player.hasCorrectToolForDrops` asks of the block).
`can_harvest` starts with vanilla's answer: false for a block that needs a tool the player's
held item is not, true otherwise. Set it for your own block; false breaks the block and drops
nothing, and the dig is slowed as vanilla slows a wrong tool. The part answers first and the
global `player_harvest_check` hears the result, so a mod reacting to every block still has the
last word. Asked wherever the harvest rule is: the dig's progress (both sides, so a client
predicts it), the break and a door's break.

NeoForge's `IItemExtension.canPerformAction`: can `stack` perform the item
ability `ability`, a plain, case-sensitive name such as `shield_block`,
`shears_harvest` or `shears_carve` (a mod's own
abilities also use plain names, such as `my_mod_chop`)? `can_perform` arrives with
vanilla's answer for that ability: the item kind's (shears shear) or the
stack's component (`blocks_attacks`, a shield's, blocks); set it either
way and the stack grants or loses the ability. Loot conditions use the shared
item defaults; action sites retain their own vanilla answers until arismoko/horizon#3330. Asked where vanilla checks
the item for an action: a raised item blocking attacks
(`shield_block`: a granted stack blocks as a bare
`blocks_attacks` component does, a denied one never blocks nor is raised);
shearing a sheep, mooshroom, snow golem or bogged, a dispenser's shears
and a bee nest's honeycombs (`shears_harvest`); carving a pumpkin
(`shears_carve`). It decides whether the stack may do the action,
not what the action does to the world or the tool (`block_tool_modification`
is the block's side of a tool action; item wear is its own). Only the
`ItemPart`s attached to `stack`'s item are asked, on both sides, so the
client's prediction agrees with the server: answer from the stack and
`ability` alone, and fast. An item with no such part costs one table lookup.

A server player tries to sleep in the bed whose head is at `pos`
(NeoForge's `CanPlayerSleepEvent`, vanilla's `ServerPlayer.startSleepInBed`).
`problem` is what vanilla found, first problem only: `too_far_away`,
`obstructed`, `not_possible_now` (not night or thunder, the bed rule),
`not_safe` (monsters near), or `None`. A mod may set `None` to let the
player sleep anyway, or one of those names (`other_problem` refuses
without a message) to refuse. The spawn point is set before it fires,
as in vanilla, only when vanilla found no problem. After it,
`player_bed_enter` still fires and may cancel. Server-side.

Whether the block state this part is attached to sticks to `other`, the state beside it
(`IBlockExtension.canStickTo`): set `sticks` to decide. `sticks` starts with vanilla's
answer: false for honey beside slime (as `is_slime_block` tells slime), otherwise true when
either state is sticky (`is_sticky_block`). Two blocks stick when each says it sticks to the
other, as `PistonStructureResolver` asks (NeoForge's `canStickToEachOther`), so a part that
answers false for one neighbour is enough to let go of it and a part cannot make a block
stick to one that refuses. The pair is asked from both sides, and the other block's part, if it
has one, answers its own side. Asked on an authoritative server while a piston resolves its
structure: answer from the two states, without touching the world. With no part attached to
the state, the cost is one table lookup. Diverges from upstream: new hook.

On an authoritative server, `BlockState.canSurvive` for `state` at
`pos` (`BlockBehaviour.canSurvive`), before the block answers it: as
it is placed (`BlockItem.canPlace`), from a shape update of a block
whose template checks it (a plant, a torch, a sign: false breaks the
block with its drops), and wherever else vanilla asks. `state` may not
be in the world yet, so decide from `state`. Answer only for your own
blocks: `Some(false)` refuses the spot, `Some(true)` allows it, and
the block's own rule doesn't run. The level is read-only. Asked on
every shape update of such a block: keep it short.

neoforge: none (vanilla BlockBehaviour.canSurvive; NeoForge adds no event or extension for it)

hooks.doc:
`can_survive` again, for the world generation of the server: while a feature places
`state` at `pos`, its parts answer `survives` here, as they answer `survives` in the
live game. Answer only for your own blocks: `Some(false)` refuses the spot, `Some(true)`
allows it, and the block's own rule doesn't run. A rule that picks the ground the block
stands on answers `may_place_on_v2` instead. Server-side, on the worldgen worker threads
and on the server thread, with the server's worldgen `context`: no `Host`, no writes. A
panicking part is contained and the block's own rule kept. Diverges from upstream:
`can_survive` in world generation.

neoforge: none (vanilla BlockBehaviour.canSurvive; NeoForge adds no event or extension for it)

hooks.doc:
On an authoritative server, `IBlockExtension.canSustainPlant` for the soil `ground` at
`ground_pos` and the plant `state` above it, asked before the plant answers its own
`mayPlaceOn` (`may_place_on`) wherever vanilla's plant rule reads its ground: when the plant is
placed, from its shape update and wherever else vanilla asks. `Some(true)` lets the plant
stand there, `Some(false)` refuses it (a planted one pops off when its ground changes to this block),
and left `None` the plant's own `may_place_on` answers, as vanilla's does. Answer only for
your own soil. The level is read-only. Runs on every shape update of a plant over a part's
block: keep it short.

`can_sustain_plant` again, for the world generation of the server: while a feature places
the plant `state` on the soil `ground` at `ground_pos`, the soil's parts answer `sustains`
here. Asked before the plant's `may_place_on_v2`, as the live game asks it before the
plant's `may_place_on`: the soil's answer is the plant's, and the plant is not asked.
`Some(true)` lets the plant stand there, `Some(false)` refuses it, and left `None` the
plant answers. Answer only for your own soil. Server-side, on the worldgen worker threads
and on the server thread, with the server's worldgen `context`: no `Host`, no writes. A
panicking part is contained and the plant's own rule kept. Diverges from upstream:
`can_sustain_plant` in world generation.

On an authoritative server, a cauldron at `pos` is about to change
fill level from `from_level` to `to_level` for `reason`. Set `cancel`
to leave it unchanged.

neoforge: none (NeoForge has no such event; Bukkit's CauldronLevelChangeEvent)

hooks.doc:
A public chat line from `sender` (`sender_name`) is about to reach the placed player
`recipient`: a player's chat after `server_chat` let it through, or a `/say` or `/me`
(signed or not). `message` is the text players see: what `server_chat` left, or the
command's text. Set `hidden` and that one receiver is not sent the line at all, no chat
index and no pending acknowledgement; the others still get it, signed as it was sent, so
its signature still verifies for them. It is asked once for each placed receiver, the
sender included, before any of them is sent the line, in the order the hub lists them.
Whispers (`/msg`) are not public and are not heard here, and neither is the line the
server's log keeps: hiding is per receiver. This is not a second `server_chat`: that
hook is heard once for a line, only for typed chat, and cancels it for everyone; this one
is per receiver, and covers `/say` and `/me`. With no listener nothing is asked and
nothing is allocated. A fault or an epoch timeout in a wasm listener answers nothing, so
the line is sent, like every cancellable hook. No player's state is swapped in.
Server-side.

neoforge: none (NeoForge sends a chat line to every player; it has no per-receiver event)

hooks.doc: `chat_suggestion_applied(original, start, end, suggestion, input)` reports a chat completion after Tab or a click. The range is in UTF-16 units of the list's original input, including when cycling; input is the resulting length-limited field value. Client-only, read-only. Bundles need "hooks": @API:chat_suggestion_applied@.

neoforge: none (vanilla command suggestions; NeoForge adds no event)

hooks.doc:
Chunk `chunk` (`[x, z]`, in chunks) of `dimension` came into the world
(NeoForge's `ChunkEvent.Load`): `new` when it was just generated, false
when read from the save. A flat world's chunk that leaves before it's
first lit isn't saved, so it's generated, and new, again; one generated
as the players left is new when it next comes, unless the server
restarts first, or the level closes for being empty, which drops its
memory of what never saved. Its blocks and block entities are there,
but its saved entities join afterwards and its light may not be ready:
change the world from a later tick. The chunks around the spawn come
before `server_started`. Not told of a chunk a client receives.
The chunks leaving in the same tick were already copied for their last
save: an edit made here to one of them (a neighbour's block entity, say)
is not in that copy, and is dropped with the chunk.
Server-side.

`chunk`'s packet went to `player` (NeoForge's `ChunkWatchEvent.Sent`,
at the end of `PlayerChunkSender.sendChunk`), after `chunk_watch`, so
a mod can send its own data for the chunk now. Told after the server's
network step for the level, with the state after that step, as
`chunk_watch`. Not told for the far ring's columns. Server-side.

`chunk`'s ticket level went from `old` to `new` (NeoForge's
`ChunkTicketLevelUpdatedEvent`, from `ChunkMap.updateChunkScheduling`):
a player, a forced chunk, a portal or the dragon fight's arena began or
ceased to keep it alive or ticking. It is the level of the chunk's
loading tickets (`DistanceManager`'s chunk tracker), not the
simulation distance's. A level is a `ChunkTicketLevel`: the number
`ChunkLevel` gives, 31 and lower entity ticking, 32 block ticking and 33
loaded without ticking, or `Unloaded`; none is clamped to the ticking
range. Never told with `old == new`.

Told in order, once for each time a chunk's level changed: a chunk that
changes twice in a tick is told twice, the second `old` the first `new`.
Within one update of the level's tickets the chunks come by position (x,
then z), which is not vanilla's order. A new level's tickets tell every
chunk they keep loaded as coming from `Unloaded`. Told once a tick, in
the server's tick of the level, after the tickets were updated for
every player there; a level with no player in it is not ticked and
tells nothing until it is. NeoForge's `chunkHolder` is not given:
Horizon keeps no chunk holders. Server-side.

Chunk `chunk` of `dimension` left the world (NeoForge's
`ChunkEvent.Unload`), with a level that closes for being empty too. Don't
read its blocks. Its block entities are still there, but changes made in
this hook aren't saved: as in vanilla, the chunk is saved before it unloads.
Not told when the world closes, which `world_lifecycle` tells.
Server-side.

`player` stopped watching `chunk` (NeoForge's `ChunkWatchEvent.UnWatch`,
`ChunkMap.dropChunk`): it left their view, or they leave the level
(through a portal or a teleport, or respawning) or the server. Once for
each chunk `chunk_watch` told of. After a disconnect the player handle
no longer reads. Told after the server's network step for the level,
with the state after that step, as `chunk_watch`. Not told when the
server stops. Server-side.

`player` started watching `chunk` (NeoForge's `ChunkWatchEvent.Watch`):
the chunk came into their view and goes to their client, once until
`chunk_unwatch`. Vanilla tells it as the chunk is queued
(`ChunkMap.markChunkPendingToSend`); Horizon picks a chunk only as it
sends it, so this comes just before `chunk_sent` for the same chunk.
Told after the server's network step for the level, and a handler sees
the state after that step; the order per player and chunk is vanilla's.
Not told for the far ring's columns past the view distance (a Horizon
server option). Server-side.

Before a client's ordinary melee click attacks entities (not a spear jab), after the
interaction-key cancellation hook. `targets` starts with the crosshair entity, if any.
Replace, clear or append targets for redirected or multi-target hits. There is no batch
cap. Duplicates are sent once, in first-occurrence order. Every target is rechecked for
the current client epoch, attackability, reach,
held-item range and occlusion. Clearing an entity hit does not mine the block behind
it; an untouched empty list keeps vanilla's block/miss path. Server checks and cooldowns
still apply to every attack. Returning `Flow::Cancel` cancels the whole batch.
NeoForge's `AttackEntityEvent` is the corresponding attack notice; this hook is client-side only.

NeoForge's `ClientChatEvent`: a client is about to send `message`.
`original_message` is immutable; change `message` or set `cancel` to
prevent sending.

NeoForge's `ClientChatReceivedEvent`: a chat line from the server is
about to show, once Chat Delay lets it through. `system` is a system
message (`ClientChatReceivedEvent.System`), shown in the action bar
when `overlay` is set; otherwise a player or disguised message in its
chat type `chat_type` (`getBoundChatType`, its registry name; `None`
for a system message or an inline chat type). `sender` is the player's
UUID, 0 (`Util.NIL_UUID`) for system and disguised messages.
`player_message` is the message as the player signed it
(`ClientChatReceivedEvent.Player.getPlayerChatMessage`): its body,
whether a signature validated, timestamp, salt, the server's unsigned
replacement and the filter mask; `None` for system and disguised
messages. `message`
starts as the decorated line; replace it and the chat shows the new
one, while the narrator still says the original. Set `cancel` and it
doesn't show: a delayed message lets the next one through. Lines the
client adds itself and validation errors are not told. Client-side.

Chunk `chunk` (`[x, z]`, in chunks) of `dimension` came into this
client's level from the server (NeoForge's `ChunkEvent.Load` on the
client, whose `isNewChunk` is always false there): once per chunk
packet the client adopts, after the column and its block entities are
in the level, so a listener reads its blocks through `ClientHost`. A
column the server sends again while it is resident is told again.
Only on a client of a server, a LAN guest included; an integrated
world's own chunks have the server's `chunk_load`. Client-side.

Chunk `chunk` (`[x, z]`, in chunks) of `dimension` is leaving this
client's level (NeoForge's `ChunkEvent.Unload` on the client): once
per resident column, with its blocks still there, just before they are
freed. Told on every route a column leaves by: the server's forget
packet, the view centre moving away, the view radius shrinking, and
the client level going (a dimension change, a respawn into another
level, leaving the server). That is wider than NeoForge, which tells
only the forget packet, so a listener never keeps state for a column
that is gone. Only on a client of a server, a LAN guest included; an
integrated world's own chunks have the server's `chunk_unload`.
Client-side.
Before an actual connection is discarded, not on a dimension change.

NeoForge's `ClientInformationUpdatedEvent`: a server player's client sent new
client information (language, view distance, chat, skin parts, main hand,
filtering, listing, particles) in play. `old` and `new` are the values before and
after this packet, one call per packet; they can be equal. The join's own
information is reported too, once, just before `player_logged_in`, with
`old` the defaults (`ClientInformation.createDefault`) and `new` what the
client joined with, as NeoForge fires it when `ServerPlayer` first sets
it. The player is not swapped in. Server-side.

The client made a new level for `dimension` (NeoForge's
`LevelEvent.Load` from the `ClientLevel` constructor): on joining a
server, single player's own included, and on changing dimension.
Its chunks come after. When the dimension changes, the old level's
`client_level_unload` follows this, as `Minecraft.setLevel`
tells it after the new level is made. Client-side, on the window; the
server's levels have `level_load`.

The client dropped its level for `dimension` (`LevelEvent.Unload`
from `Minecraft.setLevel` and `disconnect`): replaced by another
dimension's, or on leaving the server. Once for each
`client_level_load`. Not told when the game itself quits.
Client-side.

Veto a predicted client dig after the interaction mapping and vanilla eligibility checks.
Auto-tool and mining overlay mods can use this instead of a mining prediction mixin.
The snapshot is read-only. A veto skips the new mining operation and preserves any
retained dig. Release and correction still perform ordinary cleanup.

A play packet from the server reached the window's game, decoded,
just before the game handles it (`Connection.genericsFtw` handing it
to `ClientPacketListener`): every packet of the play phase, custom
payloads included, in the order the server sent them. Packets the
network thread handles itself are not heard: keep-alives, bundle
delimiters, resource pack pushes and pops, cookies, server links,
transfers, disconnects, the configuration switch, `minecraft:brand`
and far terrain tiles; neither is the configuration phase.
Read-only: the game handles the packet as it would without the mod.
Client-side, on any server, single player's own included.
Every packet exposes its protocol type id. Custom payloads also expose
their channel and raw bytes; no other decoded fields cross the API.

neoforge: none (NeoForge has no raw play-packet receive event)

hooks.doc:
A play packet the window's game is about to send to the server (`Connection.send`):
every packet of the play phase it sends, in the order it sends them, the selected slot
that goes out before an attack or a use included. Not heard: what the network thread
sends itself (keep-alives, configuration pongs, cookies, the configuration phase), the answers the
connection sends in whichever phase it is in (a resource pack's status, a dialog's custom
click action), and far terrain requests. Cancel drops the packet: the game goes on as if
it had been sent, so the server never hears of it. Client-side, on any server, single
player's own included. Every packet exposes its protocol type id; custom payloads also
expose their channel and raw bytes, as `client_packet` does for the packets that arrive.
Play-phase pongs pass through this hook; return `Flow::Cancel` to drop a packet.
Beyond NeoForge: there is no counterpart. Diverges from upstream: new hook.

neoforge: none (NeoForge has no raw play-packet send event)

hooks.doc: NeoForge's `ClientPauseChangeEvent.Post`: the pause state changed.
NeoForge's `ClientPauseChangeEvent.Pre`: cancel a proposed pause change.
NeoForge's `ClientPlayerChangeGameTypeEvent`: observe the local player info game type change.

After the client replaces its player on respawn or dimension change
(NeoForge's `ClientPlayerNetworkEvent.Clone`). Client-side.

The client accepted a play login and initialized its level and player
identity (NeoForge's `ClientPlayerNetworkEvent.LoggingIn`). `player_id`
is the server's entity ID. Client-side,
once per connection, including single player.

Before client disconnect teardown (NeoForge's
`ClientPlayerNetworkEvent.LoggingOut`). The player may be absent.
Client-side.

Render-thread notification after a resource-pack reload has applied successfully.
Atlas, models, renderer and client caches already refer to the new resources.
Selection/F3+T and server-pack reloads share this point; initial startup does not
(`client_setup` is the once-only moment after the initial load). Runs in
Reloading: published asset/data queries may refresh caches, but world
handles and transactions remain unavailable.

NeoForge's `FMLClientSetupEvent`: the client has started. It fires once per game
process, on the render thread, after the first client load has applied (the
atlas, models and every client reload listener's published state are final)
and before the title screen's first frame. Returning to the title screen and
opening another world, or adding a splitscreen player, is not a new start, so
it never fires again. This is
the opposite of `client_resources_reloaded`, which never runs at initial
startup and runs after every later reload. The listener runs on the main thread;
work a mod wants done in parallel is its own. The dedicated server has no client and never fires it
(see `server_about_to_start` for its `FMLDedicatedServerSetupEvent`). A
Setup permits client resource reads, not world handles or transactions.
The listener is a pure function of its `ClientHost` reads and its own state.

The client has finished shutting down, after `client_stopping`. Fires once
on the render thread for an orderly client exit, not for a dedicated server
or a splitscreen guest. NeoForge's `ClientStoppedEvent`.

The client is closing: it fires once per game process, on the render thread,
when the game shuts down, after the world the player was in is left and
saved, while the game still holds its settings and resources, so a listener
can read them through the `ClientHost` and save its own client state. It is the closing counterpart of `client_setup`.
Closing the window, a quit shortcut and the process's stop signals all reach
it; a crash does not. A dedicated server has no client and never fires it
(`server_stopping` is its stop), and neither does a splitscreen guest's game, as
`client_setup` skips it. Fabric's `ClientLifecycleEvents.CLIENT_STOPPING`
fires earlier, before the integrated server stops, so it is not a counterpart.
NeoForge has no event for this moment. A listener is a pure function of its
`ClientHost` reads and its own state.

Once every client tick, paused or not and on the title screen too, after the window's tick ran (NeoForge's
`ClientTickEvent.Post`): the window's `Game` only, so not on a server's
own tick (`server_tick` is that moment). Client-side.

Once every client tick, paused or not and on the title screen too, before the window's tick runs (NeoForge's
`ClientTickEvent.Pre`): the window's `Game` only, so not on a server's
own tick (`server_tick` is that moment). Client-side.

`BlockBehaviour.getCloneItemStack`, asked by
`ServerGamePacketListenerImpl.handlePickItemFromBlock`. `include_data`
is true for a creative player picking with Ctrl. Leave `stack` unset to
keep the game's item. Creative breaking, such as a beehive's
`playerWillDestroy`, does not ask this query. Server-side.

A command the local player typed or clicked in chat, without its
slash, before the server and Horizon's commands see it: set `ran`
when the mod ran it. Client-side: a server never asks, not for
command blocks, guests or the console.

neoforge: none (ClientChatEvent is for chat messages; client commands are added by RegisterClientCommandsEvent)

hooks.doc:
`GuiGraphicsExtractor.componentHoverEffect`: the hover of the text component under the
cursor, about to be drawn, in the chat, a book or a dialog. `hover` is the component's
