hover action: its text, an item or an entity. `x` and `y` are the cursor in GUI pixels.
Set `cancel` and the game draws nothing for it: no text tooltip, no item tooltip and no
entity lines. A mod can draw its own with `draw`. Left alone, a text hover is wrapped at
half the screen's width (at least 200) as vanilla wraps it, an item hover draws its stack's
tooltip (which asks `item_tooltip` and the `render_tooltip_*` hooks as any item tooltip
does), and an entity hover shows its name, type and UUID while advanced tooltips are on.
Asked each frame a hovered component shows, only while a mod listens. Client-side.
Register namespaced NBT component types before content loads.
A player added a compostable item to the composter at `pos`.

Computed world fog RGB, after ordinary effects and before upload. Title panoramas skip it.
Only finite RGB components in 0..=1 are accepted; alpha and distances stay unchanged.

World field of view, after normal calculation and zoom and before projection/Nausea.
Called for world rendering and near-plane overlays; hand/HUD FOV uses its own path.
Only finite values in 1..=179 degrees replace the computed FOV.

Player FOV scale, once per client tick with a player, after vanilla
effects and before zoom and easing.
Invalid values or values outside 0.01..=10 revert to base.

A registered config was read (`ModConfigEvent.Loading`): `config`
says whose, which file and its text, which the mod parses (TOML by
convention). Every mod hears every config, so check `mod_id`. Fired
where the config's kind loads (`register_configs`), a `Server`
one before `server_about_to_start`. Config allows settings reads
and the scoped ConfigFiles service, not world handles or transactions. Client and Common load once on their
owning side, Server once per world.

A loaded config's file changed on disk (`ModConfigEvent.Reloading`):
its new text. The game looks at the files' modification times once a
second, on the window and on the server's tick; a file saved with the
same text, removed or unreadable fires nothing and keeps its last
text. Polling does not change the current phase.

A `Server` config is dropped as its server stops
(`ModConfigEvent.Unloading`), after `server_stopping`; the next
world reads it again. `Client` and `Common` configs stay until the
game quits. This notification leaves the World phase unchanged.

Whether a fence, wall, or iron bars or pane of yours connects a side:
set `connected` to say whether the block `state` at `pos` connects toward
`neighbour`, the state beside it, `direction` pointing from the block to
that neighbour and `face_solid` whether the neighbour's face toward the
block is sturdy. `kind` names vanilla's rule, and `connected` holds its
answer: `ConnectionKind::Fence` is `FenceBlock.connectsTo` (a solid face, a
fence of the same kind or a gate across the arm), `Wall` is
`WallBlock.connectsTo` (a wall, a solid face, iron bars or a pane, or a
gate across the side; a connected side is still low or tall from the
block above) and `Bars` is `IronBarsBlock.attachsTo` for iron bars and
glass panes (a solid face, bars or a pane, or a wall; vanilla's rule
ignores `direction`). Change it, to false as well as to true, when the
block is your own. The neighbour's part answers first, in
`can_be_connected_to`, and `connected` starts from its answer: this
hook has the last word. Asked whenever the block settles its shape
toward a side or is placed, inside the level's update: answer from the
arguments without touching the world. Only the block's own part is asked, so
vanilla blocks cost nothing. Authoritative servers only. Contract version
`2`: version `1` was `fence_connects_to`, for fences alone and without
`kind`. Diverges from upstream: new hook.

A line the server logged (what its console prints and
`logs/latest.log` keeps): `level` is `INFO`, `WARN` or `ERROR`,
`thread` the thread it names (`Server thread`), `message` the line
without its time and thread. Heard at the start of the next server
tick, in the order logged; the lines logged before the first tick a mod
listens are not heard, and nor are the lines a `console_line`
listener logs itself. At most 4096 lines wait between two ticks; the
oldest are dropped with no notice. A `message` is cut to its first
8192 bytes and a `thread` to its first 128, at a character boundary.
Server-side.

neoforge: none (NeoForge has no log event; mods add a Log4j appender)

hooks.doc:
A consumable's effect of a mod's own kind: the item's `on_consume_effects`
entry is of a type in a namespace of its own, and the loader kept it
for this call. The kind and the definition payload as a borrowed `Tag` are here; the acting
player is the one consuming, and the game's own effects,
sounds, teleports and drops are open. An unclaimed kind does
nothing. This is the runtime `ConsumeEffect.apply` moment, not effect
type registration through NeoForge's `RegisterEvent`.

neoforge: none (runtime ConsumeEffect.apply; RegisterEvent registers effect types, not invocations)

hooks.doc:
The fluid a stack of a mod's own container item holds, as its
`neoforge:fluid_container` item model draws it
(`FluidUtil.getFirstStackContained`): `fluid` arrives `None` (holds
none); set it to the fluid's key, taken once at registration with
`r.fluid_key`. Asked on the client each time a stack of an item outside
`minecraft:` is drawn through a fluid container model; vanilla's items
keep their own answer and never ask. A fluid with no look in an item
draws the missing texture; a key no fluid is registered under draws the
stack as holding none, and the game logs it once per item.
Answer from the stack alone, and fast.

neoforge: none (FluidUtil.getFirstStackContained over Capabilities.Fluid.ITEM, read by DynamicFluidContainerModel; Horizon's ITEM_FLUIDS needs a server place, so the client model asks the item)

hooks.doc:
Horizon addition: no NeoForge counterpart. Fired once per container fill,
each half of a double chest separately, on the rolled list in roll order
before shuffle, splitting and slot placement. Add, replace or remove drops;
empty stacks are dropped. Stacks over their item's maximum are trimmed at
placement, after the hook; overflow that cannot fit is discarded.
The opener is named only when a player's open starts the fill, otherwise
None (hopper, comparator, break, explosion or command). The origin is the
block's centre or the container entity's position. Already filled containers
and block or mob drops do not fire this hook. Listeners run in dispatch
order, each seeing the previous list, after loot_table_load's changes.
The level Host provides reads only; only the drop list is writable.
Invalid component writes retain the prior list and warn. Panics follow the
runtime listener isolation policy. Listeners use their own randomness.
With no listener, the roll and placement random draws remain unchanged.

A player opens one of the game's own menus (`ServerPlayer.openMenu`; the
job of NeoForge's `PlayerContainerEvent.Open`, which comes after the
menu is open and cannot stop it): `kind` is the menu type
(`minecraft:generic_9x3`, `minecraft:furnace`, `minecraft:crafting`,
`minecraft:merchant`, `minecraft:anvil`, `minecraft:lectern`...; a
horse's inventory is `minecraft:horse_inventory`) and `pos` the block
it belongs to, none for a villager, a mount or a vehicle's chest.
Heard after the checks that refuse the menu (a locked container, a
spectator) and before the menu that was open closes. Set `cancel` and
nothing opens: the open menu stays as it was and the click is spent.
The player's state is swapped in for the call, as for
`run_mod_command`, so `host.players().acting_player()`, `PlayerRef::tell` and
the item helpers reach them. Not heard: a menu a mod opens
(`native_open_menu`), the inventory screen, and the editors (sign,
book, command block). Server-side, for every player of the world.

neoforge: none (not NeoForge's PlayerContainerEvent.Open: this hook can cancel the opening)

hooks.doc: A server-only, non-cancellable backing-block notice at Container.setChanged / BlockEntity.setChanged, after the write and before dirty/comparator updates. Game-held vanilla container transactions coalesce implicit notices at root commit. Explicit mod-issued set_changed notifies immediately, even for equal contents and inside a transaction; the notice survives abort. Raw mod-owned storage writes and restores synthesize no notice. Nested writes to the backing block whose notice is active still apply but do not re-enter its notice; another block notifies normally. Double containers notify each backing component, not the other half merely refreshed for comparators. Vehicle/menu placeholder coordinates are excluded. Replaces the Create port positional contents_changed mixin for depot, package and schematic storage; there is no matching NeoForge bus event.
A crafter at `pos` completed recipe `recipe`.

NeoForge's `IItemExtension.getCraftingRemainder(ItemStack)`: what `stack`
leaves when consumed by crafting, furnace fuel or brewing. `remainder` arrives
holding the item's data remainder. Replace it, or set it to `None` to
leave nothing. A part that leaves it alone preserves the data remainder.
Recipe-specific book and banner copies are handled by the recipe.
Asked for each consumption on the authoritative server, with a read-only
`Host`. Oversized counts, unknown items and invalid damage are refused by
the stack boundary, retaining the original data remainder. API stacks
cannot have count zero; use `None` to leave nothing. Native panics follow
the normal Part crash path, attributed to the owning mod and Part.

A fluid source at `pos` (`state`) is about to count towards turning
the flowing fluid beside it into a source (NeoForge's
`CreateFluidSourceEvent`, `FlowingFluid.getNewLiquid`): two counted
sources beside a block over a solid block or a source make it one.
Asked for each horizontal neighbour source, whenever the game works
out a block's new fluid, spread checks included: answer fast.
`can_convert` starts as the fluid's rule (`water_source_conversion`
or `lava_source_conversion`). Server-side.

Skull models for a mod's own skull types (NeoForge's
`EntityRenderersEvent.CreateSkullModels`): push a `SkullModel` per type, its `kind`, the
model layer it is baked from and its default texture. A `minecraft:head` item model may
then name the kind, so the head draws in hand, in a GUI and in an item frame. Asked
once at start, on the client. A kind in vanilla's namespace, not `<namespace>:<path>`,
registered already, with a layer neither a mod nor vanilla has, or with an empty texture
is logged and left out. API @API:create_skull_models@.

Before a new server level selects its initial world spawn
(NeoForge's `LevelEvent.CreateSpawnPosition`).

A creative-mode player sets a slot of their inventory from the
creative screen (`ServerGamePacketListenerImpl.handleSetCreativeModeSlot`):
`slot` is the inventory menu's slot (5 to 8 armour, 9 to 35 the
inventory, 36 to 44 the hotbar, 45 the off hand; below 0 is a stack
thrown out of the screen, which is dropped) and `item` (`minecraft:air`
for an emptied slot) and `count` what is put there. Heard once the
packet passed vanilla's checks (a creative player, a real slot, a valid
stack) and before the slot changes or the stack drops. Set `cancel`
and the packet is ignored. The player's state is swapped in for the
call, as for `run_mod_command`, so `host.players().acting_player()`,
`PlayerRef::tell` and the item helpers reach them. Not heard: stacks a
creative player gets other ways (middle-click pick block, `/give`).
Server-side, for every player of the world.

neoforge: none (vanilla ServerGamePacketListenerImpl.handleSetCreativeModeSlot; NeoForge adds no event or extension for it)

hooks.doc:
`IItemExtension.getCreatorModId`: the mod that made `stack`, which a
recipe viewer or tooltip names, instead of the mod that registered its
item. `mod_id` arrives as the item id's namespace; set it to another
mod (a universal bucket holding that mod's fluid, a facade of its
block) or `None` for no mod. Asked by `ItemResource::creator_mod_id`,
from client tooltips and viewers as well as the server: answer from
the stack alone. Only the `ItemPart`s attached to `stack`'s item are
asked: an item with none costs one table lookup.
A player ignited a creeper with an item.
Lightning charged a creeper.

NeoForge's `CriticalHitEvent`: a player's melee hit on a living
`target_kind` (`minecraft:zombie`, `minecraft:armor_stand`) that deals
damage, where `Player.attack` decides whether it is critical.
`vanilla_critical` is vanilla's answer; `critical` starts as it and may
be forced or denied (as in vanilla a critical hit prevents the sweep, so
a forced crit loses it; a denied crit loses the crit sound and
particles); `damage_multiplier` starts at 1.5 for vanilla's critical and
1.0 otherwise, and scales the damage only while `critical` ends true. Not fired for a
target that is no living entity (a dragon part) or when the hit does
no damage. Fires on the Game that runs the attack.

A crop-like block grew (NeoForge's `CropGrowEvent.Post`).
`original_state` is the block before it grew and `state` what is at
`pos` now. Sugar cane reports the new cane above it, and kelp and
vines the new head, as both states. Server-side.

A crop-like block at `pos` is about to grow on a random tick
(NeoForge's `CropGrowEvent.Pre`): crops, stems, nether wart, cocoa,
sweet berries and bamboo at their own position; cactus and chorus
flowers at the block above; sugar cane at its own position; kelp,
weeping and twisting vines and cave vines at the block they grow
into. `state` is the growing block. Leave `result` at `Default` for
vanilla's own chance, or set `True` to grow now or `False` to stop
it (`DO_NOT_GROW`). Vanilla's random roll is drawn either way, in
vanilla's order. Server-side.

NeoForge's `CustomClickActionEvent`: a server player's client sent a `custom`
click action (a dialog button or a text component's click event): its id and
optional payload. Vanilla only logs it; set `cancel` to skip that. Only play-phase
clicks are reported: one sent during configuration (no player yet) is not. The
player is not swapped in. Server-side.

`CustomSpawner.tick` for a spawner a mod added with `modify_custom_spawners`: the level
`dimension` ticks the spawner `key`, once per tick in the list's order, with
`spawn_enemies` as `ServerLevel.isSpawningMonsters` (the `spawn_monsters` rule, and not
peaceful). Every mod gets the call, and the mod that owns `key` spawns through `host`
(its spawns go through `finalize_spawn` and the spawn checks like any other); the rest
ignore it. It is called only while the `spawn_mobs` rule is on, as vanilla's custom
spawners are, and only for a key in the list, so a level with no mod spawner pays one
check per tick. Beyond NeoForge: a key and this hook stand in for the `CustomSpawner`
object. Server-side.

One boss bar is about to be drawn (NeoForge's `CustomizeGuiOverlayEvent.BossEventProgress`,
in `BossHealthOverlay`): `bar` is the bar, `x` and `y` come in as its top-left corner in GUI
pixels (91 left of the screen's centre; 12 for the first bar), and `increment` as the
spacing to the next bar's `y` (19). Move `x` and `y` to draw this bar, and its title, there;
set `increment` to space the next bar, which comes in that far below where this one came in
(moving `y` does not move the bars after it). Set `cancel` and this bar is not drawn; the
increment is still applied, leaving room for what a mod draws in its place. Asked once a
frame per bar, in the order the server added them, until the next bar would start a third
of the way down the screen; not under F1. Client-side.

The in-game chat is about to be drawn (NeoForge's `CustomizeGuiOverlayEvent.Chat`, in
`Gui.renderChat`): `x` and `y` come in as the chat's bottom-left corner in GUI pixels
(0 and the GUI height minus 40, vanilla's place); move them to draw the chat elsewhere.
`focused` is whether the chat screen is open, and `gui_width`/`gui_height` the scaled GUI
size. Asked once a frame the chat layer draws, focused or not; not while the chat is
hidden (F1 with the chat closed). Only the drawing moves: the chat screen's input box, and
clicks and hovers on messages, stay where vanilla puts them, as with NeoForge.
Client-side.

`IItemExtension.damageItem`: the wear `stack` is about to take
(`ItemStack.hurtAndBreak`: a tool that mines or hits, armour that takes
a hit, a shield, a rod, an elytra, a tool a dispenser uses, a mob's
armour), after Unbreaking has had its say, as NeoForge passes it.
`entity` is who wears or uses it: the acting player on a player's
paths, the mob, armour stand or dragon wearing it, `None` for a
dispenser's tool. `amount` is the points about to be lost; change it
(0 or less leaves the item whole) or set `canceled` for no wear at
all. Set `break_now` and the item breaks whatever durability it has
left, through the vanilla break (the sound and particles, the stack
emptied, `player_destroy_item` for a player): NeoForge's `onBroken`.
It wins over `canceled`. Not asked when
Unbreaking already saved the item, nor for a creative player's tools
(they take no wear). Only the `ItemPart`s attached to `stack`'s item
hear it: an item with none costs one table lookup, and a game with no
such part none at all. On the paths of a player the player's state is
swapped in, so `host.players().acting_player()` answers them. Once for
each wear, on a server.

The server is assembling its data tables, as for
`data_pack_files` (a world's first open and every `/reload`):
push the data map types your mod registers (NeoForge's
`RegisterDataMapTypesEvent`). A type is an `id` (`mod_id:name`, not in
`minecraft`) for a `registry`: any the game names. Its values come
from the world's data packs'
`data/<mod_id>/data_maps/<registry folder>/<name>.json` (the registry's
path for a `minecraft` registry, `<namespace>/<path>` otherwise), and
from files you push through `native_data_pack_files` under the key
`data_maps/<mod_id>:<registry folder>/<name>`: `replace`, `values`
(entry ids and `#tags` to JSON values, each optionally guarded by its
own `neoforge:conditions`) and `remove`, a newer value overriding an
older. Push a typed map's `DataMap::ty` and read its values with the
key's `data` (`ItemKey::data`, `EntityTypeKey::data`...), or by name
with `data_map_value` and `data_map_entries`. Server-side, not synced
to clients.

The data maps of a registry were reloaded on the server or synced to the
client (NeoForge's `DataMapsUpdatedEvent`): the place to build caches
from the new values or post-process them. `registry` is the registry's id
(`minecraft:item`, `minecraft:block`) and `cause` says how they arrived.
A listener cannot cancel or change anything.

`ServerReload`: the server merged the values of the types mods registered
(`data_map_types`) from the world's data packs and mods' files.
Fires once for each registry that has a type, right after
`tags_updated`'s `ServerDataLoad` (tags are bound), on a world's first open
and after every `/reload`. `ItemKey::data` and `BlockKey::data` read the
new values.

`ClientSync`: data maps are server-side and not synced to clients, so
this cause does not fire; it comes with the sync.

Runs in Reloading: published asset/data queries can rebind caches,
including on first open; world handles and transactions remain
unavailable.

The server is assembling its data tables from the world's data packs
(`ReloadableServerResources`): a world is opening, or `/reload` was
run, and the recipes, tags, loot and advancements are built after
this. Push `(path, bytes)` pack files and they join this load. `path`
is the overlay's key, `<kind>/<namespace>:<path>` without `.json`, over
the kinds the tables read: `recipe/mymod:thing`,
`tags/mymod:block/thing`, `loot_table/…`, `advancement/…`,
`trade_set/…`, `villager_trade/…`, `dialog/…`. A file that isn't JSON
is skipped with a warning. Asked once per load on both paths, so this
is where a mod recomputes them.
Contributed files sit below the world's own data packs: a pack's file
for the same path still overrides a mod's. Server-side (the single
player's integrated server included). Listener applies run first. A later reload refusal
preserves the old engine generation, but does not undo callback effects. Contributions
share one list, so a failed file cannot be attributed to a particular mod.

Collect recipe types once the joining player exists, after admission
and before that player's recipes are sent. On reload,
asked once per online player, at most once per player per reload,
before their recipes are re-sent. With nobody online this
hook is not asked. `player` always identifies the recipient.
Configuration tags precede admission. Only this player's Horizon
client receives the selected recipes; vanilla clients receive nothing
new. An empty answer retains the client's own recipes, or restores
them after an earlier nonempty answer.

The lines of one enabled F3 debug entry a mod registered (`register_debug_entries`), asked each
frame the overlay draws it. `id` is the entry's id; push its lines to `lines`, legacy colour
codes (§) work. A disabled entry is never asked. Client-side.

Draw one active debug renderer (`register_debug_renderers`), asked for each view of a world,
after `submit_custom_geometry`. `id` is the renderer's id and every mod is asked about every id,
so a mod ignores ids it does not own. `draw` shares its limits with that hook and clears every
view, so nothing outlives a frame. A renderer that is not active is never asked, and neither is
one without a world to draw in. Client-side.

Items' default components are bound and readable (NeoForge's
`DefaultDataComponentsBoundEvent`); `cause` says how, as `tags_updated`'s does. The
place to build or rebuild caches derived from item defaults (stack sizes, food,
tool rules): from now on the default-component reads return the published
defaults, `modify_default_components`' edits included.

`ServerDataLoad`: on the server once its data tables are built, on a world's first
open and after `/reload`. `ClientPacketReceived`: on a client once it applied the
tags its server sent, at login and for each update in play. Each fires right before
`tags_updated` with the same cause; `cause.should_update_static_data()` is false
for an integrated server's client, so data the two threads share is updated once.

Runs in Reloading: published asset/data queries can rebind caches; world handles
and transactions remain unavailable.

The server's difficulty changed, from `from` to `to` (`peaceful`,
`easy`, `normal`, `hard`; NeoForge's `DifficultyChangeEvent`). It is
vanilla's `MinecraftServer.setDifficulty`, which `/difficulty`, a
dedicated server's management and a test environment's difficulty all
go through, and it is told only when the difficulty is another one. It
only hears: the change has already happened. Server-side.

Draw the complete selected loading screen with its GUI drawing context. `screen` is the
id registered at startup; ignore ids you do not own. `progress` is the integrated server's
smoothed progress, or None without server progress. The game's existing tracker closes
this screen when ready; drawing cannot change readiness or the timeout. Client only.

`DispenserBlock.getDispenseMethod`: choose a behaviour for any item,
including vanilla items, on the authoritative server (not droppers).
The block the dispenser faces is asked first (`dispense_method`), and
its answer keeps this part from being asked. Leave answer None for
vanilla. Otherwise answer `(remainder, event)`:
a remainder of None empties the slot, `Some(stack)` replaces it (the hook
owns consumption: no extra item is removed afterwards). `event` is the
level event the dispenser plays with its smoke: 1000 the click, 1001 the
fail sound (`OptionalDispenseItemBehavior` without success), or 0 for
nothing at all (`DispenseItemBehavior.NOOP`). To drop one normally,
answer `(native_dispense_default(..), 1000)`.

neoforge: none (vanilla DispenserBlock.getDispenseMethod; NeoForge adds no event or extension for it)

hooks.doc:
`DispenserBlock.getDispenseMethod`, before the item's `dispense_item`:
the block the dispenser faces chooses what the dispense does, for any
item, including vanilla items, on the authoritative server (not
droppers). `state` is the block at `pos` moved by `facing` (air
included), and the part is asked only for that block. An answer wins:
no item part is asked and vanilla's behaviour
doesn't run. The answer is `dispense_item`'s: a remainder of None
empties the slot, `Some(stack)` replaces it (the hook owns
consumption: no extra item is removed afterwards), and `event` is the
level event played with the smoke: 1000 the click, 1001 the fail sound,
or 0 for nothing at all. Leave answer None and `dispense_item` decides,
as it did before.

neoforge: none (vanilla DispenserBlock.getDispenseMethod; NeoForge adds no event or extension for it)

hooks.doc:
A dispenser at `pos` in `dimension`, facing `facing`, is about to act on
`stack` (`DispenserBlock.getDispenseMethod`), once per dispenser action
on the authoritative server (not droppers). It runs before the faced
block's `dispense_method` and the item's `dispense_item`, so a mod that
cannot list every item or block at registration answers here for all of
them, vanilla ones included. A mod's answer wins: neither part is asked
and vanilla's behaviour doesn't run. The answer is `dispense_item`'s:
a remainder of None empties the slot, `Some(stack)` replaces it (the
hook owns consumption: no extra item is removed afterwards), and `event`
is the level event played with the smoke: 1000 the click, 1001 the fail
sound, or 0 for nothing at all. Leave answer None and the faced block's
and the item's parts decide, as they did before.

neoforge: none (vanilla DispenserBlock.getDispenseMethod; NeoForge adds no event or extension for it)

hooks.doc:
The Ender Dragon fight is about to place its first dragon egg at `pos`.
Set `cancel` to leave the block unchanged. Server-side.

The Ender Dragon fight is won (`EnderDragonFight.setDragonKilled`), on every win, not
only the first. `pos` is where its dragon egg forms, `won_before` whether the fight was
won before, and `forms` whether an egg forms unless a mod answers: vanilla's, on the
first win only, after `dragon_egg_form`. Return `Some(true)` to place an egg there on
this win, `Some(false)` to leave the block, `None` to keep `forms`. Server-side.

NeoForge's `EffectParticleModificationEvent`, vanilla's `LivingEntity.updateSynchronizedMobEffectParticles`: asked for each active effect `effect` of the living entity `entity` (a [`LivingRef`], a mob or a player), the ones vanilla hides included, as the server is about to send their swirls in its synched data (`DATA_EFFECT_PARTICLES`, `DATA_EFFECT_AMBIENCE_ID`). `original_particle` is vanilla's for the effect: an `entity_effect` in its colour (alpha 38 of 255 when ambient), the omens' own particles. `particle` starts as it: replace it, or set it to `None` to go back to the original. `visible` starts as the effect's own: set it to show a hidden effect's swirl or hide a visible one. The visible effects' particles are sent in the order the effects are kept; particles that need a block state, and item, trail and vibration particles, can't be sent and are left out. A mod's own particle (`ParticleOptions::simple` with its registered `ParticleKey`) goes only to Horizon clients: the others get the list without it. Whether the swirls are ambient (drawn fainter and rarer) follows from the answers as vanilla's `areAllEffectsAmbient` does: a visible effect that is not ambient makes it false, an effect a mod made visible counts as visible and one it hid doesn't, and it is true when none is visible. Asked when the entity's effects change (one is added, removed, or changes its amplifier, visibility or ambience), as vanilla recomputes them only then, and only while a mod listens; the answers are sent until the next change. The window's own player draws its swirls from its own effects, not from these answers. Server-side.

At most 32 pairs of already-loaded base and transparent overlay sprites.
Per-pixel alpha in the overlay marks full-bright material, without
illuminating the surrounding block or changing gameplay light.

`IDispensibleContainerItemExtension.emptyContents`: `stack` (a bucket
of a mod fluid, a jar, a canister) is about to be emptied at `pos`, by
`player` (the acting player) who clicked `hit` (the block and face),
or by a dispenser (`player` and `hit` are `None`). Leave
`answer` `None` for vanilla's emptying. Answer `Some(true)` when the
part placed the contents itself through the host: the stack becomes
an empty `minecraft:bucket` (a creative player keeps it), no vanilla
sound plays and the use counts as a success. Answer `Some(false)` for
a failure: nothing is placed, a player keeps the full stack and a
dispenser drops it, as vanilla's does when emptying fails. Asked for
a player once `bucket_empty` let the pour go on, and for a dispenser
before its own placement; an item with this part reaches the
dispenser's bucket behaviour even when it is no bucket of a mod
fluid, and a `dispense_item` answer still comes first. A server's
client does not predict the pour of an item with this part. The part
is asked in a transaction with the game's apply: a part that changes
the player's hand or the dispenser's slots while answering
`Some(true)` is refused and its journaled writes are undone, as a failed
use (the player keeps the stack, the dispenser fails). A player's
successful pour counts for the `placed_block` criterion. Only the
`ItemPart`s attached to `stack`'s item are asked. Server-side.

A `minecraft:post_attack` effect of a mod's own kind, on a mob a
player's weapon hit: the entry says `enchanted` attacker and `affected`
victim, its `requirements` passed, and its `effect` names a `type` in a
namespace outside `minecraft:`. Told the enchantment id, the kind, the
`effect` payload as a borrowed `Tag`, the level and the mob's id (it may have just died). The
acting player is the one whose weapon carries the enchantment. Each
such entry is told once a hit, and once for each mob a sweep lands on.
A hit on a player, and an entry inside `minecraft:all_of`, aren't told
yet. An unclaimed kind does nothing.
A server player applied an enchantment at `pos`; `item` is the finished item and `levels` the levels charged. The player's state is not swapped in.

The enchanting power the block `state` at `pos` gives the enchanting table at
`table_pos` (`IBlockExtension.getEnchantPowerBonus`), asked for each of the table's
bookshelf offsets (`EnchantingTableBlock.BOOKSHELF_OFFSETS`) whose block between it and the
table is in `#minecraft:enchantment_power_transmitter`. `power` starts at the block's own
answer, 1.0 in `#minecraft:enchantment_power_provider` and 0.0 for the rest: set 2.0 to
count as two bookshelves, 0.5 for half of one, 0.0 to give nothing. The table adds the
answers, truncates the sum to a whole number as NeoForge does and caps it at 15 for the
offers; a negative sum counts as 0, where NeoForge would throw, and a non-finite answer is
ignored. Asked as the offers are made, in a single-player world and on a LAN host for each
guest's table, with the level read-only. Client particles use the same answer, queried once
per state at world entry, parts reload and received-server-tag publication, with `pos`
and `table_pos` both at the origin. Server tags and their tag-update listeners are
published before the client snapshot. Any nonzero answer emits particles when the
intervening block transmits. Particle answers must be state-only; changing a mod's
answer requires a parts/tag reload.
No hook is called per tick or frame. With no part attached, the only dispatch cost is one
block subscription lookup before event conversion. Diverges from upstream: new hook.

NeoForge's `EnchantedBlockLootEvent`: a block's loot table is reading the level of `enchantment` on `tool` to decide what `state` at `pos` drops, in `ApplyBonusCount.run` or `BonusLevelTableCondition.test`. `level` starts as the tool's level, after `get_enchantment_level`; what is left in it is what that one count or condition uses, and the tool keeps its own. A `u32` can't be negative, the case `setEnchantmentLevel` refuses; one above 1024 counts as 1024, as vanilla's levels stop at 255 and a level sizes a formula's loop. `tool` is none for an empty hand or a break with no tool, and the read is still asked, at level 0. `entity` is `LootContextParams.THIS_ENTITY`: the player mining, the mob breaking the block, the blast's direct source (primed TNT, TNT cart, exploding mob, fireball, wither skull, end crystal), the enderman whose carried block drops, the source of `/loot ... mine`, the projectile that broke a chorus flower or a decorated pot, the villager harvesting, the ravager walking through a crop, or none for a break with no entity (a neighbour update, a piston, water, a trident through a speleothem). A boat through a lily pad also gives none, though vanilla names it. Asked once per read, so a table may ask several times per break, or not at all, and the table's draws stay in vanilla's order. It runs inside the roll, so it gets the read-only level host: no writes, no draws, and `entity` is a handle a listener can keep and compare but not read until it has a `Host`. Authoritative servers only. Use `get_enchantment_level` when the block doesn't matter. Tick-time effect: one `listened` test per roll when no mod listens.

An entity's loot table reads an enchantment's level (NeoForge's
`EnchantedEntityLootEvent`): asked in the middle of the roll, each
time an `enchanted_count_increase` function or a
`random_chance_with_enchanted_bonus` condition is evaluated, for a
death and for `/loot ... kill`. `entity` is the living entity dropping
the loot, `source` the killing blow (`minecraft:magic` for the command)
and `attacker` the attacking entity (`getAttacker`): the one that
caused the blow, or the command's source, even when `source` names
nobody. It is None without one, and it need not be living: such a read
is asked too, from a level of 0. `level` comes in as the living
attacker's level of `enchantment`; what a mod leaves in it is what the
table uses, so a level raised from 0 counts even with no attacker. A
level can't be negative, and one above 1024 counts as 1024: vanilla's
levels stop at 255, and a table's count grows with the level. Mods that don't need the entities prefer
`get_enchantment_level`; a mob's equipment drop chance isn't this
hook's (`get_equipment_drop_chance`). Not asked for a `/loot ... kill`
of an entity that isn't living, nor for a table rolled any other way.
The draws a mod makes from the level's random stay in order with the
roll's. Server-side.

An enchanting table at `pos` drew the level of one offer
(`EnchantmentMenu.slotsChanged`, after `getEnchantmentCost`): `offer`
holds the server player whose table it is, the row (0 to 2), the
power (bookshelves counted), the item and the level drawn. Change
`level` to change the offer; a level below `row + 1` offers nothing,
as vanilla's. Asked for each row in order, before
`prepare_item_enchant`. Server-side.

A guest opened an ender chest: the menu shows the guest's own inventory. Heard after
`container_opened` let the menu open, so a cancelled open is not heard. `player` is the
guest's UUID and `pos` the chest's block position. Server-side.

An enderman or a shulker is about to teleport on its own
(`EntityTeleportEvent.EnderEntity`). A mod may move `target` or cancel. It is given the loop `context` of the side that ticks the entity (its registries, settings and mod list); it fires inside the tick's own AI step, before the teleport's own random draws, so it takes no `Host`.

A server player's or mob's ender pearl is about to teleport its `owner`
(`EntityTeleportEvent.EnderPearl`, `ThrownEnderpearl.onHit`). `owner` is
the live entity handle, `pearl` its projectile id, `from` the owner's feet
and `target` the pearl's previous position. A mod may move the target;
non-finite changes keep the original spot. Canceling leaves the owner
in place with no teleport sound, damage or endermite roll; the pearl is
used up. Player owners keep their acting-player context and mutable fall
`damage` (5; nonpositive causes no health loss, but zero remains a hit
attempt that asks the invulnerability predicate). Mob owners take no fall damage and
make no endermite draw; their `damage` starts at zero and is player-only.
An owner moved, removed, killed or put to sleep by a listener is not moved
again using the old decision. The impact hook still hears the hit.
What the pearl hit (`getHitResult`), in `projectile_impact`'s shape:
the entity `hit_entity` (a dragon part is the dragon), or, with it
None, the block `hit_block` on its `hit_face` (the face's normal); `hit_at`
is the hit point. For an entity, `hit_block` is the cell of `hit_at`
and `hit_face` is `[0, 0, 0]`.

`player` stares at `enderman` (NeoForge's `EndermanAngerEvent`, at
the end of `Enderman.isBeingStaredBy`): the look is within the
enderman's cone, in line of sight, and no carved pumpkin hides the
face. Asked each time the enderman's goals check the stare: to get
angry, to freeze while looked at and to teleport away up close. Set
`cancel` and that stare doesn't count. Server-side.

Entities from `chunk` finished loading into the server world. `count`
is the number of saved entity records read.

Entities in `chunk` left the active server world and were queued for
saving. `count` is the number of entity records.
A mob broke the door at `pos`.

Two mobs completed a breeding action. `child` is absent when vanilla
lays an egg instead of creating a baby.
A mob changed a block at `pos`, after the new state was applied.

A mob or a player is about to change the block at `pos`: a landing's
trampling (farmland to dirt, a turtle egg breaking), before its
neighbour updates and events. `player` is the player whose landing it
was, `entity` and `kind` the mob for a mob's landing (`None` and the
player's type here). `from` and `to` are resolved block states. Set `cancel`
and the block stays as it was and nothing the change would have caused
happens, as Bukkit's `EntityChangeBlockEvent` (@API:entity_change_block_v2@).
The fork names this pre-change veto `entity_change_block_pre`; `entity_change_block` is the separate post-change notice.

neoforge: none (NeoForge has no such event; Bukkit's EntityChangeBlockEvent is cancellable)

hooks.doc:
A new entity is being made (NeoForge's `EntityEvent.EntityConstructing`, vanilla's
`Entity.<init>`): `kind` is its type (`minecraft:zombie`, `minecraft:player` for a
player) and `holder` holds its attachments. Set attachments here and the entity starts
with them: this runs before any mod reads them, and an entity read from disk or from a
summon's NBT reads its saved attachments over what you set. The entity may not be in
the level yet, so read nothing else of it. Nothing can be cancelled.

Told once per entity on each side that makes it, as vanilla's server and client each
construct their own: on the server (single player's included) for a spawned, summoned,
bred or loaded entity and for a guest's player when it joins and when it respawns; on
a client for each entity and player its server adds to its view, and for its own
player at login and at each respawn, a dimension change's included (vanilla makes a
new `LocalPlayer` there). A guest's file, or what its player keeps through a respawn,
is read over what you set. An entity whose chunk unloads and loads again is a new
entity, told again, as in vanilla. An entity changing dimension keeps its attachments
and is not told again, where vanilla constructs the copy it moves
(`Entity.teleportCrossDimension`, then `restoreFrom`).

A mob is about to drop `count` of `item` at `pos` (Bukkit's
`EntityDropItemEvent`).

neoforge: none (NeoForge has no such event; Bukkit's EntityDropItemEvent)

hooks.doc: A bee entered the hive at `pos` and was stored there.

A mob entered love mode after player interaction. `player` is the
feeder when known.

`entity` moved from the 16x16x16 section `old_section` into `new_section` (NeoForge's
`EntityEvent.EnteringSection`, vanilla's `EntitySectionStorage` callbacks on
`Entity.setPosRaw`). Both are section coordinates (`SectionPos`: each block coordinate
shifted right by 4), and `chunk_changed` is NeoForge's `didChunkChange`: the x or z
section differs, so the entity is in another chunk column. `host` is the side that saw
the move. Nothing can be cancelled: the entity is already in its new section.

Told on each side synchronously after the position write and section filing, once for
every section change, from the section the entity was in before that move: two moves told
apart are two events, and a move out and one back are two. The moves: an entity's own move in its tick (on the
server every kind in the level's lists, the fishing hooks and the dragon; on a client
each entity it shows, where its interpolation puts it), each move a server player sent,
a teleport (`/tp`, a mod's `teleport_to`), a piston or shulker push, and on a client
each packet that places an entity (its own player's teleport, a vehicle it drives). A
mob's teleport in its own tick (an enderman's, a pet's to its owner, a shulker's) is a
move of its own, before the walk that follows it, each one when it teleports twice; one
collision-resolved walk is one move. An entity joining a level, changing level, or a
player respawning starts in its section untold, as vanilla adds it to its section
without this event; one that moves before its first tick is told. A listener must defer
moving or removing the entity until the write completes, because the write is still in
progress while this hook runs.

Mob ticks dispatch synchronously in position-write order. During a borrowed mob pass,
the Host answers only this entity's position; other Host operations are refused.

An entity's block sweep crossed a block state this part is attached to (`Block.entityInside`), and the part is told mid-sweep, where vanilla runs the block's own `entityInside`. `event.precise` is `Entity.checkInsideBlocks`' flag: the entity moved nearly a block, or its box at the target touches the block. It runs inside the entity's move, on the level random host: it reads blocks and draws the level's random in vanilla's order, interleaved with the vanilla blocks the same walk visits; only writes are restricted to the event. `event.apply` queues one of the five `InsideBlockEffectType`s, `event.run_before`/`event.run_after` queue a typed entity write around one, and `event.request` asks for a level write that lands at the touched block once the entity's batch has ticked, if the block is still the state it touched — the same contract as a landing write, whose complete batch is checked before queuing and an invalid state refuses all writes and sibling outputs. The queued entity writes apply to the swept entity inside its own tick, in `StepBasedCollector` order, and stop when it dies; a `Hurt` whose source the entity table answers `Taken` for (its list is lifted that moment, ) is refused with a typed error, not a retry and not a panic. Fires for players, mobs, items and projectiles alike, each on the shared walk inside its own tick or batch.

neoforge: none (vanilla Block.entityInside; NeoForge adds no event or extension for it)

hooks.doc:
A player right-clicks, in the level `dimension` (a `&str`), the entity `entity` (`Entity.getId`) of type
`kind` (`minecraft:cow`) with `hand` (`Hand::Main` or `Hand::Off`), holding `stack` (none in an
empty hand): where `Player.interactOn` starts, before the entity's own
`interact` and the item's `interactLivingEntity`. Both logical sides
answer independently, once per hand, main hand before off hand.
A consuming client result ends the loop; only Success swings there.
SuccessServer and Consume consume without a client swing. Fail,
Pass and TryWithEmptyHand fall through on this entity path.
A server-only answer leaves the client's off-hand prediction unchanged.
ClientHost permits reads and local effects, not authoritative writes.

a right-click on an entity with the point clicked: `entity_interact_specific` hears the entity, its type, the held stack and the point clicked, measured from the entity's position, before `native_interact_entity` (NeoForge's `PlayerInteractEvent.EntityInteractSpecific` counterpart); a claim swings the hand and ends the click. Server-side. Bundles need "hooks": @API:entity_interact_specific@.

Decide whether an entity is invulnerable to this specific damage source
(`Entity.isInvulnerableTo`). `original_invulnerability` is the vanilla
answer and `invulnerable` starts with that value. Listeners may change it
before the hit is applied. This fires once per player or mob hit that enters the invulnerability
predicate, including creative/PvP, death, fire-resistance, shield and
cooldown refusals. Nested player predicates and equipment continuations
reuse the same base decision; a new attempt asks again. Ghast and warden
overrides are observed too, including reflected fireballs and digging.
No amount is supplied: vanilla's predicate takes a source, not an amount.
Amount mutation remains on `living_incoming_damage`, before cooldown.
Zero-damage projectile collisions and player pearl teleport damage still
ask before the zero-damage refusal. Skull impact and its explosion are
separate attempts. Fireworks directly hurt their attached entity; their
splash query excludes spectators, not dead or unloaded residents.

Vanilla paths that do not enter the predicate do not synthesize a call:
poison at one health, spectator or team-filtered explosion targets, and
a sulfur cube's body-immune override. Dragon part/phase/source refusals
before `reallyHurt` likewise do not reach the living predicate. Creative
explosion, damaging-effect and starvation attempts do reach it. Falling
blocks exclude creative, spectator and dead targets in their query;
evoker fangs exclude dead targets, and pufferfish contact excludes dead
or spectator players before the damage call.
Armor stand, item, vehicle, experience orb, end crystal, item frame and
painting damage paths also fire this hook. Explicit queries ask it too:
`EntityRef::invulnerable_to_damage` and a mod goal's
`invulnerable_to_damage`, each with the vanilla answer as the original.
The supplied level is the one where the hit occurs, read only. Asked on
both sides: on a client, where it predicts the mount it rides; the
level says which side it is. The answer must stay a pure function of
the event, as replayed ticks ask again.

An entity joins the server level `dimension` (NeoForge's
`EntityJoinLevelEvent`): vanilla's `PersistentEntitySectionManager.addEntity`.
`loaded_from_disk` is true for an entity coming back with its chunk,
false for one added fresh (`addFreshEntity`: a drop, an orb, `/summon`,
an arrival through a portal). `entity` is its ID and `kind` its type
(`minecraft:item`). It is already in the level's lists, so helpers that
take an entity ID find it. Set `canceled` to keep it out: it is taken
back out as if never added, and a `/summon` of it fails. Tells every
kind in the game's entity lists (items, orbs, mobs, boats, minecarts,
armor stands, primed TNT, falling blocks, projectiles, rockets,
tridents, end crystals, the dragon, cushions, paintings, item frames),
once each, in the order they were created; check `kind`. A drop, an
orb, a mob, a `/summon` and a chunk's entities are told at once, any
other spawn between the tick's phases (it is checked after the blocks,
the vehicles, the projectiles, the items and the mobs, and at the
tick's end). A mod that cancels one of the others sees it removed
before it ticks again. Inside a transaction (`Host::transaction`) opened
in the entity's own level the join is told at that transaction's root
commit, not at the spawn call (an entity spawned in another level, as by
a command run `in` it, is told at once): before the
commit the entity exists and `entity_constructing` has run, but no one
is told it joined, and a listener reads the entity when the commit
runs. An aborted transaction tells nothing, and the entity it spawned
is gone. A join cancelled at the commit leaves the spawn's handle
stale. Joins at one commit come in the order the entities were added,
before the removals the transaction asked for take effect.
Not told: the entities Horizon keeps without
simulating (displays, markers, interactions). Server-side.

An entity leaves the server level `dimension` (NeoForge's
`EntityLeaveLevelEvent`): vanilla's `onTrackingEnd`, when it is removed
for any reason (picked up, merged, despawned, burnt, blown up, killed,
taken by a hopper or a mob, gone through a portal) or its chunk unloads,
a level closing with nobody in it included. Not for the entities still
loaded when the server stops, as in vanilla. `entity` is its ID and
`kind` its type (`minecraft:item`); it is no longer in the level's lists.
It only hears. It tells every kind `entity_join_level` does
(`kind` is the type), each once, when the game next notices it gone
(the tick or action that removed
it). Inside a transaction (`Host::transaction`) opened in the entity's
own level an entity's removal takes effect, and this hook fires, at that
transaction's root commit, not at the removal call (an entity in another
level, as by a command run `in` it, leaves at once): from the call on its handle and selectors no longer find
it. An aborted transaction removes nothing and tells nothing. An entity
the transaction spawned and removed is never told to join, so it never
leaves. Check `kind`. Server-side.

May `entity` change the world? (NeoForge's `EntityMobGriefingEvent`,
`EventHooks.canEntityGrief`.) `can_grief` starts as the `mob_griefing`
game rule; set it either way. Asked for a mob
explosion (`ExplosionInteraction.MOB`, for the creeper, wither, ghast
fireball or wither skull), a mob picking up items, an enderman taking
or placing a block, a sheep eating grass, a mob trampling
farmland or turtle eggs, a ravager breaking leaves or crops, a wither
breaking blocks or leaving a wither rose, a silverfish leaving or
entering stone, a snow golem's snow, a fox's berries, a rabbit's
carrots, a villager's farming, an evoker's sheep, a zombie trampling
eggs, an allay's pickup, and a mob's arrow or small fireball changing
a block (asked for its owner), a zombie breaking a door, the dragon
breaking blocks, a ravager breaking pitcher crops, a burning mob
melting powder snow, a weaving mob's cobwebs, and decorations and items
in explosions (asked for the exploding entity, and for the mob that
causes the blast). Asked often: answer fast. Server-side.

An entity mounts or dismounts a vehicle (NeoForge's `EntityMountEvent`, posted from
`Entity.startRiding` and `removeVehicle`): `entity` of type `kind` (`minecraft:player`,
`minecraft:zombie`) in the server level `dimension`, getting on (`mounting`) or off the
`vehicle` of type `vehicle_kind` (`minecraft:oak_boat`, `minecraft:minecart`,
`minecraft:horse`, `minecraft:cushion`). Set `canceled` and it does not: a player stays
where they were, a mob does not board, a `/ride` fails, and a rider whose dismount is
canceled keeps riding. Players hear boarding and dismounts by input, `/ride`, hits,
bucking, teleport or spectator mode; mobs hear boarding and dismounts (jockeys,
ravager raiders, `/ride`, hits), including removal cleanup. A Mob's canceled
dismount keeps its relationship even when a boat or cart is destroyed; the
removed vehicle is not a valid handle or query result. Each later dismount asks again.
A resident Mob retries immediately before its next eligible entity tick:
its chunk must be entity-ticking and its tick must not have been canceled.
A server player retries on its next vehicle tick. Either can be later in the
same world tick. A rejected, nonresident passenger does not autonomously
tick or retry. Loading a save does not notify. Server-side.

One physical `Entity.move` invocation (arismoko/horizon#2414, design arismoko/horizon#2308, the
maintainer ruling of the same issue): the entity `entity` of `kind`
(`minecraft:zombie`) is about to move by `delta` (blocks this tick) for
`cause`'s sake - itself, the player behind a position packet, a piston,
a shulker box lid, a shulker mob's opening lid. It fires before the
move's own handling, no-physics and the stuck multiplier included, in
the one gate every kind's physics resolves through, so a forgotten
family cannot move around it. Change `delta` to replace the movement
(still through every ordinary restriction) or set `canceled` to skip
the invocation: no position, velocity, collision-flag or fall change,
and no displacement notice. A replacement component that is not a
finite number, or lies outside ±64 blocks, is refused whole - the move
stands as the requested delta would. A listener that unwinds keeps the
requested delta, not a replacement an earlier listener had proposed,
and is switched off for the session. It takes no Host - the maintainer
ruling, like the enderman's teleport: the listener only decides the
delta, and its `context` is the loop `context` of the side that ticks
the body. Server-authoritative: the client does not predict a custom
movement. Beyond NeoForge: there is no counterpart.

Whether an entity the client draws has the glowing outline, and in which
colour (`Entity.isCurrentlyGlowing` and `getTeamColor`, what Fabric's and
NeoForge's glowing and team colour overrides change). `outline` comes
in as vanilla's answer: `Some(0xRRGGBB)`, the team's colour or white,
when the entity glows, None when it doesn't. Set `Some` to make any
entity glow in that colour, None to take its outline away. It changes
only what this client draws: the entity's `Glowing` flag, what the
server and other players see, stays. Asked each frame for every mob,
player (yourself in third person), dropped item and projectile drawn.
API @API:entity_outline@.

neoforge: none (NeoForge 26.3 has no glowing or team colour override)

hooks.doc: `BlockEvent.EntityPlaceEvent` (and `EntityMultiPlaceEvent`, which extends it): `placer` set the block `state` at `pos` against `placed_against`, before it is written. `placer` is the player for `BlockItem.place` (before the stack shrinks), or the mob for an enderman putting its carried block down and a snow golem's trail; `None` is reserved for a placement with no entity. `placement` is `Single`, or `Multi` with every block the placement writes (a bed's foot and head, a door's halves, a tall plant), where `state` and `pos` stay the primary block (the foot, the lower half). For players, `placed_against` is the state adjacent to the primary placement position opposite the clicked face, including when the clicked block is replaceable. For mobs it is the state below the placement. Cancel stops the whole placement: no block is written, the stack is kept and an enderman keeps carrying its block. Server-side. Diverges from upstream: replaces the listen-only `place_block`; a mod that stopped placements by claiming `native_use_on` cancels here.

A server entity finished its portal wait and is beginning to leave
`dimension` through `pos`. The destination follows the portal rules.
A guest player's synchronized pose changed from `from` to `to`.

A player bow or crossbow launched an arrow with `force`, after the
projectile entered the level.

An entity's size was recalculated (NeoForge's `EntityEvent.Size`, vanilla's
`Entity.refreshDimensions`): its pose changed to `pose`, it grew up, its
`minecraft:scale` changed, or it is new. `size` (width, height and eye height, in
blocks) starts as vanilla's new size and `old_size` is the size it had. Change `size`
and the entity's box and eyes take it; later mods see earlier mods' edits. The answer
holds while the entity keeps that pose and vanilla size; the next change asks again,
starting from vanilla's. Changing the width or height leaves the eye height as it is:
set it too. Zero-size answers are valid. An answer is ignored if any component is
non-finite, negative or greater than 32 blocks. This bounds collision and pathfinding
work while allowing sizes larger than naturally occurring vanilla entities. `host`
reads the side that asks; the entity may be new, so read only what you need of it.

Asked on the server for its mobs (before and after their ticks) and for each LAN
guest's player (once a tick), and on a client for its own player (after its tick):
a size changed within a tick takes the answer at the next of those. Does not fire for:
other kinds of entity, whose vanilla sizes are fixed, and a client's copies of other
entities, which keep vanilla's size. Not cancellable.

A lightning bolt is about to hit `entity` (NeoForge's
`EntityStruckByLightningEvent`, before `Entity.thunderHit`): once per
bolt strike for each entity whose box meets the strike box (3 blocks
around, 9 up), players included. `bolt` is the lightning bolt. Set
`cancel` to spare the entity: no fire or damage, and no conversion
(pig, villager, mooshroom, creeper, copper golem). It still counts
as struck for Channeling's advancement. Not asked for a visual-only
bolt, which hits nothing. Server-side.
A mob became tamed after its owner and persistent state were set.

A server entity was moved by a same-level teleport command, after its
position changed. `entity` is its network id; `from` and `to` are
coordinates in `dimension`. This hook reports command teleports that
use Horizon's same-level target path; it does not change vanilla's
movement.

Whether a mod listens to `entity_tick_pre` and `entity_tick_post`: a mod
that hooks them hooks this one too and sets `listened` (HEAD, `*listened = true`).
Without it the game tells no entity's tick, and keeps no list of them. Asked once for
each family (mobs, items, minecarts, boats) each tick. Server-side.

neoforge: none (Horizon-only; NeoForge has no counterpart); an opt-in gate for a hook

hooks.doc:
The entity `entity` of type `kind` ticked in the server level `dimension` (NeoForge's
`EntityTickEvent.Post`): for each entity `entity_tick_pre` let through, after it
ticked, also one that died or was removed in its tick. Mobs and items hear their Posts
once the whole family has ticked; minecarts and boats right after their own tick. Server-side.

An entity of type `kind` (`minecraft:zombie`, `minecraft:item`) with ID `entity` is
about to tick in the server level `dimension` (NeoForge's `EntityTickEvent.Pre`, posted
around `Entity.commonTick` and `tick` in `ServerLevel.tickNonPassenger`). Set `canceled`
and it does not tick this tick: a mob has no AI, physics or effects, an item no movement,
ageing or merging, a minecart or boat no motion, and `entity_tick_post` is not told.
Horizon ticks a family of entities together, so mobs and items hear every Pre before the
first of them ticks; minecarts and boats hear theirs one by one. Told for the mobs, item
entities, minecarts and boats that tick: those in an entity-ticking chunk, not a player's
boat or cart (it ticks with the player). Check `kind`; this runs for every ticking entity
each tick, so keep it cheap. Server-side.

A guest's fall flying state changed on the server. The change has
already been applied.

`entity` is about to travel to the level `dimension` (NeoForge's
`EntityTravelToDimensionEvent`), before anything of it moves: the
entity is still where it is, in its own level. `cause` is why:
`nether_portal`, `end_portal` or `end_gateway` for a portal, or
`teleport` for a teleport that changes level (`/tp` and `/teleport`,
a spectator's teleport to a player in another level). Set `cancel` to
keep it where it is: a portal's wait is forgotten, a teleport is
dropped and `/tp` still reports success. An End gateway leads to
the level the entity is already in, so its `dimension` is the entity's
own.

Asked for server players, and for the other entities that cross a
portal or a command's teleport: items, mobs, boats, minecarts, arrows
and other projectiles, experience orbs, primed TNT, tridents,
fireworks and falling blocks. A vehicle and its passengers are asked
recursively. A refused passenger stays in the source level, dismounted,
with its own passengers; it does not veto the vehicle's travel. An entity
discarded during a callback never travels. A falling block is held out of the level while it
ticks, so its handle reads nothing yet. A respawn and a world's join
are not travel; the return from the End credits is `end_portal`.
Server-side. Diverges
from upstream: replaces `player_portal`, which covered only server
players through portals.

A leashed mob's leash was removed, before any lead drop is handled
(Bukkit's `EntityUnleashEvent`).

neoforge: none (NeoForge has no such event; Bukkit's EntityUnleashEvent)

hooks.doc: An experience bottle broke and its experience was awarded.

Experience before enchantments (`IBlockExtension.getExpDrop`). First answer
replaces vanilla sampling; the global break_block event may override it.
Answers are clamped to 0..=32767. A panic unwinds before the answer is applied.

Whether the experience orb `into` takes the orb `from` in (vanilla's
`ExperienceOrb.canMerge`): the same value, and ids a multiple of 40 apart. Asked
for each pair whose boxes meet, when an orb spawns (`tryMergeToExisting`: `from` is
0, the new orb isn't an entity yet, and only `from_value` is known) and every 20
ticks as an orb scans for neighbours (`scanForMerges`). `can_merge` holds vanilla's
answer; change it either way. A merged orb counts as `count` orbs of `into`'s
value, so forcing orbs of different values together drops points unless the mod
raises `into`'s value with `native_set_experience_orb` in `experience_orb_merge`.
Server-side.

neoforge: none (vanilla ExperienceOrb.canMerge; NeoForge adds no event or extension for it)

hooks.doc:
The experience orb `into` (`into_value` points, `into_count` orbs) is about to
take `from` (`from_value` points, `from_count` orbs) in, after
`experience_orb_can_merge` said yes (`from` is 0 and `from_count` 1 for a new orb
that is spawning). Set `canceled` to stop it: both orbs stay, and a spawning orb
tries the next orb in reach, then spawns on its own. Left alone, `into` adds
`from`'s count, as vanilla does. A mod that writes `into`'s value or count with
`set_experience_orb` here makes that write the merged orb: `from` is taken in
without adding its count, so `into_value = 11, into_count = 1` pays 11 once. The
merge is refused, and `into` put back as it was (value, count and age), when `from`
has changed or left reach by the time the merge applies. A merge whose count would
pass `i32::MAX` (what a save holds) is refused the same way. A write the listener made
to `from` itself is not undone. Server-side.

neoforge: none (vanilla ExperienceOrb.tryMergeToExisting; NeoForge adds no event or extension for it)

hooks.doc:
An explosion at `center` in `dimension` (`minecraft:overworld`) is
about to break `blocks` and reach `entities`: `ServerExplosion.explode`
with its `toBlow`, before any block or entity is hit. Take out the
positions to spare; they keep their block and get no fire. `entities`
is `getEntities(source, box)`: every entity in the box the centre
± (2 × radius + 1), in walk order, without the exploding source, those
that will ignore the blast included — the entity-list walk, then the
item frames, paintings, cushions and end crystals it misses. Take one
out and it is neither hurt nor pushed, and `explosion_knockback` is
not asked for it; one a mod adds is walked as any other, and the list
the listeners leave controls membership, subject to the usual distance,
exposure and per-kind immunity checks. Order controls the ordinary-storage
walk only, not global effect order: crystals/dragon and players run in
separate earlier passes, and decorations run last in storage order.
Block positions are shuffled before destruction, so their list order is
not destruction order either. Server-side.

An explosion at `center` in `dimension`, about to break `blocks`, pushes
`entity` (None for a player, whom `host.players().acting_player()` names):
`ServerExplosion.hurtEntities`, after the knockback is calculated. Change `knockback_velocity` to change
what is added to the entity's velocity; a player's client is sent the
same. Wind bursts too, except dragons and end crystals. End crystals
are also omitted from ordinary blasts: Horizon removes them without a
velocity to change. Server-side.

A server explosion is about to begin at `center`, with `radius` (Bukkit's
`ExplosionPrimeEvent`). This is listen-only: the explosion proceeds as
usual. Server-side, including the single-player server.

neoforge: none (NeoForge has no such event; Bukkit's ExplosionPrimeEvent)

hooks.doc:
On an authoritative server, the explosion resistance of the block `state` at `pos`
against `explosion` (`IBlockExtension.getExplosionResistance`), asked as a ray of the
blast enters the block (`ExplosionDamageCalculator.getBlockExplosionResistance`). The
answer replaces only the block's own value (`BlockProperties.explosion_resistance`);
a fluid in the cell still raises it to the fluid's 100. What vanilla applies after the
block's value keeps winning: a respawn anchor's water cell, a TNT minecart's rails and
the blocks under them (never asked) and a dangerous wither skull's 0.8 cap. A negative
or non-finite answer is refused and the block's own value is used; a panicking part is
contained and the block's own value is used. A ray asks once per block it enters, so
keep the answer a pure function of the inputs. The level is read-only. With no part
attached to the state, the cost is one table lookup. Diverges from upstream: new hook.

A server explosion is about to happen (`ExplosionEvent.Start`, in
`ServerLevel.explode` before `ServerExplosion.explode`): every one,
TNT, creepers, beds and anchors, fireballs, withers, end crystals and
wind bursts. Set `cancel` and nothing of it happens: no blocks, no
damage or knockback, no sound, particles or game event. Before
`explosion_prime`, which a cancel skips. Server-side.

A mod-started video export ended. `frames` counts complete output frames.
Heard once after `export_status` is terminal and `export.json` has been published
or its publication has failed, been cancelled, or exceeded its deadline. A timed-out
rename may still complete. A graceful stop reports `Finished`; an interrupted export
on world exit or disconnect reports `Failed`.
Starting another export from this hook returns `Busy`.

The event's fields are fixed on the wire (docs/modding/src/concepts/wire-types.md).

Add block states to an existing POI type (NeoForge `ExtendPoiTypesEvent`): a mod's
bed to `minecraft:home`, its workstation to `minecraft:armorer`. Asked once the block
registry is resolved, before any world's POI tables are built, and again on a
resource reload. Build each predicate on `event.extensions.metadata()` and hand it
to `event.extensions.extend(poi_type, states)`; a block predicate with no
constraints means all of the block's states. The engine resolves the additions
and refuses, one logged warning each naming both types, an unknown POI type and a
state vanilla or an earlier addition already gives to a different type; the rest
of a mod's additions still apply. A state added to the type it already has is a
no-op. A tag predicate is refused: additions name blocks.
Wasm subscriptions refuse at load, naming the borrowed metadata capability;
this hook is not silently skipped when its context cannot cross Wire.

Before one of the first-person view's block overlays (`ScreenEffectRenderer`) is drawn,
once a frame each is shown: `Block` with the view-blocking `state` at `pos` the camera is
inside, `Water` with the `state` at the eye's block `pos` while the eye is under water, and
`Fire` with fire's default `state` at the player's block `pos` while they burn. Never for a
spectator; `Fire` only in first person. Set `canceled` to leave that overlay out; the
frame, the other block overlays and the HUD's camera overlays are drawn as before. Set
`custom_draw` to draw it yourself (`block_screen_effect_draw`), canceled or not.
`partial_tick` is the world's.
Client-side.

An entity landed on a block state this part is attached to (`Block.fallOn`), after falling `event.distance` blocks. `event.damage` is the fall damage the entity calculated, before hurt handling and the fall sounds: change it, and zero prevents both. An entity that cannot be hurt by the fall (creative, fall immune) is told with zero damage and keeps its immunity, and a cancelled fall still lands. It runs inside the entity's move, on the level random host: it reads blocks and draws the level's random in vanilla's order, and cannot write. A write the override makes (farmland turning to dirt, a turtle egg breaking) is asked with `event.request(LandingWrite::SetBlock(state))` or `LandingWrite::DestroyBlock { drop }` and lands at the block the entity landed on once the entity's batch has ticked, in the order asked, if the block is still the state it landed on. SetBlock takes an API BlockState. The complete requested batch is checked before queuing: an invalid key or ordinal refuses all writes and sibling outputs from that callback, including damage. The original landed-state guard is checked once per batch, not between its ordered writes. Players, mobs and dropped items land here (an item as an `EntityRef` of kind `minecraft:item`, with zero damage: items take none); projectiles and the other entities do not.

A falling block of `state` ticked and is still in the air
(`IFallableExtension.fallingTick`): `entity` is the falling block, and `pos` the block
it is in (`Entity.blockPosition`) after its move. Heard once for each tick that ends with
it still falling, not in the tick it lands, drops as an item or is removed (that is
`Fallable.onLand`'s moment). The part can write to the level and, through `entity`, to
the falling block: its velocity, its position. The tick is recorded as it ends and
delivered once the level's falling blocks, primed TNT and orbs have ticked in this pass,
so a write lands on the stored falling block; a falling block gone by then is skipped.
Diverges from NeoForge: server only, where NeoForge also calls it on the client. Only a
state a part listens to is recorded; with no such part, one table lookup per falling
block per tick. Diverges from upstream: new hook.

Called on the server before a landing converts farmland to its base block. It is given the loop `context` of the side that ticks the entity (its registries, settings and mod list); it fires inside the tick's own landing, before the block is written, so it takes no `Host`.

A player fills (`stack` an empty bucket) or empties a bucket at `pos`:
`BucketItem.use`, where it asks `Level.mayInteract`. Set `canceled`
and the bucket does nothing. Server-side, for every player of the
world (`host.players().acting_player()` says who).

NeoForge's `FinalizeSpawnEvent`: the new mob of type `kind` is at `pos` and `Mob.finalizeSpawn` (equipment, attributes, variants, the class's own setup) is about to run for `reason`. `spawner` is the spawner block for a spawner or trial spawner spawn, none otherwise (a minecart spawner too). `difficulty` is the local difficulty finalization reads: change it to change what the mob gets. There are two cancels. Return `Flow::Cancel` to skip finalization: no finalizeSpawn runs, and the mob still spawns uninitialised (no equipment, attributes or class setup). Set `spawn_cancelled` to stop the spawn: no mob is added and finalization does not run. It draws nothing itself; skipped finalization skips its draws, and with no listener or an untouched event the draws are vanilla's. Fired only where vanilla 26.3 calls `finalizeSpawn` on a mob the game makes, with vanilla's `reason` at that call: natural spawning, chunk generation's animals, spawners, trial spawners, patrols, raids and sieges, zombie reinforcements, a cat spawner's cat, phantoms, jockeys, `/summon` and `/raid`, spawn eggs and dispensers, the nether portal's piglin (`Structure`), a skeleton trap's horse and riders, an evoker's vexes and wandering traders. A conversion fires with `Conversion`, and a cancel there leaves the converted mob as it is. Not fired where vanilla creates the mob without `finalizeSpawn`: breeding and a baby from a spawn egg, an infested block's or effect's silverfish, a thrown egg's chick, a thrown pearl's endermite, a hatching egg's turtle, sniffer or tadpole, a copper golem built from blocks, a slime from the oozing effect and a lightning trap's horse. Nor for entities loaded from disk or structure mobs placed by world generation. `mob` is the mob itself, not yet in a level: read it through the host (`mob.kind(host)`, `mob.equipment(host, slot)`, `mob.attribute_base(host, id)`) and change it through `edits` (`edits.set_equipment(mob, slot, item)`, `edits.set_attribute_base(mob, id, base)`, tags and the custom name); the handle and the editor reach only this mob, and after the hook returns the handle answers `Expired`. Listeners run before finalization: finalization's own rolls (equipment, attribute bonuses, variants) still run after them and overwrite what a listener put in the same slot or attribute; `Flow::Cancel` keeps every edit, since no finalization follows. A mob finalization itself makes (a chicken jockey's chicken, a zombie horse's rider) is lent with its own handle. `group` is the pack's spawn group data (`SpawnGroupData`, `SpawnGroup`): what the listener leaves there is what finalization reads for this mob. Every site this hook fires at hands it `None`: the game threads no group data through a live pack; chunk generation's animals share it only inside the generator, out of the hook's reach. The host is the read-only one, and `edits` changes nothing but this mob: listeners run on replayed ticks, so they must be pure functions of their inputs and edit only `mob` and `group`. Server-side.

On an authoritative server, how fire treats the block `state` at `pos`
(`FireBlock.setFlammable(block, igniteOdds, burnOdds)`), asked from its
side `face`, the one that faces the fire or the air fire may take: put
`(ignite, burn)` in `odds` for your own blocks, and vanilla's table
isn't read. Ignite odds above zero let fire stand beside the block and
spread into the air around it (planks 5, wool 30, leaves 30); burn odds
are how fast fire destroys it (planks 20, wool 60, leaves 60). `(0, 0)`
never burns, and a face with ignite odds of zero isn't flammable. Negative
answers become zero; burn odds cap at 300 (horizontal rolls are 300,
vertical rolls 250), and spread speed uses saturating arithmetic. A waterlogged state never burns and
isn't asked. Answer only for your own blocks and leave `odds` empty
otherwise; the level is read-only. Asked hundreds of times per fire
tick: keep it short.
A firework rocket completed its explosion effects.

Once for each frame presented, in a world or not, after that frame's
`render_frame_post` (NeoForge's `FlipFrameEvent`): the place to rotate
per-frame GPU data. Not cancellable. A frame that was not presented does
not fire it. Client-side.

The current of the fluid block at `pos` (`FlowingFluid.getFlow`, the vector that pushes an entity standing in it) is about to push a player, mob, item, experience orb, armor stand or arrow. `fluid` is the fluid's id (`minecraft:water`, `minecraft:flowing_lava`...); a mod may change `flow`, so it can rotate, strengthen or still a current. It runs for each fluid block the entity touches, so keep it short. The vector the renderer reads to turn a fluid's texture is not changed. Fires on both sides, on the client's replayed ticks too, with the loop `context` of the side that ticks the entity (its registries, settings and mod list): register the mod on both, and keep the listener a pure function of its inputs so prediction and the server agree. Beyond NeoForge: there is no counterpart. Diverges from upstream: new hook.

neoforge: none (vanilla FlowingFluid.getFlow; NeoForge adds no event or extension for it)

hooks.doc:
A flowing fluid at `pos` is about to change level. `fluid` is `water`
or `lava`; the levels are 0 through 8. Set `cancel` to keep the old
level. Server-side.

Liquid at `liquid_pos` is about to place `state` at `pos`. Set
`cancel` to prevent placement or change `new_state` to replace it.
Server-side.

How a mod's world fluid flows at `pos`, starting from what it declared (NeoForge's
`BaseFlowingFluid` and `FluidType` getters: `getTickDelay`, `getDropOff`,
`getSlopeFindDistance`, `canConvertToSource`). `fluid` is the id it was declared with.
Asked for every flow step and every cell a spread looks at: answer fast. An answer
outside what `WorldFluid` accepts is brought back within it. Server-side.

neoforge: none (BaseFlowingFluid.getTickDelay, getDropOff, getSlopeFindDistance and FluidType.canConvertToSource are overrides; NeoForge adds no event)

hooks.doc:
The fluid at `pos` is about to run its scheduled tick (`FlowingFluid.tick`). `fluid` is
`water`, `lava` or a mod fluid's id. Set `cancel` and the tick does nothing at all: no
level change, no spreading and no new tick. For a mod that simulates a fluid itself;
`fluid_level_change` and `block_spread` still ask about each change of a tick that runs.
A cancelled tick schedules nothing; a mod taking over must re-schedule itself.
It's asked once per tick, so keep it cheap. Server-side.

`FluidTooltipEvent`: the tooltip of `stack`, a fluid the game draws a slot of (the recipe
viewer's fluid wells), once its name, its amount in millibuckets and, with F3+H, its id
are in `lines`, each with a colour as `rgba` packs it (`u32::MAX` keeps the text's own).
Add, change, reorder or remove lines, and an empty list draws nothing. It fires before
the tooltip is laid out or drawn, with no item and no `item_tooltip` involved: a tank's
or a fluid slot's tooltip has neither. Asked each frame the tooltip shows, only while a
mod listens. Client-side.

The food level of the server player `player` (`name`) is about to change
from `from` to `to` (Bukkit's `FoodLevelChangeEvent`):
eating, hunger and saturation effects, the exhaustion that costs a
point, starving. Change `to` (kept between 0 and 20; saturation never
exceeds it) or set `cancel` to leave the level at `from`, saturation
included. Heard once for the change a player's turn made as a whole, so
two changes in one tick arrive as one. Not heard: the full food bar a
respawn gives, the food a player joins with and the host of a LAN
world. The player's state is swapped in, so `host.players().acting_player()`,
`PlayerRef::tell` and the item helpers reach them. On a server.

The frame rate this window is about to be held to: Max Framerate after the
inactivity throttle and Battery Mode (260 is unlimited). `focused` is whether the
window has focus, `minimized` whether it is minimised and `in_world` whether a world
is open. A mod may lower `limit`, as Dynamic FPS does for a window in the background:
Horizon keeps the lower of its own limit and the mod's, and ignores values below 1.

The friction of a block state this part is attached to (`IBlockExtension.getFriction`) is being read for the entity on it; vanilla's values are 0.6 for most blocks, 0.98 for ice, packed ice and frosted ice, 0.989 for blue ice and 0.8 for slime. `entity` and `kind` are the entity's id and type (`minecraft:player`, `minecraft:item`), `pos` the block and `state` its state. A part may change `friction` (`event.friction`), which starts at the block's own value; an answer that is not finite or is outside `0..=2` (the range a content block's declared friction takes) is dropped and the block's own value is used. This deliberately limits NeoForge's uncapped answer to protect movement from invalid mod input.
