the kind sets it). The context is an owned snapshot, captured after the subscription guard.
`tags` reads membership and ordered members by key from this evaluation's
authoritative merged tags. No enumeration or full Host is exposed.

A block broke or a mob died, and `drops` are the items about to drop, in
the order they drop: what the loot tables rolled (after
`loot_table_load`'s changes), and for a mob what it wore, held or
carried (a fox's mouth item, an allay's, piglin's or horse's inventory),
but not an enderman's carried block or a copper golem's preserved
equipment, which drop after. A charged creeper's head and a fox's mouth
item come before the mob's own table. A block's stacks get its block
entity's data (a shulker box's items) after this. Add, change or take out
stacks; empty ones don't drop (NeoForge's global loot modifiers, Fabric's
`LootTableEvents.MODIFY_DROPS`); `context` says what dropped them and
how, and it is called even when `drops` is empty. A player's use drops
through it too (`LootDrops::used`: shears, a brush, an item
frame), with that player named. Lead drops from untying or cutting a
leash, and from a mob a player killed while leashed, pass through here
too, with that player named. It hears blocks that a
player, an explosion or a mob breaks, not other breaks (leaves decaying,
a torch losing its wall, a piston, `/setblock ... destroy`), nor a
creative break or a tool that can't harvest the block, nor experience.
For deaths, `context.damage_source` carries the death invocation's
damage type and causing/direct IDs (not remembered player credit), and
`context.tool` is None (the entity context has no TOOL). Resolve the causing
ID through `host.entity` and `host.living` to read its main hand live with
`living.hand_item(host, Hand::Main)`, including earlier listeners' changes.
`context.weapon_item(host)` reads the recorded projectile weapon or the
live melee weapon, including a player's active auto-spin stack.
Block and use drops retain their tool meaning.
Server-side, for every player.

A loot function of a mod's own kind: the entry named a `type` in a
namespace outside `minecraft:`, and the roll kept it for this call.
The kind and JSON file input accompany owned API context and candidate snapshots.
Candidate counts remain signed; ordered NBT patches preserve removals and types.
Conversion happens only for subscribed hooks, and refused writeback leaves the roll unchanged.
`tags` reads membership and ordered members by key from this evaluation's
authoritative merged tags. No enumeration or full Host is exposed.

A native mod's hook point (docs/modding/src/how-to/native-mods.md), declared in `hooks/*.rs` with the game's:
the loot table `id` (`minecraft:chests/simple_dungeon`, `minecraft:blocks/stone`,
`minecraft:entities/zombie`) as it loads, its JSON after the data packs', before anything
rolls it (NeoForge's `LootTableLoadEvent`, Fabric's `LootTableEvents.MODIFY`). Add pools to
`table["pools"]` or entries to a pool's `entries`, change or replace it (no pools: it drops
nothing; keep its `random_sequence` when replacing it, as a mob's table without one drops
nothing). Called once per table in id order when the server loads or reloads its data, with the
`DataLoadContext` of that owning load (`origin()` is always `ServerDataLoad`: the client never loads
loot tables, so the hook never fires there).

Whether an open trapdoor above the block state this part is attached to climbs like a ladder (`IBlockExtension.makesOpenTrapdoorAboveClimbable`, which `LivingEntity.onClimbable` asks of the block under the open trapdoor a living entity stands in). `state` is that block's state and `pos` its position; `trapdoor` is the open trapdoor's state above it. `climbable` starts with vanilla's answer, true for a `minecraft:ladder` facing the trapdoor's way, and a part may set either value. Asked only once the trapdoor itself was not a ladder (`is_ladder` and the `#minecraft:climbable` tag), so it never makes a block that is a ladder stop climbing. A gliding entity in a `#minecraft:can_glide_through` block, a spectator and a player who is flying are never asked. Read for the player, the mobs, and the climbing a mod reads through `LivingRef::is_climbing`. It fires on both sides and on the client's replayed ticks, so register the mod on both and keep the listener a pure function of its inputs. It is given the loop `context` of the side that ticks the entity, and takes no `Host`. With no part attached to the state below, the owning game checks the hook subscription and prepared API block key before any event conversion, so the cost is one table lookup. Armor stands never ask it. Diverges from upstream: new hook.

NeoForge's `IItemExtension.makesPiglinsNeutral`: does `stack`, worn by `wearer`, keep
calm piglins from targeting it, as gold armour does (`PiglinAi.isWearingSafeArmor`)?
`neutral` arrives with vanilla's answer, whether the stack is in
`#minecraft:piglin_safe_armor`; set it `true` to make the piece count as gold, `false`
to make it not count though the tag lists it, or leave it to keep the tag's answer. Asked
for each stack in a player's armour slots, in the order feet, legs, chest, head, until one
counts. A player wearing a piece that counts is not the target a calm piglin picks
(`NEAREST_TARGETABLE_PLAYER_NOT_WEARING_GOLD`); an angry piglin attacks anyway. Only the
`ItemPart`s attached to `stack`'s item are asked. It is asked whenever the server builds
a player's view for the mobs, several times a tick, so the answer must be a pure, fast
function of `stack` and `wearer`. An item with no such part costs one table lookup.
Server-side. The contract beyond the method's name and parameters is Horizon's reading,
not checked against NeoForge's.

The map decoration types a mod adds (NeoForge's `RegisterEvent` for
`Registries.MAP_DECORATION_TYPE`): push a `MapDecorationType` per type. Asked once at
start, on every side.

Icons a mod puts on map `map` each time it is drawn: held, in an
item frame or on the cartography table's screen (a map's pixels are
its own; nothing is saved in the map). Push `MapDecoration`s
(an atlas sprite, a position in half map pixels, a rotation, and
whether it shows in a frame and on the screen like vanilla's markers
do); they are drawn after the vanilla ones with the same pose, and a
sprite the atlas lacks is left out. `map.center`, `map.scale` and
`map.dimension` say which blocks the map shows, and
`MapDecoration::x` has the formula. Vanilla's decorations are
not passed in. Asked every frame a map is drawn, so keep it cheap.
The client half of `MapDecorationType` and `addDecoration`: a type
registered on the server and saved in the map's data is not here.

On an authoritative server, `VegetationBlock.mayPlaceOn` for the
plant `state` on `ground` at `ground_pos`, before the plant answers
it: the blocks a mod plant (one whose template is a vanilla plant,
such as a crop) can stand on. Its template's `canSurvive` asks it, so
the plant is refused there and pops off when its ground changes to
one it can't stand on. Answer only for your own blocks. The level is
read-only.

`may_place_on` again, for the world generation of the server: while a feature places the
plant `state` on `ground` at `ground_pos`, its parts answer `may` here, and the soil's
parts answer `can_sustain_plant_v2` before this. `ground` is the block the plant stands
on, so a rule that only picks its soil belongs in `can_sustain_plant_v2`. Answer only
for your own blocks. Server-side, on the worldgen worker threads and on the server
thread, with the server's worldgen `context`: no `Host`, no writes. A panicking part is
contained and the plant's own rule kept. Diverges from upstream: `may_place_on` in world
generation.
The normal menu blur request, before finite/range validation. None disables it.

neoforge: none (NeoForge has no menu blur event)
none (NeoForge has no such event; vanilla AbstractContainerMenu.clickMenuButton)

hooks.doc:
A click in a menu a mod opened (`native_open_menu`), which moved
nothing: the menu's `slot` (its own first, then the player's
inventory, `native_menu_inventory_slot`; -999 outside), the `button`
and the click's `mode` (`ClickType`'s id) of the player `uuid`.
No player's state is swapped in: the menu helpers take the player's
UUID. `ItemPlace::MenuSlot` reaches the menu's own storage and its player's
inventory and hotbar slots. `PlayerSlot` and `PlayerHand` resolve the online
clicking player through the usual acting-player or guest path. All writes
use transactions; stale menus and player identities refuse writes.

neoforge: none (vanilla AbstractContainerMenu.clicked; NeoForge adds no event or extension for it)

hooks.doc:
A menu a mod opened closed: the player closed it, the server or a mod
opened another, or the player left.

Block `block` at `pos` opens its mod menu type `menu` for server
player `player`: set `data` to hand the menu's screen bytes of your
own (a machine's tier, mode or recipes), up to 32 KiB, which the
client reads with `screen_extra_data` while the screen is open
(NeoForge's `openMenu` with an extra-data writer). The first mod to
set it wins, so answer only for your blocks. The player's state is not
swapped in.

Containers exposed by linked slots of server player `player`'s open mod menu
`menu` (`namespace:path`) at `pos`. The player's state is not swapped in.
Push container positions to `links`, in order. The engine resolves containers and
refreshes their linked slots in the same tick. Asked each server tick only for open
mod menu types declaring links, and dispatched only to subscribers. With no
subscribers the linked-container tick does no work and allocates nothing.
Silently skips `pos`, duplicate positions, missing or non-lendable containers,
and positions after 64 accepted containers (`MAX_MENU_LINKS`). First accepted
occurrence wins, preserving answer order.
Native and wasm listeners append positions with identical copy-out semantics.

neoforge: none (Horizon mod menus expose linked container slots)

hooks.doc:
A player shift-clicked slot `slot` of the menu of the mod block
entity at `pos` (`AbstractContainerMenu.quickMoveStack`, the method a
Java menu overrides), on the server, before the game's own routing:
move the stack where your block wants it. `slot` is the menu's index:
below `container_slots` it is the block's own slot (`entity.items`),
from there on the player's inventory (27 main slots, then the hotbar).
`stack` is a copy of what the slot holds; take what you move out of
it (put it in `entity.items`, or in another block through its
`ITEMS` capability) and set `handled`: the slot then holds what is
left of `stack` (whatever you wrote to that slot of `entity.items`),
the game's routing is skipped, and the player's client gets the menu
again. Left unhandled, `entity.items` goes back to what it held and
the game moves the stack as for any container; a later mod sees what
an earlier one did to `stack`.

For a mod container on a vanilla menu type and on a mod menu type,
the left or right button, a slot that holds something and that the
mod's screen shows; not for a spectator or a dead player, a menu no
longer valid, nor during a drag.
Asked once per click, where vanilla asks `quickMoveStack` again while
it keeps moving the same item. The player's state is swapped in, so
`host.players().acting_player()` names them; `entity` is out of the world
during the call, as in `menu_button`.

neoforge: none (a Java menu overrides AbstractContainerMenu.quickMoveStack; no event)

hooks.doc:
Slot placement and stack limits for registered vanilla and mod menus;
mounts use `horizon:mount_inventory`, while player inventory and the
creative picker have no registered type. `slot` is the backing index,
including player inventory slots. The slot's own answers arrive first;
the maximum is bounded to 1–99 and the item limit. Refusal also prevents
quick-move top-ups. Runs on server and client prediction with the read
`Host`: it is a query, so it can neither write nor cancel. A click asks
once for each slot and stack it consults while it plans, and never again
when it validates or applies. Answer from the stack and the host alone,
and fast. On a LAN host's own click the LAN host is not reachable
through the `Host` (it answers as if no LAN were open).
`container` is the container `slot` indexes ([`MenuContainer`]): a mod
crafting grid's slots are `Grid`'s and its result `Result`'s slot 0.
`context` says who and where the ask is about ([`MenuSlotContext`]):
the player whose menu it is, the menu's block entity and a read-only
copy of the menu's own containers' slots, keyed by the same container
(`context.slot(container, index)`), built once per click plan and
filled the same on the server and on the client's prediction. Parts that read `context.setting(..)` or `side()` have no
counterpart on the Host. Named injections request `hook_version = 4`.

neoforge: none (vanilla Slot.mayPlace and mayPickup; NeoForge adds no event or extension for it)

hooks.doc:
Whether a player's block menu of a mod menu type stays open
(`AbstractContainerMenu.stillValid`). Asked on the server each tick a
player has the menu of the block at `pos` open, and before each click
on it. `valid` arrives as vanilla's answer: the block entity is there
and `eye` is within the player's block interaction range plus 4 of each
block behind the menu; a part that leaves it alone keeps that answer.
Set it to keep the menu open or close it. Vanilla menu types are never
asked, and a menu whose block entity is gone closes without asking.
Runs in the restricted context; answer from the event and context
alone, and fast.

neoforge: none (vanilla AbstractContainerMenu.stillValid, which each menu overrides)

hooks.doc:
A recipe viewer's "+" on a mod menu (JEI's `IRecipeTransferHandler`):
move one set of `recipe`'s ingredients (as many as the items allow
with `max`) from `player`'s inventory into the open menu of a mod menu
type, or with `dry_run` only say what that would do. Asked on the
server before the game's own grid transfer, only for a mod menu type
whose part answers, with `menu` its type, `pos` its block (None for a
menu with no block) and `recipe` the recipe's id as the viewer sent
it. Return `Some(Moves)` once moved, or `Missing`, `NoRoom` or
`NotIntoMenu`; a part that returns None lets the game try its own
crafting-grid transfer. A dry run must move nothing.

neoforge: none (JEI IRecipeTransferHandler, which each mod implements for its menus)

hooks.doc: A minecart passed over a rail block state this part is attached to (the moment `AbstractMinecart` calls `activateMinecart` on an activator rail, for every rail; Forge's `IBaseRailExtension.onMinecartPass`, which NeoForge 26.3 no longer has, so this hook has no counterpart). `event.entity` is the cart, `event.pos` the rail. With the old minecart physics it fires once per tick the cart is on a rail; with `minecart_improvements` once per track iteration, so a fast cart can pass several times in a tick. It fires after the cart's batch has ticked, not mid-move, so a write the part makes (a velocity change through the cart handle) lands on the stored cart, and a pass whose cart is gone or whose rail changed is dropped. Only a rail state a part listens for is recorded; with no such part nothing is kept. Diverges from upstream: new hook.

neoforge: none (Forge's IBaseRailExtension.onMinecartPass is gone in NeoForge 26.3)

hooks.doc: The minimap a native mod shows: set `minimap` when it is none yet.

NeoForge's `MobDespawnEvent`: the mob `mob` (of type `kind`, at `pos`) is about to run `Mob.checkDespawn`, which fires once per tick for every mob that is ticked or only checked for despawning, persistent ones and peaceful-mode ones included. The hook is told while the game has lent its mob list to the tick, so `mob` resolves through the tick's own read view (arismoko/horizon#795): the ticking mob itself, and the other present mobs in its tick snapshot, are readable through the host. The ticking mob is read directly; an already-ticked peer exposes its post-turn state and a not-yet-ticked peer its pre-turn state. A mob spawned during the pass does not resolve in this scoped view until the next pass. Removed mobs do not resolve; a dead-but-present mob is not a removed mob. This is the scoped read-host first step for arismoko/horizon#795, not an in-place ownership redesign. `kind` and `pos` stay as plain data for listeners that only need them. Set `result`: `Allow` discards the mob now, `Deny` keeps it this tick, and `Default` (the starting value) leaves vanilla's rules to decide. Anything but `Default` skips vanilla's checks, including the `nextInt(800)` draw of the idle-despawn roll, so the hook fires before that draw: a mob a mod denies does not consume it. A listener is a pure function of its inputs, because the hook fires on replayed ticks. The wither and the ender dragon override `checkDespawn` without `super`, so the event is not fired for them. Server-side. Tick-time effect: one `listened` branch per mob per tick with no listeners.

NeoForge's `MobEffectEvent.Added`, vanilla's `MobEffect.onEffectStarted`:
every `LivingEntity.addEffect` of the content mod's effect `effect`,
new or not, changed or not, after `on_effect_added`.
Server-side.

NeoForge's `MobEffectEvent.Applicable`, vanilla's `LivingEntity.canBeAffected`: asked wherever the game checks whether the resolved `EffectKey` `effect` (`minecraft:poison`) can land on the living entity `entity` (a [`LivingRef`], the player's own included), before `addEffect` accepts it. Unlike the effect hooks above this fires for every effect, vanilla's included, and only when an add is in flight. The first mod to answer decides: `Allow` or `Deny` overrides the vanilla tag check; an unanswered hook falls back to it. Server-side.

NeoForge's `MobEffectEvent.Expired`, vanilla `LivingEntity.tickEffects`: the resolved `EffectKey` `effect` (`minecraft:speed`, amplifier `amplifier`) on the living entity `entity` (a [`LivingRef`], the player's own included) counted down to nothing and is about to leave. Cancel and the effect stays, kept at no ticks and asked again next tick; unanswered, the expiry runs. Fires only on the tick an effect actually expires, never per tick. Server-side.

NeoForge's `MobEffectEvent.Remove`, vanilla `LivingEntity.removeEffect`: the resolved `EffectKey` `effect` (`minecraft:speed`, amplifier `amplifier`) on the living entity `entity` (a [`LivingRef`], the player's own included) is about to be removed by any path that walks the vanilla funnel: a command or milk for the player, a cure for a zombie villager, a mod's removal helper. Cancel and the effect stays. Server-side.

`player`'s melee blow killed the mob `entity` of `kind` (other deaths
aren't told yet). It only hears, after the blow landed. Server-side.

NeoForge's `MobSpawnEvent.SpawnPlacementCheck`: may the entity type `kind` spawn at `pos` in `level` for `reason`? It is asked after vanilla's own spawn predicate (`SpawnPlacements.checkSpawnRules`: light, the ground it needs, the biome, slime chunks, the peaceful rule) has run: `default_result` is what it answered, and `result` starts as `Default`, which keeps that answer. Set `Succeed` or `Fail` to force the check. It runs wherever the game calls `checkSpawnRules` with the game's level: natural spawning, a village siege's zombies, a patrol, a zombie's reinforcements, a spawner and a trial spawner. `level` is the level the mob would spawn in (`dimension` names it too), so a listener can read the blocks around `pos` through the host. `spawner` is the block that asked: `Spawner::Block` for a spawner block, `Spawner::Trial` for a trial spawner, and `None` for natural spawning, sieges, patrols, reinforcements and a spawner minecart. A spawner whose spawn data carries custom spawn rules never reaches it. The predicate always runs first, as `default_result` is its answer, so its random draws are vanilla's whatever a mod answers; a listener should be a pure function of its inputs, because the checks run again when a tick is replayed. The host is the read-only one: a listener reads the world and writes nothing. Not told of `/summon` or a spawn egg, which do not check placements. Server-side. Beyond NeoForge: one `SpawnCheck` answers this event and `mob_spawn_position_check`, which NeoForge gives two nested enums with the same three constants.

NeoForge's `MobSpawnEvent.PositionCheck`: may the freshly created mob of type `kind` stand at `pos` (its position, a mob's centre) in `level` for `reason`? Vanilla's two checks are `Mob.checkSpawnRules` (the type's own rules) and `Mob.checkSpawnObstruction` (inside blocks or fluids, an ocelot's grass and sea level). `result` starts as `Default`, which runs them; `Succeed` or `Fail` answers instead and they are skipped. It runs on natural spawning, chunk generation's creature packs and spawner blocks (where a spawner with custom spawn rules skips `Mob.checkSpawnRules` on `Default`, as vanilla does).  A trial spawner runs only `checkSpawnObstruction`, so only that is skipped. `spawner` is the block that asked (`Spawner::Block` or `Spawner::Trial`), `None` for natural spawning, chunk generation and a spawner minecart. `mob` is the mob itself, in no level yet: read it through the host (`mob.kind(host)`, `mob.position(host)`, `mob.equipment(host, slot)`); after the hook returns the handle answers `Expired`. It is the mob that spawns if the check passes, handed on rather than created again, and dropped without trace if it fails. Where the game does not create the mob fresh (chunk generation's packs, a spawner whose spawn data carries entity data) the handle answers its kind and position and `Unsupported` for the rest. Server-side. With no listener or `Default` the checks and their random draws are vanilla's (creating the mob for the listener draws nothing from the level's random); `Succeed` and `Fail` skip the checks and so their draws, and the level random's order changes only then; a listener should be a pure function of its inputs, because ticks are replayed.

A new mob of `kind` joined `dimension` at `pos`: `natural` when the
world's spawning made it, false when something else did (a breed, a
raid, a spawner, a conversion, `/summon`, and the second mob of a
jockey the world spawned). One call a mob: a `/summon` with passengers
tells each. Not told of a mob loaded with its chunk, leaving a hive or
changing level. It only hears; the mob is already among the game's
mobs. Server-side.

A slime, magma cube or sulfur cube is dying and about to split into
smaller ones (NeoForge's `MobSplitEvent`, vanilla's
`AbstractCubeMob.remove`): `parent` is its entity id, `kind` its type,
`size` its size, `child_size` the size of the children (half of it)
and `count` how many vanilla made (2 to 4 for a slime or magma cube,
2 for a sulfur cube; a primed one makes none and isn't asked). A mod
may change `count` (0 spawns none, at most 64) or set `cancel` to
spawn no children. Only for a parent above size 1, once the child
count is drawn. NeoForge's list of child mobs is this count:
changing a child or adding one of another kind needs a handle to a
mob not yet in the world, which this hook does not expose. On the
server.

The number of players with the mod container at `pos` of `dimension`
open went from `previous` to `viewers` (vanilla's
`ContainerOpenersCounter`, as a barrel keeps it): 0 to more than 0 is
`onOpen`, back to 0 is `onClose`, any change `openerCountChanged`, so a
block can show itself open while `viewers` is not 0. Counted every
tick from the players' open menus, so a player who leaves without
closing (a lost connection, death, another dimension, out of reach, the
block gone) is heard too (`recheckOpeners`). Once for each change, with
no player's state swapped in. Server-side.

neoforge: none (vanilla ContainerOpenersCounter; NeoForge adds no event or extension for it); PlayerContainerEvent.Open and Close fire per player

hooks.doc:
A saved mod list (code and content mods) was read while opening a world. Fires
even when the list is empty or unchanged, never when absent, once per open.
Versions use the loader's comparison; minecraft is excluded. Newly added mods
are not differences. Push a mod id converted with `.into()` into `resolved`.
Dispatch assigns the first resolving listener and preserves earlier markers.
When a saved mod is no longer loaded, it fires before the world opens, on the
side that asks (the client in singleplayer, the dedicated server), and a
resolved id is taken off the question; otherwise it fires on the opening
server before world-state restoration, after preparation.

A mod's own equipment slot has changed: the committed notice, after
the mod wrote its stack. The fields are `mod_slot_will_change`'s
without `cancel`: `holder`, `slot`, `index`, `cosmetic`, `old`, `new`
and `source`, the caller's own hint about why (`equip`, `unequip`,
`reload`, `death` are the usual names; any string is accepted). The mod calls
`item::mod_slots::native_mod_slot_changed` with its host once its own
write is committed. Server-side; clients get the stacks from the mod's
own sync payload.

A mod's own equipment slot is about to change: the cancellable moment,
before the mod writes its stack. `holder` is the entity, `slot` the
bare slot id (`ring`), `index` the slot's index and `cosmetic` whether
it is a cosmetic copy. `old` and `new` are the stacks before and after
and `source` is the caller's own hint about why (`equip`, `unequip`,
`reload`, `death` are the usual names; any string is accepted). Set
`cancel` to refuse the change; listeners run by `#[listener(priority)]`.
The mod calls `item::mod_slots::native_mod_slot_will_change` with its
host from its own transaction; the game does not know these slots.
Server-side.

Every model of a resource load is baked and published (`ModelEvent.BakingCompleted`): the
block and item models and the standalone ones mods asked for (`standalone_models`), in the
store `model` now reads. Fires once per successful model load, after both
`texture_atlas_stitched` calls: on the first load before `client_setup`, and after every
successful resource reload (F3+T, a pack turned on or off, a server's pack) before
`client_resources_reloaded`; a reload that fails fires nothing, and the old handles stay
right. Look the models a mod draws up here, once, through `render_assets().model`, and
keep the `ModelRef`s until the next `model_baking_completed`, when the old ones answer
`ModelError::StaleModel`. Never look them up by name every frame. Client-side.

NeoForge's `ModifyCustomSpawnersEvent`: the level `dimension` is about to tick its custom
spawners for the first time. `spawners` is the list `ServerLevel` ticks, in order, and it
starts with vanilla's (`WanderingTrader`, `Patrol`, `Cat`, `VillageSiege` and `Phantom`,
in the order Horizon ticks them). Take a vanilla spawner out with `remove` and it never
ticks, so its random draws are gone with it; add a spawner of the mod's own with `add` and
a `SpawnerKey` the mod owns, and `custom_spawner_tick` runs for it every tick, after the
ones before it in the list. A key identifies the custom spawner
because an object a guest implements cannot cross to a wasm mod (Beyond NeoForge). With
no listener, or one that leaves the list alone, the level ticks exactly vanilla's
spawners. The phantom spawner runs after the level's mobs have ticked, as the game runs
it, wherever it is in the list. It fires once per level, on the server, and listeners run on replayed ticks,
so they must be pure functions of their inputs. Not cancellable.

NeoForge 26.3's ModifyDefaultComponentsEvent: set or remove entries in
`components`, the default component map for `item`, including vanilla items.
Asked once per item after registries freeze, before the owning load
publishes immutable defaults. Receives a read-only DataLoadContext with
the actual ServerDataLoad or ClientPreload origin, frozen registry names,
settings captured once for loaded packages at this load boundary, and
the shared LoadedMods view. Readers and datapack reloads do not replay
this event. No runtime Host, world handles or transaction access.

Farmland at `pos` is about to change moisture from `from` to `to`.
Set `cancel` to keep its old moisture. Server-side.
An accepted raw button event finished dispatch, including a screen handler's early return.

Raw mouse button input on any screen, before dispatch; cancel skips dispatch and Post.
Button/modifiers use the same GLFW encoding as screen hooks. Synthetic clicks skip it.

Gameplay scrolling after accumulation, before hotbar/spectator handling.
`scroll` is scaled x/y, `accumulated` whole x/y steps, `buttons` left/middle/right,
and `cursor` the GUI position. Cancel skips gameplay scrolling.

Local player movement input, after reading it and before applying it.
All seven keys are independent; opposing direction keys cancel. If any
direction key changes, its keyboard direction replaces axis edits and
controller input. Otherwise axis edits stand and update packet flags.
With enabled listeners, false sprint holds sprint off this tick (even a
passive listener's unchanged false); true requests vanilla eligibility.
Without enabled listeners, vanilla latch, double tap and input are unchanged.

Choose this client's music, once a client tick: `music` and `volume`
hold what vanilla chose (`Minecraft.getSituationalMusic` and
`getMusicVolume`: the biome's track, the creative or underwater one, a
boss's, the menu's; None for silence). Set `music` to a track of your
own, a sound event of your content mod's `sounds.json` such as
`Music::new("mymod:music.spring", 1200, 6000, false)` (the delays in
ticks between songs, and whether it cuts off a different song playing),
None to keep vanilla's quiet, or change `volume` (0 to 1) to fade it.

The tracks to play over (or instead of) the music on this client,
asked once a client tick: push a `MusicLayer` (a sound event, looped,
and its volume, 0 to 1) for each. A layer eases to a new volume over up
to two seconds, and one left out fades out and stops; layers that
first appear in the same tick start together, so list every stem of a
piece from the start, the silent ones at volume 0, and raise them (a
fuller arrangement as a village grows). Their sound events should be
`stream: true` in `sounds.json`.

neoforge: none (SelectMusicEvent swaps the one track; NeoForge has no layered music)

hooks.doc:
An authoritative server is about to deliver `neighborChanged`.
State and block IDs are valid in this level's registries for this call.
The host is the level with its ticks, as vanilla's `neighborChanged` gets the
level: a part may read its inputs (`signal`, `has_neighbor_signal`) and
schedule its tick here, as a diode does (`DiodeBlock.checkTickOnNeighbor`).

neoforge: none (vanilla Block.neighborChanged; NeoForge adds no event or extension for it); BlockEvent.NeighborNotifyEvent is the neighbour broadcast, a different point

hooks.doc:
The block at `pos` (`state`) is about to tell its neighbours it
changed (NeoForge's `BlockEvent.NeighborNotifyEvent`): at
`ServerLevel.updateNeighborsAt`, which notifies all six sides
(`skipped_side` is `None`), and `updateNeighborsAtExceptFromFacing`,
which notifies all but `skipped_side`. Set `cancel` and no neighbour
hears, on both paths. Asked for every such update, redstone
included: answer fast. Server-side.

A player is tuning a note block on the authoritative server, not in
client prediction. `context` gives its dimension, position, instrument
and old note; `new_note` starts as vanilla's cycled note. Set it to 0
through 24; an out-of-range value keeps vanilla's. Cancel to leave the
note unchanged and prevent playback.

The note block at `pos` is about to play (NeoForge's
`NoteBlockEvent.Play`, in `NoteBlock.playNote`), once a block above
no longer mutes it. `player` and `player_entity_id` name the player
who tuned or punched it, and are `None` for redstone.
`instrument` is its instrument and `note` its note, 0 to 24; change
either to play another (a note out of range keeps the block's own).
Set `cancel` and it doesn't play: no sound, no particle, no
`note_block_play` game event. Server-side.

An explosion destroys this block, before removal and while its live block
entity is readable. Writes are allowed; the engine still replaces the cell
with air afterwards, including a replacement written by the part.

`BlockItemExtension.onBlockPlacedBy`: this item's block has been placed,
its final block state and stack block-entity data applied, and
`Block.setPlacedBy` completed (including companion blocks). Runs once,
at the primary position, before sounds, level events and stack consumption.
`stack` is the pre-shrink stack; `placer` is the placing player, or None
for a dispenser. `face` and `click` are the placement context's clicked
face and world-space hit point. Failed, refused and canceled placements
never notify. Only Parts attached to the stack's item hear this server notice.

A write through `Level.setBlock` held and the block at `pos` changed from `old` to
`new` (`IBlockExtension.onBlockStateChange`), heard at the end of the write, where
vanilla runs `updatePOIOnBlockStateChange`: after the block-entity removal, `on_place`,
the client update, the neighbour updates and the neighbours' shape updates. The parts
of `old`'s block hear it, then, when the block changed, the parts of `new`'s block;
`state` is the state whose block's parts are asked. A write that `on_place` replaced
with another block is not heard; the write that replaced it is. Heard on both sides:
a server's writes, a client's replay of a piston's move and the blocks a client takes
from the server (`LevelSide` names which). Applied local predictions are heard at once
with `predicted: true`; server writes, settled corrections and all server-side writes
have `predicted: false`. A held server update is unheard until acknowledgement; a
confirmed prediction is not heard twice, and a denial hears predicted-to-server once.
Equal-state writes and unapplied guesses are not heard. The level is read-only.
A panicking part is contained. With no listener, one flag check builds nothing.
Diverges from upstream: new hook.

On an authoritative server, a neighbour of fire passed its burn roll.
`state` is still at `pos`; `face` points toward the fire. The spread,
burn and (when replacing with fire) ignite cancel gates run first.
The listener may write or schedule ticks, but the pending fire/air
replacement overwrites any write at `pos`, then TNT is primed.
Fire spread has no igniter and an empty stack, so neither is passed.
Lava, lightning, spread into air, flint and steel, TNT use, burning
projectiles, redstone and dispensers are outside this spread-only hook.

The chunk holding this mod block entity is unloading
(`IBlockEntityExtension.onChunkUnloaded`): told once for each of its
mod block entities, on each side that holds a copy of it, before the
copy is dropped. `pos` is where it stands, `block_entity` its handle (the
one `host.block_entity` gave while it was loaded) and `entity` its data.
Release what your mod keeps for it here. On a server its chunk may have
left the level already, so don't count on the handle's reads. As
with `chunk_unload`, changes made in it aren't saved: the chunk
was saved before it unloads. Not told when the world closes, or on a
client when its level goes (a respawn, a dimension change, leaving).

A player removes the block `state` at `pos` (`IBlockExtension.onDestroyedByPlayer`, where
`ServerPlayerGameMode.destroyBlock` runs `playerWillDestroy` and removes the block), with
`tool`, the stack in the player's hand (`None` for a bare hand), and `will_harvest`, whether
the break will drop loot as far as the tool goes (never in creative, and false for a tool the
block refuses). Asked after `break_block` allowed the break, before anything of the break
changes the world. `will_harvest` is the tool's own answer; the mods' harvest listeners
(`can_harvest_block`, then `player_harvest_check`) are asked once, after the removal, of the
adjusted state and the stack in the hand then, as vanilla reads `hasCorrectToolForDrops`.
`destroyed` is whether the
block was actually destroyed: `Some(true)` says the part removed it itself, `Some(false)`
that it stays (a block of layers losing one layer: change it with the `host` and leave it
standing), and either answer replaces the game's own `playerWillDestroy` (a pot's cracking,
piglin anger, a tripwire's disarming, a creative shulker box's or beehive's drop) and
removal. `Some(false)` ends the break there: no drops, tool wear or statistic. Left `None`,
vanilla's removal runs. Server-side, for every player of the world; the first part answering
wins. Asked of the block's own parts only, so a block with none costs nothing.

On an authoritative server, a piston's move destroys the block `state` at `pos`
(`IBlockExtension.onDestroyedByPushReaction`), `direction` the way the blocks move and
`fluid` the fluid state the cell holds.
It is heard in `PistonBaseBlock.moveBlocks` after the block dropped its resources and
while it is still in its cell, before the cell becomes air. The removal still happens:
a write to `pos` is overwritten, and so is a write to any other cell of the move (the
other destroyed cells, the pushed blocks and the cells they move into, the arm), since
the pushed blocks were read before the destroy loop. Writes elsewhere stay; `ticks`
is the move's, so scheduled ticks stay too. A cancelled move (`piston_pre`) and a
client's replay of the move are not heard. A panicking part is contained. With no part
attached to the state, the cost is one table lookup per destroyed block. Diverges from
upstream: new hook; the removal is not replaceable here.

`IItemExtension.onDroppedByPlayer`: `player` (the acting player's
handle) pressed the drop key on `stack`, the whole selected stack
before anything leaves it; `all` is true when the whole stack goes,
false for one item (`ServerPlayer.drop(boolean)`). Set `canceled` and
the stack stays in the slot: nothing is taken out, no item entity is
made, no drop statistic is awarded and `item_toss` does not fire; a
server's player is sent the slot back, undoing their predicted drop.
Not asked for a menu's throw, nor for a spectator (who drops nothing).
Only the `ItemPart`s attached to `stack`'s item are asked: an item
with none costs one table lookup. Server-side, with a read-only `Host`.

`MobEffect.onEffectAdded`: `LivingEntity.addEffect` gave `entity`
(as in `native_apply_effect_tick`) the content mod's effect `effect`,
which it didn't have. Server-side.

neoforge: none (vanilla MobEffect.onEffectAdded; NeoForge adds no event or extension for it)

hooks.doc:
`IItemExtension.onEntityItemUpdate`: each tick of a dropped item
entity holding `stack`, before the entity's own tick (`ItemEntity.tick`:
its fluids, movement, pickup delay, merging and lifetime), and after
`entity_tick_pre`. `item` is the entity, in the world: read and change
it through the host, its attachments included. Set `canceled` to skip
that tick's vanilla work, as NeoForge's `true` return does; the item
skips movement and its own merge pass; another item can still merge into it.\n    /// `entity_tick_post` still hears it.
Only the `ItemPart`s attached to `stack`'s item hear it: an item with
none costs one table lookup, and a game with no such part none at all.
Server-side, for every dropped item that ticks.

`IItemExtension.onEntitySwing`: the player in place (`entity`, its
`Entity.getId` when known) is about to swing `stack` in `hand`:
where `LivingEntity.swing` starts, for an attack, a use or a swing the
server asked for. Set `canceled` and no swing starts: no animation and
no swing packet. Only the `ItemPart`s attached to `stack`'s item are
asked. Both sides, as vanilla's: answer the same on both, and change
the world only where this `Game` runs the world, not on a server's
client.

A player's equipment slot `slot` (`head`, `chest`, `legs`, `feet`,
`offhand`, and `mainhand` on a swap of the hands or `/item`) took a different
item, `new` (none when it was emptied): `LivingEntity.onEquipItem`,
before the equip sound. It only hears. Never for a spectator.
Server-side, for every player of the world (the helpers read the
acting one).

`IItemExtension.onItemUseFirst`: the held item's first say on a
click on a block, on the server for each player, after
`use_item_on_block` (`ItemBeforeBlock`) let it through and before the
block's own `useItemOn`. An answer ends the click: neither the block
nor the item's `useOn` runs. `Pass` goes on to the block.

`IItemExtension.onLeftClickEntity`: `player` (the acting player's
UUID), holding `stack` in the main hand, is about to attack the entity
`entity` (`Entity.getId`) of type `kind` (`minecraft:cow`,
`minecraft:player`, `minecraft:item_frame`): where `Player.attack`
starts, once the global `attack_entity` let the blow through and
before any damage, knockback, enchantment effect, `hurt_enemy` or the
weapon's wear. Set `canceled` and the attack ends there: the target
is not hurt, `hurt_enemy` does not fire and the stack takes no wear.
Only the `ItemPart`s attached to `stack`'s item are asked. Server-side,
for every player of the world (the helpers read the acting one).
A neighbouring block entity changed, was created or removed. Vanilla comparator processing runs first.

A trunk placer is about to place the block under its trunk at `pos`, where the soil
`state` this part is attached to stands (`IBlockExtension.onTreeGrow`, asked from
`TrunkPlacer.placeBelowTrunkBlock`). Answer `Some(Some(state))` to place `state` there
through the tree's trunk setter, `Some(None)` to place nothing, or `None` to leave it to the
tree's `below_trunk_provider` (vanilla's trees place dirt unless the soil is in
`#minecraft:cannot_replace_below_tree_trunk`). A part that answers skips the provider and
its draws. Asked once per trunk, four times for the 2×2 trunks (giant, mega jungle, dark
oak). Draw only from `event.random`, the tree's own: your draws fall between the tree's, in
call order. Server-side, on the worldgen worker threads and on the server thread when a
sapling grows, with the server's worldgen `context`: no `Host`, no writes. NeoForge's
`feature` argument is left out: an inline tree feature has no key. Diverges from upstream:
new hook.

`Item.onUseTick` of `stack`, used by `entity` with `remaining` ticks
left, always above 0: what a mod's own item does each tick it is used
(cook, charge, drain). It comes where `ItemStack.onUseTick` calls the
item, once `living_entity_use_item_tick` let the use go on:
after a consumable's crumbs, for consumables, shields and mods' items
(vanilla's other items do their own, and a kinetic weapon has none on
the server). Both sides, as `living_entity_use_item_tick`:
change the world only where this `Game` runs the world, not on a
server's client. Runs every tick of every use: check the item first.

The player did `event` on mod `mod_id`'s panel (`native_panel_items`):
act on it when it is yours.

`BonemealableBlock.performBonemeal` for a block that answered
`is_valid_bonemeal_target` and whose `is_bonemeal_success`
said yes: grow it here, `state` its state at `pos`. The meal is used up
either way. Change the block with the level's
`native_set_block_property`, and schedule with `native_schedule_block_tick`
(`ticks` is the hook's). Authoritative servers only.

neoforge: none (vanilla BonemealableBlock.performBonemeal; NeoForge adds no event or extension for it)

hooks.doc:
NeoForge's `PermissionsChangedEvent`: the operator list is about to give player
`player` (`name`) the permission level `new` in place of `old`, through `PlayerList.op`
(`/op`, the console's `op`, the management API's `operators/add` and `operators/set`)
or `PlayerList.deop` (`/deop` and the same on the console and the management API;
`new` is then `All`). Set `cancel` and the list keeps the old level. The player need
not be online: `player_entity_id` is their server entity id when they are. Clearing
the list (`operators/clear`) is not a call to either, as in vanilla. Dedicated
servers only; a single-player world has no operator list. Server-side.

Before `player` picks up orb `orb` in `dimension`. Mutations to `value`
and `count` take effect only when not canceled; value is clamped to
1..=i32::MAX and count to at least one.
Canceling leaves the orb and pickup delay unchanged. Server-side. Diverges from upstream: renamed from `experience_orb_pickup`, to NeoForge's `PlayerXpEvent.PickupXp`.

Whether a piston carries your block `state` at `pos` with its block
entity: asked at the last step of `PistonBaseBlock.isPushable`, after
the block's push reaction, for a block that is otherwise pushable,
whenever a piston's structure takes the block in. Left `None`, vanilla's
rule holds: a block with a block entity does not move, and any other
block does. `Some(false)` keeps the block in place at that position.
`Some(true)` lets a piston move it even with a block entity, which
travels with the block: taken out of the world as the move starts, with
its saved data and its attachments and without its removal side effects
(nothing drops), and put where the block lands as a new block entity of
that position, with a new ticker slot; a handle to the old position no
longer resolves. If the moving block is replaced before it lands, the
block entity is removed there as a broken block's is (a container drops
its contents). A save mid-move keeps it in the moving piston's tag. A
block entity, including a chest, moves only after its reaction permits movement
and this hook answers true. While the block moves it draws as its state, without its
block entity's drawing. Asked on both sides, as a client replays the
move on its own copy: answer the same on both, from the arguments,
without touching the world. Only attached block parts are asked; blocks
without a subscribed part pay only the dispatch guards. A block that only needs to move or not, or
to be popped or pushed only, is the push reaction's question, asked
before this one. The order is reaction first, then this shared block-entity
rule for push-pull, ignore-entity and push only; a wrong-direction push-only
answer refuses before this hook. Popped destroys and drops without asking it.
This hook is asked only for an otherwise-pushable block. A live owned payload
is required: data-only or unmaterialized vanilla entities remain refused.
Diverges from vanilla: push only never discards a block entity.
NeoForge has no counterpart: its
`IBlockExtension.getRelocability` is an unrelated region-copy query that
pistons do not ask. Diverges from upstream: new hook.

neoforge: none (NeoForge has no counterpart; IBlockExtension.getRelocability is unrelated)

hooks.doc:
On an authoritative server, the piston at `piston` pushed the blocks at
`push` one step `direction` (`[0, 1, 0]` is up; pulling when it
retracts, `extending` false) and destroyed those at `destroy`
(NeoForge's `PistonEvent.Post`, at the end of `PistonBaseBlock.moveBlocks`,
after the neighbour updates). It only hears; `piston_pre` is the veto.
Server-side. Diverges from upstream: `piston_move` is split into
`piston_pre` and `piston_post`.

On an authoritative server, the piston at `piston` is about to push
the blocks at `push` one step `direction` (`[0, 1, 0]` is up; pulling
when it retracts, `extending` false) and destroy those at `destroy`
(NeoForge's `PistonEvent.Pre`, in `PistonBaseBlock.moveBlocks`, once its
structure resolved). Set
`canceled` and nothing moves, as when the structure can't; a sticky
piston then retracts without its block, and clients are sent the
blocks rather than the retraction to replay. Diverges from upstream: `piston_move` is renamed to
`piston_pre`, and `piston_post` is new.

Resolve a state's piston reaction at load and reload on both sides. None keeps the
properties' reaction. Answers must depend only on state. Unbreakable blocks still
refuse movement. The reaction is checked first; push-pull, ignore-entity and push only
then reach the shared block-entity rule. An otherwise-pushable block with a block entity
moves only when `piston_carries_block_entity` answers true, using the carry machinery
to move its data and attachments without drops. No answer or false refuses the move.
Popped remains destruction with ordinary drops, and never asks the carries hook.
The carries hook is asked only for an otherwise-pushable block. Carrying also requires
a live owned payload; raw-only or currently borrowed native payloads remain refused.
Diverges from vanilla: push only never discards a block entity.

Asked before a mining hit sound, including the initial hit, every fourth breaking
tick, and the level-event route. Return Flow::Cancel when the part handled the
sound through ClientHost and vanilla should stay silent.
Otherwise vanilla plays the state's hit sound at (volume + 1) / 8 and pitch * 0.5.
The position and face identify the current hit; sculk growth is outside this hook.

A sound bound to `entity` is about to play (NeoForge's
`PlayLevelSoundEvent.AtEntity`, in `Level.playSeededSound`'s entity
overload, `playSound(except, sourceEntity, ...)`): a goat horn, a frog's
tongue, eating and spawn, an animal eating (frog, goat, sniffer), a long
jump, a goat's ram, a breeze's charge and deflection, shearing (sheep,
mooshroom, snow golem, bogged, copper golem), dye on a sheep, an axe on a
copper golem, an allay's item and duplication, a ghastling hatching, a
trident thrown (the trident) or riptide (the player), and a mod's sound
bound to an entity. Asked after the tick's other sounds. The fields and
their rules are `play_level_sound_at_position`'s. Client entity-sound
packets ask before playback and keep following their emitter; an absent
emitter plays nothing. `LocalPlayer.playSound` also asks this hook,
including steps, falls, hurt, bundle clicks and consumption; these remain
positional sounds, not following sounds. Both sides, distinguished by `HostSide`.

A sound is about to play at `position` in `level` (NeoForge's
`PlayLevelSoundEvent.AtPosition`, in `Level.playSeededSound`):
every server sound not bound to an entity, mobs' own sounds included
(`Entity.playSound` plays at the entity's position). A mod may change
`sound`, `source`, `volume` and `pitch`, or set `cancel` and no player
hears it; `original_volume` and `original_pitch` are as asked. A sound
left unplayable (a volume or pitch that isn't finite and at least 0)
is dropped. Sounds the server's level plays during
the tick are asked as they go out, at the end of the tick, with the state
then. `/playsound` sends its packet directly and isn't asked, as in
vanilla on the server. On the client, incoming sound packets ask before
playback, including `/playsound`; client-predicted and game-event level
requests ask here too. Canceling a sound does not cancel its action or prediction.
Server and client requests are separate:
`HostSide` identifies which one is being edited. UI and sound-engine-only
playback do not ask this hook. Both sides.

`starting` is true for starts and loop replays, false for a live channel refresh.
A live refresh applies only volume and pitch transiently; `None` stops the channel.
Invalid edited numeric values refuse that refresh.
A sound is about to play (`PlaySoundEvent`, vanilla's `SoundEngine.play`): `original` is the sound as asked for, `sound` starts as a copy of it. Edit `sound` (its volume, pitch, source, position, identifier, looping, delay, attenuation or relativeness) to change what plays, or set it to `None` to play nothing. It is asked before the engine's own checks (output open, sound resolved, volume, channel pool), for every sound the client plays, so answer fast; later mods see earlier mods' edits in `sound` and the sound as asked for in `original`. A new `identifier` is resolved again, with its own weighted pick. `context` is the client's `LoopContext`: no game is at hand inside the sound engine. Client-side only; a server has no sound.
`instance` is an engine-local sound instance id, unchanged across its live updates.

A sound that is not streamed has started on `channel` (`PlaySoundSourceEvent`), after the engine set its pitch, volume, attenuation, looping and position: `sound` is what is playing, after `play_sound`'s edits. A notice: the channel is an id only and gives no control. Streamed sounds (music, records) fire `play_streaming_source` instead. Client-side only.

A streamed sound (music, a record) has started on `channel` (`PlayStreamingSourceEvent`): `sound` is what is playing, after `play_sound`'s edits. A notice: the channel is an id only and gives no control. Other sounds fire `play_sound_source` instead. Client-side only.
A server player completed an advancement, after progress was recorded.

A criterion of a server player's advancement was granted or revoked, after its progress changed
and before any completion rewards. A grant or revoke that changes nothing is not heard.
`progress` is an owned snapshot of every criterion (including its stored grant date),
the requirement groups and their completion at this exact mutation. It belongs to
the mutated progress, including first-tick and reload grants queued by the server hub.
During a nested player turn, a suspended player's hub record may contain displaced
progress. A listener may retain a clone; later mutations do not change the snapshot.
A guest's arm swing was handled by the server. `hand` is `mainhand`. Server-side.

neoforge: none (NeoForge has no such event; Bukkit's PlayerAnimationEvent)

hooks.doc:
A server player reset their attack strength by swinging (`handlePunch`). The swing and reset
have already happened. The player's state is not swapped in. Server-side.

A server player is about to enter a bed after the sleep checks pass. Set `cancel` to keep them
out. The player's state is swapped in.

neoforge: none (NeoForge has no such event; Bukkit's PlayerBedEnterEvent)

hooks.doc:
`PlayerWakeUpEvent`: a server player is getting out of the bed at
`pos` (`Player.stopSleepInBed`), heard first, while they still read
as sleeping there. `wake_immediately` is vanilla's flag for skipping
the wake-up fade: generic stop-sleeping, death and bed-missing wakes
pass true; morning, explicit leave and bed-rule refusal pass false.
`update_level` is false for morning, true for those individual wakes.
A player's destroy speed for the block at `pos` may be changed or canceled.

A server player took `stack` from a brewing stand bottle slot
(`BrewingStandMenu.PotionSlot.onTake`): `player` is their UUID and
`player_entity_id` their network id.

A server player caught a mob in a bucket, after it was removed and the filled bucket was given.
Server-side.

A server player selected a bundle item in `slot` at `index`. The guest's
state is not swapped in during packet handling.

neoforge: none (NeoForge has no such event; Bukkit's PlayerBundleItemSelect)

hooks.doc:
A server player changed a beacon's selected effects, after they were stored. Each selected
effect is an `Option<EffectKey>`; None means no effect. Server-side.

`player` (`name`) changed dimension (NeoForge's
`PlayerChangedDimensionEvent`): `from` and `to` are dimension ids
(`minecraft:overworld`, `minecraft:the_nether`, `minecraft:the_end`).
Heard once per move, when it has ended: the portal's exit is found
and the player stands there (after the destination has loaded), a
command's teleport has landed, or a respawn in another level than the
death's is placed for good (a bed or anchor, or the world spawn's
free column, after the fallback when a respawn block was gone). The
level of `to` is the one in place, and the player's state is swapped
in, as for `run_mod_command`: `host.players().acting_player()`,
`PlayerRef::tell`, the item helpers and the rest reach them. Heard for:
Nether and End portals (also riding a vehicle, and leaving the End as
its winner), `/execute in ... run tp` and any other command that
teleports a player into another level, and the death respawn, on a
dedicated server and on the integrated server of single player and
LAN. Not heard by a remote client window; listeners run on the server that simulates the world.
Not heard: a move within a level (`/tp`, an End gateway), a
player who leaves before the move ends, and a move that ends where it
started (a respawn in the dimension of the death).

A server player finished loading the world around them after joining, respawning or changing
dimension. The guest's state is not swapped in. Server-side.

neoforge: none (NeoForge has no such event; Bukkit's PlayerClientLoadedWorld)

hooks.doc:
A player's data was copied to their new player (NeoForge's
`PlayerEvent.Clone`, from `ServerPlayer.restoreFrom`): `was_death` is
true after a death, false when they left the End after the credits
(`respawn` with `keepAllPlayerData`). `original` is a hook-scoped view
of the old player's attachments (all types), inventory, position and
level. `player` is the replacement's UUID. Heard before placement on
a server, without swapping a player's state in. Not cancellable.

A command a player typed (NeoForge's `CommandEvent`, before
`Commands.performCommand` runs it), without its slash: any command,
vanilla's and the mods' own, also one the player may not run. Set
`canceled` to stop it: nothing runs and nothing is answered but the
lines pushed to `replies`, which go to the player as system chat.
No player's state is swapped in and the server's player list is busy
with this one, so `PlayerRef::tell` and the other player helpers
reach nobody here: answer through `replies`. Once for each command a
player sends, on a server, and for each line of a quiet command batch
(`horizon:quiet_commands`, whose replies are dropped). A command the
server refuses before reading it (unsigned chat arguments, the chat
rate limit) never reaches it.

The command tree a server sends a player (NeoForge's and Paper's
"commands sent to a player" stage): when they join and when their
level changes (`/op`, `/deop`, the LAN settings). `names` are the
root commands their client would get, vanilla's they may use and the
mods'; take a name out and that client gets the tree without it
(and without what it leads to), so it neither completes nor
highlights it. This hides the command from the client only: the
server still runs a typed one, `player_command` stops it.
For a player who is already on, their state is swapped in and the
helpers (`PlayerRef::tell`...) work; for one who is joining it is not, and
their client has no world to tell yet. The tree the hub sends again by
itself (after a respawn or a change of level) keeps the last answer
and does not ask again; the integrated server's owner is not asked
when the world's cheats are switched.

`player` (`name`) closed the menu `player_container_open` told
of (NeoForge's `PlayerContainerEvent.Close`, posted in
`ServerPlayer.doCloseContainer` after the menu's `removed`): they
closed it, walked out of reach, died, changed level, or another menu
opened. A player who leaves closes it before `player_logged_out`
(vanilla posts nothing for a disconnect; Horizon does, so each open has
its close). Once for each open; not told when the server stops. The
menu's items are where it left them: the block's, and the cursor stack
back in the inventory. State swapped in, when the player has a body.
Server-side.

`player` (`name`) opened a menu (NeoForge's `PlayerContainerEvent.Open`,
posted when `ServerPlayer.openMenu` sets the new `containerMenu`): any
menu, vanilla or a mod's. `menu` is the menu type's name
(`minecraft:generic_9x3`, `minecraft:furnace`, `minecraft:merchant`,
`minecraft:crafting`, `minecraft:lectern`, a mod's own), `pos` the
block it is of in `dimension` (none for a trade, a vehicle's, a mod's
native menu or a mount's inventory, which has no menu type in vanilla
and is told as `horizon:mount_inventory`). The player's own inventory
is not one, nor is failed construction. Heard synchronously after construction, the open packet
is queued and full contents sent, with the new menu already current.
Replacing a menu follows its close; even inside one tick, open precedes
`player_container_close`. The player's state is swapped in. Server-side.

A server player has slept for 100 ticks in a bed and now counts as deeply asleep for the
night-skip check.

The item `item` of the server player `player` (`name`) broke in `slot`
(`mainhand`, `offhand`, `head`, `chest`, `legs`, `feet`, `body` or
`saddle`): `LivingEntity.onEquippedItemBroken`, Bukkit's
`PlayerItemBreakEvent`. Listen only; armour has a slot, not a hand.
The player's state is swapped in. Once for each break, on a server; a
creative player and the host of a LAN world are not heard.

neoforge: none (NeoForge's PlayerDestroyItemEvent carries the original stack and a hand, which armour has not; this hook only listens and names the slot instead. Bukkit's PlayerItemBreakEvent)

hooks.doc:
A player's break removed the block `state` from `pos`: the
`Block.destroy(level, pos, state)` call `ServerPlayerGameMode.destroyBlock` makes only
after `Level.removeBlock` succeeded, before a creative player's return and `playerDestroy`'s
drops. `state` is the block the removal took out, read just before it: what
`playerWillDestroy` left there (a cracked decorated pot; a disarmed tripwire, where vanilla
passes `Block.destroy` the armed one) or what a `break_block` listener put there.
`block_entity` is the saved data of the block entity that stood at `pos`
(`BlockEntity.saveWithoutMetadata`, read with `state`), none for a block without one;
the entity itself is gone from the level by now, so a live handle would be stale. The
level is writable. Server-side, for every player of the world: the helpers read the
acting one. Not heard for a break `break_block` canceled, nor for a break the level
makes (a piston, water, an explosion).

neoforge: none (NeoForge has no event for Block.destroy; BreakEvent fires before the removal)

hooks.doc:
`player` died: where `ServerPlayer.die` starts, with the death
message's key when the game knows it (`death.attack.lava`; none for a
message it builds from the combat). It only hears. Server-side, for
every player of the world, whether death messages are shown or not.

A server player's book edit or signing packet is about to be applied. `pages` is its page
count; `signing` means the packet has a title. Set `cancel` to drop the edit.

neoforge: none (NeoForge has no such event; Bukkit's PlayerEditBookEvent)

hooks.doc:
A server player threw an egg, after its projectile was launched and the use was applied.
Server-side.

A server player used a firework rocket to boost while gliding, after the rocket was launched
and consumed. Server-side.

A server player enchanted `item` at an enchanting table
(`EnchantmentMenu.clickMenuButton`): `enchantments` are the ones it was
given, in order, as (id, level). `item` is the enchanted stack (an
enchanted book for a book). Fires after the levels are paid, before
`enchant_item`. Server-side.

A server player's XP orb pickup cooldown changed to `ticks`. It is
reported after the value changes. Server-side.

A server player's fishing rod, with `state`: 0 the cast
(`FishingRodItem.use` throwing the bobber), 1 a fish biting
(`FishingHook.catchingFish`), 2 the reel-in of a bite, which gives the
catch, 3 the reel-in with nothing on the line, 4 the reel-in of a
bobber hooked to an entity or item (like Bukkit's `PlayerFishEvent`;
NeoForge's `ItemFishedEvent` is later, in `FishingHook.retrieve`). Set `cancel` on the cast and nothing
is thrown; on a bite the fish gets away and the wait starts over; on
a reel-in (2 to 4) nothing happens, the bobber stays out and the rod
takes no wear. The bobber ending by itself (too far, the rod put
away, the owner dying), nor the host of a LAN world's rod. The
player's state is swapped in, so `host.players().acting_player()`, `PlayerRef::tell`
and the item helpers reach them. Once for each cast, bite and reel-in,
on a server.

neoforge: none (NeoForge's ItemFishedEvent fires after the loot roll, in FishingHook.retrieve; Bukkit's PlayerFishEvent)

hooks.doc:
A server player put a plant into a flower pot, after the potted block state was stored and the
item consumed. `plant` is the item id and `pos` the pot position. Server-side.

NeoForge's `PlayerFlyableFallEvent`: server player `player` (`name`) landed after
falling `distance` blocks at damage multiplier `multiplier` while allowed to fly (a
creative or spectator player walking), so `Player.causeFallDamage` returned early
and nothing was hurt. Listen only. Once for each landing, after the fall's
block reaction. The player's state is swapped in. Server-side.

A server player's game mode is about to change (NeoForge's
`PlayerChangeGameModeEvent`): from `from` to `to`, both the shared
`GameMode` used by commands and `PlayerRef`. `player` is the UUID and
`name` the name. Heard for
the `/gamemode` command, the F3+F4 switcher's packet and a hardcore
world's respawn into spectator, once for each change to a different
mode; not for the world's default mode a player joins with. Set `to`
to send the player to another mode instead: listeners run in order and
each sees the mode the one before left. Return `Flow::Cancel`, or
leave `to` at the player's current mode, and the player keeps their
mode (nothing is sent, the command counts it as no change); the
command's message names the mode it asked for, as vanilla's does. For a change the game makes inside
a player's turn their state is swapped in; for the hardcore respawn
it is not.

The handshake of a connection that is about to log in or be
transferred in (Paper's `PlayerHandshakeEvent`), before the login
starts and before the protocol version, the proxy's forwarding, the
name, the whitelist or the bans are looked at. `host` is the server
address string the client sent, with whatever a proxy put after the
first NUL (a Bedrock bridge's encrypted player data, Forge's marker);
change it and the rest of the login and `PlayerRef::connect_address`
see the new text, so a mod may cut it back to the plain name. A `host`
longer than 32767 characters is cut at that length. `port` and
`protocol` are the client's own and cannot be changed; `address` is
the IP the connection comes from, empty for an integrated server's own
player (whose `host` is empty too). Set `cancel` to refuse the
connection: the client is disconnected before it logs in, with
`reason` (a plain "Disconnected" if it is left unset). Once for each
login or transfer connection, on a server, never for a status ping.
The hook runs on the server thread at the next tick: the connection
waits for it for 5 seconds and is refused when no answer comes. No
player exists yet, so the host's player helpers reach nobody.

neoforge: none (Bukkit's PlayerHandshakeEvent; NeoForge has no handshake event)

hooks.doc: A player's ability to harvest the block at `pos` may be changed.

Which hearts the local player's health bar draws this frame (NeoForge's
`PlayerHeartTypeEvent`, from `Gui.HeartType.forPlayer`): `kind` comes in as vanilla's pick
(poisoned, else withered, else frozen when fully frozen, else normal); set it to draw
another kind. Asked once a frame while the HUD draws the hearts (not in creative or
spectator, not under F1), before `health_hud`, whose `inputs.kind` carries the answer.
Only the heart sprites change: health, regeneration and the other rows stay vanilla's.
Client-side.
A guest sent the server's current `PlayerInput` flags, after they were applied to the hub. The guest's state is swapped in. Server-side.

neoforge: none (NeoForge has no such event; Bukkit's PlayerInputEvent)

hooks.doc:
A server player inserted a book into a lectern, after the block entity and inventory changed.
`book` is the item id. Server-side.

`player_inventory_changed(player, stacks)`: a server player's inventory changed, at the moment vanilla's `InventoryChangeTrigger` is checked (the per-tick check found another item or count in a slot), heard before any criterion and whether or not the tree has `inventory_changed` advancements. `stacks` are the 41 slots in `Inventory` numbering: 0..36 the main inventory (0..9 the hotbar), 36..40 the armour (feet, legs, chest, head), 40 the off hand. It also fires at a player's first check after joining, so a mod sees what they log in with. The player's state is swapped in, so the helpers read that player. Single player, LAN guests and a dedicated server's players; never on a client of a remote server. Quest, collection and 'obtain an item' mods need it instead of polling every inventory. Bundles need "hooks": @API:player_inventory_changed@.

neoforge: none (vanilla InventoryChangeTrigger; NeoForge adds no event)

hooks.doc:
An item cooldown is about to start for a server player. `item` is the item id and `ticks` its
duration. The player's state is not swapped in. Set `cancel` to skip starting the cooldown.
Server-side.

neoforge: none (NeoForge has no such event; Paper's PlayerItemCooldownEvent)

hooks.doc:
A server player changed an item frame after its contents or rotation changed. `action` is
`put`, `rotate`, `remove_item` or `break`; `item` is empty when no item remains, and `rotation`
is the resulting step. Server-side.

Mending repaired a server player's item with experience from an orb. `repair` is durability
restored and `experience` is the orb's value. Server-side.

`PlayerEvent.ItemSmithedEvent`: a server player took `result` from a
smithing table (`SmithingMenu.onTake`, or `onQuickCraft` for a
shift-click): `player` is their UUID and `player_entity_id` their
network id, `inputs` the template, base and addition as they were
before the take used them (`None` for an empty slot). It comes once the click is done, so the
menu already holds the used inputs, but before the table sounds.
Server-side.
A guest's accepted movement made the server jump them from the ground. Server-side.

neoforge: none (NeoForge has no such event; Bukkit's PlayerJumpEvent)

hooks.doc:
A network or fake guest was kicked, after the hub recorded the rendered `reason`. The guest's state is
swapped in unless they were already removed in the same poll.

neoforge: none (NeoForge has no such event; Bukkit's PlayerKickEvent)

hooks.doc:
A server player launched a projectile item, after it was created.
`item` is the projectile's held item.

neoforge: none (NeoForge has no such event; Bukkit's PlayerLaunchProjectile)

hooks.doc:
`player` (`name`) is about to leave, with the plain-text `reason` the
connection ended with (a kick's reason, `Disconnected`, `Timed out`, or
`Server closed` when the server stops). Heard before the player is
removed: they are still in `host.players().server_players()` and in
their level, their state is swapped in, and their inventory, open menu
and carried stack are untouched, so a listener can read or clear the
inventory, drop items, kill or send them a last message; what it does
is part of what is saved. Once for each placed network player, before
`player_logged_out`. A fake player and a player held before the
join was announced are not told of, nor is a player whose transfer to
another server is unresolved or committed: their state may already
belong there, so nothing done here could travel with them. A kick is heard by `player_kicked`
first; `player_disconnect` of the leaving player refuses, whatever ended the
connection.
Server-side.

neoforge: none (NeoForge's PlayerLoggedOutEvent is fired after the player is removed from the list; the hook listens at Bukkit's PlayerQuitEvent point)

hooks.doc:
A server player changed the page of a lectern, after its page and redstone pulse changed.
`page` is the zero-based new page. Server-side.
A server player's experience level changed, after the new level was applied.

neoforge: none (NeoForge has no such event; Bukkit's PlayerLevelChangeEvent)

hooks.doc:
A player was loaded from the world's save (NeoForge's
`PlayerEvent.LoadFromFile`, `PlayerList.loadPlayerData`): their `.dat`
has been read and applied, and they are not placed in a level yet.
`directory` is the world's player directory (`players/data`): a mod
reads its own file there, named `<uuid>.<suffix>` as
`getPlayerFile(suffix)` names it. Heard once for each join, for the
owner of an integrated server as for anyone else, on a server, with no
player's state swapped in. Not cancellable.

Not on wasm: it gives a path in the game's file system, which a wasm mod has none of; a wasm mod keeps a player's data in attachments.

`player` (`name`) joined the game (NeoForge's
`PlayerLoggedInEvent`): placed in the world and listed in
`host.players().server_players()`, so `PlayerRef::send_payload` reaches them.
Once a join, with no player's state swapped in. Server-side.

`player` (`name`) left the game (NeoForge's `PlayerLoggedOutEvent`), by
any path: a lost connection, a kick, the server stopping or failing.
Once for each player `player_logged_in` told of, and also for a kicked
fake player without a preceding login. Silent `remove_fake` sends no logout.
They've already
left `host.players().server_players()`, except when the server stops, which tells
before it saves, with them still listed and able to get a last message.
Server-side.

A player whose login the server has accepted (NeoForge's
`PlayerNegotiationEvent` stage): the name, whitelist, ban and
server-full checks have passed and the player holds a place, but their
saved state is not loaded and they are not placed in a level yet. Set
`cancel` to refuse them: they are disconnected with `reason` (a plain
"Disconnected" if it is left unset) and nothing else of the join (the
join message, `player_logged_in`) happens. Once for each player
who joins, on a server. The player is not placed yet and their client
has no world to show a message in, so no player's state is swapped in
and `PlayerRef::tell` reaches nobody: the refusal `reason` is the answer.
The checks that need no mod (name, whitelist, bans, a full server,
the proxy's forwarding) refuse earlier, on the connection, and this
hook does not hear those players.

neoforge: none (Bukkit's PlayerLoginEvent; NeoForge's PlayerNegotiationEvent is not cancellable)

hooks.doc:
A player's game profile at login, before the server sends the login
success: the UUID and name the login authenticated and the properties
it would send. Change `properties` to send a different profile: the
login success and the player list use the changed list. The UUID and
name are the login's and are not changed here.

In online mode `properties` holds the account's signed `textures`
property, the skin; a proxy's forwarded properties are here too. An
offline-mode player has none. A skin mod replaces the `textures`
property with its own signed one; keep the other properties.

Once for each player a server accepts, after the name, whitelist, ban
and server-full checks have passed and before the login success is
sent, so a changed profile reaches the player's client and the player
list. It runs on the connection thread and has no host: answer from
the arguments and the mod's own state alone, and do not block the
login. The player is not placed and `player_login` follows later; this
hook cannot refuse the login.

The properties are the profile's wire limits: at most 16, non-empty
names of 64 UTF-16 units, values of 32767 and signatures of 1024. A
list past a limit is refused and the login's own properties are sent
instead.

neoforge: none (Bukkit's AsyncPlayerPreLoginEvent carries the profile; NeoForge's PlayerNegotiationEvent is not cancellable)

hooks.doc:
A server player selected a loom pattern, after the loom menu accepted the button. `pattern` is
the zero-based button index. Server-side.

A server player filled an empty map, after the filled map and its saved data were created.
Server-side.

A player's movement report is about to be applied: they would move from
`from` to `to`, or turn from `from_rotation` to `to_rotation` (`[yaw,
pitch]`). Heard once for each validated report whose position or
rotation differs from the player's last reported location, after the
server's own validation and before the report is committed. That
location is kept on the player's connection, apart from the accepted
position: it is the position given to the listener before it runs, and
the destination of every server-side teleport (a join, a teleport in the
level, a level change, a respawn, the resend of an unconfirmed teleport,
and the correction after a veto). `from` is that location. Set `cancel`
for a real veto and not a rollback: the report is not applied and its
bookkeeping is skipped, and the client is corrected to the accepted
position and rotation through the existing teleport correction. The veto
adds no anticheat violation of its own, but the report was already seen
by the server's own checks and by the anticheat's record of the client's
ticks before the hook, and what a violation of those would have done
still happens. The values are the exact ones: there is no once-per-tick
accumulation and no threshold in the engine, so the mod filters
(`if (to - from).length() < 1.0 / 16.0 { return; }` skips anything under
1/16 of a block). Their state is swapped in
(`host.players().acting_player()`, `PlayerRef::tell`).

A held report is ruled on in the same tick, and the player's later
packets (further reports, the end of the client tick, pongs) wait in
order behind it, then go on in that tick, so each later report is heard
from the one before. A report is out of
time at its 21st tick, counting the tick it was held at as the first: it
is dropped with the correction and never committed, even when a ruling
arrives after that. A player's disconnect, teleport or level change
drops a pending report cleanly. Not heard: the first tick in a level (the
tick after a join or a level change; the second is heard), a player riding
something (`vehicle_moved` hears the vehicle), any teleport (its
confirmation is validated and committed without the hook, at the teleport's
target, and so is the veto's own correction; a report that arrives while a teleport is
unconfirmed is not heard either), and a passage crossing (its caller
reads the position at once, so the report is committed in place). The
first report after a teleport that passed validation is heard, with the
teleport's destination as its `from`. With no listener the report is
committed in place with no extra work: nothing is held, copied or
allocated. With one, the cost is one held report for each moving player
a tick.

A fault or an epoch timeout in a wasm listener answers nothing: it is
not a veto and the report is committed, like every cancellable hook; the
fault is logged, counted against the mod, and stops the mod's group for
the session. A native listener that never returns is out of scope: it
blocks the game thread like any native code, and the 20-tick deadline
covers only a report held pending across ticks. Server-side.

neoforge: none (NeoForge has no player move event; PlayerTickEvent covers the tick)

hooks.doc:
A guest's client sent a movement packet and the server's own validation accepted it
(vanilla's `ServerGamePacketListenerImpl.handleMovePlayer`, the flying packet of a packet
library). Heard once for every such packet, also one that changes nothing (a stand-still or
ground-flag packet), where `player_move` hears only a report whose position or rotation
differs. `to` and `to_rotation` (`[yaw, pitch]`) are the packet's values, repeating the
player's own where the packet carries none. `on_ground` is the packet's own on-ground flag as
the client sent it; `has_position` and `has_rotation` say whether the packet carried a
position and a rotation (a status-only packet carries neither). Not heard: the player's first
tick in a level (the tick after a join or a level change), a teleport's confirmation and a
passage crossing. Heard with the player's state swapped in, before `player_move` hears the
