same packet. Not cancellable (`player_move` vetoes). With no listener nothing is queued.
Each guest is heard at most 8 packets per tick; the packets over that wait, in order, for
the next ticks (at most 256 wait, the oldest are dropped past that). Only the hook is
budgeted, the movement itself is processed as it arrives, so a packet that waited can be
heard after `player_move` already heard or vetoed the same move. Waiting packets are dropped
when the player changes level, is frozen for a transfer or leaves.
Server-side.

neoforge: none (NeoForge has no such event; a Bukkit plugin reads the flying packet through a packet library)

hooks.doc:
A server player named a mob with a name tag, after its name and persistence changed and the tag
was consumed. Server-side.

A player's display name was formatted. Replace `displayname` to change it.
Both sides: `context.side()` says which. It runs wherever vanilla asks `Player.getDisplayName()`: when a chat line, a join or leave line, a command's feedback, a death message or an advancement message is built, and for the name tag over a player (every frame it shows, so it is not asked when no mod listens). Answer from the arguments and `context` alone, and fast: `context` holds the side, the registries and the settings of the resource generation, and a `/reload` builds the next one.

A server player opened a sign for editing, after the editor state was made. `front` selects the
front or back side. Server-side.

`player`'s client crossed `passage` (arismoko/horizon#3775), one of the player's level's, from `from`
(its feet before), and the server is about to follow: the move to `from` passed the
move checks and both ends are tracked for the player, and the server has not yet
worked out where the player comes out. Set `cancel` and the server refuses the
crossing (`PassageCrossRefusal::Vetoed`) and puts the player back at `from`, as a
portal Immersive Portals' `canTeleportEntity` turns down does. A listener that
removes the passage or teleports the player refuses it too. Server-side. Diverges
from upstream: new hook.

neoforge: none (NeoForge has no such event; Immersive Portals' Portal.canTeleportEntity)

hooks.doc:
A server player picked an item from a block or entity, before it enters the hotbar. `pos` is
zero for an entity; `entity_id` is zero for a block. The player's state is swapped in. Set
`cancel` to leave the inventory and client unchanged.

neoforge: none (NeoForge has no such event; Paper's PlayerPickItemEvent)

hooks.doc:
A server player picked up an arrow after it was removed and its pickup was applied. `item` is
the arrow's pickup item id. Server-side.

A guest's client answered a ping (`ServerboundPongPacket`, vanilla's
`ServerGamePacketListenerImpl.handlePong`): `id` is the number the ping carried. The mod
sends the ping itself with `player_send_packet` (`ping`) and measures the round trip, or
counts the client ticks between two answers, as a lag-compensating anticheat does. The
engine's own pings (a recording's end-of-tick ping, whose id is the server tick) are answered
here too, so a mod picks ids it can tell apart from small tick numbers. Heard only for a
pong that answers a ping the server sent on that connection (a mod's or the engine's), once
per ping: an unsolicited or repeated pong, one for a ping sent more than 30 seconds ago, or
one for a ping pushed out by 64 newer unanswered ones, is dropped silently, as vanilla
ignores it. Heard after the packet's turn in the guest's inbox, in order with its other
packets, with the guest's state swapped in. Not cancellable. With no listener nothing is
queued. Server-side.

neoforge: none (NeoForge has no such event; a Bukkit plugin reads the pong packet through a packet library)

hooks.doc:
A server player released a drawn bow with `arrow` selected, by the use-item
key or a mod's `LivingRef::release_using_item`. The player's state is swapped in.

neoforge: none (NeoForge has no such event; Bukkit's PlayerReadyArrow)

hooks.doc:
A server player's recipe book requested a known recipe be placed in
their crafting grid. `recipe` is the recipe id; `all` is the shift
click form. Server-side.

A server player's authoritative recipe book pair changed. `book` is a
typed RecipeBookIdentity, never a custom vanilla ordinal. Rejected and
unchanged custom requests do not notify. The guest is not swapped in.

neoforge: none (NeoForge has no such event; Bukkit's PlayerRecipeBookSettingsChange)

hooks.doc:
A recipe is about to be unlocked for a server player. Set `cancel` to keep it locked. The
player's state is not swapped in. Server-side.

neoforge: none (NeoForge has no such event; Bukkit's PlayerRecipeDiscoverEvent)

hooks.doc:
`PlayerRespawnPositionEvent`: where `player` respawns, once the server has
found it: the bed or anchor they stand up at (facing it), or the world
spawn's free column. `original_level` and `original_position` are that
point; `missing_respawn_block` says the bed or anchor was gone, so the
player came back at the world spawn. Change `level`, `position`, `yaw`
and `pitch` to send them elsewhere: within the level a teleport, into
another level a level change. `copy_original_spawn_position` (default:
the block wasn't missing) says whether they keep their respawn point for
next time. Horizon places the player first and finds the point once its
chunks have loaded, so this fires then, before `player_respawned` only
when no chunks had to load. Not for the End exit, which isn't a respawn
here (as for `player_respawned`). Server-side.

`player` (`name`) respawned (NeoForge's `PlayerRespawnEvent`): at the
end of `PlayerList.respawn`, once they are placed and their health,
food and experience reset, with their state swapped in. Once for each
death that ends in a respawn, on a server; not for the End-exit one.

A server player launched with a riptide trident, after the velocity,
spin attack and grounded lift have been applied. The player's state is
swapped in. No reply is needed.

neoforge: none (NeoForge has no such event; Bukkit's PlayerRiptideEvent)

hooks.doc:
A player was saved to the world's store (NeoForge's
`PlayerEvent.SaveToFile`, `PlayerList.save`): when they leave or the
world closes, when a dedicated or integrated server saves its guests,
and for an integrated server's owner when the world saves them.
Once for each save. `directory`
is the world's player directory (`players/data`): write your own file
there, named `<uuid>.<suffix>`, never the player's `.dat`. The player
may be leaving, so no player's state is swapped in. Not cancellable.
Autosave snapshots are written asynchronously: this notification runs
on a later server tick after a successful write, possibly after WorldSaved.
Live state may have advanced beyond the saved snapshot; a process exit
before completions are drained can prevent notification delivery.

Not on wasm: it gives a path in the game's file system, which a wasm mod has none of; a wasm mod keeps a player's data in attachments.

NeoForge's `PlayerSetSpawnEvent`: a server player's respawn point is about to be
set (`ServerPlayer.setRespawnPosition`), once for each call vanilla makes: every sleep
in a bed (the same bed too, which refreshes its angle), an anchor that is a new
point, `/spawnpoint`, and the copy to the new player when a player respawns and their
respawn block was found (`pos` is none for a player with no point). A respawn block
that is gone makes no call. `pos` is the block position and `dimension` its level;
`forced` is `/spawnpoint`'s flag. Set `cancel` and the point stays as it was (the
respawned player is left with none). `player_entity_id` is the server's entity id for
the player. Server-side.

A player shearing a mob is about to do so. Set `cancel` to leave the mob and shears unchanged.
The guest's state is swapped in.

neoforge: none (NeoForge has no such event; Bukkit's PlayerShearEntityEvent)

hooks.doc:
A server player's shield was disabled by a blocked melee hit. The shield cooldown is set
immediately after this call. Server-side.

`PlayerSpawnPhantomsEvent`: the phantom spawner is about to decide whether to try a
spawn near a non-spectator server player, before its difficulty and rest rolls.
`result` starts empty, meaning `Default` (skylight and sea level check); `Allow` skips
that check and `Deny` stops the attempt. `phantoms` starts with a randomly drawn
group size; set it to override the count. Without mods the original draw order is kept.

A server player's sprint started or stopped: their client sent
`START_SPRINTING` or `STOP_SPRINTING` (the sprint key, a double tap
forward, or letting go) and the server's player is now `sprinting`
(vanilla's `setSprinting` in `handlePlayerCommand`). Heard only when it
changes. It cannot be stopped, and it hears what the client asks, not
what the server does: a sprint that ends by itself (a hit's knockback,
hunger, a wall) is not reported. The player's state is swapped in, so
the helpers and `PlayerRef::tell` work. Once for each change, on a server.

A server player started spectating `entity_id`, after their camera moved to it
(`ServerPlayer.setCamera` with a new target: a spectator's click or `/spectate`) and their
client was told. Heard once per change of target, not again while the camera follows it.
The mirror of `player_stop_spectating_entity`.

A client started tracking an entity (NeoForge's
`PlayerEvent.StartTracking`, posted at the end of
`ServerEntity.addPairing`): `player` (`name`) is now sent `entity`
(its ID, `uuid` its UUID, `kind` its type, `minecraft:zombie`) and its
changes. It comes into range, its client's chunks reach it, or it is
put in the level; another player is an entity too, and a player never
tracks their own. A mod sends the player what they need to show it
(`PlayerRef::send_payload`). The entity is as it was last tick: it
may be gone by now. Heard after the tick's players and entities have
moved, in order, with no player's state swapped in. Server-side.

A statistic is about to be awarded to a server player, before its count and scoreboard criteria
change. `stat_type` and `stat` are ids such as `minecraft:mined` and `minecraft:stone`, and
`value` the amount. All three may be rewritten; ids must use their canonical namespaced
spelling. Unknown types or entries, noncanonical ids and negative amounts are refused
together, warning once and keeping the entire original award.
Set `cancel` to award nothing. Server-side. Ordinary interactions
fire at vanilla's award point; inside a transaction, the award and this hook wait until
the outermost successful commit, after tentative world and inventory writes.

The player's crouch edge backoff (`Player.maybeBackOffFromEdge`) asks whether the player is staying on the ground surface (`Player.isStayingOnGroundSurface`, vanilla: the shift key is down). `entity` is the player's id; a mod may change `staying`, so a mod can make the player hold to an edge without crouching, or walk off while crouching. Fires on both sides, on the client's replayed ticks too, with the loop `context` of the side that ticks the player (its registries, settings and mod list): register the mod on both, and keep the listener a pure function of its inputs so prediction and the server agree. Beyond NeoForge: there is no counterpart. Diverges from upstream: new hook.

neoforge: none (vanilla Player.isStayingOnGroundSurface; NeoForge adds no event or extension for it)

hooks.doc:
A server player selected a stonecutter recipe, after the menu accepted
its button. `recipe` is the zero-based button index. Server-side.
A server player stopped spectating `entity_id`, after their camera returned to the player.

A client stopped tracking an entity (NeoForge's
`PlayerEvent.StopTracking`, posted at the end of
`ServerEntity.removePairing`): it went out of range, left the level or
died, or `player` (`name`) left, changed level or respawned, which
stops everything they tracked. `entity`, `uuid` and `kind` are as
`player_start_tracking` told. Once for each start, a leaving
player's after `player_logged_out`. The entity is not
necessarily still there, and a player who left is gone: no player's
state is swapped in. Server-side.

A server player released the use-item key, or a mod's `LivingRef::release_using_item` did,
before the item finished being used. The player's state is swapped in.

neoforge: none (NeoForge has no such event; Bukkit's PlayerStopUsingItem)

hooks.doc:
Heard before a non-spectator player's swap-hands action.
The two mutable stacks start as the off-hand and main-hand stacks;
the hands receive the listener's outputs unless it cancels.
slots. Set `cancel` to keep the items where they are: the player's
client is sent both slots again. The player's
state is swapped in, so `host.players().acting_player()`,
`PlayerRef::tell` and the item helpers reach them. Once for each press,
on a server: a LAN or dedicated server's players, the single-player
owner and a LAN host. Not heard: the same swap made in an open inventory
(hovering a slot and pressing the key, a menu click).

A server player swapped their main and off hands, after both inventory slots changed.
Server-side.

`PlayerSwitchHotbarSlotEvent.Post`: a server player switched from hotbar slot
`old_slot` to `new_slot` (0 to 8), after the selected slot changed and a main-hand
item use stopped. Fired only when the slot differs and
`player_switch_hotbar_slot_pre` didn't cancel it. The player's state is not swapped in.

`PlayerSwitchHotbarSlotEvent.Pre`: a server player is switching from hotbar slot
`old_slot` to `new_slot` (0 to 8), after the slot range check and before the
selected slot changes. Fired only when the slot differs. The player's state is not
swapped in. Set `cancel` to keep the old slot; the client is sent that slot again,
and `player_switch_hotbar_slot_post` doesn't fire.

ServerPlayer.getTabListDisplayName: the name the Tab list shows for
`player`, None to let the client choose it. Replace `display_name` to
change it. It runs while the Tab list is built. Answer from the arguments and `context` alone, and fast: `context` holds the side, the registries and the settings of the resource generation, and a `/reload` builds the next one.

A server player took the book from a lectern, after the menu and block entity changed. `book`
is the removed item id. Server-side.

A server player is about to travel through an End gateway at `gateway`. Set `cancel` to leave
them at the entrance; the gateway is not consumed and its cooldown does not start. Server-side.

A server player a command teleported (NeoForge's
`EntityTeleportEvent`, for a player): `/tp` and `/teleport`, inside
their level or into another one. `from` and `to` are their feet before
and after, `dimension` the level they are in now. Heard after the move
has reached the player's state and their client (an inter-level
teleport: when the new level is entered, before it has loaded around
them), so it cannot stop it. The player's state is swapped in, so the
helpers that read the acting player and `PlayerRef::tell` work. Once for
each teleported player, on a server. Ender pearls and chorus fruit
have their own hooks; a spectator's teleport menu is not heard yet;
portals and respawns are not teleports here.

neoforge: none (EntityTeleportEvent.TeleportCommand fires before the move and can cancel it; this hook is told after the move)

hooks.doc:
After a player's tick on both logical sides (NeoForge 26.3
`PlayerTickEvent.Post`). Non-cancellable, including death-screen ticks.
`player` is the same identity as in `player_tick_pre`; on the server
their state is acting. Runs after body work and server-side item,
arrow and XP pickups, so reads see the completed tick. Client reads
see only the state available to that client, not future server updates.

Before a player's tick on both logical sides (NeoForge 26.3
`PlayerTickEvent.Pre`). Non-cancellable, including death-screen ticks.
`player` identifies the ticked player; on the server their state is
acting. Fires before sleep, cooldowns and body work. Players still tick
under `/tick freeze`, but not while the level is paused.

A server player toggled an ageable mob's age lock with a golden
dandelion, after the lock and item use changed.

A player's client started (`flying`) or stopped flying (vanilla's
`handlePlayerAbilities`, which honours it only for a player who may
fly: creative or spectator), heard once for each change, on a server,
with the player's state swapped in, so `PlayerRef::tell` and the other
helpers reach them. The player is already flying or not as asked, as
vanilla leaves them; set `cancel` to refuse it: they keep the state
they had and the server sends their abilities back, as vanilla does
for what it refuses, so the client lands or flies again. Only what a
client asks for is heard: not the flight a game-mode change starts or
ends (`/gamemode`), and not a LAN host's own player.

neoforge: none (NeoForge has no flight toggle event; Bukkit's PlayerToggleFlightEvent)

hooks.doc:
A guest's client changed sneaking in its player input packet, after the hub applied the new state.
The guest's state is swapped in. Server-side.

neoforge: none (NeoForge has no such event; Bukkit's PlayerToggleSneakEvent)

hooks.doc:
A totem of undying saved the server player `player` (`name`): their
hurt would have killed them and the totem held in either hand fired
(`LivingEntity.checkTotemDeathProtection`; Bukkit's
`EntityResurrectEvent`), heard just before it is used up and its
effects apply. Listen only: whether the totem saves is decided inside
the health state machine, before a mod is asked, so a mod cannot veto
it from here. The player's state is swapped in, so
`host.players().acting_player()`, `PlayerRef::tell` and the item helpers reach them.
Once for each totem, on a server; the host of a LAN world's totem is
not heard.

neoforge: none (NeoForge's LivingUseTotemEvent can cancel the save; this hook only listens. Bukkit's EntityResurrectEvent)

hooks.doc:
A server player completed a villager or wandering trader trade. `entity_id` is the merchant
network id. Server-side.
A server player removed an entity's leash, after it was cleared.
A server applied `velocity` to a player, when syncing changed motion to that player's client.

A server player's experience points are about to change through
`Player.giveExperiencePoints` (NeoForge's `PlayerXpEvent.XpChange`): an
orb pickup after mending, an advancement reward, or `/xp add ... points`.
Change the signed `amount` (in points) or set `cancel` to give nothing.
Experience bottles and furnaces make orbs, so they come through the orb
path. Server-side.

A server player's level is about to change through
`Player.giveExperienceLevels`: once per level gained or lost by points,
and for the anvil, `/experience add ... levels` and `PlayerRef::give_levels`.
Change `levels`, or set `cancel` to leave the level unchanged. The
player's state is swapped in, so `host.players().acting_player()`, `PlayerRef::tell`
and the item helpers reach them. Server-side.

A Nether portal was built for a dimension travel, or an End platform
was made for an arrival. `pos` is the lower corner of the Nether
portal rectangle or the End platform origin. The completed blocks are
already in the world.

A fire placed at `pos` (`state`) found an empty obsidian frame, `shape`,
and is about to fill it with a nether portal (`BlockEvent.PortalSpawnEvent`,
in `BaseFireBlock.onPlace`), in the Overworld or the Nether. Set
`cancel` and no portal forms: the fire stays where it can survive, as
without a frame. Server-side.

Possible natural spawns at a server position (NeoForge's
`LevelEvent.PotentialSpawns`, `NaturalSpawner.mobsAt`). Mods may add or
remove entries, or cancel to make the list empty. Mods can read the world,
but cannot write it during the spawn pass.

A brewing stand at `pos` brewed (`PotionBrewEvent.Post`, at the end of
`BrewingStandBlockEntity.doBrew`), or `potion_brew_pre` was cancelled:
`stacks` holds its five slots after the brew (or as the cancelling
mods left them), and what the mods leave there is the stand's. Fires
last, as `doBrew` ends: after `brewing_complete`, the brew sound and
the ingredient's remainder dropping. Server-side.

A brewing stand at `pos` is about to brew (`PotionBrewEvent.Pre`,
in `BrewingStandBlockEntity.doBrew`): `stacks` is a copy of its five
slots (three bottles, the ingredient, the fuel). Set `cancel` to skip
vanilla's brew: the stand then takes `stacks` as the mods left them,
uses no ingredient and plays no brew sound, and `potion_brew_post`
fires with those slots; `brewing_complete` doesn't, as nothing was
brewed. Uncancelled, changes to `stacks` are dropped. Server-side.
A thrown splash or lingering potion applied its hit effects.

`BlockEntity.preRemoveSideEffects` of a mod's block entity: an
authoritative server is removing `entity` from `pos`, where the block
`state` stood, and its updates may have side effects (not under flag
256, `UPDATE_SKIP_BLOCK_ENTITY_SIDEEFFECTS`). Put in `drops` the stacks
it held that the game doesn't: they scatter as `Containers.dropItemStack`
scatters them, after the block entity's own container. The block entity
is still in place, so its attachments read as they were. Answered from
inside the level's write: don't change the world here.

neoforge: none (vanilla BlockEntity.preRemoveSideEffects; NeoForge adds no event or extension for it)

hooks.doc:
A hopper at `pos` began an item transfer attempt. This runs after its
cooldown and enabled checks, before pushing or pulling any items.
Server-side, including the single-player server.
A crafting-grid result was prepared for a server player; `pos` is the crafting table, or None for the inventory grid. Change `result` before it is sent.
Enchanting offers were calculated for a server player at `pos`. Change `costs` before they are sent to the menu.
A smithing result was prepared for a server player at `pos`. Change it before it is sent.

A projectile hit something (NeoForge's `ProjectileImpactEvent`, posted
where vanilla's projectile has found what it meets, before the hit
acts): `projectile` (its entity id) of type `kind` (`minecraft:arrow`),
shot by `owner` (a mob's or a player's entity id, 0 for none) in the level
`dimension`. It hit the entity `entity` of type `entity_kind` (a player is
`minecraft:player`; a dragon's part is `minecraft:ender_dragon`), or, with
`entity` None, the block at `block` on its `face` (the face's normal,
`[0, 1, 0]` for the top), at the point `at`. Set `canceled` and the impact
does not happen: no damage, no knockback, no sound, no block reaction, the
arrow does not stick, a pearl does not teleport, a potion or a fireball
does not burst. Cancellation leaves the projectile alive. A flying bobber
skips hooking and redirection to the hit point, but its ordinary move
still stops against solid blocks. Water is not an impact. Bobbers notify
before vanilla's entity deflection and world-border bounce; rockets notify
after deflection and cancellation skips their impact explosion only.
Covers arrows, tridents, thrown items, fireballs, wither skulls, wind
charges, llama spit, shulker bullets, bobbers and rockets. Other families
skip breeze deflections and hits on wind charges. A dragon part or End crystal is told by the id of the
dragon or crystal. Heard only when a mod also sets
`hears_projectile_impacts`. Server-side. Version 2 adds bobbers and rockets;
listeners retaining the earlier family set filter out `minecraft:fishing_bobber`
and `minecraft:firework_rocket`. Named injections request `hook_version = 2`.

A server projectile was added to the level. `player` is set only for
a player launch; other sources have an empty `name`.

A raid wave has been spawned at `pos`; `wave` is its one-based wave
number and `raiders` counts the raiders, not the mobs they ride.

A server raid at `pos` changed to `state` (`triggered`, `victory`,
`loss` or `stopped`). `raid` identifies its owning level, including a
parked level. A terminal raid already removed from storage cannot be read.

Whether the rail `state` at `pos` may climb toward a raised rail beside it
(`IBaseRailBlockExtension.canMakeSlopes`). `can` starts true, as for every vanilla rail;
set false to keep it flat as it connects to its neighbours (`RailState`). Asked on an
authoritative server as a rail is placed or a neighbour changes it: answer from the
state and the position, without touching the world. With no part attached to the
state, the cost is one table lookup. Diverges from upstream: new hook.

The track the rail `state` at `pos` lays for `cart`
(`IBaseRailBlockExtension.getRailDirection`), so a switch track or a one-way rail can
turn a cart differently from its stored shape. `shape` starts at the rail's `shape`
property. `cart` is the minecart moving on it, or `None` when the rail asks for itself:
as it connects to its neighbours (`RailState`) and as a minecart item is placed on it.
The cart's movement asks wherever it reads the track under it. Asked on both sides,
since a client predicts its own cart's motion: register the mod on both and answer the
same on each, from the level host and the event alone. With no part attached to the
state, the cost is one table lookup per rail read. Diverges from upstream: new hook.

Whether the rail `state` at `pos` may make corners
(`IBaseRailBlockExtension.isFlexibleRail`). `flexible` starts true for a plain rail and
false for the straight ones (powered, detector, activator); set false to keep it
straight at a junction. Asked on an authoritative server as the rail and its neighbours
connect (`RailState`): answer from the state and the position, without touching the
world. With no part attached to the state, the cost is one table lookup. Diverges from
upstream: new hook.

Whether the rail `state` may take `shape` (`IBaseRailBlockExtension.isValidRailShape`),
asked as it connects to its neighbours (`RailState`) before the shape is written.
`valid` starts true when the rail's `shape` property has that value; set false to refuse
it, and the rail keeps its current shape. A part can't make valid a shape the property
lacks. Asked on an authoritative server: answer from the state and the shape, without
touching the world. With no part attached to the state, the cost is one table lookup.
Diverges from upstream: new hook.

An authoritative server's `ServerLevel.tickChunk` is about to
random-tick the block `state` at `pos` (`BlockState.randomTick`):
only blocks that tick randomly, a mod's as its vanilla template block
does. Bone meal's random ticks (`StemBlock.performBonemeal`) don't
fire it. Change the block with `native_set_block_property` and set
`handled` to skip the block's own random tick (a mod crop growing its
own way); a block changed without `handled` takes its own random tick
as it is now, if it still ticks randomly. Lava's fluid random tick
runs either way.

neoforge: none (vanilla BlockBehaviour.randomTick; NeoForge adds no event or extension for it)

hooks.doc:
Supply categories and vanilla-shaped displays for custom recipe types.
Asked lazily once per recipe table. Use the Host's recipe table to build
`RecipeBookCategory::displays` from the type's own opaque recipe JSON.
Each category names its menu, book identity and per-book search group.
The display/index load boundary returns typed errors; screen integration
is separate. This declaration does not register a settings book.

neoforge: none (RegisterRecipeBookSearchCategoriesEvent registers search groups only, not a recipe type's categories)

hooks.doc:
Items a mod's own recipe type takes in a station slot, added to the
recipe property sets (`RecipeManager.RECIPE_PROPERTY_SETS`): what a
furnace, blast furnace, smoker, campfire, smithing table slot or brewing
stand slot accepts, and what a client predicts it accepts. Push one
`RecipePropertyAddition` per set to add to; the vanilla recipes' own
items stay in. Called once per load, after the recipes are resolved, with
the `DataLoadContext` of the load that owns them (`origin()`
`ServerDataLoad` on a server, `ClientPreload` on a client's own load),
and again after `/reload`. A new namespaced key creates a set when its
namespace belongs to the listener's manifest (its ID or `namespaces`).
Later listeners may extend existing sets. Invalid or foreign new keys,
unknown vanilla keys, and air are logged and skipped; unknown items are
ignored. Custom sets are synced to clients alongside vanilla sets. The
answer must be the same every time.

Additional ingredient containers for server player `player` placing or checking a
recipe in the mod crafting menu `menu` (`namespace:path`) at `pos`. The player's
state is not swapped in. Push block positions to `sources`; containers are used
after the player's inventory, in mod order and then push order. The engine silently
skips `pos`, duplicates (first wins), unavailable or non-lendable containers, and
all containers after the first 64 accepted sources, without per-call logging.
Chest-like block entities and mod containers with declared slots are lendable.
No answer preserves vanilla placement. The engine takes ingredients and writes
changed containers back, firing `container_changed`; this hook only names sources.
Asked once per recipe-book placement/apply or server transfer check, not per tick.
Native and wasm listeners receive the same arguments and append to the same output.

neoforge: none (Horizon mod crafting menus lend ingredient containers)

hooks.doc:
The server's recipes of `recipe_types` arrived (NeoForge's
`RecipesReceivedEvent`): from now on the recipe helpers
(`native_recipes`, `native_recipes_of_type`) give the server's recipes
of those types in place of the window's own, so rebuild what you made
of them. It comes after a join, once the window has its player, and
after every `/reload`, on a server whose mods asked for them
(`native_datapack_sync`), single player included; with no types when
the server stopped sending them and the window is back on its own
recipes. A recipe's recipe book ids are not part of what arrives:
`recipe_book_ids` answers them. Client-side.

The block-state definition types a mod adds (NeoForge's `RegisterBlockStateModels`,
its `registerDefinition`): push each type id, `<mod id>:<path>`. Asked once at start on
the client, before resources load. A blockstate file whose `neoforge:definition_type` is
a registered id has each state's model picked by `instantiate_block_state_definition`, on
every load and reload. An id in vanilla's namespace, not of that form, or registered
already is logged and left out.

The tint sources of blocks (NeoForge's `RegisterColorHandlersEvent.BlockTintSources`,
vanilla's `BlockColors.register`): `register(layers, blocks)`, and a model face with
`tintindex` i is multiplied by layer i of its block's list; a face past the list is not
tinted. A layer is one of vanilla's sources (`VanillaTint`) or the mod's own
`BlockTintSource`. Blocks are ids, a mod's or vanilla's, and a later registration for a
block replaces the earlier one, vanilla's own colours included. Asked once at start on the
client, before resources load; every resource load, a pack reload included, applies the
registrations again. An id no block has is logged and skipped.

Say which fluid, and how much, one of your cauldron blocks holds (NeoForge
`RegisterCauldronFluidContentEvent`), so the fluid capability (`FLUIDS`) fills and
drains it as it does vanilla's water and lava cauldrons. Asked once the block registry
is resolved, before any world opens, and again on a resource reload. Give
`event.contents.register(block, fluid, total, level)` the block and fluid keys your
`register` hook requested, the millibuckets the cauldron holds when full, and the name
of its integer level property, or none for a cauldron only ever full. The engine
refuses, with one logged warning naming both sides, a block that already has a content,
a fluid that already has a cauldron, an unknown block or fluid, a level property the
block lacks or that isn't an integer, and a total of 0 or one that doesn't divide
evenly by the levels; the rest of a mod's contents still apply.

Register cauldron item interactions, by exact item or by item tag, on both sides before
snapshot publication. Vanilla dye tags take precedence, then exact items, then item tags
in registration order; duplicate entries refuse preparation.

The client's own commands (NeoForge's `RegisterClientCommandsEvent`), which
`command` runs: push a `Command` per usage (`x <mode:word>`).
Asked when a connection starts and again when the server sends its
own tree, so the chat box colours, completes and lists them as the
game's own; a name the game already has keeps that command's
behaviour. A client command has no operator level: one with a nonzero
`level` is left out.

The colour resolvers block tints blend over the biomes around a block (NeoForge's
`RegisterColorHandlersEvent.ColorResolvers`): `register(resolver)` adds the mod's own
`BiomeColorResolver` and returns the `ColorResolver` its block tint sources pass to
`BlockAndTintGetter::block_tint`. The game blends a mod's resolver over the biome blend
radius and caches it per section while it meshes, as it does vanilla's grass, foliage and
water. Asked once at start on the client, before `register_block_tint_sources` and before
resources load.

The commands native mods add to the server's command tree: push
yours. Asked whenever the server builds its command tree, as the reference loader's
`Commands` does: when a world opens (a dedicated server, a LAN host, single player's
server thread), before its functions load, so a function line may name your command;
on each `/reload` and data pack change, so a command you stop pushing is refused by the
next functions loaded; and after a mod calls `host.commands().refresh_commands()`.
Every player's chat box completes them as vanilla's, within their level. A
name vanilla has is left out. Each executable usage keeps its own
permission level; a lower-level child only opens traversal through a
shared prefix, not execution of that prefix. An argument's kind is one
of `word`, `text`, `integer`, `number`, `boolean`, `player`, `item`,
`block_pos` and `vec3`, or a command argument type a mod registered
(`Registrar::register_command_argument`), named by its namespaced id.

The config files native mods keep (NeoForge's `registerConfig`):
push yours, each of a kind, with the text written to `config/` when
the file is missing. Asked by the window when the game starts (its
`Client` and `Common` configs), by a dedicated server when it starts
(`Common` and `Server`) and by a server before each world it opens
(`Server`); a game reads only its own kinds, so push them all every
time. Runs in Config: settings reads and the scoped ConfigFiles service
are available; world handles and transactions panic naming the phase. A file outside `config/`, or one already registered, is skipped.

The F3 debug entries a mod adds (NeoForge's `RegisterDebugEntriesEvent`): push a `DebugEntry`
per entry, its id `<mod id>:<path>` and the vanilla group its lines join. Asked once at start,
on the client. An id in vanilla's namespace, not of that form, or registered already is logged
and left out. Each entry is listed and switched on or off with vanilla's, and `debug_entry_lines`
fills it while it is on.

The world-space debug renderers a mod has now (NeoForge's `RegisterDebugRenderersEvent`): push a
`DebugRenderer` per renderer. Asked at each renderer list refresh, on the client.

Register loading screens once at client startup (NeoForge's
`RegisterDimensionTransitionScreenEvent`). Conditional source/destination pairs take
priority over incoming registrations, which take priority over outgoing registrations.
Duplicate transition registrations keep the first; invalid ids are logged and skipped.
An unmatched transition uses vanilla's screen and every screen uses the existing tracker.

Register namespaced enchantment damage value effects once before content loads.
Custom nodes in `minecraft:damage`, including nested `minecraft:all_of`, resolve to
these callbacks at load. Unknown identifiers reject the enchantment with a diagnostic.
Callbacks receive a read-only ServerHost, actual attacker and victim handles and the
pre-hit weapon snapshot. Vanilla nodes and requirements retain their traversal and RNG
order. This is vanilla EnchantmentHelper.modifyDamage, not an incoming-damage event.

The layers a mod adds to living entity renderers (NeoForge's
`EntityRenderersEvent.AddLayers`): `add(target, layer)`, and every living entity of the
type, or every player of the player model, in view draws `EntityRenderLayer::submit` after
its model and the layers added before. `entity_types`, `is_living`, `player_models` and
`has_mod_renderer` tell what renderers this load built. A target that is no living entity
type is refused by name. Asked on the client on every resource load, the first one and each
reload, after the renderers resolve (`register_entity_renderers`): layers don't carry over
from one load to the next, so add them again each time.

The code-defined renderers of entity types (NeoForge's
`EntityRenderersEvent.RegisterRenderers`, `registerEntityRenderer`): `register(type,
renderer)`, and every entity of the type `type` (`mymod:bolt`) in view is drawn by
`EntityRenderer::submit` in place of the type's own drawing. A later registration for a
type replaces the earlier one; a type the game does not know is logged with its id and
draws nothing new. Asked once at start on the client, before resources load; the game
resolves each type's renderer on every resource load. This build draws the registered
renderers of content mods' thrown types and of the living types drawn as mobs (in place of
the model and its vanilla layers); the other entity families keep their own drawing.

Register the screen effect spectating an entity type puts on, once at client startup
(NeoForge's `RegisterEntitySpectatorShadersEvent`), as vanilla's creeper, spider and
enderman do. The first registration for an entity type wins, vanilla's own counting as
first, so a mod can't change what the vanilla mobs show; a skipped or malformed
registration is logged. The effect applies while the first-person view follows that
entity, and the third-person view or leaving it clears it.

The models of your world fluids (NeoForge's `RegisterFluidModelsEvent`): push a
`mod_api::FluidModel` per fluid whose look doesn't say all of it. Its
sprites are block atlas textures, baked at every resource load from that pack's files; the
tint stays the look's. A fluid without one draws its look's sprite on every surface, or
water's textures when it has none. Asked at startup and on resource reload before baking, and
only on the client.

Register namespaced test functions before the world's test definitions load.
Each function runs with a ServerHost once per attempt in the real test level.
The runner retains ownership of retries, timeout and completion.

The HUD layers a mod adds among vanilla's (NeoForge's `RegisterGuiLayersEvent`): push a
`GuiLayer` per layer, its id `<mod id>:<path>` and its `GuiLayerPlacement`. Asked once at
start, on the client. `gui_layer_draw` draws each layer, between `gui_layer_pre` and
`gui_layer_post` like a vanilla layer, so other mods can hide it or draw around it.

The item model node types a mod adds (NeoForge's `RegisterItemModelsEvent`): push each
type id, `<mod id>:<path>`. Asked once at start on the client, before resources load. An
item definition's node whose `type` is a registered id draws, per stack, the named models
`item_model_update` answers. An id in vanilla's namespace, not of that form, or registered
already is logged and left out.

The item tint sources a mod adds (NeoForge's `RegisterColorHandlersEvent.ItemTintSources`):
push each id, `<mod id>:<path>`. Asked once at start on the client, before resources load.
An entry in a `minecraft:model`'s `tints` whose `type` is a registered id colours its
`tintindex` with what `item_tint_source` answers per stack, also after a resource reload. An id
in vanilla's namespace, not of that form, or registered already is logged and left out; a
tint source nobody registers draws white.

The animation targets and interpolations a mod adds for keyframe animation files to name
(NeoForge's `RegisterJsonAnimationTypesEvent`): push each id, `<namespace>:<path>`, as a
`JsonAnimationType::Target` or `JsonAnimationType::Interpolation`. Asked once at start on
the client, before resources load. An id in vanilla's namespace, not of that form, or
registered already as the same kind is logged and left out.

Entity model layers built in code (NeoForge's
`EntityRenderersEvent.RegisterLayerDefinitions`): push each one's id,
`<mod id>:<model>#<layer>` as a `ModelLayerLocation` names it
(`mymod:golem#main`), and its `LayerDefinition`, as the mod's
`createBodyLayer()` builds it. `native_bake_layer` bakes one into the
`ModelPart` tree `native_draw_model_part` draws. Asked once at start,
on the client. An id in vanilla's namespace, not of that form, or
registered already is logged and left out. API @API:model_layers@.

Register named conditions once at mod load, before server data admission.
Each handler is a raw-JSON handler: it reads the condition's JSON value.
Names must belong to the registering mod's namespace. Native and wasm
handlers use the same registration and evaluation route. Registering one
name owns that namespace; an unknown condition in it refuses data reload.
Foreign unknown ids omit their file with one ERROR-level log entry,
even inside `or(true, unknown)`; every combinator branch is visited.

The model loaders a mod adds (NeoForge's `ModelEvent.RegisterLoaders`): push each loader
id, `<mod id>:<path>`. Asked once at start on the client, before resources load. A model
whose `loader` is a registered id gets the quads `bake_model_loader` answers, baked with
its elements, on every load and reload. An id in vanilla's namespace, not of that form, or
registered already is logged and left out.

The render groups a mod's particles draw in (NeoForge's `RegisterParticleGroupsEvent`): push a
`ParticleGroup` per group, its id `<mod id>:<path>`, how it blends and the particle types in
it. Asked once at start, on the client, before resources load; the game resolves each
type's group when the particle sprite sets load, on every resource load as well. An id in
vanilla's namespace, not of that form, or registered already is logged and left out.

The code-defined particle providers of a mod's own particle types (NeoForge's
`RegisterParticleProvidersEvent`): `register(name, provider)`, and every particle of the
type `name` (`ParticleOptions::named("mymod:spark")`) is moved each tick by
`ParticleProvider::tick`. The sprite set and the declarative spawn values stay in
`assets/<namespace>/particles/<path>.json`. A later registration for a name replaces the
earlier one; a name no sprite set matches is logged and draws nothing. Asked once at start
on the client, before resources load; the game resolves each type's provider when the
sprite sets load, on every resource load as well.

Register client screens for world-preset keys once at startup. The first
registration for a key wins. Invalid ids are refused. Unregistered presets
retain their built-in editor, or their disabled Customize button.

The numeric item model properties a mod adds (NeoForge's
`RegisterRangeSelectItemModelPropertyEvent`): push each id, `<mod id>:<path>`. Asked once at
start on the client, before resources load. A `minecraft:range_dispatch` naming a registered
property thresholds on the number `item_model_range_property` answers per stack, also after a
resource reload. An id in vanilla's namespace, not of that form, or registered already is
logged and left out; a property nobody registers reads 0.

Register the mod's own render pipelines, once at client startup (NeoForge's
`RegisterRenderPipelinesEvent`; 1.21.1 mods used `RegisterShadersEvent`): push a
[`RenderPipeline`] for each into `event.pipelines`. The game builds them with its own at
startup and again on every resource reload. An id outside the mod's namespaces, one an
earlier registration took are logged with the mod and
dropped. A required pipeline whose shader is missing or doesn't build fails the load: the
game does not start, and a reload fails and keeps the previous resources. An
[optional](RenderPipeline::optional()) one is logged and resolves to
[`RenderPipelineError::Invalid`].

Collect static, mod-generated PNGs for the block and GUI atlases. Called at
first client load and every resource reload, before textures are stitched.

neoforge: none (runtime registration before client atlas construction)

hooks.doc:
The categorical item model properties a mod adds (NeoForge's
`RegisterSelectItemModelPropertyEvent`): push each id, `<mod id>:<path>`. Asked once at start
on the client, before resources load. A `minecraft:select` naming a registered property picks
the case whose `when` string equals what `item_model_select_property` answers per stack, also
after a resource reload. An id in vanilla's namespace, not of that form, or registered already
is logged and left out; a select on a property nobody registers draws its fallback.

The special item model types a mod draws (NeoForge's `RegisterSpecialModelRendererEvent`):
`register(type, renderer)`, and every `minecraft:special` item model whose `model` object
has the type `type` (`mymod:skillet`) is drawn by `SpecialModelRenderer::extract`. A later
registration of a type replaces the earlier one, vanilla's types included, and the log
names both mods. Asked once at start on the client, before resources load; a special
model of a type no mod registered and vanilla doesn't have is an error naming it, and its
item draws the missing model.

The atlas sprite source types a mod adds (NeoForge's `RegisterSpriteSourcesEvent`): push
each type id, `<mod id>:<path>`. Asked once at start on the client, before resources load.
An entry of an atlas definition's `sources` whose `type` is a registered id is answered by
`sprite_source` at its place in the list, on every load and reload. An id in vanilla's
namespace, not of that form, or registered already is logged and left out.

Declare atlases beside the game's (`RegisterTextureAtlasesEvent`), each with the atlas
definition that lists its sprites. Called at first client load and every resource reload,
before textures are stitched.

Declare villager professions once per mod load, before world admission.
The engine resolves every reference atomically with the owning resource tables.
Vanilla replacement and overlapping custom acquisition POIs are refused.
NeoForge adds a profession through `RegisterEvent` on `Registries.VILLAGER_PROFESSION`;
this hook declares it as data, so only the registration moment corresponds.

A player submitted a command whose root appears in the mod command tree
and whose root permission the player meets. The player's state is in place.
This runs before argument parsing, so listeners that own the root can apply
their own syntax and subcommand permissions. Return `Flow::Cancel` once
handled. Otherwise the command goes through ordinary parsing and resolution.
The text has no leading slash and is untrusted. Console, function and
nested `execute` invocations use the regular command path.

`Item.releaseUsing` of `stack`: `entity` let it go with `time_left`
ticks of its `use_duration` left, so it was held for
`duration - time_left` (a bow-like item shoots by that charge). Set
`used` as vanilla's return, and the stack's use cooldown starts
(`ItemStack.releaseUsing`). After the vanilla item's own release, once
`living_entity_use_item_stop` let it through. Both sides, as
vanilla's: change the world only where this `Game` runs the world,
not on a server's client.

Choose the state left by removing your block. Return a state in `answer`
to replace vanilla's fluid block (air when dry), or leave it unanswered.
Only the removed block's Part is asked, on the authoritative server.
The replacement must be a registered block state; an invalid answer is
refused with a diagnostic and vanilla's replacement is written instead.
The normal setBlock effects and flags 3 (+64 when moved by a piston)
apply to the written state. The level is read-only during this call.

neoforge: none (vanilla Level.removeBlock; no NeoForge event covers this call)

hooks.doc:
Before this window's player's first-person `left` or right arm is
drawn (`RenderArmEvent`, in `renderPlayerArm` and `renderMapHand`):
the empty main hand's arm, and the arms under a held map, never while
the player is invisible. `player` and `player_entity_id` are the
local player's UUID and entity id. `draw`'s pose stack starts at the
arm model's origin, in blocks, posed as vanilla's arm is (with any
`render_hand`), lit with the light at the eyes; add
geometry with `native_draw_cube`, `native_draw_quad`, `native_draw_block`
and `native_draw_item`. Set `canceled` to leave out vanilla's arm;
what the mods drew stays. Client-side.

Final world fog, after the computed color hook, ordinary calculations and Horizon's fog
option, before upload. Title panoramas skip it. Invalid color or distance values retain the
original whole fog.

Once a frame, in a world or not, right after the frame was rendered
(NeoForge's `RenderFrameEvent.Post`). `elapsed` is the frame's time. It
fires for a frame that was skipped too; `flip_frame` is the moment a
frame was presented. `world_partial_tick` is the interpolation used by
that frame, held while paused or frozen; `partial_tick` is the advancing
window clock. Outside a world both use the window clock. Neither is
recomputed after listeners run. Client-side.

Once a frame, in a world or not, after Horizon's extras and just before
the frame is rendered (NeoForge's `RenderFrameEvent.Pre`). `elapsed` is
the frame's time. `world_partial_tick` is the interpolation about to be
drawn, held while paused or frozen; `partial_tick` is the window clock,
which keeps advancing. Outside a world both use the window clock.
Listener writes do not change this frame's captured interpolation. Client-side.

The HUD (not drawn under F1), after the minimap (NeoForge's
`RenderGuiEvent.Post`): place a box with `corners.place` (boxes stack
away from their edge) and draw it with `native_fill` and `native_text`.
Skip a corner `host.native_corner_shown` says F3 takes. Not heard when a mod
canceled `render_gui_pre`. Client-side.

Before the in-world HUD is drawn (NeoForge's `RenderGuiEvent.Pre`):
return `Flow::Cancel` and none of it is, as under F1: no vanilla layer (and so
no `gui_layer_pre` or `gui_layer_post`), no `render_gui_post`, and no
chat or toasts. Fires once a frame in a world, not under F1 and not
while a server dialog or the connection screen covers the window.
Client-side.

Before one first-person hand of this window's player is drawn
(`RenderHandEvent`, client): a hand that holds an item or a map, the
empty main hand's arm, and the empty off hand, where vanilla draws
nothing. Adjust `render`'s pose, draw in the hand with `draw`, or
cancel the default geometry; what the mods drew stays. Equip progress
includes the item's swap scale. `draw`'s pose stack starts in the
hands' view space, in blocks, +x right, +y up, -z into the screen,
under the hand sway and before vanilla's per-item transforms; both
hands share it, and `render.hand` says which one is asked. It is lit
with the light at the eyes; add geometry with `native_draw_cube`,
`native_draw_quad`, `native_draw_block` and `native_draw_item`. It
joins the hand's own vertices, ahead of vanilla's: the hand's field of
view, the view bob, a shader pack's hand pass and `hand_drawn`
see it as they see vanilla's hand. Unlike NeoForge, the pose stack is
`draw`'s own: turning it moves what you draw, `render`'s pose moves
the default geometry, and player render state is not exposed.
Before a visible item frame's item or map is drawn. Cancel hides the item, not the frame.

Draw world geometry at one stage of a world view (NeoForge 26.3's
`RenderLevelStageEvent`), asked for each `RenderLevelStage` in frame order. `draw` is
the view's `WorldDrawContext` and shares its limits with `submit_custom_geometry`; its
lines and quads draw at `stage`. Client-only, noncancellable.

After a living entity is drawn (NeoForge's `RenderLivingEvent.Post`): once a frame for each
mob and player in view whose `render_living_pre` wasn't canceled, after its model, its vanilla
layers and the mods' layers. `entity` is its render state, as `render_living_pre` has it;
`draw` is posed at its feet, turned with its body, and what it draws is kept. `parts` is a
humanoid model's parts as vanilla posed them this frame (`HumanoidModel.setupAnim`), taken
from the body's own draw, so a part a pre hook hid reads as not visible; read-only: attach
geometry to an arm or the head without animating it again; None for a model that isn't
humanoid. The order today: before this hook its model, its vanilla layers and the mods'
layers are drawn; after it, in the frame's later passes, its name tag, its leash, its
flames and its shadow (the reference draws the leash and the name tag first, arismoko/horizon#3915). A type
with a mod's registered renderer (`register_entity_renderers`) has its own model's order,
the renderer in the model's place, so it changes with arismoko/horizon#3915 and not before. For a player,
its `render_player_post` follows.

Before a living entity is drawn (NeoForge's `RenderLivingEvent.Pre`): once a frame for each
mob and player in view (one the frame culls is not asked), before its pose, model and
layers. `entity` is its render state (its id, kind, custom name, the frame's partial tick,
its body and head turns and walk cycle, `LivingEntityRenderState`). `draw` is posed at its
feet, turned with its body: +z the way it faces, +x its left, +y up, in blocks, with the
helpers block entities draw with (`cube`, `quad`, `block`, `item`, `model_part`); what it
draws is kept. Set `canceled` to skip all of the entity's drawing this frame: its model,
armour, held items and layers, the mods' layers, its name tag, shadow, flames, leash and
glowing outline, and `render_living_post`, and the renderer a mod registered for its type
(`register_entity_renderers`), which draws in the model's place; a mod drawing a model of
its own draws it here and cancels. A player's `render_player_pre` comes first, and a cancel here still asks its
`render_player_post`. Left uncanceled, `hidden.hide_named(name)` leaves only the part of
that name out of the vanilla model this frame (a villager's `nose`), drawn on the CPU or the
GPU: a hidden part takes its children with it and leaves the layers drawn on the model itself
(`getParentModel()`: a villager's type, profession and level, a spider's eyes), while its
armour, held items and other layers keep every part. An entity is drawn afresh each frame:
`draw.keep()` does nothing here.
Name tag visibility and optional replacement text.

Asked as a frame is built and drawn: set what your mod needs in
`RenderNeeds`, including entity runs and the world's depth without a shader pack.

After a player is drawn (NeoForge's `RenderPlayerEvent.Post`): once a frame for each player
whose `render_player_pre` wasn't canceled, after its `render_living_post`, or right after its
`render_living_pre` when only that one was canceled. `player`, `who` and `draw` are as
`render_player_pre` has them, and what it draws is kept; `parts` are the posed parts
`render_living_post` gets, None when the living pre hook was canceled. The player's name tag, leash,
flames and shadow are drawn after it, as `render_living_post` says.

Before a player is drawn (NeoForge's `RenderPlayerEvent.Pre`): once a frame for each other
player in view and for this window's player in third person (and F5 front view), before its
`render_living_pre`. `player` is its render state, `who` its profile name and whether it is
this window's own player, and `draw` the frame `render_living_pre` gets. Set `canceled` to
skip all of the player's drawing this frame, `render_living_pre`, `render_living_post` and
`render_player_post` included. Left uncanceled, `hidden.hide(part)` (or
`hidden.hide_named(name)`) leaves only that part out of the vanilla model this frame (after
Skin Customization), as a mod drawing its own outer skin layer does: a hidden part takes its
children with it (the hat goes with the head), while its armour, held items and other
layers, the cape among them, keep every part.

`RenderTooltipEvent.GatherComponents`: the elements of `stack`'s
tooltip (`ItemStack.getTooltipLines` as text lines, then the image
component its item's `tooltip_component` part answered), once
`item_tooltip` has run and before any wrapping or measuring. Add,
change, reorder or remove elements; the lines draw in order, then the
images in order, under any bundle's contents. `max_width` starts at -1,
no limit, which leaves the lines as they are; a mod that sets it
wraps every line wider than that, in GUI pixels. Set `cancel` and
nothing is drawn, and no `render_tooltip_texture` is asked. Asked each frame
the tooltip shows, never for one the stack hides. Client-side.

`RenderTooltipEvent.Pre`: a tooltip, laid out and about to be placed and drawn. `place`
holds the point it hangs from in GUI pixels (the cursor, or the point the screen gives
it), before the tooltip positioner adds its offset and keeps the box on screen; set `x`
and `y` to move it. `screen_width` and `screen_height` are the screen's size. `elements` are its text lines, then its images, as `render_tooltip_gather_components`
left them (a tooltip with no item has only lines), and are read-only here. `stack` is the
item the tooltip describes, `None` for a text tooltip. Set `cancel` and nothing is drawn,
and no `render_tooltip_texture` is asked. Asked each frame a tooltip shows, only while a mod listens.
`draw` is the tooltip's GUI drawing context. Custom drawing stays visible even when
the tooltip is cancelled; `draw.gui_draw_item_with` draws a stack with optional count text.
Client-side.

`RenderTooltipEvent.Texture`: the look of a tooltip box about to be drawn. Set `texture`
to a tooltip style (`<namespace>:<name>`) and the box draws as vanilla draws a
`tooltip_style`: the GUI sprites `<namespace>:tooltip/<name>_background` and
`<namespace>:tooltip/<name>_frame` from the resource packs, each nine-sliced as its
`gui.scaling` says or stretched without one. A style whose background or frame no pack
has keeps the fills, where vanilla draws the missing texture. Left `None`, the box is
Horizon's solid fills, in `background` and the `border_top` to `border_bottom` gradient,
as ARGB. `stack` is the item the tooltip describes, `None` for a text tooltip. Asked each
frame a tooltip shows, only while a mod listens. Client-side.

A once-a-frame sample of the replay's clock, on a frame it moved: `position_ms` is where
it is now, in ms from the recording's start (0 to its length), after the recording's
packets up to there were processed in order (a packet the game cannot decode or apply
is skipped). Not heard on a frame the clock stood still (paused,
at the end, or the frame it opened on, which `replay_opened` tells of). After a seek,
the next one is heard on the frame the seek is first drawn, with exactly the position
the seek applied, even when that is where the clock already was; the clock runs on from
there on the frame after. For a timeline or a camera path that follows playback.

Its event's fields are fixed: on the wire every field is encoded and its layout hashed,
so adding one later breaks wasm mods built against this one; `#[non_exhaustive]` is for
Rust callers only (docs/modding/src/concepts/wire-types.md).

neoforge: none (Horizon's replays; NeoForge has no replay playback)

hooks.doc:
The replay of `recording` closed, whatever closed it: a mod's `replay_close`, Escape,
the pause menu's Disconnect, or another replay opening over it. Heard once, after
the replay is gone (`host.replay_state()` is none, or already the next replay's
only after its `replay_opened`) and before a standalone replay's world is left.

Its event's fields are fixed: on the wire every field is encoded and its layout hashed,
so adding one later breaks wasm mods built against this one; `#[non_exhaustive]` is for
Rust callers only (docs/modding/src/concepts/wire-types.md).

neoforge: none (Horizon's replays; NeoForge has no replay playback)

hooks.doc:
A `replay_open` the game accepted opened nothing: `request` is the id the call
returned, `recording` the id it was asked for, `error` why:
- `Superseded`: a later `replay_open` replaced it before the game took up its read
  recording;
- `Unreadable`: the recording turned out damaged or of another version once read;
- `WorldBusy`: a world was joined, left or opened, or the replay playing closed or
  replaced, before it was ready, or another world entry took its place while it waited;
- `Unavailable`: the replay's session couldn't start, the game began closing, the
  person cancelled the wait for it (Escape while the world loads), or the replay playing
  kept its place: the camera path edited in it couldn't be saved, or the editor saved
  into the very archive this request read (which holds it as it was before).

Every accepted request ends in exactly one `replay_opened` or `replay_open_failed` with
its id; only a game closing first promises neither. A single-player world already left
for the replay stays left; anything else stays as it was.

Its event's fields are fixed: on the wire every field is encoded and its layout hashed,
so adding one later breaks wasm mods built against this one; `#[non_exhaustive]` is for
Rust callers only (docs/modding/src/concepts/wire-types.md).

neoforge: none (Horizon's replays; NeoForge has no replay playback)

hooks.doc:
A replay is open and its first frame is set up: `recording` is its id (as
`replay_open` takes it; empty for a recording no id names), `duration_ms` its length,
`standalone` whether it owns its session, and `request` the id `replay_open` returned
for the mod request that opened it, or 0 for a replay opened any other way (the
replays list, `/studio replay open`, the control socket). Heard for every opening, and
only once the recording has been read: one that can't be played opens nothing and is
not heard of here (a mod's request hears `replay_open_failed`). `host.replay_state()`
reads the replay from here on. A replay opened over another one is heard after
`replay_closed` of that one.

Its event's fields are fixed: on the wire every field is encoded and its layout hashed,
so adding one later breaks wasm mods built against this one; `#[non_exhaustive]` is for
Rust callers only (docs/modding/src/concepts/wire-types.md).

neoforge: none (Horizon's replays; NeoForge has no replay playback)

hooks.doc:
A server player's client answered a resource pack in play (vanilla's
`ServerboundResourcePackPacket`): `status` is `Action`'s number, 0
successfully loaded, 1 declined, 2 failed download, 3 accepted, 4
downloaded, 5 invalid URL, 6 failed reload, 7 discarded. Heard when the
packet arrives, after the server has handled it; it cannot be stopped.
The player's state is swapped in, so the helpers and `PlayerRef::tell`
work. The pack a dedicated server offers in the configuration
(`resource-pack` in `server.properties`) is answered before the
player has joined, and those answers are not heard. Once for each
answer, on a server.

neoforge: none (NeoForge has no resource-pack status event)

hooks.doc:
Where a player whose respawn point is the block `state` at `pos` stands up when they
respawn there (`IBlockExtension.getRespawnPosition`), or that they can't respawn there.
`entity_type` is the respawning entity's type, always `minecraft:player`, and
`orientation` the yaw saved with the respawn point. `position` starts at vanilla's answer:
a bed's or a charged respawn anchor's stand-up spot facing the block, a forced point's
free column, or empty where vanilla finds no spot. Set `Some((position, yaw, pitch))` to
stand the player there, or `None` to send them to the world spawn with
`missing_respawn_block` set. An answer with a non-finite value is ignored. An anchor still
loses a charge only when the answer is a spot. Asked on the server as the respawn point
is resolved, before `player_respawn_position`, which receives the answer as its original
position and may still redirect it, and as a player leaves the End, which resolves the
point the same way. The level is read-only. NeoForge asks only beds; this is asked
for any block, so a mod block that is neither a bed nor an anchor can be a respawn point.
With no part attached to the state, the game checks the hook subscription and the block
key before any event conversion, so the cost is one table lookup per respawn. Diverges
from upstream: new hook.

A player right clicks a block (NeoForge's
`PlayerInteractEvent.RightClickBlock`): once per hand, where
`useItemOn` starts, on the clicking client and on the server (`click`
says which, with the block, the hit, the hand and its stack, and the
player), for a spectator too (the server then only lets one open a
menu). Before the block's own use (a chest, a door, a lever) and the
item's (`Item.useOn`, `native_use_on`).

`use_block`: False skips; True overrides sneak; Default skips when sneaking with either hand full
(sneaking still blocks use when both stacks bypass sneak use). `use_item`: False skips; True forces
even an empty hand or cooldown; Default requires a held stack off cooldown. Empty hands reach
ItemAfterBlock with no stack, but no item Part. Adventure restrictions still apply; block consumption ends the click. Cancelling
skips both and answers `cancellation_result` in their place:
`Pass` (the default) goes on to the item's own use (`Item.use`) and
then the other hand, `Fail` ends the click, and `Success`,
`SuccessServer` or `Consume` end it as used, with the swing they name.
A spectator never reaches item use after a `Pass`; the client goes
straight to the other hand instead.
A mod that keeps players out of land cancels with `Fail`.
On the server, a consuming result fires `any_block_use` once, including
a consuming cancel. The inner criteria are skipped by cancellation unless
the mod explicitly triggers them; the helpers fire only their named criterion.
A consuming item phase fires `item_used_on_block` with the pre-block
snapshot (including an empty hand) before the outer criterion.
The outer criterion sees the stack held when block use started, with the
action's own in-place changes: consumption, damage, component edits, and
the creative-mode count restore. It sees an empty stack if the action
used it up. Neither a listener's hand replacement nor the action's whole
replacement (such as a bucket becoming a water bucket) changes this original.
This matches vanilla, which passes the same stack object it read before
the action. Single player uses this same server contract.
Item-internal triggers (such as shears) can legitimately
fire `item_used_on_block` in addition to the game mode's trigger.

The local player right-clicks empty space with an empty `hand`.
Client-side only; the server does not receive this event.

`PlayerInteractEvent.RightClickItem`, immediately before `Item.use`.
Cancel skips its Part and vanilla behaviour; its result defaults to
`Pass`. `Success`, `SuccessServer` and `Consume` end the client's
hand loop. `Success` swings on the client, `SuccessServer` on the
server, and `Consume` has no swing.

A structure template is about to place the block `state` at `pos` turned by `rotation`
(`IBlockExtension.rotate`, where vanilla runs `state.mirror(mirror).rotate(rotation)`):
`state` is already mirrored, and `rotated` starts at the game's own answer (vanilla's
table, or a mod block's template's). Set it to another state of the same block to place
that instead. A state of another block, or one the game does not have, is refused and
the game's answer kept. Asked for every block a template places: world generation's
structures, `/place template`, the structure block and the jigsaw pieces that join
them, and the template snapshots `structure_template` reads. Mirroring stays the
game's. Server-side, on the worldgen worker threads and on the server thread, with the
server's worldgen `context`: no `Host`, no writes; `context.state_with_property` builds
states. A panicking part is contained and the game's answer kept. Diverges from
upstream: new hook.

Execute a parsed mod command after permission checks and argument resolution.
Return `Flow::Cancel` when handled. `source` identifies origin and permission,
independent of `execute as`. Feedback honours silence, track-output and the swapped-in player.

neoforge: none (a command's executor is part of the Brigadier node added in RegisterCommandsEvent; CommandEvent only watches executions)

hooks.doc:
A task a mod scheduled with `schedule_task` is due, at the start of the server tick it
was due on, after `server_tick`'s start phase, in the order the tasks were scheduled.
`id` is the id `schedule_task` returned, `owner` the `[mod] id` of the mod that scheduled
it and `token` the value it passed. Every mod is asked about every task, so a mod ignores
tasks it does not own. Server-side.

neoforge: none (vanilla MinecraftServer.tell(TickTask); NeoForge adds no event for it)

hooks.doc:
A menu opens on this client for block `block`, a mod's: set `screen`
when the block is yours, to lay its screen out (`screen_draw`
draws it). The server asks it too: a slot it hides is not in the menu
there either, so shift-clicks never fill it.

neoforge: none (Horizon declares a block's screen through hooks; NeoForge registers a Screen class per menu with RegisterMenuScreensEvent)

hooks.doc: A typed character that no text box took (`ScreenEvent.CharacterTyped.Post`, vanilla's `Screen.charTyped` returning false), once per printable character that `screen_char_typed_pre` let through: `c` and `modifiers` as there. Set `canceled` and it counts as handled (nothing further reads it, so it changes nothing). It does not fire for text a box took, nor on Options and the title's own screens, where the key's text is routed in place between their boxes. A held edit modifier makes the key a shortcut, so its character is not taken and fires it. Same screens as the key press. Fires on the window only, while a screen of the game's or the title's is open (the screens the `_pre` input hooks cover), for real mouse or keyboard input and not a pad's or the keyboard focus's, and only when the matching Pre did not cancel it. It fires on the screen open after the key acted, as for the Pre.

A character was typed at the open screen
(`ScreenEvent.CharacterTyped.Pre`, vanilla's `Screen.charTyped`):
`screen` is the screen it is, `c` the character, `modifiers` GLFW's
bits (shift 1, control 2, alt 4, super 8), and `field` a copy of the
focused text box. Set `canceled` and that one character never reaches
a text box.

`field` is `None` with no box focused, and for the boxes that keep
their own validators: Options' and World Options' fields, the game
rules' and the block editor's. `cursor` and `highlight` count Unicode
scalar characters, and a character sees the box as the one before it
left it. Change `value`, `cursor` or `highlight` and the box takes the
change, cancelled or not, so cancel to replace the character yourself.
New text goes through the box's own filter and length limit, and what
follows the box (chat suggestions, a search's results, the anvil's
name) follows it. `max_length`, `multiline` and whether `field` is
`None` stay the box's: a change to them does nothing.

It fires once per printable character of a key press's text and once
per character of the input method's committed text, never for a control
character (Enter, Backspace, Tab, Delete, Escape, a Control letter):
those are keys, and the game reads them as keys, not as text. A key's
characters fire after the key has acted, as GLFW's char callback comes
after its key callback (`KeyboardHandler.charTyped`): `screen` is the
screen open then, so a key that closes the screen (the inventory key)
leaves none to hear its character, where vanilla's closed screen hears
nothing, and one that moves the focus types into the box it moved to.
They fire even when `screen_key_pressed_pre` cancelled the press
that carried the text, as NeoForge delivers `CharacterTyped.Pre` for a
cancelled `KeyPressed.Pre`: the characters left reach the text box
without the key's own effects. Cancelling one character drops only that
one. The control socket's `type` fires it too, but not for its `\b`
backspace. Same screens as the key press, and it fires with no text box
focused (there is nothing to take the character then).

A left or right (`right`) press at `at` (GUI pixels from the screen's
top left, so outside it too) on block `block`'s screen, a mod's, over
no slot: set `button` to a menu button id when it is on one of yours.
Horizon sends it to the server (`ContainerButtonClick`,
`menu_button` there) and the press goes no further.
The `screen` that was open is being replaced (`ScreenEvent.Closing`), after `screen_opening` let it.

Draw block `block`'s screen at `origin` (its top left, GUI pixels),
over a plain panel with its slots' frames and under the items and
labels, from the menu's data slots `data` (the block entity's `data`
on the server): data slots are 16-bit on the wire as in vanilla (a
bigger value wraps), and `data` is empty until the server's first
values arrive, so read it with `get`. Draw with `native_sprite`, `native_fill` and
`native_text`.

The hook `native_screen_exclusion` asks: a mod adds the rectangles it
draws over `screen` (a side panel, a button column) to `areas`, in GUI
pixels, `[x, y, width, height]`. NeoForge has no counterpart in the
game; recipe viewers ask for it through their own API
(`EmiExclusionArea`, JEI's `IGuiContainerHandler.getGuiExtraAreas`).
Client-side.

neoforge: none (NeoForge has no counterpart in the game; recipe viewers define their own API)

hooks.doc:
A screen was observed opening or changing rectangle, at most once per frame
(`ScreenEvent.Init.Post`).

A key press that no screen took (`ScreenEvent.KeyPressed.Post`, vanilla's `Screen.keyPressed` returning false): `key`, `repeat` and `modifiers` as in `screen_key_pressed_pre`. Set `canceled` and the press counts as handled: the game's own key handling (its key bindings, hotbar and toggles) never sees it. It does not fire for a key a screen took (a text box, the focus keys, Escape-close, an inventory key, a merchant or recipe-book key). A key that has no vanilla name fires nothing. The control socket's `key` fires it too, for a press (never a release). Fires on the window only, while a screen of the game's or the title's is open (the screens the `_pre` input hooks cover), for real mouse or keyboard input and not a pad's or the keyboard focus's, and only when the matching Pre did not cancel it. It fires on the screen open after the game handled the input, so an input that closed the screen fires nothing.

A key went down over the open screen (`ScreenEvent.KeyPressed.Pre`,
vanilla's `Screen.keyPressed`): `screen` is the screen it is, `key`
vanilla's name for the key (`key.keyboard.e`) — a key with no name
fires nothing — `repeat` whether it is
the keyboard's auto-repeat of a held press (Horizon's extra; NeoForge
folds repeats into the event), and `modifiers` GLFW's bits (shift 1,
control 2, alt 4, super 8). Set `canceled` and the press goes no
further: no focus move, no Escape-close, no inventory or hotbar key, no
typing by the key itself.

It fires for the window's presses and their repeats, and for the
control socket's `key` (a release fires nothing), after the window's
own shortcuts have run — the fullscreen and screenshot keys, the debug
keys and the narrator — and while a screen of the game's or the title's
is open (Options and the pack list opened from the title screen count,
with no player and no `menu`; the title's own). It does
not fire on the connect and loading screens, nor for a server dialog, the server pack,
link and code-of-conduct prompts, a book or a sign editor drawn over
gameplay, nor while a world loads or saves: the key there stays the
game's own. A cancelled press's release still runs, and its characters
are GLFW's separate char callback and still come; see
`screen_char_typed_pre`.

A key release that no screen took (`ScreenEvent.KeyReleased.Post`, vanilla's `Screen.keyReleased` returning false): `key` and `modifiers` as in `screen_key_released_pre`. Set `canceled` and the release counts as handled: the game's own key handling never sees it, so a held mapping stays down; cancel a release only when you cancelled the press it ends. Fires on the window only, while a screen of the game's or the title's is open (the screens the `_pre` input hooks cover), for real mouse or keyboard input and not a pad's or the keyboard focus's, and only when the matching Pre did not cancel it. It fires on the screen open after the game handled the input, so an input that closed the screen fires nothing.

Before an open screen handles a named key's release (same screen gate as key presses).
Cancel bypasses screen handling; physical keys and mapped keyboard hold/toggle state release.

A mouse button went down over the open screen and the screen has handled it (`ScreenEvent.MouseButtonPressed.Post`, vanilla's `Screen.mouseClicked` returning): `screen`, `button` and `modifiers` as in `screen_mouse_button_pressed_pre`. Not cancellable. NeoForge's event also carries `wasClickHandled` / `wasReleaseHandled`; this one has no such field, because Horizon's screens take their input in their own arms and report nothing back. There is no double-click flag: Horizon does not track double clicks. Fires on the window only, while a screen of the game's or the title's is open (the screens the `_pre` input hooks cover), for real mouse or keyboard input and not a pad's or the keyboard focus's, and only when the matching Pre did not cancel it. It fires on the screen open after the screen's arms ran, so a press that closed the screen fires nothing.

A mouse button went down over the open screen
(`ScreenEvent.MouseButtonPressed.Pre`, vanilla's
`Screen.mouseClicked`): `screen` is the screen it is, `screen.mouse`
where the pointer is (so there is no position of its own), `button` the
button's GLFW index (0 left, 1 right, 2 middle, 3 back, 4 forward; a
button past those is the platform's own number, which differs between
systems) and `modifiers` GLFW's bits (shift 1, control 2,
alt 4, super 8). Set `canceled` and the press goes no further: no slot,
no screen button, no drag, no hotbar key, no sort or header button.

It fires before anything the screen does with the press, on the window
only, and while a screen of the game's or the title's is open (Options
and the pack list opened from the title screen count, with no player
and no `menu`; the title's own screens, their
`screen.id` from the title state machine). It does not fire on the
connect and loading screens, nor for a server
dialog, the server pack, link and code-of-conduct prompts, a book or a
sign editor drawn over gameplay, nor while a world loads or saves: the
click there stays the game's own. A gamepad click or a click the
keyboard's focus sends is not the mouse and fires nothing.

A mouse button went up over the open screen and the screen has handled it (`ScreenEvent.MouseButtonReleased.Post`, vanilla's `Screen.mouseReleased` returning), with the fields of `screen_mouse_button_released_pre`. Not cancellable. NeoForge's event also carries `wasClickHandled` / `wasReleaseHandled`; this one has no such field, because Horizon's screens take their input in their own arms and report nothing back.
