Fires on the window only, while a screen of the game's or the title's is open (the screens the `_pre` input hooks cover), for real mouse or keyboard input and not a pad's or the keyboard focus's, and only when the matching Pre did not cancel it. It fires on the screen open after the screen's arms ran, so a release that closed the screen fires nothing.

A mouse button went up over the open screen
(`ScreenEvent.MouseButtonReleased.Pre`, vanilla's
`Screen.mouseReleased`), with the same `screen`, `button` and
`modifiers` as `screen_mouse_button_pressed_pre` and fired at
the same point. Set `canceled` and the release goes no further: a
pressed slot keeps what it took and no drag, slider or scrollbar lets
go.

Cancel a release only when the press it ends was cancelled too: a
release the screen took ends the drag or the scroll it began, as it
does in vanilla, and no guard here un-cancels it. Same screens as the
press; a press that opened another screen ends on that one.

A held-button pointer movement has gone through the open screen's drag handlers (`ScreenEvent.MouseDragged.Post`, vanilla's `Screen.mouseDragged`): `button`, `delta` (GUI pixels, `screen.mouse` the new position) and `modifiers` as in `screen_mouse_dragged_pre`. Not cancellable. Horizon's drag handlers report nothing back, so it fires whether or not one of them used the drag. Fires on the window only, while a screen of the game's or the title's is open (the screens the `_pre` input hooks cover), for real mouse or keyboard input and not a pad's or the keyboard focus's, and only when the matching Pre did not cancel it. It fires on the screen open after the game handled the input, so an input that closed the screen fires nothing.

Before a real held-button movement reaches screen drag handlers.
`screen.mouse` is the current GUI position; `delta` is its GUI-space movement.
Cancel keeps the new cursor position but skips all screen drag handlers.

The wheel turned over the open screen and the screen's scroll handlers have run (`ScreenEvent.MouseScrolled.Post`, vanilla's `Screen.mouseScrolled`): `scroll` and `modifiers` as in `screen_mouse_scrolled_pre`. Not cancellable. Horizon's scroll handlers report nothing back, so it fires whether or not one of them scrolled. Fires on the window only, while a screen of the game's or the title's is open (the screens the `_pre` input hooks cover), for real mouse or keyboard input and not a pad's or the keyboard focus's, and only when the matching Pre did not cancel it. It fires on the screen open after the game handled the input, so an input that closed the screen fires nothing.

The wheel turned over the open screen (`ScreenEvent.MouseScrolled.Pre`,
vanilla's `Screen.mouseScrolled`): `screen` is the screen it is,
`screen.mouse` where the pointer is (so there is no position of its
own), `scroll` the wheel's movement in x and y as the game's own scroll
handler scales it (a line times the wheel sensitivity: with Discrete
Scrolling on, a notch is ±1, its sign only; a touchpad's pixels are
divided by 30), and
`modifiers` GLFW's bits (shift 1, control 2, alt 4, super 8). Set
`canceled` and nothing the screen would scroll moves: not the bundle
under the pointer, nor a list, slider, scrollbar or map. Nothing else
reads the wheel while a screen of the game's is open, so no hotbar slot
changes either.

It fires before the screen scrolls anything, for the window's wheel
(horizon-ctl's `scroll-at` sends it through the window too), and
while a screen of the game's or the title's is open (Options and the
pack list opened from the title screen count, with no player and no
`menu`; the title's own). It
does not fire on the connect and loading
screens, nor for a server dialog, the server pack, link and
code-of-conduct prompts, a book or a sign editor drawn over gameplay,
nor while a world loads or saves: the scroll there stays the game's
own. A wheel a gamepad or the keyboard's focus sends is not the mouse
and fires nothing.

`Gui.setScreen` is about to replace the `current` screen with `new`
(`ScreenEvent.Opening`; the screen `playing` is none: vanilla's null).
Answer `ScreenOpening::Cancel` to keep the current one, or
`ScreenOpening::ModScreen` to open a mod's own screen instead.

After a screen's preedit handler (`ScreenEvent.Preedit.Post`) and only
when no text field took the composition (the handler returned false:
vanilla's focused field takes it, so this is a preedit no field
wanted) and `screen_preedit_pre` did not cancel. Same arguments.

Before a screen's preedit handler (`ScreenEvent.Preedit.Pre`, vanilla's
`GuiEventListener.preeditUpdated`): the input method is composing
`full_text` (empty when the composition ended), with the caret at
byte `caret_position`, split into `blocks` of which `focused_block` is
the one being converted. Set `canceled` and no text field sees it, and
`screen_preedit_post` does not fire. Fires on the window while a
screen is open, even when no text field is focused.

The open screen is about to draw its contents (`ScreenEvent.Render.Background`, after vanilla's `renderBackground` and before `render`): draw here for what must sit under the screen's widgets, items and tooltips. Not cancellable. The screen has drawn its background panel; its widgets, slots and items draw over this hook. Screens without a panel, such as the title and chat, fire it before their contents. It does not fire when `screen_render_pre` cancelled. Fires once a frame on the window, for the screens `screen_render_post` covers: a screen of the game's, the title's own screens, Win and Options. Not while playing with no screen, nor for a server dialog, the server pack, link and code-of-conduct prompts, a book or a sign editor drawn over gameplay. Draw with `native_fill`, `native_sprite` and `native_text`; `screen.rect` is the screen's container panel (or the whole window).

The open screen has drawn its contents (`ScreenEvent.Render.Foreground`, vanilla's point before the deferred tooltips and the preedit overlay). Not cancellable. Tooltips, the dragged stack and the preedit overlay draw over this hook; use `screen_render_post` for drawing over the screen's tooltips. It does not fire when `screen_render_pre` cancelled. Fires once a frame on the window, for the screens `screen_render_post` covers: a screen of the game's, the title's own screens, Win and Options. Not while playing with no screen, nor for a server dialog, the server pack, link and code-of-conduct prompts, a book or a sign editor drawn over gameplay. Draw with `native_fill`, `native_sprite` and `native_text`; `screen.rect` is the screen's container panel (or the whole window).

Ahead of the effect panels beside the survival and creative
inventories (`ScreenEvent.RenderInventoryMobEffects`, vanilla's
`EffectsInInventory.extractRenderState`): `available_space` is the
width in GUI pixels right of the container, at least 32 (with no effect
to show, or less room, vanilla draws nothing and this does not fire).
`compact` picks icons over full panels (vanilla's choice is compact
under 120) and `horizontal_offset` shifts the stack right (negative
left). Set `canceled` and the panels are not drawn: draw your own with
`screen_render_post`. Once a frame while the screen draws them,
on the window only; if the effects space changes within a frame (the
recipe book opening between two layout builds), it is asked again for
the new space. The exclusion areas follow this choice in the same frame.

The open screen has drawn itself and its tooltips (`Screen.extractRenderStateWithTooltipAndSubtitles`,
the point of `ScreenEvent.Render.Post`): draw over it with
`native_fill`, `native_sprite` and `native_text`, `screen.rect` being
its container panel (or the whole window) and `screen.id` the screen
it is. Once a frame on the window, never while playing with no screen;
`&self`, so it reads and draws only. The Win and Options screens call
it on their own path, after their drawing.

It does not fire for the screens drawn over gameplay after it (a
server dialog, the server pack, link and code-of-conduct prompts, a
book, a sign editor): those keep `Screen::Playing`, which it skips (the
server pack prompt hides an open screen too, and that screen does not
fire under it), and draw over what it drew, while vanilla's
`ScreenEvent.Render.Post` fires for them. The title's own screens
(`title`, `world_select`, `world_create`, `multiplayer`…) fire it too,
their `screen.id` from the title state machine and the whole window
their `rect`, and no dialog or prompt over them.

Before the open screen draws itself (`ScreenEvent.Render.Pre`, vanilla's `Screen.renderWithTooltips`): draw to put something under it, or set `canceled` and the screen is not drawn, and neither is its `screen_render_background` or `screen_render_foreground`. The world, the HUD layers and the toasts still draw, and `screen_render_post` still fires. Fires once a frame on the window, for the screens `screen_render_post` covers: a screen of the game's, the title's own screens, Win and Options. Not while playing with no screen, nor for a server dialog, the server pack, link and code-of-conduct prompts, a book or a sign editor drawn over gameplay. Draw with `native_fill`, `native_sprite` and `native_text`; `screen.rect` is the screen's container panel (or the whole window).

Room for a mod's own panel right of the open container screen's window, in GUI pixels:
`right` starts at 0; raise it to the width your panel takes beside the window, its gap
included, and leave it be otherwise. Later mods see earlier mods' answers: keep the larger
(`event.right = event.right.max(mine)`). When the window, the recipe book open beside it and
that room all fit across the screen, the window and the book move left by half the room
(rounded down), so the three stay centred as vanilla's recipe book moves the window right to
make room for itself (`RecipeBookComponent.updateScreenPosition`); when they don't fit,
nothing moves. This API is right-only: mod panels reserve the right while the existing
recipe book occupies the left; left reservations are not part of this hook.
The query's `ScreenView::rect` is pre-reservation. Later draw/input views expose the
shifted window; check that rectangle's right edge plus the room against the viewport.
Keep this query pure and cheap. Its answer is memoized for the frame and screen; recursive
queries during dispatch see zero. Asked once a
frame while the player's inventory, a container or a mod's menu screen is open, not for the
creative inventory, a merchant's or a beacon's screen, nor while the recipe book covers the
window of a narrow screen; an answer that changes geometry builds the layout again in the
same frame (slots, book and effect panels move with the window). Not finite or below 0
counts as 0. Beyond NeoForge: a mod there reads the container screen's `leftPos` but has no
event to move it, so it draws in the space that's left.

neoforge: none (a NeoForge mod reads AbstractContainerScreen.leftPos and cannot move it)

hooks.doc:
The tooltip at `at` (as in `screen_click`) on block `block`'s
screen, a mod's, over no item: push its lines when it is over
something of yours. Legacy colour codes (§) work.

`Screen.extractTransparentBackground`: draws the translucent dark background
behind an in-game screen (inventory, container, creative, book, sign, editor).
Set `canceled` (or return `Flow::Cancel`) to suppress the vanilla dark gradient,
allowing a mod to draw its own background or apply menu background blur
via `Host::apply_screen_blur`. API @API:screen_transparent_background@.

An F2 screenshot has been read back, before either PNG is written
(`ScreenshotEvent`). Runs on the client thread with a `ClientHost`.
`image` is the in-memory frame (`getImage`): RGBA8, top to bottom,
`width * height * 4` bytes. Change it and the normal PNG is that image.
A length other than `width * height * 4` writes nothing and reports
screenshot failure. The HDR copy is not this image. Change `file_name`,
a relative path inside the player's screenshots folder, or set `message`
to replace the success chat line. `None` uses the normal translated,
clickable line for the final file name. Return `Flow::Cancel` to write
no files and post `message`, or the translated cancellation line when
`message` is `None`. Invalid paths (including symlinks) report screenshot
failure; parent folders are created. HDR copies follow the final name
with `-hdr.png`. Agent captures and world icons do not fire this hook.

A sculk catalyst at `pos` has begun blooming after taking experience.
The catalyst block state has changed. Server-side.

The server is about to open its worlds: nothing of the world is
loaded yet (NeoForge's `ServerAboutToStartEvent`, "called before the
server begins loading anything"). Vanilla's `MinecraftServer.loadLevel`
start. Server-side: the single player server thread once Play is
pressed, a dedicated server once its settings are read. Each is
followed by `server_started` or
`world_lifecycle`'s `WorldOpenFailed`. `dedicated` tells a dedicated server from the single
player one.

NeoForge's `ServerChatEvent`: a player's chat message, through their
chain and the chat filter, is about to be broadcast.
`player_id` is the server's entity id for the player, `player` their
UUID, `username` their name and `raw_text` what they typed. `message`
starts as that text; replace it and players see the new message
(`withUnsignedContent`: a signed message keeps its signature), and
the log shows it. Set `cancel` and nobody sees it, and it doesn't
count toward the chat spam limit. Commands (`/say`, `/msg`...) are
not chat here. Server-side, with no player's state swapped in.
A component deeper than 512 nodes refuses capture or the whole writeback;
no event field is applied if any Text field fails conversion.

Paper's `PaperServerListPingEvent`: a client asked a server for its
status (the server list's ping, the status request in the status
protocol state), and the answer is about to be sent. `protocol` is the
protocol version the client's handshake stated and `virtual_host` the
host name it connected to (the part before its first NUL, empty when
it stated none). The writable fields start as what vanilla's
`MinecraftServer.buildServerStatus` sends: `motd` the description,
`favicon` the server icon as PNG bytes (`None`: no icon; bytes that
are not a PNG send no icon either), `online` and `max_players` the
counts, `sample` the names and UUIDs the player list shows (vanilla's
shuffled pick of at most 12; empty when the server hides its online
players), and `hide_players` false. Set `hide_players` and the
answer has no players part at all. Set `cancel` and the connection is
closed without an answer. At most 64 sample entries are kept. An
answer that is longer than a client reads (32767 characters) is
replaced by the plain one. Server-side, once for each status request,
on the game thread: the connection waits half a second for the mods,
and sends the plain answer if they have not finished. There is no
player, so no player's state is swapped in.

neoforge: none (NeoForge has no such event; Bukkit's ServerListPingEvent)

hooks.doc:
The server has opened its worlds and is about to run its tick loop
(NeoForge's `ServerStartedEvent`): every level is loaded, no player has
joined, and the first tick has not run. Fired where `WorldOpenReady` was,
on the single player server thread and on a dedicated server, once per
open that succeeds (a failed open fires `WorldOpenFailed` instead).
`dedicated` tells a dedicated server from the single player one.

Fired once immediately after `server_about_to_start`, before the server
accepts play, on both integrated and dedicated servers. A failed startup
still reaches `server_stopped`.

Fired once at the end of server teardown, after `server_stopping` and
the final save attempt and storage release. Also fired when startup or
teardown fails after startup began, including when a shutdown listener
panics, on integrated and dedicated servers.
Failed opens save only worlds already adopted by the server (the prepared
level is installed; the session lock alone is not adoption). A failed
save still reaches this hook, but does not emit `WorldCloseFinal`.

The server begins teardown (NeoForge's `ServerStoppingEvent`), including
after startup or the tick loop failed:
the start of vanilla's `MinecraftServer.stopServer`, with the worlds
still loaded and the players still connected and not yet saved, so a
mod can save its own data or tell them. `world_lifecycle`'s
`WorldCloseFinal` follows once the worlds are saved. A server whose loop
fails still fires this before the final save attempt and `server_stopped`.

The authoritative server tick's phases: `ServerTickStart` before any
level is ticked (NeoForge's `ServerTickEvent.Pre`), `ServerTickEnd`
after the last (`.Post`). Read blocks with `native_server_block`, by
dimension: which level `self.world` holds here is not defined. A paused
pass fires nothing; a frozen world carries `world_running` false except
during a requested step. `host.server_has_time()` says whether optional
work still fits before the next tick is due (`ServerTickEvent.hasTime`).

`/tick rate` set the server's rate, or a `/tick sprint` ended
(`MinecraftServer.onTickRateChanged`, before its autosave wait is adjusted). Vanilla calls
this for every `/tick rate`, the rate it already had included, and at each end of a sprint:
on its own, by `/tick sprint stop` or by `/tick freeze`, the rate then being what it was.
`host.tick_stats()` reads the rate. A client told the server's rate is not a server:
nothing fires there. Server-side. Beyond NeoForge: there is no counterpart.

neoforge: none (vanilla MinecraftServer.onTickRateChanged; NeoForge adds no event or extension for it)

hooks.doc:
The player changed setting `key` of mod `mod_id` on its page in Options > Mods
(`Registrar::register_setting`); the new value is kept already, so read it with
`setting_bool` and its siblings. Only mod `mod_id` hears it: a mod is told of its own
settings, never another's.

neoforge: ModConfigEvent.Reloading (a ModConfigSpec value set on the config screen)

hooks.doc:
The values native mods hand their shader packs in this frame,
`partial` ticks past the last tick (0 to 1): a pack's WGSL reads
them as `frame.mods` (eight `vec4<f32>`). Write the slots your own
pack reads; a mod that bundles its pack as `native-<mod id>` is the
one that pack is for. Asked once a frame while a pack is on; a value
that isn't finite reads as 0 (`native_shader_params_now`).

`MobEffect.shouldApplyEffectTickThisTick` for a content mod's effect
`effect` (an `EffectKey` for `ruby:bleeding`), each tick a player or a mob has it, in
`MobEffectInstance.tickServer` before it counts down: `tick_count` is
the ticks left (the entity's tick count when infinite). Set `apply`
and `native_apply_effect_tick` follows. Server-side.

neoforge: none (vanilla MobEffect.shouldApplyEffectTickThisTick; NeoForge adds no event or extension for it)

hooks.doc:
NeoForge's `IItemExtension.shouldCauseBlockBreakReset`: does a break
restart because the main hand changed? `stack` is the stack the break
began with (vanilla's `destroyingItem`), `held` the main hand now
(`None` for an empty hand). `reset` arrives with vanilla's answer: not
`ItemStack.isSameItemSameComponents(held, stack)` (count and damage
left out). `false` keeps the break and its progress going; `true`
aborts it and starts it again from 0. A `true` for an unchanged stack
restarts the break every tick, so it never finishes. Asked on each
`continueDestroyBlock` and `startDestroyBlock` of the block the break
targets, on the local player's client (single player and a server's
client alike). Only the `ItemPart`s attached to `stack`'s item are
asked. Client-side.

NeoForge's `IItemExtension.shouldCauseReequipAnimation`: does the
first-person hand lower and raise again to show `stack`, the stack the
hand holds now? `old` is the stack the hand shows (`None` for an empty
hand), `slot_changed` whether `stack` came from another slot (always
false for the off hand). `reequip` arrives with vanilla's answer
(`!FirstPersonHandsAndItems.shouldInstantlyReplaceVisibleItem`: the
same stack changed in place, or an equal one but for its damage, is
shown at once). `true` lowers the hand and raises it with `stack`;
`false` shows `stack` at once. Asked each client tick, for each hand,
while the shown stack differs from the held one by slot or by value;
an unchanged hand and an empty hand aren't asked. Only the `ItemPart`s
attached to `stack`'s item are asked. Client-side.

`IBlockExtension.shouldCheckWeakPower`: set `check` to decide whether
indirect power is read through this block. `check` starts with vanilla's
conductor answer. `direction` is the input side of the block being powered,
opposite the queried block's output side. Authoritative servers only.

Whether a fluid's side beside a block state uses the fluid's overlay sprite (water's `water_overlay`)
instead of its flowing sprite (`IBlockExtension.shouldDisplayFluidOverlay`): set `event.overlay`.
`overlay` starts with vanilla's test, true beside a `HalfTransparentBlock` or `LeavesBlock` (for a content
block, its template's class), so a part can turn the overlay on or off. `event.fluid` is the fluid as it is
asked: a source at amount 8, or a flowing fluid at amount 7, not falling. A fluid with no overlay sprite,
such as lava, draws its flowing sprite whatever the answer. The answer depends on the state and the fluid
alone and is resolved at join or explicit visibility refresh, never on a meshing worker: the client asks once for every state and fluid where
it resolves `block_render_visibility` (joining a world, `ClientHost::refresh_render_visibility`), and the
meshing workers read the table. The level and position are dropped: the meshing workers run no mod code.
With no part answering, nothing is asked and meshes are unchanged. Diverges from upstream: new hook.

Whether a block state hides the face a fluid beside it draws toward it
(`IBlockExtension.shouldHideAdjacentFluidFace`): set `event.hidden` and the fluid's face toward the block is
not drawn. `event.direction` points from the fluid to the block (Horizon's reading, not checked), and
`event.fluid` is the fluid as it is asked: a source at amount 8, or a flowing fluid at amount 7, not falling.
`hidden` starts false. Vanilla's tests still apply first: a fluid beside the same fluid, or behind a face
that occludes it, draws no face there whatever the answer. The answer depends on the state and the fluid
alone and is resolved at join or explicit visibility refresh, never on a meshing worker: the client asks once for every state and fluid where
it resolves `block_render_visibility` (joining a world, `ClientHost::refresh_render_visibility`), and the
meshing workers read the table. The level and position are not arguments. With no part answering, nothing
is asked and meshes are unchanged. Diverges from upstream: new hook.

`BlockBehaviour.shouldRedstoneWireConnectTo`: set `connected` to say
whether redstone wire connects to the block `state` at `pos`.
`direction` points from the wire toward the neighbouring block, or is
None when the wire asks about the block above or below. `connected` holds vanilla's answer: change
it when the block is yours. Asked whenever wire settles its shape:
answer from `state` and `pos` without touching the world. When the
answer changes, and once the wire is placed, update its neighbours
(`level.update_neighbors`). Authoritative servers only.

neoforge: none (vanilla BlockBehaviour.shouldRedstoneWireConnectTo; NeoForge adds no event or extension for it)

hooks.doc:
A player finished editing a sign: `ServerGamePacketListenerImpl.updateSignText`
has taken their update packet and every check has passed (they were
editing that sign, within reach, the sign is not waxed, the chat filter
let the text through), right before the lines go on the sign. `pos` in
`dimension`, the `front` or back side, and the four `lines` as written,
plain text with the formatting codes still in (vanilla strips them
afterwards). Rewrite `lines` (made four lines again) and that is what
the sign gets, without a second look from the chat filter, or set
`cancel` and the sign keeps its old text. With the player's state
swapped in, so `PlayerRef::tell` and the helpers that act on the player
reach them. Once for each update a player sends on a server. Not told:
the host's own editing of a sign on a LAN or single-player world
(the editor writes into their world directly), and the sign changes
that are no edit of the text (dyeing, glow ink, waxing, `/data`,
`/setblock`, mods' `native_with_mod_block_entity`).

Enough players have slept through the night in level `dimension`
and the clock is about to move to the morning (NeoForge's
`SleepFinishedTimeEvent`, vanilla's `ServerLevel.tick` when it moves
the clock to `wake_up_from_sleep`). `adjustment` says where the clock
goes and may be changed: it comes in as
`Marker(minecraft:wake_up_from_sleep)`, vanilla's own, and a mod may
set `Absolute`, `Relative` (from `current`, the day time now) or
another `Marker`; a later mod reads what an earlier one left.
`new_time` is the morning vanilla resolved, read only, for a mod that
computes from it. Contract version `2`: in version `1`, `new_time`
was the value a mod wrote; a time is now written as `Absolute`.
`current` and the result are times of the level's own clock (its
dimension type's default clock, else the Overworld's). The game
resolves `adjustment` once after every mod: a time before `current`,
a time past `i64::MAX`, or a marker the level's clock does not define
is refused, as `setTimeAddition` refuses one, and the clock moves to
the morning. Only the Overworld's clock defines markers today, so on
any other clock every `Marker`, vanilla's included, falls back to the
morning. When even the morning is past `i64::MAX`, `new_time` is
`current` and the clock stays. On the server, only when the `advance_time` rule is on;
`time_skip` then hears the jump to the resolved time and may
still cancel it. The players wake and the weather resets as usual
either way. Set `canceled` and the clock is left where it is, as
NeoForge's cancel leaves it: `time_skip` is not asked either.

On an authoritative server, `CampfireBlock.isSmokeSource` for the
block `state` under a campfire, as the campfire is placed or the block
under it changes: `Some(true)` for your own blocks makes the campfire a
signal fire whose smoke rises higher, as over a hay bale. The level is
read-only.

neoforge: none (vanilla CampfireBlock.isSmokeSource; NeoForge adds no event or extension for it)

hooks.doc: The sound engine opened its output (`SoundEngineLoadEvent`): once at window start, after each resource reload (with the `context` of the new resource generation) and when the output device changes. Nothing fires with no sound output (no device, or audio turned off). Client-side only.

The sound type of a block state this part is attached to (`IBlockExtension.getSoundType`) is being read, to play one of its sounds. `pos` is the block and `state` its state; `entity` is nullable, as NeoForge's: the id and type (`minecraft:player`, `minecraft:creeper`) of the entity stepping on it, landing on it, placing it or digging it (a sniffer), and `None` for a break and for a placement by no entity (a dispenser); `cause` says which sound is about to play (`BlockSoundCause::Step`, `Fall`, `Place`, `Break` or `Dig`). It is asked only where NeoForge asks it, not for the hit sound while a block is mined (that has its own client hook upstream) nor for sculk growth. A part may change `sound` (`event.sound`), which starts as the state's own sound type: its event names, volume and pitch. The game then applies vanilla's factors for `cause` to the volume and pitch and plays that one sound. An answer whose volume or pitch is not finite and at least 0, or one of whose events is not a `namespace:path` id, is dropped whole and the state's own sound type is used. An event the resources lack plays nothing, as in vanilla; a mod's own event (from its content mod's `assets/<id>/sounds.json`) is sent to players by name. It runs for each sound, on the side that plays it, so register the mod on both and keep the listener a pure function of its inputs: the placer's client and the server ask for the same placement and must agree. It is given the loop `context` of the side that asks, and takes no `Host`. It cannot play no sound, several sounds, or a sound somewhere else (`playStepSound` and `playFallSound` can). Diverges from upstream: new hook.
The world's spawn point changed to `pos` and `angle`.
A sponge at `pos` absorbed water and became wet. Server-side.

A server entity is about to be placed by `/spreadplayers` (NeoForge's
`EntityTeleportEvent.SpreadPlayersCommand`, vanilla's
`SpreadPlayersCommand.setPlayerPositions`): once per entity, after the
spread worked out its spot. `entity` is its network id, `player` its UUID (None for a
non-player), `from` where
it stands and `target` the spot. A mod may move `target` (a value that
is not a number is ignored). Canceling leaves the entity where it is;
the spread's other entities, its random draws and its feedback are
unchanged.

An entry of an atlas definition whose `type` a mod registered (`register_sprite_sources`,
vanilla's `SpriteSource.run`), asked at the entry's place in the definition's `sources`,
each time the atlas is loaded or reloaded, on the resource loader. `config` is the entry's
JSON object converted to a `Tag`, `atlas` the atlas being listed and `listed` the sprites
the entries before it listed. Push `SpriteSourceOutput`s to `output` only for a source your
mod owns; they apply in order once every mod has answered.

neoforge: none (vanilla SpriteSource.run of a type RegisterSpriteSourcesEvent registers; NeoForge adds no event for it)

hooks.doc:
Models no blockstate names, registered once on the client before resources load.
`models` collects plain namespaced file ids, baked unturned. `forms` collects
rotated/UV-locked or combined dependencies under a namespaced result id.
Every resource load rebakes both from the active pack files. A missing dependency
drops the entire form and logs its registering mod. Resolve the results through
`RenderAssets::model` after `model_baking_completed`, just like plain ids.

The block state the camera at `viewpoint` sees of the block `state` at `pos`
(`IBlockExtension.getStateAtViewpoint`), so a partial fluid block, a tank or a
waterlogged mod block can show underwater fog only while the eye is really inside the
liquid. `seen` starts at `state`: set it to the state whose fluid and powder snow the
camera should read. Asked as the client finds the fluid at the camera
(`Camera.getFluidInCamera`) for the block at the eye, the block above it and the blocks
at the near plane's centre and corners: the fog, the field of view in a fluid, the
water vision, the sky's dark disc and conduit power's underwater vision read it. The
client host is read-only; answer from the event alone, as the game asks every frame. With no
part on any block the subscription check skips the asks; otherwise each block read costs
one table lookup. Diverges from upstream: new hook.

A block is about to take the state it is placed in
(`Block.getStateForPlacement(BlockPlaceContext)`), `state` the block's
own default state. Answer only for your blocks: put the state you want
in `answer` as `Some(Some(state))` — a state of that block, as vanilla
sets properties on its own `defaultBlockState` (another block's is
ignored) — or refuse the placement with `Some(None)`: the block goes
nowhere and the stack is kept, as vanilla's `null`. Left empty, the
block's own placement runs. `context` is
vanilla's `BlockPlaceContext` (the clicked face, the placer's rotation,
the clicked position, whether the clicked block is being replaced, the
item in hand) and `fluid` the fluid in the position the block would go
in, which a waterlogged block reads. Build the state from `state` with
`native_state_with_property`, and know whether `state` is yours with
`native_state_block`. It is asked for every placer that goes
through vanilla's placement (a player's `BlockItem.place`, a
dispenser's `DirectionalPlaceContext`), and the answer still takes its
survival and entity obstruction checks. A trait mod returns
`Some(Some(state))` to choose a state, `Some(None)` to refuse, or
`None` to leave the answer to the next mod or vanilla. Changes to the event's fluid
copy are mod-provided data forwarded to later Parts, never consumed by the engine.
Authoritative servers only.

neoforge: none (vanilla Block.getStateForPlacement; NeoForge adds no event or extension for it)

hooks.doc:
Opt a block with a registered block entity type into state-aware creation.
Asked once per block when a level's immutable factory ownership table is built.
Set true and never clear an earlier answer. For these blocks, `block_entity`
receives the actual state and no answer creates no entity. Existing entities
survive property changes within the same block.

neoforge: none (static factory ownership for vanilla EntityBlock.newBlockEntity)

hooks.doc:
A workstation `PlayerRef::open_station` opened is closing for `player` (UUID): the player
closed it, it was no longer valid or another menu replaced it. `window`
is the id `open_station` returned and `menu` its type. `inputs` holds its input slots
(the crafting grid's nine, row by row; a station's in its menu's order) before they go
back to the player's inventory, or drop when it is full (`clearContainer`). A listener
may empty a slot to keep its stack itself, in an item's container component; only
emptied slots count, and any other change to `inputs` is ignored, so no stack is made
or grown here. Stations the game opened on a block never fire it, nor does a player
leaving: their inputs go back to the inventory before it is saved.

Submit unlit geometry after particle submission, before opaque rendering
(NeoForge 26.3 `SubmitCustomGeometryEvent`, vanilla `LevelRenderer.submitFeatures`).
Client-only, noncancellable. `view` holds only camera, partial tick and game time,
not full extracted level state or visible sections. Submit from extracted state.

NeoForge's `SweepAttackEvent`: a player's damaging melee hit on a
`target` (`minecraft:zombie`, `minecraft:oak_boat`) is about to sweep or
not, after `critical_hit`. `vanilla_sweep` is `Player.isSweepAttack`
(a charged, grounded, not critical sword hit below the speed limit);
`sweeping` starts as it and may force or stop the sweep; `canceled` skips
the later mods and keeps `sweeping` as it is (a mod doing its own sweep
cancels with `sweeping` false). A critical hit that sweeps has both
sounds. Fires on the Game that runs the attack, and on the attacking
client, which only asks.

A guest asked to complete `command`; owned API `Suggestion` records may be
added to or filtered from `suggestions`. `range` is the replaced byte range.
The game snapshots completions only when a listener subscribes.

neoforge: none (NeoForge has no generic tab completion event)

hooks.doc:
Tags changed, and what depends on them should be rebuilt (NeoForge's
`TagsUpdatedEvent`); `cause` says how. The place to drop caches
derived from the data and to rebind what depends on it.

`ServerDataLoad`: the server's data tables are built. The recipes,
tags, loot and advancements of the world's data packs, and the files
mods added through `data_pack_files`, are what the helpers read
from now on. `reload` is false on a world's first open, before its
chunks and players are loaded, and true after `/reload` rebuilt them,
once the players were sent the new data. Fires on the server, the
single player's integrated server included.

`ClientPacketReceived`: a client applied the block, item and fluid
tags its server sent, and `block_in_tag`, `fluid_in_tag` and the
`tags()` service read them from now on. Fires once at login, for
configuration's tags, and once for each update in play, on the game
thread. `integrated_server` is true in single player, where both
causes fire: `cause.should_update_static_data()` is then false here,
so that data the two threads share is updated once, on the server.

Runs in Reloading: published asset/data queries can rebind caches,
including on first open; world handles and transactions remain
unavailable.

A projectile hit the target block at `pos`, which now has `strength`
output power. Server-side.

A server entity is about to be teleported by `/tp` or `/teleport` (NeoForge's
`EntityTeleportEvent.TeleportCommand`, in `TeleportCommand.performTeleport`, once per
teleported entity): `dimension` is the level it arrives in, `entity` its network id,
`from` its feet now and `to` where the command sends it. A mod may move `to` (a value
that is not a number is ignored). Canceling leaves the entity where it is; the command
still reports success. `entity_teleport` and `player_teleported` hear it after.
Server-side. Diverges from upstream: new hook.

An atlas was stitched and published (`TextureAtlasStitchedEvent`): `atlas` names it. Fires
once per atlas, the blocks' first and then the GUI's, on the first load before
`client_setup` and after every successful resource reload (F3+T, a pack turned on or off, a
server's pack) before `client_resources_reloaded`; a reload that fails fires nothing. Look
the sprites a mod draws up here, once, and keep what it finds until the next stitch of that
atlas: `texture_sprites` for [`TextureAtlas::Blocks`], `gui_sprite` for
[`TextureAtlas::Gui`]. Never look them up by name every frame. Client-side.

The server changed its thunder state through `/weather`. Set `cancel`
to keep the previous thunder state and timer. Server-side.

An authoritative server's `ServerLevel.tickBlock` is about to run a
due scheduled tick of the block `state` at `pos` (`BlockState.tick`):
the block is still the one the tick was scheduled for. Change the
block with `native_set_block_property` and set `handled` to skip the
block's own tick; a block changed without `handled` takes its own
tick as it is now, if it is still the tick's block.

neoforge: none (vanilla BlockBehaviour.tick; NeoForge adds no event or extension for it)

hooks.doc:
How many milliseconds a client tick lasts (`Minecraft.getTickTargetMillis`, the target the
window's `DeltaTracker.Timer` divides the frame's time by): `millis` comes in as vanilla's
(50 at 20 ticks a second, longer when the server's `/tick rate` is slower); set it to speed
up or slow down the client's fixed-step clock, a "timer". Asked once a frame, in menus too,
before the frame's client ticks run (at most ten a frame). An answer that is not a finite
number above zero keeps vanilla's. Only the window's clock changes: a server still ticks
at its own rate. Client-side. Beyond NeoForge: there is no counterpart. Diverges from
upstream: new hook.

neoforge: none (vanilla Minecraft.getTickTargetMillis; NeoForge adds no event or extension for it)

hooks.doc:
The overworld clock is about to jump, from sleep or `/time`. Set
`cancel` to keep `from`.

TNT at `pos` is about to be lit (primed): a flint and steel or a fire
charge on it, fire burning it, a redstone signal, an arrow, or a
dispenser's flint and steel or TNT item. `player` is the server player
whose click lit it, with their state swapped in (so `PlayerRef::tell`
answers them), None when no player is behind it (fire, redstone, an
arrow, a dispenser). Set `cancel` and it is not primed: a TNT block
stays where it is (one that fire or a signal had already taken out is
put back, without a block update), a dispenser's TNT item stays in it.
Not asked: TNT set off by a blast (`explosion_detonate` spares
blocks), a TNT minecart and a sulfur cube. Server-side and in single
player.

neoforge: none (NeoForge has no TNT priming event; the primed TNT entity joins with EntityJoinLevelEvent)

hooks.doc:
A client toast is about to enter its queue (`ToastAddEvent`). Return
`Flow::Cancel` to discard only this candidate, before slot allocation,
animation or sound. `kind` identifies its family; music is `Other`.
Replace `title` and `description` to change the displayed components.
For advancements the title is the frame label and the description is
the advancement name. Existing recipe/system toasts updated in place
do not fire another add event. Client-lib and title producers prepare
candidates for the game to admit with a `ClientHost` before applying.

The state the block `state` becomes under a tool action (`IBlockExtension.getToolModifiedState`:
an axe's strip, scrape or wax-off, a shovel's flatten or douse, a hoe's till), asked of the
block a tool is used on (`tool.pos`). `final_state` starts with vanilla's answer, `None` for a
block the tool does nothing to: set it to `Some(new)` to allow the action or replace its
result (a mod log an axe strips, a path a shovel makes), and `Cancel` it to deny the action,
so the tool does nothing. `tool.simulated` says the game is only asking what the tool would
do (`LevelRef::block_transform`, NeoForge's `simulate`): answer the same and change nothing in
the world. A part answers before the global `block_tool_modification`, which still hears the
result and may change or cancel it; a cancelled part skips it. Asked for the block's own parts only, so
a block with none costs nothing.

`Item.appendHoverText`: an item's own lines in its tooltip, after its
name and before its components' (enchantments, lore, attributes). Add
lines to `lines`, which arrives empty, each with a colour as `rgba` packs
it (`u32::MAX` keeps the text's own); `Text::legacy` reads `§` codes.
The stack has its components (`stack.data()`). Asked each frame the
tooltip shows, never for one the stack hides or a crossbow's loaded
projectile. NeoForge's `ItemTooltipEvent` is the corresponding line-building event;
this scoped hook adds attached parts' lines before component lines are assembled.
Afterwards [`Hooks::item_tooltip`]
sees the finished list, including these parts' lines.

Client-side image component for this stack's tooltip. Answer its width/height
in GUI pixels; finite positive dimensions reserve space after text and any
vanilla bundle component. None keeps the vanilla tooltip unchanged.

Render the measured component at origin, inside the tooltip background.
Stack is the component's data. Use native_sprite/native_fill/native_text;
Size is the whole tooltip content box: the widest component and the sum
of component heights (minus 2 normally; no subtraction for an item
tooltip with multiple components). Origin is this component's running
top and the box's left edge. All text is drawn before any images.
A server player selected trade `index` from `villager` in the trading menu.

A trade of a villager or a wandering trader was made
(`MerchantResultSlot.onTake` once the offer is taken): `merchant` is
the trader's entity id and `kind` its type (`minecraft:villager`,
`minecraft:wandering_trader`), `offer` the live one in the trading
session (not a copy) as the trade left it: `uses` counted, `result`
what the player got. Once per trade, so a shift-click that trades
several times is heard for each, after the trade's statistic and
`villager_trade` trigger. A mod may change the offer (Bukkit's
`PlayerTradeEvent#getTrade` is mutable): `uses`, `max_uses`, `demand`,
`special_price_diff`, `price_multiplier`, `xp`. The change stands: the
next click and the offers sent to the player see it. Not asked for a
trade window without a trader. The player's state is swapped in
(`host.players().acting_player()`). Server-side. Version 2: was a listen hook
returning the offer read-only; now collects the live offer as `out`
(the moment upstream's separate `merchant_offer_traded` covered).

An authoritative server is about to compute the state the block
`state` at `pos` takes now that its neighbour in `direction` is
`neighbour` (`BlockBehaviour.updateShape`). `state` may not be in the
world yet (a piston landing it): decide from `state`, not from the
block at `pos`. Answer only for your own blocks: put the new state in
`new` (`state` keeps the block as it is; air breaks it, with its drops,
on a neighbour update) and the block's own `updateShape` doesn't run,
nor the ticks it would schedule. The level is read-only, as vanilla's
`LevelReader`; ticks go through `native_schedule_block_tick` and
`native_schedule_fluid_tick` with `ticks` (`ScheduledTickAccess`). It
runs often, at least six times per `setBlock` that updates shapes
(more for redstone wire's diagonals and knock-on updates): keep it
short.

neoforge: none (vanilla BlockBehaviour.updateShape; NeoForge adds no event or extension for it)

hooks.doc:
`Item.getUseAnimation` of `stack` in use, for first- and third-person
rendering. `animation` arrives with the item's vanilla answer; mods may
change it. A `Spear` override on an item without kinetic data is refused
as `None`. Asked on the client when each render consumer updates; answer
from the stack alone.

neoforge: none (vanilla Item.getUseAnimation; NeoForge adds no event or extension for it)

hooks.doc:
`Item.getUseDuration` of `stack`, in ticks: `duration` arrives with
vanilla's (a consumable's time, 72000 for a shield, a spear, a bow,
0 for an item with no use over time). A mod's own item (outside
`minecraft:`) with no `consumable`, `blocks_attacks` or kinetic
weapon that answers above 0 is used over time on a right click, as an
`Item.use` that calls `startUsingItem`, until it is let go or the time
runs out (`living_entity_use_item_finish`). A consumable's time
changes too, potions and the other vanilla items keep their own.
Asked when a use starts, each tick a mod's item is in use, and each
frame the hand draws one in use, on both sides. It has no user, as
it is asked so often: answer from the stack alone.

neoforge: none (vanilla Item.getUseDuration; NeoForge adds no event or extension for it); LivingEntityUseItemEvent.Start can set a use's duration

hooks.doc:
A player uses `stack` (right click) with `self.hand`: in the air, or
on a block once `native_use_on` let it through, where `Item.use`
starts. Runs on both logical sides after the global right-click event.
Return an interaction result: Success swings on the client, SuccessServer
swings on the server, Consume handles without swinging. Fail skips this
item's use without swinging, then the off hand may be tried.
None lets later Parts answer; if none answers, the item's own use runs.
Some(Pass) skips later Parts and continues to the item's own use.
TryWithEmptyHand is block-phase-only and is treated as Pass here.
Cooldown items are skipped.
A server-only answer does not stop the client's off-hand prediction.
ClientHost permits reads and local effects, not authoritative writes.
`hand` is the interaction hand of THIS click, including an instantaneous
air use. Unlike this field, `living_used_item_hand` answers only during
active item use. This is `PlayerInteractEvent.RightClickItem.getHand`.
`player` is the clicking player's UUID and `player_entity_id` that
player's entity id on this logical side: the acting player's on a server
(a guest's own, never the host's), this client's own player on a client.
They name who clicked from the event alone, unlike `players().acting_player()`,
which only answers while the host has set the acting player.

`BlockBehaviour.useItemOn`: the block's own behaviour, with the
held item, on the server for each player. An answer replaces the
template's behaviour; `TryWithEmptyHand` tries `useWithoutItem` on
the main hand, and `Pass` goes on to the item's `useOn`.

neoforge: none (vanilla BlockBehaviour.useItemOn; PlayerInteractEvent.RightClickBlock cancels or answers before it)

hooks.doc:
`UseItemOnBlockEvent`: after a phase was chosen, before its Part or
vanilla behaviour. Cancel skips that behaviour and returns
`cancellation_result` (initially `TryWithEmptyHand`). In `ItemBeforeBlock`,
`Pass` continues to the block, skipping the item's `on_item_use_first`
Part; any result other than `Pass` ends the block interaction.
A block-phase `TryWithEmptyHand` can still try the empty-hand behaviour.

A player uses `stack` (right click) with `self.hand` on the block at
`pos`, `face` the face clicked (`[0, 1, 0]` is the top), once the
block itself let the click through (a chest still opens): where
`ItemStack.useOn` starts. Both logical sides answer independently:
a consuming client result ends the hand loop; only Success swings
there. SuccessServer and Consume consume without a client swing.
Fail ends the block path; Pass and TryWithEmptyHand fall through.
A server-only answer does not stop the client's off-hand prediction.
ClientHost permits reads and local effects, not authoritative writes.
Cooldown items are skipped. `hand` and `hit` describe this click;
`player` and `player_entity_id` identify its player on this side.

Client prediction cannot invoke server services:
```compile_fail
use mod_api::{ClientHost, prelude::*};
fn predict(host: &mut dyn ClientHost) {
    host.commands().run_command("say not a client prediction");
}
```

`BlockBehaviour.useWithoutItem`: the captured state's empty-hand method,
after useItemOn asks for it, on the server and main hand only.

neoforge: none (vanilla BlockBehaviour.useWithoutItem; PlayerInteractEvent.RightClickBlock cancels or answers before it)

hooks.doc:
`dimension`'s level has loaded the saved chunk tickets of `controller`
(NeoForge's `LoadingValidationCallback.validateTickets`), before its
first tick and after `level_load`, once for each open and each
controller registered with a validator that has tickets in the level.
`validation` holds that controller's tickets, block owners and entity
owners apart; the mod that owns the controller removes the ones that no
longer hold (a machine that is gone), and they stop forcing their
chunks. Server-side.

A vanilla game event is about to reach its listeners (NeoForge's
`VanillaGameEvent`, vanilla's `Level.gameEvent`): every event, in
`dimension`. `event` is its id (`minecraft:step`), `pos` where it
happened and `cause` the network id of the entity that caused it
(None for none). `affected_state` is the block state the event touched
(`GameEvent.Context.affectedState`, with `cause` its `sourceEntity`): the
block a player broke or placed, the block a mob stepped on; None where
vanilla passes none (`Context.of(entity)`).
Canceling keeps the sculk sensors, wardens and allays from hearing it.
Server-side.

A vault at `pos` changed to `state`. Its block state is updated.
Server-side.
A vault at `pos` is about to eject a loot item.

neoforge: none (NeoForge has no such event; Bukkit's BlockDispenseLoot)

hooks.doc:
A boat or minecart was created at `pos`, after it joined the level.
`kind` is the vehicle type. Server-side.

neoforge: none (NeoForge has no such event; Bukkit's VehicleCreateEvent)

hooks.doc:
A vehicle is about to take damage from a player's attack. `kind` is
`boat` or the minecart type; mods may change `damage` or set `cancel`
to leave its damage and wobble unchanged. The attack itself still
completes. Server-side.

neoforge: none (NeoForge has no such event; Bukkit's VehicleDamageEvent)

hooks.doc:
A boat or minecart is about to be destroyed at `pos`. TNT minecarts
that prime instead of breaking are not heard. Server-side.

neoforge: none (NeoForge has no such event; Bukkit's VehicleDestroyEvent)

hooks.doc:
A boat or minecart (`kind`, `minecraft:oak_boat`) moved since the last
tick (`VehicleMoveEvent`): `from` and `to` are its positions, heard
after the tick moved it. Once a tick for each vehicle that carries a
server player, whose state is then swapped in (as for
`run_mod_command`: `host.players().acting_player()`, `PlayerRef::tell` and
the item helpers reach them; `player` is their UUID), and for one a
server player rode and left, until it has stood still for ten
seconds (`player` is none, nobody is swapped in). It only hears.
Cheap when nothing moves: one position compare a tick for each watched
vehicle. Not heard: a vehicle moved before anyone rode it, a mount
(horse, pig...) or a vehicle carrying only a mob. Server-side, in the
level the vehicle is in.

neoforge: none (NeoForge has no vehicle move event; EntityTickEvent covers the tick)

hooks.doc:
A sound of a level the server opened for viewing (arismoko/horizon#3716) reached this client, and the
client asks where in the player's own level to play it. `level` is the viewed level's
handle (what `host.level` gives for it) and `position` the sound's position there; `sound`,
`source` and `seed` are the server's. `play_at` starts as None, and a sound left None is not
played. Set it to a position in the player's level and the sound plays there, as the
player's own level plays a sound packet (no distance delay), with the `volume` and `pitch`
the listeners leave and the same seed. A `play_at` that is not finite, or a volume or pitch
that is not finite and at least 0, plays nothing. Only a server of `horizon:levels`
revision 3 sends these. A sound bound to an entity of the viewed level has that entity's
position there, and plays at `play_at` without following it. Sounds of the player's own
level ask `play_level_sound_at_position` and
`play_level_sound_at_entity`, never this hook. With no listener the sound is dropped after
one check, with nothing decoded or allocated. Client-side. Diverges from upstream: new
hook, a Horizon addition with no NeoForge counterpart.

A village siege found a spawn position on the server. Set `canceled`
to stop the siege. There is one siege per dimension.

The world frame's local, world-space rim and colored-light sources.
Push requests; Horizon validates and limits them before rendering.
Called only while a world is visible.
Whether this block receives block entity changes through an adjacent conductor. Starts false.

The server changed its weather parameters. `raining` and `thundering`
are the requested final states. Set `cancel` to keep the previous
weather parameters. Server-side.
The dedicated server's whitelist changed to `enabled`.

neoforge: none (NeoForge has no such event; Bukkit's WhitelistToggleEvent)

hooks.doc: Before a wind burst interacts with blocks, `wind_burst(dimension, center, blocks)` receives the shuffled candidate positions. Remove positions to spare those blocks; entity knockback and the shuffle's random draws are unchanged. Not called when mob_griefing prevents a breeze from interacting with blocks. Bundles need "hooks": @API:wind_burst@.

neoforge: none (vanilla wind-charge block interaction; NeoForge adds no event)

hooks.doc:
After a window resize or applying a changed GUI scale, fullscreen, or Unicode font setting.
`width` and `height` are physical pixels; `gui_width` and `gui_height` are scaled GUI pixels.
Fires only when physical or scaled dimensions change.

A timed world-border size change finished on the server, after its
final size was applied. Server-side, including the single-player
server.

neoforge: none (NeoForge has no such event; Bukkit's WorldBorderBoundsChangeFinish)

hooks.doc:
The server world's border bounds changed, either immediately or when
its timed size change was requested.
The server world's border center changed.
The world is drawn (see [`WorldDrawn`]). Not called on the title screen's panorama.

The world's phases, read-only; `error_text` carries the engine's
own open-failure text, empty otherwise. Server-side. A server loop or final
save failure fires `WorldCloseFailed` with the error text.

The server completed a world save cycle. `wait` says chunk writes were
flushed before returning.

A world view is drawn (see [`WorldViewDrawn`]): once per view taken this frame, after
the frame's world and before [`world_drawn`], the views seen in a view (its `parent`,
one `nesting_depth` deeper) before it.

Asked once as each frame is built (not on the title screen's panorama): push the world
views (see [`WorldView`]) your mod wants drawn this frame, each parent before the views
seen in it. The world is drawn again from each one's camera into a target of its own.

An experience orb looks for a player to follow (NeoForge's
`XpOrbTargetingEvent`, `ExperienceOrb.followNearbyPlayer`), on a
server. `following` starts as the default: the nearest living player
within `scan_distance` (8) blocks who isn't a spectator, or `None`.
Set another player, or `None` to follow no one. The orb only goes
for a living player who isn't a spectator, in its level, and only
moves once they are within 8 blocks. Horizon looks again on every
orb tick (vanilla keeps the player it follows while they stay
within 8 blocks), so this is asked every tick for each orb: answer
fast.

`IItemExtension.getXpRepairRatio`: the durability points Mending
restores to `stack` per point of experience, where
`ExperienceOrb.repairPlayerItems` repairs the damaged Mending item it
picked, once per item it repairs. `experience` is the points being
spent (never 0) and `player` the player they go to. `ratio` arrives
holding vanilla's: the stack's `minecraft:repair_with_xp` repair
divided by `experience`, 2.0 for vanilla Mending. The repair becomes
`floor(experience × ratio)`, capped at the stack's damage; a ratio left
as it arrived keeps vanilla's repair exactly. A ratio that isn't finite
is refused and vanilla's repair is used; a negative one counts as 0.
A ratio that takes a positive repair to 0 leaves the experience
unspent, for the player. Only the parts attached to `stack`'s item are
asked: to change Mending for every item, change the enchantment's
`minecraft:repair_with_xp` effect in a data pack. Server-side,
including `PlayerRef::give_experience_points`.

The zoom a native mod asks for, applied while playing (the spyglass's
own view wins): set `zoom` when it is none yet.

neoforge: none (Horizon-only; ViewportEvent.ComputeFov is the nearest way to change the view)

traits.doc:
What a mod's registered targets and interpolations do (the `AnimationTarget` and
`AnimationChannel.Interpolation` a `RegisterJsonAnimationTypesEvent` listener registers). The
mod that plays an animation gives them to [`AnimationHolder::bake_with`], and they run in that
mod, called directly while it plays: no hook is dispatched per sample. An id one mod
registered loads in any mod's file, but plays only where an implementation of it exists: the
registering mod's own, or one a mod that depends on it supplies.

required.name: interpolate
required.signature: fn interpolate(&self, _: &Identifier, _: &[Keyframe], _: usize, _: usize, _: f32, _: f32) -> [f32; 3]

methods.doc: The target's `apply`: puts the sampled `value` on `part`.

The target's conversion of a keyframe's file values, applied once at bake as the built-in
targets apply `posVec`, `degreeVec` and `scaleVec`; the values unchanged by default.

The interpolation's answer for the segment from `keyframes[prev]` to `keyframes[next]`,
`alpha` of the way along (0 to 1, or NaN where vanilla's is: two keyframes at one time, or a
NaN time), times `scale`. `prev` and `next` are valid indexes.
methods.signature: fn interpolate(&self, _: &Identifier, _: &[Keyframe], _: usize, _: usize, _: f32, _: f32) -> [f32; 3]

methods.doc:
Whether this implementation plays `kind`, a registered target or interpolation: a target
and an interpolation of one id are separate types.

traits.doc: Client humanoid pose registrations, shared by native and wasm mods.

methods.doc:
Register a pose once in `Hooks::register`, keeping the returned token for
`get_arm_pose`. `name` must be namespaced in the registering mod's namespace.
Duplicate or malformed names refuse registration. The flags independently
select two-arm ordering and whether the opposite hand's pose gives way.
methods.signature: fn register_arm_pose(&mut self, _: &str, _: bool, _: bool) -> CustomArmPose

traits.doc: Read queries available on either host side.

methods.doc:
Capture a SNAPSHOT of membership and value bindings in the current dimension.
Later changes appear only in fresh queries. This is a residency view: an
entity removed but not yet swept may still appear; stale writes fail.
Construction never clones or decodes values; iteration decodes lazily.
methods.signature: fn query<'key, T: Send + Sync + 'static>(&self, _: &'key AttachmentType<T>) -> Result<AttachmentQuery<'key, T>, AttachmentError>

traits.doc: Explicit write-through queries, available only on server hosts.

methods.doc:
Capture a SNAPSHOT, not mutable references into the live store.
Set/remove join the caller's journal; no implicit transaction or Drop commit
occurs. Later changes require a fresh query, and stale writes fail.
methods.signature: fn query_mut<'key, T: Clone + Send + Sync + 'static>(&mut self, _: &'key AttachmentType<T>) -> Result<AttachmentQueryMut<'key, T>, AttachmentError>

traits.doc:
The current server's holders' values, erased to what crosses any boundary: the typed
[`AttachmentType`] methods are built on it, for a native mod and a wasm mod alike.

methods.doc: The value under `namespace:name` if it has been decoded.
methods.signature: fn decoded(&mut self, _: Holder, _: &str, _: &str) -> Result<Option<AttachmentValue>, AttachmentError>

methods.doc: Drop the value under `namespace:name`, saved or decoded; clients hear of it if `sync`.
methods.signature: fn discard(&mut self, _: Holder, _: &str, _: &str, _: bool) -> Result<(), AttachmentError>

methods.doc: Whether `holder` keeps a value under `namespace:name`, saved or decoded.
methods.signature: fn holds(&mut self, _: Holder, _: &str, _: &str) -> Result<bool, AttachmentError>

methods.doc: Send the value under `namespace:name` to the clients that see the holder again.
methods.signature: fn queue_sync(&mut self, _: Holder, _: &str, _: &str) -> Result<(), AttachmentError>

methods.doc: The saved form under `namespace:name` if it hasn't been decoded yet.
methods.signature: fn saved(&mut self, _: Holder, _: &str, _: &str) -> Result<Option<Compound>, AttachmentError>

methods.doc: Keep `value` under `namespace:name`, with what comes with it.
methods.signature: fn store(&mut self, _: Holder, _: &str, _: &str, _: AttachmentValue, _: AttachmentForm) -> Result<(), AttachmentError>

traits.doc:
Registration of new attribute types ([`Registrar::declare_attribute`](AttributesRegistrar::declare_attribute))
and wider bounds for existing ones ([`Registrar::widen_attribute_bounds`](AttributesRegistrar::widen_attribute_bounds)).

methods.doc:
Declare an attribute type of the mod's own (vanilla's
`RangedAttribute` in `BuiltInRegistries.ATTRIBUTE`, NeoForge's
`RegisterEvent`): `path` in the mod's namespace (`mana` of `mymod` is
`mymod:mana`), its `default` and `[min, max]` bounds, whether it
joins the attribute sync (`Attribute.setSyncable`), and the sentiment
that colors its tooltip lines (`Attribute.setSentiment`, POSITIVE by
default; the translation key is `attribute.name.<ns>.<path>`), and how its
tooltip lines read (`tooltip`: percentages, on/off, a base modifier; NeoForge's
`PercentageAttribute`, `BooleanAttribute` and `IAttributeExtension.getBaseId`).

Only both-side packages may declare attributes; other sides refuse because
declarations assign network registry IDs.
The declarations join the attribute catalog once, at load, appended
after every vanilla attribute **sorted by declaring mod id, then by
attribute id** — the order is the network id's, so every side running
the same mods builds the same numbers and vanilla ids never shift —
before entity attribute rows resolve, so a mod entity's declared set
may name the mod's own new attribute. Sanitizing a value (NaN → min,
else clamp) is the definition's own `sanitize`.

An id outside the mod's manifest-owned namespaces (a vanilla attribute's included),
a malformed id, a duplicate — of this mod's or another's, caught
where the declarations join the catalog — a non-finite default or
bound, bounds the default is not inside (`min > max` included), or a
base modifier that is not a namespaced id refuses, naming the mod.
methods.signature: fn declare_attribute(&mut self, _: &str, _: f64, _: f64, _: f64, _: bool, _: Sentiment, _: AttributeTooltip) -> Result<(), AttributeRegistrationError>

methods.doc:
Widen the `[min, max]` bounds of an attribute that already exists,
vanilla's or another mod's (`id` in full: `minecraft:max_health`), as
Java mods do with a mixin or an access transformer on
`RangedAttribute.minValue` / `maxValue`: every clamp of the attribute's
value, on both sides, then follows the wider bounds.

The asks of every mod join the catalog once, at load, after the
declared attributes and before entity attribute rows resolve. The
result is their union, whatever the load order: the lowest `min` and
the highest `max` asked, and never narrower than the attribute's own
bounds, so an ask narrower than what another mod widened to changes
nothing. The default value never moves. An attribute without bounds
stays without them.

Only both-side packages may widen bounds, so the client and the server
build the same catalog; the mod-set check at join is all a client
needs. A non-finite bound or `min > max` refuses here, naming the mod;
an attribute the catalog does not have, or one whose default is not
inside `[min, max]`, refuses the load where the asks join the catalog,
naming the mod.
methods.signature: fn widen_attribute_bounds(&mut self, _: &str, _: f64, _: f64) -> Result<(), AttributeRegistrationError>

traits.doc:
A mod's own brain behavior, run by the species' brain beside vanilla's:
started by `Brain.tick`'s start pass when its activity is active and its
entry condition holds, ticking until its duration runs out or
[`can_still_use`](Behavior::can_still_use) fails, stopped with vanilla's
own `stopAll`. One object per mob, built in
[`crate::EntityPart::register_behaviors`] wherever the brain is built, so
nothing of it is saved and a rebuilt brain starts fresh.

methods.doc:
`Behavior.canStillUse`: whether a running behavior keeps running.
Defaults to `false`, as vanilla's does — a behavior that does not
override it lives out the brain tick that started it.

`Behavior.checkExtraStartConditions`: asked after the entry condition
holds, before the duration is drawn.
The behavior's name for debugging (`Behavior.debugString`).
`Behavior.start`: the behavior began running.

`Behavior.stop`: the behavior stopped — its end, `can_still_use`
failing, or the brain's own `stopAll`.
`Behavior.tick`: every brain tick while the behavior runs.

traits.doc:
A mod's colour resolver: vanilla's `ColorResolver`, which the game blends over the biomes
around a block as it blends its own (`ClientLevel.calculateBlockTint`, over the biome blend
radius) and caches per section while it meshes. Held by the game and asked on the meshing
workers, so it keeps no mutable state and gets no `Host`.

methods.doc:
`getColor(biome, x, z)`: the colour of `biome` (`minecraft:plains`) at block column
`(x, z)`, 0xRRGGBB.

traits.doc: Registrar operations for biome modifiers.

methods.doc:
Declare a biome modifier `path` (`no_zombies` or `mymod:no_zombies`) in code: the same
operations as the data files in `data/<ns>/neoforge/biome_modifier/` (add and remove
features, add and remove spawns, add and remove spawn costs) on the biomes it names.
The game applies it with the data-file modifiers, once, when the world's tables build:
every addition first, then every removal, then every `ModifyBiome`, each in mod and
registration order. A world
no modifier names generates exactly as before.

`ModifyBiome` is NeoForge's MODIFY phase: it sets a biome's climate values and effects
colours (`horizon:modify_biome` in a file).
A modifier naming a biome, feature or entity type the world lacks (another mod's, a
convention tag) is skipped with a line in the log, as a data file is.

An id outside the mod's namespace, a repeated id, an empty list, a name that is not
namespaced, an unknown generation step, a spawner of weight 0 or with its smallest group
above its largest, a spawn cost that is not finite, and a climate number that is not finite, a colour above
0xFFFFFF or a temperature modifier other than `none` or `frozen` refuse the mods, naming the mod.
methods.signature: fn declare_biome_modifier(&mut self, _: &str, _: BiomeModifier) -> Result<(), BiomeModifierError>

traits.doc: Registrar operations for biome regions.

methods.doc:
Declare a biome region `path` (`highlands` or `mymod:highlands`): the mod's own biomes,
laid out by climate in `region.points`, in a share of the Overworld or the Nether set by
`region.weight` against vanilla's whole layout at 10. Each area belongs to one region,
and the nearest-point search runs among that region's points only, so a region never
competes with another's points.

The declared weight is the default a new world records; a world's saved layout, not the
mod, decides its regions from then on, and an existing world takes a new or changed
region only when its owner opts in. Regions are ordered by declaring mod id, then
region id.

An id outside the mod's namespaces, a malformed or repeated id, a dimension other than
`minecraft:overworld` or `minecraft:nether`, a weight of 0 or above 1000, no points, or
a point with no biome, an interval outside -2 to 2 or inverted, or an offset outside 0 to
1 refuses the mods, naming the mod. Biome existence and ownership are not checked
here; world setup must resolve names and refuse missing biomes.
methods.signature: fn declare_biome_region(&mut self, _: &str, _: BiomeRegion) -> Result<(), BiomeRegionError>

traits.doc:
A mod's biome source: vanilla's `BiomeSource`, whose code answers for a
level stem with `"biome_source": {"type": "modid:chaos"}`. Implemented once,
kept by the game; deterministic and stateless.

methods.doc:
`BiomeResolver.getNoiseBiome`: the biome at quart cell `quart` (a block
position >> 2, as `[x, y, z]`) of a world with `seed`, as an index into
[`possible_biomes`](Self::possible_biomes); an index past the list wraps
around it. Asked for every 4x4x4 cell of every chunk generated, so keep it
cheap and allocation-free. The same seed and cell give the same biome.

`BiomeSource.possibleBiomes`: the biome ids (`minecraft:desert`, a data
pack's or the mod's own) the source places, at least one. Asked once, at
startup; a level whose world lacks one of them refuses to open, naming it.
Structures and decoration read this list, as vanilla's do.

traits.doc:
What a tint source reads of the world around the block it colours: vanilla's
`BlockAndTintGetter`, over the region a section is meshed from (`RenderSectionRegion`: the
section's chunk and its eight neighbours). A position outside that region reads as air, no
fluid and the light of an unloaded chunk. Block entities are not part of the region.

methods.doc: `BlockGetter.getBlockState`: the state at `pos`.

`getBlockTint(pos, resolver)`: the resolver's colour at `pos` blended over the biome blend
radius, as opaque ARGB. A mod's resolver blends as vanilla's do.
`BlockAndLightGetter.getBrightness`: the stored light of one layer at `pos`, 0 to 15.
`BlockAndLightGetter.canSeeSky`: the sky light at `pos` is full.

`BlockGetter.getFluidState`: the fluid at `pos`, the empty fluid where there is none.
None outside the region, as `LevelHost::fluid_state` reads an unloaded position.
`LevelHeightAccessor.getHeight`: the build height.
`LevelHeightAccessor.getMinY`: the lowest block Y.

`BlockAndLightGetter.getRawBrightness(pos, darkening)`: the brighter of the block light
and the sky light less `sky_darken`.

`cardinalLighting().byFace(face)`: how much a face toward `face` is shaded, 0 to 1 (the
Nether's flat lighting in the Nether).

traits.doc:
What answers a capability for a block entity of one type: given the block entity and the
side asked about, its handler, or none to leave it to the next provider. A closure
`|host, at| Some(Box::new(Tank(at)))` is one.

methods.signature: fn attach_block_entity_part(&mut self, _: &BlockEntityTypeKey, _: &'static str, _: Arc<dyn BlockEntityPart>) -> Result<(), BlockEntityPartError>

methods.doc: Look up a vanilla or another mod's type. The final registry validates it at load.

Record the state declaration of Part `part`, or refuse it (as the mod's registration
refusal too): see `PartStateDeclaration::check`, and a key outside this mod's
namespaces or one it declared with another type. Mods reach it through
`block_entity_part_with_state`.
methods.signature: fn declare_block_entity_part_state(&mut self, _: &'static str, _: PartStateDeclaration) -> Result<(), BlockEntityStateError>

methods.doc:
Declare block entity type `path` in a namespace owned by this mod's manifest, held by `blocks`
(a bare name is this mod's); mods usually reach it through `block_entity_type`.

Answer block entity capability `name` for type `kind` with `provider`, asked ahead of the
game's own when `before_game`; mods reach it through `block_entity_capability`.
methods.signature: fn provide_block_entity_capability(&mut self, _: &'static str, _: &BlockEntityTypeKey, _: bool, _: BlockProviderOf)

methods.doc: Set the transform of a type declared by this mod.
methods.signature: fn set_block_entity_transform(&mut self, _: BlockEntityTypeKey, _: Arc<dyn BlockEntityTransform>)

traits.doc: What a block entity, mob or player submit hook draws with, in blocks under a pose stack (`PoseStack`): one per hook call.

methods.doc:
The frame on this client's animation clock, in ticks with the partial tick: what
turns `spin` parts. It counts the ticks this client's level has run (vanilla's
`TextureManager.tick` count): pausing and `/tick freeze` hold it, and the server's
time updates never set it back, unlike `game_time`. Each client counts from its
own start, so it means nothing on the server or to another client.

Draws block `block`'s model (`mymod:cog`, any block with a model) in
the state with `properties` (`[("axis", "x")]`, the rest default)
under `draw`'s pose, as vanilla's `submitBlockModel` draws a block in
an entity's place: a block's baked model, with its default tints. A
moving part that is no block is a standalone model
(`native_draw_model`). False for an unknown block or property.

Draws a box from `from` to `to` (texels of 16 per block, as a block
model's element) under `draw`'s pose, with the faces given, by
`Direction` (down, up, north, south, west, east), baked as a model
element's are (`FaceBakery`), times the 0xRRGGBB `tint`. A turned box
is drawn under a turned pose (`BlockEntityDraw::rotate_about`). False
when a face's sprite is unknown; that face is left out.

Draws `stack` as a still fluid filling `bounds` (`[x0, y0, z0, x1, y1, z1]` in blocks
under `draw`'s pose), as a tank's contents: `minecraft:water` or `minecraft:lava` with no
components. Each face tiles the fluid's animated still sprite (`block/water_still`), one
tile per block, cut at whole-block lines and keeping each part's place in its tile, with
no inset of the box. The tint is the stack's, not the biome's water colour, unless
`options.argb` replaces it. Sky light stays as `draw.light`; block light rises to the
fluid's own (15 for lava). No face is shaded by direction. Faces are sorted far to
near, alpha blended, culled from behind and write depth, drawn with the block entities
before the level's translucent terrain. A stack of 0 draws nothing and is `Ok` without
checking `bounds`; a refusal draws nothing.
methods.signature: fn fluid_box(&mut self, _: &FluidStack, _: [f32; 6], _: FluidBoxOptions) -> Result<(), FluidBoxError>

methods.doc: The level's game time, for animations.

Draws `stack` under `draw`'s pose as an item is drawn in the world
(`ItemModelResolver.updateForTopItem` and `ItemStackRenderState.submit`), centred on the
pose's origin, in its model's `display` transform: `Fixed` as a
campfire's or an item frame's, `Ground` as a dropped item's. `seed`
picks among random models (a campfire passes its slot plus its
position's hash). `owner_yaw` makes the block entity the item's
owner (`ItemOwner`), at the block's centre and turned that many
degrees (`getVisualRotationYInDegrees`), as a shelf is: a compass on
it points to its target from there. None draws it with no owner, as
a campfire does. False for an empty stack or one with no model. The
client's copy of a block entity has no item slots (`entity.items` is
empty there): send the stacks you draw in
`block_entity_update_tag` and read them from `entity.nbt`.
methods.signature: fn item(&mut self, _: &item::item_stack::ItemStack, _: ItemDisplayContext, _: Option<f32>, _: i32) -> bool

methods.doc:
Keeps what this call drew, with neither `block_entity_submit` nor
`block_entity_render_bounding_box` called until its state, block entity,
light or resource packs change. Parts marked with `spin` keep turning on the
animation clock (`animation_time`); other geometry stays as submitted. Do not bake frame-dependent
values into kept vertices: item glint and time-dependent item models stop
where they were, and neighboring blocks do not invalidate the cache.

The light the helpers draw with: the block's own
(`LevelRenderer.getLightCoords`), 16 times sky light in bits 0..8 and
16 times block light in bits 8..16.

Draws the resolved standalone model under `draw`'s pose: unturned, from
the block's lower north-west corner, lit by `draw.light`. Faces with a tint
index are multiplied by `tint` (`0xAARRGGBB`, the same as [`crate::WorldQuad::color`];
`0xFFFFFFFF` for none), alpha included. Faces with no tint index stay opaque.
A stale generation or absent slot returns an error without appending geometry.
methods.signature: fn model(&mut self, _: ModelRef, _: u32) -> Result<(), ModelError>

methods.doc:
Draws model part `part` and the parts under it under `draw`'s pose, as
vanilla's `ModelPart.render` does: each part moved to its place (in
texels, 16 to a block), turned about z, then y, then x, and scaled,
its faces textured from `sprite` (`mymod:entity/golem`, a content
mod's `assets/mymod/textures/entity/golem.png`, or vanilla's
`entity/zombie/zombie`) times the 0xRRGGBB `tint`. A part that isn't
`visible` draws nothing, one that skips drawing (`skip_draw`) only its
children. A mob's model is built in the model's own frame (+y down,
its front towards -z, its feet 24 texels down): in `render_living_pre`,
`draw.scale([1.0, -1.0, -1.0])` then `draw.translate([0.0, -1.501,
0.0])` first, as `LivingEntityRenderer` does. False for an unknown
sprite. API @API:model_layers@.
The frame's partial tick, 0 to 1 (`BlockEntityRenderState`).
`PoseStack.popPose`; the block's own pose is never popped.
`PoseStack.pushPose`: `pop` comes back to the pose as it is now.

Draws a quad with `corners` in blocks under `draw`'s pose, in a model
face's order (top left, bottom left, bottom right, top right as seen
from its front), textured with the `uv` rectangle (u0, v0, u1, v1 in
texels of 16 per side) of `sprite` (`mymod:entity/screen`,
`mymod:block/casing`, `block/stone`) times the 0xRRGGBB `tint`
(0xFFFFFF for none). False for an unknown sprite.

Turns what is drawn next by `degrees` about `axis` (counterclockwise
seen from the axis' positive end, as `Axis.rotationDegrees`) through
`pivot`, in blocks from the pose's origin: `[0.5; 3]` is the block's centre.
Scales what is drawn next by `by` about the pose's origin.
Lights what is drawn next with `light` (as `native_draw_light` reads it).

What is drawn next turns by itself: `degrees_per_tick` degrees each tick of the
animation clock (`animation_time`; a shaft at `rpm` turns `rpm * 0.3`), about `axis`
through `pivot`, both in blocks from the block's corner whatever the pose,
counterclockwise seen from the axis' positive end. Its angle is
`animation_time * degrees_per_tick + phase`: parts drawn with the same speed keep
their phases apart (a cog meshing with its neighbour). Draw the part at rest; the
game turns it each frame, and with `keep` without asking again until the block
entity changes. With a new speed, pass `old_angle - animation_time() * new_speed`
