as the phase to keep the part where it was. Quads drawn while it is active are lit
where they turn to. Until `still` or the next `spin`. A mob's frame draws it at rest.
What is drawn next stands still again, after `spin`.

Draws the resolved standalone model under `draw`'s pose, as [`Self::model`] places it,
with the terrain's own materials: the block sprites (animated, mipmapped as the options
set), back faces culled, colour and depth written as opaque terrain, lit by
`draw.light` raised by each quad's own emission. `options` picks the material
(each quad's `solid`, `cutout` or `cutout_mipped`, or one for all: cutout discards
under alpha 0.1 without mipmaps, cutout-mipped under 0.5 with them), the directional
shading (independent of light), one sprite drawn as another with moved UVs, a UV
shrink, and a `0xRRGGBB` tint on quads with a tint index. What a machine's belts,
shafts and casings draw with. A refusal draws nothing.
methods.signature: fn terrain_model(&mut self, _: ModelRef, _: TerrainModelOptions<'_>) -> Result<(), TerrainModelError>

methods.doc:
Draws `text` under `draw`'s pose as vanilla's `Font.drawInBatch` draws a component in
the world (a sign's line, a text display's): in the pose's x-y plane, one unit a font
pixel, y down, its left end at `at`, facing +z. Scale the pose first as a sign does
(`draw.scale([1.0 / 64.0, -1.0 / 64.0, 1.0 / 64.0])` for its letters, 8 pixels high).
Styles are drawn as name tags and text displays draw them: each span's colour (the
rest in the 0xRRGGBB `color`), bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, obfuscated, its
font, inline objects and `§` codes, right-to-left text in visual order. `glowing` text
is full bright (a glow ink sac's), the rest lit by `light`. With `outline`, a 0xRRGGBB
colour (`Some(0)` is black), each glyph is ringed with it as glowing sign text is
(`Font.drawInBatch8xOutline`; nine glyphs' worth of quads each). Returns the width
drawn, in font pixels (`Font.width`): centre a line by starting it at minus half its
width. Obfuscated glyphs change only when the block is drawn again: kept text stands
still. Clamp text read from NBT, and widen `block_entity_render_bounding_box`
for a long line. API @API:draw_text@.
Refuses text deeper than 512 component nodes before applying any changes.
methods.signature: fn text(&mut self, _: &text::Text, _: [f32; 2], _: u32, _: bool, _: Option<u32>) -> Result<f32, text::TextFormError>

methods.doc:
The width of `text` in font pixels, as `text` draws it, styles included
(`Font.width`), to lay a line out before drawing it.
Refuses text deeper than 512 component nodes.
Moves what is drawn next by `by`, in blocks.

traits.doc: A block's part that also answers for its block entity, and for the block like a [`BlockPart`].

methods.doc:
Initial saved data for a declared block entity (`EntityBlock.newBlockEntity`),
fired inside the write that creates it (`LevelChunk.setBlockState`), on
a server and on a client of one. `state` is the actual placed state for a
block declared through `stateful_block_entity`; its properties are available
through the Host's state registry. The declaration owns the type id. No
answer creates no entity for a state-aware factory; other declared types
start with an empty compound. The level is read-only, as `newBlockEntity`
gets no level.
Side: both.

Return `Some` to set `entity`; the first part returning `Some` wins.

A client tick of this client's copy of the mod block entity at `pos`
(`ClientLevel.tickBlockEntities`), when its `id` is yours and its
block's state ticks on the client (`block_entity_client_ticks`):
once per client tick while the level runs, in vanilla's ticker order
among the others, whether or not the copy is drawn. `block_entity` is
its handle, `state` its block's state and `entity` its data, read only,
as the frame's handling of the server's packets merged it before the
frame's ticks (`block_entity_update_tag`). Start, stop and fade
its sounds and add its particles here. Never called on a server, and
never again for a copy removed or whose chunk unloaded.
Side: client.

Whether block `block`'s block entity ticks on the client
(`EntityBlock.getTicker` asked with the client level): set `ticks` when
it is yours, and `block_entity_client_tick` runs for it once per
client tick. Asked once for each mod block, for all of its states,
the first time a client level ticks with a part that has a client tick.
Set `ticks` to true to make it tick, and never clear a value an earlier mod or mixin set.
Side: client.

The synchronized `tag` has been merged into this client's block entity.
`source` distinguishes chunk data from a later update packet. Empty chunk
compounds send no notice; empty update-packet compounds do. Absent tags
send no notice. Called once for each accepted tag,
only for a matching mod block entity that the client created.
Reads through `entity` already see the merged data. This notice cannot
change the received tag. Missing tags and vanilla block entities call nothing.
Related NeoForge receive paths `IBlockEntityExtension.onDataPacket` and
`handleUpdateTag` perform loading; they are not counterparts of this notice,
which runs after the merge.
Side: client.

The mod block entity `entity` has been added to its level, with saved
data already applied, before its first tick (`IBlockEntityExtension.onLoad`).
Fires once for each instance on both logical sides, including placement.
A chunk loaded again creates new instances and calls this hook again.
Read saved data through the attached handle and the supplied `HostSide`.
Side: both.

Where the mod block entity at `pos` draws, for culling
(NeoForge's `getRenderBoundingBox`): `bounds` is min x, y, z then max
x, y, z, in blocks from the block's lower north-west corner. It starts
as the block with a block of margin around it; widen it when your
`block_entity_submit` draws further (a tall shaft, a beam), or
set an infinite value for one never culled. Asked once a frame for each
within its view distance (`block_entity_view_distance`) whose chunk is drawn.
Side: client.

Every part gets `event.bounds` in order and may add, change or remove bounds.

Draw the mod block entity at `pos`, of block `block`
(`mymod:machine`), on this client: once a frame while it is in view
(vanilla's `BlockEntityRenderer.submit`: within its view distance, 64 blocks unless
`block_entity_view_distance` says otherwise, its chunk
faded in, and its bounds, `block_entity_render_bounding_box`,
in the frustum), when its `id` is yours. `state` is the block's state
(`blockEntity.getBlockState()`: read its `facing` with
`native_block_state_property`), `entity` holds what the server sent
(`block_entity_update_tag`). Add geometry with
`native_draw_quad`, `native_draw_cube`, `native_draw_block` and
`native_draw_item` under `draw`'s pose stack, which starts at the
block's lower north-west corner, in blocks; `draw` also has the partial
tick, the game time and the block's light.
Side: client.

A server tick of the block entity at `pos`, in vanilla's order among
the others (`Level.tickBlockEntities`), when its `id` is yours: read
and change its saved compound `nbt`, its item slots `items` (keep
their count: as many as its container has, none without one) and the
data slots its menu shows (`data`). It is out of the world during the
call (the block entity at `pos` reads as a `Mod` with an empty id, and
a save leaves it out); if the call removes or replaces it, `entity` is
dropped. Clients, the window's own in single player included, get
what `block_entity_update_tag` gives when its chunk is sent or
its block changes.
Each Part starts with `Changed` and sees the preceding accepted payload.
`*event.reply = BlockEntityTickReply::Unchanged` discards only this Part's
payload edits: no reply snapshot is encoded, decoded or applied. Earlier
Parts' `Changed` edits survive later `Unchanged` replies.
If all Parts answer `Unchanged`, ticking alone does not dirty the chunk,
advance its revision or notify containers/comparators. The original
placeholder must still exist; independent Host writes keep their own effects,
including accepted item writes, while aborted Host transactions stay aborted.
The default `Changed` retains full checked write-back.
Side: server.

Whether block `block`'s block entity ticks (`EntityBlock.getTicker`):
set `ticks` when it is yours. Asked for each of the block's states
when a world opens.
Set `ticks` to true to make it tick, and never clear a value an earlier mod or mixin set.
Side: server.

What clients get of the block entity at `pos` when its `id` is
yours (`BlockEntity.getUpdateTag`): set `tag` to it, read from
`entity` alone. Asked on the server whenever a chunk holding it is
sent and whenever its block changes, on the server thread or, for a
saved chunk sent past the view distance (`lan::far`), another one; a client's copy of the block
entity (made by `block_entity` there) merges it into its `nbt`.
Leave it unset to send no tag of yours. A block change puts the one-shot fields of
`ModBlockEntityView::set_client_update_fields` over it, and sends them alone when it is unset.
Side: server.

Return `Some` to set `tag`; the first part returning `Some` wins.

How far from the camera the mod block entity of block `block` draws, in blocks
(vanilla's `BlockEntityRenderer.getViewDistance`): 64 unless a part answers. Set
`distance` for your own block: further for something seen from afar (a beacon-like
beam, a large display), nearer for small detail. It is asked once for each mod block,
the first time this client draws block entities, and kept: never per frame. A value
that isn't finite and above 0 is ignored. Beyond NeoForge: the renderer's own method,
no event.
Side: client.

Every part gets `event.distance` in order and may add, change or remove distance.

A player pressed a mod container's button (`clickMenuButton`), on
the server. The block entity is out of the world during the call;
mods may change it and the clicking player's carried stack.
Side: server.

A player shift-clicked slot `slot` of the menu of the mod block
entity at `pos` (`AbstractContainerMenu.quickMoveStack`, the method a
Java menu overrides), on the server, before the game's own routing:
move the stack where your block wants it. `slot` is the menu's index:
below `container_slots` it is the block's own slot (`entity.items`),
from there on the player's inventory (27 main slots, then the hotbar).
`stack` is a copy of what the slot holds; take what you move out of
it (put it in `entity.items`, or in another block through its
`ITEMS` capability) and set `handled`: the slot then holds what is
left of `stack` (whatever you wrote to that slot of `entity.items`),
the game's routing is skipped, and the player's client gets the menu
again. Left unhandled, `entity.items` goes back to what it held and
the game moves the stack as for any container; a later mod sees what
an earlier one did to `stack`.

For a mod container on a vanilla menu type and on a mod menu type,
the left or right button, a slot that holds something and that the
mod's screen shows; not for a spectator or a dead player, a menu no
longer valid, nor during a drag.
Asked once per click, where vanilla asks `quickMoveStack` again while
it keeps moving the same item. The player's state is swapped in, so
`host.players().acting_player()` names them; `entity` is out of the world
during the call, as in `menu_button`.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `handled`, and later parts are skipped.
methods.signature: fn menu_quick_move(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut MenuQuickMoveEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
The chunk holding this mod block entity is unloading
(`IBlockEntityExtension.onChunkUnloaded`): told once for each of its
mod block entities, on each side that holds a copy of it, before the
copy is dropped. `pos` is where it stands, `block_entity` its handle (the
one `host.block_entity` gave while it was loaded) and `entity` its data.
Release what your mod keeps for it here. On a server its chunk may have
left the level already, so don't count on the handle's reads. As
with `chunk_unload`, changes made in it aren't saved: the chunk
was saved before it unloads. Not told when the world closes, or on a
client when its level goes (a respawn, a dimension change, leaving).
Side: both.

`BlockEntity.preRemoveSideEffects` of a mod's block entity: an
authoritative server is removing `entity` from `pos`, where the block
`state` stood, and its updates may have side effects (not under flag
256, `UPDATE_SKIP_BLOCK_ENTITY_SIDEEFFECTS`). Put in `drops` the stacks
it held that the game doesn't: they scatter as `Containers.dropItemStack`
scatters them, after the block entity's own container. The block entity
is still in place, so its attachments read as they were. Answered from
inside the level's write: don't change the world here.
Side: server.

Every part gets `event.drops` in order and may add, change or remove drops.

A menu opens on this client for block `block`, a mod's: set `screen`
when the block is yours, to lay its screen out (`screen_draw`
draws it). The server asks it too: a slot it hides is not in the menu
there either, so shift-clicks never fill it.
Side: both.

Return `Some` to set `screen`; the first part returning `Some` wins.

A left or right (`right`) press at `at` (GUI pixels from the screen's
top left, so outside it too) on block `block`'s screen, a mod's, over
no slot: set `button` to a menu button id when it is on one of yours.
Horizon sends it to the server (`ContainerButtonClick`,
`menu_button` there) and the press goes no further.
Side: client.

Return `Some` to set `button`; the first part returning `Some` wins.

Draw block `block`'s screen at `origin` (its top left, GUI pixels),
over a plain panel with its slots' frames and under the items and
labels, from the menu's data slots `data` (the block entity's `data`
on the server): data slots are 16-bit on the wire as in vanilla (a
bigger value wraps), and `data` is empty until the server's first
values arrive, so read it with `get`. Draw with `native_sprite`, `native_fill` and
`native_text`.
Side: client.

The tooltip at `at` (as in `screen_click`) on block `block`'s
screen, a mod's, over no item: push its lines when it is over
something of yours. Legacy colour codes (§) work.
Side: client.

Every part gets `event.lines` in order and may add, change or remove lines.

Opt a block with a registered block entity type into state-aware creation.
Asked once per block when a level's immutable factory ownership table is built.
Set true and never clear an earlier answer. For these blocks, `block_entity`
receives the actual state and no answer creates no entity. Existing entities
survive property changes within the same block.
Side: both.

required.name: Data
required.signature: type Data: Clone + Send + Sync + wire::Wire + 'static

methods.doc:
Changes the block entity's value with `edit`, starting from the default when it has
none, and stores the result: see [`edit_part_state`].
methods.signature: fn edit_state<R>(_: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: BlockEntityRef, _: impl FnOnce(&mut dyn ServerHost, &mut Self::Data) -> R) -> Result<R, PartStateError>

methods.doc: The block entity's value, or the default when it has none. Inserts nothing.
methods.signature: fn state(_: &dyn Host, _: BlockEntityRef) -> Result<Self::Data, PartStateError>

methods.doc: The block entity's value, or `None` when it has none. Inserts nothing.
methods.signature: fn state_existing(_: &dyn Host, _: BlockEntityRef) -> Result<Option<Self::Data>, PartStateError>

associated.doc:
Its attachment key, default and codec. The key is in a namespace the mod owns;
without a codec the value is kept for the session only (and a wasm mod needs one).
The value each block entity of the Part's type keeps.
associated.signature: type Data: Clone + Send + Sync + wire::Wire + 'static

traits.doc:
Saved-data transform, shared by native and wasm declarations.
Runs on the server during structure placement, possibly on worldgen worker threads.
Its only inputs are saved data, rotation and mirror. Determinism is the mod's
obligation, not enforced: any matching `Send + Sync` closure is accepted.
The engine preserves the original `id` and any original `x`, `y`, `z` fields.
Return a refusal to keep the original data. Output must fit standard NBT limits
(64 MiB, one million nodes, depth 512); invalid output keeps the original.
Do not panic: native unwinds are caught, and wasm traps refuse the call.

methods.doc: Transform saved data; no Host or world handle is supplied.

traits.doc:
Read-only metadata, lent by a host's block-states service or a tint worker.
This is the low-level resource contract; mods call the BlockState facade instead.
Native and generated WebAssembly forwards invoke the same immutable table implementation.

methods.doc: Borrow the canonical block name from this context's retained registry.
Apply partial constraints to the block's default state.
Borrow a property's serialized value; a missing property returns None.
Change one property while retaining the others.

traits.doc:
A block's part: code attached through [`Registrar`] to one block, a mod's own or vanilla's.
Its methods are the scoped hooks', asked only for the blocks it is attached to: a scoped
hook has no [`Hooks`] method. They may run on the window's thread or the server thread.
Annotate each part trait implementation with [`horizon_part`] to derive its subscriptions.

methods.doc:
The optional contribution of the neighbour `event.state` at `event.pos`
(`IBlockExtension.getAdjacentBlockPathType`). `event.path_type` is that
neighbour's own classified type, not the node's type. The readonly host
reads the owning level. `Some` immediately becomes the node's type and
ends the scan, even if equal to its current type; `None` keeps that
neighbour's fluid and vanilla fallback, never suppressing it. Neighbours
are visited x, then y, then z, each from -1 to 1, excluding the node's
own column. No mob is supplied. These answers run after static
classification; per-search evaluator caches remain.
Diverges from upstream: new hook.
Side: server.

Return `Some` to set `adjacent`; the first part returning `Some` wins.

`Block.affectNeighborsAfterRemoval` for a mod's block: an authoritative server removed the
block `state` from `pos` (`moved`: a piston pushed it) and has run its template class's own
updates. Push onto `updates` the neighbour updates it wants, in order: `OutputSignal`
(`updateNeighbourForOutputSignal`), `Neighbours` (`updateNeighborsAt`) and
`NeighboursExcept(direction)` (`updateNeighborsAtExceptFromFacing`); the level runs each
at once, as the block's own override would. Answered from inside the level's write: it
reads, and cannot write blocks or spawn entities.
Side: server.

Every part gets `event.updates` in order and may add, change or remove updates.

`BlockState.getAnalogOutputSignal`: the signal a comparator reads from
the block `state` at `pos`, `face` the side that touches the comparator
(or the conductor in front of it). `output` holds vanilla's answer:
change it when the block is yours (0 to 15; anything else is clamped).
Asked only for blocks `has_analog_output` answered for, from
inside the level's update: don't change the world here. When the
answer changes without the block's state changing, call
`level.update_neighbors(host, pos, state, NeighbourUpdate::OutputSignal)`; a change of
state through
`native_set_block` or `native_set_block_property` (neighbour updates
on) tells the comparators itself, as vanilla's `Level.setBlock` does.
Authoritative servers only.
Side: server.

Every part gets `event.output` in order and may add, change or remove output.

The colour the block `state` at `pos` gives the beam of the beacon at `beacon_pos`
(`IBlockExtension.getBeaconColorMultiplier`), asked as the beacon builds its beam sections
one block at a time. `color` starts at the block's own answer: the beacon's white and a
stained glass block's or pane's dye colour, empty for the rest. Set `Some(rgb)` to tint
the beam as stained glass does (a colour unlike the section below starts a new section
mixed half and half with it), or `None` to let the beam pass untinted, or stop at an
opaque block other than bedrock, as vanilla does. The beam takes the red, green and blue
channels; alpha is ignored. Asked on both sides, since a client builds the beam it draws
from the blocks it has, with the level read-only: register the mod on both and answer
the same on each. With no part attached to the state, the game checks the hook
subscription and the block key before any event conversion, so the cost is one table
lookup per block above a beacon. Diverges from upstream: new hook.
Side: both.

Every part gets `event.color` in order and may add, change or remove color.

The jump factor of a block state this part is attached to (`Block.getJumpFactor`, which `Entity.getBlockJumpFactor` reads for the player, the cube, the panda, the rabbit and every other living jumper) is being read; vanilla's values are 0.5 for honey and 1.0 for the rest. A part may change `factor` (`event.factor`). The entity reads the block at its feet and, when that gives 1.0, the block below it, so a changed factor takes part in that choice exactly as the block's own would. It runs for each read, on both sides and on the client's replayed ticks, so register the mod on both and keep the listener a pure function of its inputs. It is given the loop `context` of the side that ticks the entity, and takes no `Host`. NeoForge's counterpart `Block.getJumpFactor()` is a method of the block, with no bus event, so this is a part method only; a mod reacting to its own blocks uses this part. Diverges from upstream: new hook.
Side: both.

The optional classification of `event.state` at `event.pos`
(`IBlockExtension.getBlockPathType`). Asked before every vanilla rule,
including air and `is_pathfindable`. `Some` replaces the whole static
classification; `None` declines to vanilla. The readonly host reads the
owning level, so the same state may answer differently at different positions.
No mob is supplied: engine callers in NeoForge pass null. The server's
4096-slot positional cache stores the final static classification, including
Open, until a matching block-updated notification or slot collision. It
survives time, reload and chunk lifetime. Ordinary writes clear only on
actual change with UPDATE_CLIENTS and full status at least BLOCK_TICKING;
direct block-entity notifications clear even unchanged state. Neighbour
and mob-specific adjustments run afterwards, outside that cache.
Diverges from upstream: new hook.
Side: server.

Return `Some` to set `path_type`; the first part returning `Some` wins.

Hides a block state from the mesher: set `event.hidden` and the state draws nothing, as if its blocks were air. Its neighbours' faces toward it show, it no longer hides what is behind it, and its fluid layer and block entity are not drawn; light, collision and the server are untouched. The answer depends on the state alone and is resolved at mesh time, never per frame: the game asks once for every state when the client joins a world, and again for every state each time a mod calls `ClientHost::refresh_render_visibility` (a toggle, an ore scanner). Attach the part to vanilla blocks with `block_part_tag`. With no mod answering, the mesher pays nothing.
Side: client.

Every part gets `event.hidden` in order and may add, change or remove hidden.

The redstone signal the block `state` at `pos` gives on its `face`, the
side that touches the block reading it: `BlockState.getDirectSignal`
when `direct` (what passes through a block it touches, as a lever's
does), else `getSignal`. `signal` holds vanilla's answer: change it when
the block is yours (0 to 15; anything else is clamped). Asked very often,
from inside the level's update, so answer from your own state: check the
block first, and don't read or change the world here. When the answer
changes, and once the block is placed, call
`level.update_neighbors(host, pos, state, NeighbourUpdate::Neighbours)`. Authoritative
servers only.
Side: server.

The speed factor of a block state this part is attached to (`Block.getSpeedFactor`, which `Entity.getBlockSpeedFactor` reads for the player, mobs, boats and minecarts where vanilla reads it) is being read; vanilla's values are 0.4 for honey and soul sand and 1.0 for the rest. A part may change `factor` (`event.factor`). The entity reads the block at its feet and, when that is not water or a bubble column and gives 1.0, the block below it, so a changed factor takes part in that choice exactly as the block's own would. It runs for each read, on both sides and on the client's replayed ticks, so register the mod on both and keep the listener a pure function of its inputs. It is given the loop `context` of the side that ticks the entity, and takes no `Host`. NeoForge's counterpart `Block.getSpeedFactor()` is a method of the block, with no bus event, so this is a part method only; a mod reacting to its own blocks uses this part. Diverges from upstream: new hook.
Side: both.

An entity bounced off a block state this part is attached to (`Block.bounceOn`), after falling `event.fall_distance` blocks. It fires only when the entity bounced, just before vanilla sets its movement. `event.movement` is the movement the bounce leaves it (`x`, `y`, `z`): change it to change what the entity keeps. It runs inside the entity's move, on the level random host: it reads blocks and draws the level's random in vanilla's order, but writes nothing. Players and mobs bounce here; dropped items and the other entities do not.
Side: server.

Every part gets `event.movement` in order and may add, change or remove movement.

An entity landed on a block state this part is attached to and asks its restitution
(`IBlockExtension.getBounceRestitution`, which `Entity.getBlockBounciness` asks of the block
an entity lands on): the factor its vertical speed is multiplied by when it hits the block
from above. Set `factor` (`event.factor`) to change it; it starts at the block's own value,
1.0 for slime, 0.75 for a bed or a shelf mushroom and zero for the rest. `event.entity` and
`event.kind` are the entity that landed and its type, and `event.pos` is the block it
reads (`Entity.getOnPosLegacy`). The entity takes the larger of the factor and its own
bounciness and, unless it is a living one, multiplies it by 0.8 as vanilla does, so 0.5
bounces an entity half as high as slime. A sneaking player, a block tagged
`#minecraft:suppresses_bounce` and a fall too slow to matter still do not bounce, and
`bounce_on` still hears the bounce afterwards. A non-finite answer is ignored.

Asked for the player and the mobs on both sides, so a client predicts its own bounce with
the answer: register the mod on both and answer the same on each. The level host reads
the entity's level (match `LevelSide` for its side) and cannot write; the question can be
asked more than once for one tick: a client predicting its own move and a server
replaying a client's tick ask again. The answer must be a pure function of the host
and the event: no random draws, no part state that changes per call, and no counting
calls. The same inputs must give the same factor.
Dropped items keep their own slime rule. With no part attached to the state, the
owning game checks the hook subscription and prepared API block key before any event
conversion, so the cost is one table lookup. Diverges from upstream: new hook.
Side: both.

Every part gets `event.factor` in order and may add, change or remove factor.

On an authoritative server, whether the block `state` at `pos` lets the fence, wall, or
iron bars or pane `connector` beside it connect to it
(`IBlockExtension.canBeConnectedTo`): the block being connected to answers, not the
connecting one. `kind` names the connector's vanilla rule, `direction` points from the
block toward the connector and `face_solid` is whether the block's face toward it is
sturdy. Asked once the connector's vanilla rule answered, each time the connector is
placed or settles its shape toward the block. `Some(true)` connects, `Some(false)`
refuses and `None` keeps vanilla's rule. The connector's own `connects_to` is asked
after, starting from this answer, and has the last word. A panicking part is contained
and vanilla's answer is used. The level is read-only. With no part attached to the
state, the cost is one table lookup. Diverges from upstream: new hook.
Side: server.

Return `Some` to set `answer`; the first part returning `Some` wins.

Whether `fluid` at `fluid_pos` waters the farmland this part is attached to, the block
`state` at `pos` (`IBlockExtension.canBeHydrated`): set `hydrates` to `Some(true)` or
`Some(false)`, or leave it `None` for vanilla's rule, a fluid in `#minecraft:water`.
`FarmlandBlock.randomTick` scans the 9×2×9 box from `pos` (x and z from −4 to 4, y 0 and 1)
and asks only where the fluid is not empty, in x, then y, then z order; the first position
that hydrates ends the scan, and the farmland goes to moisture 7. Rain on the block above,
moisture changes and drying out are unchanged. The farmland decides which fluids water it.
Asked on an authoritative server; the level is read-only. With no part attached to the
farmland, the scan is vanilla's. Diverges from upstream: new hook.
Side: server.

Return `Some` to set `hydrates`; the first part returning `Some` wins.

On an authoritative server, whether the block `state` at `pos`, destroyed by
`explosion`, drops (`IBlockExtension.canDropFromExplosion`), asked where
`BlockBehaviour.onExplosionHit` asks `Block.dropFromExplosion`. `Some(false)` skips
what the drop runs: the block's `spawnAfterBreak` (an infested block's silverfish, an
ore's experience) and its loot; `Some(true)` runs them, even for TNT; `None` keeps
vanilla's answer, where only TNT drops nothing. The block is removed either way, and a
TNT still primes (`TntBlock.wasExploded` is not part of the answer). A panicking part
is contained and vanilla's answer is used. The level is read-only. With no part
attached to the state, the cost is one table lookup. Diverges from upstream: new hook.
Side: server.

Return `Some` to set `drops`; the first part returning `Some` wins.

On an authoritative server, whether `entity` may destroy the block `state` at `pos`
(`IBlockExtension.canEntityDestroy`), asked where vanilla asks its per-block rule: the
wither's block break (`WitherBoss.canDestroy`: not `#wither_immune`), a dangerous
wither skull's blast (the entity is the skull, readable during the blast; only a block
it may destroy has its resistance capped at 0.8), the dragon's `checkWalls` (a
`#dragon_transparent` block is skipped before the part is asked, and a
`#dragon_immune` block stays even on a yes), a zombie's door breaking (asked as the
goal starts) and the turtle-egg `RemoveBlockGoal`'s target choice. `Some(true)` makes a
block vanilla spares destroyable for that entity, `Some(false)` spares one it would
break (the dragon is then in a wall), and `None` keeps vanilla's rule. The griefing
gate (`entity_mob_griefing`) runs first, so with griefing off nothing breaks whatever
the part says, and `living_destroy_block` can still keep a block the part allowed (the
egg goal's target choice fires no such event). Ravager: griefing event only. A
panicking part is contained and vanilla's rule is used. Asked every tick for each
block in the dragon's head, neck and body: answer fast, from the inputs. The host is
read-only. With no part attached to the state, the cost is one table lookup. Diverges
from upstream: new hook.
Side: server.

Return `Some` to set `may_destroy`; the first part returning `Some` wins.

Whether the player `player`'s tool harvests the block `state` at `pos`
(`IBlockExtension.canHarvestBlock`, what `Player.hasCorrectToolForDrops` asks of the block).
`can_harvest` starts with vanilla's answer: false for a block that needs a tool the player's
held item is not, true otherwise. Set it for your own block; false breaks the block and drops
nothing, and the dig is slowed as vanilla slows a wrong tool. The part answers first and the
global `player_harvest_check` hears the result, so a mod reacting to every block still has the
last word. Asked wherever the harvest rule is: the dig's progress (both sides, so a client
predicts it), the break and a door's break.
Side: both.

Every part gets `event.can_harvest` in order and may add, change or remove can_harvest.

Whether the block state this part is attached to sticks to `other`, the state beside it
(`IBlockExtension.canStickTo`): set `sticks` to decide. `sticks` starts with vanilla's
answer: false for honey beside slime (as `is_slime_block` tells slime), otherwise true when
either state is sticky (`is_sticky_block`). Two blocks stick when each says it sticks to the
other, as `PistonStructureResolver` asks (NeoForge's `canStickToEachOther`), so a part that
answers false for one neighbour is enough to let go of it and a part cannot make a block
stick to one that refuses. The pair is asked from both sides, and the other block's part, if it
has one, answers its own side. Asked on an authoritative server while a piston resolves its
structure: answer from the two states, without touching the world. With no part attached to
the state, the cost is one table lookup. Diverges from upstream: new hook.
Side: server.

Every part gets `event.sticks` in order and may add, change or remove sticks.

On an authoritative server, `BlockState.canSurvive` for `state` at
`pos` (`BlockBehaviour.canSurvive`), before the block answers it: as
it is placed (`BlockItem.canPlace`), from a shape update of a block
whose template checks it (a plant, a torch, a sign: false breaks the
block with its drops), and wherever else vanilla asks. `state` may not
be in the world yet, so decide from `state`. Answer only for your own
blocks: `Some(false)` refuses the spot, `Some(true)` allows it, and
the block's own rule doesn't run. The level is read-only. Asked on
every shape update of such a block: keep it short.
Side: server.

Return `Some` to set `survives`; the first part returning `Some` wins.

`can_survive` again, for the world generation of the server: while a feature places
`state` at `pos`, its parts answer `survives` here, as they answer `survives` in the
live game. Answer only for your own blocks: `Some(false)` refuses the spot, `Some(true)`
allows it, and the block's own rule doesn't run. A rule that picks the ground the block
stands on answers `may_place_on_v2` instead. Server-side, on the worldgen worker threads
and on the server thread, with the server's worldgen `context`: no `Host`, no writes. A
panicking part is contained and the block's own rule kept. Diverges from upstream:
`can_survive` in world generation.
Side: server.

Return `Some` to set `survives`; the first part returning `Some` wins.

On an authoritative server, `IBlockExtension.canSustainPlant` for the soil `ground` at
`ground_pos` and the plant `state` above it, asked before the plant answers its own
`mayPlaceOn` (`may_place_on`) wherever vanilla's plant rule reads its ground: when the plant is
placed, from its shape update and wherever else vanilla asks. `Some(true)` lets the plant
stand there, `Some(false)` refuses it (a planted one pops off when its ground changes to this block),
and left `None` the plant's own `may_place_on` answers, as vanilla's does. Answer only for
your own soil. The level is read-only. Runs on every shape update of a plant over a part's
block: keep it short.
Side: server.

Return `Some` to set `sustains`; the first part returning `Some` wins.

`can_sustain_plant` again, for the world generation of the server: while a feature places
the plant `state` on the soil `ground` at `ground_pos`, the soil's parts answer `sustains`
here. Asked before the plant's `may_place_on_v2`, as the live game asks it before the
plant's `may_place_on`: the soil's answer is the plant's, and the plant is not asked.
`Some(true)` lets the plant stand there, `Some(false)` refuses it, and left `None` the
plant answers. Answer only for your own soil. Server-side, on the worldgen worker threads
and on the server thread, with the server's worldgen `context`: no `Host`, no writes. A
panicking part is contained and the plant's own rule kept. Diverges from upstream:
`can_sustain_plant` in world generation.
Side: server.

Return `Some` to set `sustains`; the first part returning `Some` wins.

`BlockBehaviour.getCloneItemStack`, asked by
`ServerGamePacketListenerImpl.handlePickItemFromBlock`. `include_data`
is true for a creative player picking with Ctrl. Leave `stack` unset to
keep the game's item. Creative breaking, such as a beehive's
`playerWillDestroy`, does not ask this query. Server-side.
Side: server.

Return `Some` to set `stack`; the first part returning `Some` wins.

Whether a fence, wall, or iron bars or pane of yours connects a side:
set `connected` to say whether the block `state` at `pos` connects toward
`neighbour`, the state beside it, `direction` pointing from the block to
that neighbour and `face_solid` whether the neighbour's face toward the
block is sturdy. `kind` names vanilla's rule, and `connected` holds its
answer: `ConnectionKind::Fence` is `FenceBlock.connectsTo` (a solid face, a
fence of the same kind or a gate across the arm), `Wall` is
`WallBlock.connectsTo` (a wall, a solid face, iron bars or a pane, or a
gate across the side; a connected side is still low or tall from the
block above) and `Bars` is `IronBarsBlock.attachsTo` for iron bars and
glass panes (a solid face, bars or a pane, or a wall; vanilla's rule
ignores `direction`). Change it, to false as well as to true, when the
block is your own. The neighbour's part answers first, in
`can_be_connected_to`, and `connected` starts from its answer: this
hook has the last word. Asked whenever the block settles its shape
toward a side or is placed, inside the level's update: answer from the
arguments without touching the world. Only the block's own part is asked, so
vanilla blocks cost nothing. Authoritative servers only. Contract version
`2`: version `1` was `fence_connects_to`, for fences alone and without
`kind`. Diverges from upstream: new hook.
Side: server.

Every part gets `event.connected` in order and may add, change or remove connected.

A server-only, non-cancellable backing-block notice at Container.setChanged / BlockEntity.setChanged, after the write and before dirty/comparator updates. Game-held vanilla container transactions coalesce implicit notices at root commit. Explicit mod-issued set_changed notifies immediately, even for equal contents and inside a transaction; the notice survives abort. Raw mod-owned storage writes and restores synthesize no notice. Nested writes to the backing block whose notice is active still apply but do not re-enter its notice; another block notifies normally. Double containers notify each backing component, not the other half merely refreshed for comparators. Vehicle/menu placeholder coordinates are excluded. Replaces the Create port positional contents_changed mixin for depot, package and schematic storage; there is no matching NeoForge bus event.
Side: server.

`DispenserBlock.getDispenseMethod`, before the item's `dispense_item`:
the block the dispenser faces chooses what the dispense does, for any
item, including vanilla items, on the authoritative server (not
droppers). `state` is the block at `pos` moved by `facing` (air
included), and the part is asked only for that block. An answer wins:
no item part is asked and vanilla's behaviour
doesn't run. The answer is `dispense_item`'s: a remainder of None
empties the slot, `Some(stack)` replaces it (the hook owns
consumption: no extra item is removed afterwards), and `event` is the
level event played with the smoke: 1000 the click, 1001 the fail sound,
or 0 for nothing at all. Leave answer None and `dispense_item` decides,
as it did before.
Side: server.

Return `Some` to set `answer`; the first part returning `Some` wins.
methods.signature: fn dispense_method(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut DispenseMethodEvent<'_>) -> Option<Dispensed>

methods.doc:
The enchanting power the block `state` at `pos` gives the enchanting table at
`table_pos` (`IBlockExtension.getEnchantPowerBonus`), asked for each of the table's
bookshelf offsets (`EnchantingTableBlock.BOOKSHELF_OFFSETS`) whose block between it and the
table is in `#minecraft:enchantment_power_transmitter`. `power` starts at the block's own
answer, 1.0 in `#minecraft:enchantment_power_provider` and 0.0 for the rest: set 2.0 to
count as two bookshelves, 0.5 for half of one, 0.0 to give nothing. The table adds the
answers, truncates the sum to a whole number as NeoForge does and caps it at 15 for the
offers; a negative sum counts as 0, where NeoForge would throw, and a non-finite answer is
ignored. Asked as the offers are made, in a single-player world and on a LAN host for each
guest's table, with the level read-only. Client particles use the same answer, queried once
per state at world entry, parts reload and received-server-tag publication, with `pos`
and `table_pos` both at the origin. Server tags and their tag-update listeners are
published before the client snapshot. Any nonzero answer emits particles when the
intervening block transmits. Particle answers must be state-only; changing a mod's
answer requires a parts/tag reload.
No hook is called per tick or frame. With no part attached, the only dispatch cost is one
block subscription lookup before event conversion. Diverges from upstream: new hook.
Side: both.

Every part gets `event.power` in order and may add, change or remove power.

An entity's block sweep crossed a block state this part is attached to (`Block.entityInside`), and the part is told mid-sweep, where vanilla runs the block's own `entityInside`. `event.precise` is `Entity.checkInsideBlocks`' flag: the entity moved nearly a block, or its box at the target touches the block. It runs inside the entity's move, on the level random host: it reads blocks and draws the level's random in vanilla's order, interleaved with the vanilla blocks the same walk visits; only writes are restricted to the event. `event.apply` queues one of the five `InsideBlockEffectType`s, `event.run_before`/`event.run_after` queue a typed entity write around one, and `event.request` asks for a level write that lands at the touched block once the entity's batch has ticked, if the block is still the state it touched — the same contract as a landing write, whose complete batch is checked before queuing and an invalid state refuses all writes and sibling outputs. The queued entity writes apply to the swept entity inside its own tick, in `StepBasedCollector` order, and stop when it dies; a `Hurt` whose source the entity table answers `Taken` for (its list is lifted that moment, ) is refused with a typed error, not a retry and not a panic. Fires for players, mobs, items and projectiles alike, each on the shared walk inside its own tick or batch.
Side: server.

Every part gets `event.effects` in order and may add, change or remove effects.

Experience before enchantments (`IBlockExtension.getExpDrop`). First answer
replaces vanilla sampling; the global break_block event may override it.
Answers are clamped to 0..=32767. A panic unwinds before the answer is applied.
Side: server.

Return `Some` to set `experience`; the first part returning `Some` wins.

On an authoritative server, the explosion resistance of the block `state` at `pos`
against `explosion` (`IBlockExtension.getExplosionResistance`), asked as a ray of the
blast enters the block (`ExplosionDamageCalculator.getBlockExplosionResistance`). The
answer replaces only the block's own value (`BlockProperties.explosion_resistance`);
a fluid in the cell still raises it to the fluid's 100. What vanilla applies after the
block's value keeps winning: a respawn anchor's water cell, a TNT minecart's rails and
the blocks under them (never asked) and a dangerous wither skull's 0.8 cap. A negative
or non-finite answer is refused and the block's own value is used; a panicking part is
contained and the block's own value is used. A ray asks once per block it enters, so
keep the answer a pure function of the inputs. The level is read-only. With no part
attached to the state, the cost is one table lookup. Diverges from upstream: new hook.
Side: server.

Return `Some` to set `resistance`; the first part returning `Some` wins.

Whether this part's `explosion_resistance` answer depends only on the state and the explosion, not on the position or the level around it: then a batched read (`LevelRef::explosion_resistances`) asks it once a state per call instead of once a cell. False unless the part says so; the answer stays a pure function of its inputs either way.

An entity landed on a block state this part is attached to (`Block.fallOn`), after falling `event.distance` blocks. `event.damage` is the fall damage the entity calculated, before hurt handling and the fall sounds: change it, and zero prevents both. An entity that cannot be hurt by the fall (creative, fall immune) is told with zero damage and keeps its immunity, and a cancelled fall still lands. It runs inside the entity's move, on the level random host: it reads blocks and draws the level's random in vanilla's order, and cannot write. A write the override makes (farmland turning to dirt, a turtle egg breaking) is asked with `event.request(LandingWrite::SetBlock(state))` or `LandingWrite::DestroyBlock { drop }` and lands at the block the entity landed on once the entity's batch has ticked, in the order asked, if the block is still the state it landed on. SetBlock takes an API BlockState. The complete requested batch is checked before queuing: an invalid key or ordinal refuses all writes and sibling outputs from that callback, including damage. The original landed-state guard is checked once per batch, not between its ordered writes. Players, mobs and dropped items land here (an item as an `EntityRef` of kind `minecraft:item`, with zero damage: items take none); projectiles and the other entities do not.
Side: server.

Every part gets `event.damage` in order and may add, change or remove damage.

A falling block of `state` ticked and is still in the air
(`IFallableExtension.fallingTick`): `entity` is the falling block, and `pos` the block
it is in (`Entity.blockPosition`) after its move. Heard once for each tick that ends with
it still falling, not in the tick it lands, drops as an item or is removed (that is
`Fallable.onLand`'s moment). The part can write to the level and, through `entity`, to
the falling block: its velocity, its position. The tick is recorded as it ends and
delivered once the level's falling blocks, primed TNT and orbs have ticked in this pass,
so a write lands on the stored falling block; a falling block gone by then is skipped.
Diverges from NeoForge: server only, where NeoForge also calls it on the client. Only a
state a part listens to is recorded; with no such part, one table lookup per falling
block per tick. Diverges from upstream: new hook.
Side: server.

On an authoritative server, how fire treats the block `state` at `pos`
(`FireBlock.setFlammable(block, igniteOdds, burnOdds)`), asked from its
side `face`, the one that faces the fire or the air fire may take: put
`(ignite, burn)` in `odds` for your own blocks, and vanilla's table
isn't read. Ignite odds above zero let fire stand beside the block and
spread into the air around it (planks 5, wool 30, leaves 30); burn odds
are how fast fire destroys it (planks 20, wool 60, leaves 60). `(0, 0)`
never burns, and a face with ignite odds of zero isn't flammable. Negative
answers become zero; burn odds cap at 300 (horizontal rolls are 300,
vertical rolls 250), and spread speed uses saturating arithmetic. A waterlogged state never burns and
isn't asked. Answer only for your own blocks and leave `odds` empty
otherwise; the level is read-only. Asked hundreds of times per fire
tick: keep it short.
Side: server.

Return `Some` to set `odds`; the first part returning `Some` wins.
methods.signature: fn fire_odds(&self, _: &dyn LevelHost, _: &mut FireOddsEvent) -> Option<(i32, i32)>

methods.doc:
The friction of a block state this part is attached to (`IBlockExtension.getFriction`) is being read for the entity on it; vanilla's values are 0.6 for most blocks, 0.98 for ice, packed ice and frosted ice, 0.989 for blue ice and 0.8 for slime. `entity` and `kind` are the entity's id and type (`minecraft:player`, `minecraft:item`), `pos` the block and `state` its state. A part may change `friction` (`event.friction`), which starts at the block's own value; an answer that is not finite or is outside `0..=2` (the range a content block's declared friction takes) is dropped and the block's own value is used. This deliberately limits NeoForge's uncapped answer to protect movement from invalid mod input. It is read where vanilla reads the block's friction: a living entity's ground travel (the player, mobs and armor stands), an item's and an experience orb's ground drag, a boat's ground friction and a lead's angular friction on the ground. It runs for each read, on both sides and on the client's replayed ticks, so register the mod on both and keep the listener a pure function of its inputs. It is given the loop `context` of the side that ticks the entity, and takes no `Host`, so a part answers from its inputs alone and cannot read the neighbouring blocks. Diverges from upstream: new hook.
Side: both.

`BlockState.hasAnalogOutputSignal`: set `output` for a block of yours
that comparators read (how full or far along it is, as a composter's
level), so they ask `analog_output`. Asked from inside the
level's update: answer from `state` alone. Authoritative servers only.
Side: server.

Every part gets `event.output` in order and may add, change or remove output.

On an authoritative server, whether lava sets fire beside the block
`state` at `pos` (`LavaFluid.isFlammable`, the only reader of
`BlockStateBase.ignitedByLava`), asked from its side `face`, the one
that faces the air the fire would take, as lava's random tick looks
for something to light. `Some(true)` lets lava light it, `Some(false)`
refuses it, and left `None` the block's own flag answers, as vanilla's
does (planks, wool and leaves yes; stone no). Answer only for your own
blocks. The level is read-only.
Side: server.

Return `Some` to set `ignites`; the first part returning `Some` wins.

`BonemealableBlock.isBonemealSuccess` for a block that answered
`is_valid_bonemeal_target`, after it did: set `success` to grow
it this time. Vanilla draws the level's random here
(`isBonemealSuccess(Level, RandomSource, BlockPos, BlockState)`), so
draw from `native_level_random` to keep vanilla's order.
Authoritative servers only.
Side: server.

Every part gets `event.success` in order and may add, change or remove success.

Whether the soil this part is attached to, the block `state` at `pos` under a growing crop,
counts as moist (`IBlockExtension.isFertile`): set `fertile` to decide. `fertile` starts
with vanilla's answer, `moisture > 0`. `CropBlock.getGrowthSpeed` asks it for each of the
3×3 blocks under a crop, stem or pitcher crop on its random tick, but only for a block in
`#minecraft:grows_crops`: a fertile one adds 3 to the speed, any other tagged block 1
(a quarter of that off-centre), so a block outside the tag is never asked. Asked on an
authoritative server; the level is read-only. With no part attached to the state, the
cost is one table lookup. Diverges from upstream: new hook.
Side: server.

Every part gets `event.fertile` in order and may add, change or remove fertile.

On an authoritative server, whether the block `state` at `pos`, under a
fire, keeps that fire burning (`FireBlock.tick`'s check of the
dimension's `infiniburn` tag), asked on every tick of the fire above it:
`Some(true)` makes the fire endless, as netherrack does in the
overworld (rain doesn't put it out and it never burns out), and
`Some(false)` refuses a block the tag lists. Left `None`, the
dimension's tag answers. Asked only for the block under a fire, so its
side is always the top. Answer only for your own blocks. The level is
read-only.
Side: server.

Return `Some` to set `source`; the first part returning `Some` wins.

Whether a living entity climbs the block state this part is attached to (`IBlockExtension.isLadder`, which `LivingEntity.onClimbable` asks of the block the entity stands in). `entity` is the climber's id and `pos` the block it stands in; `state` is that block's state. `ladder` starts with vanilla's answer, whether the block is in `#minecraft:climbable`, and a part may set either value: `true` makes the block climbable as a ladder is, `false` refuses it though the tag lists it. A gliding entity (`isFallFlying`) in a `#minecraft:can_glide_through` block, a spectator and a player who is flying are never asked, as vanilla never climbs for them, and an open trapdoor over a ladder climbs as before. Read for the player, the mobs, and the climbing a mod reads through `LivingRef::is_climbing`. It fires on both sides and on the client's replayed ticks, so register the mod on both and keep the listener a pure function of its inputs. It is given the loop `context` of the side that ticks the entity, and takes no `Host`. With no part attached to the state, the owning game checks the hook subscription and prepared API block key before any event conversion, so the cost is one table lookup. Armor stands never ask it. Diverges from upstream: new hook.
Side: both.

Changes whether a path of a `PathComputationType` (`Land`, `Water` or `Air`) may go through a block state. `event.pathfindable` starts with the block's own answer. The answer depends on the state and the type alone: the game asks once per state and type when parts resolve, at world load and on every `/reload`, so path finding and spawning read the stored answer and a part cannot answer from a position, level or time. The state's `PathType` follows the `Land` answer as vanilla's does, unless the block has a type of its own (air, doors, fences, leaves, rails...): `Blocked` when it is no, else `Water` for a water state, else `Open`. `block_path_type` is asked after it.
Side: server.

Every part gets `event.pathfindable` in order and may add, change or remove pathfindable.

`BlockState.isSignalSource`: set `source` for a block of yours that
gives a signal, so redstone wire beside it connects to it. Authoritative
servers only.
Side: server.

Whether the block state this part is attached to counts as a slime block to a piston
(`IBlockExtension.isSlimeBlock`, which `PistonStructureResolver` asks wherever it tells slime
from honey): set `slime` to decide. `slime` starts with vanilla's answer, true for
`minecraft:slime_block` only. The structure resolver reads it for the one pair that never
sticks, slime beside honey, so a block answering true is held apart from honey as slime is;
stickiness itself is `is_sticky_block`'s. Asked on an authoritative server while a piston
resolves its structure: answer from the state, without touching the world. With no part
attached to the state, the cost is one table lookup. Diverges from upstream: new hook.
Side: server.

Every part gets `event.slime` in order and may add, change or remove slime.

Whether the block state this part is attached to is sticky to a piston
(`IBlockExtension.isStickyBlock`): set `sticky` to decide. `sticky` starts with vanilla's
answer, true for `minecraft:slime_block` and `minecraft:honey_block`. A sticky block pulls
along the blocks beside it that `can_stick_to` lets it hold, so a piston moving one drags
its neighbours, and a structure of them moves as one (still at most twelve blocks). A
block that is not sticky still moves with a sticky neighbour that holds on to it, because
sticking needs one sticky side. Asked on an authoritative server while a piston resolves its
structure: answer from the state, without touching the world. With no part attached to the
state, the cost is one table lookup. Diverges from upstream: new hook.
Side: server.

Every part gets `event.sticky` in order and may add, change or remove sticky.

A block nothing in Horizon knows a `BonemealableBlock` for is about to
take bone meal: vanilla's `BonemealableBlock.isValidBonemealTarget`,
`state` the block's own state at `pos`. Answer `valid` for your own
blocks: the meal is used up on one as vanilla uses it up (the growth
particles and the sound follow, whether or not the roll below grows
it), from a player's `BoneMealItem.useOn`, from a dispenser and, on a
crop (a villager bonemeals only a `CropBlock`), from a villager. Asked
on both sides, as vanilla asks it on both, so a client predicts the
use with your answer: say no where you can only grow on a server
(match `LevelSide`). `Some(false)` refuses the meal, even on a block
whose template takes it (vanilla's `growCrop` then keeps the meal);
left `None`, the block keeps the `BonemealableBlock` its template gives
it, or takes no bone meal.
Side: both.

Return `Some` to set `valid`; the first part returning `Some` wins.

`native_item_after_vertical_collision` lends a dropped item's active stack after vertical collision response, before block effects, merging and pickup. The block is the one selected by the legacy on-position query. `client` identifies prediction. Set `discard` (trait `Flow::Cancel`) or set the stack to None to consume the item without loot or pickup. A movement skipped by the normal item tick sends no notification. Bundles need "hooks": @API:item_after_vertical_collision@.
Side: both.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `discard`, and later parts are skipped.

The light the block `state` emits at `pos` in `dimension`
(`IBlockExtension.getLightEmission`), for a block that declares
`dynamic_light: true`. The declaration is per block, not per state as
`hasDynamicLightEmission` is, because it lives on the block's row: every state
of a declared block is asked, and parts on other blocks are never asked, at any
moment (NeoForge asks on a block change and a queued check whether or not the
block declares). `emission` starts empty: set `Some(level)` to replace the
state's own light at that position, or leave it empty to keep it. An answer
above 15 is clamped to 15 here, so an out-of-range value never reaches the
light queue; NeoForge clamps only the value its light manager stores. Asked
only on the thread that owns the level, both sides, with that level read-only,
as a chunk holding the block comes in, as an edit sets it and at
`LevelRef::check_light` (`LevelLightEngine.checkBlock`); the light engine keeps
the answer until the cell's state changes or the chunk unloads, its workers
read only that answer, and it never asks on its own: an answer that reads more
than the state (the block below, the depth) calls `check_light` when that
changes. A client also asks its own parts again, at most once per cell, for the
sections a server's light update changed: a Horizon addition, as the contract
asks on no light packet, for an answer that reads data the client receives
later. Not asked for the block's own rendered light, ambient occlusion or the
spawn rule, which take the state's light. The game may ask more often than the
contract does, so keep the answer a pure function of the level, `pos` and
`state`. Diverges from upstream: new hook.
Side: both.

Return `Some` to set `emission`; the first part returning `Some` wins.

Whether an open trapdoor above the block state this part is attached to climbs like a ladder (`IBlockExtension.makesOpenTrapdoorAboveClimbable`, which `LivingEntity.onClimbable` asks of the block under the open trapdoor a living entity stands in). `state` is that block's state and `pos` its position; `trapdoor` is the open trapdoor's state above it. `climbable` starts with vanilla's answer, true for a `minecraft:ladder` facing the trapdoor's way, and a part may set either value. Asked only once the trapdoor itself was not a ladder (`is_ladder` and the `#minecraft:climbable` tag), so it never makes a block that is a ladder stop climbing. A gliding entity in a `#minecraft:can_glide_through` block, a spectator and a player who is flying are never asked. Read for the player, the mobs, and the climbing a mod reads through `LivingRef::is_climbing`. It fires on both sides and on the client's replayed ticks, so register the mod on both and keep the listener a pure function of its inputs. It is given the loop `context` of the side that ticks the entity, and takes no `Host`. With no part attached to the state below, the owning game checks the hook subscription and prepared API block key before any event conversion, so the cost is one table lookup. Armor stands never ask it. Diverges from upstream: new hook.
Side: both.

On an authoritative server, `VegetationBlock.mayPlaceOn` for the
plant `state` on `ground` at `ground_pos`, before the plant answers
it: the blocks a mod plant (one whose template is a vanilla plant,
such as a crop) can stand on. Its template's `canSurvive` asks it, so
the plant is refused there and pops off when its ground changes to
one it can't stand on. Answer only for your own blocks. The level is
read-only.
Side: server.

Return `Some` to set `may`; the first part returning `Some` wins.

`may_place_on` again, for the world generation of the server: while a feature places the
plant `state` on `ground` at `ground_pos`, its parts answer `may` here, and the soil's
parts answer `can_sustain_plant_v2` before this. `ground` is the block the plant stands
on, so a rule that only picks its soil belongs in `can_sustain_plant_v2`. Answer only
for your own blocks. Server-side, on the worldgen worker threads and on the server
thread, with the server's worldgen `context`: no `Host`, no writes. A panicking part is
contained and the plant's own rule kept. Diverges from upstream: `may_place_on` in world
generation.
Side: server.

Return `Some` to set `may`; the first part returning `Some` wins.

A minecart passed over a rail block state this part is attached to (the moment `AbstractMinecart` calls `activateMinecart` on an activator rail, for every rail; Forge's `IBaseRailExtension.onMinecartPass`, which NeoForge 26.3 no longer has, so this hook has no counterpart). `event.entity` is the cart, `event.pos` the rail. With the old minecart physics it fires once per tick the cart is on a rail; with `minecart_improvements` once per track iteration, so a fast cart can pass several times in a tick. It fires after the cart's batch has ticked, not mid-move, so a write the part makes (a velocity change through the cart handle) lands on the stored cart, and a pass whose cart is gone or whose rail changed is dropped. Only a rail state a part listens for is recorded; with no such part nothing is kept. Diverges from upstream: new hook.
Side: server.

An authoritative server is about to deliver `neighborChanged`.
State and block IDs are valid in this level's registries for this call.
The host is the level with its ticks, as vanilla's `neighborChanged` gets the
level: a part may read its inputs (`signal`, `has_neighbor_signal`) and
schedule its tick here, as a diode does (`DiodeBlock.checkTickOnNeighbor`).
Side: server.

An explosion destroys this block, before removal and while its live block
entity is readable. Writes are allowed; the engine still replaces the cell
with air afterwards, including a replacement written by the part.
Side: server.

A write through `Level.setBlock` held and the block at `pos` changed from `old` to
`new` (`IBlockExtension.onBlockStateChange`), heard at the end of the write, where
vanilla runs `updatePOIOnBlockStateChange`: after the block-entity removal, `on_place`,
the client update, the neighbour updates and the neighbours' shape updates. The parts
of `old`'s block hear it, then, when the block changed, the parts of `new`'s block;
`state` is the state whose block's parts are asked. A write that `on_place` replaced
with another block is not heard; the write that replaced it is. Heard on both sides:
a server's writes, a client's replay of a piston's move and the blocks a client takes
from the server (`LevelSide` names which). Applied local predictions are heard at once
with `predicted: true`; server writes, settled corrections and all server-side writes
have `predicted: false`. A held server update is unheard until acknowledgement; a
confirmed prediction is not heard twice, and a denial hears predicted-to-server once.
Equal-state writes and unapplied guesses are not heard. The level is read-only.
A panicking part is contained. With no listener, one flag check builds nothing.
Diverges from upstream: new hook.
Side: both.

On an authoritative server, a neighbour of fire passed its burn roll.
`state` is still at `pos`; `face` points toward the fire. The spread,
burn and (when replacing with fire) ignite cancel gates run first.
The listener may write or schedule ticks, but the pending fire/air
replacement overwrites any write at `pos`, then TNT is primed.
Fire spread has no igniter and an empty stack, so neither is passed.
Lava, lightning, spread into air, flint and steel, TNT use, burning
projectiles, redstone and dispensers are outside this spread-only hook.
Side: server.

A player removes the block `state` at `pos` (`IBlockExtension.onDestroyedByPlayer`, where
`ServerPlayerGameMode.destroyBlock` runs `playerWillDestroy` and removes the block), with
`tool`, the stack in the player's hand (`None` for a bare hand), and `will_harvest`, whether
the break will drop loot as far as the tool goes (never in creative, and false for a tool the
block refuses). Asked after `break_block` allowed the break, before anything of the break
changes the world. `will_harvest` is the tool's own answer; the mods' harvest listeners
(`can_harvest_block`, then `player_harvest_check`) are asked once, after the removal, of the
adjusted state and the stack in the hand then, as vanilla reads `hasCorrectToolForDrops`.
`destroyed` is whether the
block was actually destroyed: `Some(true)` says the part removed it itself, `Some(false)`
that it stays (a block of layers losing one layer: change it with the `host` and leave it
standing), and either answer replaces the game's own `playerWillDestroy` (a pot's cracking,
piglin anger, a tripwire's disarming, a creative shulker box's or beehive's drop) and
removal. `Some(false)` ends the break there: no drops, tool wear or statistic. Left `None`,
vanilla's removal runs. Server-side, for every player of the world; the first part answering
wins. Asked of the block's own parts only, so a block with none costs nothing.
Side: server.

Return `Some` to set `destroyed`; the first part returning `Some` wins.
methods.signature: fn on_destroyed_by_player(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut OnDestroyedByPlayerEvent<'_>) -> Option<bool>

methods.doc:
On an authoritative server, a piston's move destroys the block `state` at `pos`
(`IBlockExtension.onDestroyedByPushReaction`), `direction` the way the blocks move and
`fluid` the fluid state the cell holds.
It is heard in `PistonBaseBlock.moveBlocks` after the block dropped its resources and
while it is still in its cell, before the cell becomes air. The removal still happens:
a write to `pos` is overwritten, and so is a write to any other cell of the move (the
other destroyed cells, the pushed blocks and the cells they move into, the arm), since
the pushed blocks were read before the destroy loop. Writes elsewhere stay; `ticks`
is the move's, so scheduled ticks stay too. A cancelled move (`piston_pre`) and a
client's replay of the move are not heard. A panicking part is contained. With no part
attached to the state, the cost is one table lookup per destroyed block. Diverges from
upstream: new hook; the removal is not replaceable here.
Side: server.

A neighbouring block entity changed, was created or removed. Vanilla comparator processing runs first.
Side: server.

A trunk placer is about to place the block under its trunk at `pos`, where the soil
`state` this part is attached to stands (`IBlockExtension.onTreeGrow`, asked from
`TrunkPlacer.placeBelowTrunkBlock`). Answer `Some(Some(state))` to place `state` there
through the tree's trunk setter, `Some(None)` to place nothing, or `None` to leave it to the
tree's `below_trunk_provider` (vanilla's trees place dirt unless the soil is in
`#minecraft:cannot_replace_below_tree_trunk`). A part that answers skips the provider and
its draws. Asked once per trunk, four times for the 2×2 trunks (giant, mega jungle, dark
oak). Draw only from `event.random`, the tree's own: your draws fall between the tree's, in
call order. Server-side, on the worldgen worker threads and on the server thread when a
sapling grows, with the server's worldgen `context`: no `Host`, no writes. NeoForge's
`feature` argument is left out: an inline tree feature has no key. Diverges from upstream:
new hook.
Side: server.

Return `Some` to set `soil`; the first part returning `Some` wins.

`BonemealableBlock.performBonemeal` for a block that answered
`is_valid_bonemeal_target` and whose `is_bonemeal_success`
said yes: grow it here, `state` its state at `pos`. The meal is used up
either way. Change the block with the level's
`native_set_block_property`, and schedule with `native_schedule_block_tick`
(`ticks` is the hook's). Authoritative servers only.
Side: server.

Whether a piston carries your block `state` at `pos` with its block
entity: asked at the last step of `PistonBaseBlock.isPushable`, after
the block's push reaction, for a block that is otherwise pushable,
whenever a piston's structure takes the block in. Left `None`, vanilla's
rule holds: a block with a block entity does not move, and any other
block does. `Some(false)` keeps the block in place at that position.
`Some(true)` lets a piston move it even with a block entity, which
travels with the block: taken out of the world as the move starts, with
its saved data and its attachments and without its removal side effects
(nothing drops), and put where the block lands as a new block entity of
that position, with a new ticker slot; a handle to the old position no
longer resolves. If the moving block is replaced before it lands, the
block entity is removed there as a broken block's is (a container drops
its contents). A save mid-move keeps it in the moving piston's tag. A
block entity, including a chest, moves only after its reaction permits movement
and this hook answers true. While the block moves it draws as its state, without its
block entity's drawing. Asked on both sides, as a client replays the
move on its own copy: answer the same on both, from the arguments,
without touching the world. Only attached block parts are asked; blocks
without a subscribed part pay only the dispatch guards. A block that only needs to move or not, or
to be popped or pushed only, is the push reaction's question, asked
before this one. The order is reaction first, then this shared block-entity
rule for push-pull, ignore-entity and push only; a wrong-direction push-only
answer refuses before this hook. Popped destroys and drops without asking it.
This hook is asked only for an otherwise-pushable block. A live owned payload
is required: data-only or unmaterialized vanilla entities remain refused.
Diverges from vanilla: push only never discards a block entity.
NeoForge has no counterpart: its
`IBlockExtension.getRelocability` is an unrelated region-copy query that
pistons do not ask. Diverges from upstream: new hook.
Side: both.

Return `Some` to set `movable`; the first part returning `Some` wins.

Resolve a state's piston reaction at load and reload on both sides. None keeps the
properties' reaction. Answers must depend only on state. Unbreakable blocks still
refuse movement. The reaction is checked first; push-pull, ignore-entity and push only
then reach the shared block-entity rule. An otherwise-pushable block with a block entity
moves only when `piston_carries_block_entity` answers true, using the carry machinery
to move its data and attachments without drops. No answer or false refuses the move.
Popped remains destruction with ordinary drops, and never asks the carries hook.
The carries hook is asked only for an otherwise-pushable block. Carrying also requires
a live owned payload; raw-only or currently borrowed native payloads remain refused.
Diverges from vanilla: push only never discards a block entity.
Side: both.

Return `Some` to set `reaction`; the first part returning `Some` wins.

Asked before a mining hit sound, including the initial hit, every fourth breaking
tick, and the level-event route. Return Flow::Cancel when the part handled the
sound through ClientHost and vanilla should stay silent.
Otherwise vanilla plays the state's hit sound at (volume + 1) / 8 and pitch * 0.5.
The position and face identify the current hit; sculk growth is outside this hook.
Side: client.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later parts are skipped.
methods.signature: fn play_hit_sound(&self, _: &mut dyn ClientHost, _: &mut PlayHitSoundEvent) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
Whether the rail `state` at `pos` may climb toward a raised rail beside it
(`IBaseRailBlockExtension.canMakeSlopes`). `can` starts true, as for every vanilla rail;
set false to keep it flat as it connects to its neighbours (`RailState`). Asked on an
authoritative server as a rail is placed or a neighbour changes it: answer from the
state and the position, without touching the world. With no part attached to the
state, the cost is one table lookup. Diverges from upstream: new hook.
Side: server.

Every part gets `event.can` in order and may add, change or remove can.

The track the rail `state` at `pos` lays for `cart`
(`IBaseRailBlockExtension.getRailDirection`), so a switch track or a one-way rail can
turn a cart differently from its stored shape. `shape` starts at the rail's `shape`
property. `cart` is the minecart moving on it, or `None` when the rail asks for itself:
as it connects to its neighbours (`RailState`) and as a minecart item is placed on it.
The cart's movement asks wherever it reads the track under it. Asked on both sides,
since a client predicts its own cart's motion: register the mod on both and answer the
same on each, from the level host and the event alone. With no part attached to the
state, the cost is one table lookup per rail read. Diverges from upstream: new hook.
Side: both.

Every part gets `event.shape` in order and may add, change or remove shape.

Whether the rail `state` at `pos` may make corners
(`IBaseRailBlockExtension.isFlexibleRail`). `flexible` starts true for a plain rail and
false for the straight ones (powered, detector, activator); set false to keep it
straight at a junction. Asked on an authoritative server as the rail and its neighbours
connect (`RailState`): answer from the state and the position, without touching the
world. With no part attached to the state, the cost is one table lookup. Diverges from
upstream: new hook.
Side: server.

Every part gets `event.flexible` in order and may add, change or remove flexible.

Whether the rail `state` may take `shape` (`IBaseRailBlockExtension.isValidRailShape`),
asked as it connects to its neighbours (`RailState`) before the shape is written.
`valid` starts true when the rail's `shape` property has that value; set false to refuse
it, and the rail keeps its current shape. A part can't make valid a shape the property
lacks. Asked on an authoritative server: answer from the state and the shape, without
touching the world. With no part attached to the state, the cost is one table lookup.
Diverges from upstream: new hook.
Side: server.

Every part gets `event.valid` in order and may add, change or remove valid.

An authoritative server's `ServerLevel.tickChunk` is about to
random-tick the block `state` at `pos` (`BlockState.randomTick`):
only blocks that tick randomly, a mod's as its vanilla template block
does. Bone meal's random ticks (`StemBlock.performBonemeal`) don't
fire it. Change the block with `native_set_block_property` and set
`handled` to skip the block's own random tick (a mod crop growing its
own way); a block changed without `handled` takes its own random tick
as it is now, if it still ticks randomly. Lava's fluid random tick
runs either way.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `handled`, and later parts are skipped.
methods.signature: fn random_tick(&self, _: &mut dyn LevelWriteHost, _: &mut RandomTickEvent) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
Choose the state left by removing your block. Return a state in `answer`
to replace vanilla's fluid block (air when dry), or leave it unanswered.
Only the removed block's Part is asked, on the authoritative server.
The replacement must be a registered block state; an invalid answer is
refused with a diagnostic and vanilla's replacement is written instead.
The normal setBlock effects and flags 3 (+64 when moved by a piston)
apply to the written state. The level is read-only during this call.
Side: server.

Return `Some` to set `answer`; the first part returning `Some` wins.

Where a player whose respawn point is the block `state` at `pos` stands up when they
respawn there (`IBlockExtension.getRespawnPosition`), or that they can't respawn there.
`entity_type` is the respawning entity's type, always `minecraft:player`, and
`orientation` the yaw saved with the respawn point. `position` starts at vanilla's answer:
a bed's or a charged respawn anchor's stand-up spot facing the block, a forced point's
free column, or empty where vanilla finds no spot. Set `Some((position, yaw, pitch))` to
stand the player there, or `None` to send them to the world spawn with
`missing_respawn_block` set. An answer with a non-finite value is ignored. An anchor still
loses a charge only when the answer is a spot. Asked on the server as the respawn point
is resolved, before `player_respawn_position`, which receives the answer as its original
position and may still redirect it, and as a player leaves the End, which resolves the
point the same way. The level is read-only. NeoForge asks only beds; this is asked
for any block, so a mod block that is neither a bed nor an anchor can be a respawn point.
With no part attached to the state, the game checks the hook subscription and the block
key before any event conversion, so the cost is one table lookup per respawn. Diverges
from upstream: new hook.
Side: server.

Every part gets `event.position` in order and may add, change or remove position.

A structure template is about to place the block `state` at `pos` turned by `rotation`
(`IBlockExtension.rotate`, where vanilla runs `state.mirror(mirror).rotate(rotation)`):
`state` is already mirrored, and `rotated` starts at the game's own answer (vanilla's
table, or a mod block's template's). Set it to another state of the same block to place
that instead. A state of another block, or one the game does not have, is refused and
the game's answer kept. Asked for every block a template places: world generation's
structures, `/place template`, the structure block and the jigsaw pieces that join
them, and the template snapshots `structure_template` reads. Mirroring stays the
game's. Server-side, on the worldgen worker threads and on the server thread, with the
server's worldgen `context`: no `Host`, no writes; `context.state_with_property` builds
states. A panicking part is contained and the game's answer kept. Diverges from
upstream: new hook.
Side: server.

Every part gets `event.rotated` in order and may add, change or remove rotated.

`IBlockExtension.shouldCheckWeakPower`: set `check` to decide whether
indirect power is read through this block. `check` starts with vanilla's
conductor answer. `direction` is the input side of the block being powered,
opposite the queried block's output side. Authoritative servers only.
