Side: server.

Every part gets `event.check` in order and may add, change or remove check.

Whether a fluid's side beside a block state uses the fluid's overlay sprite (water's `water_overlay`)
instead of its flowing sprite (`IBlockExtension.shouldDisplayFluidOverlay`): set `event.overlay`.
`overlay` starts with vanilla's test, true beside a `HalfTransparentBlock` or `LeavesBlock` (for a content
block, its template's class), so a part can turn the overlay on or off. `event.fluid` is the fluid as it is
asked: a source at amount 8, or a flowing fluid at amount 7, not falling. A fluid with no overlay sprite,
such as lava, draws its flowing sprite whatever the answer. The answer depends on the state and the fluid
alone and is resolved at join or explicit visibility refresh, never on a meshing worker: the client asks once for every state and fluid where
it resolves `block_render_visibility` (joining a world, `ClientHost::refresh_render_visibility`), and the
meshing workers read the table. The level and position are dropped: the meshing workers run no mod code.
With no part answering, nothing is asked and meshes are unchanged. Diverges from upstream: new hook.
Side: client.

Every part gets `event.overlay` in order and may add, change or remove overlay.

Whether a block state hides the face a fluid beside it draws toward it
(`IBlockExtension.shouldHideAdjacentFluidFace`): set `event.hidden` and the fluid's face toward the block is
not drawn. `event.direction` points from the fluid to the block (Horizon's reading, not checked), and
`event.fluid` is the fluid as it is asked: a source at amount 8, or a flowing fluid at amount 7, not falling.
`hidden` starts false. Vanilla's tests still apply first: a fluid beside the same fluid, or behind a face
that occludes it, draws no face there whatever the answer. The answer depends on the state and the fluid
alone and is resolved at join or explicit visibility refresh, never on a meshing worker: the client asks once for every state and fluid where
it resolves `block_render_visibility` (joining a world, `ClientHost::refresh_render_visibility`), and the
meshing workers read the table. The level and position are not arguments. With no part answering, nothing
is asked and meshes are unchanged. Diverges from upstream: new hook.
Side: client.

Every part gets `event.hidden` in order and may add, change or remove hidden.

`BlockBehaviour.shouldRedstoneWireConnectTo`: set `connected` to say
whether redstone wire connects to the block `state` at `pos`.
`direction` points from the wire toward the neighbouring block, or is
None when the wire asks about the block above or below. `connected` holds vanilla's answer: change
it when the block is yours. Asked whenever wire settles its shape:
answer from `state` and `pos` without touching the world. When the
answer changes, and once the wire is placed, update its neighbours
(`level.update_neighbors`). Authoritative servers only.
Side: server.

Every part gets `event.connected` in order and may add, change or remove connected.

On an authoritative server, `CampfireBlock.isSmokeSource` for the
block `state` under a campfire, as the campfire is placed or the block
under it changes: `Some(true)` for your own blocks makes the campfire a
signal fire whose smoke rises higher, as over a hay bale. The level is
read-only.
Side: server.

Return `Some` to set `smoke`; the first part returning `Some` wins.

The sound type of a block state this part is attached to (`IBlockExtension.getSoundType`) is being read, to play one of its sounds. `pos` is the block and `state` its state; `entity` is nullable, as NeoForge's: the id and type (`minecraft:player`, `minecraft:creeper`) of the entity stepping on it, landing on it, placing it or digging it (a sniffer), and `None` for a break and for a placement by no entity (a dispenser); `cause` says which sound is about to play (`BlockSoundCause::Step`, `Fall`, `Place`, `Break` or `Dig`). It is asked only where NeoForge asks it, not for the hit sound while a block is mined (that has its own client hook upstream) nor for sculk growth. A part may change `sound` (`event.sound`), which starts as the state's own sound type: its event names, volume and pitch. The game then applies vanilla's factors for `cause` to the volume and pitch and plays that one sound. An answer whose volume or pitch is not finite and at least 0, or one of whose events is not a `namespace:path` id, is dropped whole and the state's own sound type is used. An event the resources lack plays nothing, as in vanilla; a mod's own event (from its content mod's `assets/<id>/sounds.json`) is sent to players by name. It runs for each sound, on the side that plays it, so register the mod on both and keep the listener a pure function of its inputs: the placer's client and the server ask for the same placement and must agree. It is given the loop `context` of the side that asks, and takes no `Host`. It cannot play no sound, several sounds, or a sound somewhere else (`playStepSound` and `playFallSound` can). Diverges from upstream: new hook.
Side: both.

The block state the camera at `viewpoint` sees of the block `state` at `pos`
(`IBlockExtension.getStateAtViewpoint`), so a partial fluid block, a tank or a
waterlogged mod block can show underwater fog only while the eye is really inside the
liquid. `seen` starts at `state`: set it to the state whose fluid and powder snow the
camera should read. Asked as the client finds the fluid at the camera
(`Camera.getFluidInCamera`) for the block at the eye, the block above it and the blocks
at the near plane's centre and corners: the fog, the field of view in a fluid, the
water vision, the sky's dark disc and conduit power's underwater vision read it. The
client host is read-only; answer from the event alone, as the game asks every frame. With no
part on any block the subscription check skips the asks; otherwise each block read costs
one table lookup. Diverges from upstream: new hook.
Side: client.

Every part gets `event.seen` in order and may add, change or remove seen.

A block is about to take the state it is placed in
(`Block.getStateForPlacement(BlockPlaceContext)`), `state` the block's
own default state. Answer only for your blocks: put the state you want
in `answer` as `Some(Some(state))` — a state of that block, as vanilla
sets properties on its own `defaultBlockState` (another block's is
ignored) — or refuse the placement with `Some(None)`: the block goes
nowhere and the stack is kept, as vanilla's `null`. Left empty, the
block's own placement runs. `context` is
vanilla's `BlockPlaceContext` (the clicked face, the placer's rotation,
the clicked position, whether the clicked block is being replaced, the
item in hand) and `fluid` the fluid in the position the block would go
in, which a waterlogged block reads. Build the state from `state` with
`native_state_with_property`, and know whether `state` is yours with
`native_state_block`. It is asked for every placer that goes
through vanilla's placement (a player's `BlockItem.place`, a
dispenser's `DirectionalPlaceContext`), and the answer still takes its
survival and entity obstruction checks. A trait mod returns
`Some(Some(state))` to choose a state, `Some(None)` to refuse, or
`None` to leave the answer to the next mod or vanilla. Changes to the event's fluid
copy are mod-provided data forwarded to later Parts, never consumed by the engine.
Authoritative servers only.
Side: server.

Return `Some` to set `answer`; the first part returning `Some` wins.

An authoritative server's `ServerLevel.tickBlock` is about to run a
due scheduled tick of the block `state` at `pos` (`BlockState.tick`):
the block is still the one the tick was scheduled for. Change the
block with `native_set_block_property` and set `handled` to skip the
block's own tick; a block changed without `handled` takes its own
tick as it is now, if it is still the tick's block.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `handled`, and later parts are skipped.
methods.signature: fn tick_block(&self, _: &mut dyn LevelWriteHost, _: &mut TickBlockEvent) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
The state the block `state` becomes under a tool action (`IBlockExtension.getToolModifiedState`:
an axe's strip, scrape or wax-off, a shovel's flatten or douse, a hoe's till), asked of the
block a tool is used on (`tool.pos`). `final_state` starts with vanilla's answer, `None` for a
block the tool does nothing to: set it to `Some(new)` to allow the action or replace its
result (a mod log an axe strips, a path a shovel makes), and `Cancel` it to deny the action,
so the tool does nothing. `tool.simulated` says the game is only asking what the tool would
do (`LevelRef::block_transform`, NeoForge's `simulate`): answer the same and change nothing in
the world. A part answers before the global `block_tool_modification`, which still hears the
result and may change or cancel it; a cancelled part skips it. Asked for the block's own parts only, so
a block with none costs nothing.
Side: both.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later parts are skipped.

An authoritative server is about to compute the state the block
`state` at `pos` takes now that its neighbour in `direction` is
`neighbour` (`BlockBehaviour.updateShape`). `state` may not be in the
world yet (a piston landing it): decide from `state`, not from the
block at `pos`. Answer only for your own blocks: put the new state in
`new` (`state` keeps the block as it is; air breaks it, with its drops,
on a neighbour update) and the block's own `updateShape` doesn't run,
nor the ticks it would schedule. The level is read-only, as vanilla's
`LevelReader`; ticks go through `native_schedule_block_tick` and
`native_schedule_fluid_tick` with `ticks` (`ScheduledTickAccess`). It
runs often, at least six times per `setBlock` that updates shapes
(more for redstone wire's diagonals and knock-on updates): keep it
short.
Side: server.

Return `Some` to set `new`; the first part returning `Some` wins.

`BlockBehaviour.useItemOn`: the block's own behaviour, with the
held item, on the server for each player. An answer replaces the
template's behaviour; `TryWithEmptyHand` tries `useWithoutItem` on
the main hand, and `Pass` goes on to the item's `useOn`.
Side: server.

Return `Some` to set `answer`; the first part returning `Some` wins.

methods.doc:
`BlockBehaviour.useWithoutItem`: the captured state's empty-hand method,
after useItemOn asks for it, on the server and main hand only.
Side: server.

Whether this block receives block entity changes through an adjacent conductor. Starts false.

A mod's block tint source: vanilla's `BlockTintSource`. Colours are ARGB, and a face it colours
is multiplied by their RGB, as vanilla's block renderer does. Implemented once, held by the game, asked on the meshing workers, so it
keeps no mutable state.

`color(state)`: the colour without a world, where the block is drawn away from a level (a
block in a minecart, a mod's drawn block). Also the default of the two below.

`colorAsTerrainParticle(state, level, pos)`: the colour of the bits the block breaks into
and of falling dust.

`colorInWorld(state, level, pos)`: the colour of the block at `pos`, as the chunk mesher
draws it. The mesher asks once per block and tint index each time it meshes the section.

`relevantProperties()`: the property names the colour depends on. Vanilla groups states
for shared baked models by them (`ModelGroupCollector`); Horizon bakes every state, so the
game does not read it.

The block tint registry `register_block_tint_sources` hands out: NeoForge's

`register(sources, blocks...)`, vanilla's `BlockColors.register`: `layers[i]` colours the
faces of `blocks` whose `tintindex` is i, and a face whose index is past the list is not
tinted. Blocks are ids, a mod's (`mymod:cable`) or vanilla's (`minecraft:oak_leaves`); a
later registration for a block replaces the earlier one, vanilla's own included.

`block` holds `total` millibuckets of `fluid` when full. `level` names the block's
integer level property, whose greatest value is the number of levels the cauldron
fills by; none means the cauldron is only ever full, as a lava cauldron. Each level
holds `total` ÷ the number of levels, so `total` must divide evenly by it.
Totals must be in `1..=i32::MAX`, the fluid capability amount range. The property
must contain every canonical integer from 1 through its maximum (and may include 0).

A client-side `SimplePreparableReloadListener`, as `ServerReloadListener`
reads data: prepare reads the new pack view without changing live state;
its returned apply publishes the result. All prepares finish before any
apply, including vanilla's, runs. Prepare cannot see another listener's new
published state. Dependencies order both phases deterministically; they do
not remove the barrier. On any error all pending applies are dropped,
keeping every listener's previous assets.

listener that parses its files logs and skips one that won't parse,
carrying the rest through; returning `Err` aborts the whole reload and
keeps every listener's previous assets. A panic in `prepare` or the
returned apply is not recovered: it stops the game, and the crash report
names the listener and the mod that registered it.

(`PlayerInfo.getLatency`): the server's smoothed keep-alive average, refreshed by its own

traits.doc:
A command argument type a mod registers: how one kind of argument is validated and completed.

Register it once, from `Hooks::register`, with `Registrar::register_command_argument`. Its
namespaced id (`mymod:machine`) is the kind a `Command` usage names after the argument
name: `Command::new("machine use <machine:mymod:machine>")`. The game then parses the
argument with [`parse`](Self::parse) before calling `run_mod_command`, and asks
[`suggest`](Self::suggest) for the chat box's completions. Players' clients that do not know
the type complete it from the server's answer.

The game keeps one value per registered id and asks it from the server thread and, for a
client command, from the window's thread: implement it to be shared, without mutable state.

methods.doc: The part of the line the argument takes. The same on every client.

Validate the text a client wrote and return the value `run_mod_command` receives.

`input` is one word (see [`CommandArgumentKind::Word`] for its characters), or the rest
of the line for [`CommandArgumentKind::Greedy`]. Return the canonical text to deliver (an
id, a lower-cased name, `"3"` for `"03"`), or the message shown to the player when the
input is not valid.

The completions for the text `prefix` being typed at this argument, for `sender`.

`prefix` is the text the argument holds so far: one word's worth for
[`Word`](CommandArgumentKind::Word), and the whole tail of the line up to the cursor for
[`Greedy`](CommandArgumentKind::Greedy). Return the values that match, in the order the
chat should show them; the game keeps each suggestion's replacement range and tooltip. A
suggestion replaces the whole prefix unless it names a
[`replace_start`](CommandSuggestion::replace_start), which is how a type completes the
token being typed inside a longer greedy text. An empty list leaves the input as typed.

`sender` is the player asking, with their permission level: a provider that completes names
from a mod's registry returns only the entries that sender may use, because the game keeps
its answer unfiltered. It is `None` when no player asks: the console, and a client
completing its own client commands before its own profile is known.

Native and wasm results share the vanilla packet limits: completion text may contain
at most 32767 UTF-16 code units; a literal tooltip may occupy at most 65535 bytes in
Java modified UTF-8 (the NBT string limit). If any result exceeds either limit, the
engine reports the refusal and discards the callback's results, rather than truncating
player-visible text. A panicking native callback is also refused.

A mod changed the commands it registers (`register_commands`):
at the start of the next server tick every mod is asked again, the
commands players may run are rebuilt, and every player on the server is
sent their tree again, after `player_commands_sent`. Nothing
happens where no world is open to players, and nothing for a server
whose mods never call it. API @API:refresh_commands@.

Side: server.
Runs `line` (no slash) as the server's console does: permission
level 4, from the overworld's spawn, with no output. A teleport to
another level (`execute in minecraft:the_nether run tp Alex 0 70 0`)
happens at the next tick's start, as the console's. Whether it ran
without failing. During a guest's turn, live players (including the
acting player) are reachable; displaced outer players are excluded
from name, UUID and selector resolution on this path only.

Side: server.
`run_command` with its feedback kept: the same line, source and run
path (one leading slash is dropped here), answering with whether it
ran without failing (`success`, what `run_command` returns) and what the
console would have printed for it as plain text (`feedback`, as a mod
that answers a remote console wants; Paper's `Server.dispatchCommand`
with a capturing `CommandSender`). The feedback of the command alone is
kept, never the lines other code logs meanwhile; a call made while
another one runs captures its own lines and the outer capture goes on
unchanged. At most 256 lines of 4096 bytes each
come back (a longer line is cut at a character boundary). A command that ran and failed
is `success: false` with its message in `feedback`. A line run where no server
is open to players, or empty once its whitespace and slash are
dropped, runs nothing and is `success: false` with no feedback, exactly as
`run_command` answers `false` for it; no refusal type tells those
apart from a failed command, as `run_command` has none either. The
dedicated console's own commands (`stop`, `op`, `whitelist`, `ban`...)
are not reached: they answer as an unknown command.

the block position: the same seed and position give the same value on every thread, every
run and every machine, or chunks, far terrain and structures disagree. It must not panic: a
panic is not caught and goes to whatever asked for the value, as one in any native worldgen
hook does (on the worldgen workers, a crash report naming the mod and the type, then exit). A
NaN or a value outside [`range`](Self::range) panics the same way.

and z. `out` holds exactly that many, y fastest, then x, then z (the game's own buffer
order, no copy). The default asks [`sample`](Self::sample) for each; override it to reuse
work across a column or a volume. It must give what `sample` gives at each position and
must write every slot: `out` may hold other values when called, and a slot left unwritten
or NaN is rejected.

beyond it the density JSON fails to load): every value [`sample`](Self::sample) and
[`fill`](Self::fill) give lies in it, or the game panics naming the type. Read once, when the node decodes; vanilla's interval
arithmetic (spline ranges, range choices, aquifer and vein bounds) works from it, so a
wrong range gives wrong terrain.

terrain and structure heights otherwise ask [`fill`](Self::fill). NaN is rejected.

column. Read once, when the node decodes.

alone keeps no state. Refused by name ([`SceneError`]): over a cap (16
entities, 512 live particles, 4 animating scenes a frame), an entity

Declare the initial attribute set of the mod's entity type `path`
(NeoForge's `EntityAttributeCreationEvent`), starting from `template`'s
(`minecraft:zombie`, the one the type's content file copies, as
`Zombie.createAttributes` builds on the template's): each attribute's
id (`minecraft:max_health`) and the base value that differs from the
template's. The values reach the type's own fields, its live attribute
map and the attribute sync, so attribute reads answer the
same defaults with no second copy.

refuses the mods, naming the mod; an attribute the game does not know,

Add attributes to an existing entity type's default set (NeoForge's
`EntityAttributeModificationEvent`): `entity` is any type with an
attribute row (`minecraft:zombie`; a bare name is in `minecraft`): a
vanilla type, or a mod's type with a declared set. A living type that
only a content file defines has no row of its own yet; declare its set
with [`declare_entity_attributes`](Self::declare_entity_attributes)
first, and the additions apply on top of it. Each attribute's id
(`minecraft:luck`) takes its base, or with none the attribute's own
default, as the event's one-argument `add`. An attribute the type
already has takes the new base. The change is the type's default:
entities created after load have it, through their spawn fields, their
live attribute map and the attribute sync; nothing edits a live entity.

Applied once, at load, after every declared set
([`declare_entity_attributes`](Self::declare_entity_attributes)), in
registration order, so a later addition of the same attribute wins.

non-finite base refuses the mods, naming the mod; an attribute the
game does not know, or a type without an attribute row, refuses the
resource load, naming the type.

traits.doc:
An entity type's part (arismoko/horizon#1077): code attached through
`RegistrationContext::entity_part` to one entity type, a mod's own or vanilla's
(`minecraft:zombie`). Its `register_goals` runs at every `Mob` construction of that
type, spawned or loaded, right after the species' own goals — vanilla's `registerGoals`
moment — and the goals it adds join the mob's two selectors beside vanilla's, same
priorities and interruption. Its `register_behaviors` runs wherever a brain-driven
species' brain is built (#824). Its `spawn_cluster_size` answers how large a spawn group of the
type may grow. Its `general_entity_tick` runs for one general entity row's authoritative
tick (#792). Annotate each part trait implementation with
[`horizon_part`] to derive its subscriptions; the goal, behavior and spawn-size methods
are not hooks, so they subscribe nothing whatever they override.

methods.doc:
The authoritative tick of one general entity row of type `kind`
(`mymod:robot`), with ID `entity`, in the server level's entity phase:
`ServerLevel.tickNonPassenger`'s `entity.tick()` for a row the type
registry owns (arismoko/horizon#792 stage 4). The row's common bookkeeping has run
(its previous position is its current one); a rider is ticked after
its vehicle inside the vehicle's own tick, depth-first as
`tickPassenger` recurses, and is never ticked as a root. Rows that
joined this tick tick from the next, parked levels and rows outside
entity-ticking chunks do not tick, and a `entity_tick_pre` that
cancels the row cancels its whole rider subtree. Read and change the
row's data through its attachments (`event.entity` is their holder);
there is no parallel per-entity state. Told only for general entity
types: vanilla families tick their own paths (#6509 owns bringing
them to one join-order walk), so a part attached to `minecraft:zombie`
hears no tick from this hook. Server-side.
Side: server.

Whether `entity` can be sheared now with `shears` (NeoForge's `IShearable.isShearable`), asked
where a player's shears (`player` is who holds them) or a dispenser's (`player` none) meet it,
before the `player_shear_entity` or `block_shear_entity` hook. The first part to answer wins, in
dispatch order: `Some(true)` shears it through [`EntityPart::on_sheared`] in place of the
species' own shearing, `Some(false)` leaves it unsheared (a player's click then does nothing),
and `None` leaves it to the next part and then to the species. Server-side.

[`EntityPart::is_shearable`] said `Some(true)`, once the shear hooks let it through. Change
the entity and play its sound here, and return the drops: the game spawns each as
`spawnShearedDrop` does (one block above the entity's feet, with a small random push), posts
the shear game event and damages the shears. Server-side.

Native mods only: entity parts do not cross to wasm yet.
The mob's mod brain behaviors, joined into the species' brain beside
vanilla's (#824): built wherever the brain is built — its first tick and
every rebuild — started and stopped in `Brain.tick`'s order, fresh state
each build, nothing saved. Branch on the mob with `behaviors.mob()`.

The mob's mod goals, added to its two selectors as `GoalSelector.addGoal`
does in vanilla's `registerGoals`: fresh at every construction, so a goal's
state is never saved. Branch on the mob with `goals.mob()`.

How many mobs one spawn group of this mob's type may grow to (`Mob.getMaxSpawnClusterSize`), asked
where the spawner has just added a mob to a group and compares the group's size with the limit:
natural spawning's packs. `mob` is the mob just spawned, finalized and in
no level yet, to read through `host`; `reason` and `spawner` say why and from what it spawned
(`spawner` is none but for a spawner block's mobs); `vanilla` is the limit the species has. Answer
`Some(limit)` to replace it and `None` to leave it to the next part and then to vanilla's. The
first part to answer wins, in dispatch order, and the group stops growing once its size reaches
the limit, so a limit of 0 or 1 ends it with the mob just spawned. The host is the read-only
one: a listener runs on replayed ticks and must be a pure function of its inputs.

traits.doc:
A mod's layer: NeoForge's `RenderLayer`, held by the game for every entity of its target.
Entities of a target share one layer, so what differs between them comes from
[`EntityRenderState`].

A frame has no `Host`: drawing reads nothing of the world but what the state, the parts and
`draw` give. A layer that needs more reads it in a hook and keeps what it read.

required.name: submit
required.signature: fn submit(&self, _: &EntityRenderState, _: Option<&PosedParts>, _: &mut dyn BlockEntityDrawContext) -> Result<(), String>

methods.doc:
`RenderLayer.submit`: draw over `entity` with `draw`'s helpers (`quad`, `cube`, `block`,
`item`, `model_part`), after its model and the layers before this one. The pose stack starts
in the entity's frame: at its feet, turned with its body, +z the way it faces, +x its left,
+y up, in blocks (`entity.yaw` is the body's turn, `entity.pitch` the head's). `parts` are a
humanoid model's parts as vanilla posed them this frame, to attach to an arm or the head;
None for a model that isn't humanoid. `draw` also has the partial tick, the game time and
the entity's light. Asked once a frame for each entity of the target in view, but not for
one whose `render_living_pre` or `render_player_pre` a mod canceled: as with NeoForge's
canceled `RenderLivingEvent.Pre`, none of its layers draw then. A frame is
drawn afresh: `draw.keep()` does nothing here. `Ok(())` keeps what it drew. An `Err`, a
panic, and a wasm call that is refused or traps all mean the same: what it drew this frame
is dropped, the error is logged once, and the layer is asked no more until the next
resource load adds it again.
methods.signature: fn submit(&self, _: &EntityRenderState, _: Option<&PosedParts>, _: &mut dyn BlockEntityDrawContext) -> Result<(), String>

A mod's entity renderer: NeoForge's `EntityRenderer`, held by the game for every entity of the
type it is registered for. Entities of a type share one renderer, so what differs between them
comes from [`EntityRenderState`].

A frame has no `Host`: drawing reads nothing of the world but what the state and `draw` give.
A renderer that needs more reads it in a hook and keeps what it read.

methods.doc:
`EntityRenderer.submit`: draw `entity` with `draw`'s helpers (`quad`, `cube`, `block`,
`item`, `model_part`) under its pose stack, which starts at the entity's position, not
turned: turn it by `entity.yaw` and `entity.pitch` as the model needs. `draw` also has
the partial tick, the game time and the entity's light. Asked once a frame for each entity
of the type in view; what it draws replaces the type's own drawing. A frame is drawn
afresh: `draw.keep()` does nothing here. A native implementation returns `Ok(())` in the
normal case, and that keeps what it drew. Diverges: Horizon's `submit` returns a `Result`
so a refused or trapped call is visible. An `Err`, a panic, and a wasm call that is
refused or traps all mean the same: what it drew this frame is dropped, the error is
logged once, and the renderer is asked no more until the next resource load resolves it
again; until then its type draws as it would without one.

methods.doc:
`AddAttributeTooltipsEvent`: the lines that follow a stack's attribute lines
(`ItemStack.addAttributeTooltips`), after the modifiers the stack shows and
`gather_skipped_attribute_tooltips` left in. Push lines to `lines`, each with a colour as
`rgba` packs it (`u32::MAX` keeps the text's own); they land beside the attribute lines
without finding where those end. `shown` is whether the stack's
`minecraft:tooltip_display` shows the attribute modifiers (`shouldShow`); the hook is
asked either way. `player` and `player_entity_id` are the local player's,
`None` for the recipe book's search text, which has none and drops the colours, and for a stack
nested in another's tooltip (a crossbow's loaded projectile); `advanced`
(F3+H) and `creative` (a creative tab's own slot) are the tooltip's `TooltipFlag`. Asked
each frame the tooltip shows, only while a mod listens. Client-side.
A component deeper than 512 nodes refuses capture or the whole writeback;
no event field is applied if any Text field fails conversion.
Side: client.

Register client asset reload listeners before a reload stages its
assets (NeoForge's `AddClientReloadListenersEvent`, the client's
counterpart of `add_server_reload_listeners`): the first load
on the loader thread, then every later reload — the player
changed resource packs, F3+T was pressed, or a server sent its packs.
The listener's `prepare` then reads the merged asset view with
resource-pack overrides resolved, and its returned apply publishes the
parsed state, all applies after all prepares, before
`client_resources_reloaded`. A listener that returns an error
aborts the reload and keeps every listener's previous assets.
Client-side, in Reloading nested in Setup initially and World later.
Later registration is on the render thread, prepare on the loader,
and apply on the owning game thread; completion restores the entering
phase. Startup's empty Host grants no extra access.
Side: client.

Add discoverable resource or data packs before a repository selects its
packs (`AddPackFindersEvent`). The builder reports the repository's pack
type. Runs at startup and whenever that repository is rediscovered; no
world state is available during startup registration.
Side: both.

Extra geometry in chunk section meshes (NeoForge's `AddSectionGeometryEvent`):
`register(renderer)` adds the mod's own `SectionGeometry`, which the mesher asks to add its
quads every time it meshes a section, on its worker threads. The quads are part of that
section's mesh: they follow its rebuilds, are never drawn twice, and go when it unloads.
Asked once at start on the client, before resources load.
Side: client.

Register server data reload listeners after packs are selected. The
host gives registry access at registration, as
`AddServerReloadListenersEvent.getRegistryAccess` does. Runs every data
load on the owning server thread in Reloading: only registry facts,
settings and mod-list reads are available through this Host. World
handles, services and transactions panic naming the phase. Existing
data-load callbacks retain their DataLoadContext; no setup event is added.
Side: server.

A tree's `alter_ground` decorator (`AlterGroundDecorator.place`, the
podzol under a big spruce) is about to turn the ground around
`positions`: the lowest of its trunk or roots (`logs` if it has no roots,
`logs` and `roots` when they start level, else `roots`); only those at
the first one's Y are placed around. `logs`, `leaves` and `roots` are the
decorator context's lists, each sorted by Y. Set `provider` to your own
`GroundProvider::Mod` to choose the ground; to change it only where you
like, wrap the provider you found and ask it for the rest, since several
mods may each wrap the one before. Once per decorated tree, before any
ground is placed; the hook itself draws nothing. Server-side, on the
worldgen worker threads (and on the server thread when a sapling grows),
with the server's worldgen `context`: no `Host`, no writes.
Side: server.

Every mod gets `event.provider` in order and may add, change or remove provider.

The player `tamer` (UUID) and `tamer_entity_id` is about to tame the
mob `entity` of `kind` (`AnimalTameEvent`): its taming roll succeeded
(a wolf's bone, a cat's fish, a parrot's seeds or a nautilus's food;
a horse, donkey, mule or llama the player rides). Set `cancel` for the

in reach, where `Player.attack` starts. The swing has not begun, so the
attacking player's attack strength is still the charge the blow uses
(vanilla reads it at the start of `Player.attack`; the swing resets it
afterwards). Set `canceled` and the blow does nothing (no damage, no
knockback, the frame keeps its item). Server-side, for every player of

`BabyEntitySpawnEvent`, vanilla's `Animal.spawnChildFromBreeding`):
`parent` and `partner` are entity ids, `player` and `player_entity_id`
the UUID and entity id of the player who fed them into love
(`getCausedByPlayer`, None when none), `kind` the baby's type (a horse
and a donkey have a mule). NeoForge's `setChild` (another baby)
needs a handle to a mob not yet in the world, which this hook does not expose. Set `cancel` for no baby: the
parents still rest and lose their love (their ages were already set
to 6000), but there is no baby, no experience, no `animals_bred`
statistic, no advancement and no heart particles. Not fired for
turtles, frogs and sniffers (an egg, no baby) or armadillos' own paths.
Villagers do not post this animal-only event, matching NeoForge's
documented `Animal.spawnChildFromBreeding` posting site; a rejected
villager join instead leaves the child's bed free. On the server.
Side: server.

quads to `quads` for a loader your mod owns. `config` is the model's JSON object converted
to a `Tag`, and `model` names the model. It is asked once per model on each resource load,
on the resource loader, never per frame.
Side: client.

Every mod gets `event.quads` in order and may add, change or remove quads.

A beacon at `pos` activated or deactivated after its beam was checked.
`active` says whether it now has a complete pyramid. Server-side.

Change the colours of `biome` (`minecraft:plains`) on this client: the
grass, foliage (leaves, vines), dry foliage (leaf litter) and water
tints, 0xRRGGBB, as its biome file and the colormaps set them. Asked
for every biome when a mod calls `native_refresh_biome_colors`, which
rebuilds the terrain with them; a season mod answers from its season
and calls that when the season turns. The dark forest's modifier
still applies to the grass set here; the swamp's noise colours
replace it.
Side: client.

A server guest's block-breaking animation changed to `progress` at
`pos` (0 through 9).
Side: server.

The world contains `new`; block side effects and neighbour updates follow.
Side: server.

A block finished cooking `item` into `result` at `pos`.
Side: server.

A server player stopped digging `pos` before the block broke, after
the server cleared the dig and sent the block back to the client.
The player's state is not swapped in.
Side: server.

A dispenser equipped `item` on the first eligible `target` in front
of its block at `pos`. `target` is `player`, `mob` or `armor_stand`.
The equip, item consumption, sound and game event have completed.
Server-side.
Side: server.

NeoForge's `BlockDropsEvent`: a block `state` broke at `pos` and `Block.dropResources` has built the item entities `drops` it will spawn, but nothing is in the world yet. `breaker` is the breaking player's UUID (none for a break the level makes: a piston, water, a neighbour update, `/setblock destroy`) and `tool` the stack they used (none when no tool). `breaker_entity` is the entity that broke the block (NeoForge's `getBreaker()`): the player, or the mob whose own break of this block is running (a ravager's, a wither's). It is none when no entity broke it: a piston, water, a neighbour update, `/setblock destroy` and explosions. `block_entity` is the block's block entity (NeoForge's `getBlockEntity()`), none for a block without one and for explosions (their blocks are already gone). For a player's break the removal has already taken the block entity out of the world, so its saved data, read before the removal (its `CustomName` too), is held through the event: `level.block_entity_data(entity)` reads it, and the handle is stale (reads refuse) once the event ends, also if a listener panics. `drops` is the list `Block.popResource` built: each stack with the position, motion and pickup delay its item entity will have, drawn before the event as vanilla draws them, so the level random's order does not depend on whether a mod listens. Edit the list (take out, change or add drops; empty stacks don't spawn) or `experience`, the points `spawnAfterBreak` would award at the block's centre (ores, sculk, spawners; silk touch has already zeroed it, as NeoForge's description says, "the true value, after enchantments"). Set `cancel` and nothing spawns: no drops, no experience, and none of `spawnAfterBreak`'s other effects (an infested block's silverfish); a bee nest's bees are `playerDestroy`'s, not `spawnAfterBreak`'s, and still come out. With the `block_drops` rule off the list and the experience are emptied after the event. It fires on the player's break, a mob's block break that drops loot, explosions and every level-side `Block.dropResources` (a piston breaking a block, water washing one away, a removed support). Player, explosion and mob block loot passes through `loot_drops` first; level-side breaks are not asked `loot_drops`. Explosion events run after the blast has removed its blocks and merged their loot, before any items spawn, with no breaker or tool and zero initial experience. Each block's event owns only its share of a merged stack, at that entity's prepared position and velocity; cancellation cannot remove another block's share. Unchanged shares rejoin the original merged entity, while edited or added entities spawn exactly as returned. Even a block with no loot gets an event (TNT that primes instead does not). Neither registration nor a no-op listener changes the merge or the level random's draws. It does not fire for dispensers or a block's own loot-table drop through another path. It runs inside the level's write, so the level host reads blocks and draws the level's random in vanilla's order and writes nothing. Authoritative servers only. Replaces `block_exp`, whose catalog row named no NeoForge event (`none`) and fired only on the level-side path: the amount is `experience` here. Diverges from upstream: `block_exp` is removed into this hook.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.

Extend existing types' valid blocks (NeoForge `BlockEntityTypeAddBlocksEvent`).
Fired after content declarations, before worlds load. `types` contains every
registered type. Append `(type, block)` pairs to `additions`; this never changes
the block's factory or ticker. Filter `types` to implement predicate selection.
Use `event.modify(kind, blocks)` for a direct addition, or
`event.modify_matching(predicate, blocks)` for all matching registered keys.
Duplicate additions are harmless; unknown keys or incompatible classes fail startup.
Existing sign-template memberships remain valid without a listener.
Blocks must share the common vanilla superclass of the type's existing blocks.
Side: both.

Draw a block overlay a mod said it draws itself (`custom_draw` in
`extract_block_screen_effect`), before vanilla's overlay of that kind, once a frame each.
A canceled overlay is asked too. Set `replace_vanilla` to leave vanilla's overlay out.
`effect`, `state` and `pos` are the extract event's; `partial_tick` is the world's and
`hide_gui` says the HUD is hidden. Every mod is asked about every such overlay, so a mod
ignores those it did not claim. Client-side.
Side: client.

A dispenser sheared `entity` of kind `kind` at the block in front of
its own block at `pos`, after the shearing effects. Server-side.
Side: server.

into `to` (`kind` is `fluid` or `fire`): `FlowingFluid.spreadTo`, and
`FireBlock.tick` setting fire to `to` or burning it (`checkBurnOut`).
Set `canceled` to leave the block at `to` as it is. Fluids ask on
every flow: answer fast.

No self: the simulation owns the entity during this callback.
Side: server.

A tool is about to transform a block. Cancel or replace the final state;
`None` suppresses the transformation. The block's own `tool_modified_state` part answers
first, and a block whose part cancelled the action never reaches this hook.

Blocks this mod adds, declared in code rather than one file each
(NeoForge's `DeferredRegister.Blocks` drained by `RegisterEvent`):
push a `mod_api::Block` per block, the same declaration
a content mod's `data/<id>/horizon/block/<path>.json` holds (a
vanilla `template`, `properties`, `state_properties`, `shapes`...),
with its id in a namespace owned by your mod's manifest. It has a block
item, as a file's does, unless `item` is false (`Block::with_item(false)`).
They join the content mods' blocks: the one whose
id is that namespace when it is on (your models, textures, loot and
recipes are its files), else one of their own, with the template's
look. Ids, saves and the check that a joining client has the same
blocks are the files' (docs/modding/src/how-to/content-mods.md). Asked once at start, on every
side, before any resource loads: push the same ones every time, from
nothing but your code. Unowned namespaces refuse registration, naming the mod
and namespace. Each mod receives its own declaration batch. Declarations
that don't pass the other files' checks
are logged and that namespace's are left out.
Side: both.

Each mod receives its own empty `event.blocks` batch. A bare name, in an identifier or
in `block_item`, `pick_item`, `wall_block`, `base_block`, `crafting_remainder` or `Item::block`,
is that mod's own; declared identifiers must belong to
that mod's manifest-owned namespaces, and unowned identifiers refuse registration.

`BonemealEvent`: bone meal from `stack` used on the block `state` at
`pos` (`BoneMealItem.growCrop`), by `player` or, when it is `None`, by
a dispenser or a villager. `valid_bonemeal_target` is the block's
`isValidBonemealTarget`. Cancel skips vanilla's growth, the block's
own bone meal Parts and the meal's use: `growCrop` then answers
`successful` (`setSuccessful`), which is `false` unless a mod sets it.
Fired on both sides; changes to `stack` stay. Set it to None to consume
the whole stack; a nonempty result is validated before any write-back.
Side: both.

(the held item can break blocks, the debug stick didn't take the
click): where `ServerPlayerGameMode.destroyBlock` starts. Set
`canceled` to keep the block: nothing is destroyed or dropped, and a
guest sees it back. Set `exp_to_drop` to `Some(amount)` to replace
the experience sample later, after item drops are prepared;
`None` keeps sampling. A subscribed block part's `exp_drop` answer is
supplied as this event's initial amount. `block_drops` sees and may change that
amount afterwards; cancellation or disabled block drops suppresses it.
Server-side, for every player of the world (the
helpers read the acting one). Diverges from upstream: renamed from
`destroy_block`, to NeoForge's `BreakBlockEvent`.
Side: server.

The player's state is swapped in, so `PlayerRef::tell` answers them. Only
for guests of a server. `fill_bucket` hears this click too (and
the filling one) without the player and the fluid. Not heard: a
dispenser, a cauldron, and a fluid a block places itself.

The stacks a mod adds to the creative tab `tab` (`minecraft:ingredients`, or another mod's
`<mod id>:<name>`) while the tabs' contents are built (NeoForge's
`BuildCreativeModeTabContentsEvent`, during vanilla's `CreativeModeTabs.buildAllTabContents`):
push each stack to `items`, in order (`accept`). They come after the tab's own items and
those of the mods before, and join the end of the search tab. A stack the tab or the search
tab already lists (the same item and components) is not listed twice there, and an empty
stack is left out. `has_permissions` is the build's `hasPermissions`: whether the operator
items tab is allowed (the player can use game master blocks and the Operator Items Tab
option is on). Asked for every item tab, the operator items tab and the mods' tabs among
them, not for the search, saved toolbars or survival inventory tabs. Asked when the tabs
are built: the first time the creative inventory opens after the game's resources load,
and again whenever `has_permissions` changes. Client-side.
Side: client.

Every mod gets `event.items` in order and may add, change or remove items.

The mouse sensitivity and cinematic camera option a grabbed player's
mouse turn reads this frame (`MouseHandler.turnPlayer`). Change either
for this turn only; the options are unchanged. Client-side. This shapes how far the
mouse turns the view; `ClientHost::set_local_rotation` sets the view directly, and the
two meet in the same angles the tick's move packet sends.
Side: client.

Final scaled third-person camera distance, before visual-shape collision clipping.
`entity` includes its living scale/distance and optional mount scale/distance.
Only finite requests in 0..=1024 blocks replace the vanilla distance.
Side: client.

The camera this frame is drawn from, `partial` ticks past the last tick, after vanilla
placed it (`Camera.update`): its position, and its yaw and pitch in degrees. Set them to
draw the world from anywhere: a cinematic or replay camera. Only the picture, the sound's
listener and the billboards facing the camera follow it; the player, where they aim, the
first-person hand and which chunks load stay the player's. Values that aren't finite keep
vanilla's. Not called on the title screen's panorama.
`camera_roll`, asked right after, rolls it.
Side: client.

The roll of the camera this frame is drawn from, in degrees about its view direction,
asked right after `camera_pose` with the same `partial`. It starts at 0 each frame and is
kept within a turn. It turns the drawn camera, a front view's too: at +90 the world's up
is at the screen's left, as `Camera.setRotation`'s roll and NeoForge's
`ViewportEvent.ComputeCameraAngles` turn it. The picture, the frustum, the billboards facing the camera, `Camera.view`
and `project` follow it; the first-person hand, the HUD and where the player aims don't.
Distortion Effects doesn't scale it, unlike `camera_shake`. A value that isn't finite is
0. Not called on the title screen's panorama.
Side: client.

The camera shake native mods ask for in this frame, `partial` ticks
past the last tick (0 to 1): add your pitch, yaw and roll in degrees
and your offset in blocks, along the camera's right, up and back, to
`shake`, so several mods' shakes add up. Read while playing only;
Horizon scales the sum by Distortion Effects and bounds it
(`native_shake_matrix`).
Side: client.

Camera submersion fog type (`Camera.getFluidInCamera`), checked before fog and camera
fluid effects are set up. Allows native mods (such as Freecam) to clear underwater,
lava or powder snow submersion by setting `fog_type` to `FogType::Atmospheric`.
Side: client.

`key.togglePerspective` (F5) is cycling the window's camera type (`Minecraft.handleKeybinds`
calling `Options.setCameraType(getCameraType().cycle())`): `previous` is the type it leaves,
and `next` comes in as vanilla's next one (first person, third person behind, third person
in front, then first person again); set `next` to another, to skip a type or keep one.
Once a press, before the type changes; the post effect of the camera entity follows the
answer as it follows vanilla's. `camera_type` and `set_camera_type` read and set the type
at any other moment. Client-side. Beyond NeoForge: there is no counterpart. Diverges from
upstream: new hook.
Side: client.

An item was placed on a campfire at `pos` and began cooking.
Side: server.

`CanContinueSleepingEvent`: a sleeping living entity's check that it may go on
sleeping, run each tick for a server player the dead and health checks would not
already wake, and for a sleeping villager or wandering trader. `entity` is its UUID,
`name` a player's name (empty for a mob) and `kind` its type (`minecraft:player`).
`problem` is what vanilla found (`getProblem`): `NotPossibleHere` when the bed at `pos`
is gone, `NotPossibleNow` when a player's bed rule no longer lets them sleep (daytime),
none when nothing is wrong. `may_continue` starts empty, meaning `problem.is_none()` (`mayContinueSleeping`);
set it `Some(true)` to keep them asleep, `Some(false)` to wake them. The player's state is not swapped in
on a guest tick.
Side: server.

Return `Some` to set `may_continue`; the first mod returning `Some` wins.
methods.signature: fn can_continue_sleeping(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut CanContinueSleepingEvent<'_>) -> Option<bool>

methods.doc:
`Player.canEat` for `stack`, from `Consumable.canConsume` when eating
starts and block interaction eligibility for cake and candle cake.
For cake, `stack` is the held stack (None for an empty hand), and
`can_always_eat` is false. `vanilla_can_eat` is vanilla's answer (creative,
`can_always_eat`, or hungry). Answer `Some(false)` to refuse the food,
`Some(true)` to let a full player eat; `can_eat` left `None` keeps
`vanilla_can_eat`. Both sides (the client starts eating as the
server does), so answer from the stack and the player alone.
Side: both.

Return `Some` to set `can_eat`; the first mod returning `Some` wins.

A server player tries to sleep in the bed whose head is at `pos`
(NeoForge's `CanPlayerSleepEvent`, vanilla's `ServerPlayer.startSleepInBed`).
`problem` is what vanilla found, first problem only: `too_far_away`,
`obstructed`, `not_possible_now` (not night or thunder, the bed rule),
`not_safe` (monsters near), or `None`. A mod may set `None` to let the
player sleep anyway, or one of those names (`other_problem` refuses
without a message) to refuse. The spawn point is set before it fires,
as in vanilla, only when vanilla found no problem. After it,
`player_bed_enter` still fires and may cancel. Server-side.
Side: server.

On an authoritative server, a cauldron at `pos` is about to change
fill level from `from_level` to `to_level` for `reason`. Set `cancel`
to leave it unchanged.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.

A public chat line from `sender` (`sender_name`) is about to reach the placed player
`recipient`: a player's chat after `server_chat` let it through, or a `/say` or `/me`
(signed or not). `message` is the text players see: what `server_chat` left, or the
command's text. Set `hidden` and that one receiver is not sent the line at all, no chat
index and no pending acknowledgement; the others still get it, signed as it was sent, so
its signature still verifies for them. It is asked once for each placed receiver, the
sender included, before any of them is sent the line, in the order the hub lists them.
Whispers (`/msg`) are not public and are not heard here, and neither is the line the
server's log keeps: hiding is per receiver. This is not a second `server_chat`: that
hook is heard once for a line, only for typed chat, and cancels it for everyone; this one
is per receiver, and covers `/say` and `/me`. With no listener nothing is asked and
nothing is allocated. A fault or an epoch timeout in a wasm listener answers nothing, so
the line is sent, like every cancellable hook. No player's state is swapped in.
Server-side.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `hidden`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn chat_recipient(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut ChatRecipientEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
`chat_suggestion_applied(original, start, end, suggestion, input)` reports a chat completion after Tab or a click. The range is in UTF-16 units of the list's original input, including when cycling; input is the resulting length-limited field value. Client-only, read-only. Bundles need "hooks": @API:chat_suggestion_applied@.
Side: client.

Chunk `chunk` (`[x, z]`, in chunks) of `dimension` came into the world
(NeoForge's `ChunkEvent.Load`): `new` when it was just generated, false
when read from the save. A flat world's chunk that leaves before it's
first lit isn't saved, so it's generated, and new, again; one generated
as the players left is new when it next comes, unless the server
restarts first, or the level closes for being empty, which drops its
memory of what never saved. Its blocks and block entities are there,
but its saved entities join afterwards and its light may not be ready:
change the world from a later tick. The chunks around the spawn come
before `server_started`. Not told of a chunk a client receives.
The chunks leaving in the same tick were already copied for their last
save: an edit made here to one of them (a neighbour's block entity, say)
is not in that copy, and is dropped with the chunk.
Server-side.
Side: server.

`chunk`'s packet went to `player` (NeoForge's `ChunkWatchEvent.Sent`,
at the end of `PlayerChunkSender.sendChunk`), after `chunk_watch`, so
a mod can send its own data for the chunk now. Told after the server's
network step for the level, with the state after that step, as
`chunk_watch`. Not told for the far ring's columns. Server-side.
Side: server.

`chunk`'s ticket level went from `old` to `new` (NeoForge's
`ChunkTicketLevelUpdatedEvent`, from `ChunkMap.updateChunkScheduling`):
a player, a forced chunk, a portal or the dragon fight's arena began or
ceased to keep it alive or ticking. It is the level of the chunk's
loading tickets (`DistanceManager`'s chunk tracker), not the
simulation distance's. A level is a `ChunkTicketLevel`: the number
`ChunkLevel` gives, 31 and lower entity ticking, 32 block ticking and 33
loaded without ticking, or `Unloaded`; none is clamped to the ticking
range. Never told with `old == new`.

Told in order, once for each time a chunk's level changed: a chunk that
changes twice in a tick is told twice, the second `old` the first `new`.
Within one update of the level's tickets the chunks come by position (x,
then z), which is not vanilla's order. A new level's tickets tell every
chunk they keep loaded as coming from `Unloaded`. Told once a tick, in
the server's tick of the level, after the tickets were updated for
every player there; a level with no player in it is not ticked and
tells nothing until it is. NeoForge's `chunkHolder` is not given:
Horizon keeps no chunk holders. Server-side.
Side: server.

Chunk `chunk` of `dimension` left the world (NeoForge's
`ChunkEvent.Unload`), with a level that closes for being empty too. Don't
read its blocks. Its block entities are still there, but changes made in
this hook aren't saved: as in vanilla, the chunk is saved before it unloads.
Not told when the world closes, which `world_lifecycle` tells.
Server-side.
Side: server.

`player` stopped watching `chunk` (NeoForge's `ChunkWatchEvent.UnWatch`,
`ChunkMap.dropChunk`): it left their view, or they leave the level
(through a portal or a teleport, or respawning) or the server. Once for
each chunk `chunk_watch` told of. After a disconnect the player handle
no longer reads. Told after the server's network step for the level,
with the state after that step, as `chunk_watch`. Not told when the
server stops. Server-side.
Side: server.

`player` started watching `chunk` (NeoForge's `ChunkWatchEvent.Watch`):
the chunk came into their view and goes to their client, once until
`chunk_unwatch`. Vanilla tells it as the chunk is queued
(`ChunkMap.markChunkPendingToSend`); Horizon picks a chunk only as it
sends it, so this comes just before `chunk_sent` for the same chunk.
Told after the server's network step for the level, and a handler sees
the state after that step; the order per player and chunk is vanilla's.
Not told for the far ring's columns past the view distance (a Horizon
server option). Server-side.
Side: server.

Before a client's ordinary melee click attacks entities (not a spear jab), after the
interaction-key cancellation hook. `targets` starts with the crosshair entity, if any.
Replace, clear or append targets for redirected or multi-target hits. There is no batch
cap. Duplicates are sent once, in first-occurrence order. Every target is rechecked for
the current client epoch, attackability, reach,
held-item range and occlusion. Clearing an entity hit does not mine the block behind
it; an untouched empty list keeps vanilla's block/miss path. Server checks and cooldowns
still apply to every attack. Returning `Flow::Cancel` cancels the whole batch.
NeoForge's `AttackEntityEvent` is the corresponding attack notice; this hook is client-side only.
Side: client.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `canceled`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn client_attack_target(&self, _: &mut dyn ClientHost, _: &mut ClientAttackTargetEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
NeoForge's `ClientChatEvent`: a client is about to send `message`.
`original_message` is immutable; change `message` or set `cancel` to
prevent sending.
Side: client.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn client_chat(&self, _: &mut dyn ClientHost, _: &mut ClientChatEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
NeoForge's `ClientChatReceivedEvent`: a chat line from the server is
about to show, once Chat Delay lets it through. `system` is a system
message (`ClientChatReceivedEvent.System`), shown in the action bar
when `overlay` is set; otherwise a player or disguised message in its
chat type `chat_type` (`getBoundChatType`, its registry name; `None`
for a system message or an inline chat type). `sender` is the player's
UUID, 0 (`Util.NIL_UUID`) for system and disguised messages.
`player_message` is the message as the player signed it
(`ClientChatReceivedEvent.Player.getPlayerChatMessage`): its body,
whether a signature validated, timestamp, salt, the server's unsigned
replacement and the filter mask; `None` for system and disguised
messages. `message`
starts as the decorated line; replace it and the chat shows the new
one, while the narrator still says the original. Set `cancel` and it
doesn't show: a delayed message lets the next one through. Lines the
client adds itself and validation errors are not told. Client-side.
Side: client.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn client_chat_received(&self, _: &mut dyn ClientHost, _: &mut ClientChatReceivedEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
Chunk `chunk` (`[x, z]`, in chunks) of `dimension` came into this
client's level from the server (NeoForge's `ChunkEvent.Load` on the
client, whose `isNewChunk` is always false there): once per chunk
packet the client adopts, after the column and its block entities are
in the level, so a listener reads its blocks through `ClientHost`. A
column the server sends again while it is resident is told again.
Only on a client of a server, a LAN guest included; an integrated
world's own chunks have the server's `chunk_load`. Client-side.
Side: client.

Chunk `chunk` (`[x, z]`, in chunks) of `dimension` is leaving this
client's level (NeoForge's `ChunkEvent.Unload` on the client): once
per resident column, with its blocks still there, just before they are
freed. Told on every route a column leaves by: the server's forget
packet, the view centre moving away, the view radius shrinking, and
the client level going (a dimension change, a respawn into another
level, leaving the server). That is wider than NeoForge, which tells
only the forget packet, so a listener never keeps state for a column
that is gone. Only on a client of a server, a LAN guest included; an
integrated world's own chunks have the server's `chunk_unload`.
Client-side.
Side: client.

Before an actual connection is discarded, not on a dimension change.
Side: client.

NeoForge's `ClientInformationUpdatedEvent`: a server player's client sent new
client information (language, view distance, chat, skin parts, main hand,
filtering, listing, particles) in play. `old` and `new` are the values before and
after this packet, one call per packet; they can be equal. The join's own
information is reported too, once, just before `player_logged_in`, with
`old` the defaults (`ClientInformation.createDefault`) and `new` what the
client joined with, as NeoForge fires it when `ServerPlayer` first sets
it. The player is not swapped in. Server-side.
Side: server.

The client made a new level for `dimension` (NeoForge's
`LevelEvent.Load` from the `ClientLevel` constructor): on joining a
server, single player's own included, and on changing dimension.
Its chunks come after. When the dimension changes, the old level's
`client_level_unload` follows this, as `Minecraft.setLevel`
tells it after the new level is made. Client-side, on the window; the
server's levels have `level_load`.
Side: client.

The client dropped its level for `dimension` (`LevelEvent.Unload`
from `Minecraft.setLevel` and `disconnect`): replaced by another
dimension's, or on leaving the server. Once for each
`client_level_load`. Not told when the game itself quits.
Client-side.
Side: client.

Veto a predicted client dig after the interaction mapping and vanilla eligibility checks.
Auto-tool and mining overlay mods can use this instead of a mining prediction mixin.
The snapshot is read-only. A veto skips the new mining operation and preserves any
retained dig. Release and correction still perform ordinary cleanup.
Side: client.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `canceled`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.

A play packet from the server reached the window's game, decoded,
just before the game handles it (`Connection.genericsFtw` handing it
to `ClientPacketListener`): every packet of the play phase, custom
payloads included, in the order the server sent them. Packets the
network thread handles itself are not heard: keep-alives, bundle
delimiters, resource pack pushes and pops, cookies, server links,
transfers, disconnects, the configuration switch, `minecraft:brand`
and far terrain tiles; neither is the configuration phase.
Read-only: the game handles the packet as it would without the mod.
Client-side, on any server, single player's own included.
Every packet exposes its protocol type id. Custom payloads also expose
their channel and raw bytes; no other decoded fields cross the API.
Side: client.

A play packet the window's game is about to send to the server (`Connection.send`):
every packet of the play phase it sends, in the order it sends them, the selected slot
that goes out before an attack or a use included. Not heard: what the network thread
sends itself (keep-alives, configuration pongs, cookies, the configuration phase), the answers the
connection sends in whichever phase it is in (a resource pack's status, a dialog's custom
click action), and far terrain requests. Cancel drops the packet: the game goes on as if
it had been sent, so the server never hears of it. Client-side, on any server, single
player's own included. Every packet exposes its protocol type id; custom payloads also
expose their channel and raw bytes, as `client_packet` does for the packets that arrive.
Play-phase pongs pass through this hook; return `Flow::Cancel` to drop a packet.
Beyond NeoForge: there is no counterpart. Diverges from upstream: new hook.
Side: client.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `canceled`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.

NeoForge's `ClientPauseChangeEvent.Post`: the pause state changed.
Side: client.

NeoForge's `ClientPauseChangeEvent.Pre`: cancel a proposed pause change.
Side: client.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn client_pause_change_pre(&self, _: &mut dyn ClientHost, _: &mut ClientPauseChangePreEvent) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
NeoForge's `ClientPlayerChangeGameTypeEvent`: observe the local player info game type change.
Side: client.

After the client replaces its player on respawn or dimension change
(NeoForge's `ClientPlayerNetworkEvent.Clone`). Client-side.
Side: client.

The client accepted a play login and initialized its level and player
identity (NeoForge's `ClientPlayerNetworkEvent.LoggingIn`). `player_id`
is the server's entity ID. Client-side,
once per connection, including single player.
Side: client.

Before client disconnect teardown (NeoForge's
`ClientPlayerNetworkEvent.LoggingOut`). The player may be absent.
Client-side.
Side: client.

Render-thread notification after a resource-pack reload has applied successfully.
Atlas, models, renderer and client caches already refer to the new resources.
Selection/F3+T and server-pack reloads share this point; initial startup does not
(`client_setup` is the once-only moment after the initial load). Runs in
Reloading: published asset/data queries may refresh caches, but world
handles and transactions remain unavailable.
Side: client.

NeoForge's `FMLClientSetupEvent`: the client has started. It fires once per game
process, on the render thread, after the first client load has applied (the
atlas, models and every client reload listener's published state are final)
and before the title screen's first frame. Returning to the title screen and
opening another world, or adding a splitscreen player, is not a new start, so
it never fires again. This is
the opposite of `client_resources_reloaded`, which never runs at initial
startup and runs after every later reload. The listener runs on the main thread;
work a mod wants done in parallel is its own. The dedicated server has no client and never fires it
(see `server_about_to_start` for its `FMLDedicatedServerSetupEvent`). A
Setup permits client resource reads, not world handles or transactions.
The listener is a pure function of its `ClientHost` reads and its own state.
Side: client.

The client has finished shutting down, after `client_stopping`. Fires once
on the render thread for an orderly client exit, not for a dedicated server
or a splitscreen guest. NeoForge's `ClientStoppedEvent`.
Side: client.

The client is closing: it fires once per game process, on the render thread,
when the game shuts down, after the world the player was in is left and
saved, while the game still holds its settings and resources, so a listener
can read them through the `ClientHost` and save its own client state. It is the closing counterpart of `client_setup`.
Closing the window, a quit shortcut and the process's stop signals all reach
it; a crash does not. A dedicated server has no client and never fires it
(`server_stopping` is its stop), and neither does a splitscreen guest's game, as
`client_setup` skips it. Fabric's `ClientLifecycleEvents.CLIENT_STOPPING`
fires earlier, before the integrated server stops, so it is not a counterpart.
NeoForge has no event for this moment. A listener is a pure function of its
`ClientHost` reads and its own state.
Side: client.

Once every client tick, paused or not and on the title screen too, after the window's tick ran (NeoForge's
`ClientTickEvent.Post`): the window's `Game` only, so not on a server's
own tick (`server_tick` is that moment). Client-side.
Side: client.

Once every client tick, paused or not and on the title screen too, before the window's tick runs (NeoForge's
`ClientTickEvent.Pre`): the window's `Game` only, so not on a server's
own tick (`server_tick` is that moment). Client-side.
Side: client.

A command the local player typed or clicked in chat, without its
slash, before the server and Horizon's commands see it: set `ran`
when the mod ran it. Client-side: a server never asks, not for
command blocks, guests or the console.
Side: client.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `ran`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn command(&self, _: &mut dyn ClientHost, _: &mut CommandEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
`GuiGraphicsExtractor.componentHoverEffect`: the hover of the text component under the
cursor, about to be drawn, in the chat, a book or a dialog. `hover` is the component's
hover action: its text, an item or an entity. `x` and `y` are the cursor in GUI pixels.
Set `cancel` and the game draws nothing for it: no text tooltip, no item tooltip and no
entity lines. A mod can draw its own with `draw`. Left alone, a text hover is wrapped at
half the screen's width (at least 200) as vanilla wraps it, an item hover draws its stack's
tooltip (which asks `item_tooltip` and the `render_tooltip_*` hooks as any item tooltip
does), and an entity hover shows its name, type and UUID while advanced tooltips are on.
Asked each frame a hovered component shows, only while a mod listens. Client-side.
Side: client.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.

Register namespaced NBT component types before content loads.
Side: both.

Every mod gets `event.types` in order and may add, change or remove types.

A player added a compostable item to the composter at `pos`.
Side: server.

Computed world fog RGB, after ordinary effects and before upload. Title panoramas skip it.
Only finite RGB components in 0..=1 are accepted; alpha and distances stay unchanged.
Side: client.

World field of view, after normal calculation and zoom and before projection/Nausea.
Called for world rendering and near-plane overlays; hand/HUD FOV uses its own path.
Only finite values in 1..=179 degrees replace the computed FOV.
Side: client.

Player FOV scale, once per client tick with a player, after vanilla
effects and before zoom and easing.
Invalid values or values outside 0.01..=10 revert to base.
Side: client.

A registered config was read (`ModConfigEvent.Loading`): `config`
says whose, which file and its text, which the mod parses (TOML by
convention). Every mod hears every config, so check `mod_id`. Fired
where the config's kind loads (`register_configs`), a `Server`
one before `server_about_to_start`. Config allows settings reads
and the scoped ConfigFiles service, not world handles or transactions. Client and Common load once on their
owning side, Server once per world.
Side: both.

A loaded config's file changed on disk (`ModConfigEvent.Reloading`):
its new text. The game looks at the files' modification times once a
second, on the window and on the server's tick; a file saved with the
same text, removed or unreadable fires nothing and keeps its last
text. Polling does not change the current phase.
Side: both.

A `Server` config is dropped as its server stops
(`ModConfigEvent.Unloading`), after `server_stopping`; the next
world reads it again. `Client` and `Common` configs stay until the
game quits. This notification leaves the World phase unchanged.
Side: server.

A line the server logged (what its console prints and
`logs/latest.log` keeps): `level` is `INFO`, `WARN` or `ERROR`,
`thread` the thread it names (`Server thread`), `message` the line
without its time and thread. Heard at the start of the next server
tick, in the order logged; the lines logged before the first tick a mod
listens are not heard, and nor are the lines a `console_line`
listener logs itself. At most 4096 lines wait between two ticks; the
oldest are dropped with no notice. A `message` is cut to its first
8192 bytes and a `thread` to its first 128, at a character boundary.
Server-side.
Side: server.

A consumable's effect of a mod's own kind: the item's `on_consume_effects`
entry is of a type in a namespace of its own, and the loader kept it
for this call. The kind and the definition payload as a borrowed `Tag` are here; the acting
player is the one consuming, and the game's own effects,
sounds, teleports and drops are open. An unclaimed kind does
nothing. This is the runtime `ConsumeEffect.apply` moment, not effect
type registration through NeoForge's `RegisterEvent`.
Side: server.

Horizon addition: no NeoForge counterpart. Fired once per container fill,
each half of a double chest separately, on the rolled list in roll order
before shuffle, splitting and slot placement. Add, replace or remove drops;
empty stacks are dropped. Stacks over their item's maximum are trimmed at
placement, after the hook; overflow that cannot fit is discarded.
The opener is named only when a player's open starts the fill, otherwise
None (hopper, comparator, break, explosion or command). The origin is the
block's centre or the container entity's position. Already filled containers
and block or mob drops do not fire this hook. Listeners run in dispatch
order, each seeing the previous list, after loot_table_load's changes.
The level Host provides reads only; only the drop list is writable.
Invalid component writes retain the prior list and warn. Panics follow the
runtime listener isolation policy. Listeners use their own randomness.
With no listener, the roll and placement random draws remain unchanged.
Side: server.

Every mod gets `event.drops` in order and may add, change or remove drops.

A player opens one of the game's own menus (`ServerPlayer.openMenu`; the
job of NeoForge's `PlayerContainerEvent.Open`, which comes after the
menu is open and cannot stop it): `kind` is the menu type
(`minecraft:generic_9x3`, `minecraft:furnace`, `minecraft:crafting`,
`minecraft:merchant`, `minecraft:anvil`, `minecraft:lectern`...; a
horse's inventory is `minecraft:horse_inventory`) and `pos` the block
it belongs to, none for a villager, a mount or a vehicle's chest.
Heard after the checks that refuse the menu (a locked container, a
spectator) and before the menu that was open closes. Set `cancel` and
nothing opens: the open menu stays as it was and the click is spent.
The player's state is swapped in for the call, as for
`run_mod_command`, so `host.players().acting_player()`, `PlayerRef::tell` and
the item helpers reach them. Not heard: a menu a mod opens
(`native_open_menu`), the inventory screen, and the editors (sign,
book, command block). Server-side, for every player of the world.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn container_opened(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut ContainerOpenedEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
A crafter at `pos` completed recipe `recipe`.
Side: server.

A fluid source at `pos` (`state`) is about to count towards turning
the flowing fluid beside it into a source (NeoForge's
`CreateFluidSourceEvent`, `FlowingFluid.getNewLiquid`): two counted
sources beside a block over a solid block or a source make it one.
Asked for each horizontal neighbour source, whenever the game works
out a block's new fluid, spread checks included: answer fast.
`can_convert` starts as the fluid's rule (`water_source_conversion`
or `lava_source_conversion`). Server-side.
Side: server.

Skull models for a mod's own skull types (NeoForge's
`EntityRenderersEvent.CreateSkullModels`): push a `SkullModel` per type, its `kind`, the
model layer it is baked from and its default texture. A `minecraft:head` item model may
then name the kind, so the head draws in hand, in a GUI and in an item frame. Asked
once at start, on the client. A kind in vanilla's namespace, not `<namespace>:<path>`,
registered already, with a layer neither a mod nor vanilla has, or with an empty texture
is logged and left out. API @API:create_skull_models@.
Side: client.

Every mod gets `event.models` in order and may add, change or remove models.

Before a new server level selects its initial world spawn
(NeoForge's `LevelEvent.CreateSpawnPosition`).
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn create_spawn_position(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut CreateSpawnPositionEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
A creative-mode player sets a slot of their inventory from the
creative screen (`ServerGamePacketListenerImpl.handleSetCreativeModeSlot`):
`slot` is the inventory menu's slot (5 to 8 armour, 9 to 35 the
inventory, 36 to 44 the hotbar, 45 the off hand; below 0 is a stack
thrown out of the screen, which is dropped) and `item` (`minecraft:air`
for an emptied slot) and `count` what is put there. Heard once the
packet passed vanilla's checks (a creative player, a real slot, a valid
stack) and before the slot changes or the stack drops. Set `cancel`
and the packet is ignored. The player's state is swapped in for the
call, as for `run_mod_command`, so `host.players().acting_player()`,
`PlayerRef::tell` and the item helpers reach them. Not heard: stacks a
creative player gets other ways (middle-click pick block, `/give`).
Server-side, for every player of the world.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn creative_slot(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut CreativeSlotEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
A player ignited a creeper with an item.
Side: server.

Lightning charged a creeper.
Side: server.

NeoForge's `CriticalHitEvent`: a player's melee hit on a living
`target_kind` (`minecraft:zombie`, `minecraft:armor_stand`) that deals
damage, where `Player.attack` decides whether it is critical.
`vanilla_critical` is vanilla's answer; `critical` starts as it and may
be forced or denied (as in vanilla a critical hit prevents the sweep, so
a forced crit loses it; a denied crit loses the crit sound and
particles); `damage_multiplier` starts at 1.5 for vanilla's critical and
1.0 otherwise, and scales the damage only while `critical` ends true. Not fired for a
target that is no living entity (a dragon part) or when the hit does
no damage. Fires on the Game that runs the attack.
Side: server.

A crop-like block grew (NeoForge's `CropGrowEvent.Post`).
`original_state` is the block before it grew and `state` what is at
`pos` now. Sugar cane reports the new cane above it, and kelp and
