`states` that draws a model, or one `Refuse` if the file doesn't read, for a type your mod
owns. `config` is the file's JSON object converted to a `Tag`, `block` the block it
belongs to. It is asked once per file on each resource load, on the resource loader,
never per frame.
Side: client.

Every mod gets `event.models` in order and may add, change or remove models.

An interaction mapping is about to act on the tick's crosshair target. `attempt`
distinguishes a queued press from held use or mining. Use asks for each hand tried,
main first. Cancelling the main hand ends the click. Attack and use honour
`swing_hand` independently: it governs only the acting player's own screen.
False suppresses natural local swings; true preserves natural no-swing outcomes.
A cancelled use with true requests a local swing only: neither a use packet nor
a swing packet is sent, so observers see no swing. An uncancelled use sends no
extra client swing packet: observers see the server's success swing, regardless
of this flag. Attack and mining swing packets also honour the item swing veto. Pick
only vetoes its packet and never swings. Fires on the window client.
Side: client.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `canceled`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn interaction_key_mapping_triggered(&self, _: &mut dyn ClientHost, _: &mut InteractionKeyMappingTriggeredEvent) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
A server player is about to open an inventory supplied by a block at
`pos`. Set `cancel` to leave the inventory closed. The player's state
is not swapped in.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn inventory_block_start(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut InventoryBlockStartEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
A hopper is about to move one item between containers, a composter's
bone meal included. Set `cancel` to leave it in its source slot. A chest
boat or minecart is reported at the block it is in.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.

`ItemAttributeModifierEvent`: the attribute modifiers `stack` grants
(`ItemStack.getAttributeModifiers`), starting from its own
`minecraft:attribute_modifiers` or its item's. Add, replace or remove
entries in `modifiers`; what is left is what every reader of the stack's
modifiers uses: the equipment of players, mobs, armor stands and the
dragon when it changes, mobs' gear knockback and pickup choices, the
attribute sync and the tooltip. A worn stack is asked again only when it
changes (`ItemStack.matches`), so the answer must be the same for the
same stack. Asked on the server and on a client (its tooltips).
Side: both.

A server player or fox that ate chorus fruit (or another item with the
`teleport_randomly` consume effect) is about to try a random spot
(NeoForge's `EntityTeleportEvent.ItemConsumption`, vanilla's
`TeleportRandomlyConsumeEffect.apply`): once per attempt (up to 16),
after they stopped riding. `from` is their feet, `target` the spot
drawn; a mod may move it (its y kept inside the level's height, a
value that is not a number ignored), and the game still looks down
from it for ground it may land on. Canceling ends the effect: no teleport and no
more attempts. `consumer` names the living actor through its handle.
`consumed` is the stack captured before consumption, including
its count and components; it is not reread from the hand after listener writes.
A player's state is swapped in (`host.players().acting_player()`). A fox's
callback has the full server host before its living AI/movement step and
before the next mob ticks. Listener writes survive; changing the consumer's
item, position or eligibility refuses the captured effect instead of
overwriting that write. Cancellation still finishes consumption.
Diverges from upstream: renamed from
`chorus_fruit_teleport`.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn item_consumption_teleport(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut ItemConsumptionTeleportEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
A player took a crafting grid's result (`ResultSlot.onTake`, NeoForge's
`PlayerEvent.ItemCraftedEvent`): `player` is the player's uuid, `recipe`
the recipe the grid matched (`minecraft:oak_planks`) and `stack` the
result it took, with its components. `inputs` is the grid row by row
as it was before this take used it (4 cells for an inventory's grid,
9 for a crafting table's; `None` for an empty cell): a shift-click
that crafts several times is heard once per craft, each with the grid
before that craft. It only hears: the take has
already happened. It fires for the crafting grid of an inventory or a
crafting table, on the integrated server and a dedicated server, guests
included, and not for a stonecutter's, a smithing table's or a
furnace's result. Server-side.
Side: server.

A dropped item entity reached its 6000-tick lifetime and is about to be
removed (Bukkit's `ItemDespawnEvent`).
Side: server.

A dropped item reaches its lifetime on the server (`ItemEntity.tick`,
NeoForge's `ItemExpireEvent`). Every mod may set or add to `extra_life`,
in ticks, which starts at zero; a positive total keeps the item that much
longer, zero or less lets it expire. Extensions are capped at 32766
ticks.
Side: server.

A server player `player` (UUID) and `player_entity_id` reels in a catch:
`ItemFishedEvent` in `FishingHook.retrieve`, after fishing loot and its modifiers roll.
`fished` holds the bobber's id and position; listeners may change `drops` and set
absolute non-negative `rod_damage` (`damageRodBy`): vanilla uses 1, or 2 with the
bobber on the ground. After `player_fish`'s reel-in, before rewards. Server-side.
The final list reaches `fishing_rod_hooked`, then each stack spawns its item,
one experience orb, and its fish statistic if it belongs to `#minecraft:fishes`.
Empty stacks are removed. A cancel removes the bobber and skips the trigger,
items, experience and statistic; the rod still takes `rod_damage` last.
An emptied list without cancel gives no items, experience or statistic; the trigger
still fires with an empty list and the rod is still damaged.
An invalid `drops` write (a stack the game refuses, such as a count over the item's
maximum) discards the whole event's write-back, every listener's `cancel` and
`rod_damage` included, and logs a warning naming the hook and the conversion error.
Diverges: Horizon lets a listener change the drop list itself; the reference lets a
listener change the stacks but not the list.
Side: server.

Every mod gets `event.drops` in order and may add, change or remove drops.
methods.signature: fn item_fished(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut ItemFishedEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
Client-side evaluation of a mod's namespaced conditional item model property.
Set value only for a property your mod owns; unhandled properties stay false.
The owned stack snapshot is the one being resolved, including nested bundle items.
`bundle_selected` is the runtime bundle selection index; -1 means none.
Side: client.

Client-side value of a numeric item model property a mod registered
(`register_range_select_item_model_property`), asked each time a `minecraft:range_dispatch`
on it picks a branch. Set value only for a property your mod owns; unanswered it stays 0.
The model's `scale` is applied afterwards. The owned stack snapshot is the one being resolved,
including nested bundle items.
`bundle_selected` is the runtime bundle selection index; -1 means none.
Side: client.

Client-side value of a categorical item model property a mod registered
(`register_select_item_model_property`), asked each time a `minecraft:select` on it picks a
case. Set value only for a property your mod owns; left `None`, the model's fallback is drawn.
The owned stack snapshot is the one being resolved, including nested bundle items.
`bundle_selected` is the runtime bundle selection index; -1 means none.
Side: client.

A node of a type a mod registered (`register_item_models`, vanilla's `ItemModel.update`)
is resolved for a stack, in hand, in a screen or on the ground: push the names of the
node's `models` to draw, in order, only for a type your mod owns. `config` borrows the
node's JSON object, converted once at load. The owned stack snapshot is the one being
resolved, including nested bundle items. `bundle_selected` is the runtime bundle selection
index; -1 means none. As `ItemModel.update` reads them: `display` is where the item is
drawn (a screen, a hand, the ground), `owner` the living entity holding it (`None` in a
screen with no holder), `level` the level it is drawn in (`None` outside a world), and
`seed` the draw's random seed.
Side: client.

`player` touches the ground item entity `item`
(`ItemEntity.playerTouch`), before its pickup delay and target are
checked: it is asked on every tick the two touch, even while the item
can't be taken. Leave `can_pickup` at `Default` for vanilla's rule,
set `True` to take it despite its delay or another player's target
(a full inventory still leaves it), or `False` to leave it there: the
fork sets a vanilla eligibility delay of at least 10 ticks. The hook
still runs on each touch, and a later `True` overrides that delay. The last mod to set it
decides. The handle reads the whole stack on the ground; for the
window's own player of a world it ticks itself, whose pickup pass
lifts the items out of the level, it reads as unavailable. Server-side.
Side: server.

`player` picked up part of a ground stack (`ItemEntity.playerTouch`,
right after `Inventory.add` took some of it and left the rest).
`original` is a copy of the stack as it lay before the pickup:
changing it does nothing. `remaining` is what the item entity still
holds, so it starts as the part that did not fit. Set another stack
there to leave the entity holding it, or `None` to empty it: the
pickup then counts `original`'s count less what is left. The amount
taken is `original`'s count less `remaining`'s. A mod that removes the
item entity meanwhile keeps it removed: no take animation, the stat
and criteria still run. Of the two notices, this one hears a partial
pickup and `item_picked_up_post` a whole one; a pickup is never told
to both. Not called when `item_picked_up` refused the pickup or the
inventory took nothing. A creative player always takes the whole
stack. Server-side; no NeoForge counterpart.
Side: server.

`player` picked up the whole stack of the ground item entity `item`
(`ItemEntity.playerTouch`, right after `Inventory.add` took all of
it), the entity `item_picked_up` named. `original` is a copy of
the stack as it lay before the pickup: changing it does nothing.
`remaining` is what the item entity still holds, so it starts as
`None` (empty). Set a stack there to leave the entity on the ground
holding it: the pickup then counts only `original`'s count less its
count. Neither says how many were picked up; that is `original`'s
count less `remaining`'s. A mod that removes the item entity meanwhile
keeps it removed: no take animation, the stat and criteria still run.
Not called on a partial pickup, where some of the stack went in and
the rest stayed on the ground: `item_picked_up_partial` hears that one,
and a pickup is never told to both. Nor when `item_picked_up` refused
the pickup or the inventory took nothing; a forced `True` from
`item_picked_up` changes none of this. A creative player always takes
the whole stack. Server-side.
Side: server.

`FurnaceResultSlot.checkTakeAchievements` ran for a server player at a
furnace, blast furnace or smoker's result slot: `player` is their UUID
and `player_entity_id` their network id; `stack` and `amount_removed`
are what vanilla passes there (`getSmelting`, `getAmountRemoved`). A
click or a throw passes the taken stack and its count; a shift-click
passes the slot's stack as it was with the count moved, then what
stayed in the slot (`None` once it is empty) with 0; a hotbar swap
passes the taken stack with 0. Fires before `furnace_extract`.
Server-side.
Side: server.

A dropped item entity was successfully added to the server level.
Side: server.

NeoForge's `ItemStackedOnOtherEvent`, before either item override. It runs inside a pickup click. Answer from the arguments and `context` alone, and fast: `context` holds the side, the registries and the settings of the resource generation, and a `/reload` builds the next one.
Side: both.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `canceled`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event_.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.

Client-side colour of an item tint source a mod registered (`register_item_tint_sources`,
vanilla's `ItemTintSource.calculate`), asked for each entry on it each time the item is
resolved, in hand, in a screen or on the ground. `config` borrows the entry converted once to a `Tag` at load from the JSON object in the
model's `tints`, so a source reads its own fields there. Set color, ARGB with an alpha of
`0xFF` as vanilla's sources give, only for a source your mod owns; left alone, the entry draws
white. The owned stack snapshot is the one being resolved, including nested bundle items.
`bundle_selected` is the runtime bundle selection index; -1 means none.
Side: client.

`ItemTooltipEvent`: the whole tooltip of `stack` (`ItemStack.getTooltipLines`),
once its name, the item's own lines, the components' lines, the
advanced lines and the operator warning are in `lines`, each with a
colour as `rgba` packs it (`u32::MAX` keeps the text's own). Add,
change, reorder or remove lines. `player` and `player_entity_id` are
the local player's, `display` the stack's `minecraft:tooltip_display`,
`advanced` (F3+H) and `creative` (a creative tab's own slot) its
`TooltipFlag`. Asked each frame the tooltip shows, never for one the
stack hides or a crossbow's loaded projectile. Client-side.
This global event is distinct from [`ItemPart::tooltip`], which runs at
the earlier `Item.appendHoverText` position, before component lines.
Parts' lines therefore come first; this event sees the finished list
including them, for any item, even one with no attached parts.
A component deeper than 512 nodes refuses capture or the whole writeback;
no event field is applied if any Text field fails conversion.
Side: client.

`ItemTossEvent`: `player` tosses the item entity `item` (`Player.drop`: the drop key, a menu's throw, what no longer fits in the inventory), not what scatters when they die. The entity is made, with its thrower, but has not joined the level yet: its handle reads and changes the whole stack, the pickup delay and the target, and those changes stay. Set `canceled` and it never joins the level; the items are already out of the inventory and are lost. A canceled toss awards no drop statistic, as vanilla awards one only when an item entity came of it. Server-side. Diverges from upstream: replaces the listen-only `item_dropped`, which fired for the drop key and menu throws only.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `canceled`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn item_toss(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut ItemTossEvent) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
Items this mod adds, declared in code (NeoForge's
`DeferredRegister.Items`), as `blocks` declares blocks: a
`mod_api::Item` per item, a content mod's
`data/<id>/horizon/item/<path>.json` (a vanilla `template`,
`max_stack_size`, `rarity`, `components`, `crafting_remainder`). A
block's item comes with its block (`item: true`), not from here.
Each mod receives its own batch; IDs must use a namespace owned by its
manifest (bare paths use its mod ID). Unowned namespaces refuse registration.
Asked once at start, on every side.
Side: both.

Each mod receives its own empty `event.items` batch. A bare name, in an identifier or
in `block_item`, `pick_item`, `wall_block`, `base_block`, `crafting_remainder` or `Item::block`,
is that mod's own; declared identifiers must belong to
that mod's manifest-owned namespaces, and unowned identifiers refuse registration.

A physical key or mouse button bound to the gameplay mapping `mapping` (`key.jump`,
`key.attack`...) changes state while playing, before the game acts on it. `pressed` is true
for a press (a key's repeat counts as one, as the game takes it) and false for a release.
Cancel a press to drop it for every mapping bound to its input: the game holds nothing and
acts on nothing. A release cannot be canceled, so what the game holds is always let go.
Told for the keys and mouse buttons the window takes (agent control's included), after the
window's own shortcuts (fullscreen, screenshot, debug keys), and only with no screen open;
not for a controller, whose presses go straight to the mappings, nor for a mod's
`set_mapping_down` and `click_mapping`, which are no physical input. No NeoForge counterpart.
Client-side.
Side: client.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `canceled`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn key_mapping_pre(&self, _: &mut dyn ClientHost, _: &mut KeyMappingPreEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
A non-persistent leaf block at distance 7 is about to decay at `pos`.
Set `cancel` to keep it. Server-side.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.

A player left-clicks the block `state` at `pos`, `face` the face hit
(`[0, 1, 0]` is the top): where `ServerPlayerGameMode.handleBlockBreakAction`
takes a dig's start, after its reach, spawn protection and world border
checks, before `Block.attack` (a note block plays) or a creative break.
Set `canceled` to ignore the click: the block isn't attacked, dug or
broken on the server, and the player's client gets it back (its own
predicted crack still shows to the clicking player). Server-side, for
every player of the world (the helpers read the acting one).
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `canceled`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn left_click_block(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut LeftClickBlockEvent) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
The local player left-clicks empty space, with any main-hand stack.
Client-side only; the server does not receive this event.
Side: client.

`dimension`'s level opened on the server (NeoForge's `LevelEvent.Load`,
posted in `MinecraftServer.createLevels`): before any of its chunks
(`chunk_load`), so a mod sets up what it keeps for the level
here. The level the world opens in comes before `server_started`; the
others open when someone first goes there (a player, a portal, an
`execute in` command), with the level in place. Once for each open:
`level_unload` follows. Explicitly opened runtime levels also fire this while
parked: `event.dimension` names the opened level, not the Host's current level.
Server-side.
Side: server.

`dimension`'s level was saved (NeoForge's `LevelEvent.Save`, in
`ServerLevel.save`): its level data, chunks and entities, by the
autosave, `/save-all`, a pause, a closing level or the server
stopping; each level of a world save in turn. Server-side.
Side: server.

After a successful level tick pass on either logical side; never after a failed tick.
`host.server_has_time()` says whether optional work still fits in the tick
(`LevelTickEvent.hasTime`); always true on a client.
Side: both.

Before a level's tick pass on either logical side. `level` identifies the level.
`host.server_has_time()` says whether optional work still fits in the tick
(`LevelTickEvent.hasTime`); always true on a client.
Side: both.

`dimension`'s level closed (NeoForge's `LevelEvent.Unload`, posted after
`level.close()` in `MinecraftServer.stopServer`), after its last save:
drop what the mod kept for it. A level other than the Overworld closes
once nobody has been in it for 300 ticks, after its chunks' unloads;
every level still open closes when the server stops, before
`WorldCloseFinal`, and when its open or its loop fails, before
`WorldOpenFailed` or `WorldCloseFailed`. Once for each
`level_load`. Don't read its blocks. Server-side.
Side: server.

The Overworld, the Nether and the End were regenerated by a mod's `RuntimeLevels::reset_vanilla`, after their terrain was removed, with the new seed already in effect; they open from it the next time somebody enters them. `level_unload` fired for each of them that was open before, and `level_load` fires for each that opens again. Server-side.
Side: server.

A server lightning bolt is about to be created. `cause` is `weather`,
`trident`, `command` or `mod` (a native mod's `strike_lightning`); `player` is the responsible player when known.
Set `cancel` to prevent the bolt and its effects.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn lightning_strike(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut LightningStrikeEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
An entity's breathing this tick (`LivingBreatheEvent`, posted from
`LivingEntity.baseTick` every tick for a living entity with the generic
air logic): `entity` is its ID and `kind` its type (`minecraft:player`,
`minecraft:zombie`). `can_breathe`, `consume` and `refill` come in as
Horizon does it (a mod-free game changes nothing); set them to
change this tick. With `can_breathe` the air rises by `refill`, up to its
maximum (300 for every entity except dolphins, which have 4800); a dolphin's
vanilla `refill` is its maximum minus its current air. Without breath,
air falls by `consume`, and at -20 it is set to 0
and the entity takes 2 drowning damage. Negative amounts count as 0.
Asked on servers for players and mobs. A water animal, axolotl or
nautilus comes in with its own air logic's answer: where it breathes
(water, or rain for an axolotl) `can_breathe` and a `refill` to its full
air; elsewhere no breath and `consume` 1. Running out deals its own
damage (drowning, or drying out). It is given the loop `context` of the server that ticks the entity (its registries, settings and mod list), because it fires inside the tick's own air update.
Side: server.

A mob is about to change its target. `original_target` is the target
requested by the game, or none when it is clearing the target.
`new_target` starts as that value; a listener can redirect or clear it.
Set `cancel` to retain the mob's existing target. `is_brain` identifies
a brain-driven target change; false identifies a goal or other mob target
setter. Handles may be read through the host. During the lifted mob tick
pass, the scoped view reads the ticking mob directly and peers from the
tick snapshot: an already-ticked peer exposes post-turn state, and a
not-yet-ticked peer pre-turn state. A mob spawned during that pass does
not resolve in the scoped view until the next pass. Removed mobs do not
resolve; dead-but-present mobs are distinct from removed mobs. Outside
this scoped tick path, dispatch reads the entities available in the game
host rather than this snapshot.
A stale or invalid replacement, including a fake player, is refused.
Authoritative server only.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.

A mob converted into another type (NeoForge's
`LivingConversionEvent.Post`): `converted` replaces `entity`. Fires
after the finalized new mob joined the level and before the old mob
is removed, for the conversions `living_conversion_pre` tells.
Side: server.

A mob is about to convert into another type (NeoForge's
`LivingConversionEvent.Pre`, vanilla's `Mob.convertTo`): a zombie
drowning, a piglin or hoglin in the Overworld, a tadpole growing, a
mooshroom sheared by a dispenser, a pig or villager struck by
lightning. `outcome` is the new type. Set `cancel` to keep the mob as
it is; a drowning zombie starts its timers again. Not told: a
mooshroom a player shears, a zombie villager's cure, a villager turned
by a zombie.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn living_conversion_pre(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut LivingConversionPreEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
NeoForge's `LivingDamageEvent.Post`: entity `entity` of type `kind` has been hurt by the
hit `container` describes, with its final values (health damage, the reductions, the
post-attack invulnerability ticks). It fires once for every hit that passed
`living_incoming_damage` and the invulnerability cooldown, at the very end of
`hurtServer`: after a totem and the hurt sounds. The death hooks come after it, which is
Horizon's order, not NeoForge's (there Post follows the death processing): a player's `die`
is only a death request at that point, and a mob's death (`living_death`) is settled by the
game once its hurt has returned. A hit that took no
health (a shield, absorption, armor or a `living_damage_pre` listener took it all) fires
it too, with `container.health_damage()` 0. `container.should_cause_side_effects()`
carries `hurtServer`'s fresh-hit decision (`shouldCauseSideEffects`): false for a stronger
hit inside the cooldown unless its source bypasses it, independent of the final damage
or modded invulnerability ticks. It only listens. It can't write the
entity or the world's blocks: the level host gives the hit's random and level attachments.
The container is an API-owned scalar snapshot; the engine retains sequencing and normalization.
Side: server.

NeoForge's `LivingDamageEvent.Pre`: `LivingEntity.actuallyHurt` of entity `entity` of
type `kind` (`minecraft:player`, `minecraft:zombie`) by `source` (named as
`native_living_incoming_damage` names it) has taken armor and magic, and the absorption
hearts are next: `container` holds the damage it started with, what it is now
(`new_damage`, which may be 0) and each reduction so far (armor, enchantments, mob
effects). Change its
`new_damage` and the health takes that; set its post-attack invulnerability ticks and the
entity keeps them instead of vanilla's. A value that is not a number is put back as it
was. It fires for players, mobs and the ender dragon; a wolf whose armor takes the hit and
armor stands do not fire it. The level is the hit's: its blocks, random and own
attachments; the hurt entity is in the middle of its hit.
The container is an API-owned scalar snapshot; the engine retains sequencing and normalization.
Side: server.

A mob or server player is about to die (NeoForge's `LivingDeathEvent`,
vanilla's `LivingEntity.die`): its health has run out, and the loot,
experience and death message have not run. `entity` is its id and
`kind` its type (`minecraft:zombie`, `minecraft:player`). `source` and
`weapon` are the complete killing blow, as `living_incoming_damage` saw
it. `source.causing` is the mob or player's entity id when known, or 0
when there is no attacker or the attacking player is unknown; the source
also retains the direct projectile and weapon components.
Cancellation skips death and loot without changing the listener's health:
heal it to keep it alive; at health <= 0 its body is removed after 20 ticks.
Armor stands, boats and other non-mob entities are not told.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn living_death(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut LivingDeathEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
`living_death_message` is asked for the death message a tamed mob sends its owner (`TamableAnimal.die`), once the message is built and only when it would be sent (owner online, `show_death_messages` on). `message` holds the text: replace it, or set it to `None` to tell the owner nothing. Every mod is asked in order. Server and host.
Side: server.

Every mod gets `event.message` in order and may add, change or remove message.

A mob or server player's death has finished (Fabric's
`ServerLivingEntityEvents.AFTER_DEATH`, vanilla's `LivingEntity.die`
at its `broadcastEntityEvent`): the loot, equipment and experience
dropped and the death message went out. `entity` is its id;
`damage_type` names the killing blow (`minecraft:player_attack`) and
`attacker` is the mob that dealt it, 0 for none or a player. It only
hears. The tail of `living_death`, a separate moment, and not fired
when that hook cancelled the death. Server-side, once per death, for
every ordinary living entity. The ender dragon uses a separate death
sequence and fires neither living death hook. Armor stands, boats and other non-mob entities
are not told.
Side: server.

A mob is about to destroy a block (NeoForge's `LivingDestroyBlockEvent`):
a wither breaking blocks around it, a ravager breaking leaves, the ender
dragon's wall check, an enderman picking a block up, a silverfish waking
its friends (the infested blocks break), a zombie breaking a door or a
turtle egg. `entity` is its entity id, `kind` its type (`minecraft:wither`),
`pos` the block and `state` its state. Canceling keeps the block (an
enderman then holds nothing). Asked once per block, only while a mod is
loaded. Server-side.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn living_destroy_block(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut LivingDestroyBlockEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
Not `loot_drops`: that is the loot-modifier step, which edits
the stacks a table rolled (blocks, shearing, a mob's table). This hook
fires once after it, on the entity's whole collected drop list, and
nothing is spawned until it returns.
A dying mob, server player or armor stand `entity` of `kind` (`player`
is a player's UUID) is about to drop `drops`, the items
`LivingEntity.dropAllDeathLoot` collected (NeoForge's
`LivingDropsEvent`): the loot tables' stacks (after `loot_drops`),
the equipment that rolled to drop, a mob's own extras (an enderman's
carried block, a fox's mouth item, a piglin's inventory, a copper golem's
preserved equipment) and a player's inventory, each with the position,
motion and pickup delay its item entity will have. Edit the list (take
out, change or add drops) or set `cancel` for no drops at all; empty
stacks don't drop. `source` is the killing blow (`causing` and `direct`
entity ids, 0 when none or not known) and `recently_hit` is whether a
player hurt it within 100 ticks, which is what lets a mob drop its
equipment. An armor stand fires it from `brokenByAnything` with an
empty list (its stand item and its equipment pop outside the list, as
in vanilla). Experience orbs are not in the list
(`living_experience_drop`); a spectator, who drops nothing,
doesn't call this. Each `ItemDrop` also sets the item entity's
`thrower`, `target` (the only player who may pick it up), `no_gravity`
and starting `age` (`ItemDrop::UNLIMITED_LIFETIME` never despawns); a
drop left as it was spawns as before. Server-side.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn living_drops(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut LivingDropsEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
An entity that can't breathe and has no air (`LivingDrownEvent`, posted
from `LivingEntity.baseTick`), with vanilla's answers as the defaults: it
drowns at -20 air, for 2 damage and 8 bubbles. Change `is_drowning`,
`damage_amount` or `bubble_count`, or cancel to skip drowning this tick.
Eight bubbles are the vanilla entity event; another positive count is
sent as that many bubble particles, and none sends nothing. Asked on
servers, for the entities `living_breathe` is; a water animal,
axolotl or nautilus shows no bubbles, as in vanilla.
It is given the loop `context` of the server that ticks the entity (its
registries, settings and mod list), because it fires inside the tick's
own air and damage update.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.

NeoForge's `LivingEntityUseItemEvent.Finish`: `entity`'s use of
`stack` in `hand` ran its time (`LivingEntity.completeUsingItem`),
`duration` the ticks left, always 0. `entity` is as in
`living_entity_use_item_start`. `result` arrives with what
`finishUsingItem` left in the hand (the bowl of a stew, none for the
last apple; a mod's own item is kept) and may be replaced. Fired for
consumables, potions, spyglasses and mods' items. Both sides, as
vanilla's `completeUsingItem`: answer the same on both, and change the
world only on the server (`native_window` is false there), not on a
server's client. On the server it fires for every player of the world
(the helpers read the acting one). On a server's client the result
arrives as vanilla's client `finishUsingItem` leaves it: an item that
is not a consumable unchanged (a spyglass), a consumable less one, and
its use remainder (the bowl of the last stew) once that empties the
hand; nothing is used up in creative mode. The hand holds the result,
a mod's replacement included, until the server's inventory update.
Side: both.

NeoForge's `LivingEntityUseItemEvent.Start`: `entity` starts using
`stack` in `hand` (`LivingEntity.startUsingItem`), for `duration`
ticks (`use_duration`'s answer). `entity` is a mob's
`Entity.getId`, None for a player (`host.players().acting_player()` says who);
a mob fires it only for `LivingRef::start_using_item`. Change `duration` (consumables, potions,
spyglasses and mods' items count to it; below 0 refuses the use, and
0 runs it out on its first tick, as `living_entity_use_item_tick`
running it out, unless the item's own is 0 already), or set
`canceled` and the use doesn't start. Both sides, as
vanilla's: on the server for every player of the world, and on a
server's client for the uses it predicts. Answer the same on both,
and change the world only on the server (`native_window` is false
there), not on a server's client.
Side: both.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `canceled`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.

NeoForge's `LivingEntityUseItemEvent.Stop`: `entity` lets go of
`stack` in `hand` before its use ran its time
(`LivingEntity.releaseUsingItem`: the use button let go, a screen
opened), `duration` the ticks left. Set `canceled` to skip the item's
release (a bow doesn't shoot, a spyglass makes no sound,
`release_using` isn't called); the use stops anyway. Not when
the hand changed item, which stops the use without a release. Both
sides, as `living_entity_use_item_tick`.
Side: both.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `canceled`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.

NeoForge's `LivingEntityUseItemEvent.Tick`: each tick `entity` uses
`stack` in `hand`, where `LivingEntity.updatingUsingItem` starts,
`duration` the ticks left. `entity` is as in
`living_entity_use_item_start`. Change `duration` to move the
end (consumables, potions, spyglasses and mods' items count to it,
and so do a client's eating crumbs and first person pose, as the
started duration of `living_entity_use_item_start` does). A
cancel sets it to -1. Once a mod set it, the use goes on
only while it is above 0: at 0 or less, by a cancel or set, the
item's tick is skipped and the server finishes the use
(`completeUsingItem`: `finishUsingItem`, the food eaten,
`living_entity_use_item_finish`), while an item used on
release (a crossbow) stays frozen until let go. NeoForge's javadoc
says a cancel stops the use, but its code finishes it; this follows
the code. On a server's client a run-out use stays in use, frozen,
so letting go still tells the server. Both sides, as vanilla's
`updatingUsingItem`: answer the same on both, and change the world
only on the server (`native_window` is false there), not on a
server's client. Runs every tick of every use:
check the item first.
Side: both.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `canceled`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.

A mob's, an armor stand's or a player's equipment slot took a different
stack (NeoForge's `LivingEquipmentChangeEvent`, posted in
`LivingEntity.collectEquipmentChanges`): `entity` is its ID and `kind`
its type (`minecraft:zombie`, `minecraft:player`), `slot` the
`EquipmentSlot` (`mainhand`, `offhand`, `feet`, `legs`, `chest`, `head`,
`body`, `saddle`), `from` what the slot held when this was last heard
(none for empty) and `to` what it holds now. Once for each slot that
changed, in that order, after the mobs' tick, so a mob that joins the
level wearing something counts from empty on its first tick. It only
hears: change the entity with its own helpers.

Players are told the same way, once a tick, for the players connected
to the server (a dedicated server's, a published world's guests): a
player new to the level counts from empty, and the main hand is the
selected hotbar slot, so a hotbar selection or a pickup into the
selected slot is a `mainhand` change. Only their six slots `mainhand`,
`offhand`, `feet`, `legs`, `chest` and `head` are told: a player's
`body` and `saddle` slots are never told. Mobs and players are told
only while an enabled mod subscribes to this hook: no other hook has
to be heard with it. The world
host's own player, in single player or hosting a LAN world, isn't told
here: `on_equip` hears it. Server-side.
Side: server.

No longer needed: the game reads every mob's and connected player's
equipment each tick, and tells `living_equipment_change`, whenever an
enabled mod subscribes to that hook. A mod that still sets `listened`
(HEAD, `*listened = true`) is honoured as before. Without either the
game does not read the equipment, and neither is told (armor stands
still are). A mob that ticks, or a player who is in the level, once it
is read counts from empty. Asked once a tick for the mobs, after their
tick, and once for the players. Server-side.
Side: server.

Every mod gets `event.listened` in order and may add, change or remove listened.

A dying mob or player `entity` of `kind` is about to drop `original`
points of experience; the vanilla conditions have been checked.
`attacking_player` is the player who last hurt it, if any. Change
`amount` (0 or less drops nothing), or set `cancel` to drop none. A
sculk catalyst that takes the experience does not call this.
Server-side.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn living_experience_drop(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut LivingExperienceDropEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
A living entity is about to handle a fall (`LivingFallEvent`). Mods may
change the distance and damage multiplier, or cancel fall handling. It is given the loop `context` of the side that ticks the entity (its registries, settings and mod list); it fires inside the tick's own landing, before its damage and block effects, so it takes no `Host`.
Side: both.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.

A living entity's airborne acceleration (`LivingEntity.getFlyingSpeed`) is about to be used by its travel. `entity` is its id and `kind` its type; a mod may change `speed`. Fires on both sides, on the client's replayed ticks too, with the loop `context` of the side that ticks the entity (its registries, settings and mod list): register the mod on both, and keep the listener a pure function of its inputs so prediction and the server agree. Beyond NeoForge: there is no counterpart. Diverges from upstream: new hook.
Side: both.

`LivingEntity.getProjectile(weapon)` (NeoForge's
`LivingGetProjectileEvent`) for a player (`player` and `name`) or a
mob (`entity`, `kind`): a skeleton or illusioner's shot, or the crossbow
load of a pillager or piglin. `projectile` is the vanilla
ammunition; replace it to choose another. A replaced stack is not taken
from the inventory.
Side: both.

Every mod gets `event.projectile` in order and may add, change or remove projectile.

A living entity is about to heal. Mods may change the amount or cancel.
`entity` identifies the affected entity. It is given the loop `context` of the side that ticks the entity (its registries, settings and mod list), because it fires inside the tick's own health update, where a deferred call would reorder vanilla's effects.
Side: both.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.

NeoForge's `LivingIncomingDamageEvent`: `LivingEntity.hurtServer`, past its guards (an
invulnerable or dead entity, fire on a fire-resistant one), is about to hurt entity
`entity` of type `kind` (`minecraft:zombie`, `minecraft:player`) by `source`: its damage
type (`minecraft:fall`), causing entity (`DamageSource.getEntity`: the shooter of an
arrow), direct entity (`getDirectEntity`: the projectile's entity id when the
damage type names one, on a player, mob or ender dragon; 0 for `magic()` and any
other source with no direct entity, even during that projectile's impact), and
where it comes from (`getSourcePosition`). `victim` is where the entity stands and
looks, and `weapon` the direct entity's weapon (`getWeaponItem`) when it is known.
`container` is an API-owned snapshot before any reduction; engine sequencing
remains game-owned. Change its `new_damage`, the invulnerability ticks a fresh hit
leaves (vanilla's 20), or add an ordered reduction modifier with
`add_reduction_modifier`. Set `canceled` and nothing
of `hurtServer` happens (no damage, hurt sound, knockback, cooldown, statistics or
criteria); a canceled hit on the ender dragon still counts as landed (`EnderDragon.hurt`
returns true whatever `reallyHurt` did). It fires on every damage route, for players,
mobs and the ender dragon. The level is the hit's: its blocks, random and own
attachments; the hurt entity is in the middle of its hit.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `canceled`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn living_incoming_damage(&self, _: &mut dyn LevelRandomHost, _: &mut LivingIncomingDamageEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
A living entity jumped (`LivingEvent.LivingJumpEvent`). It is given the loop `context` of the side that ticks the entity (its registries, settings and mod list); it fires inside the tick's own jump, after the velocity write, so it takes no `Host`.
Side: both.

A living entity's jump power (`LivingEntity.getJumpPower`: jump strength attribute, block jump factor and Jump Boost) is about to be used by `jumpFromGround`. `entity` is its id and `kind` its type; a mod may change `power`. The rabbit's own hop and the player, cube, panda and ordinary mob jumps all pass through it. Fires on both sides, on the client's replayed ticks too, with the loop `context` of the side that ticks the entity (its registries, settings and mod list): register the mod on both, and keep the listener a pure function of its inputs so prediction and the server agree. Beyond NeoForge: there is no counterpart. Diverges from upstream: new hook.
Side: both.

NeoForge's `LivingKnockBackEvent`: `LivingEntity.knockback` is about to push entity
`entity` of type `kind` (`minecraft:zombie`, `minecraft:player`) `strength` away from the
direction (`x`, `z`), on the raw strength, before the entity's knockback resistance takes
its share and its motion changes. Vanilla's direction points at the source of a hit (the
attacker's side), and the entity is pushed the other way. `source` is the push's
`DamageSource`, named as `native_living_incoming_damage` names a hit's. `attacker` is the
attacking entity's network id, falling back to the victim's last hurt-by mob, or 0 when
unknown; `attacker_main` and `attacker_off` are what it holds (a player's selected and
off-hand stacks, a mob's main hand), none when unknown. `entry` is `Short` when the push
came in through `knockback(power, x, z)`, which only delegates to the full entry, and `Full`
when the full entry was called directly. The hook fires once per call of the full entry
either way, so a listener that wants its change applied twice for a short-entry push, as
a mixin on both entries would, applies it twice when `entry` is `Short`. Change
`strength`, `x` or `z`, or
set `canceled`, and the push follows them: canceled, the entity's motion is left alone. A
`strength` of 0 or less after the hook is no push, and a direction too short to tell
draws a random one after it, as in vanilla. A value a mod leaves that is not a finite
number is put back as it was. It fires for the players, mobs and armor stands the game
knocks back: a hit's own push, a sprinting or Knockback hit, a sweep, a spear, a
shield's push on its holder, a goat's ram and a mob's melee push. It does not fire for a
sulfur cube with a block that a hit with a causing entity knocks back
(`SulfurCube.knockback` does not call `super` there), for the pushes vanilla doesn't make
with `LivingEntity.knockback` (the ender dragon's wings, Punch arrows, explosions, wind
charges, a mace smash's area, a hoglin's throw), nor for the ones Horizon makes another
way (the ender dragon's). The level is the hit's: its blocks, random and own attachments.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `canceled`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn living_knockback(&self, _: &mut dyn LevelRandomHost, _: &mut LivingKnockbackEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
NeoForge's `LivingShieldBlockEvent`: entity `entity` of type `kind`
(`minecraft:player`, `minecraft:zombie`) is hit for `damage` from `source` (its
type and entities, as `native_living_incoming_damage` names them), and
`LivingEntity.applyItemBlocking` is
about to resolve what a raised `blocks_attacks` item stops. Every hit with damage
asks, raised item or not: `original_blocked` is whether vanilla blocks (only a
player raises one). Change `block`: `blocked` makes the entity block or not (a block
forced on a hit vanilla lets through stops all of it), `blocked_damage` what is
stopped (kept within 0 and `damage`) and `shield_damage` the durability a raised
item loses (below 0: vanilla's `itemDamage` of what is stopped). Set `blocked` to false and nothing is blocked, as NeoForge's `setBlocked(false)`; the event has no cancel. The level is the hit's: its blocks, random and own
attachments.
Side: server.

A living entity's movement speed (`LivingEntity.getSpeed`) is about to drive its travel on the ground and through fluids. `entity` is its id and `kind` its type; a mod may change `speed`. Fires on both sides, on the client's replayed ticks too, with the loop `context` of the side that ticks the entity (its registries, settings and mod list): register the mod on both, and keep the listener a pure function of its inputs so prediction and the server agree. Beyond NeoForge: there is no counterpart. Diverges from upstream: new hook.
Side: both.

NeoForge's `LivingUseTotemEvent`: a killing blow on entity `entity` of type `kind`
from `source` (named as `native_living_incoming_damage` names it) would be taken by the
`death_protection` item `item` in its `hand` (main or off;
`LivingEntity.checkTotemDeathProtection`). Set `cancel` and the entity gets no
protection: it dies and the item is kept. A player or a mob holding a totem fires it; a
source that bypasses invulnerability never reaches it. `player_totem` still
hears a server player's totem that did save them, after this. The level is the hit's: its blocks, random and own
attachments.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn living_use_totem(&self, _: &mut dyn LevelRandomHost, _: &mut LivingUseTotemEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
How visible `entity` is to `looking` (NeoForge's
`LivingVisibilityEvent`, last in `LivingEntity.getVisibilityPercent`):
the range a mob's targeting check sees it from is scaled by
`visibility`. It comes in as vanilla's percent (sneaking 0.8,
invisibility by armour cover, a worn head's `mob_visibility`: 0.5 to
its own mob type); multiply it to scale. Values below 0 count as 0,
and the result is clamped to 10. Asked for any living target, by the
mobs whose targeting checks scale by visibility (hostile targeting,
sensors, the happy ghast's tempt). A mob target comes in without the
sneaking factor, which vanilla reads through `isDiscrete`.
Server-side.
Side: server.

A loot condition of a mod's own kind: the entry named a `type` in a
namespace outside `minecraft:`. The kind, the JSON, the context and
whether it holds are here (`holds` starts `false`; a mod that claims
the kind sets it). The context is an owned snapshot, captured after the subscription guard.
`tags` reads membership and ordered members by key from this evaluation's
authoritative merged tags. No enumeration or full Host is exposed.
Side: server.

Every mod gets `event.holds` in order and may add, change or remove holds.

A block broke or a mob died, and `drops` are the items about to drop, in
the order they drop: what the loot tables rolled (after
`loot_table_load`'s changes), and for a mob what it wore, held or
carried (a fox's mouth item, an allay's, piglin's or horse's inventory),
but not an enderman's carried block or a copper golem's preserved
equipment, which drop after. A charged creeper's head and a fox's mouth
item come before the mob's own table. A block's stacks get its block
entity's data (a shulker box's items) after this. Add, change or take out
stacks; empty ones don't drop (NeoForge's global loot modifiers, Fabric's
`LootTableEvents.MODIFY_DROPS`); `context` says what dropped them and
how, and it is called even when `drops` is empty. A player's use drops
through it too (`LootDrops::used`: shears, a brush, an item
frame), with that player named. Lead drops from untying or cutting a
leash, and from a mob a player killed while leashed, pass through here
too, with that player named. It hears blocks that a
player, an explosion or a mob breaks, not other breaks (leaves decaying,
a torch losing its wall, a piston, `/setblock ... destroy`), nor a
creative break or a tool that can't harvest the block, nor experience.
For deaths, `context.damage_source` carries the death invocation's
damage type and causing/direct IDs (not remembered player credit), and
`context.tool` is None (the entity context has no TOOL). Resolve the causing
ID through `host.entity` and `host.living` to read its main hand live with
`living.hand_item(host, Hand::Main)`, including earlier listeners' changes.
`context.weapon_item(host)` reads the recorded projectile weapon or the
live melee weapon, including a player's active auto-spin stack.
Block and use drops retain their tool meaning.
Server-side, for every player.
Side: server.

Every mod gets `event.drops` in order and may add, change or remove drops.

A loot function of a mod's own kind: the entry named a `type` in a
namespace outside `minecraft:`, and the roll kept it for this call.
The kind and JSON file input accompany owned API context and candidate snapshots.
Candidate counts remain signed; ordered NBT patches preserve removals and types.
Conversion happens only for subscribed hooks, and refused writeback leaves the roll unchanged.
`tags` reads membership and ordered members by key from this evaluation's
authoritative merged tags. No enumeration or full Host is exposed.
Side: server.

Every mod gets `event.stack` in order and may add, change or remove stack.

A native mod's hook point (docs/modding/src/how-to/native-mods.md), declared in `hooks/*.rs` with the game's:
the loot table `id` (`minecraft:chests/simple_dungeon`, `minecraft:blocks/stone`,
`minecraft:entities/zombie`) as it loads, its JSON after the data packs', before anything
rolls it (NeoForge's `LootTableLoadEvent`, Fabric's `LootTableEvents.MODIFY`). Add pools to
`table["pools"]` or entries to a pool's `entries`, change or replace it (no pools: it drops
nothing; keep its `random_sequence` when replacing it, as a mob's table without one drops
nothing). Called once per table in id order when the server loads or reloads its data, with the
`DataLoadContext` of that owning load (`origin()` is always `ServerDataLoad`: the client never loads
loot tables, so the hook never fires there).
Side: server.

Every mod gets `event.table` in order and may add, change or remove table.

The map decoration types a mod adds (NeoForge's `RegisterEvent` for
`Registries.MAP_DECORATION_TYPE`): push a `MapDecorationType` per type. Asked once at
start, on every side.
Side: both.

Every mod gets `event.types` in order and may add, change or remove types.

Icons a mod puts on map `map` each time it is drawn: held, in an
item frame or on the cartography table's screen (a map's pixels are
its own; nothing is saved in the map). Push `MapDecoration`s
(an atlas sprite, a position in half map pixels, a rotation, and
whether it shows in a frame and on the screen like vanilla's markers
do); they are drawn after the vanilla ones with the same pose, and a
sprite the atlas lacks is left out. `map.center`, `map.scale` and
`map.dimension` say which blocks the map shows, and
`MapDecoration::x` has the formula. Vanilla's decorations are
not passed in. Asked every frame a map is drawn, so keep it cheap.
The client half of `MapDecorationType` and `addDecoration`: a type
registered on the server and saved in the map's data is not here.
Side: client.

Every mod gets `event.decorations` in order and may add, change or remove decorations.

The normal menu blur request, before finite/range validation. None disables it.
Side: client.

A click in a menu a mod opened (`native_open_menu`), which moved
nothing: the menu's `slot` (its own first, then the player's
inventory, `native_menu_inventory_slot`; -999 outside), the `button`
and the click's `mode` (`ClickType`'s id) of the player `uuid`.
No player's state is swapped in: the menu helpers take the player's
UUID. `ItemPlace::MenuSlot` reaches the menu's own storage and its player's
inventory and hotbar slots. `PlayerSlot` and `PlayerHand` resolve the online
clicking player through the usual acting-player or guest path. All writes
use transactions; stale menus and player identities refuse writes.
Side: server.

A menu a mod opened closed: the player closed it, the server or a mod
opened another, or the player left.
Side: server.

Block `block` at `pos` opens its mod menu type `menu` for server
player `player`: set `data` to hand the menu's screen bytes of your
own (a machine's tier, mode or recipes), up to 32 KiB, which the
client reads with `screen_extra_data` while the screen is open
(NeoForge's `openMenu` with an extra-data writer). The first mod to
set it wins, so answer only for your blocks. The player's state is not
swapped in.
Side: server.

Return `Some` to set `data`; the first mod returning `Some` wins.
methods.signature: fn menu_extra_data(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut MenuExtraDataEvent<'_>) -> Option<Vec<u8>>

methods.doc:
Containers exposed by linked slots of server player `player`'s open mod menu
`menu` (`namespace:path`) at `pos`. The player's state is not swapped in.
Push container positions to `links`, in order. The engine resolves containers and
refreshes their linked slots in the same tick. Asked each server tick only for open
mod menu types declaring links, and dispatched only to subscribers. With no
subscribers the linked-container tick does no work and allocates nothing.
Silently skips `pos`, duplicate positions, missing or non-lendable containers,
and positions after 64 accepted containers (`MAX_MENU_LINKS`). First accepted
occurrence wins, preserving answer order.
Native and wasm listeners append positions with identical copy-out semantics.
Side: server.

Every mod gets `event.links` in order and may add, change or remove links.

The minimap a native mod shows: set `minimap` when it is none yet.
Side: client.

Return `Some` to set `minimap`; the first mod returning `Some` wins.

NeoForge's `MobDespawnEvent`: the mob `mob` (of type `kind`, at `pos`) is about to run `Mob.checkDespawn`, which fires once per tick for every mob that is ticked or only checked for despawning, persistent ones and peaceful-mode ones included. The hook is told while the game has lent its mob list to the tick, so `mob` resolves through the tick's own read view (arismoko/horizon#795): the ticking mob itself, and the other present mobs in its tick snapshot, are readable through the host. The ticking mob is read directly; an already-ticked peer exposes its post-turn state and a not-yet-ticked peer its pre-turn state. A mob spawned during the pass does not resolve in this scoped view until the next pass. Removed mobs do not resolve; a dead-but-present mob is not a removed mob. This is the scoped read-host first step for arismoko/horizon#795, not an in-place ownership redesign. `kind` and `pos` stay as plain data for listeners that only need them. Set `result`: `Allow` discards the mob now, `Deny` keeps it this tick, and `Default` (the starting value) leaves vanilla's rules to decide. Anything but `Default` skips vanilla's checks, including the `nextInt(800)` draw of the idle-despawn roll, so the hook fires before that draw: a mob a mod denies does not consume it. A listener is a pure function of its inputs, because the hook fires on replayed ticks. The wither and the ender dragon override `checkDespawn` without `super`, so the event is not fired for them. Server-side. Tick-time effect: one `listened` branch per mob per tick with no listeners.
Side: server.

NeoForge's `MobEffectEvent.Added`, vanilla's `MobEffect.onEffectStarted`:
every `LivingEntity.addEffect` of the content mod's effect `effect`,
new or not, changed or not, after `on_effect_added`.
Server-side.
Side: server.

NeoForge's `MobEffectEvent.Applicable`, vanilla's `LivingEntity.canBeAffected`: asked wherever the game checks whether the resolved `EffectKey` `effect` (`minecraft:poison`) can land on the living entity `entity` (a [`LivingRef`], the player's own included), before `addEffect` accepts it. Unlike the effect hooks above this fires for every effect, vanilla's included, and only when an add is in flight. The first mod to answer decides: `Allow` or `Deny` overrides the vanilla tag check; an unanswered hook falls back to it. Server-side.
Side: server.

Return `Some` to set `applicable`; the first mod returning `Some` wins.
methods.signature: fn mob_effect_applicable(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut MobEffectApplicableEvent) -> Option<EffectApplicable>

methods.doc:
NeoForge's `MobEffectEvent.Expired`, vanilla `LivingEntity.tickEffects`: the resolved `EffectKey` `effect` (`minecraft:speed`, amplifier `amplifier`) on the living entity `entity` (a [`LivingRef`], the player's own included) counted down to nothing and is about to leave. Cancel and the effect stays, kept at no ticks and asked again next tick; unanswered, the expiry runs. Fires only on the tick an effect actually expires, never per tick. Server-side.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.

NeoForge's `MobEffectEvent.Remove`, vanilla `LivingEntity.removeEffect`: the resolved `EffectKey` `effect` (`minecraft:speed`, amplifier `amplifier`) on the living entity `entity` (a [`LivingRef`], the player's own included) is about to be removed by any path that walks the vanilla funnel: a command or milk for the player, a cure for a zombie villager, a mod's removal helper. Cancel and the effect stays. Server-side.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn mob_effect_remove(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut MobEffectRemoveEvent) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
`player`'s melee blow killed the mob `entity` of `kind` (other deaths
aren't told yet). It only hears, after the blow landed. Server-side.
Side: server.

NeoForge's `MobSpawnEvent.SpawnPlacementCheck`: may the entity type `kind` spawn at `pos` in `level` for `reason`? It is asked after vanilla's own spawn predicate (`SpawnPlacements.checkSpawnRules`: light, the ground it needs, the biome, slime chunks, the peaceful rule) has run: `default_result` is what it answered, and `result` starts as `Default`, which keeps that answer. Set `Succeed` or `Fail` to force the check. It runs wherever the game calls `checkSpawnRules` with the game's level: natural spawning, a village siege's zombies, a patrol, a zombie's reinforcements, a spawner and a trial spawner. `level` is the level the mob would spawn in (`dimension` names it too), so a listener can read the blocks around `pos` through the host. `spawner` is the block that asked: `Spawner::Block` for a spawner block, `Spawner::Trial` for a trial spawner, and `None` for natural spawning, sieges, patrols, reinforcements and a spawner minecart. A spawner whose spawn data carries custom spawn rules never reaches it. The predicate always runs first, as `default_result` is its answer, so its random draws are vanilla's whatever a mod answers; a listener should be a pure function of its inputs, because the checks run again when a tick is replayed. The host is the read-only one: a listener reads the world and writes nothing. Not told of `/summon` or a spawn egg, which do not check placements. Server-side. Beyond NeoForge: one `SpawnCheck` answers this event and `mob_spawn_position_check`, which NeoForge gives two nested enums with the same three constants.
Side: server.

NeoForge's `MobSpawnEvent.PositionCheck`: may the freshly created mob of type `kind` stand at `pos` (its position, a mob's centre) in `level` for `reason`? Vanilla's two checks are `Mob.checkSpawnRules` (the type's own rules) and `Mob.checkSpawnObstruction` (inside blocks or fluids, an ocelot's grass and sea level). `result` starts as `Default`, which runs them; `Succeed` or `Fail` answers instead and they are skipped. It runs on natural spawning, chunk generation's creature packs and spawner blocks (where a spawner with custom spawn rules skips `Mob.checkSpawnRules` on `Default`, as vanilla does).  A trial spawner runs only `checkSpawnObstruction`, so only that is skipped. `spawner` is the block that asked (`Spawner::Block` or `Spawner::Trial`), `None` for natural spawning, chunk generation and a spawner minecart. `mob` is the mob itself, in no level yet: read it through the host (`mob.kind(host)`, `mob.position(host)`, `mob.equipment(host, slot)`); after the hook returns the handle answers `Expired`. It is the mob that spawns if the check passes, handed on rather than created again, and dropped without trace if it fails. Where the game does not create the mob fresh (chunk generation's packs, a spawner whose spawn data carries entity data) the handle answers its kind and position and `Unsupported` for the rest. Server-side. With no listener or `Default` the checks and their random draws are vanilla's (creating the mob for the listener draws nothing from the level's random); `Succeed` and `Fail` skip the checks and so their draws, and the level random's order changes only then; a listener should be a pure function of its inputs, because ticks are replayed.
Side: server.

A new mob of `kind` joined `dimension` at `pos`: `natural` when the
world's spawning made it, false when something else did (a breed, a
raid, a spawner, a conversion, `/summon`, and the second mob of a
jockey the world spawned). One call a mob: a `/summon` with passengers
tells each. Not told of a mob loaded with its chunk, leaving a hive or
changing level. It only hears; the mob is already among the game's
mobs. Server-side.
Side: server.

A slime, magma cube or sulfur cube is dying and about to split into
smaller ones (NeoForge's `MobSplitEvent`, vanilla's
`AbstractCubeMob.remove`): `parent` is its entity id, `kind` its type,
`size` its size, `child_size` the size of the children (half of it)
and `count` how many vanilla made (2 to 4 for a slime or magma cube,
2 for a sulfur cube; a primed one makes none and isn't asked). A mod
may change `count` (0 spawns none, at most 64) or set `cancel` to
spawn no children. Only for a parent above size 1, once the child
count is drawn. NeoForge's list of child mobs is this count:
changing a child or adding one of another kind needs a handle to a
mob not yet in the world, which this hook does not expose. On the
server.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn mob_split(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut MobSplitEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
The number of players with the mod container at `pos` of `dimension`
open went from `previous` to `viewers` (vanilla's
`ContainerOpenersCounter`, as a barrel keeps it): 0 to more than 0 is
`onOpen`, back to 0 is `onClose`, any change `openerCountChanged`, so a
block can show itself open while `viewers` is not 0. Counted every
tick from the players' open menus, so a player who leaves without
closing (a lost connection, death, another dimension, out of reach, the
block gone) is heard too (`recheckOpeners`). Once for each change, with
no player's state swapped in. Server-side.
Side: server.

A saved mod list (code and content mods) was read while opening a world. Fires
even when the list is empty or unchanged, never when absent, once per open.
Versions use the loader's comparison; minecraft is excluded. Newly added mods
are not differences. Push a mod id converted with `.into()` into `resolved`.
Dispatch assigns the first resolving listener and preserves earlier markers.
When a saved mod is no longer loaded, it fires before the world opens, on the
side that asks (the client in singleplayer, the dedicated server), and a
resolved id is taken off the question; otherwise it fires on the opening
server before world-state restoration, after preparation.
Side: both.

Every mod gets `event.resolved` in order and may add, change or remove resolved.

A mod's own equipment slot has changed: the committed notice, after
the mod wrote its stack. The fields are `mod_slot_will_change`'s
without `cancel`: `holder`, `slot`, `index`, `cosmetic`, `old`, `new`
and `source`, the caller's own hint about why (`equip`, `unequip`,
`reload`, `death` are the usual names; any string is accepted). The mod calls
`item::mod_slots::native_mod_slot_changed` with its host once its own
write is committed. Server-side; clients get the stacks from the mod's
own sync payload.
Side: server.

A mod's own equipment slot is about to change: the cancellable moment,
before the mod writes its stack. `holder` is the entity, `slot` the
bare slot id (`ring`), `index` the slot's index and `cosmetic` whether
it is a cosmetic copy. `old` and `new` are the stacks before and after
and `source` is the caller's own hint about why (`equip`, `unequip`,
`reload`, `death` are the usual names; any string is accepted). Set
`cancel` to refuse the change; listeners run by `#[listener(priority)]`.
The mod calls `item::mod_slots::native_mod_slot_will_change` with its
host from its own transaction; the game does not know these slots.
Server-side.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.

Every model of a resource load is baked and published (`ModelEvent.BakingCompleted`): the
block and item models and the standalone ones mods asked for (`standalone_models`), in the
store `model` now reads. Fires once per successful model load, after both
`texture_atlas_stitched` calls: on the first load before `client_setup`, and after every
successful resource reload (F3+T, a pack turned on or off, a server's pack) before
`client_resources_reloaded`; a reload that fails fires nothing, and the old handles stay
right. Look the models a mod draws up here, once, through `render_assets().model`, and
keep the `ModelRef`s until the next `model_baking_completed`, when the old ones answer
`ModelError::StaleModel`. Never look them up by name every frame. Client-side.
Side: client.

NeoForge's `ModifyCustomSpawnersEvent`: the level `dimension` is about to tick its custom
spawners for the first time. `spawners` is the list `ServerLevel` ticks, in order, and it
starts with vanilla's (`WanderingTrader`, `Patrol`, `Cat`, `VillageSiege` and `Phantom`,
in the order Horizon ticks them). Take a vanilla spawner out with `remove` and it never
ticks, so its random draws are gone with it; add a spawner of the mod's own with `add` and
a `SpawnerKey` the mod owns, and `custom_spawner_tick` runs for it every tick, after the
ones before it in the list. A key identifies the custom spawner
because an object a guest implements cannot cross to a wasm mod (Beyond NeoForge). With
no listener, or one that leaves the list alone, the level ticks exactly vanilla's
spawners. The phantom spawner runs after the level's mobs have ticked, as the game runs
it, wherever it is in the list. It fires once per level, on the server, and listeners run on replayed ticks,
so they must be pure functions of their inputs. Not cancellable.
Side: server.

NeoForge 26.3's ModifyDefaultComponentsEvent: set or remove entries in
`components`, the default component map for `item`, including vanilla items.
Asked once per item after registries freeze, before the owning load
publishes immutable defaults. Receives a read-only DataLoadContext with
the actual ServerDataLoad or ClientPreload origin, frozen registry names,
settings captured once for loaded packages at this load boundary, and
the shared LoadedMods view. Readers and datapack reloads do not replay
this event. No runtime Host, world handles or transaction access.
Side: both.

Every mod gets `event.components` in order and may add, change or remove components.

Farmland at `pos` is about to change moisture from `from` to `to`.
Set `cancel` to keep its old moisture. Server-side.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.

An accepted raw button event finished dispatch, including a screen handler's early return.
Side: client.

Raw mouse button input on any screen, before dispatch; cancel skips dispatch and Post.
Button/modifiers use the same GLFW encoding as screen hooks. Synthetic clicks skip it.
Side: client.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `canceled`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn mouse_button_pre(&self, _: &mut dyn ClientHost, _: &mut MouseButtonPreEvent) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
Gameplay scrolling after accumulation, before hotbar/spectator handling.
`scroll` is scaled x/y, `accumulated` whole x/y steps, `buttons` left/middle/right,
and `cursor` the GUI position. Cancel skips gameplay scrolling.
Side: client.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `canceled`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn mouse_scrolling(&self, _: &mut dyn ClientHost, _: &mut MouseScrollingEvent) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
Local player movement input, after reading it and before applying it.
All seven keys are independent; opposing direction keys cancel. If any
direction key changes, its keyboard direction replaces axis edits and
controller input. Otherwise axis edits stand and update packet flags.
With enabled listeners, false sprint holds sprint off this tick (even a
passive listener's unchanged false); true requests vanilla eligibility.
Without enabled listeners, vanilla latch, double tap and input are unchanged.
Side: client.

Choose this client's music, once a client tick: `music` and `volume`
hold what vanilla chose (`Minecraft.getSituationalMusic` and
`getMusicVolume`: the biome's track, the creative or underwater one, a
boss's, the menu's; None for silence). Set `music` to a track of your
own, a sound event of your content mod's `sounds.json` such as
`Music::new("mymod:music.spring", 1200, 6000, false)` (the delays in
ticks between songs, and whether it cuts off a different song playing),
None to keep vanilla's quiet, or change `volume` (0 to 1) to fade it.
Side: client.

The tracks to play over (or instead of) the music on this client,
asked once a client tick: push a `MusicLayer` (a sound event, looped,
and its volume, 0 to 1) for each. A layer eases to a new volume over up
to two seconds, and one left out fades out and stops; layers that
first appear in the same tick start together, so list every stem of a
piece from the start, the silent ones at volume 0, and raise them (a
fuller arrangement as a village grows). Their sound events should be
`stream: true` in `sounds.json`.
Side: client.

Every mod gets `event.layers` in order and may add, change or remove layers.

The block at `pos` (`state`) is about to tell its neighbours it
changed (NeoForge's `BlockEvent.NeighborNotifyEvent`): at
`ServerLevel.updateNeighborsAt`, which notifies all six sides
(`skipped_side` is `None`), and `updateNeighborsAtExceptFromFacing`,
which notifies all but `skipped_side`. Set `cancel` and no neighbour
hears, on both paths. Asked for every such update, redstone
included: answer fast. Server-side.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.

A player is tuning a note block on the authoritative server, not in
client prediction. `context` gives its dimension, position, instrument
and old note; `new_note` starts as vanilla's cycled note. Set it to 0
through 24; an out-of-range value keeps vanilla's. Cancel to leave the
note unchanged and prevent playback.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.

The note block at `pos` is about to play (NeoForge's
`NoteBlockEvent.Play`, in `NoteBlock.playNote`), once a block above
no longer mutes it. `player` and `player_entity_id` name the player
who tuned or punched it, and are `None` for redstone.
`instrument` is its instrument and `note` its note, 0 to 24; change
either to play another (a note out of range keeps the block's own).
Set `cancel` and it doesn't play: no sound, no particle, no
`note_block_play` game event. Server-side.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.

`MobEffect.onEffectAdded`: `LivingEntity.addEffect` gave `entity`
(as in `native_apply_effect_tick`) the content mod's effect `effect`,
which it didn't have. Server-side.
Side: server.

A player's equipment slot `slot` (`head`, `chest`, `legs`, `feet`,
`offhand`, and `mainhand` on a swap of the hands or `/item`) took a different
item, `new` (none when it was emptied): `LivingEntity.onEquipItem`,
before the equip sound. It only hears. Never for a spectator.
Server-side, for every player of the world (the helpers read the
acting one).
Side: server.

The player did `event` on mod `mod_id`'s panel (`native_panel_items`):
act on it when it is yours.
Side: client.

NeoForge's `PermissionsChangedEvent`: the operator list is about to give player
`player` (`name`) the permission level `new` in place of `old`, through `PlayerList.op`
(`/op`, the console's `op`, the management API's `operators/add` and `operators/set`)
or `PlayerList.deop` (`/deop` and the same on the console and the management API;
`new` is then `All`). Set `cancel` and the list keeps the old level. The player need
not be online: `player_entity_id` is their server entity id when they are. Clearing
the list (`operators/clear`) is not a call to either, as in vanilla. Dedicated
servers only; a single-player world has no operator list. Server-side.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn permissions_changed(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut PermissionsChangedEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
Before `player` picks up orb `orb` in `dimension`. Mutations to `value`
and `count` take effect only when not canceled; value is clamped to
1..=i32::MAX and count to at least one.
Canceling leaves the orb and pickup delay unchanged. Server-side. Diverges from upstream: renamed from `experience_orb_pickup`, to NeoForge's `PlayerXpEvent.PickupXp`.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `canceled`, and later mods are skipped unless they
