listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn pickup_xp(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut PickupXpEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
On an authoritative server, the piston at `piston` pushed the blocks at
`push` one step `direction` (`[0, 1, 0]` is up; pulling when it
retracts, `extending` false) and destroyed those at `destroy`
(NeoForge's `PistonEvent.Post`, at the end of `PistonBaseBlock.moveBlocks`,
after the neighbour updates). It only hears; `piston_pre` is the veto.
Server-side. Diverges from upstream: `piston_move` is split into
`piston_pre` and `piston_post`.
Side: server.

On an authoritative server, the piston at `piston` is about to push
the blocks at `push` one step `direction` (`[0, 1, 0]` is up; pulling
when it retracts, `extending` false) and destroy those at `destroy`
(NeoForge's `PistonEvent.Pre`, in `PistonBaseBlock.moveBlocks`, once its
structure resolved). Set
`canceled` and nothing moves, as when the structure can't; a sticky
piston then retracts without its block, and clients are sent the
blocks rather than the retraction to replay. Diverges from upstream: `piston_move` is renamed to
`piston_pre`, and `piston_post` is new.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `canceled`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.

A sound bound to `entity` is about to play (NeoForge's
`PlayLevelSoundEvent.AtEntity`, in `Level.playSeededSound`'s entity
overload, `playSound(except, sourceEntity, ...)`): a goat horn, a frog's
tongue, eating and spawn, an animal eating (frog, goat, sniffer), a long
jump, a goat's ram, a breeze's charge and deflection, shearing (sheep,
mooshroom, snow golem, bogged, copper golem), dye on a sheep, an axe on a
copper golem, an allay's item and duplication, a ghastling hatching, a
trident thrown (the trident) or riptide (the player), and a mod's sound
bound to an entity. Asked after the tick's other sounds. The fields and
their rules are `play_level_sound_at_position`'s. Client entity-sound
packets ask before playback and keep following their emitter; an absent
emitter plays nothing. `LocalPlayer.playSound` also asks this hook,
including steps, falls, hurt, bundle clicks and consumption; these remain
positional sounds, not following sounds. Both sides, distinguished by `HostSide`.
Side: both.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.

A sound is about to play at `position` in `level` (NeoForge's
`PlayLevelSoundEvent.AtPosition`, in `Level.playSeededSound`):
every server sound not bound to an entity, mobs' own sounds included
(`Entity.playSound` plays at the entity's position). A mod may change
`sound`, `source`, `volume` and `pitch`, or set `cancel` and no player
hears it; `original_volume` and `original_pitch` are as asked. A sound
left unplayable (a volume or pitch that isn't finite and at least 0)
is dropped. Sounds the server's level plays during
the tick are asked as they go out, at the end of the tick, with the state
then. `/playsound` sends its packet directly and isn't asked, as in
vanilla on the server. On the client, incoming sound packets ask before
playback, including `/playsound`; client-predicted and game-event level
requests ask here too. Canceling a sound does not cancel its action or prediction.
Server and client requests are separate:
`HostSide` identifies which one is being edited. UI and sound-engine-only
playback do not ask this hook. Both sides.
Side: both.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.

`starting` is true for starts and loop replays, false for a live channel refresh.
A live refresh applies only volume and pitch transiently; `None` stops the channel.
Invalid edited numeric values refuse that refresh.
A sound is about to play (`PlaySoundEvent`, vanilla's `SoundEngine.play`): `original` is the sound as asked for, `sound` starts as a copy of it. Edit `sound` (its volume, pitch, source, position, identifier, looping, delay, attenuation or relativeness) to change what plays, or set it to `None` to play nothing. It is asked before the engine's own checks (output open, sound resolved, volume, channel pool), for every sound the client plays, so answer fast; later mods see earlier mods' edits in `sound` and the sound as asked for in `original`. A new `identifier` is resolved again, with its own weighted pick. `context` is the client's `LoopContext`: no game is at hand inside the sound engine. Client-side only; a server has no sound.
`instance` is an engine-local sound instance id, unchanged across its live updates.
Side: client.

A sound that is not streamed has started on `channel` (`PlaySoundSourceEvent`), after the engine set its pitch, volume, attenuation, looping and position: `sound` is what is playing, after `play_sound`'s edits. A notice: the channel is an id only and gives no control. Streamed sounds (music, records) fire `play_streaming_source` instead. Client-side only.
Side: client.

A streamed sound (music, a record) has started on `channel` (`PlayStreamingSourceEvent`): `sound` is what is playing, after `play_sound`'s edits. A notice: the channel is an id only and gives no control. Other sounds fire `play_sound_source` instead. Client-side only.
Side: client.

A server player completed an advancement, after progress was recorded.
Side: server.

A criterion of a server player's advancement was granted or revoked, after its progress changed
and before any completion rewards. A grant or revoke that changes nothing is not heard.
`progress` is an owned snapshot of every criterion (including its stored grant date),
the requirement groups and their completion at this exact mutation. It belongs to
the mutated progress, including first-tick and reload grants queued by the server hub.
During a nested player turn, a suspended player's hub record may contain displaced
progress. A listener may retain a clone; later mutations do not change the snapshot.
Side: server.

A guest's arm swing was handled by the server. `hand` is `mainhand`. Server-side.
Side: server.

A server player reset their attack strength by swinging (`handlePunch`). The swing and reset
have already happened. The player's state is not swapped in. Server-side.
Side: server.

A server player is about to enter a bed after the sleep checks pass. Set `cancel` to keep them
out. The player's state is swapped in.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn player_bed_enter(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut PlayerBedEnterEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
`PlayerWakeUpEvent`: a server player is getting out of the bed at
`pos` (`Player.stopSleepInBed`), heard first, while they still read
as sleeping there. `wake_immediately` is vanilla's flag for skipping
the wake-up fade: generic stop-sleeping, death and bed-missing wakes
pass true; morning, explicit leave and bed-rule refusal pass false.
`update_level` is false for morning, true for those individual wakes.
Side: server.

A player's destroy speed for the block at `pos` may be changed or canceled.
Side: both.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `canceled`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.

A server player took `stack` from a brewing stand bottle slot
(`BrewingStandMenu.PotionSlot.onTake`): `player` is their UUID and
`player_entity_id` their network id.
Side: server.

A server player caught a mob in a bucket, after it was removed and the filled bucket was given.
Server-side.
Side: server.

A server player selected a bundle item in `slot` at `index`. The guest's
state is not swapped in during packet handling.
Side: server.

A server player changed a beacon's selected effects, after they were stored. Each selected
effect is an `Option<EffectKey>`; None means no effect. Server-side.
Side: server.

`player` (`name`) changed dimension (NeoForge's
`PlayerChangedDimensionEvent`): `from` and `to` are dimension ids
(`minecraft:overworld`, `minecraft:the_nether`, `minecraft:the_end`).
Heard once per move, when it has ended: the portal's exit is found
and the player stands there (after the destination has loaded), a
command's teleport has landed, or a respawn in another level than the
death's is placed for good (a bed or anchor, or the world spawn's
free column, after the fallback when a respawn block was gone). The
level of `to` is the one in place, and the player's state is swapped
in, as for `run_mod_command`: `host.players().acting_player()`,
`PlayerRef::tell`, the item helpers and the rest reach them. Heard for:
Nether and End portals (also riding a vehicle, and leaving the End as
its winner), `/execute in ... run tp` and any other command that
teleports a player into another level, and the death respawn, on a
dedicated server and on the integrated server of single player and
LAN. Not heard by a remote client window; listeners run on the server that simulates the world.
Not heard: a move within a level (`/tp`, an End gateway), a
player who leaves before the move ends, and a move that ends where it
started (a respawn in the dimension of the death).
Side: server.

A server player finished loading the world around them after joining, respawning or changing
dimension. The guest's state is not swapped in. Server-side.
Side: server.

A player's data was copied to their new player (NeoForge's
`PlayerEvent.Clone`, from `ServerPlayer.restoreFrom`): `was_death` is
true after a death, false when they left the End after the credits
(`respawn` with `keepAllPlayerData`). `original` is a hook-scoped view
of the old player's attachments (all types), inventory, position and
level. `player` is the replacement's UUID. Heard before placement on
a server, without swapping a player's state in. Not cancellable.
Side: server.

A command a player typed (NeoForge's `CommandEvent`, before
`Commands.performCommand` runs it), without its slash: any command,
vanilla's and the mods' own, also one the player may not run. Set
`canceled` to stop it: nothing runs and nothing is answered but the
lines pushed to `replies`, which go to the player as system chat.
No player's state is swapped in and the server's player list is busy
with this one, so `PlayerRef::tell` and the other player helpers
reach nobody here: answer through `replies`. Once for each command a
player sends, on a server, and for each line of a quiet command batch
(`horizon:quiet_commands`, whose replies are dropped). A command the
server refuses before reading it (unsigned chat arguments, the chat
rate limit) never reaches it.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `canceled`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn player_command(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut PlayerCommandEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
The command tree a server sends a player (NeoForge's and Paper's
"commands sent to a player" stage): when they join and when their
level changes (`/op`, `/deop`, the LAN settings). `names` are the
root commands their client would get, vanilla's they may use and the
mods'; take a name out and that client gets the tree without it
(and without what it leads to), so it neither completes nor
highlights it. This hides the command from the client only: the
server still runs a typed one, `player_command` stops it.
For a player who is already on, their state is swapped in and the
helpers (`PlayerRef::tell`...) work; for one who is joining it is not, and
their client has no world to tell yet. The tree the hub sends again by
itself (after a respawn or a change of level) keeps the last answer
and does not ask again; the integrated server's owner is not asked
when the world's cheats are switched.
Side: server.

Every mod gets `event.names` in order and may add, change or remove names.

`player` (`name`) closed the menu `player_container_open` told
of (NeoForge's `PlayerContainerEvent.Close`, posted in
`ServerPlayer.doCloseContainer` after the menu's `removed`): they
closed it, walked out of reach, died, changed level, or another menu
opened. A player who leaves closes it before `player_logged_out`
(vanilla posts nothing for a disconnect; Horizon does, so each open has
its close). Once for each open; not told when the server stops. The
menu's items are where it left them: the block's, and the cursor stack
back in the inventory. State swapped in, when the player has a body.
Server-side.
Side: server.

`player` (`name`) opened a menu (NeoForge's `PlayerContainerEvent.Open`,
posted when `ServerPlayer.openMenu` sets the new `containerMenu`): any
menu, vanilla or a mod's. `menu` is the menu type's name
(`minecraft:generic_9x3`, `minecraft:furnace`, `minecraft:merchant`,
`minecraft:crafting`, `minecraft:lectern`, a mod's own), `pos` the
block it is of in `dimension` (none for a trade, a vehicle's, a mod's
native menu or a mount's inventory, which has no menu type in vanilla
and is told as `horizon:mount_inventory`). The player's own inventory
is not one, nor is failed construction. Heard synchronously after construction, the open packet
is queued and full contents sent, with the new menu already current.
Replacing a menu follows its close; even inside one tick, open precedes
`player_container_close`. The player's state is swapped in. Server-side.
Side: server.

A server player has slept for 100 ticks in a bed and now counts as deeply asleep for the
night-skip check.
Side: server.

The item `item` of the server player `player` (`name`) broke in `slot`
(`mainhand`, `offhand`, `head`, `chest`, `legs`, `feet`, `body` or
`saddle`): `LivingEntity.onEquippedItemBroken`, Bukkit's
`PlayerItemBreakEvent`. Listen only; armour has a slot, not a hand.
The player's state is swapped in. Once for each break, on a server; a
creative player and the host of a LAN world are not heard.
Side: server.

A player's break removed the block `state` from `pos`: the
`Block.destroy(level, pos, state)` call `ServerPlayerGameMode.destroyBlock` makes only
after `Level.removeBlock` succeeded, before a creative player's return and `playerDestroy`'s
drops. `state` is the block the removal took out, read just before it: what
`playerWillDestroy` left there (a cracked decorated pot; a disarmed tripwire, where vanilla
passes `Block.destroy` the armed one) or what a `break_block` listener put there.
`block_entity` is the saved data of the block entity that stood at `pos`
(`BlockEntity.saveWithoutMetadata`, read with `state`), none for a block without one;
the entity itself is gone from the level by now, so a live handle would be stale. The
level is writable. Server-side, for every player of the world: the helpers read the
acting one. Not heard for a break `break_block` canceled, nor for a break the level
makes (a piston, water, an explosion).
Side: server.

`player` died: where `ServerPlayer.die` starts, with the death
message's key when the game knows it (`death.attack.lava`; none for a
message it builds from the combat). It only hears. Server-side, for
every player of the world, whether death messages are shown or not.
Side: server.

A server player's book edit or signing packet is about to be applied. `pages` is its page
count; `signing` means the packet has a title. Set `cancel` to drop the edit.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn player_edit_book(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut PlayerEditBookEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
A server player threw an egg, after its projectile was launched and the use was applied.
Server-side.
Side: server.

A server player used a firework rocket to boost while gliding, after the rocket was launched
and consumed. Server-side.
Side: server.

A server player enchanted `item` at an enchanting table
(`EnchantmentMenu.clickMenuButton`): `enchantments` are the ones it was
given, in order, as (id, level). `item` is the enchanted stack (an
enchanted book for a book). Fires after the levels are paid, before
`enchant_item`. Server-side.
Side: server.

A server player's XP orb pickup cooldown changed to `ticks`. It is
reported after the value changes. Server-side.
Side: server.

A server player's fishing rod, with `state`: 0 the cast
(`FishingRodItem.use` throwing the bobber), 1 a fish biting
(`FishingHook.catchingFish`), 2 the reel-in of a bite, which gives the
catch, 3 the reel-in with nothing on the line, 4 the reel-in of a
bobber hooked to an entity or item (like Bukkit's `PlayerFishEvent`;
NeoForge's `ItemFishedEvent` is later, in `FishingHook.retrieve`). Set `cancel` on the cast and nothing
is thrown; on a bite the fish gets away and the wait starts over; on
a reel-in (2 to 4) nothing happens, the bobber stays out and the rod
takes no wear. The bobber ending by itself (too far, the rod put
away, the owner dying), nor the host of a LAN world's rod. The
player's state is swapped in, so `host.players().acting_player()`, `PlayerRef::tell`
and the item helpers reach them. Once for each cast, bite and reel-in,
on a server.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn player_fish(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut PlayerFishEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
A server player put a plant into a flower pot, after the potted block state was stored and the
item consumed. `plant` is the item id and `pos` the pot position. Server-side.
Side: server.

NeoForge's `PlayerFlyableFallEvent`: server player `player` (`name`) landed after
falling `distance` blocks at damage multiplier `multiplier` while allowed to fly (a
creative or spectator player walking), so `Player.causeFallDamage` returned early
and nothing was hurt. Listen only. Once for each landing, after the fall's
block reaction. The player's state is swapped in. Server-side.
Side: server.

A server player's game mode is about to change (NeoForge's
`PlayerChangeGameModeEvent`): from `from` to `to`, both the shared
`GameMode` used by commands and `PlayerRef`. `player` is the UUID and
`name` the name. Heard for
the `/gamemode` command, the F3+F4 switcher's packet and a hardcore
world's respawn into spectator, once for each change to a different
mode; not for the world's default mode a player joins with. Set `to`
to send the player to another mode instead: listeners run in order and
each sees the mode the one before left. Return `Flow::Cancel`, or
leave `to` at the player's current mode, and the player keeps their
mode (nothing is sent, the command counts it as no change); the
command's message names the mode it asked for, as vanilla's does. For a change the game makes inside
a player's turn their state is swapped in; for the hardcore respawn
it is not.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn player_game_mode_changed(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut PlayerGameModeChangedEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
The handshake of a connection that is about to log in or be
transferred in (Paper's `PlayerHandshakeEvent`), before the login
starts and before the protocol version, the proxy's forwarding, the
name, the whitelist or the bans are looked at. `host` is the server
address string the client sent, with whatever a proxy put after the
first NUL (a Bedrock bridge's encrypted player data, Forge's marker);
change it and the rest of the login and `PlayerRef::connect_address`
see the new text, so a mod may cut it back to the plain name. A `host`
longer than 32767 characters is cut at that length. `port` and
`protocol` are the client's own and cannot be changed; `address` is
the IP the connection comes from, empty for an integrated server's own
player (whose `host` is empty too). Set `cancel` to refuse the
connection: the client is disconnected before it logs in, with
`reason` (a plain "Disconnected" if it is left unset). Once for each
login or transfer connection, on a server, never for a status ping.
The hook runs on the server thread at the next tick: the connection
waits for it for 5 seconds and is refused when no answer comes. No
player exists yet, so the host's player helpers reach nobody.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn player_handshake(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut PlayerHandshakeEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
A player's ability to harvest the block at `pos` may be changed.
Side: both.

Every mod gets `event.can_harvest` in order and may add, change or remove can_harvest.

Which hearts the local player's health bar draws this frame (NeoForge's
`PlayerHeartTypeEvent`, from `Gui.HeartType.forPlayer`): `kind` comes in as vanilla's pick
(poisoned, else withered, else frozen when fully frozen, else normal); set it to draw
another kind. Asked once a frame while the HUD draws the hearts (not in creative or
spectator, not under F1), before `health_hud`, whose `inputs.kind` carries the answer.
Only the heart sprites change: health, regeneration and the other rows stay vanilla's.
Client-side.
Side: client.

A guest sent the server's current `PlayerInput` flags, after they were applied to the hub. The guest's state is swapped in. Server-side.
Side: server.

A server player inserted a book into a lectern, after the block entity and inventory changed.
`book` is the item id. Server-side.
Side: server.

`player_inventory_changed(player, stacks)`: a server player's inventory changed, at the moment vanilla's `InventoryChangeTrigger` is checked (the per-tick check found another item or count in a slot), heard before any criterion and whether or not the tree has `inventory_changed` advancements. `stacks` are the 41 slots in `Inventory` numbering: 0..36 the main inventory (0..9 the hotbar), 36..40 the armour (feet, legs, chest, head), 40 the off hand. It also fires at a player's first check after joining, so a mod sees what they log in with. The player's state is swapped in, so the helpers read that player. Single player, LAN guests and a dedicated server's players; never on a client of a remote server. Quest, collection and 'obtain an item' mods need it instead of polling every inventory. Bundles need "hooks": @API:player_inventory_changed@.
Side: server.

An item cooldown is about to start for a server player. `item` is the item id and `ticks` its
duration. The player's state is not swapped in. Set `cancel` to skip starting the cooldown.
Server-side.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn player_item_cooldown(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut PlayerItemCooldownEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
A server player changed an item frame after its contents or rotation changed. `action` is
`put`, `rotate`, `remove_item` or `break`; `item` is empty when no item remains, and `rotation`
is the resulting step. Server-side.
Side: server.

Mending repaired a server player's item with experience from an orb. `repair` is durability
restored and `experience` is the orb's value. Server-side.
Side: server.

`PlayerEvent.ItemSmithedEvent`: a server player took `result` from a
smithing table (`SmithingMenu.onTake`, or `onQuickCraft` for a
shift-click): `player` is their UUID and `player_entity_id` their
network id, `inputs` the template, base and addition as they were
before the take used them (`None` for an empty slot). It comes once the click is done, so the
menu already holds the used inputs, but before the table sounds.
Server-side.
Side: server.

A guest's accepted movement made the server jump them from the ground. Server-side.
Side: server.

A network or fake guest was kicked, after the hub recorded the rendered `reason`. The guest's state is
swapped in unless they were already removed in the same poll.
Side: server.

A server player launched a projectile item, after it was created.
`item` is the projectile's held item.
Side: server.

`player` (`name`) is about to leave, with the plain-text `reason` the
connection ended with (a kick's reason, `Disconnected`, `Timed out`, or
`Server closed` when the server stops). Heard before the player is
removed: they are still in `host.players().server_players()` and in
their level, their state is swapped in, and their inventory, open menu
and carried stack are untouched, so a listener can read or clear the
inventory, drop items, kill or send them a last message; what it does
is part of what is saved. Once for each placed network player, before
`player_logged_out`. A fake player and a player held before the
join was announced are not told of, nor is a player whose transfer to
another server is unresolved or committed: their state may already
belong there, so nothing done here could travel with them. A kick is heard by `player_kicked`
first; `player_disconnect` of the leaving player refuses, whatever ended the
connection.
Server-side.
Side: server.

A server player changed the page of a lectern, after its page and redstone pulse changed.
`page` is the zero-based new page. Server-side.
Side: server.

A server player's experience level changed, after the new level was applied.
Side: server.

A player was loaded from the world's save (NeoForge's
`PlayerEvent.LoadFromFile`, `PlayerList.loadPlayerData`): their `.dat`
has been read and applied, and they are not placed in a level yet.
`directory` is the world's player directory (`players/data`): a mod
reads its own file there, named `<uuid>.<suffix>` as
`getPlayerFile(suffix)` names it. Heard once for each join, for the
owner of an integrated server as for anyone else, on a server, with no
player's state swapped in. Not cancellable.

Not on wasm: it gives a path in the game's file system, which a wasm mod has none of; a wasm mod keeps a player's data in attachments.
Side: server.
methods.wasm_reason: it gives a path in the game's file system, which a wasm mod has none of; a wasm mod keeps a player's data in attachments. Side: server.

methods.doc:
`player` (`name`) joined the game (NeoForge's
`PlayerLoggedInEvent`): placed in the world and listed in
`host.players().server_players()`, so `PlayerRef::send_payload` reaches them.
Once a join, with no player's state swapped in. Server-side.
Side: server.

`player` (`name`) left the game (NeoForge's `PlayerLoggedOutEvent`), by
any path: a lost connection, a kick, the server stopping or failing.
Once for each player `player_logged_in` told of, and also for a kicked
fake player without a preceding login. Silent `remove_fake` sends no logout.
They've already
left `host.players().server_players()`, except when the server stops, which tells
before it saves, with them still listed and able to get a last message.
Server-side.
Side: server.

A player whose login the server has accepted (NeoForge's
`PlayerNegotiationEvent` stage): the name, whitelist, ban and
server-full checks have passed and the player holds a place, but their
saved state is not loaded and they are not placed in a level yet. Set
`cancel` to refuse them: they are disconnected with `reason` (a plain
"Disconnected" if it is left unset) and nothing else of the join (the
join message, `player_logged_in`) happens. Once for each player
who joins, on a server. The player is not placed yet and their client
has no world to show a message in, so no player's state is swapped in
and `PlayerRef::tell` reaches nobody: the refusal `reason` is the answer.
The checks that need no mod (name, whitelist, bans, a full server,
the proxy's forwarding) refuse earlier, on the connection, and this
hook does not hear those players.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn player_login(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut PlayerLoginEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
A player's game profile at login, before the server sends the login
success: the UUID and name the login authenticated and the properties
it would send. Change `properties` to send a different profile: the
login success and the player list use the changed list. The UUID and
name are the login's and are not changed here.

In online mode `properties` holds the account's signed `textures`
property, the skin; a proxy's forwarded properties are here too. An
offline-mode player has none. A skin mod replaces the `textures`
property with its own signed one; keep the other properties.

Once for each player a server accepts, after the name, whitelist, ban
and server-full checks have passed and before the login success is
sent, so a changed profile reaches the player's client and the player
list. It runs on the connection thread and has no host: answer from
the arguments and the mod's own state alone, and do not block the
login. The player is not placed and `player_login` follows later; this
hook cannot refuse the login.

The properties are the profile's wire limits: at most 16, non-empty
names of 64 UTF-16 units, values of 32767 and signatures of 1024. A
list past a limit is refused and the login's own properties are sent
instead.
Side: server.

A server player selected a loom pattern, after the loom menu accepted the button. `pattern` is
the zero-based button index. Server-side.
Side: server.

A server player filled an empty map, after the filled map and its saved data were created.
Server-side.
Side: server.

A player's movement report is about to be applied: they would move from
`from` to `to`, or turn from `from_rotation` to `to_rotation` (`[yaw,
pitch]`). Heard once for each validated report whose position or
rotation differs from the player's last reported location, after the
server's own validation and before the report is committed. That
location is kept on the player's connection, apart from the accepted
position: it is the position given to the listener before it runs, and
the destination of every server-side teleport (a join, a teleport in the
level, a level change, a respawn, the resend of an unconfirmed teleport,
and the correction after a veto). `from` is that location. Set `cancel`
for a real veto and not a rollback: the report is not applied and its
bookkeeping is skipped, and the client is corrected to the accepted
position and rotation through the existing teleport correction. The veto
adds no anticheat violation of its own, but the report was already seen
by the server's own checks and by the anticheat's record of the client's
ticks before the hook, and what a violation of those would have done
still happens. The values are the exact ones: there is no once-per-tick
accumulation and no threshold in the engine, so the mod filters
(`if (to - from).length() < 1.0 / 16.0 { return; }` skips anything under
1/16 of a block). Their state is swapped in
(`host.players().acting_player()`, `PlayerRef::tell`).

A held report is ruled on in the same tick, and the player's later
packets (further reports, the end of the client tick, pongs) wait in
order behind it, then go on in that tick, so each later report is heard
from the one before. A report is out of
time at its 21st tick, counting the tick it was held at as the first: it
is dropped with the correction and never committed, even when a ruling
arrives after that. A player's disconnect, teleport or level change
drops a pending report cleanly. Not heard: the first tick in a level (the
tick after a join or a level change; the second is heard), a player riding
something (`vehicle_moved` hears the vehicle), any teleport (its
confirmation is validated and committed without the hook, at the teleport's
target, and so is the veto's own correction; a report that arrives while a teleport is
unconfirmed is not heard either), and a passage crossing (its caller
reads the position at once, so the report is committed in place). The
first report after a teleport that passed validation is heard, with the
teleport's destination as its `from`. With no listener the report is
committed in place with no extra work: nothing is held, copied or
allocated. With one, the cost is one held report for each moving player
a tick.

A fault or an epoch timeout in a wasm listener answers nothing: it is
not a veto and the report is committed, like every cancellable hook; the
fault is logged, counted against the mod, and stops the mod's group for
the session. A native listener that never returns is out of scope: it
blocks the game thread like any native code, and the 20-tick deadline
covers only a report held pending across ticks. Server-side.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn player_move(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut PlayerMoveEvent) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
A guest's client sent a movement packet and the server's own validation accepted it
(vanilla's `ServerGamePacketListenerImpl.handleMovePlayer`, the flying packet of a packet
library). Heard once for every such packet, also one that changes nothing (a stand-still or
ground-flag packet), where `player_move` hears only a report whose position or rotation
differs. `to` and `to_rotation` (`[yaw, pitch]`) are the packet's values, repeating the
player's own where the packet carries none. `on_ground` is the packet's own on-ground flag as
the client sent it; `has_position` and `has_rotation` say whether the packet carried a
position and a rotation (a status-only packet carries neither). Not heard: the player's first
tick in a level (the tick after a join or a level change), a teleport's confirmation and a
passage crossing. Heard with the player's state swapped in, before `player_move` hears the
same packet. Not cancellable (`player_move` vetoes). With no listener nothing is queued.
Each guest is heard at most 8 packets per tick; the packets over that wait, in order, for
the next ticks (at most 256 wait, the oldest are dropped past that). Only the hook is
budgeted, the movement itself is processed as it arrives, so a packet that waited can be
heard after `player_move` already heard or vetoed the same move. Waiting packets are dropped
when the player changes level, is frozen for a transfer or leaves.
Server-side.
Side: server.

A server player named a mob with a name tag, after its name and persistence changed and the tag
was consumed. Server-side.
Side: server.

A player's display name was formatted. Replace `displayname` to change it.
Both sides: `context.side()` says which. It runs wherever vanilla asks `Player.getDisplayName()`: when a chat line, a join or leave line, a command's feedback, a death message or an advancement message is built, and for the name tag over a player (every frame it shows, so it is not asked when no mod listens). Answer from the arguments and `context` alone, and fast: `context` holds the side, the registries and the settings of the resource generation, and a `/reload` builds the next one.
Side: both.

Every mod gets `event.displayname` in order and may add, change or remove displayname.

A server player opened a sign for editing, after the editor state was made. `front` selects the
front or back side. Server-side.
Side: server.

`player`'s client crossed `passage` (arismoko/horizon#3775), one of the player's level's, from `from`
(its feet before), and the server is about to follow: the move to `from` passed the
move checks and both ends are tracked for the player, and the server has not yet
worked out where the player comes out. Set `cancel` and the server refuses the
crossing (`PassageCrossRefusal::Vetoed`) and puts the player back at `from`, as a
portal Immersive Portals' `canTeleportEntity` turns down does. A listener that
removes the passage or teleports the player refuses it too. Server-side. Diverges
from upstream: new hook.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn player_passage_cross(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut PlayerPassageCrossEvent) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
A server player picked an item from a block or entity, before it enters the hotbar. `pos` is
zero for an entity; `entity_id` is zero for a block. The player's state is swapped in. Set
`cancel` to leave the inventory and client unchanged.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.

methods.doc:
A server player picked up an arrow after it was removed and its pickup was applied. `item` is
the arrow's pickup item id. Server-side.
Side: server.

A guest's client answered a ping (`ServerboundPongPacket`, vanilla's
`ServerGamePacketListenerImpl.handlePong`): `id` is the number the ping carried. The mod
sends the ping itself with `player_send_packet` (`ping`) and measures the round trip, or
counts the client ticks between two answers, as a lag-compensating anticheat does. The
engine's own pings (a recording's end-of-tick ping, whose id is the server tick) are answered
here too, so a mod picks ids it can tell apart from small tick numbers. Heard only for a
pong that answers a ping the server sent on that connection (a mod's or the engine's), once
per ping: an unsolicited or repeated pong, one for a ping sent more than 30 seconds ago, or
one for a ping pushed out by 64 newer unanswered ones, is dropped silently, as vanilla
ignores it. Heard after the packet's turn in the guest's inbox, in order with its other
packets, with the guest's state swapped in. Not cancellable. With no listener nothing is
queued. Server-side.
Side: server.

A server player released a drawn bow with `arrow` selected, by the use-item
key or a mod's `LivingRef::release_using_item`. The player's state is swapped in.
Side: server.

A server player's recipe book requested a known recipe be placed in
their crafting grid. `recipe` is the recipe id; `all` is the shift
click form. Server-side.
Side: server.

A server player's authoritative recipe book pair changed. `book` is a
typed RecipeBookIdentity, never a custom vanilla ordinal. Rejected and
unchanged custom requests do not notify. The guest is not swapped in.
Side: server.

A recipe is about to be unlocked for a server player. Set `cancel` to keep it locked. The
player's state is not swapped in. Server-side.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn player_recipe_discovered(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut PlayerRecipeDiscoveredEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
`PlayerRespawnPositionEvent`: where `player` respawns, once the server has
found it: the bed or anchor they stand up at (facing it), or the world
spawn's free column. `original_level` and `original_position` are that
point; `missing_respawn_block` says the bed or anchor was gone, so the
player came back at the world spawn. Change `level`, `position`, `yaw`
and `pitch` to send them elsewhere: within the level a teleport, into
another level a level change. `copy_original_spawn_position` (default:
the block wasn't missing) says whether they keep their respawn point for
next time. Horizon places the player first and finds the point once its
chunks have loaded, so this fires then, before `player_respawned` only
when no chunks had to load. Not for the End exit, which isn't a respawn
here (as for `player_respawned`). Server-side.
Side: server.

`player` (`name`) respawned (NeoForge's `PlayerRespawnEvent`): at the
end of `PlayerList.respawn`, once they are placed and their health,
food and experience reset, with their state swapped in. Once for each
death that ends in a respawn, on a server; not for the End-exit one.
Side: server.

A server player launched with a riptide trident, after the velocity,
spin attack and grounded lift have been applied. The player's state is
swapped in. No reply is needed.
Side: server.

A player was saved to the world's store (NeoForge's
`PlayerEvent.SaveToFile`, `PlayerList.save`): when they leave or the
world closes, when a dedicated or integrated server saves its guests,
and for an integrated server's owner when the world saves them.
Once for each save. `directory`
is the world's player directory (`players/data`): write your own file
there, named `<uuid>.<suffix>`, never the player's `.dat`. The player
may be leaving, so no player's state is swapped in. Not cancellable.
Autosave snapshots are written asynchronously: this notification runs
on a later server tick after a successful write, possibly after WorldSaved.
Live state may have advanced beyond the saved snapshot; a process exit
before completions are drained can prevent notification delivery.

Not on wasm: it gives a path in the game's file system, which a wasm mod has none of; a wasm mod keeps a player's data in attachments.
Side: server.
methods.wasm_reason: it gives a path in the game's file system, which a wasm mod has none of; a wasm mod keeps a player's data in attachments. Side: server.

methods.doc:
NeoForge's `PlayerSetSpawnEvent`: a server player's respawn point is about to be
set (`ServerPlayer.setRespawnPosition`), once for each call vanilla makes: every sleep
in a bed (the same bed too, which refreshes its angle), an anchor that is a new
point, `/spawnpoint`, and the copy to the new player when a player respawns and their
respawn block was found (`pos` is none for a player with no point). A respawn block
that is gone makes no call. `pos` is the block position and `dimension` its level;
`forced` is `/spawnpoint`'s flag. Set `cancel` and the point stays as it was (the
respawned player is left with none). `player_entity_id` is the server's entity id for
the player. Server-side.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn player_set_spawn(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut PlayerSetSpawnEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
A player shearing a mob is about to do so. Set `cancel` to leave the mob and shears unchanged.
The guest's state is swapped in.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn player_shear_entity(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut PlayerShearEntityEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
A server player's shield was disabled by a blocked melee hit. The shield cooldown is set
immediately after this call. Server-side.
Side: server.

`PlayerSpawnPhantomsEvent`: the phantom spawner is about to decide whether to try a
spawn near a non-spectator server player, before its difficulty and rest rolls.
`result` starts empty, meaning `Default` (skylight and sea level check); `Allow` skips
that check and `Deny` stops the attempt. `phantoms` starts with a randomly drawn
group size; set it to override the count. Without mods the original draw order is kept.
Side: server.

Return `Some` to set `result`; the first mod returning `Some` wins.
methods.signature: fn player_spawn_phantoms(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut PlayerSpawnPhantomsEvent<'_>) -> Option<PhantomSpawnResult>

methods.doc:
A server player's sprint started or stopped: their client sent
`START_SPRINTING` or `STOP_SPRINTING` (the sprint key, a double tap
forward, or letting go) and the server's player is now `sprinting`
(vanilla's `setSprinting` in `handlePlayerCommand`). Heard only when it
changes. It cannot be stopped, and it hears what the client asks, not
what the server does: a sprint that ends by itself (a hit's knockback,
hunger, a wall) is not reported. The player's state is swapped in, so
the helpers and `PlayerRef::tell` work. Once for each change, on a server.
Side: server.

A server player started spectating `entity_id`, after their camera moved to it
(`ServerPlayer.setCamera` with a new target: a spectator's click or `/spectate`) and their
client was told. Heard once per change of target, not again while the camera follows it.
The mirror of `player_stop_spectating_entity`.
Side: server.

A client started tracking an entity (NeoForge's
`PlayerEvent.StartTracking`, posted at the end of
`ServerEntity.addPairing`): `player` (`name`) is now sent `entity`
(its ID, `uuid` its UUID, `kind` its type, `minecraft:zombie`) and its
changes. It comes into range, its client's chunks reach it, or it is
put in the level; another player is an entity too, and a player never
tracks their own. A mod sends the player what they need to show it
(`PlayerRef::send_payload`). The entity is as it was last tick: it
may be gone by now. Heard after the tick's players and entities have
moved, in order, with no player's state swapped in. Server-side.
Side: server.

A statistic is about to be awarded to a server player, before its count and scoreboard criteria
change. `stat_type` and `stat` are ids such as `minecraft:mined` and `minecraft:stone`, and
`value` the amount. All three may be rewritten; ids must use their canonical namespaced
spelling. Unknown types or entries, noncanonical ids and negative amounts are refused
together, warning once and keeping the entire original award.
Set `cancel` to award nothing. Server-side. Ordinary interactions
fire at vanilla's award point; inside a transaction, the award and this hook wait until
the outermost successful commit, after tentative world and inventory writes.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn player_stat_award(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut PlayerStatAwardEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
The player's crouch edge backoff (`Player.maybeBackOffFromEdge`) asks whether the player is staying on the ground surface (`Player.isStayingOnGroundSurface`, vanilla: the shift key is down). `entity` is the player's id; a mod may change `staying`, so a mod can make the player hold to an edge without crouching, or walk off while crouching. Fires on both sides, on the client's replayed ticks too, with the loop `context` of the side that ticks the player (its registries, settings and mod list): register the mod on both, and keep the listener a pure function of its inputs so prediction and the server agree. Beyond NeoForge: there is no counterpart. Diverges from upstream: new hook.
Side: both.

A server player selected a stonecutter recipe, after the menu accepted
its button. `recipe` is the zero-based button index. Server-side.
Side: server.

A server player stopped spectating `entity_id`, after their camera returned to the player.
Side: server.

A client stopped tracking an entity (NeoForge's
`PlayerEvent.StopTracking`, posted at the end of
`ServerEntity.removePairing`): it went out of range, left the level or
died, or `player` (`name`) left, changed level or respawned, which
stops everything they tracked. `entity`, `uuid` and `kind` are as
`player_start_tracking` told. Once for each start, a leaving
player's after `player_logged_out`. The entity is not
necessarily still there, and a player who left is gone: no player's
state is swapped in. Server-side.
Side: server.

A server player released the use-item key, or a mod's `LivingRef::release_using_item` did,
before the item finished being used. The player's state is swapped in.
Side: server.

Heard before a non-spectator player's swap-hands action.
The two mutable stacks start as the off-hand and main-hand stacks;
the hands receive the listener's outputs unless it cancels.
slots. Set `cancel` to keep the items where they are: the player's
client is sent both slots again. The player's
state is swapped in, so `host.players().acting_player()`,
`PlayerRef::tell` and the item helpers reach them. Once for each press,
on a server: a LAN or dedicated server's players, the single-player
owner and a LAN host. Not heard: the same swap made in an open inventory
(hovering a slot and pressing the key, a menu click).
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn player_swap_hands(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut PlayerSwapHandsEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
A server player swapped their main and off hands, after both inventory slots changed.
Server-side.
Side: server.

`PlayerSwitchHotbarSlotEvent.Post`: a server player switched from hotbar slot
`old_slot` to `new_slot` (0 to 8), after the selected slot changed and a main-hand
item use stopped. Fired only when the slot differs and
`player_switch_hotbar_slot_pre` didn't cancel it. The player's state is not swapped in.
Side: server.

`PlayerSwitchHotbarSlotEvent.Pre`: a server player is switching from hotbar slot
`old_slot` to `new_slot` (0 to 8), after the slot range check and before the
selected slot changes. Fired only when the slot differs. The player's state is not
swapped in. Set `cancel` to keep the old slot; the client is sent that slot again,
and `player_switch_hotbar_slot_post` doesn't fire.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn player_switch_hotbar_slot_pre(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut PlayerSwitchHotbarSlotPreEvent) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
ServerPlayer.getTabListDisplayName: the name the Tab list shows for
`player`, None to let the client choose it. Replace `display_name` to
change it. It runs while the Tab list is built. Answer from the arguments and `context` alone, and fast: `context` holds the side, the registries and the settings of the resource generation, and a `/reload` builds the next one.
Side: server.

Every mod gets `event.display_name` in order and may add, change or remove display_name.

A server player took the book from a lectern, after the menu and block entity changed. `book`
is the removed item id. Server-side.
Side: server.

A server player is about to travel through an End gateway at `gateway`. Set `cancel` to leave
them at the entrance; the gateway is not consumed and its cooldown does not start. Server-side.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn player_teleport_end_gateway(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut PlayerTeleportEndGatewayEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
A server player a command teleported (NeoForge's
`EntityTeleportEvent`, for a player): `/tp` and `/teleport`, inside
their level or into another one. `from` and `to` are their feet before
and after, `dimension` the level they are in now. Heard after the move
has reached the player's state and their client (an inter-level
teleport: when the new level is entered, before it has loaded around
them), so it cannot stop it. The player's state is swapped in, so the
helpers that read the acting player and `PlayerRef::tell` work. Once for
each teleported player, on a server. Ender pearls and chorus fruit
have their own hooks; a spectator's teleport menu is not heard yet;
portals and respawns are not teleports here.
Side: server.

After a player's tick on both logical sides (NeoForge 26.3
`PlayerTickEvent.Post`). Non-cancellable, including death-screen ticks.
`player` is the same identity as in `player_tick_pre`; on the server
their state is acting. Runs after body work and server-side item,
arrow and XP pickups, so reads see the completed tick. Client reads
see only the state available to that client, not future server updates.
Side: both.

Before a player's tick on both logical sides (NeoForge 26.3
`PlayerTickEvent.Pre`). Non-cancellable, including death-screen ticks.
`player` identifies the ticked player; on the server their state is
acting. Fires before sleep, cooldowns and body work. Players still tick
under `/tick freeze`, but not while the level is paused.
Side: both.

A server player toggled an ageable mob's age lock with a golden
dandelion, after the lock and item use changed.
Side: server.

A player's client started (`flying`) or stopped flying (vanilla's
`handlePlayerAbilities`, which honours it only for a player who may
fly: creative or spectator), heard once for each change, on a server,
with the player's state swapped in, so `PlayerRef::tell` and the other
helpers reach them. The player is already flying or not as asked, as
vanilla leaves them; set `cancel` to refuse it: they keep the state
they had and the server sends their abilities back, as vanilla does
for what it refuses, so the client lands or flies again. Only what a
client asks for is heard: not the flight a game-mode change starts or
ends (`/gamemode`), and not a LAN host's own player.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn player_toggle_flight(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut PlayerToggleFlightEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
A guest's client changed sneaking in its player input packet, after the hub applied the new state.
The guest's state is swapped in. Server-side.
Side: server.

A totem of undying saved the server player `player` (`name`): their
hurt would have killed them and the totem held in either hand fired
(`LivingEntity.checkTotemDeathProtection`; Bukkit's
`EntityResurrectEvent`), heard just before it is used up and its
effects apply. Listen only: whether the totem saves is decided inside
the health state machine, before a mod is asked, so a mod cannot veto
it from here. The player's state is swapped in, so
`host.players().acting_player()`, `PlayerRef::tell` and the item helpers reach them.
Once for each totem, on a server; the host of a LAN world's totem is
not heard.
Side: server.

A server player completed a villager or wandering trader trade. `entity_id` is the merchant
network id. Server-side.
Side: server.

A server player removed an entity's leash, after it was cleared.
Side: server.

A server applied `velocity` to a player, when syncing changed motion to that player's client.
Side: server.

A server player's experience points are about to change through
`Player.giveExperiencePoints` (NeoForge's `PlayerXpEvent.XpChange`): an
orb pickup after mending, an advancement reward, or `/xp add ... points`.
Change the signed `amount` (in points) or set `cancel` to give nothing.
Experience bottles and furnaces make orbs, so they come through the orb
path. Server-side.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn player_xp_change(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut PlayerXpChangeEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
A server player's level is about to change through
`Player.giveExperienceLevels`: once per level gained or lost by points,
and for the anvil, `/experience add ... levels` and `PlayerRef::give_levels`.
Change `levels`, or set `cancel` to leave the level unchanged. The
player's state is swapped in, so `host.players().acting_player()`, `PlayerRef::tell`
and the item helpers reach them. Server-side.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn player_xp_level_change(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut PlayerXpLevelChangeEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
A Nether portal was built for a dimension travel, or an End platform
was made for an arrival. `pos` is the lower corner of the Nether
portal rectangle or the End platform origin. The completed blocks are
already in the world.
Side: server.

A fire placed at `pos` (`state`) found an empty obsidian frame, `shape`,
and is about to fill it with a nether portal (`BlockEvent.PortalSpawnEvent`,
in `BaseFireBlock.onPlace`), in the Overworld or the Nether. Set
`cancel` and no portal forms: the fire stays where it can survive, as
without a frame. Server-side.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.

Possible natural spawns at a server position (NeoForge's
`LevelEvent.PotentialSpawns`, `NaturalSpawner.mobsAt`). Mods may add or
remove entries, or cancel to make the list empty. Mods can read the world,
but cannot write it during the spawn pass.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `canceled`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.

A brewing stand at `pos` brewed (`PotionBrewEvent.Post`, at the end of
`BrewingStandBlockEntity.doBrew`), or `potion_brew_pre` was cancelled:
`stacks` holds its five slots after the brew (or as the cancelling
mods left them), and what the mods leave there is the stand's. Fires
last, as `doBrew` ends: after `brewing_complete`, the brew sound and
the ingredient's remainder dropping. Server-side.
Side: server.

A brewing stand at `pos` is about to brew (`PotionBrewEvent.Pre`,
in `BrewingStandBlockEntity.doBrew`): `stacks` is a copy of its five
slots (three bottles, the ingredient, the fuel). Set `cancel` to skip
vanilla's brew: the stand then takes `stacks` as the mods left them,
uses no ingredient and plays no brew sound, and `potion_brew_post`
fires with those slots; `brewing_complete` doesn't, as nothing was
brewed. Uncancelled, changes to `stacks` are dropped. Server-side.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn potion_brew_pre(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut PotionBrewPreEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
A thrown splash or lingering potion applied its hit effects.
Side: server.

A hopper at `pos` began an item transfer attempt. This runs after its
cooldown and enabled checks, before pushing or pulling any items.
Server-side, including the single-player server.
Side: server.

A crafting-grid result was prepared for a server player; `pos` is the crafting table, or None for the inventory grid. Change `result` before it is sent.
Side: server.

Return `Some` to set `result`; the first mod returning `Some` wins.
methods.signature: fn prepare_item_craft(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut PrepareItemCraftEvent<'_>) -> Option<item::item_stack::ItemStack>

methods.doc:
Enchanting offers were calculated for a server player at `pos`. Change `costs` before they are sent to the menu.
Side: server.

A smithing result was prepared for a server player at `pos`. Change it before it is sent.
Side: server.

Return `Some` to set `result`; the first mod returning `Some` wins.
methods.signature: fn prepare_smithing(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut PrepareSmithingEvent<'_>) -> Option<item::item_stack::ItemStack>

methods.doc:
A projectile hit something (NeoForge's `ProjectileImpactEvent`, posted
where vanilla's projectile has found what it meets, before the hit
acts): `projectile` (its entity id) of type `kind` (`minecraft:arrow`),
shot by `owner` (a mob's or a player's entity id, 0 for none) in the level
`dimension`. It hit the entity `entity` of type `entity_kind` (a player is
`minecraft:player`; a dragon's part is `minecraft:ender_dragon`), or, with
`entity` None, the block at `block` on its `face` (the face's normal,
`[0, 1, 0]` for the top), at the point `at`. Set `canceled` and the impact
does not happen: no damage, no knockback, no sound, no block reaction, the
arrow does not stick, a pearl does not teleport, a potion or a fireball
does not burst. Cancellation leaves the projectile alive. A flying bobber
skips hooking and redirection to the hit point, but its ordinary move
still stops against solid blocks. Water is not an impact. Bobbers notify
before vanilla's entity deflection and world-border bounce; rockets notify
after deflection and cancellation skips their impact explosion only.
Covers arrows, tridents, thrown items, fireballs, wither skulls, wind
charges, llama spit, shulker bullets, bobbers and rockets. Other families
skip breeze deflections and hits on wind charges. A dragon part or End crystal is told by the id of the
dragon or crystal. Heard only when a mod also sets
`hears_projectile_impacts`. Server-side. Version 2 adds bobbers and rockets;
listeners retaining the earlier family set filter out `minecraft:fishing_bobber`
and `minecraft:firework_rocket`. Named injections request `hook_version = 2`.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `canceled`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn projectile_impact(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut ProjectileImpactEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
A server projectile was added to the level. `player` is set only for
a player launch; other sources have an empty `name`.
Side: server.

A raid wave has been spawned at `pos`; `wave` is its one-based wave
number and `raiders` counts the raiders, not the mobs they ride.
Side: server.

A server raid at `pos` changed to `state` (`triggered`, `victory`,
`loss` or `stopped`). `raid` identifies its owning level, including a
parked level. A terminal raid already removed from storage cannot be read.
Side: server.

Supply categories and vanilla-shaped displays for custom recipe types.
Asked lazily once per recipe table. Use the Host's recipe table to build
`RecipeBookCategory::displays` from the type's own opaque recipe JSON.
Each category names its menu, book identity and per-book search group.
The display/index load boundary returns typed errors; screen integration
is separate. This declaration does not register a settings book.
Side: both.

Items a mod's own recipe type takes in a station slot, added to the
recipe property sets (`RecipeManager.RECIPE_PROPERTY_SETS`): what a
furnace, blast furnace, smoker, campfire, smithing table slot or brewing
stand slot accepts, and what a client predicts it accepts. Push one
`RecipePropertyAddition` per set to add to; the vanilla recipes' own
items stay in. Called once per load, after the recipes are resolved, with
the `DataLoadContext` of the load that owns them (`origin()`
`ServerDataLoad` on a server, `ClientPreload` on a client's own load),
and again after `/reload`. A new namespaced key creates a set when its
namespace belongs to the listener's manifest (its ID or `namespaces`).
Later listeners may extend existing sets. Invalid or foreign new keys,
unknown vanilla keys, and air are logged and skipped; unknown items are
ignored. Custom sets are synced to clients alongside vanilla sets. The
answer must be the same every time.
Side: both.

Every mod gets `event.additions` in order and may add, change or remove additions.

Additional ingredient containers for server player `player` placing or checking a
recipe in the mod crafting menu `menu` (`namespace:path`) at `pos`. The player's
state is not swapped in. Push block positions to `sources`; containers are used
after the player's inventory, in mod order and then push order. The engine silently
skips `pos`, duplicates (first wins), unavailable or non-lendable containers, and
all containers after the first 64 accepted sources, without per-call logging.
Chest-like block entities and mod containers with declared slots are lendable.
No answer preserves vanilla placement. The engine takes ingredients and writes
changed containers back, firing `container_changed`; this hook only names sources.
Asked once per recipe-book placement/apply or server transfer check, not per tick.
Native and wasm listeners receive the same arguments and append to the same output.
Side: server.

Every mod gets `event.sources` in order and may add, change or remove sources.

The server's recipes of `recipe_types` arrived (NeoForge's
`RecipesReceivedEvent`): from now on the recipe helpers
(`native_recipes`, `native_recipes_of_type`) give the server's recipes
of those types in place of the window's own, so rebuild what you made
of them. It comes after a join, once the window has its player, and
after every `/reload`, on a server whose mods asked for them
(`native_datapack_sync`), single player included; with no types when
the server stopped sending them and the window is back on its own
recipes. A recipe's recipe book ids are not part of what arrives:
`recipe_book_ids` answers them. Client-side.
Side: client.
Once, at startup: attach this mod's parts (`let shaft = r.block_key("mymod:shaft"); r.block_part(shaft, Shaft)`).

The block-state definition types a mod adds (NeoForge's `RegisterBlockStateModels`,
its `registerDefinition`): push each type id, `<mod id>:<path>`. Asked once at start on
the client, before resources load. A blockstate file whose `neoforge:definition_type` is
a registered id has each state's model picked by `instantiate_block_state_definition`, on
every load and reload. An id in vanilla's namespace, not of that form, or registered
already is logged and left out.
Side: client.

Every mod gets `event.definitions` in order and may add, change or remove definitions.

The tint sources of blocks (NeoForge's `RegisterColorHandlersEvent.BlockTintSources`,
vanilla's `BlockColors.register`): `register(layers, blocks)`, and a model face with
`tintindex` i is multiplied by layer i of its block's list; a face past the list is not
tinted. A layer is one of vanilla's sources (`VanillaTint`) or the mod's own
`BlockTintSource`. Blocks are ids, a mod's or vanilla's, and a later registration for a
block replaces the earlier one, vanilla's own colours included. Asked once at start on the
client, before resources load; every resource load, a pack reload included, applies the
registrations again. An id no block has is logged and skipped.
Side: client.

Say which fluid, and how much, one of your cauldron blocks holds (NeoForge
`RegisterCauldronFluidContentEvent`), so the fluid capability (`FLUIDS`) fills and
drains it as it does vanilla's water and lava cauldrons. Asked once the block registry
is resolved, before any world opens, and again on a resource reload. Give
`event.contents.register(block, fluid, total, level)` the block and fluid keys your
`register` hook requested, the millibuckets the cauldron holds when full, and the name
of its integer level property, or none for a cauldron only ever full. The engine
refuses, with one logged warning naming both sides, a block that already has a content,
a fluid that already has a cauldron, an unknown block or fluid, a level property the
block lacks or that isn't an integer, and a total of 0 or one that doesn't divide
evenly by the levels; the rest of a mod's contents still apply.
Side: server.

Every mod gets `event.contents` in order and may add, change or remove contents.

Register cauldron item interactions, by exact item or by item tag, on both sides before
snapshot publication. Vanilla dye tags take precedence, then exact items, then item tags
in registration order; duplicate entries refuse preparation.
Side: both.

The client's own commands (NeoForge's `RegisterClientCommandsEvent`), which
`command` runs: push a `Command` per usage (`x <mode:word>`).
Asked when a connection starts and again when the server sends its
own tree, so the chat box colours, completes and lists them as the
game's own; a name the game already has keeps that command's
behaviour. A client command has no operator level: one with a nonzero
`level` is left out.
Side: client.

Every mod gets `event.commands` in order and may add, change or remove commands.

The colour resolvers block tints blend over the biomes around a block (NeoForge's
`RegisterColorHandlersEvent.ColorResolvers`): `register(resolver)` adds the mod's own
`BiomeColorResolver` and returns the `ColorResolver` its block tint sources pass to
`BlockAndTintGetter::block_tint`. The game blends a mod's resolver over the biome blend
radius and caches it per section while it meshes, as it does vanilla's grass, foliage and
water. Asked once at start on the client, before `register_block_tint_sources` and before
resources load.
Side: client.

The commands native mods add to the server's command tree: push
yours. Asked whenever the server builds its command tree, as the reference loader's
`Commands` does: when a world opens (a dedicated server, a LAN host, single player's
server thread), before its functions load, so a function line may name your command;
on each `/reload` and data pack change, so a command you stop pushing is refused by the
next functions loaded; and after a mod calls `host.commands().refresh_commands()`.
Every player's chat box completes them as vanilla's, within their level. A
name vanilla has is left out. Each executable usage keeps its own
permission level; a lower-level child only opens traversal through a
shared prefix, not execution of that prefix. An argument's kind is one
of `word`, `text`, `integer`, `number`, `boolean`, `player`, `item`,
`block_pos` and `vec3`, or a command argument type a mod registered
(`Registrar::register_command_argument`), named by its namespaced id.
Side: server.

Every mod gets `event.commands` in order and may add, change or remove commands.

The config files native mods keep (NeoForge's `registerConfig`):
push yours, each of a kind, with the text written to `config/` when
the file is missing. Asked by the window when the game starts (its
`Client` and `Common` configs), by a dedicated server when it starts
(`Common` and `Server`) and by a server before each world it opens
(`Server`); a game reads only its own kinds, so push them all every
time. Runs in Config: settings reads and the scoped ConfigFiles service
are available; world handles and transactions panic naming the phase. A file outside `config/`, or one already registered, is skipped.
Side: both.

Every mod gets `event.configs` in order and may add, change or remove configs.

The F3 debug entries a mod adds (NeoForge's `RegisterDebugEntriesEvent`): push a `DebugEntry`
per entry, its id `<mod id>:<path>` and the vanilla group its lines join. Asked once at start,
on the client. An id in vanilla's namespace, not of that form, or registered already is logged
and left out. Each entry is listed and switched on or off with vanilla's, and `debug_entry_lines`
fills it while it is on.
Side: client.

Every mod gets `event.entries` in order and may add, change or remove entries.

The world-space debug renderers a mod has now (NeoForge's `RegisterDebugRenderersEvent`): push a
`DebugRenderer` per renderer. Asked at each renderer list refresh, on the client.
Side: client.

Every mod gets `event.renderers` in order and may add, change or remove renderers.

Register loading screens once at client startup (NeoForge's
`RegisterDimensionTransitionScreenEvent`). Conditional source/destination pairs take
priority over incoming registrations, which take priority over outgoing registrations.
Duplicate transition registrations keep the first; invalid ids are logged and skipped.
An unmatched transition uses vanilla's screen and every screen uses the existing tracker.
Side: client.

Every mod gets `event.screens` in order and may add, change or remove screens.

Register namespaced enchantment damage value effects once before content loads.
Custom nodes in `minecraft:damage`, including nested `minecraft:all_of`, resolve to
these callbacks at load. Unknown identifiers reject the enchantment with a diagnostic.
Callbacks receive a read-only ServerHost, actual attacker and victim handles and the
pre-hit weapon snapshot. Vanilla nodes and requirements retain their traversal and RNG
order. This is vanilla EnchantmentHelper.modifyDamage, not an incoming-damage event.
Side: server.

Every mod gets `event.effects` in order and may add, change or remove effects.

The layers a mod adds to living entity renderers (NeoForge's
`EntityRenderersEvent.AddLayers`): `add(target, layer)`, and every living entity of the
type, or every player of the player model, in view draws `EntityRenderLayer::submit` after
its model and the layers added before. `entity_types`, `is_living`, `player_models` and
`has_mod_renderer` tell what renderers this load built. A target that is no living entity
type is refused by name. Asked on the client on every resource load, the first one and each
reload, after the renderers resolve (`register_entity_renderers`): layers don't carry over
from one load to the next, so add them again each time.
Side: client.

The code-defined renderers of entity types (NeoForge's
`EntityRenderersEvent.RegisterRenderers`, `registerEntityRenderer`): `register(type,
renderer)`, and every entity of the type `type` (`mymod:bolt`) in view is drawn by
`EntityRenderer::submit` in place of the type's own drawing. A later registration for a
type replaces the earlier one; a type the game does not know is logged with its id and
draws nothing new. Asked once at start on the client, before resources load; the game
resolves each type's renderer on every resource load. This build draws the registered
renderers of content mods' thrown types and of the living types drawn as mobs (in place of
the model and its vanilla layers); the other entity families keep their own drawing.
Side: client.

Register the screen effect spectating an entity type puts on, once at client startup
(NeoForge's `RegisterEntitySpectatorShadersEvent`), as vanilla's creeper, spider and
enderman do. The first registration for an entity type wins, vanilla's own counting as
first, so a mod can't change what the vanilla mobs show; a skipped or malformed
registration is logged. The effect applies while the first-person view follows that
entity, and the third-person view or leaving it clears it.
Side: client.

Every mod gets `event.shaders` in order and may add, change or remove shaders.

The models of your world fluids (NeoForge's `RegisterFluidModelsEvent`): push a
`mod_api::FluidModel` per fluid whose look doesn't say all of it. Its
sprites are block atlas textures, baked at every resource load from that pack's files; the
tint stays the look's. A fluid without one draws its look's sprite on every surface, or
water's textures when it has none. Asked at startup and on resource reload before baking, and
only on the client.
Side: client.

Every mod gets `event.models` in order and may add, change or remove models.

Register namespaced test functions before the world's test definitions load.
Each function runs with a ServerHost once per attempt in the real test level.
The runner retains ownership of retries, timeout and completion.
Side: server.

The HUD layers a mod adds among vanilla's (NeoForge's `RegisterGuiLayersEvent`): push a
`GuiLayer` per layer, its id `<mod id>:<path>` and its `GuiLayerPlacement`. Asked once at
start, on the client. `gui_layer_draw` draws each layer, between `gui_layer_pre` and
`gui_layer_post` like a vanilla layer, so other mods can hide it or draw around it.
Side: client.

Every mod gets `event.layers` in order and may add, change or remove layers.

The item model node types a mod adds (NeoForge's `RegisterItemModelsEvent`): push each
type id, `<mod id>:<path>`. Asked once at start on the client, before resources load. An
item definition's node whose `type` is a registered id draws, per stack, the named models
`item_model_update` answers. An id in vanilla's namespace, not of that form, or registered
already is logged and left out.
Side: client.

Every mod gets `event.models` in order and may add, change or remove models.

The item tint sources a mod adds (NeoForge's `RegisterColorHandlersEvent.ItemTintSources`):
push each id, `<mod id>:<path>`. Asked once at start on the client, before resources load.
An entry in a `minecraft:model`'s `tints` whose `type` is a registered id colours its
`tintindex` with what `item_tint_source` answers per stack, also after a resource reload. An id
in vanilla's namespace, not of that form, or registered already is logged and left out; a
tint source nobody registers draws white.
Side: client.

Every mod gets `event.sources` in order and may add, change or remove sources.

The animation targets and interpolations a mod adds for keyframe animation files to name
(NeoForge's `RegisterJsonAnimationTypesEvent`): push each id, `<namespace>:<path>`, as a
`JsonAnimationType::Target` or `JsonAnimationType::Interpolation`. Asked once at start on
the client, before resources load. An id in vanilla's namespace, not of that form, or
registered already as the same kind is logged and left out.
Side: client.

Each mod receives its own empty `event.types` batch; every entry it adds is recorded
as that mod's.

Entity model layers built in code (NeoForge's
`EntityRenderersEvent.RegisterLayerDefinitions`): push each one's id,
`<mod id>:<model>#<layer>` as a `ModelLayerLocation` names it
(`mymod:golem#main`), and its `LayerDefinition`, as the mod's
`createBodyLayer()` builds it. `native_bake_layer` bakes one into the
`ModelPart` tree `native_draw_model_part` draws. Asked once at start,
on the client. An id in vanilla's namespace, not of that form, or
registered already is logged and left out. API @API:model_layers@.
Side: client.

Every mod gets `event.layers` in order and may add, change or remove layers.

Register named conditions once at mod load, before server data admission.
Each handler is a raw-JSON handler: it reads the condition's JSON value.
Names must belong to the registering mod's namespace. Native and wasm
