handlers use the same registration and evaluation route. Registering one
name owns that namespace; an unknown condition in it refuses data reload.
Foreign unknown ids omit their file with one ERROR-level log entry,
even inside `or(true, unknown)`; every combinator branch is visited.
Side: server.

Every mod gets `event.conditions` in order and may add, change or remove conditions.

The model loaders a mod adds (NeoForge's `ModelEvent.RegisterLoaders`): push each loader
id, `<mod id>:<path>`. Asked once at start on the client, before resources load. A model
whose `loader` is a registered id gets the quads `bake_model_loader` answers, baked with
its elements, on every load and reload. An id in vanilla's namespace, not of that form, or
registered already is logged and left out.
Side: client.

Every mod gets `event.loaders` in order and may add, change or remove loaders.

The render groups a mod's particles draw in (NeoForge's `RegisterParticleGroupsEvent`): push a
`ParticleGroup` per group, its id `<mod id>:<path>`, how it blends and the particle types in
it. Asked once at start, on the client, before resources load; the game resolves each
type's group when the particle sprite sets load, on every resource load as well. An id in
vanilla's namespace, not of that form, or registered already is logged and left out.
Side: client.

Every mod gets `event.groups` in order and may add, change or remove groups.

The code-defined particle providers of a mod's own particle types (NeoForge's
`RegisterParticleProvidersEvent`): `register(name, provider)`, and every particle of the
type `name` (`ParticleOptions::named("mymod:spark")`) is moved each tick by
`ParticleProvider::tick`. The sprite set and the declarative spawn values stay in
`assets/<namespace>/particles/<path>.json`. A later registration for a name replaces the
earlier one; a name no sprite set matches is logged and draws nothing. Asked once at start
on the client, before resources load; the game resolves each type's provider when the
sprite sets load, on every resource load as well.
Side: client.

Register client screens for world-preset keys once at startup. The first
registration for a key wins. Invalid ids are refused. Unregistered presets
retain their built-in editor, or their disabled Customize button.
Side: client.

Every mod gets `event.editors` in order and may add, change or remove editors.

The numeric item model properties a mod adds (NeoForge's
`RegisterRangeSelectItemModelPropertyEvent`): push each id, `<mod id>:<path>`. Asked once at
start on the client, before resources load. A `minecraft:range_dispatch` naming a registered
property thresholds on the number `item_model_range_property` answers per stack, also after a
resource reload. An id in vanilla's namespace, not of that form, or registered already is
logged and left out; a property nobody registers reads 0.
Side: client.

Every mod gets `event.properties` in order and may add, change or remove properties.

Register the mod's own render pipelines, once at client startup (NeoForge's
`RegisterRenderPipelinesEvent`; 1.21.1 mods used `RegisterShadersEvent`): push a
[`RenderPipeline`] for each into `event.pipelines`. The game builds them with its own at
startup and again on every resource reload. An id outside the mod's namespaces, one an
earlier registration took are logged with the mod and
dropped. A required pipeline whose shader is missing or doesn't build fails the load: the
game does not start, and a reload fails and keeps the previous resources. An
[optional](RenderPipeline::optional()) one is logged and resolves to
[`RenderPipelineError::Invalid`].
Side: client.

Every mod gets `event.pipelines` in order and may add, change or remove pipelines.

Collect static, mod-generated PNGs for the block and GUI atlases. Called at
first client load and every resource reload, before textures are stitched.
Side: client.

Every mod gets `event.sprites` in order and may add, change or remove sprites.

The categorical item model properties a mod adds (NeoForge's
`RegisterSelectItemModelPropertyEvent`): push each id, `<mod id>:<path>`. Asked once at start
on the client, before resources load. A `minecraft:select` naming a registered property picks
the case whose `when` string equals what `item_model_select_property` answers per stack, also
after a resource reload. An id in vanilla's namespace, not of that form, or registered already
is logged and left out; a select on a property nobody registers draws its fallback.
Side: client.

Every mod gets `event.properties` in order and may add, change or remove properties.

The special item model types a mod draws (NeoForge's `RegisterSpecialModelRendererEvent`):
`register(type, renderer)`, and every `minecraft:special` item model whose `model` object
has the type `type` (`mymod:skillet`) is drawn by `SpecialModelRenderer::extract`. A later
registration of a type replaces the earlier one, vanilla's types included, and the log
names both mods. Asked once at start on the client, before resources load; a special
model of a type no mod registered and vanilla doesn't have is an error naming it, and its
item draws the missing model.
Side: client.

The atlas sprite source types a mod adds (NeoForge's `RegisterSpriteSourcesEvent`): push
each type id, `<mod id>:<path>`. Asked once at start on the client, before resources load.
An entry of an atlas definition's `sources` whose `type` is a registered id is answered by
`sprite_source` at its place in the list, on every load and reload. An id in vanilla's
namespace, not of that form, or registered already is logged and left out.
Side: client.

Every mod gets `event.sources` in order and may add, change or remove sources.

Declare atlases beside the game's (`RegisterTextureAtlasesEvent`), each with the atlas
definition that lists its sprites. Called at first client load and every resource reload,
before textures are stitched.
Side: client.

Every mod gets `event.atlases` in order and may add, change or remove atlases.

Declare villager professions once per mod load, before world admission.
The engine resolves every reference atomically with the owning resource tables.
Vanilla replacement and overlapping custom acquisition POIs are refused.
NeoForge adds a profession through `RegisterEvent` on `Registries.VILLAGER_PROFESSION`;
this hook declares it as data, so only the registration moment corresponds.
Side: server.

Every mod gets `event.professions` in order and may add, change or remove professions.

A player submitted a command whose root appears in the mod command tree
and whose root permission the player meets. The player's state is in place.
This runs before argument parsing, so listeners that own the root can apply
their own syntax and subcommand permissions. Return `Flow::Cancel` once
handled. Otherwise the command goes through ordinary parsing and resolution.
The text has no leading slash and is untrusted. Console, function and
nested `execute` invocations use the regular command path.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `ran`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn registered_player_command(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut RegisteredPlayerCommandEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
Before this window's player's first-person `left` or right arm is
drawn (`RenderArmEvent`, in `renderPlayerArm` and `renderMapHand`):
the empty main hand's arm, and the arms under a held map, never while
the player is invisible. `player` and `player_entity_id` are the
local player's UUID and entity id. `draw`'s pose stack starts at the
arm model's origin, in blocks, posed as vanilla's arm is (with any
`render_hand`), lit with the light at the eyes; add
geometry with `native_draw_cube`, `native_draw_quad`, `native_draw_block`
and `native_draw_item`. Set `canceled` to leave out vanilla's arm;
what the mods drew stays. Client-side.
Side: client.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `canceled`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.

Final world fog, after the computed color hook, ordinary calculations and Horizon's fog
option, before upload. Title panoramas skip it. Invalid color or distance values retain the
original whole fog.
Side: client.

Once a frame, in a world or not, right after the frame was rendered
(NeoForge's `RenderFrameEvent.Post`). `elapsed` is the frame's time. It
fires for a frame that was skipped too; `flip_frame` is the moment a
frame was presented. `world_partial_tick` is the interpolation used by
that frame, held while paused or frozen; `partial_tick` is the advancing
window clock. Outside a world both use the window clock. Neither is
recomputed after listeners run. Client-side.
Side: client.

Once a frame, in a world or not, after Horizon's extras and just before
the frame is rendered (NeoForge's `RenderFrameEvent.Pre`). `elapsed` is
the frame's time. `world_partial_tick` is the interpolation about to be
drawn, held while paused or frozen; `partial_tick` is the window clock,
which keeps advancing. Outside a world both use the window clock.
Listener writes do not change this frame's captured interpolation. Client-side.
Side: client.

The HUD (not drawn under F1), after the minimap (NeoForge's
`RenderGuiEvent.Post`): place a box with `corners.place` (boxes stack
away from their edge) and draw it with `native_fill` and `native_text`.
Skip a corner `host.native_corner_shown` says F3 takes. Not heard when a mod
canceled `render_gui_pre`. Client-side.
Side: client.

Before the in-world HUD is drawn (NeoForge's `RenderGuiEvent.Pre`):
return `Flow::Cancel` and none of it is, as under F1: no vanilla layer (and so
no `gui_layer_pre` or `gui_layer_post`), no `render_gui_post`, and no
chat or toasts. Fires once a frame in a world, not under F1 and not
while a server dialog or the connection screen covers the window.
Client-side.
Side: client.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `canceled`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.

Before one first-person hand of this window's player is drawn
(`RenderHandEvent`, client): a hand that holds an item or a map, the
empty main hand's arm, and the empty off hand, where vanilla draws
nothing. Adjust `render`'s pose, draw in the hand with `draw`, or
cancel the default geometry; what the mods drew stays. Equip progress
includes the item's swap scale. `draw`'s pose stack starts in the
hands' view space, in blocks, +x right, +y up, -z into the screen,
under the hand sway and before vanilla's per-item transforms; both
hands share it, and `render.hand` says which one is asked. It is lit
with the light at the eyes; add geometry with `native_draw_cube`,
`native_draw_quad`, `native_draw_block` and `native_draw_item`. It
joins the hand's own vertices, ahead of vanilla's: the hand's field of
view, the view bob, a shader pack's hand pass and `hand_drawn`
see it as they see vanilla's hand. Unlike NeoForge, the pose stack is
`draw`'s own: turning it moves what you draw, `render`'s pose moves
the default geometry, and player render state is not exposed.
Side: client.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `canceled`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.

Before a visible item frame's item or map is drawn. Cancel hides the item, not the frame.
Side: client.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `canceled`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.

Draw world geometry at one stage of a world view (NeoForge 26.3's
`RenderLevelStageEvent`), asked for each `RenderLevelStage` in frame order. `draw` is
the view's `WorldDrawContext` and shares its limits with `submit_custom_geometry`; its
lines and quads draw at `stage`. Client-only, noncancellable.
Side: client.

After a living entity is drawn (NeoForge's `RenderLivingEvent.Post`): once a frame for each
mob and player in view whose `render_living_pre` wasn't canceled, after its model, its vanilla
layers and the mods' layers. `entity` is its render state, as `render_living_pre` has it;
`draw` is posed at its feet, turned with its body, and what it draws is kept. `parts` is a
humanoid model's parts as vanilla posed them this frame (`HumanoidModel.setupAnim`), taken
from the body's own draw, so a part a pre hook hid reads as not visible; read-only: attach
geometry to an arm or the head without animating it again; None for a model that isn't
humanoid. The order today: before this hook its model, its vanilla layers and the mods'
layers are drawn; after it, in the frame's later passes, its name tag, its leash, its
flames and its shadow (the reference draws the leash and the name tag first, arismoko/horizon#3915). A type
with a mod's registered renderer (`register_entity_renderers`) has its own model's order,
the renderer in the model's place, so it changes with arismoko/horizon#3915 and not before. For a player,
its `render_player_post` follows.
Side: client.

Before a living entity is drawn (NeoForge's `RenderLivingEvent.Pre`): once a frame for each
mob and player in view (one the frame culls is not asked), before its pose, model and
layers. `entity` is its render state (its id, kind, custom name, the frame's partial tick,
its body and head turns and walk cycle, `LivingEntityRenderState`). `draw` is posed at its
feet, turned with its body: +z the way it faces, +x its left, +y up, in blocks, with the
helpers block entities draw with (`cube`, `quad`, `block`, `item`, `model_part`); what it
draws is kept. Set `canceled` to skip all of the entity's drawing this frame: its model,
armour, held items and layers, the mods' layers, its name tag, shadow, flames, leash and
glowing outline, and `render_living_post`, and the renderer a mod registered for its type
(`register_entity_renderers`), which draws in the model's place; a mod drawing a model of
its own draws it here and cancels. A player's `render_player_pre` comes first, and a cancel here still asks its
`render_player_post`. Left uncanceled, `hidden.hide_named(name)` leaves only the part of
that name out of the vanilla model this frame (a villager's `nose`), drawn on the CPU or the
GPU: a hidden part takes its children with it and leaves the layers drawn on the model itself
(`getParentModel()`: a villager's type, profession and level, a spider's eyes), while its
armour, held items and other layers keep every part. An entity is drawn afresh each frame:
`draw.keep()` does nothing here.
Side: client.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `canceled`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.

Name tag visibility and optional replacement text.
Side: client.

After a player is drawn (NeoForge's `RenderPlayerEvent.Post`): once a frame for each player
whose `render_player_pre` wasn't canceled, after its `render_living_post`, or right after its
`render_living_pre` when only that one was canceled. `player`, `who` and `draw` are as
`render_player_pre` has them, and what it draws is kept; `parts` are the posed parts
`render_living_post` gets, None when the living pre hook was canceled. The player's name tag, leash,
flames and shadow are drawn after it, as `render_living_post` says.
Side: client.

Before a player is drawn (NeoForge's `RenderPlayerEvent.Pre`): once a frame for each other
player in view and for this window's player in third person (and F5 front view), before its
`render_living_pre`. `player` is its render state, `who` its profile name and whether it is
this window's own player, and `draw` the frame `render_living_pre` gets. Set `canceled` to
skip all of the player's drawing this frame, `render_living_pre`, `render_living_post` and
`render_player_post` included. Left uncanceled, `hidden.hide(part)` (or
`hidden.hide_named(name)`) leaves only that part out of the vanilla model this frame (after
Skin Customization), as a mod drawing its own outer skin layer does: a hidden part takes its
children with it (the hat goes with the head), while its armour, held items and other
layers, the cape among them, keep every part.
Side: client.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `canceled`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.

`RenderTooltipEvent.GatherComponents`: the elements of `stack`'s
tooltip (`ItemStack.getTooltipLines` as text lines, then the image
component its item's `tooltip_component` part answered), once
`item_tooltip` has run and before any wrapping or measuring. Add,
change, reorder or remove elements; the lines draw in order, then the
images in order, under any bundle's contents. `max_width` starts at -1,
no limit, which leaves the lines as they are; a mod that sets it
wraps every line wider than that, in GUI pixels. Set `cancel` and
nothing is drawn, and no `render_tooltip_texture` is asked. Asked each frame
the tooltip shows, never for one the stack hides. Client-side.
Side: client.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.

`RenderTooltipEvent.Pre`: a tooltip, laid out and about to be placed and drawn. `place`
holds the point it hangs from in GUI pixels (the cursor, or the point the screen gives
it), before the tooltip positioner adds its offset and keeps the box on screen; set `x`
and `y` to move it. `screen_width` and `screen_height` are the screen's size. `elements` are its text lines, then its images, as `render_tooltip_gather_components`
left them (a tooltip with no item has only lines), and are read-only here. `stack` is the
item the tooltip describes, `None` for a text tooltip. Set `cancel` and nothing is drawn,
and no `render_tooltip_texture` is asked. Asked each frame a tooltip shows, only while a mod listens.
`draw` is the tooltip's GUI drawing context. Custom drawing stays visible even when
the tooltip is cancelled; `draw.gui_draw_item_with` draws a stack with optional count text.
Client-side.
Side: client.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.

`RenderTooltipEvent.Texture`: the look of a tooltip box about to be drawn. Set `texture`
to a tooltip style (`<namespace>:<name>`) and the box draws as vanilla draws a
`tooltip_style`: the GUI sprites `<namespace>:tooltip/<name>_background` and
`<namespace>:tooltip/<name>_frame` from the resource packs, each nine-sliced as its
`gui.scaling` says or stretched without one. A style whose background or frame no pack
has keeps the fills, where vanilla draws the missing texture. Left `None`, the box is
Horizon's solid fills, in `background` and the `border_top` to `border_bottom` gradient,
as ARGB. `stack` is the item the tooltip describes, `None` for a text tooltip. Asked each
frame a tooltip shows, only while a mod listens. Client-side.
Side: client.

A once-a-frame sample of the replay's clock, on a frame it moved: `position_ms` is where
it is now, in ms from the recording's start (0 to its length), after the recording's
packets up to there were processed in order (a packet the game cannot decode or apply
is skipped). Not heard on a frame the clock stood still (paused,
at the end, or the frame it opened on, which `replay_opened` tells of). After a seek,
the next one is heard on the frame the seek is first drawn, with exactly the position
the seek applied, even when that is where the clock already was; the clock runs on from
there on the frame after. For a timeline or a camera path that follows playback.

Its event's fields are fixed: on the wire every field is encoded and its layout hashed,
so adding one later breaks wasm mods built against this one; `#[non_exhaustive]` is for
Rust callers only (docs/modding/src/concepts/wire-types.md).
Side: client.

The replay of `recording` closed, whatever closed it: a mod's `replay_close`, Escape,
the pause menu's Disconnect, or another replay opening over it. Heard once, after
the replay is gone (`host.replay_state()` is none, or already the next replay's
only after its `replay_opened`) and before a standalone replay's world is left.

Its event's fields are fixed: on the wire every field is encoded and its layout hashed,
so adding one later breaks wasm mods built against this one; `#[non_exhaustive]` is for
Rust callers only (docs/modding/src/concepts/wire-types.md).
Side: client.

A `replay_open` the game accepted opened nothing: `request` is the id the call
returned, `recording` the id it was asked for, `error` why:
- `Superseded`: a later `replay_open` replaced it before the game took up its read
  recording;
- `Unreadable`: the recording turned out damaged or of another version once read;
- `WorldBusy`: a world was joined, left or opened, or the replay playing closed or
  replaced, before it was ready, or another world entry took its place while it waited;
- `Unavailable`: the replay's session couldn't start, the game began closing, the
  person cancelled the wait for it (Escape while the world loads), or the replay playing
  kept its place: the camera path edited in it couldn't be saved, or the editor saved
  into the very archive this request read (which holds it as it was before).

Every accepted request ends in exactly one `replay_opened` or `replay_open_failed` with
its id; only a game closing first promises neither. A single-player world already left
for the replay stays left; anything else stays as it was.

Its event's fields are fixed: on the wire every field is encoded and its layout hashed,
so adding one later breaks wasm mods built against this one; `#[non_exhaustive]` is for
Rust callers only (docs/modding/src/concepts/wire-types.md).
Side: client.

A replay is open and its first frame is set up: `recording` is its id (as
`replay_open` takes it; empty for a recording no id names), `duration_ms` its length,
`standalone` whether it owns its session, and `request` the id `replay_open` returned
for the mod request that opened it, or 0 for a replay opened any other way (the
replays list, `/studio replay open`, the control socket). Heard for every opening, and
only once the recording has been read: one that can't be played opens nothing and is
not heard of here (a mod's request hears `replay_open_failed`). `host.replay_state()`
reads the replay from here on. A replay opened over another one is heard after
`replay_closed` of that one.

Its event's fields are fixed: on the wire every field is encoded and its layout hashed,
so adding one later breaks wasm mods built against this one; `#[non_exhaustive]` is for
Rust callers only (docs/modding/src/concepts/wire-types.md).
Side: client.

A server player's client answered a resource pack in play (vanilla's
`ServerboundResourcePackPacket`): `status` is `Action`'s number, 0
successfully loaded, 1 declined, 2 failed download, 3 accepted, 4
downloaded, 5 invalid URL, 6 failed reload, 7 discarded. Heard when the
packet arrives, after the server has handled it; it cannot be stopped.
The player's state is swapped in, so the helpers and `PlayerRef::tell`
work. The pack a dedicated server offers in the configuration
(`resource-pack` in `server.properties`) is answered before the
player has joined, and those answers are not heard. Once for each
answer, on a server.
Side: server.

A player right clicks a block (NeoForge's
`PlayerInteractEvent.RightClickBlock`): once per hand, where
`useItemOn` starts, on the clicking client and on the server (`click`
says which, with the block, the hit, the hand and its stack, and the
player), for a spectator too (the server then only lets one open a
menu). Before the block's own use (a chest, a door, a lever) and the
item's (`Item.useOn`, `native_use_on`).

`use_block`: False skips; True overrides sneak; Default skips when sneaking with either hand full
(sneaking still blocks use when both stacks bypass sneak use). `use_item`: False skips; True forces
even an empty hand or cooldown; Default requires a held stack off cooldown. Empty hands reach
ItemAfterBlock with no stack, but no item Part. Adventure restrictions still apply; block consumption ends the click. Cancelling
skips both and answers `cancellation_result` in their place:
`Pass` (the default) goes on to the item's own use (`Item.use`) and
then the other hand, `Fail` ends the click, and `Success`,
`SuccessServer` or `Consume` end it as used, with the swing they name.
A spectator never reaches item use after a `Pass`; the client goes
straight to the other hand instead.
A mod that keeps players out of land cancels with `Fail`.
On the server, a consuming result fires `any_block_use` once, including
a consuming cancel. The inner criteria are skipped by cancellation unless
the mod explicitly triggers them; the helpers fire only their named criterion.
A consuming item phase fires `item_used_on_block` with the pre-block
snapshot (including an empty hand) before the outer criterion.
The outer criterion sees the stack held when block use started, with the
action's own in-place changes: consumption, damage, component edits, and
the creative-mode count restore. It sees an empty stack if the action
used it up. Neither a listener's hand replacement nor the action's whole
replacement (such as a bucket becoming a water bucket) changes this original.
This matches vanilla, which passes the same stack object it read before
the action. Single player uses this same server contract.
Item-internal triggers (such as shears) can legitimately
fire `item_used_on_block` in addition to the game mode's trigger.
Side: both.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `canceled`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.

The local player right-clicks empty space with an empty `hand`.
Client-side only; the server does not receive this event.
Side: client.

`PlayerInteractEvent.RightClickItem`, immediately before `Item.use`.
Cancel skips its Part and vanilla behaviour; its result defaults to
`Pass`. `Success`, `SuccessServer` and `Consume` end the client's
hand loop. `Success` swings on the client, `SuccessServer` on the
server, and `Consume` has no swing.
Side: both.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `canceled`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.

Execute a parsed mod command after permission checks and argument resolution.
Return `Flow::Cancel` when handled. `source` identifies origin and permission,
independent of `execute as`. Feedback honours silence, track-output and the swapped-in player.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `ran`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn run_mod_command(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut RunModCommandEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
A task a mod scheduled with `schedule_task` is due, at the start of the server tick it
was due on, after `server_tick`'s start phase, in the order the tasks were scheduled.
`id` is the id `schedule_task` returned, `owner` the `[mod] id` of the mod that scheduled
it and `token` the value it passed. Every mod is asked about every task, so a mod ignores
tasks it does not own. Server-side.
Side: server.

A typed character that no text box took (`ScreenEvent.CharacterTyped.Post`, vanilla's `Screen.charTyped` returning false), once per printable character that `screen_char_typed_pre` let through: `c` and `modifiers` as there. Set `canceled` and it counts as handled (nothing further reads it, so it changes nothing). It does not fire for text a box took, nor on Options and the title's own screens, where the key's text is routed in place between their boxes. A held edit modifier makes the key a shortcut, so its character is not taken and fires it. Same screens as the key press. Fires on the window only, while a screen of the game's or the title's is open (the screens the `_pre` input hooks cover), for real mouse or keyboard input and not a pad's or the keyboard focus's, and only when the matching Pre did not cancel it. It fires on the screen open after the key acted, as for the Pre.
Side: client.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `canceled`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.

A character was typed at the open screen
(`ScreenEvent.CharacterTyped.Pre`, vanilla's `Screen.charTyped`):
`screen` is the screen it is, `c` the character, `modifiers` GLFW's
bits (shift 1, control 2, alt 4, super 8), and `field` a copy of the
focused text box. Set `canceled` and that one character never reaches
a text box.

`field` is `None` with no box focused, and for the boxes that keep
their own validators: Options' and World Options' fields, the game
rules' and the block editor's. `cursor` and `highlight` count Unicode
scalar characters, and a character sees the box as the one before it
left it. Change `value`, `cursor` or `highlight` and the box takes the
change, cancelled or not, so cancel to replace the character yourself.
New text goes through the box's own filter and length limit, and what
follows the box (chat suggestions, a search's results, the anvil's
name) follows it. `max_length`, `multiline` and whether `field` is
`None` stay the box's: a change to them does nothing.

It fires once per printable character of a key press's text and once
per character of the input method's committed text, never for a control
character (Enter, Backspace, Tab, Delete, Escape, a Control letter):
those are keys, and the game reads them as keys, not as text. A key's
characters fire after the key has acted, as GLFW's char callback comes
after its key callback (`KeyboardHandler.charTyped`): `screen` is the
screen open then, so a key that closes the screen (the inventory key)
leaves none to hear its character, where vanilla's closed screen hears
nothing, and one that moves the focus types into the box it moved to.
They fire even when `screen_key_pressed_pre` cancelled the press
that carried the text, as NeoForge delivers `CharacterTyped.Pre` for a
cancelled `KeyPressed.Pre`: the characters left reach the text box
without the key's own effects. Cancelling one character drops only that
one. The control socket's `type` fires it too, but not for its `\b`
backspace. Same screens as the key press, and it fires with no text box
focused (there is nothing to take the character then).
Side: client.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `canceled`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.

The `screen` that was open is being replaced (`ScreenEvent.Closing`), after `screen_opening` let it.
Side: client.

The hook `native_screen_exclusion` asks: a mod adds the rectangles it
draws over `screen` (a side panel, a button column) to `areas`, in GUI
pixels, `[x, y, width, height]`. NeoForge has no counterpart in the
game; recipe viewers ask for it through their own API
(`EmiExclusionArea`, JEI's `IGuiContainerHandler.getGuiExtraAreas`).
Client-side.
Side: client.

Every mod gets `event.areas` in order and may add, change or remove areas.

A screen was observed opening or changing rectangle, at most once per frame
(`ScreenEvent.Init.Post`).
Side: client.

A key press that no screen took (`ScreenEvent.KeyPressed.Post`, vanilla's `Screen.keyPressed` returning false): `key`, `repeat` and `modifiers` as in `screen_key_pressed_pre`. Set `canceled` and the press counts as handled: the game's own key handling (its key bindings, hotbar and toggles) never sees it. It does not fire for a key a screen took (a text box, the focus keys, Escape-close, an inventory key, a merchant or recipe-book key). A key that has no vanilla name fires nothing. The control socket's `key` fires it too, for a press (never a release). Fires on the window only, while a screen of the game's or the title's is open (the screens the `_pre` input hooks cover), for real mouse or keyboard input and not a pad's or the keyboard focus's, and only when the matching Pre did not cancel it. It fires on the screen open after the game handled the input, so an input that closed the screen fires nothing.
Side: client.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `canceled`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.

A key went down over the open screen (`ScreenEvent.KeyPressed.Pre`,
vanilla's `Screen.keyPressed`): `screen` is the screen it is, `key`
vanilla's name for the key (`key.keyboard.e`) — a key with no name
fires nothing — `repeat` whether it is
the keyboard's auto-repeat of a held press (Horizon's extra; NeoForge
folds repeats into the event), and `modifiers` GLFW's bits (shift 1,
control 2, alt 4, super 8). Set `canceled` and the press goes no
further: no focus move, no Escape-close, no inventory or hotbar key, no
typing by the key itself.

It fires for the window's presses and their repeats, and for the
control socket's `key` (a release fires nothing), after the window's
own shortcuts have run — the fullscreen and screenshot keys, the debug
keys and the narrator — and while a screen of the game's or the title's
is open (Options and the pack list opened from the title screen count,
with no player and no `menu`; the title's own). It does
not fire on the connect and loading screens, nor for a server dialog, the server pack,
link and code-of-conduct prompts, a book or a sign editor drawn over
gameplay, nor while a world loads or saves: the key there stays the
game's own. A cancelled press's release still runs, and its characters
are GLFW's separate char callback and still come; see
`screen_char_typed_pre`.
Side: client.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `canceled`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.

A key release that no screen took (`ScreenEvent.KeyReleased.Post`, vanilla's `Screen.keyReleased` returning false): `key` and `modifiers` as in `screen_key_released_pre`. Set `canceled` and the release counts as handled: the game's own key handling never sees it, so a held mapping stays down; cancel a release only when you cancelled the press it ends. Fires on the window only, while a screen of the game's or the title's is open (the screens the `_pre` input hooks cover), for real mouse or keyboard input and not a pad's or the keyboard focus's, and only when the matching Pre did not cancel it. It fires on the screen open after the game handled the input, so an input that closed the screen fires nothing.
Side: client.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `canceled`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.

Before an open screen handles a named key's release (same screen gate as key presses).
Cancel bypasses screen handling; physical keys and mapped keyboard hold/toggle state release.
Side: client.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `canceled`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.

A mouse button went down over the open screen and the screen has handled it (`ScreenEvent.MouseButtonPressed.Post`, vanilla's `Screen.mouseClicked` returning): `screen`, `button` and `modifiers` as in `screen_mouse_button_pressed_pre`. Not cancellable. NeoForge's event also carries `wasClickHandled` / `wasReleaseHandled`; this one has no such field, because Horizon's screens take their input in their own arms and report nothing back. There is no double-click flag: Horizon does not track double clicks. Fires on the window only, while a screen of the game's or the title's is open (the screens the `_pre` input hooks cover), for real mouse or keyboard input and not a pad's or the keyboard focus's, and only when the matching Pre did not cancel it. It fires on the screen open after the screen's arms ran, so a press that closed the screen fires nothing.
Side: client.

A mouse button went down over the open screen
(`ScreenEvent.MouseButtonPressed.Pre`, vanilla's
`Screen.mouseClicked`): `screen` is the screen it is, `screen.mouse`
where the pointer is (so there is no position of its own), `button` the
button's GLFW index (0 left, 1 right, 2 middle, 3 back, 4 forward; a
button past those is the platform's own number, which differs between
systems) and `modifiers` GLFW's bits (shift 1, control 2,
alt 4, super 8). Set `canceled` and the press goes no further: no slot,
no screen button, no drag, no hotbar key, no sort or header button.

It fires before anything the screen does with the press, on the window
only, and while a screen of the game's or the title's is open (Options
and the pack list opened from the title screen count, with no player
and no `menu`; the title's own screens, their
`screen.id` from the title state machine). It does not fire on the
connect and loading screens, nor for a server
dialog, the server pack, link and code-of-conduct prompts, a book or a
sign editor drawn over gameplay, nor while a world loads or saves: the
click there stays the game's own. A gamepad click or a click the
keyboard's focus sends is not the mouse and fires nothing.
Side: client.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `canceled`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.

A mouse button went up over the open screen and the screen has handled it (`ScreenEvent.MouseButtonReleased.Post`, vanilla's `Screen.mouseReleased` returning), with the fields of `screen_mouse_button_released_pre`. Not cancellable. NeoForge's event also carries `wasClickHandled` / `wasReleaseHandled`; this one has no such field, because Horizon's screens take their input in their own arms and report nothing back. Fires on the window only, while a screen of the game's or the title's is open (the screens the `_pre` input hooks cover), for real mouse or keyboard input and not a pad's or the keyboard focus's, and only when the matching Pre did not cancel it. It fires on the screen open after the screen's arms ran, so a release that closed the screen fires nothing.
Side: client.

A mouse button went up over the open screen
(`ScreenEvent.MouseButtonReleased.Pre`, vanilla's
`Screen.mouseReleased`), with the same `screen`, `button` and
`modifiers` as `screen_mouse_button_pressed_pre` and fired at
the same point. Set `canceled` and the release goes no further: a
pressed slot keeps what it took and no drag, slider or scrollbar lets
go.

Cancel a release only when the press it ends was cancelled too: a
release the screen took ends the drag or the scroll it began, as it
does in vanilla, and no guard here un-cancels it. Same screens as the
press; a press that opened another screen ends on that one.
Side: client.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `canceled`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.

A held-button pointer movement has gone through the open screen's drag handlers (`ScreenEvent.MouseDragged.Post`, vanilla's `Screen.mouseDragged`): `button`, `delta` (GUI pixels, `screen.mouse` the new position) and `modifiers` as in `screen_mouse_dragged_pre`. Not cancellable. Horizon's drag handlers report nothing back, so it fires whether or not one of them used the drag. Fires on the window only, while a screen of the game's or the title's is open (the screens the `_pre` input hooks cover), for real mouse or keyboard input and not a pad's or the keyboard focus's, and only when the matching Pre did not cancel it. It fires on the screen open after the game handled the input, so an input that closed the screen fires nothing.
Side: client.

Before a real held-button movement reaches screen drag handlers.
`screen.mouse` is the current GUI position; `delta` is its GUI-space movement.
Cancel keeps the new cursor position but skips all screen drag handlers.
Side: client.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `canceled`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.

The wheel turned over the open screen and the screen's scroll handlers have run (`ScreenEvent.MouseScrolled.Post`, vanilla's `Screen.mouseScrolled`): `scroll` and `modifiers` as in `screen_mouse_scrolled_pre`. Not cancellable. Horizon's scroll handlers report nothing back, so it fires whether or not one of them scrolled. Fires on the window only, while a screen of the game's or the title's is open (the screens the `_pre` input hooks cover), for real mouse or keyboard input and not a pad's or the keyboard focus's, and only when the matching Pre did not cancel it. It fires on the screen open after the game handled the input, so an input that closed the screen fires nothing.
Side: client.

The wheel turned over the open screen (`ScreenEvent.MouseScrolled.Pre`,
vanilla's `Screen.mouseScrolled`): `screen` is the screen it is,
`screen.mouse` where the pointer is (so there is no position of its
own), `scroll` the wheel's movement in x and y as the game's own scroll
handler scales it (a line times the wheel sensitivity: with Discrete
Scrolling on, a notch is ±1, its sign only; a touchpad's pixels are
divided by 30), and
`modifiers` GLFW's bits (shift 1, control 2, alt 4, super 8). Set
`canceled` and nothing the screen would scroll moves: not the bundle
under the pointer, nor a list, slider, scrollbar or map. Nothing else
reads the wheel while a screen of the game's is open, so no hotbar slot
changes either.

It fires before the screen scrolls anything, for the window's wheel
(horizon-ctl's `scroll-at` sends it through the window too), and
while a screen of the game's or the title's is open (Options and the
pack list opened from the title screen count, with no player and no
`menu`; the title's own). It
does not fire on the connect and loading
screens, nor for a server dialog, the server pack, link and
code-of-conduct prompts, a book or a sign editor drawn over gameplay,
nor while a world loads or saves: the scroll there stays the game's
own. A wheel a gamepad or the keyboard's focus sends is not the mouse
and fires nothing.
Side: client.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `canceled`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.

`Gui.setScreen` is about to replace the `current` screen with `new`
(`ScreenEvent.Opening`; the screen `playing` is none: vanilla's null).
Answer `ScreenOpening::Cancel` to keep the current one, or
`ScreenOpening::ModScreen` to open a mod's own screen instead.
Side: client.

Return `Some` to set `outcome`; the first mod returning `Some` wins.

After a screen's preedit handler (`ScreenEvent.Preedit.Post`) and only
when no text field took the composition (the handler returned false:
vanilla's focused field takes it, so this is a preedit no field
wanted) and `screen_preedit_pre` did not cancel. Same arguments.
Side: client.

Before a screen's preedit handler (`ScreenEvent.Preedit.Pre`, vanilla's
`GuiEventListener.preeditUpdated`): the input method is composing
`full_text` (empty when the composition ended), with the caret at
byte `caret_position`, split into `blocks` of which `focused_block` is
the one being converted. Set `canceled` and no text field sees it, and
`screen_preedit_post` does not fire. Fires on the window while a
screen is open, even when no text field is focused.
Side: client.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `canceled`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.

The open screen is about to draw its contents (`ScreenEvent.Render.Background`, after vanilla's `renderBackground` and before `render`): draw here for what must sit under the screen's widgets, items and tooltips. Not cancellable. The screen has drawn its background panel; its widgets, slots and items draw over this hook. Screens without a panel, such as the title and chat, fire it before their contents. It does not fire when `screen_render_pre` cancelled. Fires once a frame on the window, for the screens `screen_render_post` covers: a screen of the game's, the title's own screens, Win and Options. Not while playing with no screen, nor for a server dialog, the server pack, link and code-of-conduct prompts, a book or a sign editor drawn over gameplay. Draw with `native_fill`, `native_sprite` and `native_text`; `screen.rect` is the screen's container panel (or the whole window).
Side: client.

The open screen has drawn its contents (`ScreenEvent.Render.Foreground`, vanilla's point before the deferred tooltips and the preedit overlay). Not cancellable. Tooltips, the dragged stack and the preedit overlay draw over this hook; use `screen_render_post` for drawing over the screen's tooltips. It does not fire when `screen_render_pre` cancelled. Fires once a frame on the window, for the screens `screen_render_post` covers: a screen of the game's, the title's own screens, Win and Options. Not while playing with no screen, nor for a server dialog, the server pack, link and code-of-conduct prompts, a book or a sign editor drawn over gameplay. Draw with `native_fill`, `native_sprite` and `native_text`; `screen.rect` is the screen's container panel (or the whole window).
Side: client.

Ahead of the effect panels beside the survival and creative
inventories (`ScreenEvent.RenderInventoryMobEffects`, vanilla's
`EffectsInInventory.extractRenderState`): `available_space` is the
width in GUI pixels right of the container, at least 32 (with no effect
to show, or less room, vanilla draws nothing and this does not fire).
`compact` picks icons over full panels (vanilla's choice is compact
under 120) and `horizontal_offset` shifts the stack right (negative
left). Set `canceled` and the panels are not drawn: draw your own with
`screen_render_post`. Once a frame while the screen draws them,
on the window only; if the effects space changes within a frame (the
recipe book opening between two layout builds), it is asked again for
the new space. The exclusion areas follow this choice in the same frame.
Side: client.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `canceled`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.

The open screen has drawn itself and its tooltips (`Screen.extractRenderStateWithTooltipAndSubtitles`,
the point of `ScreenEvent.Render.Post`): draw over it with
`native_fill`, `native_sprite` and `native_text`, `screen.rect` being
its container panel (or the whole window) and `screen.id` the screen
it is. Once a frame on the window, never while playing with no screen;
`&self`, so it reads and draws only. The Win and Options screens call
it on their own path, after their drawing.

It does not fire for the screens drawn over gameplay after it (a
server dialog, the server pack, link and code-of-conduct prompts, a
book, a sign editor): those keep `Screen::Playing`, which it skips (the
server pack prompt hides an open screen too, and that screen does not
fire under it), and draw over what it drew, while vanilla's
`ScreenEvent.Render.Post` fires for them. The title's own screens
(`title`, `world_select`, `world_create`, `multiplayer`…) fire it too,
their `screen.id` from the title state machine and the whole window
their `rect`, and no dialog or prompt over them.
Side: client.

Before the open screen draws itself (`ScreenEvent.Render.Pre`, vanilla's `Screen.renderWithTooltips`): draw to put something under it, or set `canceled` and the screen is not drawn, and neither is its `screen_render_background` or `screen_render_foreground`. The world, the HUD layers and the toasts still draw, and `screen_render_post` still fires. Fires once a frame on the window, for the screens `screen_render_post` covers: a screen of the game's, the title's own screens, Win and Options. Not while playing with no screen, nor for a server dialog, the server pack, link and code-of-conduct prompts, a book or a sign editor drawn over gameplay. Draw with `native_fill`, `native_sprite` and `native_text`; `screen.rect` is the screen's container panel (or the whole window).
Side: client.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `canceled`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.

Room for a mod's own panel right of the open container screen's window, in GUI pixels:
`right` starts at 0; raise it to the width your panel takes beside the window, its gap
included, and leave it be otherwise. Later mods see earlier mods' answers: keep the larger
(`event.right = event.right.max(mine)`). When the window, the recipe book open beside it and
that room all fit across the screen, the window and the book move left by half the room
(rounded down), so the three stay centred as vanilla's recipe book moves the window right to
make room for itself (`RecipeBookComponent.updateScreenPosition`); when they don't fit,
nothing moves. This API is right-only: mod panels reserve the right while the existing
recipe book occupies the left; left reservations are not part of this hook.
The query's `ScreenView::rect` is pre-reservation. Later draw/input views expose the
shifted window; check that rectangle's right edge plus the room against the viewport.
Keep this query pure and cheap. Its answer is memoized for the frame and screen; recursive
queries during dispatch see zero. Asked once a
frame while the player's inventory, a container or a mod's menu screen is open, not for the
creative inventory, a merchant's or a beacon's screen, nor while the recipe book covers the
window of a narrow screen; an answer that changes geometry builds the layout again in the
same frame (slots, book and effect panels move with the window). Not finite or below 0
counts as 0. Beyond NeoForge: a mod there reads the container screen's `leftPos` but has no
event to move it, so it draws in the space that's left.
Side: client.

Every mod gets `event.right` in order and may add, change or remove right.

`Screen.extractTransparentBackground`: draws the translucent dark background
behind an in-game screen (inventory, container, creative, book, sign, editor).
Set `canceled` (or return `Flow::Cancel`) to suppress the vanilla dark gradient,
allowing a mod to draw its own background or apply menu background blur
via `Host::apply_screen_blur`. API @API:screen_transparent_background@.
Side: client.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `canceled`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.

An F2 screenshot has been read back, before either PNG is written
(`ScreenshotEvent`). Runs on the client thread with a `ClientHost`.
`image` is the in-memory frame (`getImage`): RGBA8, top to bottom,
`width * height * 4` bytes. Change it and the normal PNG is that image.
A length other than `width * height * 4` writes nothing and reports
screenshot failure. The HDR copy is not this image. Change `file_name`,
a relative path inside the player's screenshots folder, or set `message`
to replace the success chat line. `None` uses the normal translated,
clickable line for the final file name. Return `Flow::Cancel` to write
no files and post `message`, or the translated cancellation line when
`message` is `None`. Invalid paths (including symlinks) report screenshot
failure; parent folders are created. HDR copies follow the final name
with `-hdr.png`. Agent captures and world icons do not fire this hook.
Side: client.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn screenshot(&self, _: &mut dyn ClientHost, _: &mut ScreenshotEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
A sculk catalyst at `pos` has begun blooming after taking experience.
The catalyst block state has changed. Server-side.
Side: server.

The server is about to open its worlds: nothing of the world is
loaded yet (NeoForge's `ServerAboutToStartEvent`, "called before the
server begins loading anything"). Vanilla's `MinecraftServer.loadLevel`
start. Server-side: the single player server thread once Play is
pressed, a dedicated server once its settings are read. Each is
followed by `server_started` or
`world_lifecycle`'s `WorldOpenFailed`. `dedicated` tells a dedicated server from the single
player one.
Side: server.

NeoForge's `ServerChatEvent`: a player's chat message, through their
chain and the chat filter, is about to be broadcast.
`player_id` is the server's entity id for the player, `player` their
UUID, `username` their name and `raw_text` what they typed. `message`
starts as that text; replace it and players see the new message
(`withUnsignedContent`: a signed message keeps its signature), and
the log shows it. Set `cancel` and nobody sees it, and it doesn't
count toward the chat spam limit. Commands (`/say`, `/msg`...) are
not chat here. Server-side, with no player's state swapped in.
A component deeper than 512 nodes refuses capture or the whole writeback;
no event field is applied if any Text field fails conversion.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn server_chat(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut ServerChatEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
Paper's `PaperServerListPingEvent`: a client asked a server for its
status (the server list's ping, the status request in the status
protocol state), and the answer is about to be sent. `protocol` is the
protocol version the client's handshake stated and `virtual_host` the
host name it connected to (the part before its first NUL, empty when
it stated none). The writable fields start as what vanilla's
`MinecraftServer.buildServerStatus` sends: `motd` the description,
`favicon` the server icon as PNG bytes (`None`: no icon; bytes that
are not a PNG send no icon either), `online` and `max_players` the
counts, `sample` the names and UUIDs the player list shows (vanilla's
shuffled pick of at most 12; empty when the server hides its online
players), and `hide_players` false. Set `hide_players` and the
answer has no players part at all. Set `cancel` and the connection is
closed without an answer. At most 64 sample entries are kept. An
answer that is longer than a client reads (32767 characters) is
replaced by the plain one. Server-side, once for each status request,
on the game thread: the connection waits half a second for the mods,
and sends the plain answer if they have not finished. There is no
player, so no player's state is swapped in.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn server_list_ping(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut ServerListPingEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
The server has opened its worlds and is about to run its tick loop
(NeoForge's `ServerStartedEvent`): every level is loaded, no player has
joined, and the first tick has not run. Fired where `WorldOpenReady` was,
on the single player server thread and on a dedicated server, once per
open that succeeds (a failed open fires `WorldOpenFailed` instead).
`dedicated` tells a dedicated server from the single player one.
Side: server.

Fired once immediately after `server_about_to_start`, before the server
accepts play, on both integrated and dedicated servers. A failed startup
still reaches `server_stopped`.
Side: server.

Fired once at the end of server teardown, after `server_stopping` and
the final save attempt and storage release. Also fired when startup or
teardown fails after startup began, including when a shutdown listener
panics, on integrated and dedicated servers.
Failed opens save only worlds already adopted by the server (the prepared
level is installed; the session lock alone is not adoption). A failed
save still reaches this hook, but does not emit `WorldCloseFinal`.
Side: server.

The server begins teardown (NeoForge's `ServerStoppingEvent`), including
after startup or the tick loop failed:
the start of vanilla's `MinecraftServer.stopServer`, with the worlds
still loaded and the players still connected and not yet saved, so a
mod can save its own data or tell them. `world_lifecycle`'s
`WorldCloseFinal` follows once the worlds are saved. A server whose loop
fails still fires this before the final save attempt and `server_stopped`.
Side: server.

The authoritative server tick's phases: `ServerTickStart` before any
level is ticked (NeoForge's `ServerTickEvent.Pre`), `ServerTickEnd`
after the last (`.Post`). Read blocks with `native_server_block`, by
dimension: which level `self.world` holds here is not defined. A paused
pass fires nothing; a frozen world carries `world_running` false except
during a requested step. `host.server_has_time()` says whether optional
work still fits before the next tick is due (`ServerTickEvent.hasTime`).
Side: server.

`/tick rate` set the server's rate, or a `/tick sprint` ended
(`MinecraftServer.onTickRateChanged`, before its autosave wait is adjusted). Vanilla calls
this for every `/tick rate`, the rate it already had included, and at each end of a sprint:
on its own, by `/tick sprint stop` or by `/tick freeze`, the rate then being what it was.
`host.tick_stats()` reads the rate. A client told the server's rate is not a server:
nothing fires there. Server-side. Beyond NeoForge: there is no counterpart.
Side: server.

The player changed setting `key` of mod `mod_id` on its page in Options > Mods
(`Registrar::register_setting`); the new value is kept already, so read it with
`setting_bool` and its siblings. Only mod `mod_id` hears it: a mod is told of its own
settings, never another's.
Side: client.

The values native mods hand their shader packs in this frame,
`partial` ticks past the last tick (0 to 1): a pack's WGSL reads
them as `frame.mods` (eight `vec4<f32>`). Write the slots your own
pack reads; a mod that bundles its pack as `native-<mod id>` is the
one that pack is for. Asked once a frame while a pack is on; a value
that isn't finite reads as 0 (`native_shader_params_now`).
Side: client.

`MobEffect.shouldApplyEffectTickThisTick` for a content mod's effect
`effect` (an `EffectKey` for `ruby:bleeding`), each tick a player or a mob has it, in
`MobEffectInstance.tickServer` before it counts down: `tick_count` is
the ticks left (the entity's tick count when infinite). Set `apply`
and `native_apply_effect_tick` follows. Server-side.
Side: server.

A player finished editing a sign: `ServerGamePacketListenerImpl.updateSignText`
has taken their update packet and every check has passed (they were
editing that sign, within reach, the sign is not waxed, the chat filter
let the text through), right before the lines go on the sign. `pos` in
`dimension`, the `front` or back side, and the four `lines` as written,
plain text with the formatting codes still in (vanilla strips them
afterwards). Rewrite `lines` (made four lines again) and that is what
the sign gets, without a second look from the chat filter, or set
`cancel` and the sign keeps its old text. With the player's state
swapped in, so `PlayerRef::tell` and the helpers that act on the player
reach them. Once for each update a player sends on a server. Not told:
the host's own editing of a sign on a LAN or single-player world
(the editor writes into their world directly), and the sign changes
that are no edit of the text (dyeing, glow ink, waxing, `/data`,
`/setblock`, mods' `native_with_mod_block_entity`).
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn sign_changed(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut SignChangedEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
Enough players have slept through the night in level `dimension`
and the clock is about to move to the morning (NeoForge's
`SleepFinishedTimeEvent`, vanilla's `ServerLevel.tick` when it moves
the clock to `wake_up_from_sleep`). `adjustment` says where the clock
goes and may be changed: it comes in as
`Marker(minecraft:wake_up_from_sleep)`, vanilla's own, and a mod may
set `Absolute`, `Relative` (from `current`, the day time now) or
another `Marker`; a later mod reads what an earlier one left.
`new_time` is the morning vanilla resolved, read only, for a mod that
computes from it. Contract version `2`: in version `1`, `new_time`
was the value a mod wrote; a time is now written as `Absolute`.
`current` and the result are times of the level's own clock (its
dimension type's default clock, else the Overworld's). The game
resolves `adjustment` once after every mod: a time before `current`,
a time past `i64::MAX`, or a marker the level's clock does not define
is refused, as `setTimeAddition` refuses one, and the clock moves to
the morning. Only the Overworld's clock defines markers today, so on
any other clock every `Marker`, vanilla's included, falls back to the
morning. When even the morning is past `i64::MAX`, `new_time` is
`current` and the clock stays. On the server, only when the `advance_time` rule is on;
`time_skip` then hears the jump to the resolved time and may
still cancel it. The players wake and the weather resets as usual
either way. Set `canceled` and the clock is left where it is, as
NeoForge's cancel leaves it: `time_skip` is not asked either.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `canceled`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn sleep_finished_time(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut SleepFinishedTimeEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
The sound engine opened its output (`SoundEngineLoadEvent`): once at window start, after each resource reload (with the `context` of the new resource generation) and when the output device changes. Nothing fires with no sound output (no device, or audio turned off). Client-side only.
Side: client.

The world's spawn point changed to `pos` and `angle`.
Side: server.

A sponge at `pos` absorbed water and became wet. Server-side.
Side: server.

A server entity is about to be placed by `/spreadplayers` (NeoForge's
`EntityTeleportEvent.SpreadPlayersCommand`, vanilla's
`SpreadPlayersCommand.setPlayerPositions`): once per entity, after the
spread worked out its spot. `entity` is its network id, `player` its UUID (None for a
non-player), `from` where
it stands and `target` the spot. A mod may move `target` (a value that
is not a number is ignored). Canceling leaves the entity where it is;
the spread's other entities, its random draws and its feedback are
unchanged.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn spread_players_teleport(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut SpreadPlayersTeleportEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
An entry of an atlas definition whose `type` a mod registered (`register_sprite_sources`,
vanilla's `SpriteSource.run`), asked at the entry's place in the definition's `sources`,
each time the atlas is loaded or reloaded, on the resource loader. `config` is the entry's
JSON object converted to a `Tag`, `atlas` the atlas being listed and `listed` the sprites
the entries before it listed. Push `SpriteSourceOutput`s to `output` only for a source your
mod owns; they apply in order once every mod has answered.
Side: client.

Every mod gets `event.output` in order and may add, change or remove output.

Models no blockstate names, registered once on the client before resources load.
`models` collects plain namespaced file ids, baked unturned. `forms` collects
rotated/UV-locked or combined dependencies under a namespaced result id.
Every resource load rebakes both from the active pack files. A missing dependency
drops the entire form and logs its registering mod. Resolve the results through
`RenderAssets::model` after `model_baking_completed`, just like plain ids.
Side: client.

Each mod receives its own empty `event.forms` batch; every entry it adds is recorded
as that mod's.

A workstation `PlayerRef::open_station` opened is closing for `player` (UUID): the player
closed it, it was no longer valid or another menu replaced it. `window`
is the id `open_station` returned and `menu` its type. `inputs` holds its input slots
(the crafting grid's nine, row by row; a station's in its menu's order) before they go
back to the player's inventory, or drop when it is full (`clearContainer`). A listener
may empty a slot to keep its stack itself, in an item's container component; only
emptied slots count, and any other change to `inputs` is ignored, so no stack is made
or grown here. Stations the game opened on a block never fire it, nor does a player
leaving: their inputs go back to the inventory before it is saved.
Side: server.

Every mod gets `event.inputs` in order and may add, change or remove inputs.

Submit unlit geometry after particle submission, before opaque rendering
(NeoForge 26.3 `SubmitCustomGeometryEvent`, vanilla `LevelRenderer.submitFeatures`).
Client-only, noncancellable. `view` holds only camera, partial tick and game time,
not full extracted level state or visible sections. Submit from extracted state.
Side: client.

NeoForge's `SweepAttackEvent`: a player's damaging melee hit on a
`target` (`minecraft:zombie`, `minecraft:oak_boat`) is about to sweep or
not, after `critical_hit`. `vanilla_sweep` is `Player.isSweepAttack`
(a charged, grounded, not critical sword hit below the speed limit);
`sweeping` starts as it and may force or stop the sweep; `canceled` skips
the later mods and keeps `sweeping` as it is (a mod doing its own sweep
cancels with `sweeping` false). A critical hit that sweeps has both
sounds. Fires on the Game that runs the attack, and on the attacking
client, which only asks.
Side: both.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `canceled`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.

A guest asked to complete `command`; owned API `Suggestion` records may be
added to or filtered from `suggestions`. `range` is the replaced byte range.
The game snapshots completions only when a listener subscribes.
Side: server.

Every mod gets `event.suggestions` in order and may add, change or remove suggestions.

Tags changed, and what depends on them should be rebuilt (NeoForge's
`TagsUpdatedEvent`); `cause` says how. The place to drop caches
derived from the data and to rebind what depends on it.

`ServerDataLoad`: the server's data tables are built. The recipes,
tags, loot and advancements of the world's data packs, and the files
mods added through `data_pack_files`, are what the helpers read
from now on. `reload` is false on a world's first open, before its
chunks and players are loaded, and true after `/reload` rebuilt them,
once the players were sent the new data. Fires on the server, the
single player's integrated server included.

`ClientPacketReceived`: a client applied the block, item and fluid
tags its server sent, and `block_in_tag`, `fluid_in_tag` and the
`tags()` service read them from now on. Fires once at login, for
configuration's tags, and once for each update in play, on the game
thread. `integrated_server` is true in single player, where both
causes fire: `cause.should_update_static_data()` is then false here,
so that data the two threads share is updated once, on the server.

Runs in Reloading: published asset/data queries can rebind caches,
including on first open; world handles and transactions remain
unavailable.
Side: both.

A projectile hit the target block at `pos`, which now has `strength`
output power. Server-side.
Side: server.

A server entity is about to be teleported by `/tp` or `/teleport` (NeoForge's
`EntityTeleportEvent.TeleportCommand`, in `TeleportCommand.performTeleport`, once per
teleported entity): `dimension` is the level it arrives in, `entity` its network id,
`from` its feet now and `to` where the command sends it. A mod may move `to` (a value
that is not a number is ignored). Canceling leaves the entity where it is; the command
still reports success. `entity_teleport` and `player_teleported` hear it after.
Server-side. Diverges from upstream: new hook.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn teleport_command(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut TeleportCommandEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
An atlas was stitched and published (`TextureAtlasStitchedEvent`): `atlas` names it. Fires
once per atlas, the blocks' first and then the GUI's, on the first load before
`client_setup` and after every successful resource reload (F3+T, a pack turned on or off, a
server's pack) before `client_resources_reloaded`; a reload that fails fires nothing. Look
the sprites a mod draws up here, once, and keep what it finds until the next stitch of that
atlas: `texture_sprites` for [`TextureAtlas::Blocks`], `gui_sprite` for
[`TextureAtlas::Gui`]. Never look them up by name every frame. Client-side.
Side: client.

The server changed its thunder state through `/weather`. Set `cancel`
to keep the previous thunder state and timer. Server-side.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn thunder_change(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut ThunderChangeEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
How many milliseconds a client tick lasts (`Minecraft.getTickTargetMillis`, the target the
window's `DeltaTracker.Timer` divides the frame's time by): `millis` comes in as vanilla's
(50 at 20 ticks a second, longer when the server's `/tick rate` is slower); set it to speed
up or slow down the client's fixed-step clock, a "timer". Asked once a frame, in menus too,
before the frame's client ticks run (at most ten a frame). An answer that is not a finite
number above zero keeps vanilla's. Only the window's clock changes: a server still ticks
at its own rate. Client-side. Beyond NeoForge: there is no counterpart. Diverges from
upstream: new hook.
Side: client.

The overworld clock is about to jump, from sleep or `/time`. Set
`cancel` to keep `from`.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn time_skip(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut TimeSkipEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
TNT at `pos` is about to be lit (primed): a flint and steel or a fire
charge on it, fire burning it, a redstone signal, an arrow, or a
dispenser's flint and steel or TNT item. `player` is the server player
whose click lit it, with their state swapped in (so `PlayerRef::tell`
answers them), None when no player is behind it (fire, redstone, an
arrow, a dispenser). Set `cancel` and it is not primed: a TNT block
stays where it is (one that fire or a signal had already taken out is
put back, without a block update), a dispenser's TNT item stays in it.
Not asked: TNT set off by a blast (`explosion_detonate` spares
blocks), a TNT minecart and a sulfur cube. Server-side and in single
player.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn tnt_primed(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut TntPrimedEvent) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
A client toast is about to enter its queue (`ToastAddEvent`). Return
`Flow::Cancel` to discard only this candidate, before slot allocation,
animation or sound. `kind` identifies its family; music is `Other`.
Replace `title` and `description` to change the displayed components.
For advancements the title is the frame label and the description is
the advancement name. Existing recipe/system toasts updated in place
do not fire another add event. Client-lib and title producers prepare
candidates for the game to admit with a `ClientHost` before applying.
Side: client.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.

A server player selected trade `index` from `villager` in the trading menu.
Side: server.

A trade of a villager or a wandering trader was made
(`MerchantResultSlot.onTake` once the offer is taken): `merchant` is
the trader's entity id and `kind` its type (`minecraft:villager`,
`minecraft:wandering_trader`), `offer` the live one in the trading
session (not a copy) as the trade left it: `uses` counted, `result`
what the player got. Once per trade, so a shift-click that trades
several times is heard for each, after the trade's statistic and
`villager_trade` trigger. A mod may change the offer (Bukkit's
`PlayerTradeEvent#getTrade` is mutable): `uses`, `max_uses`, `demand`,
`special_price_diff`, `price_multiplier`, `xp`. The change stands: the
next click and the offers sent to the player see it. Not asked for a
trade window without a trader. The player's state is swapped in
(`host.players().acting_player()`). Server-side. Version 2: was a listen hook
returning the offer read-only; now collects the live offer as `out`
(the moment upstream's separate `merchant_offer_traded` covered).
Side: server.

Every mod gets `event.offer` in order and may add, change or remove offer.

`UseItemOnBlockEvent`: after a phase was chosen, before its Part or
vanilla behaviour. Cancel skips that behaviour and returns
`cancellation_result` (initially `TryWithEmptyHand`). In `ItemBeforeBlock`,
`Pass` continues to the block, skipping the item's `on_item_use_first`
Part; any result other than `Pass` ends the block interaction.
A block-phase `TryWithEmptyHand` can still try the empty-hand behaviour.
Side: both.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `canceled`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.

`dimension`'s level has loaded the saved chunk tickets of `controller`
(NeoForge's `LoadingValidationCallback.validateTickets`), before its
first tick and after `level_load`, once for each open and each
controller registered with a validator that has tickets in the level.
`validation` holds that controller's tickets, block owners and entity
owners apart; the mod that owns the controller removes the ones that no
longer hold (a machine that is gone), and they stop forcing their
chunks. Server-side.
Side: server.

A vanilla game event is about to reach its listeners (NeoForge's
`VanillaGameEvent`, vanilla's `Level.gameEvent`): every event, in
`dimension`. `event` is its id (`minecraft:step`), `pos` where it
happened and `cause` the network id of the entity that caused it
(None for none). `affected_state` is the block state the event touched
(`GameEvent.Context.affectedState`, with `cause` its `sourceEntity`): the
block a player broke or placed, the block a mob stepped on; None where
vanilla passes none (`Context.of(entity)`).
Canceling keeps the sculk sensors, wardens and allays from hearing it.
Server-side.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event_.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn vanilla_game_event(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut VanillaGameEventEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
A vault at `pos` changed to `state`. Its block state is updated.
Server-side.
Side: server.

A vault at `pos` is about to eject a loot item.
Side: server.

A boat or minecart was created at `pos`, after it joined the level.
`kind` is the vehicle type. Server-side.
Side: server.

A vehicle is about to take damage from a player's attack. `kind` is
`boat` or the minecart type; mods may change `damage` or set `cancel`
to leave its damage and wobble unchanged. The attack itself still
completes. Server-side.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn vehicle_damage(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut VehicleDamageEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
A boat or minecart is about to be destroyed at `pos`. TNT minecarts
that prime instead of breaking are not heard. Server-side.
Side: server.

A boat or minecart (`kind`, `minecraft:oak_boat`) moved since the last
tick (`VehicleMoveEvent`): `from` and `to` are its positions, heard
after the tick moved it. Once a tick for each vehicle that carries a
server player, whose state is then swapped in (as for
`run_mod_command`: `host.players().acting_player()`, `PlayerRef::tell` and
the item helpers reach them; `player` is their UUID), and for one a
server player rode and left, until it has stood still for ten
seconds (`player` is none, nobody is swapped in). It only hears.
Cheap when nothing moves: one position compare a tick for each watched
vehicle. Not heard: a vehicle moved before anyone rode it, a mount
(horse, pig...) or a vehicle carrying only a mob. Server-side, in the
level the vehicle is in.
Side: server.

A sound of a level the server opened for viewing (arismoko/horizon#3716) reached this client, and the
client asks where in the player's own level to play it. `level` is the viewed level's
handle (what `host.level` gives for it) and `position` the sound's position there; `sound`,
`source` and `seed` are the server's. `play_at` starts as None, and a sound left None is not
played. Set it to a position in the player's level and the sound plays there, as the
