player's own level plays a sound packet (no distance delay), with the `volume` and `pitch`
the listeners leave and the same seed. A `play_at` that is not finite, or a volume or pitch
that is not finite and at least 0, plays nothing. Only a server of `horizon:levels`
revision 3 sends these. A sound bound to an entity of the viewed level has that entity's
position there, and plays at `play_at` without following it. Sounds of the player's own
level ask `play_level_sound_at_position` and
`play_level_sound_at_entity`, never this hook. With no listener the sound is dropped after
one check, with nothing decoded or allocated. Client-side. Diverges from upstream: new
hook, a Horizon addition with no NeoForge counterpart.
Side: client.

A village siege found a spawn position on the server. Set `canceled`
to stop the siege. There is one siege per dimension.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `canceled`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn village_siege(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut VillageSiegeEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
The world frame's local, world-space rim and colored-light sources.
Push requests; Horizon validates and limits them before rendering.
Called only while a world is visible.
Side: client.

The server changed its weather parameters. `raining` and `thundering`
are the requested final states. Set `cancel` to keep the previous
weather parameters. Server-side.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `cancel`, and later mods are skipped unless they
listen with `#[listener(receive_cancelled)]`; those see `event.cancelled` and may set it back to
`false`.
methods.signature: fn weather_change(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut WeatherChangeEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
The dedicated server's whitelist changed to `enabled`.
Side: server.

Before a wind burst interacts with blocks, `wind_burst(dimension, center, blocks)` receives the shuffled candidate positions. Remove positions to spare those blocks; entity knockback and the shuffle's random draws are unchanged. Not called when mob_griefing prevents a breeze from interacting with blocks. Bundles need "hooks": @API:wind_burst@.
Side: server.

Every mod gets `event.blocks` in order and may add, change or remove blocks.

After a window resize or applying a changed GUI scale, fullscreen, or Unicode font setting.
`width` and `height` are physical pixels; `gui_width` and `gui_height` are scaled GUI pixels.
Fires only when physical or scaled dimensions change.
Side: client.

A timed world-border size change finished on the server, after its
final size was applied. Server-side, including the single-player
server.
Side: server.

The server world's border bounds changed, either immediately or when
its timed size change was requested.
Side: server.

The server world's border center changed.
Side: server.

The world's phases, read-only; `error_text` carries the engine's
own open-failure text, empty otherwise. Server-side. A server loop or final
save failure fires `WorldCloseFailed` with the error text.
Side: server.

The server completed a world save cycle. `wait` says chunk writes were
flushed before returning.
Side: server.

An experience orb looks for a player to follow (NeoForge's
`XpOrbTargetingEvent`, `ExperienceOrb.followNearbyPlayer`), on a
server. `following` starts as the default: the nearest living player
within `scan_distance` (8) blocks who isn't a spectator, or `None`.
Set another player, or `None` to follow no one. The orb only goes
for a living player who isn't a spectator, in its level, and only
moves once they are within 8 blocks. Horizon looks again on every
orb tick (vanilla keeps the player it follows while they stay
within 8 blocks), so this is asked every tick for each orb: answer
fast.
Side: server.

The zoom a native mod asks for, applied while playing (the spyglass's
own view wins): set `zoom` when it is none yet.
Side: client.

Return `Some` to set `zoom`; the first mod returning `Some` wins.

traits.doc:
Services supplied by the game to trait mods.
Methods default to a named panic unless they specify a default value on refusal. The game implements every method.
The backend accessors are the exception: they default to None, so a double without a backend answers every handle's typed refusal.
Its methods are declared by area in `host/<area>.rs`; `use mod_api::prelude::*` names every area trait.
Reaches [`BlockStates`] from any host.

methods.doc: Facts about block states, as the game's tables hold them.

traits.doc: Reaches fluid-state facts from any host.

methods.doc: Facts about registered world and tank-only fluids.

required.name: transaction
required.signature: fn transaction<T, E>(&mut self, _: impl FnOnce(&mut Self, &Transaction) -> Result<T, E>) -> Result<T, E>

methods.doc:
Runs `f` in a transaction, nested in the open one if any (`Transaction.openRoot` and
`open`): `Ok` commits it (`commit`), into the transaction around it or, at the
outermost, for good, with the world told of each change once; `Err` aborts it
(`close` without `commit`), putting every storage it wrote back as it was. A panic
unwinding out of `f` aborts this transaction as it passes, so whoever catches it sees
nothing `f` changed, and the transaction around it stays open. A transaction `f` opened
itself and left open is aborted first, when this one closes.

`f` gets the [`Transaction`] to write in, never its [`TransactionSeal`]: only this
guard ends the transaction.

Covered: block entities (item slots, saved compound, custom name and attachments), cauldrons,
players' inventories and cursors, entities' inventories
([`ItemPlace::EntitySlot`](crate::ItemPlace::EntitySlot)) and item entities' stacks.

use enqueue_work; main-thread submissions execute immediately.

methods.doc:
Allocate up to 16,384 copies, initially length zero. Each mod may reserve 65,536
copies total (an empty group reserves one slot). Only visible copies in the drawn
length, not capacity, consume the view budget. At most 16,384 groups per view.
Create at setup/reload, not each frame. Visible GPU-routed copies upload each drawn frame.
Reload, world close, disabling the owning mod, or explicit destroy retires the group.
Re-enabling a mod never revives its old handles; recreate groups after publication.
methods.signature: fn create_group(&self, _: ModelRef, _: u32) -> Result<InstanceGroupRef, GroupError>

traits.doc:
NeoForge's documented `RegisterCauldronInteractionEvent.Interaction` counterpart.
Uses the shared transaction and runtime limits; no cauldron-specific budget.
Custom handlers are server-only: clients suppress prediction and wait for the server result.
Vanilla handlers still predict locally. Matching custom builds and resource generations
are not established by the current handshake.

methods.doc: Decide through read-only host access on either side, without authoritative writes.
Additional server writes run inside the existing action savepoint.

traits.doc:
What answers an item capability for one item: given where the stack lives, its handler, or
none to leave it to the next provider. A closure is one.

methods.doc: The handler for the stack at `at`, or none.

traits.doc:
A registered item's dynamic slot count. The item type is bound at registration; this
callback runs only for an actual runtime lookup, never to infer whether it is registered.

methods.doc: The item's slot count now, or none to let the next registration answer.

traits.doc: An item's part.

methods.doc:
NeoForge's `IItemExtension.applyEnchantments`: the enchanting table applies
`enchantments`, the list it chose for the clicked row as (id, level), to `stack`, the
item in its input slot (`EnchantmentMenu.clickMenuButton`). `result` arrives with
vanilla's result: a book becomes an enchanted book with the same count and components,
then each level is added as `ItemStack.enchant` adds it, keeping the higher one.
Replace or change it, and the input slot holds it; `player_enchant_item`, the
`enchanted_item` trigger and `enchant_item` then see it. The levels and lapis paid stay
as without the part. The result goes through the stack boundary: an unknown item,
invalid damage or an oversized count is refused, and so is a count other than the
input's, since the table holds one input; a refused result keeps vanilla's. Only the
`ItemPart`s attached to `stack`'s item are asked, on the server, with a read-only
`Host`. Loot, trades and spawn gear (`EnchantmentHelper.enchantItem`) don't ask. The
contract beyond the method's name and parameters is Horizon's reading, not checked
against NeoForge's.
Side: server.

NeoForge's `IItemExtension.canEquip`: may `stack` go into the equipment
slot `slot` of the living entity `entity`, of type `kind`
(`minecraft:player`)? `slot` is an `EquipmentSlot` name: `head`,
`chest`, `legs`, `feet`, `mainhand` or `offhand`, and `body` or
`saddle` from a dispenser. `can_equip` arrives holding the data answer,
as `LivingEntity.isEquippableInSlot` and `Equippable.canBeEquippedBy`
read the stack's own `equippable` component (a stack's override
replaces the item's): yes when it names that slot and its
`allowed_entities` is absent or lists the entity type (an empty list
allows none); with no component, removed or never there, yes for
`mainhand` only. Set it either way. Asked where vanilla asks: the
armour slots of a player's inventory menu (`ArmorSlot.mayPlace`, which a
shift-click into one reaches too), a dispenser equipping what stands in
front of it (`EquipmentDispenseItemBehavior`, one entity at a time) and
a mob picking an item up off the ground (`Mob.equipItemIfPossible`). It
decides whether the stack fits the slot, not what the slot holds,
whether the entity may wear one at all (`canUseSlot`) or the dispenser's
own rules for the entity. Only the `ItemPart`s attached to `stack`'s
item are asked, on both sides, as the client's menu predicts the slot.
`host` is read-only: read `entity` through it (its position, its
equipment) to answer from its state when asked. The stack is converted
once and lent to each slot and entity a native menu click, dispense or pickup
asks about. Each decision prepares one owned copy per participating wasm guest
instance and lends it by token to every candidate. Mutable access invalidates
the source revision; replacing or removing it changes its identity. Stale
preparation and stale apply preconditions refuse without asking again. Pickup
scope is one mob's attempt. Missing prepared exports refuse at load or part
registration. A stale or missing target refuses wherever a part is asked;
the no-listener data path performs no conversion or entity lookup.
Target type, position, health, maximum health, alive/living status and physical
equipment are retained outside traversal; other Host reads can allocate.
Side: both.

NeoForge's `IItemExtension.canFitInsideContainerItems`: may `stack` go inside an item
that holds items? `fits` arrives with vanilla's answer
(`Item.canFitInsideContainerItems`): every stack fits except a shulker box. Set it
`true` or `false`. It is asked, on both sides, wherever that rule is:
- a shulker box's slots (`ShulkerBoxSlot.mayPlace`), in its menu and a guest's;
- a bundle (`BundleContents.canItemBeInBundle`): a click that puts the stack in a
  bundle, and the `/item` bundle contents;
- the item slots a mod gives an item (`item_container`) and its bundle slots.

A hopper filling a shulker box doesn't ask: vanilla tests the block there, not this.
A `true` for a shulker box lets shulker boxes nest. That is the mod's choice, and the
NBT readers' depth limit still bounds it. Only the `ItemPart`s attached to `stack`'s
item are asked. It is given the loop `context` of the side that runs the menu or the
insert and takes no `Host`, so answer from the stack and `context` alone, and fast:
a click may ask it for each slot it checks. With no part on the stack's item the cost
is one table lookup, and the stack isn't converted. The contract beyond the method's
name and parameters is Horizon's reading, not checked against NeoForge's. Diverges
from upstream: new hook.
Side: both.

NeoForge's `IItemExtension.canGrindstoneRepair`: does the grindstone repair `stack` as
it repairs a damageable item? `can_repair` arrives with vanilla's answer, whether the
stack is damageable (`ItemStack.isDamageableItem`); set it `true` or `false`. It is
asked at two places, on both sides (the server's menus and the client's own result):
- `GrindstoneMenu.mergeItems`, for the top stack when both inputs are single stacks of
  the same item. `true` takes the repair branch: one item, the enchantments of both
  merged, then all but the curses removed. Durability is merged only when the result
  has durability, as vanilla checks it again on the copy. `false` takes the other
  branch: two matching stacks of an item that stacks give two, and anything else
  gives nothing.
- The input slots' `mayPlace` (damageable or enchanted): a granted stack can be placed.
  This site is Horizon's reading.

A single enchanted input is never asked: that branch merges nothing. Only the
`ItemPart`s attached to `stack`'s item are asked. It is given the loop `context` of the
side that runs the menu and takes no `Host`, so answer from the stack and `context`
alone, and fast. With no part on the stack's item the cost is one table lookup, and
the stack isn't converted. The contract beyond the method's name and parameters is
Horizon's reading, not checked against NeoForge's. Diverges from upstream: new hook.
Side: both.

NeoForge's `IItemExtension.canPerformAction`: can `stack` perform the item
ability `ability`, a plain, case-sensitive name such as `shield_block`,
`shears_harvest` or `shears_carve` (a mod's own
abilities also use plain names, such as `my_mod_chop`)? `can_perform` arrives with
vanilla's answer for that ability: the item kind's (shears shear) or the
stack's component (`blocks_attacks`, a shield's, blocks); set it either
way and the stack grants or loses the ability. Loot conditions use the shared
item defaults; action sites retain their own vanilla answers until arismoko/horizon#3330. Asked where vanilla checks
the item for an action: a raised item blocking attacks
(`shield_block`: a granted stack blocks as a bare
`blocks_attacks` component does, a denied one never blocks nor is raised);
shearing a sheep, mooshroom, snow golem or bogged, a dispenser's shears
and a bee nest's honeycombs (`shears_harvest`); carving a pumpkin
(`shears_carve`). It decides whether the stack may do the action,
not what the action does to the world or the tool (`block_tool_modification`
is the block's side of a tool action; item wear is its own). Only the
`ItemPart`s attached to `stack`'s item are asked, on both sides, so the
client's prediction agrees with the server: answer from the stack and
`ability` alone, and fast. An item with no such part costs one table lookup.
Side: both.

The fluid a stack of a mod's own container item holds, as its
`neoforge:fluid_container` item model draws it
(`FluidUtil.getFirstStackContained`): `fluid` arrives `None` (holds
none); set it to the fluid's key, taken once at registration with
`r.fluid_key`. Asked on the client each time a stack of an item outside
`minecraft:` is drawn through a fluid container model; vanilla's items
keep their own answer and never ask. A fluid with no look in an item
draws the missing texture; a key no fluid is registered under draws the
stack as holding none, and the game logs it once per item.
Answer from the stack alone, and fast.
Side: client.

NeoForge's `IItemExtension.getCraftingRemainder(ItemStack)`: what `stack`
leaves when consumed by crafting, furnace fuel or brewing. `remainder` arrives
holding the item's data remainder. Replace it, or set it to `None` to
leave nothing. A part that leaves it alone preserves the data remainder.
Recipe-specific book and banner copies are handled by the recipe.
Asked for each consumption on the authoritative server, with a read-only
`Host`. Oversized counts, unknown items and invalid damage are refused by
the stack boundary, retaining the original data remainder. API stacks
cannot have count zero; use `None` to leave nothing. Native panics follow
the normal Part crash path, attributed to the owning mod and Part.
Side: server.

`IItemExtension.getCreatorModId`: the mod that made `stack`, which a
recipe viewer or tooltip names, instead of the mod that registered its
item. `mod_id` arrives as the item id's namespace; set it to another
mod (a universal bucket holding that mod's fluid, a facade of its
block) or `None` for no mod. Asked by `ItemResource::creator_mod_id`,
from client tooltips and viewers as well as the server: answer from
the stack alone. Only the `ItemPart`s attached to `stack`'s item are
asked: an item with none costs one table lookup.
Side: both.

Every part gets `event.mod_id` in order and may add, change or remove mod_id.

`IItemExtension.damageItem`: the wear `stack` is about to take
(`ItemStack.hurtAndBreak`: a tool that mines or hits, armour that takes
a hit, a shield, a rod, an elytra, a tool a dispenser uses, a mob's
armour), after Unbreaking has had its say, as NeoForge passes it.
`entity` is who wears or uses it: the acting player on a player's
paths, the mob, armour stand or dragon wearing it, `None` for a
dispenser's tool. `amount` is the points about to be lost; change it
(0 or less leaves the item whole) or set `canceled` for no wear at
all. Set `break_now` and the item breaks whatever durability it has
left, through the vanilla break (the sound and particles, the stack
emptied, `player_destroy_item` for a player): NeoForge's `onBroken`.
It wins over `canceled`. Not asked when
Unbreaking already saved the item, nor for a creative player's tools
(they take no wear). Only the `ItemPart`s attached to `stack`'s item
hear it: an item with none costs one table lookup, and a game with no
such part none at all. On the paths of a player the player's state is
swapped in, so `host.players().acting_player()` answers them. Once for
each wear, on a server.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `canceled`, and later parts are skipped.
methods.signature: fn damage_item(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut DamageItemEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
`DispenserBlock.getDispenseMethod`: choose a behaviour for any item,
including vanilla items, on the authoritative server (not droppers).
The block the dispenser faces is asked first (`dispense_method`), and
its answer keeps this part from being asked. Leave answer None for
vanilla. Otherwise answer `(remainder, event)`:
a remainder of None empties the slot, `Some(stack)` replaces it (the hook
owns consumption: no extra item is removed afterwards). `event` is the
level event the dispenser plays with its smoke: 1000 the click, 1001 the
fail sound (`OptionalDispenseItemBehavior` without success), or 0 for
nothing at all (`DispenseItemBehavior.NOOP`). To drop one normally,
answer `(native_dispense_default(..), 1000)`.
Side: server.

Return `Some` to set `answer`; the first part returning `Some` wins.
methods.signature: fn dispense_item(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut DispenseItemEvent<'_>) -> Option<Dispensed>

methods.doc:
`IDispensibleContainerItemExtension.emptyContents`: `stack` (a bucket
of a mod fluid, a jar, a canister) is about to be emptied at `pos`, by
`player` (the acting player) who clicked `hit` (the block and face),
or by a dispenser (`player` and `hit` are `None`). Leave
`answer` `None` for vanilla's emptying. Answer `Some(true)` when the
part placed the contents itself through the host: the stack becomes
an empty `minecraft:bucket` (a creative player keeps it), no vanilla
sound plays and the use counts as a success. Answer `Some(false)` for
a failure: nothing is placed, a player keeps the full stack and a
dispenser drops it, as vanilla's does when emptying fails. Asked for
a player once `bucket_empty` let the pour go on, and for a dispenser
before its own placement; an item with this part reaches the
dispenser's bucket behaviour even when it is no bucket of a mod
fluid, and a `dispense_item` answer still comes first. A server's
client does not predict the pour of an item with this part. The part
is asked in a transaction with the game's apply: a part that changes
the player's hand or the dispenser's slots while answering
`Some(true)` is refused and its journaled writes are undone, as a failed
use (the player keeps the stack, the dispenser fails). A player's
successful pour counts for the `placed_block` criterion. Only the
`ItemPart`s attached to `stack`'s item are asked. Server-side.
Side: server.

Return `Some` to set `answer`; the first part returning `Some` wins.
methods.signature: fn empty_contents(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut EmptyContentsEvent<'_>) -> Option<bool>

methods.doc:
NeoForge's `IItemExtension.getEquipSound`: the sound event `stack`
plays when it is equipped in equipment slot `slot` (`head`, `chest`,
`legs`, `feet`, `offhand`, `mainhand`, or a mod's own place name such as
`curios:ring`). `sound` arrives with the stack's own
`Equippable.equipSound`, `None` for the generic armour sound; a part
attached to `stack`'s item may change it to any `namespace:path` id,
including one from its own content mod's `assets/<id>/sounds.json`
(Horizon sends a mod's sound to players by name). `None` keeps the
generic armour sound. The slot name lets one item answer differently
for different places. Asked on the server wherever the game plays an
equip sound: a player's armour and off hand, a mob's or an armor
stand's equipment through a `LivingRef`, a mount's saddle or body
armour, and a dispenser's armour. The sound is chosen before it is
played; changing other state here is not a safe way to cancel the
equip itself. Only the `ItemPart`s attached to `stack`'s item are asked.
Server-side.
Side: server.

NeoForge's `IItemExtension.getHighlightTip`: the name drawn above the
hotbar when `stack` is selected. `name` arrives with what
`Hud.extractSelectedItemName` draws (the hover name in its rarity
colour, italic when the stack has a `custom_name`); the text the part
leaves is drawn in its place, centred at the same height and fade, cut
at the screen edge as a long custom name is. Asked once each client
tick while the name shows. The display timer still restarts only when
the selected item or its hover name changes, so a tip that changes
every tick doesn't keep the name up. Only the `ItemPart`s attached to
`stack`'s item are asked. Client-side.
Side: client.

A player's hit landed on the mob `entity` of type `kind`
(`minecraft:zombie`), holding `stack`: where `Item.hurtEnemy` is called,
before the post-attack enchantments and the weapon's wear. It only
hears. Another player as the target is not told. Server-side, for
every player of the world (the helpers read the acting one).
Side: server.

A server tick of `stack`, the stack a player carries in `slot`: where
`Inventory.tick` calls `Item.inventoryTick`, for every stack, each tick,
`/tick freeze` included (it stops the world, not the player). `slot` is
as `Inventory` saves it (0 to 35; the armour 100 feet to 103 head; -106
the off hand), and `selected` says it is the held slot.
`ItemPlace::PlayerSlot { player, slot }` reads and changes the stack,
which stays in its slot: an emptied one empties the slot, and the
player's client gets the change. Only the `ItemPart`s attached to
`stack`'s item hear it. Server-side, for every living player of the world (the helpers
read the acting one).
Side: server.

NeoForge's `IItemExtension.isCombineRepairable`: may two of `stack`'s item be combined
in a crafting grid to repair it (`RepairItemRecipe.canCombine`)? `repairable` arrives
with vanilla's answer, whether the stack has durability (`minecraft:max_damage` and
`minecraft:damage`); set it `true` or `false`. It is asked for each of the two stacks,
once they are found to be single stacks of the same item, and both must answer `true`.
A `true` for a stack with no durability (a maximum damage of 0) is refused with a
warning, and vanilla's `false` is kept, because the result needs a positive maximum.
The anvil's combining of two of the same item keeps vanilla's test and doesn't ask.
It is asked on both sides, wherever the grid's result is matched: a crafting table, the
inventory grid, a crafter and the client's own result. Only the `ItemPart`s attached to
`stack`'s item are asked. It is given the loop `context` of the side that runs the
match and takes no `Host`, so answer from the stack and `context` alone, and fast: a
match may ask it many times. With no part on the stack's item the cost is one table
lookup, and the stack isn't converted. The contract beyond the method's name and
parameters is Horizon's reading, not checked against NeoForge's. Diverges from
upstream: new hook.
Side: both.

NeoForge's `IItemExtension.isNotReplaceableByPickAction`: must a pick (the pick-block
key) leave `stack`, in hotbar `slot` (0 to 8), where it is? `player` is the player
picking. `not_replaceable` arrives with vanilla's answer, whether the stack is
enchanted; set it `true` to keep the stack in place or `false` to let the pick swap it
out. Asked in `Inventory.getSuitableHotbarSlot`'s second pass, when a pick moves an item
into the hotbar and no hotbar slot is empty: from the selected slot on, for each hotbar
stack, until one answers `false`, which is the slot the pick uses; when all answer
`true`, the selected slot is used. A pick that selects a matching hotbar stack, or
finds an empty slot, doesn't ask, nor one `player_pick_item` cancelled. Only the
`ItemPart`s attached to `stack`'s item are asked, on the server (the host's own player
and its guests), with a read-only `Host`. The contract beyond the method's name and
parameters is Horizon's reading, not checked against NeoForge's.
Side: server.

NeoForge's `IItemExtension.isPiglinCurrency`: is `stack` barter currency to a piglin
(`PiglinAi.isBarterCurrency`)? `currency` arrives with vanilla's answer, whether the
stack is a `minecraft:gold_ingot`; set it `true` to make the stack currency, `false` to
refuse it (a gold ingot included), or leave it to keep vanilla's answer. Asked where
vanilla asks: whether a piglin wants a stack on the ground (currency is wanted whenever
its off hand holds no `#minecraft:piglin_loved` item, with no inventory-space check);
whether an adult piglin that isn't admiring takes the stack from a player's hand, on the
server and in the client's prediction of that click; and when a piglin stops holding the
item it admired, where an adult barters currency (`minecraft:gameplay/piglin_bartering`,
thrown toward the nearest player) after admiring it, loses it when hit, and equips or
keeps anything else. A currency stack picked up from the ground is admired, and so
bartered, only when it is also in `#minecraft:piglin_loved`, as vanilla admires loved
items only; otherwise the piglin equips or keeps it. Only the `ItemPart`s attached to
`stack`'s item are asked, on both sides, so register the part on both for the client's
prediction to agree with the server: answer from the stack alone, and fast. An item with
no such part costs one table lookup. The contract beyond the method's name and
parameters is Horizon's reading, not checked against NeoForge's.
Side: both.

NeoForge's `IItemExtension.isPrimaryItemFor`: is `stack`'s item primary for
`enchantment` (an id such as `minecraft:sharpness`), so that enchantment selection may
offer it? Selection (`EnchantmentHelper.getAvailableEnchantmentResults`) chooses the
enchanting table's offers and clues, loot `enchant_with_levels`, trades and spawn gear.
A book skips the question and is offered every enchantment. `primary` arrives with
vanilla's `Enchantment.isPrimaryItem`: the item is in the enchantment's
`supported_items`, and in its `primary_items` when that is set; set it `true` to offer
the enchantment to the item or `false` to withhold it. The answer is per item and
enchantment: selection runs inside rolls that can't ask a part, so each item's parts
are asked once per registered enchantment when parts install (world open and
`/reload`), with `stack` the item's default stack, and selection reads the answers
stored on that server's enchantment registry until its next install or its world
closes. Answer from the item and `enchantment` alone. Only the `ItemPart`s attached to
`stack`'s item are asked, on the logical server, with a read-only `Host`. The contract
beyond the method's name and parameters is Horizon's reading, not checked against
NeoForge's.
Side: server.

The small bar `GuiGraphicsExtractor.itemDecorations` draws under an
item, wherever the game shows one: `bar` arrives holding vanilla's value
(the damage bar, or a bundle's fullness already applied) and may be
replaced (width `0..=13`, colour `rgb`) or set to `None` to hide it.
Asked each frame a stack is drawn. Client-side.
Side: client.

Append an item's custom decorations after its default bar, cooldown and count.
Coordinates are the icon's top-left in GUI units, as the batch takes them;
no item translation is active.
Runs wherever the shared item-decoration path is used (hotbar, menus, tooltips,
and the other screens that draw item icons: advancements, beacon, stats, trading).
The NeoForge counterpart is `IItemDecorator.render`; registration through
`RegisterItemDecorationsEvent` is a separate moment.
Side: client.

`ItemStack.interactLivingEntity`: after ordinary entity interactions
pass, for an alive native Mob and a nonempty stack in `hand`.
Both logical sides answer independently. A consuming client result
ends the hand loop; only Success swings there. SuccessServer and
Consume consume without a client swing; Fail, Pass and TryWithEmptyHand
fall through. A server-only answer leaves client off-hand prediction
unchanged. ClientHost permits reads and local effects, not authoritative
writes. Armor stands, other players and dragon parts are not covered.
Side: both.

Return `Some` to set `result`; the first part returning `Some` wins.

NeoForge's `IItemExtension.makesPiglinsNeutral`: does `stack`, worn by `wearer`, keep
calm piglins from targeting it, as gold armour does (`PiglinAi.isWearingSafeArmor`)?
`neutral` arrives with vanilla's answer, whether the stack is in
`#minecraft:piglin_safe_armor`; set it `true` to make the piece count as gold, `false`
to make it not count though the tag lists it, or leave it to keep the tag's answer. Asked
for each stack in a player's armour slots, in the order feet, legs, chest, head, until one
counts. A player wearing a piece that counts is not the target a calm piglin picks
(`NEAREST_TARGETABLE_PLAYER_NOT_WEARING_GOLD`); an angry piglin attacks anyway. Only the
`ItemPart`s attached to `stack`'s item are asked. It is asked whenever the server builds
a player's view for the mobs, several times a tick, so the answer must be a pure, fast
function of `stack` and `wearer`. An item with no such part costs one table lookup.
Server-side. The contract beyond the method's name and parameters is Horizon's reading,
not checked against NeoForge's.
Side: server.

`BlockItemExtension.onBlockPlacedBy`: this item's block has been placed,
its final block state and stack block-entity data applied, and
`Block.setPlacedBy` completed (including companion blocks). Runs once,
at the primary position, before sounds, level events and stack consumption.
`stack` is the pre-shrink stack; `placer` is the placing player, or None
for a dispenser. `face` and `click` are the placement context's clicked
face and world-space hit point. Failed, refused and canceled placements
never notify. Only Parts attached to the stack's item hear this server notice.
Side: server.

`IItemExtension.onDroppedByPlayer`: `player` (the acting player's
handle) pressed the drop key on `stack`, the whole selected stack
before anything leaves it; `all` is true when the whole stack goes,
false for one item (`ServerPlayer.drop(boolean)`). Set `canceled` and
the stack stays in the slot: nothing is taken out, no item entity is
made, no drop statistic is awarded and `item_toss` does not fire; a
server's player is sent the slot back, undoing their predicted drop.
Not asked for a menu's throw, nor for a spectator (who drops nothing).
Only the `ItemPart`s attached to `stack`'s item are asked: an item
with none costs one table lookup. Server-side, with a read-only `Host`.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `canceled`, and later parts are skipped.

`IItemExtension.onEntityItemUpdate`: each tick of a dropped item
entity holding `stack`, before the entity's own tick (`ItemEntity.tick`:
its fluids, movement, pickup delay, merging and lifetime), and after
`entity_tick_pre`. `item` is the entity, in the world: read and change
it through the host, its attachments included. Set `canceled` to skip
that tick's vanilla work, as NeoForge's `true` return does; the item
skips movement and its own merge pass; another item can still merge into it.\n    /// `entity_tick_post` still hears it.
Only the `ItemPart`s attached to `stack`'s item hear it: an item with
none costs one table lookup, and a game with no such part none at all.
Server-side, for every dropped item that ticks.
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `canceled`, and later parts are skipped.
methods.signature: fn on_entity_item_update(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut OnEntityItemUpdateEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
`IItemExtension.onEntitySwing`: the player in place (`entity`, its
`Entity.getId` when known) is about to swing `stack` in `hand`:
where `LivingEntity.swing` starts, for an attack, a use or a swing the
server asked for. Set `canceled` and no swing starts: no animation and
no swing packet. Only the `ItemPart`s attached to `stack`'s item are
asked. Both sides, as vanilla's: answer the same on both, and change
the world only where this `Game` runs the world, not on a server's
client.
Side: both.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `canceled`, and later parts are skipped.

`IItemExtension.onItemUseFirst`: the held item's first say on a
click on a block, on the server for each player, after
`use_item_on_block` (`ItemBeforeBlock`) let it through and before the
block's own `useItemOn`. An answer ends the click: neither the block
nor the item's `useOn` runs. `Pass` goes on to the block.
Side: server.

Return `Some` to set `answer`; the first part returning `Some` wins.
methods.signature: fn on_item_use_first(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut OnItemUseFirstEvent<'_>) -> Option<InteractionResult>

methods.doc:
`IItemExtension.onLeftClickEntity`: `player` (the acting player's
UUID), holding `stack` in the main hand, is about to attack the entity
`entity` (`Entity.getId`) of type `kind` (`minecraft:cow`,
`minecraft:player`, `minecraft:item_frame`): where `Player.attack`
starts, once the global `attack_entity` let the blow through and
before any damage, knockback, enchantment effect, `hurt_enemy` or the
weapon's wear. Set `canceled` and the attack ends there: the target
is not hurt, `hurt_enemy` does not fire and the stack takes no wear.
Only the `ItemPart`s attached to `stack`'s item are asked. Server-side,
for every player of the world (the helpers read the acting one).
Side: server.

Return `Flow::Cancel` to take it: this sets `canceled`, and later parts are skipped.
methods.signature: fn on_left_click_entity(&self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &mut OnLeftClickEntityEvent<'_>) -> runtime::Flow

methods.doc:
`Item.onUseTick` of `stack`, used by `entity` with `remaining` ticks
left, always above 0: what a mod's own item does each tick it is used
(cook, charge, drain). It comes where `ItemStack.onUseTick` calls the
item, once `living_entity_use_item_tick` let the use go on:
after a consumable's crumbs, for consumables, shields and mods' items
(vanilla's other items do their own, and a kinetic weapon has none on
the server). Both sides, as `living_entity_use_item_tick`:
change the world only where this `Game` runs the world, not on a
server's client. Runs every tick of every use: check the item first.
Side: both.

`Item.releaseUsing` of `stack`: `entity` let it go with `time_left`
ticks of its `use_duration` left, so it was held for
`duration - time_left` (a bow-like item shoots by that charge). Set
`used` as vanilla's return, and the stack's use cooldown starts
(`ItemStack.releaseUsing`). After the vanilla item's own release, once
`living_entity_use_item_stop` let it through. Both sides, as
vanilla's: change the world only where this `Game` runs the world,
not on a server's client.
Side: both.

NeoForge's `IItemExtension.shouldCauseBlockBreakReset`: does a break
restart because the main hand changed? `stack` is the stack the break
began with (vanilla's `destroyingItem`), `held` the main hand now
(`None` for an empty hand). `reset` arrives with vanilla's answer: not
`ItemStack.isSameItemSameComponents(held, stack)` (count and damage
left out). `false` keeps the break and its progress going; `true`
aborts it and starts it again from 0. A `true` for an unchanged stack
restarts the break every tick, so it never finishes. Asked on each
`continueDestroyBlock` and `startDestroyBlock` of the block the break
targets, on the local player's client (single player and a server's
client alike). Only the `ItemPart`s attached to `stack`'s item are
asked. Client-side.
Side: client.

NeoForge's `IItemExtension.shouldCauseReequipAnimation`: does the
first-person hand lower and raise again to show `stack`, the stack the
hand holds now? `old` is the stack the hand shows (`None` for an empty
hand), `slot_changed` whether `stack` came from another slot (always
false for the off hand). `reequip` arrives with vanilla's answer
(`!FirstPersonHandsAndItems.shouldInstantlyReplaceVisibleItem`: the
same stack changed in place, or an equal one but for its damage, is
shown at once). `true` lowers the hand and raises it with `stack`;
`false` shows `stack` at once. Asked each client tick, for each hand,
while the shown stack differs from the held one by slot or by value;
an unchanged hand and an empty hand aren't asked. Only the `ItemPart`s
attached to `stack`'s item are asked. Client-side.
Side: client.

`Item.appendHoverText`: an item's own lines in its tooltip, after its
name and before its components' (enchantments, lore, attributes). Add
lines to `lines`, which arrives empty, each with a colour as `rgba` packs
it (`u32::MAX` keeps the text's own); `Text::legacy` reads `§` codes.
The stack has its components (`stack.data()`). Asked each frame the
tooltip shows, never for one the stack hides or a crossbow's loaded
projectile. NeoForge's `ItemTooltipEvent` is the corresponding line-building event;
this scoped hook adds attached parts' lines before component lines are assembled.
Afterwards [`Hooks::item_tooltip`]
sees the finished list, including these parts' lines.
Side: client.

Every part gets `event.lines` in order and may add, change or remove lines.

Client-side image component for this stack's tooltip. Answer its width/height
in GUI pixels; finite positive dimensions reserve space after text and any
vanilla bundle component. None keeps the vanilla tooltip unchanged.
Side: client.

Return `Some` to set `size`; the first part returning `Some` wins.

Render the measured component at origin, inside the tooltip background.
Stack is the component's data. Use native_sprite/native_fill/native_text;
Size is the whole tooltip content box: the widest component and the sum
of component heights (minus 2 normally; no subtraction for an item
tooltip with multiple components). Origin is this component's running
top and the box's left edge. All text is drawn before any images.
Side: client.

`Item.getUseAnimation` of `stack` in use, for first- and third-person
rendering. `animation` arrives with the item's vanilla answer; mods may
change it. A `Spear` override on an item without kinetic data is refused
as `None`. Asked on the client when each render consumer updates; answer
from the stack alone.
Side: client.

`Item.getUseDuration` of `stack`, in ticks: `duration` arrives with
vanilla's (a consumable's time, 72000 for a shield, a spear, a bow,
0 for an item with no use over time). A mod's own item (outside
`minecraft:`) with no `consumable`, `blocks_attacks` or kinetic
weapon that answers above 0 is used over time on a right click, as an
`Item.use` that calls `startUsingItem`, until it is let go or the time
runs out (`living_entity_use_item_finish`). A consumable's time
changes too, potions and the other vanilla items keep their own.
Asked when a use starts, each tick a mod's item is in use, and each
frame the hand draws one in use, on both sides. It has no user, as
it is asked so often: answer from the stack alone.
Side: both.

A player uses `stack` (right click) with `self.hand`: in the air, or
on a block once `native_use_on` let it through, where `Item.use`
starts. Runs on both logical sides after the global right-click event.
Return an interaction result: Success swings on the client, SuccessServer
swings on the server, Consume handles without swinging. Fail skips this
item's use without swinging, then the off hand may be tried.
None lets later Parts answer; if none answers, the item's own use runs.
Some(Pass) skips later Parts and continues to the item's own use.
TryWithEmptyHand is block-phase-only and is treated as Pass here.
Cooldown items are skipped.
A server-only answer does not stop the client's off-hand prediction.
ClientHost permits reads and local effects, not authoritative writes.
`hand` is the interaction hand of THIS click, including an instantaneous
air use. Unlike this field, `living_used_item_hand` answers only during
active item use. This is `PlayerInteractEvent.RightClickItem.getHand`.
`player` is the clicking player's UUID and `player_entity_id` that
player's entity id on this logical side: the acting player's on a server
(a guest's own, never the host's), this client's own player on a client.
They name who clicked from the event alone, unlike `players().acting_player()`,
which only answers while the host has set the acting player.
Side: both.

Return `Some` to set `result`; the first part returning `Some` wins.

A player uses `stack` (right click) with `self.hand` on the block at
`pos`, `face` the face clicked (`[0, 1, 0]` is the top), once the
block itself let the click through (a chest still opens): where
`ItemStack.useOn` starts. Both logical sides answer independently:
a consuming client result ends the hand loop; only Success swings
there. SuccessServer and Consume consume without a client swing.
Fail ends the block path; Pass and TryWithEmptyHand fall through.
A server-only answer does not stop the client's off-hand prediction.
ClientHost permits reads and local effects, not authoritative writes.
Cooldown items are skipped. `hand` and `hit` describe this click;
`player` and `player_entity_id` identify its player on this side.

Client prediction cannot invoke server services:
```compile_fail
use mod_api::{ClientHost, prelude::*};
fn predict(host: &mut dyn ClientHost) {
    host.commands().run_command("say not a client prediction");
}
```
Side: both.

Return `Some` to set `result`; the first part returning `Some` wins.

`IItemExtension.getXpRepairRatio`: the durability points Mending
restores to `stack` per point of experience, where
`ExperienceOrb.repairPlayerItems` repairs the damaged Mending item it
picked, once per item it repairs. `experience` is the points being
spent (never 0) and `player` the player they go to. `ratio` arrives
holding vanilla's: the stack's `minecraft:repair_with_xp` repair
divided by `experience`, 2.0 for vanilla Mending. The repair becomes
`floor(experience × ratio)`, capped at the stack's damage; a ratio left
as it arrived keeps vanilla's repair exactly. A ratio that isn't finite
is refused and vanilla's repair is used; a negative one counts as 0.
A ratio that takes a positive repair to 0 leaves the experience
unspent, for the player. Only the parts attached to `stack`'s item are
asked: to change Mending for every item, change the enchantment's
`minecraft:repair_with_xp` effect in a data pack. Server-side,
including `PlayerRef::give_experience_points`.
Side: server.

Slot placement and stack limits for registered vanilla and mod menus;
mounts use `horizon:mount_inventory`, while player inventory and the
creative picker have no registered type. `slot` is the backing index,
including player inventory slots. The slot's own answers arrive first;
the maximum is bounded to 1–99 and the item limit. Refusal also prevents
quick-move top-ups. Runs on server and client prediction with the read
`Host`: it is a query, so it can neither write nor cancel. A click asks
once for each slot and stack it consults while it plans, and never again
when it validates or applies. Answer from the stack and the host alone,
and fast. On a LAN host's own click the LAN host is not reachable
through the `Host` (it answers as if no LAN were open).
`container` is the container `slot` indexes ([`MenuContainer`]): a mod
crafting grid's slots are `Grid`'s and its result `Result`'s slot 0.
`context` says who and where the ask is about ([`MenuSlotContext`]):
the player whose menu it is, the menu's block entity and a read-only
copy of the menu's own containers' slots, keyed by the same container
(`context.slot(container, index)`), built once per click plan and
filled the same on the server and on the client's prediction. Parts that read `context.setting(..)` or `side()` have no
counterpart on the Host. Named injections request `hook_version = 4`.
Side: both.

Whether a player's block menu of a mod menu type stays open
(`AbstractContainerMenu.stillValid`). Asked on the server each tick a
player has the menu of the block at `pos` open, and before each click
on it. `valid` arrives as vanilla's answer: the block entity is there
and `eye` is within the player's block interaction range plus 4 of each
block behind the menu; a part that leaves it alone keeps that answer.
Set it to keep the menu open or close it. Vanilla menu types are never
asked, and a menu whose block entity is gone closes without asking.
Runs in the restricted context; answer from the event and context
alone, and fast.
Side: server.

A recipe viewer's "+" on a mod menu (JEI's `IRecipeTransferHandler`):
move one set of `recipe`'s ingredients (as many as the items allow
with `max`) from `player`'s inventory into the open menu of a mod menu
type, or with `dry_run` only say what that would do. Asked on the
server before the game's own grid transfer, only for a mod menu type
whose part answers, with `menu` its type, `pos` its block (None for a
menu with no block) and `recipe` the recipe's id as the viewer sent
it. Return `Some(Moves)` once moved, or `Missing`, `NoRoom` or
`NotIntoMenu`; a part that returns None lets the game try its own
crafting-grid transfer. A dry run must move nothing.
Side: server.

asking Mojang, these lookups ask the session server and can resolve an account the server has
never seen, whatever its online mode.

Side: server.
Resolve an account's UUID through the game's profile resolver, as `resolve_name` does
by name. The profile's name is the account's current one, and new lookups share the same
per-minute budget.

Side: server.
Resolve a Minecraft account name (`Notch`) through the game's profile resolver: the
session server's profile, with the signed `textures` property a skin mod replaces a
player's skin with. The resolver caches answers and paces a mod's new lookups at 60 a
minute, so it stays within Mojang's rate limit; the game's own lookups are not paced. It
reaches Mojang's services whatever the server's online mode, and a name that is not a
valid player name is [`ProfileResolution::Done`] with `None` without a lookup.

The lookup runs in the background: the first call answers
[`ProfileResolution::Pending`], and a later call (poll it from `server_tick`) the answer,
which is also cached for the game's own uses. `Pending` can also mean the per-minute
budget is refilling; poll again later.

traits.doc:
The runtime_levels service, reached through its host.
Success from `open` or `unload` admits a queued request, not its completion.
Apply failures are logged with the requesting mod and level id. A failed open
leaves the id unpublished and free to retry; a failed unload keeps it open for retry.

methods.doc:
Side: server.
Remove the level `id` the calling mod owns, folder and all, once this server tick's levels
have ticked. A level that is open is saved and closed first (`level_unload` fires), as by
`unload`; a level that is not open, such as the leftovers of a crash, only has its files
removed, and a level with no files is nothing to delete. The structure references the
game keeps beside the world for the level go with its folder, unless another id would
share the file (`a_b:c` and `a:b_c` do) and that level exists. Links under `dimensions` or
`data` are never followed: the removal fails and is logged. Refused, now and again when
it is applied, with [`RuntimeLevelError::PlayersInside`] while a player or an arrival not
yet landed is in the level, with [`RuntimeLevelError::LevelsBelow`] while a level below
the id exists (`mymod:instance/ab` below `mymod:instance`: the folders nest), and with
[`RuntimeLevelError::AlreadyOpen`] for a level still waiting to open. An `open` of a level
that is open and being deleted is `AlreadyOpen` until the delete is applied; one of a
level that was not open, made after the `delete`, is applied after it and starts empty.
If the level closed but its files could not all be removed, it stays closed and
`is_open` is false, `open` of the id is [`RuntimeLevelError::Removing`] and an `open`
already queued is dropped with a log line, until a second `delete` has removed them.

Side: server.
Whether the level `id` is open: false until a queued `open` is applied, true until a
queued `unload` or `delete` is. Takes `&mut self` as the service's other methods do: a frame
resource is reached one way.

Side: server.
Open the level `id` (`mymod:instance/ab`), in the calling mod's namespace, as `level`
describes. The request is checked now and applied after this server tick's levels have
ticked, never inside a level's tick: the level is not open, and `is_open` says false, until
then. The handle names this open of the level and never a later one. A folder that
exists under the id is reopened as it was saved. `level_load` fires when it opens.
Refused with [`RuntimeLevelError`] for an id outside the mod's namespace, one already
open or waiting, an unknown dimension type or generator, a noise generator, and when
the server's cap of open runtime levels (`horizon-max-runtime-levels`, 64) is reached.
methods.signature: fn open(&mut self, _: &str, _: RuntimeLevel) -> Result<LevelRef, RuntimeLevelError>

methods.doc:
Side: server.
Regenerate the Overworld, the Nether and the End with `seed`, once this server tick's levels have ticked: their chunk files, entities, structure references, raids, the dragon fight and the world spawn are replaced by a fresh world's; game rules, the clock, the weather, the scoreboard, the world border settings and the players' files are kept. The request is checked now and again when it is applied. Refused with [`LevelResetError::PlayersInside`] while a player or an arrival not yet landed is in one of the three levels (the mod moves its players out first, for example into a runtime level it opened: `entity_teleport_to_level`), with [`LevelResetError::NoHoldingLevel`] when the mod has no runtime level open, and with [`LevelResetError::NotPermitted`] unless the mod's manifest declares `[native] level_reset`. Maps are kept. `levels_reset` fires once the old terrain is gone and not when a removal failed; the levels open again from the new seed when somebody next enters them.

methods.doc:
Side: server.
Save and close the level `id` the calling mod opened, keeping its folder, once this server
tick's levels have ticked: `level_unload` fires then. Refused with
[`RuntimeLevelError::PlayersInside`] while a player or an arrival not yet landed is in the
level, now and again when it is applied: the mod moves its players out first
(`entity_teleport_to_level`).

special model of the type it is registered for. Models of a type share one renderer, so what
differs between them comes from the model object (`config`) and the stack.
Renderer answers depend only on stack and configuration. Host-state changes do not invalidate a continuously drawn unchanged stack. Answers drop after all views stop drawing the stack or resources reload.

methods.doc:
`extractArgument` and `submit` in one: the models to draw for `stack`, in order, from the
special model's `model` object (`config`, its JSON as NBT, converted once at load). Asked

from the last one this model was asked about: an unchanged stack is asked once, however
many frames draw it. Every display context (a hand, a screen, the ground, a frame, a head)
draws the same answer, under the `base` model's display transforms. Diverges: vanilla's
renderer submits geometry; Horizon's answers resource models, so geometry stays in the
packs.

An `Err`, a panic, a wasm call that is refused or traps, more than
[`MAX_SPECIAL_MODEL_PARTS`] parts, and a transform that isn't finite all refuse the answer
whole: the special model draws the missing model, the error is logged once with the type,
and the renderer is asked no more until resources reload. A part naming a model no pack
has refuses the answer too, logged once for the model.

traits.doc:
The edits a hook may make to the mob it was lent, beside the handle's reads.

The game hands this out with the [`UnspawnedMobRef`](crate::UnspawnedMobRef) for one hook
call and keeps neither after it returns. Each method takes that handle and reaches only that
mob: another lend's handle, or one kept from an earlier call, is refused with
[`UnspawnedMobError::Expired`]. An edit applies at once, so the handle's reads, and the next
listener, see it. The editor works where the hook's host is the read-only one: it changes
nothing in the level, only the mob that is about to join it.

traits.doc: Per-view untextured geometry, cleared even without listeners; `usage` reports fixed setup-time limits shared across listeners and depth modes.

methods.doc:
Draw a retained group once per view, with per-view culling and the batch route rules.
Repeated submissions in one view are ignored. Only visible copies consume its budget.
The shared limit is 16,384 visible copies and 16,384 groups per view. Refusal is atomic.
Shader packs and overlays use the same CPU path as transient model batches.
Retired or foreign groups return [`GroupError::Stale`], even if drawn earlier this view.
methods.signature: fn draw_instance_group(&mut self, _: InstanceGroupRef) -> Result<(), GroupError>

methods.doc:
Draw every copy in `instances` of the resolved `model`.

One batch per model. The engine uploads only the instance records on the opaque
and cutout route, and bakes the same prepared geometry on the CPU when a shader
pack, a copy with an [`Overlay`], or another route cannot take instances. A
`shaders/` pack shades those copies as block entities, with the program that shades
[`BlockEntityDrawContext::model`]. A model with a translucent face is refused with
[`InstanceError::Translucent`] and is never drawn as solid.
Tint is `0xAARRGGBB` and light is [`LightCoords`]: both stay in
vanilla's space, and the engine converts them to the frame. A tint's alpha
multiplies only faces that have a tint index, the same as vanilla's model
renderer. The view budget is 16,384 copies. Pass at most that many: a longer
list is refused with [`InstanceError::CapacityExceeded`] before any copy is
examined. On wasm the guest pays for the list it passes, because the runtime
lifts the slice before that check. Within the bound, copies outside the frustum
are omitted and do not count. On `Err`, nothing from this call is drawn.
methods.signature: fn draw_model_instances(&mut self, _: ModelRef, _: &[ModelInstance]) -> Result<(), InstanceError>

methods.doc:
Submit unlit ARGB world lines atomically. Invalid coordinates or widths,
or a batch exceeding the view's fixed capacity, leave the batch unchanged.

Submit world quads drawn by the mod pipeline `pipeline`, atomically: its shader gets each
quad's texture coordinate and colour, and its blend and depth modes apply. The quads
count against the same per-view capacity as [`quads`](Self::quads), and within a stage
they draw after its plain quads and lines, in the order submitted. On `Err`, nothing
from this call is drawn.
methods.signature: fn pipeline_quads(&mut self, _: RenderPipelineRef, _: &[PipelineQuad]) -> Result<(), PipelineDrawError>

methods.doc: Submit unlit, alpha-blended world quads atomically, using the white atlas texel.

Queued counts and fixed capacities, shared by both depth modes and all listeners.
Capacity is allocated during setup, never grown during submission.
The same loaded-mod view available during registration.
Registry names in ID order, from the server's resource generation.
A loaded mod's setting captured when the server built this view, without file I/O.

traits.doc: The host's methods both sides share of the `block_entities` area, implemented by the game and reached through [`Host`].

methods.doc:
Side: both.
Find a block entity in a loaded chunk of an open level, or on a client in
the level it shows. An entity taken out for its tick cannot be read in that tick.

Side: both.
The handle [`BlockEntitiesHost::block_entity`] gives, and also for a block entity
out of the world for its own tick, whose identity and attachments stay in place
meanwhile: what its Part state (`BlockEntityPartState`) checks a handle against.
Its data reads still find nothing during that tick.

traits.doc: The server host's methods of the `block_entities` area, implemented by the game and reached through [`ServerHost`].

methods.doc:
Side: server.
Sends clients the block at `pos` and its block entity's update tag
(`block_entity_update_tag`) again, as `Level.sendBlockUpdated`
does: with the level's other block changes, to the players who see its
chunk, once however often it is called before then. Changes made in a
block entity's tick go out at the start of the next tick, as vanilla's
do (`ServerLevel.tick` broadcasts chunks before it ticks block
entities). Call it when what clients show changed (a machine started),
not for every tick's progress: a menu's data slots carry that. Nothing
happens for an unloaded block. It also sends the one-shot fields of
`ModBlockEntityView::set_client_update_fields`.

traits.doc: The host's methods both sides share of the `block_states` area, implemented by the game and reached through [`Host`].

methods.doc:
Side: both.
`Block.asItem`: the block's item identity, including air for a block with
no item; None if either resolved identity is unavailable.

Side: both.
The default state of the resolved `block` key:
`Block.defaultBlockState`, the one a block takes when nothing else
says. None for an unknown block.

Side: both.
The state `name` names, read as `/setblock` reads a block
(`BlockStateParser.parseForBlock`): `minecraft:oak_stairs[facing=east]`,
`stone` for `minecraft:stone`, the properties left out at their
default. Returns an owned block key and canonical local ordinal, never
vanilla's numeric `Block.getId`. None for an unknown block,
a property it doesn't have or a value it can't take, or block NBT
(`{...}`); and, as `/setblock`'s argument, for anything after the
block.

Side: both.
The state `state` as `/setblock` takes it back
(`BlockStateParser.serialize`): its block, then each property in
name order, `minecraft:oak_stairs[facing=east,half=bottom,...]`, or
the block alone for one with no properties. None for an unknown key
or local ordinal; an invalid value never falls back to air.

Side: both.
Resolve a registered fluid identifier.

Side: both.
The block `item` places (`BlockItem.getBlock`, as `Block.byItem` reads
it): `minecraft:wheat_seeds` places `minecraft:wheat`, and a
standing/wall item places its standing block, not the wall variant.
None for an item that places no block, and for an unknown item.

Side: both.
`Item.getCraftingRemainder`: Horizon currently stores the remainder's
item id, so the result is a single plain stack.

Side: both.
Read a loaded, light-emitting block. No implicit chunk loading.

traits.doc: The server host's methods of the `block_states` area, implemented by the game and reached through [`ServerHost`].

methods.doc:
Side: server.
Sets property `key` of the block at `pos` to `value`, as a furnace's
tick sets its `lit` (`Level.setBlock` with `UPDATE_ALL`: neighbours
and clients are told); true when the block changed, false when the
block has no such property or value, or the property already has
`value` (as `Level.setBlock` for an unchanged state). The block
entity stays.

Side: server.
`native_set_block_property` with `Level.setBlock`'s `flags`, as a
brewing stand's tick sets its bottles with `flags::UPDATE_CLIENTS`.
Players get the write when `UPDATE_CLIENTS` is set; false when this
window isn't a server, and in each case `native_set_block_property`
returns false.

traits.doc: The server host's methods of the `boss_bars` area, implemented by the game and reached through [`ServerHost`].

methods.doc:
Side: server.
An existing custom boss bar by id (`minecraft:` when no namespace), or
None. Saved bars are there from the world's start, as vanilla's
`CustomBossEvents`. Boss bars of mobs and raids are not custom boss
events.

Side: server.
Every custom boss bar, in the order `/bossbar list` shows them.

Side: server.
`/bossbar add`: a new bar, visible, white, `progress`, at 0 of 100, with
nobody added. None if the id is taken or invalid, or outside a server.
Refuses text deeper than 512 component nodes before applying any changes.
methods.signature: fn create_boss_bar(&mut self, _: &str, _: text::Text) -> Result<Option<BossBarRef>, text::TextFormError>

traits.doc: The client host's methods of the `client_input` area, implemented by the game and reached through [`crate::ClientHost`].

methods.doc:
Side: client.
Right-clicks with these items (at most 64 ids) are mod `mod_id`'s; a later call replaces the list.

Side: client.
Adds one click to the vanilla gameplay mapping `key` (`KeyMapping.click`), as a press of
its key does: the attack, use or pick a click starts on a subsequent client tick, through the
checks of `startAttack` and `startUseItem` (the miss cooldown, busy hands, the item, the
target under the crosshair) and the packets the player's own click sends; the hotbar slot,
drop, inventory or hand swap of the inventory keys. With a screen or overlay open the click
is dropped, as `KeyMapping.releaseAll` drops it. `interaction_key_mapping_triggered` fires
at the action as for the player's click; `key_mapping_pre` is not asked.
Queued actions drain oldest first, at most 64 entries per queue per drain, with at most
1024 pending. Excess entries wait for later drains (normally later client ticks); hotbar
selection can drain more than once per tick. A full queue refuses the new entry and returns
normally, logging only its first refusal for that queue's lifetime. These bounds also apply
to physical input queued through the same routes.

Side: client.
The clipboard's text (`KeyboardHandler.getClipboard`), empty when it holds none,
while the game handles a key, mouse or typed-text event: a mod's key or screen hook
pasting into its own field. None at any other moment (a tick, a frame, a packet),
so no mod reads the clipboard without the player doing something, and None on a
server.

Side: client.
Takes one click off mod `mod_id`'s registered mapping `id` (`KeyMapping.consumeClick`):
true when it had one. A press, each auto-repeat while its key is held, and a mouse press
add one, with no screen open and its conflict context and modifiers active, from the
window or the control socket alike; a screen opening drops them all. False for an
unregistered id.

Side: client.
Where the mouse is, in GUI pixels.

Side: client.
Whether mod `mod_id`'s registered mapping `id` is held (`KeyMapping.isDown`): its key or
mouse button is down and its conflict context and modifiers are active. False for an
unregistered id.

Side: client.
A vanilla mapping (`key.forward`, `key.jump`, `key.attack`…): whether
it is held (`KeyMapping.isDown`), and its key's name as Controls shows
it. `Ok(None)` for a mapping it doesn't answer for. Refuses an invalid
label with [`TextFormError`], including components deeper than 512 nodes.

Side: client.
Milliseconds on the game's own clock (`Util.getMillis`), counting from the game's start:
what a text field's cursor blinks by and what tells a double click from two clicks.
Only differences between two readings mean anything.

Side: client.
The saved key and modifiers for an owner-bound registration, or its declared default.

Side: client.
The current window modifier keys in the same GLFW encoding as input hooks.
Cleared when the window loses focus; available even outside a world.

Side: client.
Playing, with nothing over the world: keys and zoom apply.

Side: client.
Mod `mod_id`'s events since its last poll (at most 256 wait).

Side: client.
Puts `text` on the clipboard (`KeyboardHandler.setClipboard`) on the same terms as
`native_clipboard_text` reads it. False, with nothing copied, at any other moment or
on a server; empty text copies nothing, as vanilla's.

Side: client.
Holds the vanilla gameplay mapping `key` down or lets it go (`KeyMapping.setDown`): the
held state its key gives it, without the click a press adds. `key` is a mapping of the
movement, gameplay or inventory category (`key.attack`, `key.use`, `key.sprint`,
`key.forward`, `key.hotbar.1`...); a toggled mapping (sneak, sprint, attack, use with their
toggle option on) flips on `true`, as `ToggleKeyMapping.setDown` does. The client tick's
key step acts on it with all its checks: a held use repeats every four ticks, a held attack
goes on breaking the block. With a screen or overlay open a press does nothing, and opening
one lets go of every mapping, as `KeyMapping.releaseAll` does. `key_mapping_pre` is not
asked: it is about physical keys.
methods.signature: fn set_mapping_down(&mut self, _: &str, _: bool) -> Result<(), MappingError>

traits.doc: Lines a client mod hands the player's narrator (`Minecraft.getNarrator()`).

methods.doc:
Side: client.
Has the narrator say `text` as a system message, through the same
`GameNarrator` the game's own narration uses: `Narration::Now` is
`saySystemNow` (cuts off what is being said), `Narration::Queued` is
`saySystemQueued`. The player's Narrator option, the voice volume and
the narrator's log of recent lines apply as to vanilla's lines. The
text is the component's plain string (`Component.getString`) in the
current language, bounded only by the component's own form limits.
Nothing reaches the server. Refused with nothing said, by name, as
[`NarrateError`] lists: an empty line, the option Off or Chat only, or
no speech. Available from client setup on, on native and wasm alike.
methods.signature: fn narrate(&mut self, _: &text::Text, _: Narration) -> Result<(), NarrateError>

Side: client.
A snapshot of the current audio preferences.

Side: client.
