Side: client.
A snapshot of the current graphics preferences.

Side: client.
A snapshot of the current GUI and accessibility preferences. Its
`gui_scale` is only the option, where 0 means automatic; read
[`Self::gui_scale`] for the scale the window applies.

Side: client.
The GUI scale in effect (`Window.getGuiScale`), at least 1; none on a
server or when no window exists. Vanilla's `Window.calculateScale`
resolves it from the GUI Scale option and the window size: the option is
a maximum (0 = automatic, not a guarantee), and with the Unicode font
forced an odd result is raised by one. This read returns the scale the
window applies, never a separate recomputation. The framebuffer size
stays `native_physical_window_size()`; divide it by this scale, rounding
up, for the GUI-scaled width and height
(`Window.getGuiScaledWidth/Height`).

Side: client.
A snapshot of the current input preferences.

traits.doc: The client host's methods of the `client_render` area, implemented by the game and reached through [`crate::ClientHost`].

methods.doc:
Side: client.
Published asset/data read: available in Setup, Reloading and World.
For a client mod: what each resolved block state draws on its six sides, preserving
its properties without reparsing names. Resolve states once at load. Each face's sprite (array and
layer, as `WorldDrawn::block_sprites` cuts them) and its texture by the name `cube` and `quad` take,
where it lies on the side, how its texture runs across it (`FaceSprite::quad_on` draws it on another
block's box, turned as its model turns it), its tint source and index (`block_tint_color`) and
whether it is cut out, translucent or animated; its particle sprite; whether it is a plain
cube. None for a block the game does not know. The model is the state's first random variant. API
380.

Side: client.
Published asset/data read: available in Setup, Reloading and World.
For a client mod: changes each time the resources load (a resource pack turned on or off can move every
sprite): ask `native_block_sprites` again then. API 380.

Side: client.
For a client mod drawing a block's faces itself (a copycat drawing its material's, from
`block_sprites`): the 0xRRGGBB colour a face of `state` with tint index `tint_index`
(`FaceSprite::tint_index`) is multiplied by at `pos`, as the chunk mesher tints it there
(`BlockColors.getColor`, biome blend included: grass, foliage and water follow the biome
around `pos`). None for an untinted face (-1, or an index past the state's tints). Reads
this client's copy of the world.

Side: client.
Published asset/data read: available in Setup, Reloading and World.
For a client mod: where GUI sprite `sprite` lies in the GUI atlas and its size, none for one the atlas lacks
(a server's metrics-only atlas lacks them all). The atlas names vanilla's sprites by path alone
(`gui/sprites/container/slot`) and a mod's with its namespace (`mymod:gui/panel`).
Retire retained model copies; use [`InstanceGroupRef::destroy`].
Set the drawn length; use [`InstanceGroupRef::set_len`].
methods.signature: fn instance_group_set_len(&self, _: InstanceGroupRef, _: u32) -> Result<(), GroupError>

methods.doc: Replace the group pose; use [`InstanceGroupRef::set_group_transform`].
Atomically overwrite retained model copies; use [`InstanceGroupRef::write`].
methods.signature: fn instance_group_write(&self, _: InstanceGroupRef, _: u32, _: &[ModelInstance]) -> Result<(), GroupError>

methods.doc:
Side: client.
A mod's own RGBA image, uploaded into the HUD atlas slot
`MOD_IMAGE_SPRITE` and drawn with
`native_sprite`: its own source rectangle crops and stretches it. `rgba`
is `width * height` pixels of four bytes, each side at most
`MOD_IMAGE_SIZE`; false when it is not that
size. The upload costs a texture patch of the image, so send one when the
image changed, not every frame.

The slot exists whenever a client mod, native or wasm, is loaded: the atlas packs it at
load and on a resource reload, with no mixin and no opt-in. It is one image for all mods
together: a second mod's write replaces the first's.
methods.signature: fn mod_image(&mut self, _: u32, _: u32, _: &[u8]) -> bool

methods.doc:
Side: client.
Asks `biome_colors` again for every biome and, when the colours
differ from those in use, rebuilds every loaded section and the far
terrain with them (`LevelRenderer.allChanged`, as changing Biome Blend
does). Call it when your colours change (a new season, a new day of a
slow fade) and once when the player joins, not every frame: a rebuild
takes the workers a few seconds.

Side: client.
Asks `block_render_visibility` again for every state and, when the answers differ
from those in use, remeshes every loaded section with them. Call it when your answer changes (a toggle key, a scan
finishing) and once when the player joins, not every frame: a rebuild takes the workers a
few seconds. With no part answering, nothing is asked and the mesher keeps its no-mod path.

Side: client.
Published asset/data read: available in Setup, Reloading and World.
For a client mod reading the player's own block textures (resource packs included) on the CPU: a map
averaging each block's top colour, a software renderer. Each sprite's (`block_sprites`, `texture_sprites`)
RGBA8, rows top to bottom, square, every one the arrays' edge (`rgba.len()` is edge × edge × 4): the pixels
the arrays were filled with when the resources loaded, so an animated sprite's is the frame it starts on.
None for a sprite past the arrays' layers, and for all of them on a client that loaded no pixels. The
pixels are kept compressed once the GPU has them: one call uncompresses them all once, so ask for every
sprite at once and again only when `block_sprites_version` changes. `Err`, reading nothing, for more than
256 MiB of pixels in one call (`MAX_SPRITE_PIXEL_BYTES`, the default texture budget: every layer fits
unless the player raised `textureBudgetMiB`; ask in parts then).

Side: client.
Published asset/data read: available in Setup, Reloading and World.
For a client mod: each texture's sprite by name (`minecraft:block/stone`, `block/stone`), none for one no
model uses. API 380.

traits.doc: Read-only component resolution and access to the client tooltip font.

methods.doc:
Side: client.
`Font.split(FormattedText, width)`: wrap a component at `width` unscaled
GUI pixels. Lines retain styles, resolve the current language and use
the same active font as tooltip layout. Newlines force breaks; a width
below one follows vanilla's one-pixel minimum, without rejecting input.
Available outside drawing on native and wasm alike.

Side: client.
`Component.getString()`: resolve a component to its plain characters,
including current-language translations, arguments, key names and siblings.
Styles do not contribute characters; literal legacy formatting codes remain
in the string, as in vanilla. Available outside drawing, including client
setup, on native and wasm. Invalid components return their boundary error.
Action keybind IDs such as `key.jump` resolve through the client's current
key binding to their assigned physical key, matching vanilla KeybindContents.

Side: client.
`Component.getVisualOrderText()`: current-language, styled characters in
visual order, including bidi shaping and mirroring. Available outside
drawing on native and wasm, including client setup. Invalid components
return the same boundary errors as `text_string`. Sink indices are local
UTF-16 offsets, not offsets into the input component tree.
Action keybinds resolve to their assigned keys as in `text_string`.
No NeoForge hook counterpart is documented.

Side: client.
`Font.width(FormattedText)`: the width of a component in unscaled GUI
pixels, using the current language, styles and resource-pack fonts.
Available outside a draw, including client setup and tooltip-component
sizing. Like `ClientTooltipComponent.getWidth(Font)`, this measures with
the rendering client's active font, not a font chosen by the mod.
Build owned components with `Text`, or validate a flat `TextForm` with
`Text::try_from(form)`. Invalid component input returns its boundary error.

traits.doc: The client host's methods of the `client_view` area, implemented by the game and reached through [`crate::ClientHost`].

methods.doc:
Side: client.
The most recently extracted world frame's camera, if one exists.
During GUI rendering this is the current frame, including bob/spin and FOV.

Side: client.
The entity the view follows (`Minecraft.getCameraEntity`): the entity a server attached
the camera to, else the local player. None outside a client world.

Side: client.
The window's camera type (`Options.getCameraType`), including its latest pending request.

Side: client.
For a client mod drawing a map past the loaded chunks: each column's surface as this window's far
terrain (the LOD Distance setting) holds it, whether or not the chunk is loaded. It is the finest
far tile sampled there, so a far column is the reduced surface of a cell up to many blocks wide, and
it comes from wherever the far terrain does (this world's generator, the server's offer, the chunks
kept from earlier visits). None for a column no tile covers yet, and for every
column while far terrain is off or not started; the tiles follow the camera, so a column far from it
can go back to None. Inside the loaded chunks read them instead (`client_surface_heights`): a tile can
lag an edit. `Err`, reading nothing, for no client world (the title screen) or more than 65,536
columns (`MAX_COLUMNS`).

Side: client.
Each column's height by `heightmap` in the world this window shows
(`LevelReader.getHeight(type, x, z)` on a client level): one above the highest block that
counts on that map, from the blocks the server has sent, none for a column whose chunk this
client does not hold. `Err`, reading nothing, for no client world (the title screen) or more
than 65,536 columns (`MAX_COLUMNS`).
methods.signature: fn client_surface_heights(&self, _: &[(i32, i32)], _: Heightmap) -> Result<Vec<Option<i32>>, String>

methods.doc:
Side: client.
The clock of the world this window shows, for client mods: its game
time and time of day as the server last sent them
(`ClientboundSetTimePacket`), advanced each tick between packets; none
on the title screen.

Side: client.
The ordinary block-or-entity pick (Minecraft.hitResult), using the
game's targeting ray, reach and occlusion. None without a client world
or on a miss. Entity hits carry this client level's epoch. Unlike
native_view_hit, this never traces distant terrain.

Side: client.
Read effective HUD visibility independently of first-person hands.

Side: client.
The applied client pause state, not whether a pause screen is open.

Side: client.
The local player's item use as the client sees it: the hand, ticks used and ticks left
(`isUsingItem`, `getUsedItemHand`, `getTicksUsingItem`, `getUseItemRemainingTicks`).
None when the player uses no item or no client world is open. Sends nothing.

Side: client.
Whether F3's debug screen leaves `corner` free this frame for a box `render_gui_post`
places: false for a corner it takes (`DebugScreenOverlay`), both top corners while it
is open (its left and right columns) and a bottom corner while one of its charts is
drawn there. Only F3: read [`Self::hud_mode`] for whether the HUD is drawn at all (F1).

Side: client.
World point `at` projected on this frame's screen (`GameRenderer.projectPointToScreen`):
normalised device x and y, -1 to 1 across the screen (x to the right, y up), and depth z
(reversed: nearer is larger). The view is the camera's rotation without bob or spin, as
vanilla's. Unlike vanilla, None for a point behind the camera or a non-finite `at`; also None
outside a world, before extraction, and between render frames. Supported during GUI,
screen and world drawing after camera extraction. In GUI pixels of a [`DrawContext`] of size
`[w, h]`: `((x + 1) / 2 * w, (1 - y) / 2 * h)`.

Side: client.
The first block along the view within `distance` (at most 1024), past the loaded chunks over the distant terrain.

Side: client.
Points the view at `entity` (`Minecraft.setCameraEntity`), as a server's camera packet
does; the local player's own ref puts it back. True when the view now follows it; false,
with nothing changed, for a stale ref, an entity this window is not shown, or one the
camera cannot follow (only the local player and mobs). While the view is off the player,
the player sends no moves (`LocalPlayer.isControlledCamera`). When the camera entity is
removed, the view returns to the local player. A mod can also release the view by calling
this with the player's ref; this client-only selection does not notify the server.

Side: client.
Request the window's camera type without cycling, also from shared-host callbacks.
The last request wins and [`Self::camera_type`] reports it immediately. Requests before
or during `camera_pose` apply to that frame's camera, FOV and spectator post effects;
later requests apply at the next frame's camera extraction. Explicit pose overrides
remain unchanged when vanilla placement is refreshed. No cycle hook is emitted.

Side: client.
Select HUD and hand visibility, including after vanilla F1 input handling.
Other first-person hand restrictions and render cancellation still apply.

Side: client.
Turns the local player's view to `yaw` and `pitch` (degrees), as `setYRot` and `setXRot`
store them: yaw as given (not wrapped; the server wraps it), pitch `% 360` then clamped to
-90..90. The previous-frame angles move by the same amount, as `Entity.turn` does for the
mouse, so the view doesn't jump for a frame. Sends no packet: the game's own player sync of
this client tick sends the look in its one move packet, only while the camera is the player
(the rotation-only packet when riding); a call after that step goes out the next tick.
`NotFinite`, changing nothing, for a NaN or infinite value; `NoWorld` outside a client world.
methods.signature: fn set_local_rotation(&mut self, _: f32, _: f32) -> Result<(), LocalRotationError>

methods.doc:
Side: client.
Set the window's targeting controls for subsequent picks. False, without changing any
control, outside a client world or for a stale/self entity. Entity range, item attack
range and (unless enabled here) occlusion are checked again when attacking. This does
not change server reach checks or attack cooldowns. None clears an entity override.

Side: client.
Current targeting controls. Stale entity overrides are omitted. Reach comes from the
player's vanilla interaction-range attributes, including server and equipment modifiers:
this is the read for the player's block and entity reach.

Side: client.
The first block along the view within `RAYCAST_MAX`, and its distance.

traits.doc: The host's methods both sides share of the `client_view` area, implemented by the game and reached through [`Host`].

methods.doc:
Side: both.
Collision boxes in block-local coordinates with an empty collision context.

traits.doc: The client host's methods of the `config` area, implemented by the game and reached through [`crate::ClientHost`].

methods.doc:
Side: client.
The calling mod's old settings from `horizon-extras.txt`, when it is the official mod
that took over a built-in extra (`fps_overlay`, `keystrokes`, `minimap`, `zoom`): each
of that extra's keys the file has a line for, with the value the extra used, as it wrote
it (`("fpsCorner", "top_left")`). A written key doesn't mean the player changed it: the
game writes every key once any extra differs from its default, so a line can hold the
extra's default. Empty for any other mod (the file isn't read), outside a mod's call,
for a player who never changed the extras, and for a file that isn't a regular UTF-8
file of at most 1 MiB. Read-only and read from disk on each call: a port reads it once,
keeps what it takes in its own settings, and remembers that it did.

Side: client.
The calling mod's toggle `key` (`Registrar::register_setting`): the player's choice, else
its default. None when the mod registered no toggle by that key.

Side: client.
The index of the option the player picked for the calling mod's choice `key`, else its
default. None when the mod registered no choice by that key.

Side: client.
The calling mod's colour `key`, `0xRRGGBB`: the player's choice, else its default. None
when the mod registered no colour by that key.

Side: client.
The calling mod's range `key`: the player's value, else its default; a kept value outside
the range reads as the default. None when the mod registered no range by that key.

Side: client.
The selected language's text for a translation key (`Component.translatable`'s lookup), `None`
when no language layer defines it.

traits.doc: The host's methods both sides share of the `config` area, implemented by the game and reached through [`Host`].

methods.doc:
Side: both.
The calling mod's own files in the game's `config/` folder, beside
`options.txt` (beside `server.properties` on a dedicated server):
its folder `config/<mod id>/` and the files beside it named
`<mod id>.<ext>` or `<mod id>-<rest>`, as Fabric and NeoForge mods
keep theirs. The service is bound to the mod whose hook or part is
running, so a mod never names its id and can't reach another mod's
files; a world's `serverconfig/` is read only through
`config_loading`.

Side: both. The calling mod's bulk files in
`horizon-mod-data/<mod id>/` in the game folder, never scanned as
settings or config. Paths omit the mod id; `ConfigPath::root()` names
its root. Horizon allows at most `DATA_FILE_MAX` bytes per file.

Side: both.
The level in place (`minecraft:overworld`), for a hook that isn't told
which it runs in.
Physical process, not the logical side of this hook.
Exact Minecraft version supported by this process.
Horizon version printed in crash reports.

Side: both.
The instance (game) folder, which its players share: `saves/`,
`resourcepacks/`, `shaderpacks/` and `horizon-mods/` are in it, and the
title's screens create worlds and read packs there. A world's own
`datapacks/` is in that world's folder (`saves/<world>/datapacks`).
The folder the game runs in (`--player-dir` moves a player's options
and servers only, not the instance). Nothing is created.

Not on wasm: a path in the game's file system, which a wasm mod has none of; a wasm mod
reads its own data and assets through reload listeners.
methods.wasm_reason: a path in the game's file system, which a wasm mod has none of; a wasm mod reads its own data and assets through reload listeners.

methods.doc:
Side: both.
Whether the player left mod `mod_id` on in Options > Mods. A mod
turned off does nothing (check this first in each hook) until the
launcher's next build leaves it out.

The engine's `DataVersion` written into level data and chunks.
Constant on both sides, including before a world is open; this describes this
game build, not the version of a remote server or an older save.

Side: both.
Whether the server's current tick still has time before the next one is
due (`MinecraftServer.haveTime`, NeoForge's `ServerTickEvent.hasTime` and
`LevelTickEvent.hasTime`): a mod doing optional work in `server_tick` or
`level_tick_pre`/`level_tick_post` skips it when this is false. Always
true on a client, and outside a scheduled tick.

Side: both.
Keeps a mod's registered setting `key`. Another mod's id or an unregistered key keeps
nothing. A successful write invalidates the typed read cache for this data folder and key;
a failed write leaves it unchanged. This raw write does not fire `setting_changed`.

Side: both.
A mod's setting `key` (one file per key in `native_data_dir`). A mod reads only its own:
another mod's id or a key not registered by that owner gives None.

traits.doc: The server host's methods of the `config` area, implemented by the game and reached through [`ServerHost`].

methods.doc:
Side: server.
Counts every player's play packets by id and direction from now on, or no longer, for
`player_take_packet_counts`. While on, each packet costs its connection a lock and a
map update; off, one atomic read. One switch for the whole server, shared by every
mod. False on a client.

Side: server.
The entity broadcast range the server hosts with, in percent of vanilla's range
(`entity-broadcast-range-percentage` of server.properties, `/serversettings`). 100 when
no server is hosting a world, as vanilla's default is.

Side: server.
Read the server-wide rule from the first server hook onward.
Returns `UnknownRule` for an unknown id; level reads use the same store.

Side: server.
Every current rule in the one server-wide store, by namespaced id.
Readable from `server_about_to_start`, before any level exists.
Level game-rule reads use this same store once their level exists.
Startup opt-in for test-only content. Test registration runs regardless.

Side: server.
Times every mob's own tick (its riders inside it) from now on, or no longer, summed by
level and mob type for `take_mob_costs`, as a profiler samples them: while on, two
clock reads and a map update a mob; off, one thread-local read. Apart from the server's
own performance report, so both can run. Off drops what was sampled. False on a client.

Side: server.
The retained server reload listeners of the last successful reload.

Side: server.
Sets the server's simulation distance live, as `PlayerList.setSimulationDistance`
does: every player is sent `ClientboundSetSimulationDistancePacket`, and the chunks
around the players tick to the new distance from the next tick. `server.properties`
is not written. False for a distance outside 2 to 32, and off a dedicated server.

Side: server.
Sets the server's view distance live, as `PlayerList.setViewDistance` (and the
management protocol's `serversettings/view_distance/set`) do: every player is sent
`ClientboundSetChunkCacheRadiusPacket` and their chunks follow, each up to what their
client asked for. `server.properties` is not written, so a restart goes back to it.
False for a distance outside 2 to 32, and off a dedicated server (an integrated
server follows its window's option).

Side: server.
The server's simulation distance in chunks (`PlayerList.getSimulationDistance`,
`simulation-distance`): how far around each player chunks tick. None off a server open
to players.

Side: server.
The server's view distance in chunks (`PlayerList.getViewDistance`, `view-distance`):
how far players are sent chunks at most. None off a server open to players.

Side: server.
Sets the server's tick rate, as `/tick rate` does (`ServerTickRateManager.setTickRate`):
the game ticks `rate` times a second from the next tick on, an autosave wait already
running is shortened when the new rate asks for less, and `server_tick_rate_changed`
fires. The players' clients follow on the next sync. False, with nothing changed, for a
rate outside 1 to 10000 (the command's range), one that isn't finite, a call from
inside `server_tick_rate_changed` (which would hear itself again without end), or on a
client.

Side: server.
The server's tick rate (20 unless `/tick rate` changed it) and the
milliseconds its ticks took on average lately, as `/tick query`
reports them. The ticks a second it keeps up is the rate, or
1000 / milliseconds when that is lower.

Side: server.
The last 100 server ticks' durations in nanoseconds, as
`MinecraftServer.getTickTimesNanos` lays them out: the tick numbered `n` at index
`n % 100`, 0 where none was recorded yet. Sort a copy for percentiles; `tick_stats`
has the average.

Side: server. The calling mod's bulk files in the current save's
`horizon-mod-data/<mod id>/`, copied, backed up and deleted with that
save. Paths omit the mod id. Calls refuse with `NoWorld` before a
save is open; this service never outlives its borrowed world host.

Side: server.
The open world's folder (`world/`, beside its `level.dat`): a server
mod keeps its data in a folder of its own there, so the world's
backups carry it. None when no world is open.

Not on wasm: a path in the game's file system, which a wasm mod has none of; a wasm mod
keeps world data in level attachments.
methods.wasm_reason: a path in the game's file system, which a wasm mod has none of; a wasm mod keeps world data in level attachments.

traits.doc: The server host's methods of the `displays` area, implemented by the game and reached through [`ServerHost`].

methods.doc:
Side: server.
Narrows an entity to a display, or None for another kind, a stale
handle or a client.

traits.doc: The client host's methods of the `draw` area, implemented by the game and reached through [`crate::ClientHost`].

methods.doc:
Side: client.
Entity model layer `layer` baked into its `ModelPart` tree, each part
at its pose, as `EntityModelSet.bakeLayer` bakes it: one a native mod
registered (`register_layer_definitions`), or vanilla's, by the name
`entity-models.json` gives it (`minecraft:zombie#main`,
`minecraft:player#main`). The tree is the caller's own copy: bake it
once, as a renderer does, and set its parts' poses each frame. None
for a layer neither has. A vanilla layer no mob has (a player's, a
chest's) is read from the resources each call, so slow. API
@API:model_layers@.

Side: client.
Fluid `fluid`'s name as the lang names it (`fluid_type.<mod>.<name>`, vanilla's by its block),
else its path in words.

traits.doc: The client host's methods of the `effects` area, implemented by the game and reached through [`crate::ClientHost`].

methods.doc:
Side: client.
ClientLevel.addParticle: submits one local particle through the ordinary provider, camera-distance, setting and population limits. False without a loaded client world or for non-finite input. True means submitted, not necessarily visible.

Side: client.
The output device the options ask for (`Options.soundDevice`).

Side: client.
The output devices sound can play on (`SoundEngine.getAvailableSoundDevices`).

Side: client.
`ParticleEngine.clearParticles`: every particle and emitter goes before the next
frame is drawn or the next particle tick runs, whichever comes first. It takes
`&self`, so a screen or render hook can ask, as with `native_play_local_sound`.
False on a server.

Side: client.
`ClientLevel.createFireworks`: draws a firework's explosions in this client's world as a
bursting rocket draws them (`FireworkParticles.Starter`): each explosion's shape, colours,
fade colours, trail and twinkle, one every other tick. The blast, and the crackle after a
twinkling explosion, play only when `request.audible`, as for a rocket that isn't silent.
Only the picture and the sound: no entity, no damage, nothing sent to the server, and other
players see nothing (a mod's server half tells each client half to draw it). True means
queued; false on a server, without a client player or world, for non-finite input or for
more than 256 explosions. API @API:client_fireworks@.

Side: client.
A small local vanilla particle; caller should rate-limit emission.

Muffles the game's sounds for a while, as ears ringing after a close
blast hear them: `amount` (0 to 1) of every sound's volume is taken
away and `lowpass` (0 to 1) dulls it, from untouched to a 300 Hz
low-pass. Both start in full and fade back in a straight line over
`ticks` client ticks, held while the game is paused. The sound events in
`exempt` (`mymod:ear.ringing`) play clearly through it, those already
playing too, so the mod's own ringing stays sharp. Everything else is
muffled, music and the interface's clicks included. A new call replaces
the muffle in place; `ticks` 0 ends it at once. Nothing changes while no
mod calls it. False, with nothing changed, on a server, for an amount or
strength outside 0 to 1, or for an exempt event that isn't
`namespace:path` or more than 64 of them. API @API:muffle_sounds@.
methods.signature: fn muffle_sounds(&mut self, _: f32, _: f32, _: u32, _: &[&str]) -> bool

methods.doc:
Side: client.
The particles alive in the client's level (`ParticleEngine.countParticles`): 0 once
a clear is asked, and on a server.

Side: client.
Plays `sound` for this player only (`SoundPlay`'s event: `minecraft:ui.button.click`,
or a mod's own from its `assets/<id>/sounds.json`): nothing is sent to the server, and
other players don't hear it. It takes `&self`, so a screen, key or mouse hook can play
one: the sound is queued and starts at the next audio update (once a client tick),
`after` ticks counted from then (0 to 1200, a minute; `SoundEngine.playDelayed`). `SoundPlay::ui` plays it at the listener as an interface sound
(`SimpleSoundInstance.forUI`); `SoundPlay::at` at a position in the client's level,
fading with distance (`volume` past 1 carries farther, 16 blocks times the volume), as
thunder heard after the flash or a blast heard when its shock wave arrives. Its
`SoundRef` follows and controls this play: `state`, `stop` and `fade`. None, with nothing
played, on a server or for a value out of range; an event the resources don't have plays
nothing, as vanilla's, and its handle reads `Stopped` once the update has tried it.
Every sound event the client's resources have (`SoundManager.getAvailableSounds`).

traits.doc: The host's methods both sides share of the `entities` area, implemented by the game and reached through [`Host`].

methods.doc:
Side: both.
The entity `id` (the id events carry) as a handle for the `entity_*`
methods: None with no world open, or for no such entity in the level
in place or among the server's players. On a client (API
@API:client_entity_refs@), any entity the server shows this window,
this window's own player included. API 373.

Side: server.
Whether the entity is still in the world and not removed (`Entity.isValid`): a mob queued for
removal, a frame or painting broken, and a stale handle are not valid. Only the handle's
entity is asked about; the answer changes nothing.

Side: both.
Where the entity `entity` names is now, as its Part state (`EntityPartState`) checks it:
resident in the level this host is in, out of its lists for its own tick, resident in
another level, or gone (removed or its removal pending, unloaded, moved under a new
id, or a handle of another world open). On a client, in place for an entity the
client has in the level it shows.

Side: both.
Whether `id` names an entity type in the game's registry (`EntityType.byString` finds it),
such as `minecraft:zombie` or a mod's type. The check is literal: `id` is compared as
written, with its namespace (a bare `zombie` is not in the registry). The answer comes
from the loaded entity-type registry, which loads with the first world, so it is false
while no world has loaded it. Use it to validate a configured id before a mod acts on it,
for example whitelist or blacklist entries, which the game drops when unknown.

Side: both.
The level `dimension` (`minecraft:the_nether`) as a handle: on a client,
the level it shows, whatever the server calls it, and each level the
server opened for viewing (`horizon:levels`) while that view is open. A
viewed level's handle answers its block reads from its own world:
`block_state`, `block`, `block_property`, `clip`, `collision_boxes`,
`has_collisions`, and the fluid reads built on `block_state`
(`fluid_shape`, `fluid_height`, `fluid_height_for_camera`,
`fluid_can_be_replaced_with`). Its other reads, its entity reads and
every write refuse it. It answers None while the server has the level
closed; a close and a later open within the same client level make the
old handle read again. A login, a reconfiguration or a respawn into
another level replaces the client level: the old handle stays stale and
the mod asks `host.level` again. None with no world open, or for a
dimension the server hasn't loaded. API 373.

traits.doc: The server host's methods of the `entities` area, implemented by the game and reached through [`ServerHost`].

methods.doc:
Side: server.
Finds a loaded entity by UUID in the server level in place for this
hook. Returns `None` for unloaded entities, entities in another level,
and dragon parts. It also returns `None` for entities held out of
lookup, taken from their resident storage, unavailable under a scoped
item loan, queued for removal, or vehicles undergoing destruction.
The lookup leaves entity and level state alone.

Side: server.
The experience orbs of the server level `dimension` whose box meets
the box `min`..`max`, in the level's order: what a mod reads before it
cancels an orb in `entity_join_level`, to give its points with
`PlayerRef::give_experience_points`. Empty for a level not in place, on a
client of a server and for a bound that is not finite (NaN or infinite); a
minimum above its maximum is the same box with the two swapped (`AABB`).

Side: server.
Writes the experience orb `id`'s `value` (the points a pickup gives), `count`
(orbs merged into it, each worth `value`) and `age` (ticks lived; an orb
despawns at 6000); a `None` is left as it is. Signed values are preserved,
including zero and negative values.
False, and nothing written, for an orb not in the server level `dimension`,
a `count` of 0 or above `i32::MAX`, a `value` outside -32768..=32767 (a save
keeps `Value` as a short and `Count` as an int, so a write it accepts reloads
unchanged), and on a client of a server. In `experience_orb_merge`, a write to
`into` is the merged orb.
methods.signature: fn set_experience_orb(&mut self, _: &str, _: u32, _: Option<i32>, _: Option<u32>, _: Option<u32>) -> bool

methods.doc:
Side: server.
Throws a falling block of `state` from `pos` (its bottom centre) at
`velocity` (blocks a tick) in the level in place, `dimension`: it
falls, lands and places itself as sand does, or drops as an item
where it can't. The block at `pos` is left as it is: take it away first
with `native_set_block` to make a block fall out of the world. False,
with nothing thrown, on a client's copy of the world, for another
dimension, an air or unknown state, a chunk that isn't loaded, a value
that isn't finite, or with 1024 falling blocks in the level already.
Each axis of `velocity` is cut to 3.9.
methods.signature: fn spawn_falling_block(&mut self, _: &str, _: BlockState, _: [f64; 3], _: [f64; 3], _: Falling) -> bool

methods.doc:
Side: server.
Spawns an entity of `kind` (`minecraft:item_display`) at `pos` in the
level in place, `dimension`, from `nbt` (its compound, as `/summon
<kind> <pos> <nbt>` takes it; passengers included): its id. None on a
client's copy of the world, for another dimension, a position outside
`/summon`'s bounds, a chunk that isn't loaded, a kind Horizon can't
load, or one a mod kept out (`entity_join_level`). Inside a transaction its join waits for
the root commit, so a mod keeping it out is not known at the call: the id is returned and
names nothing from the commit on.

traits.doc: Fixed-clock video export methods reached through [`crate::ClientHost`].

methods.doc:
Side: client.
The active mod-started export, or the most recent mod-started result if one has ended.
During `camera_pose` and the other frame hooks, `frame` is the index being prepared.
Control-socket exports do not appear here.

Side: client.
Reserves the output directory and queues a fixed-clock capture on an offscreen client.
The capture starts between callbacks. The nonzero request id is unique in this client
session. Each accepted request reports its outcome through `export_ended` unless the
game exits first. A capture in progress from any source prevents a new one.

Side: client.
Requests a graceful stop of the active mod export. The current frame and accepted
output drain before `export_ended`; a stop before frame zero still captures that frame.
Repeated stops during a mod export's drain are accepted. A control-socket export alone
returns `NotRunning`.

traits.doc: The host's current cauldron content table, including mod registrations.

methods.doc:
Side: both.
Contents registered for `block`, or none if absent or no table has been built.
Reads the current resource generation, including after reload.

Side: both.
Contents registered for `fluid`, or none if absent or no table has been built.

Side: both.
Current level of `state`, or none without registered contents or a built table.
Always-full contents answer their maximum level.

traits.doc: The host's methods both sides share of the `item_entities` area, implemented by the game and reached through [`Host`].

methods.doc:
Side: both.
Narrows an entity to a dropped item, or None for another kind, a
stale handle, a client, or an item temporarily taken out for ticking.

traits.doc: Item particle model resolution on the client.

methods.doc:
Resolve vanilla's `ItemParticleOption` for this stack using the ground
display context and seed 0, exactly like the game's eating particles.
Includes every resolved model layer's particle sprite, respecting resource
packs and stack component overrides. Returns `None` for an invalid stack
or unavailable resources/provider. Available in Setup, Reloading and World.
Resolve again after a resource reload; this read allocates the sprite list.

traits.doc: The client host's methods of the `items` area, implemented by the game and reached through [`crate::ClientHost`].

methods.doc:
Side: client.
`Enchantment.getMinCost(level)`: the enchanting power needed, or None for an unknown id.

Side: client.
Whether enchantment `id` can go on `item` (`Enchantment.isSupportedItem`).

Side: client.
Registered enchantments, in registry order.

Side: client.
Creative mode only: gives the player `count` of `item`
(`minecraft:diamond`) as taking it from the creative inventory does
(`ServerboundSetCreativeModeSlot`): the selected slot first, then the
hotbar, then the inventory. The count is cut to one stack.
methods.signature: fn give(&mut self, _: ItemKey, _: u32) -> Result<(), String>

methods.doc:
Side: client.
`ItemStack.getHoverName()` as plain text: the custom name, else a written book's non-blank
title, else the item's name in the client's language (potion contents, a head's owner and
the `item_name` component as vanilla). No rarity colour or italics. An invalid stack reads
an empty string.

traits.doc: The host's methods both sides share of the `items` area, implemented by the game and reached through [`Host`].

methods.doc:
Side: both.
Whether enchantments `a` and `b` may share an item (`Enchantment.areCompatible`), by the
world's enchantment definitions. API @API:item_components@.

Side: both.
`EntityType.is(TagKey)`: whether `entity_type` (`minecraft:player`) is in the entity
type tag `tag` (`minecraft:cannot_be_pushed_onto_boats`).

Side: both.
Item `item`'s cooking-fuel burn time in ticks (`FuelValues.burnDuration` of its `cooking_fuel`
component, the data pack's context int provider resolved), None where it is no fuel. API
@API:item_components@.

Side: both.
Item `item`'s chance to raise a composter's level (its `compostable` component's layers provider
resolved), None where it is not compostable. API @API:item_components@.

Side: both.
Item `item`'s default value of component `component`, in its prototype
(`Item.components().get`): `minecraft:max_damage` on an iron sword is `250`, data
packs' and native mods' changes included. Read from the item report's JSON, so a
number is an `Int`, `Long` or `Double` and a boolean a `Byte`. None where the item
hasn't the component, and for an unknown item.

Side: both.
The stack an SNBT item compound stands for, read as `ItemStack.CODEC` reads a saved
item: `{id:"minecraft:diamond_sword",count:1,components:{"minecraft:damage":5}}`
(`count` 1 when missing, `stone` is `minecraft:stone`). This API refuses with None:
text that is no SNBT compound or has anything but whitespace after it, a `count`
outside 1 to 99 (the codec's range; it is not clamped to 1), air, and an item this
world does not have. It also refuses text over 2 MiB and nesting past 512 levels. Those
two are this API's own safety bound, the one place it differs from vanilla: vanilla's
SNBT parser has no size or depth limit (very deep text ends in a stack overflow), and
2 MiB and 512 are binary NBT's limits, taken here so text a mod supplies cannot
overflow the parser.

Side: both.
Resolve an item once at load, including vanilla items, to its process-local identity.
None if the completed registry does not contain the identifier.

Side: both.
Default durability of the resolved item, or none if its metadata is unavailable.
Stack-specific component overrides are checked at the game's write boundary.

Side: both.
The most of the item `item` one slot holds (`Item.getDefaultMaxStackSize`),
or `None` for an unknown item: for a mod's container that fills or
merges stacks itself.

traits.doc: The server host's methods of the `items` area, implemented by the game and reached through [`ServerHost`].

methods.doc:
Side: server.
Drop one item as DefaultDispenseItemBehavior does. For a dispenser hook:
return this remainder in its answer with `CLICK`; the caller plays the
answer's event and smoke once. A client, another dimension or an unloaded
chunk keeps the input stack unchanged.
methods.signature: fn dispense_default(&mut self, _: &str, _: [i32; 3], _: Direction, _: item::item_stack::ItemStack) -> Result<Option<item::item_stack::ItemStack>, item::item_stack::StackWriteError>

methods.doc:
Side: server.
`DefaultDispenseItemBehavior.consumeWithRemainder`: one of `stack` is used and
`remainder` replaces it, a single `stack` by becoming it, else into the dispenser at
`pos` (`DispenserBlockEntity.insertItem`) or, where it doesn't fit, out of its front with
the click and smoke. What the slot holds then. A client, another dimension or an unloaded
chunk keeps `stack` unchanged.
methods.signature: fn dispense_with_remainder(&mut self, _: &str, _: [i32; 3], _: Direction, _: item::item_stack::ItemStack, _: item::item_stack::ItemStack) -> Result<Option<item::item_stack::ItemStack>, item::item_stack::StackWriteError>

Side: server.
Holds `stack` outside the world in a two-slot copy whose item may change, in the open
transaction `tx`: the [`ItemPlace::ScratchSlots`] a dispensed fluid container runs in
(`DispenseFluidContainer`), `stack` in its first slot. It lives as a
[`scratch_stack`](Self::scratch_stack) place does. None where `tx` is not open.
methods.signature: fn scratch_slots(&mut self, _: &Transaction, _: item::item_stack::ItemStack) -> Result<Option<ItemPlace>, item::item_stack::StackWriteError>

methods.doc:
Side: server.
Holds `stack` outside the world, in the open transaction `tx` (`ItemAccess.forStack`):
the [`ItemPlace::Scratch`] to run item capabilities against. It lives until the
outermost transaction closes, and an abort of the one that made it drops it. None
where `tx` is not open.
methods.signature: fn scratch_stack(&mut self, _: &Transaction, _: item::item_stack::ItemStack) -> Result<Option<ItemPlace>, item::item_stack::StackWriteError>

Side: server.
Takes the stack out of scratch place `place`, in `tx`, ending the place: none where it
is empty, no longer held, or not a scratch place.

Side: server.
Takes both slots out of two-slot place `place`, in `tx`, ending the place: what the
first holds and what the second caught. None where it is no longer held or not a
two-slot place.

The host's registry-wide key reads of the `keys` area, implemented by the game
and reached through [`Host`].

methods.doc:
Side: server. The biome in the installed world registry, or None on a client,
before world data is installed, or for an unknown id. Reacquire after reload.

Side: both.
The key of the block named `id`, for a name that only arrives at run time (data, config,
a command, a network message). `id` is the full registry name, `minecraft:stone` or
`mymod:machine`. None for a name the registry does not hold, and before the registry is
complete (during registration, use `Registrar::block_key`). Does not allocate.

Side: both.
Every block key in the registry's registration order: vanilla's first, then
mod blocks in the order they registered. A block registry lists a name once
per state; this yields it once. Empty before the block table completes.

Side: both.
The key of the effect named `id`: the full registry name, `minecraft:speed` or
`mymod:rage`. None for a name the registry does not hold, and before the registry is
complete (during registration, use `Registrar::effect_key`). Does not allocate.

Side: both.
Every enchantment key in global sorted loaded-registry order, including
vanilla and mod data-pack entries together (`RegistryDataLoader` sorts by id).

Side: both.
Every built-in entity-type key in registry order (`BuiltInRegistries.ENTITY_TYPE`
order): vanilla's first, then mod types in the order they registered.
Side: both. Exact startup game-event id; None before registry completion or for an unknown id.

Side: both.
Every item key in the registry's registration order: vanilla's first, then
mod items in the order they registered. Empty before the item table completes.

Side: both.
Every built-in menu-type key in registry order (`BuiltInRegistries.MENU` order):
vanilla's first, then mod types in the order they registered.

Side: both.
Entry identifiers in the current table, each once. None for an unavailable or unknown
registry; an available empty registry returns an empty list.

Side: both.
Resolve a canonical entry in the current side's live registry. None for an
unknown registry or entry, or before that registry is available.

Side: both.
Membership in the current side's merged tags. None for an unavailable registry or
entry; an absent tag, or a tag not containing the entry, returns false.

Side: both.
The network id of `name` in `registry` (`Registry.getId`): the number a packet carries for
it, for a mod that builds or reads raw packets (`minecraft:particle_type` and
`minecraft:flame`). Built-in registries answer their fixed ids, mod entries included;
data-driven ones (`minecraft:damage_type`, `minecraft:biome`, ...) answer the order the
server synced them in; custom data component types are included. A client reads its own
connection's registries, a server the ones it sends. The id holds for one connection and one
data reload: do not keep it across a reconnect, a reconfiguration or `/reload`. None for an
unknown registry or name, on a client before that registry was synced, and with no
connection. Allocates nothing; each registry is searched in order.

Side: both.
Find a loaded chunk in an open server level.

native, wasm or content package (Fabric's `FabricLoader.isModLoaded`,
NeoForge's `ModList.isLoaded`). The list is fixed at startup.

The entity as a living entity (vanilla's `LivingEntity`: a mob, a
player, an armor stand or the dragon), or None for another kind or a
stale handle.

On a client, only the local player is one: the client keeps the others'
equipment, effects and health only as far as it draws them. API 382.

traits.doc: Math selection reads available through [`Host`] on both sides.

methods.doc:
Side: both.
The native engine's fixed selection for the seven platform-dependent
Java Math operations. This read allocates nothing on the native path.
It identifies behavior, not the machine, and does not implement guest
math. See [`MathProfile`] for the exact mixed paths and guest limitations.

traits.doc: The client host's methods of the `menus` area, implemented by the game and reached through [`crate::ClientHost`].

methods.doc:
Side: client.
The local player in a logged-in client world.

traits.doc: The server host's methods of the `menus` area, implemented by the game and reached through [`ServerHost`].

methods.doc:
Side: server.
Closes the player's native menu (a `menu_closed` follows).

Side: server.
The menu `open_menu` opened that the player has open as window
`window` (the window id `open_menu`, `menu_clicked` and `menu_closed`
give). Its slots are written as `ItemPlace::MenuSlot` in a
transaction, and the client is sent each changed slot with the next
tick's container sync (`AbstractContainerMenu.broadcastChanges`), as
for any open menu. None for another window, a menu the game opened, or
a player who isn't here.

Side: server.
Replaces everything the player's open `open_menu` menu `window` shows with `items` (by
slot, padded with empty ones, extra ones dropped, as `open_menu` takes them) and sends
it at once as one `ClientboundContainerSetContentPacket`
(`AbstractContainerMenu.sendAllDataToRemote`), without reopening the menu: the title,
the cursor and the screen stay. Writing slots through `menu` sends each changed slot with
the next tick's sync instead; this is the whole-contents form, for a page turned or a
list rebuilt. Each refusal sends nothing and changes nothing, and is named by
`MenuItemsRefusal`: `Client`, `NoPlayer` (no placed player of that UUID), `NotOpen`
(`window` is not their open `open_menu` menu) and `Stack` (a stack the game's item
conversion refuses).
methods.signature: fn menu_set_items(&mut self, _: u128, _: i32, _: Vec<Option<item::item_stack::ItemStack>>) -> Result<(), MenuItemsRefusal>

methods.doc:
Side: server.
Opens a chest menu of `rows` rows (1 to 6) titled `title` for the
player, showing `items` (by slot, padded with empty ones), in place of
the menu they had open: its window id, a new one each time
(`ServerPlayer.openMenu`). The old menu closes as a close does, its
cursor stack going back to the player's inventory; `replace` says
whether the client is first sent a close for it
(`MenuProvider.shouldTriggerClientSideContainerClosingOnOpen`).
`MenuReplace::InPlace` changes the title and rows without the client
centring the mouse again. Packets for the old window are ignored. The
items of an open menu change through its slots (`menu`), not by
opening it again.
methods.signature: fn open_menu(&mut self, _: u128, _: u8, _: text::Text, _: Vec<Option<item::item_stack::ItemStack>>, _: MenuReplace) -> Result<Option<i32>, item::item_stack::StackWriteError>

and the caller's `mod_slot` named, so a mod can apply a per-wearer
level. Call this from the mod's own equip moment; the engine's

write is committed. Call this after the mod has written its stack.
