traits.doc: The host's methods both sides share of the `mod_state` area, implemented by the game and reached through [`Host`].

methods.doc:
Side: both.
Capture a SNAPSHOT of the current dimension's attachment residency and values.
Later changes require a fresh query. Removed-but-unswept entities may appear;
writes through stale holders fail. Values are neither cloned nor eagerly decoded.

Side: both.
The server-owned holders' attachments; `TYPE.get(host, holder)` reads
one. On a client it is the copy of what the server synced: `set` and
`remove` change only the copy.

traits.doc: The server host's methods of the `mod_state` area, implemented by the game and reached through [`ServerHost`].

methods.doc:
Side: server.
Validate captured residency against the current dimension immediately before
an ordinary journaled attachment write. This does not open a transaction.

Side: server.
Withdraws a task the calling mod scheduled: true if it was still waiting.

Side: server.
Asks for `Hooks::scheduled_task` to be called with `token` after `delay_ticks` server
ticks (`MinecraftServer.tell(new TickTask(getTickCount() + delay, ..))`; 0 and 1 both
mean the next tick, and a paused server does not advance it). Tasks due together run in
the order they were scheduled. Only inside a mod's hook; the task belongs to that mod and
is dropped with the world.
methods.signature: fn schedule_task(&mut self, _: u32, _: u64) -> Result<TaskId, ScheduleError>

methods.doc:
Side: server.
Closes the transaction `seal` ends, committed or aborted, aborting first any opened
inside it and left open. Refused when `seal` names no open transaction, so a mod ends
only a transaction it opened. `host.transaction` calls it.

Side: server.
The innermost open transaction, to write in (`Transaction.getCurrentOpenedTransaction`);
none when none is open. It names the transaction only: ending it still takes the seal its
opener holds.

Side: server.
How deeply `tx` is nested (`TransactionContext.depth`): 0 for the outermost, none for a
transaction that is not open.

Side: server.
Where the transaction system is (`Transaction.getLifecycle`): none open, one open, a
nested one closing, or the outermost closing while the game tells the world of a commit.

Side: server.
Opens a transaction, nested in the open one if any (`Transaction.open`), and gives back
the seal that ends it. `host.transaction` calls it; use that instead.

traits.doc: The client host's methods of the `network` area, implemented by the game and reached through [`crate::ClientHost`].

methods.doc:
Side: client.
Adds `line` to this client's chat HUD and history (vanilla's
`ChatComponent.addClientSystemMessage`): it shows here only, so
nothing is sent to the server. The Chat option's server-message filter
doesn't hide it (`GuiMessageSource.SYSTEM_CLIENT`), and
`client_chat_received` is not told: vanilla fires that event from
`ChatListener` for lines the server sent, not for lines the client adds
itself. Returns an error if the text exceeds the boundary's size or
nesting limits; rejected text is not added.
methods.signature: fn chat_line(&mut self, _: text::Text) -> Result<(), text::TextFormError>

methods.doc:
Side: client.
Leaves the server or the single-player world (NeoForge's
`IClientCommonPacketListenerExtension.disconnect(Component)`), at the end of this frame,
not inside the calling hook. With a reason, the disconnect screen shows it (a
single-player world is saved first); with none, it leaves as the pause menu's Disconnect
does. The request belongs to the world it was made in: one made while that world closes
is dropped, never carried into the next. A second call in the same frame replaces the
reason. The retained reason renders in the active language at draw and narration time;
literal text stays unchanged. `DisconnectError::Unavailable` when no server or world is joined.
Refuses text deeper than 512 component nodes before applying any changes.
methods.signature: fn disconnect(&mut self, _: Option<text::Text>) -> Result<(), DisconnectError>

methods.doc:
Side: client.
Opens the chat screen with `text` typed in for the player to finish and
send, as T and / open it; nothing is sent. Returns an error with no
player in a world or while another screen is open.

Side: client.
A mod's chat line or command (`/` first), sent as `send_chat` sends
it (ClientPacketListener.sendChat / sendCommand), to any server: no
chat history, and no client chat event (vanilla's `ClientChatEvent`
comes only from ChatScreen). An error when the player isn't in a
server's play state or the Chat option blocks the message. API
404.

Side: client.
Submits a vanilla play packet to any server, including unrelated plugin
payloads. The body is validated once and outgoing credit is reserved before
acceptance. Publication waits for the current root transaction to commit;
rollback, disconnect, or a protocol incarnation change cancels it.
Registered and engine-reserved channels are refused: use their payload or
service API. Unrelated plugin bodies retain vanilla's discard-codec limit.
No effects are applied locally. Sequence numbers, signatures, and client
state required by a packet remain the mod's responsibility. API 409.
methods.signature: fn send_packet(&mut self, _: ServerboundPlayPacket) -> Result<(), SendPacketError>

traits.doc: The server host's methods of the `network` area, implemented by the game and reached through [`ServerHost`].

methods.doc:
Side: server.
Sends `packet` to that player's client as it is (`ServerPlayer.connection.send`), as a
Paper plugin sends a packet through ProtocolLib or PacketEvents: a team, an objective, a
score, a Tab-list entry the server doesn't keep. Only that player gets it, at once, or
after the hook for the acting player. Nothing on the server changes, so the game may
later send its own state over it. Errors: `NotConnected` for a stale, offline or fake
player and on a client, `UnknownPacket` for a name that is not a clientbound play
packet, `InvalidBody` for a body that does not decode whole (or a custom payload on an
engine `horizon:` channel), and `PayloadTooLarge` for a custom payload past
`ClientboundCustomPayloadPacket.MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE`. A packet the client reads but
cannot apply is the mod's to get right.
methods.signature: fn player_send_packet(&mut self, _: PlayerRef, _: ClientboundPlayPacket) -> Result<(), SendPacketError>

traits.doc:
The typed payload token check both sides share, reached through [`Host`]: what
[`ToServer::send`] and [`ToClient::send`] run before they encode.

methods.doc:
Side: both.
Whether `token` is one this load's registrar handed out: the frozen declaration at its
slot has its id, protocol, direction and schema, and its owning mod is on. Anything
else (forged, from another load, of another type) is `StaleToken`, and nothing is sent.

traits.doc: Player-targeted sends, exposed naturally through [`PlayerRef::send_payload`].

methods.doc:
Side: server.
Queue exact application bytes for this live player's connection. The channel
must be declared locally and negotiated for the current phase and direction.
Publication waits for root commit; abort publishes nothing. Queued is not a
delivery acknowledgement. No generic registered-body or per-tick count cap applies.
methods.signature: fn player_send_payload(&mut self, _: PlayerRef, _: &PayloadId, _: PayloadBytes) -> Result<PayloadAccepted, PayloadSendError>

traits.doc: Client connection sends, available during configuration as well as play.

methods.doc:
Side: client.
Queue exact application bytes to the connected server, using the frozen
declaration for its current protocol. Optional absent channels return
UnsupportedPeer. Frame refusal and Backpressure write no application bytes.
The root transaction owns publication and cancellation on both native and wasm.
methods.signature: fn send_payload_to_server(&mut self, _: &PayloadId, _: PayloadBytes) -> Result<PayloadAccepted, PayloadSendError>

traits.doc: The client host's methods of the `players` area, implemented by the game and reached through [`crate::ClientHost`].

methods.doc:
Moves the window's player through `passage` (arismoko/horizon#3775), one its server told it of, as
Immersive Portals' client does: its feet, where it was a tick ago (so the frames
between two ticks do not jump), its velocity and its look come out at the far side,
turned with the passage, and the server is told the passage and where the feet were.
Nothing else of the player changes: on ground, fall distance, sprinting, what it
uses. The server checks the move to there as any move, then answers with a position
packet that changes nothing (all relative and zero), so the player keeps its velocity;
as any position packet does, it stops mining (a passage crossed while mining aborts
the dig). A refused crossing puts the player back where the server has it
([`Self::last_passage_refusal`] says why). One crossing at a time: the next waits
for the server's answer. Refused, with nothing moved or sent, when not connected to
a server, with no player, while riding, for a passage the window does not hold, when
the feet are more than 20 blocks from the opening, and when a mod's
`client_packet_send` cancels the crossing's payload.
methods.signature: fn cross_passage(&mut self, _: PassageId) -> Result<(), PassageCrossError>

methods.doc:
Side: client.
The server's refusal of the window's last crossing ([`Self::cross_passage`]) and the
passage it named, until the next crossing; None when it was not refused or no answer
came yet.

Side: client.
For a client mod: a push added to the local player's velocity, in blocks a tick, as an
explosion's knockback is (the window's player moves itself, as vanilla's client does). Each component is
clamped to -4..4; a spectator, or a value that is not a number, is left alone.

Side: client.
For a client mod: chooses the local player's hotbar slot, `slot` (0 to 8), as
`Inventory.setSelectedSlot` does for a number key. It sends nothing itself: the game
sends the carried-item packet at the next tick's start at the latest, and before the
packets of an attack, a use, an interact, a release, a drop and a continued block break
(not before a block break start). Refused above 8 with `OutOfRange`, without a client
world with `NoWorld`, and for a spectator with `Refused` (its number keys open the
spectator menu), leaving the selection as it was.
methods.signature: fn select_hotbar_slot(&mut self, _: u8) -> Result<(), HotbarSlotError>

methods.doc:
Side: client.
For a client mod: the local player's collision exclusions, the client half of
`EntityRef::set_collision_exclusions`, with the same boxes, rules and refusals (a client
with no player of its own answers `Stale`). The client moves its player itself, so a mod
sets the same boxes on both sides: the engine sends neither set to the other.

traits.doc: The host's methods both sides share of the `players` area, implemented by the game and reached through [`Host`].

methods.doc:
Side: both.
`ItemCooldowns.getCooldownGroup(stack)`: the group `stack`'s
cooldown is filed under, the group its `use_cooldown` component names
(its own, else its item's default), else its item id.

Side: both.
Resolve a real online player by UUID, never a fake. A fake is reached
through the handle returned by its factory. During a nested player swap,
outer players whose records are displaced return None.

traits.doc: The server host's methods of the `players` area, implemented by the game and reached through [`ServerHost`].

methods.doc:
Side: server.
Create or retrieve a connectionless player for the level currently in place.
methods.signature: fn fake_player(&mut self, _: LevelRef, _: u128, _: &str) -> Option<PlayerRef>

methods.doc:
Side: server.
The text of the mod command whose `run_mod_command` listeners are running, as
submitted and without its leading slash; for `execute … run` and `return run`,
the leaf command after `run`. Whitespace is kept as typed. This is untrusted
input: read validated values from `CommandInvocation`'s typed arguments. None
outside a `run_mod_command` listener.

Side: server.
Select the calling mod's view for this connected player and dimension, or release its
selection with `None`. The first mod to select owns the slot until it releases it.
The UUID can come from `player_login`, before a player has a world handle. A changed
selection requeues terrain already sent in that dimension. Rules apply to both native and Wasm mods.
methods.signature: fn player_set_terrain_view(&mut self, _: u128, _: &str, _: Option<u32>) -> Result<(), TerrainViewError>

methods.doc:
Side: server.
The profile of the player with this name, any case, as
`profile_by_uuid` knows it: an online player's, else an unexpired
user cache entry. Never asked of Mojang, and an unknown name is not
made an offline player. For a current Mojang lookup, including an
account the server has never seen, use
[`Profiles::resolve_name`](crate::Profiles).

Side: server.
The profile of the player with this UUID, as the server knows it,
never asked of Mojang: an online player's whole profile (the properties
the player list gives, so with those `player_set_profile_property` set),
else the user cache's name (`usercache.json`, a dedicated server's),
without properties. None when neither knows them. For a current Mojang
lookup, including an account the server has never seen, use
[`Profiles::resolve_id`](crate::Profiles).

Side: server.
Define or replace a view owned by the calling mod. Its ID is local to that mod.
An identical definition does nothing. Replacing rules refreshes every selection of that ID.
methods.signature: fn server_define_terrain_view(&mut self, _: u32, _: &TerrainView) -> Result<(), TerrainViewError>

methods.doc:
Side: server.
The most players who may be on at once (`PlayerList.getMaxPlayers`,
`max-players`), as the server list shows it and logins are refused
beyond. None where no server is open to players (a client, or a server
nobody can join): the one reason there is none.

Side: server.
Move the exact stack an inventory snapshot showed. Fills matching stacks before
empty slots; a player inventory receives into its 36 main slots. The move can
change one existing saved player file and a live player, or two live inventories.
A move within one saved player can change both of their inventories in one write.
Refuses with no change if the stack no longer matches, it cannot fit whole,
or a required file write fails. Call outside a transaction and a player swap.

Side: server.
Read a real player's inventory by UUID. Reads live slots when they are online,
or the existing player file after pending saves finish. Refuses while the
player is joining, dead or swapped out.
methods.signature: fn server_player_inventory(&mut self, _: u128, _: PlayerInventoryKind) -> Result<PlayerInventorySnapshot, PlayerInventoryError>

methods.doc:
Side: server.
Sets the player limit from the next login and server list ping on
(Paper's `Server.setMaxPlayers`); players already on stay, even when
they are more than the new limit. `server.properties` is not changed,
so a restart goes back to its `max-players`. Writes nothing and refuses
with `PlayerLimitRefusal::NotOpen` where no server is open to players,
and with `TooHigh { maximum }` for a limit above `i32::MAX`, as vanilla
keeps the limit in an `int` (Paper's `setMaxPlayers` takes one). Zero is
taken: it lets nobody else on.
methods.signature: fn server_set_max_players(&mut self, _: u32) -> Result<(), PlayerLimitRefusal>

traits.doc: The server host's methods of the `projectiles` area, implemented by the game and reached through [`ServerHost`].

methods.doc:
Side: server.
Narrows an entity to a cast fishing hook. None for another kind, a
stale handle, a client, or a hook taken out for its tick.

Side: server.
Narrows an entity to a projectile: one in the projectile list, a trident
a player threw or a firework rocket. None for another kind, a stale
handle or a client.

Side: server. `Projectile.spawnProjectileFromRotation` for a thrown item
projectile: snowball, egg, pearl, potion, experience bottle, wind charge,
or a registered mod thrown type. Constructs at the owner's eyes minus
0.1F blocks (wind charges use eye height directly), sets ownership before
shooting, inherits known movement
(vertical only while airborne), adds to the level and fires projectile_launch.
Spread draws x, y, z triangular noise from the new projectile's own random.
Once it is in the level, `stack`'s enchantments run their
`projectile_spawned` effects on it (`Projectile.applyOnProjectileSpawned`):
in the stack's order, each effect's requirements tested with the level
random just before it applies, its own draws from the projectile's random.
Does not consume the stack or apply item-use cooldowns or statistics.
None for an unavailable owner or one in another level, unsupported type,
invalid stack or non-finite shot parameter. Also refuses a stack with a
`projectile_spawned` effect the engine does not apply: `ignite`,
`apply_impulse`, `play_sound` and `all_of` of those apply
(`apply_mob_effect` and `apply_exhaustion` do nothing to a projectile,
as in vanilla); the block, damage, explosion, particle, summon,
function and item-damage effects are refused rather than skipped. No
random is drawn and nothing spawns on those refusals. Unsupported
requirement contexts (including entity flags) and invalid clamped
level-value ranges also refuse before insertion. Type predicates,
random chance and their boolean combinations are supported.
The original stack
is unchanged; carried count is one; the effects see the stack as given.
methods.signature: fn spawn_projectile_from_rotation(&mut self, _: LivingRef, _: &Identifier, _: &item::item_stack::ItemStack, _: f32, _: f32, _: f32) -> Option<ProjectileRef>

traits.doc: The host's read-only mod recipe property membership service.

methods.doc:
Side: both.
Whether a mod-created recipe property set accepts an item ID. Unknown
sets/items and vanilla keys return false. The server uses its current
load, and clients use the server's last synchronized generation (local
preload before the first packet). The same read on `LoopContext` lets
`menu_slot_rules` filter a slot identically for server and prediction.
Membership reads allocate nothing and perform no registry scans.

traits.doc: The client host's methods of the `recipes` area, implemented by the game and reached through [`crate::ClientHost`].

methods.doc:
Side: client.
Shows the panel beside container screens with these items (at most
8192), as the game's own slots in pages, with a search box; the
player's clicks, searches and keys over items come back as
`panel_event`. The panel is the last mod's to show one; empty
items and no recipe page take yours away.

Side: client.
How mod `mod_id`'s item panel (`panel_items`) looks from now on:
`PanelStyle::RecipeBook` (the default: the recipe book's page arrows
and a plain search box), `PanelStyle::Viewer` (square page buttons on
a bar over the items and the viewer's search box, as Horizon's Recipes
panel draws them) or `PanelStyle::Classic` (JEI's list on Minecraft
1.12: flush right under page buttons that always show and wrap around,
the search box at the foot of the screen with a settings button that
opens the mod's page in Options > Mods). The viewer's look changes
only the drawing; the classic one also lays the panel out. Kept for
the session, whether or not the panel is showing.

Side: client.
Places a recipe in the open screen's grid as a click in the recipe
book does (`ServerboundPlaceRecipePacket`): the inventory's grid or a
crafting table's. `all` places as many as the items allow, as with
Shift. Refused while no such screen is open and for a recipe the
player's book doesn't hold; one missing items shows as a ghost.
methods.signature: fn place_recipe(&mut self, _: i32, _: bool) -> Result<(), String>

methods.doc:
Side: client.
The `book_id`s of the recipe `recipe_id` (`minecraft:stick`), the ids
`transfer_recipe`, `transfer_recipe_check`, `place_recipe` and
`known_recipes` use: one for each way the recipe book shows it, in the
book's order. For a recipe viewer, which has the recipe from
`recipes_of_type` and needs its id for "+". A server numbers its
recipes itself and names none of them, so an id is given only when the
server sent the recipe book entry with that number and this client's
own numbering of the recipe agrees with it: the entry is the same
recipe (the same result, category and ingredients), so two different
recipes with identical displays cannot be told apart. Empty otherwise: a
recipe the server sent no entry for (the player's book does not hold
it, or it was removed), one the server numbers differently, one the
book doesn't show (campfire, stonecutting, smithing, a mod's own
type), an unknown id, and outside a world. The answer changes when
the server adds, replaces or removes entries and when recipes reload
or arrive, and no hook announces a recipe book change: query it when
you use it, rather than keeping an answer from `recipes_received`.

Side: client.
Move available ingredients for a viewer recipe into the open crafting grid,
without requiring the recipe to be learned. The screen shows any refusal.

Side: client.
What `transfer_recipe(book_id)` would do now, worked out by the server
without moving anything: the player's inventory, the grid and every
container a mod lends the grid's recipes (a crafting station's chests,
which the client can't see) counted. For a viewer's "+", to mark the
inputs it lacks. The first call for a recipe asks and returns None;
the answer comes a moment later and is kept for that recipe while the
menu, the inventory and the grid stay as they were; while it is still
wanted it is asked again every two seconds, at most fifteen times for
one state of the menu. None outside a screen that
takes `transfer_recipe` and on a server that doesn't answer it.

Side: client.
A viewer's "+" for a recipe by its id, into the open menu: a machine's mod menu as
well as a crafting grid. The server asks the `menu_transfer` part of the open mod menu's
type first, then makes the game's own grid transfer; the screen shows the result as for
`transfer_recipe`. `max` moves as many sets as the items allow (Shift). Shown as
`NotIntoMenu` with no container screen open, in spectator mode, and on a server that
doesn't take viewer transfers. In a solo world or on a LAN host the game is the server:
its own player's transfer takes the same path, part first, then the grid.

traits.doc: The host's methods both sides share of the `recipes` area, implemented by the game and reached through [`Host`].

methods.doc:
Side: both.
The `book_id`s of the recipes the player's recipe book holds now
(the server's book on a server); empty outside a world.

Side: both.
Published asset/data read: available in Setup, Reloading and World.
The validated category and icon of a custom recipe type, or None for
an undeclared/invalid type, before resources load, or outside a world.
Returns the first category in category-id order when a type has several.
Any invalid declaration refuses the complete generation.
Rebuilt when the recipe table changes. Does not unlock any recipes.

Side: both.
Published asset/data read: available in Setup, Reloading and World.
An ingredient from recipe-file JSON text: an item, a `#tag`, or a list
of them, a bare id as `minecraft:` (as vanilla reads it); `test` says
whether a stack fits. Items the game doesn't know are left out; None
for missing tags, invalid ingredients or no known named items, and
outside a world. An existing-empty tag returns an empty ingredient.
Invalid JSON is refused with `RecipeJsonError::InvalidJson`.

Side: both.
Published asset/data read: available in Setup, Reloading and World.
A stack from recipe-file `result` JSON text: `id` (a bare one as
`minecraft:`), `count` (1 by default, up to 99) and `components`. None
without an `id`, for an item the game doesn't know or a count outside
that, and outside a world.
Invalid JSON is refused with `RecipeJsonError::InvalidJson`.

Side: both.
Published asset/data read: available in Setup, Reloading and World.
The recipes of registered recipe type `kind` (`minecraft:crafting`, `mymod:crusher`), vanilla's
types and mods' own alike, from `data/<namespace>/recipe/*.json` of vanilla,
the content mods (`.hmod`) and the world's data packs, in file order: each
one typed (`Recipe`: its ingredients, results, group, cooking time and
experience, or its stonecutting, smithing or special crafting rule),
with its file as JSON for a mod's own type. The file's type field names its
serializer; this can differ from the reported recipe kind. Dynamic rules are not fixed
outputs; use `LevelRef::recipe_for` for engine-matchable recipe types.
Registered crafting kinds match through LevelRef::recipe_for. Cache other mod-owned
types once per load/reload and match those in mod memory; those return
RecipeLookupError::NotMatchable. These are the
recipes in force (`RecipeManager.getAllRecipesFor`): data packs merged and
load conditions held, so a pack's override or removal shows. A data pack
changes them on `/reload`, so look them up again when you need them. Empty
for a type nobody uses and outside a world. These are the server's table on
the server thread, a dedicated server or a LAN host; a client, the
single-player window included, sees vanilla's and the content mods' recipes,
not the world's data packs', unless a mod had the server send it the type
(`native_datapack_sync`).

traits.doc: The client host's methods of the `replay` area, implemented by the game and reached through [`crate::ClientHost`].

methods.doc:
Side: client.
Closes the replay at the end of this frame, as Escape does: a replay opened from the
title screen goes back there. `replay_closed` tells when it is closed. A later
`replay_close` or `replay_seek` in the same frame replaces this request, and a request
for a replay closed or replaced since is dropped.
`NotOpen` while no replay is open.

Side: client.
Asks to open the recording `recording` for playback. The id is the recording's file
name in the recordings folder without `.mcpr`, never a path: what an id may hold is in
[`ReplayError::InvalidId`], and an id naming no regular file directly in the folder is
`NotFound`. The call opens the file once, through the folder it checked, and checks it
starts with a zip signature (`Unreadable` if not); the file is then read and indexed
off the game's thread, never reopened by name, and an archive found broken there fails
through `replay_open_failed` with `Unreadable`.

`Ok(request)` means the request is accepted: `request` is a non-zero id, never given
twice while the game runs (once every `u32` has been given, `replay_open` is
`Unavailable`). Exactly one of `replay_opened` or `replay_open_failed` follows with that
id, whatever happens, except when the game closes first (then no event is promised). A
later `replay_open` replaces a request still waiting or being read, which then fails
with `Superseded`; once a read request waits for a world to be left, a later one is
`WorldBusy` instead. An open asked while a replay plays fails with
`Unavailable` when the camera path edited in that replay can't be saved first, or when
it reads the very archive the editor saved into since the request (its camera path or a
marker); the replay playing stays.

A replay is never played over a live session it would end: from a plain single-player
world, the world is saved and left as Save and Quit does once the recording is ready,
and the replay opens on the title; a replay already playing is closed first
(`replay_closed`). `WorldBusy` while a world is being joined, a multiplayer server is
connected, or the single-player world is open to LAN or has splitscreen players; an
accepted request whose session changes before it is ready (a world joined, left or
opened, or the replay playing closed or replaced) fails with `WorldBusy` too.
`Unavailable` for a splitscreen guest, a server, or while the game is closing.

Side: client.
Pauses the replay's clock now; pausing a paused replay changes nothing. `NotOpen` while
no replay is open.

Side: client.
Starts the replay's clock again now. `NotOpen` while no replay is open.

Side: client.
Moves the replay's clock to `ms` from the recording's start (at most its length) at
the end of this frame. Then the recording's packets up to the position the seek applied
have been processed in order (a packet the game cannot decode or apply is skipped), and
the next `replay_advanced` reports exactly that position, on the frame drawn with it; the clock runs on from there only on the frame
after. A standalone replay sought back starts again from a fresh session; what the game
keeps outside that session may carry over (today the difficulty shown, and the backing
state of a screen a packet opened). State that came only from the client's own
simulation between packets (an entity moving between its updates, particles) is not
promised either way. How the game gets there, and how long it takes, is not part of this
contract: today a seek forward costs the packets between the clock and the target,
while a seek back in a standalone replay replays every packet from the start, as does a
seek forward across a relative teleport of the player or one whose read fails. When a
rebuild fails, or the forward read fails in a replay that doesn't own its session, the
replay closes (`replay_closed`) and no `replay_advanced` reports the seek.
A standalone replay seeks either way; one that doesn't own its session only forward
(`BackwardSeek`). A later `replay_close` or `replay_seek` in the same frame
replaces this request, and a request for a replay closed or replaced since is
dropped. `NotOpen` while no replay is open.
methods.signature: fn replay_seek(&mut self, _: u32) -> Result<(), ReplayError>

methods.doc:
Side: client.
Sets the playback speed now: 1 is real time, 0.5 half and 2 twice as fast.
`InvalidSpeed`, changing nothing, for a speed that is not finite or is outside
[`REPLAY_MIN_SPEED`]..=[`REPLAY_MAX_SPEED`]; `NotOpen` while no replay is open.
methods.signature: fn replay_set_speed(&mut self, _: f64) -> Result<(), ReplayError>

methods.doc:
Side: client.
The replay this window plays, if any, as its clock stands now; none while no replay
plays. While one asked for by `replay_open` is still opening, this is the replay
playing, if any.

traits.doc: The host's methods both sides share of the `resources` area, implemented by the game and reached through [`Host`].

methods.doc:
Side: both.
The winning bytes of resource `id` in `pack_type`'s stack, as
`ResourceManager.getResource` answers it: the highest selected pack that
supplies the file wins. Client resources are the selected asset packs over
the game's assets; server data is the world's selected data packs over the
game's and mods' data, with `minecraft:vanilla` kept unless disabled.
`identifier` is the resource name without its `assets/<namespace>/` or
`data/<namespace>/` prefix, e.g. `minecraft:models/block/stone.json` or
`mymod:machines/furnace.json`. Missing, unreadable and files above
[`MAX_RESOURCE_BYTES`](crate::MAX_RESOURCE_BYTES) return `None`; a client side (or one without that
stack) also returns `None`. This read never reloads packs.

traits.doc: The client host's methods of the `screens` area, implemented by the game and reached through [`crate::ClientHost`].

methods.doc:
Side: client.
Requests vanilla's menu background blur for this frame, with a per-frame guard
so blur is applied at most once per frame. Returns true if blur was newly
requested this frame, or false if it was already applied/requested this frame.
API @API:screen_transparent_background@.

Side: client.
Closes the open screen as its Escape key does: a container screen
closes as the player's container close (`ServerboundContainerClosePacket`
with the menu's id, then the client menu closed), a pause menu closes
to the game, and another screen runs its own close. The sign editor
sends its sign update (`ServerboundSignUpdatePacket`), as Escape does.
The screen hooks fire as for Escape. The death screen does not close
this way. False when no screen is open (or, outside a world, when it
cannot act).

Side: client.
Whether a specific key is currently held down.
`key` is the vanilla physical key name (`key.keyboard.left.shift`, for example).
Unknown names are not down. Modifier combinations use `ClientHost::modifiers`.

Side: client.
The user's configured menu background blur radius (`menuBackgroundBlurriness` in options.txt,
usually 0.0 to 10.0; default 5.0). 0.0 means blur is turned off. API @API:screen_transparent_background@.

Side: client.
The mod whose own screen is open, if one is (Escape, or another screen
replacing it, closes it).

Side: client.
Closes mod `mod_id`'s own screen, if it is open.

Side: client.
Opens a screen of mod `mod_id`'s own over the world: the screen hooks
fire over it as over any other, so the mod draws it in
`screen_render_post` and takes its clicks, scroll, keys and
typing there; the mouse is freed, and Escape closes it. Every mod's own
screen has the `ScreenView.id` `mod`, so a mod's screen hooks
check `native_mod_screen()` is its own before drawing. It doesn't pause
a single-player game (as the inventory doesn't). True when it is open:
false while another screen is (or another mod's), over the title
screen, a book, a sign editor, a dialog or a prompt, while the world
loads, and anywhere but the window's own client (the server thread, a
dedicated server). A gamepad can close it (B, Start) but not click on
it: its clicks don't reach the mouse hooks.

Side: client.
The same screen identifier provided to screen hooks.

Side: client.
Opens the player's inventory as the inventory key does: locally, with
no packet (the player menu is always open on the server). Riding a
vehicle with its own inventory sends the open-inventory player command
(`ServerboundPlayerCommandPacket`), as the key does. False with a
screen already open, for a spectator, in a portal transition, or with
no world.
The world-preset editor currently open over Create World, or none.
A copy of the open preset editor's working dimension stems.

Queues the primary window's normal Quit Game action after the current
hook dispatch. The game follows its usual shutdown path, including
saving and stopping an integrated server when one is open.
Returns true when the request is queued. Returns false for a headless
client, a splitscreen guest, a server, a load phase without client
services, or a quit already queued or in progress.

Not on wasm: process-wide quit is a native client action.
methods.wasm_reason: process-wide quit is a native client action.

methods.doc:
Side: client.
Takes a screenshot as the screenshot key (F2) does (`Screenshot.grab`): the
next frame is read back at the size F2 saves (the game's resolution times the
screenshot quality), the `screenshot` hook runs on it as for F2, so every mod's
screenshot listener sees it, and it is written to the player's `screenshots`
folder under vanilla's file name, with F2's chat line. `Ok` means queued: the
files are written, or the hook cancels them, after the next frame. Unlike F2's,
its files never replace one: each is written to a temporary file and published
only under a name no file has (a name the hook picked that exists keeps the
existing file and reports failure), a failed write leaves no partial file, and
a name the hook picked may create at most one new folder (a deeper one reports
failure). One screenshot runs at a time, and all mods together may write 4 GiB
of screenshots per game session, each counted at its uncompressed size after the
hook (4 bytes a pixel, 6 more for an HDR copy) and at least 1 MiB: about 500 at
1920 by 1080, and never more than 4096. A capture that would pass the budget is
not written and reports failure. Refused with nothing
queued, by name, as [`ScreenshotError`] lists: one still in progress, the
session's budget used up, no screenshots folder, or no window here. Native and
wasm alike.

Side: client.
Where the open screen draws outside its `rect`, and where mods draw
over it: the recipe book's panel, the creative tab rows, the active
effects beside the inventory, then whatever `screen_exclusion_areas`
adds. Each is `[x, y, width, height]` in GUI pixels; an empty or
non-finite one is dropped. A mod that lays out its own panels
(a recipe viewer) keeps them clear of these. Client-side; empty with
no screen up.

Side: client.
What the block's mod wrote for the mod screen that is open
(`menu_extra_data` on the server), empty when it wrote nothing;
None when no mod screen is open. The same for a menu `PlayerRef::open_mod_menu`
opened with its `extra`. A copy, so native and wasm read it alike. @API:menu_extra_data@.

Side: client.
The id of the item in the slot under the pointer on the open container screen
(`AbstractContainerScreen.getHoveredSlot().getItem()`), None over no slot or an empty one.

Side: client.
The block of the mod screen that is open (`screen`), as the
server named it when the block opened its menu type; None when no mod
screen is open. 401.

Side: client.
The open menu's title (the block's name, or the one it was given),
as plain text.

Replace the open editor's working dimension stems. Requires an overworld,
valid dimension ids and type/generator declarations. Returns false outside
the editor or for malformed data; Done commits, Cancel discards the copy.
Interior screen state permits use from the read-only screen input hooks.

Side: client.
The sign the sign editor is on, its block position and side; None when
no sign editor is open or outside a world.

Side: client.
The last window focus state reported by the window system.

traits.doc: The host's methods both sides share of the `tags` area, implemented by the game and reached through [`Host`].

methods.doc:
Side: both.
Whether the resolved block is in the world's merged block tag, on a client the tag its
server sent. Unknown tags return false; unavailable tags or owning-thread block mappings
return None.

Side: both.
The bucket item that picks `fluid` up (`Fluid.getBucket`), `minecraft:water_bucket` for
water and flowing water. None for `minecraft:empty`, whose bucket is air, and for a name
no fluid has.

Side: both.
The sound event a bucket plays as it empties `fluid` (`BucketItem.playEmptySound`, the
`BUCKET_EMPTY` sound of NeoForge's `FluidType`), `minecraft:item.bucket.empty_lava` for
lava and flowing lava and `minecraft:item.bucket.empty` for water and a mod's world
fluid. None for `minecraft:empty`, for a tank-only fluid, which has no world form, and
for a name no fluid has.

Side: both.
Whether `fluid` is in the fluid tag `tag` (`FluidState.is(TagKey)`, `minecraft:water` or
`water`), over the merged fluid tags, on a client those its server sent. An unknown tag
is false. None as for `native_block_in_tag`.

Side: both.
Whether `fluid` and `other` are the same fluid (`Fluid.isSame`): a source and its
flowing form are, so `minecraft:water` and `minecraft:flowing_water` are the same, water
and lava not. Names are fluid ids, with or without `minecraft:`; false when either
names no fluid.

Side: both.
The sound event a bucket plays as it picks `fluid` up (`Fluid.getPickupSound`),
`minecraft:item.bucket.fill_lava` for lava and flowing lava. None for
`minecraft:empty`, which has none, and for a name no fluid has.

Side: both.
The fluid state `state` holds (`BlockState.getFluidState`): water for a waterlogged state,
the empty fluid for most. None for an id no state has.

Side: both.
The outline of `state` as `BlockState.getShape` answers it with an empty getter at the
origin (`EmptyBlockGetter.INSTANCE`, `BlockPos.ZERO`): its boxes, each `[min x, y, z,
max x, y, z]` in the block's own space, with no random offset and none of a world's
context (a state that reads its neighbours or block entity answers what its state alone
gives). Empty for a state with no outline, such as air. None for an id no state has.

The merged-tag service, using load-resolved item and tag keys.
Not on wasm: a frame resource; its methods are the imports.
methods.wasm_reason: a frame resource; its methods are the imports.

methods.doc:
Side: both.
The saved name for an engine-issued unresolved fluid.

traits.doc: The methods of the `text` area on both sides, implemented by the game and reached through [`Host`].

methods.doc:
Side: both.
Reads a text component as `/tellraw` and `ComponentSerialization.CODEC` take it: one
JSON or SNBT value (`"plain"`, `{"text":"Hi","color":"gold"}`, `["a",{"text":"b"}]`,
`translate`, `extra`, click and hover events), with nothing but whitespace after it
(Paper's `GsonComponentSerializer.deserialize`). None when it does not parse as one component:
an object needs one content key (a `type` binds alone, a null `type` counts as absent),
`text` must be a string, `extra` a non-empty list, and a style field that is present and
wrong refuses the whole component. An object whose only content key is `index` is refused,
as in vanilla's codec; Horizon follows vanilla there.

Side: both.
Reads legacy formatting codes (`§a`, `§l`, `§r`...) as the font draws them
(`Style.applyLegacyFormat`; Bukkit's `ChatColor` strings): a colour code resets the
decorations, `§r` resets everything, an unknown code is dropped. `&` codes are not
read; a mod that takes them replaces `&` with `§` first, as
`ChatColor.translateAlternateColorCodes` does.

Side: both.
The text as item components and block entities store it (`ComponentSerialization`
to NBT): what `minecraft:custom_name` and each `minecraft:lore` line hold. See
`ItemStack::set_display`.

traits.doc: The server host's methods of the `world_edit` area, implemented by the game and reached through [`ServerHost`].

methods.doc:
Side: server.
For a server mod: the runs made at once, straight into the chunks of the authoritative level `dimension`
(the one being ticked, as for `native_set_block`), with what `fill ... strict` does for block entities (a
block replaced by another loses its block entity, and a new block gets the one `native_set_block` would
give it, a mod block's included); no neighbour is told, and the chunks changed go to the players whole.
Runs in chunks not loaded, and the parts of runs outside the column, are left out. The blocks changed, or
why the edit was left out, with nothing changed: another dimension, a client of a server, a palette entry
or predicate that fails typed validation, a run naming a palette entry or filter past the end,
or more than 65536 filters.

Side: server.
For a server mod: `below` blocks under and `above` blocks from each column's height by `heightmap`, as a
palette of complete `BlockState` values and indexes, with biome tints (air outside the column and in columns
not loaded). The tints are the biome's at the column's top, not blended over the biome blend radius as the
game draws them: near a biome border they can differ from what players see. `Err` says why nothing was
read: another dimension or a client of a server, `below + above` of 0 or more than the level's height, or
a read of more than 1,048,576 blocks (`MAX_READ`; it runs on the server tick, so read big areas in pieces).
methods.signature: fn read_columns(&self, _: &str, _: &[(i32, i32)], _: Heightmap, _: (u32, u32)) -> Result<ColumnBlocks, String>

methods.doc:
Side: server.
For a server mod: structure template `id` (`mymod:hut`, found as
`StructureTemplateManager.get` finds it: the world's saved structures,
then the game's and the mods' own) as `/place template id` would place
it at `at` with `rotation` and `mirror`, without placing anything. The
blocks come in vanilla's placement order (full blocks, the others, then
those with a block entity, each by y, x, z), from the palette
`/place template` picks at `at`; no processor runs, and the template's
entities are left out. None for an id that doesn't parse or has a `.`
or `..` part, a template the game doesn't have, and on a client.
API @API:structure_template@.
methods.signature: fn structure_template(&mut self, _: &str, _: [i32; 3], _: StructureRotation, _: StructureMirror) -> Option<StructureTemplateSnapshot>

methods.doc:
Side: server.
For a server mod: each column's height by `heightmap` in the authoritative level `dimension` (the one being
ticked), none for a column not loaded. `Err` says why nothing was read: another dimension or a client of a
server, or more than 65,536 columns (`MAX_COLUMNS`).
methods.signature: fn surface_heights(&self, _: &str, _: &[(i32, i32)], _: Heightmap) -> Result<Vec<Option<i32>>, String>

methods.doc:
Side: server.
For a server mod: what the generator makes at each of `columns` of the level `dimension` (the one being

methods.doc:
Side: client.
Asks the player whether to open `saves/<folder>` the way the title screen's Play button does: the
request is queued, and the title's next frame shows a question that names the mod and the save, with
Yes and No. Yes runs Play's own checks (a locked world, links in the save, the session lock, recovery,
an incompatible version, the backup before an upgrade or downgrade); No or Escape changes nothing.
Only on the title's main page with no world open. Only the calling mod's own bundle's
`[native] world_control` grants it (default off), even if another enabled mod declares it; a request
whose caller is unidentified is refused with `NotPermitted`. Creating a world, and level create, unload
or delete, are not in it.

Not on wasm: a native mod's title request; a wasm mod has no title screen to ask on.

Answers `Queued` (accepted: the title's next frame asks the player, and the world opens only on Yes),
`NotTitle`, `NotPermitted` (also when the caller is unidentified), `InvalidRequest` (the folder is not one
plain segment of 1 to 64 characters with no `/`, `\`, `:`, control character or leading dot, or
`saves/<folder>` is not an existing save the title's world list recognizes: an empty directory is not one,
a link that leaves `saves/` does not count, and nothing is created) or `Busy` (another request is queued for
the next title frame, the question is on screen and unanswered, or a world entry is already waiting for its
resources).
methods.wasm_reason: a native mod's title request; a wasm mod has no title screen to ask on.

time, thunder, a spawn attempt) while it lies in the spawning area of a

two controllers, release separately. They are saved in

the world loads, those of a controller no loaded mod registers are
discarded. False outside a mod's hook, for another mod's controller, on
a client, for a chunk outside the world and for a level the server has

handles.doc:
Decodes the winning file of every entry of every declared registry in `files`
(`data/<entry namespace>/<registry namespace>/<registry path>/<entry>.json`, each with
its versions in pack order, the last winning as `ResourceManager` hands them out), then
resolves every reference to a declared registry against the whole candidate, so a
forward reference works and an absent target refuses everything. A reference to a
registry no declaration here covers (a vanilla one) is not checked. The caller has
already dropped files whose pack conditions do not hold. Each version is its pack's id
and its bytes, so a refusal names the pack. A candidate over a limit is refused whole:
[`MAX_SNAPSHOT_REGISTRIES`] registries, [`MAX_DATAPACK_ENTRY_BYTES`] per entry,
[`MAX_SNAPSHOT_ENTRIES`] entries per registry and [`MAX_SNAPSHOT_BYTES`] of winning files
in all, the bounds its snapshot must also fit, and a trial encode refuses a candidate whose
snapshot of every synchronized registry would be over [`MAX_SNAPSHOT_BYTES`]. The error is boxed: it is large, and a
refused candidate is rare.
handles.signature: fn build(_: &[DatapackRegistryDeclaration], _: &[(String, Vec<(String, Vec<u8>)>)]) -> Result<Self, Box<DatapackLoadError>>

The tick scope below is the port's own transactional requirement:
NeoForge adds no event, deferral or drop capture around a block entity's
tick, and new item spawning stays immediate. With no scope open the
engine behaves exactly as vanilla for these item operations: removal
is immediate, no overlay is created, and nothing is staged.

discarded on writeback rejection. Non-item removal and spawning are
deliberately immediate and are not undone by rejection.

Runs the command `line` (a leading slash allowed) with the entity as
its source, as vanilla runs a portal's or a sign's command:
`ServerPlayer.createCommandSourceStack` (another entity:
`Entity.createCommandSourceStackForNameResolution`), `.withPermission(level)`,
then `Commands.performPrefixedCommand`. `level` is the mod's choice, taken
as given whether it is above or below the entity's own: the line is parsed
and checked at it. `@s` is the entity, and the command runs from its
position and rotation in its level. A player is answered as for their own
command: its feedback and failures reach their chat, and the other
operators hear of it (`broadcastToAdmins`). Another entity's source is
silent: nothing reaches anyone (`CommandSource.NULL`). A command a mod
registered hears a player as `CommandSource::Player` and another entity as
`CommandSource::Console`, both at `level`. A teleport to another level
happens at the next tick's start, as `Commands::run_command`'s. Whether
the command ran: false for a line that fails to parse or to run, and,
with nothing run, for a stale or removed entity, an entity outside the
level in place (a player in another level included: that level is
parked while the hook runs), and on a client.
During a guest's turn, live players (the acting one included) can run it
and are reachable; displaced outer players are neither, as on
`Commands::run_command`.

Side: server.
Sends the entity to `pos` in the level `dimension` (`minecraft:the_nether`,
or a level a mod registered), as `Entity.teleport` does with a portal's
transition: `pos` is in that level's own coordinates (nothing scales it
by `coordinate_scale`), a level nobody has entered opens first, and the
entity keeps its motion as it is, unturned (`Relative.DELTA`; a
minecart's is clamped to 0.4 along x and z, its `getKnownMovement`). A
mod that wants it stopped or turned sets its velocity first
(`entity_set_velocity`). It takes a player, a mob, a boat, a minecart (a
vehicle takes its passengers along), an item, a primed TNT, an experience
orb, an arrow, a trident, a firework and the thrown items and fireballs a
chunk saves. Into another level anything but a player is recreated there
with its stack, owner, thrower and portal cooldown, under a new handle:
the old one is stale. That move is a change of level, not a section
crossing: the section-crossing report (`entity_entering_section`) does not
tell it, the entity's later moves there are told as any entity's, and this
call adds no report of its own. A player arrives after the current tick,
still (its client holds its motion), and `player_teleported` and
`player_changed_dimension` report the move. In the entity's own level it
moves as `entity_teleport_to` does, keeping its motion. False for a stale
handle, what `entity_teleport_to` refuses, a dimension that isn't
registered, a primed TNT a mob rides, and the kinds it cannot move into
another level (armor stands, falling blocks, ender pearls, wind charges,
entities Horizon doesn't simulate). A fake player stays where it is, and
so does an entity whose travel a mod cancels (`entity_travel_to_dimension`);
the call is still true. Nothing builds ground at the destination.

Side: server.
Mark the half-open box `min <= pos < max` as watered (`FarmlandWaterManager.addAABBTicket`).
For 5x1x5 farmland starting at [0, 64, 0], use min [0, 64, 0], max [5, 65, 5].
Farmland checks tickets before its vanilla water scan; rain and water still hydrate it.
The calling mod owns this ticket; overlaps are independent. Remove it when the sprinkler
stops. It is also removed on owner disable and level unload, never saved: re-add in
`level_load` or the block entity's load listener. Reads/writes reach parked server levels.
None outside an enabled mod call, on clients, for stale/unavailable levels, empty or
reversed bounds, or a box spanning more than 65,536 x/z chunks. Does not load chunks.

Side: server.
Every available member of the server level's entity lookup
(`ServerLevel.getAllEntities`), including spectators and entities outside
any spatial query. Dragon parts are not lookup members.
Returns None on a remote client, for a stale handle or a parked level.
Returns None while any lookup member is temporarily extracted, rather
than returning an incomplete list.
Order is lookup admission order, preserved across temporary extraction;
removal and re-admission moves an entity to the end. A chunk's entities
join in the order it stored them: section by section, each in admission
order, as vanilla stores them. An entity that moved into another section
since it joined keeps its admission place there, where vanilla moves it
to the end of that section. Zero runtime IDs fall back to stable storage
join order, not runtime admission order. Unregistered entity kinds have
no authoritative lookup handle and are omitted. These limitations mean
saved-world and whole-level ordering parity is not guaranteed.
Allocates a result buffer, not one allocation per entity; sorting is
O(n log n), followed by one authoritative handle lookup per candidate.

does: orbs of the largest sizes first (2477, 1237, ... 3, 1), each
drawing the id `tryMergeToExisting` compares from the level random and
merging into an orb of the same value whose box meets the 1 block box
around `x y z`, or else a new orb with its own random motion. The
`block_drops` rule doesn't apply (vanilla's blocks check it before
they award). True once the orbs are awarded, even if a mod keeps a new
one out (`entity_join_level`). False, with no orbs, for 0, a
value that isn't finite, on a client, for a stale handle or a level
not in place.

entity, tool)`), without breaking it or spawning anything: its loot table rolled with

parked handle, a client, an unloaded or out-of-height position, and a stale `entity`.

players' copy of the block. The same event queued twice runs once; one in a chunk
that isn't ticking waits for it. True means queued, not handled. False for a block
key no block has, a position outside the level's build height, a parked level, a stale
handle or a client.

their own parts again. False, with nothing queued, off the level in place, for a stale
handle, on a client and for a position that isn't loaded.

The next clock time after [`level_clock_time`](Self::level_clock_time) at which the
level's own clock reaches `marker`, a time marker of its timelines (as `/time set <marker>`
moves to it). Today only the Overworld's clock defines markers, so a level following any
other clock (a mod dimension's own) answers None for every marker. None too for a marker
the clock does not define, a time past `i64::MAX`, a level without a default clock, a stale
handle and a client.

Side: server.
The time of the level's own clock in ticks: the clock its dimension type names as
`default_clock`, which its sky, spawning and beds go by and `/time` sets there. A mod's
level with a `day_cycle` clock of its own counts it apart from the Overworld's; a level
without a default clock, like the Nether, is None, as is a stale handle and a client.

Side: both.
World-space block collision boxes under an empty collision context, without entities or border. Refuses a stale or nonresident level and invalid or overlarge boxes.
On a client, the level it shows or a viewed one (`host.level`), each through its own
world; None where the walk reaches a column the client doesn't hold.

Side: both.
The entry ids (`addon:fire`) of a datapack registry a mod declared
(`declare_datapack_registry`), sorted, as this world session last loaded them. On a client
they are the ones its server sent at the join and after each reload, and only for a
registry declared `Required` or `Optional`. None for a stale or parked level and a
registry no mod declared (or, on a client, one the server did not send). Reads nothing
from disk.

Side: both.
A handle to `entry` of `registry` at the generation now loaded (on a client, the one its
server last sent). A handle kept across a reload fails its next read with
`StaleGeneration`, one from an earlier world session with `WrongSession`. A stale or parked
level and a registry no mod declared are `UnknownRegistry`; an entry no pack defines is
`MissingEntry`.

Side: both.
The decoded fields of the entry a handle names, in the registry's schema order, as plain
values: a copy, which carries no authority after the read. The handle is checked first
(session, then generation), then the entry; the errors are those of
[`level_datapack_handle`](Self::level_datapack_handle).

The time of day in ticks (`Level.getOverworldClockTime`), shared by
every level; it keeps counting past 24000. On a client, the synchronized
Overworld clock, advanced at its server-supplied rate, even when the
displayed dimension has a different default clock. API 381.

Destroy a block in the level in place (`Level.destroyBlock`), optionally dropping
resources with `tool` (None is an empty hand). With `collect`, return the dropped
stacks without spawning their item entities; otherwise return an empty list after
spawning them. The one level drop path runs loot, block-drop hooks and experience
once, in vanilla's random order. `drop` false suppresses resources entirely.
None means nothing broke: air, a refused write, a stale handle, a client, an
unloaded/out-of-height position, or a parked level.

or `hard`, as `/difficulty` names it.
The level's dimension. `level.dimension().id(host)` gives its name.

Side: both.
Dimension shape of a loaded server level, including parked levels.

Side: both.
The level's dimension type (`Level.dimensionType()` and its gameplay attributes): coordinate
scale, ambient light, fixed time, infiniburn, monster spawn light, sky and the gameplay
switches a mod's `DimensionSettings` or a data pack sets. A level whose type neither gave
fields for has the Overworld's. None for a stale handle; on a client, the level it shows.

The strong power alone that the block at `pos` gives that way
(`SignalGetter.getDirectSignal(pos, direction)`), 0 to 15. None as for `signal`.

Side: server.
The strongest strong power reaching the block at `pos` from its six neighbours
(`SignalGetter.getDirectSignalTo`), 0 to 15. None as for `signal`.

`LevelReader.enabledFeatures` of the level a handle names. Every level of a world shares
the world's flags. None for a stale handle and on a client.

Side: both.
Entities whose bounding boxes intersect this box (`Level.getEntities`).
Face-only contact does not intersect; spectator players are excluded.
Returns None for a stale handle or a parked level: its entity handles
cannot resolve until the level is in place, and for a bound that is not
finite (NaN or infinite). A minimum above its maximum is the same box
with the two swapped, as vanilla's `AABB`. On a client (`ClientLevel`),
the entities the server tracks to it, other players among them, and the
window's own player, with the same walk.
None there before login and for a level it does not show. The walk
is in entity-list order followed by players. Every entity list is walked
once per call: O(entities) regardless of the box. Each overlapping mob
resolves through a mob-list scan: O(K*N) for K overlapping mobs and N mobs. Tridents do not
resolve; frames, paintings and other special entities
are not on the entity-list walk. The dragon follows ordinary entities;
its eight intersecting parts follow players in vanilla hash-table order (`Level.getEntities`).
During `hears_projectile_impacts`, the projectile list is taken out of
the game and is not visible; it is restored for `projectile_impact`.

Side: server.
`Some(true)` when this resident, in-bounds position has entity-ticking tickets.
`Some(false)` for unloaded or out-of-bounds positions or tickets that forbid ticking.
With no ticket system, resident in-bounds chunks tick; an active but empty ticket
system permits none. This reads the current ticket decision, not a tick guarantee.
`None` for stale handles, a client or a level not currently in place. Parked
levels cannot answer because the live ticket state belongs to the level in place.
Does not load chunks. Each call shares the ticket map through a reference count;
it does not allocate a memo table or refresh a resident-chunk cache.
The open of the world the handle belongs to.

Side: server.
Explodes at `center` as vanilla's full `Level.explode(source,
damageSource, calculator, x, y, z, radius, fire, interaction,
smallParticles, largeParticles, blockParticles, sound)` does
(`native_explode`), `source` being the exploding entity, or none. The
causing entity comes from it, never from the caller: a primed TNT's
owner, a living entity itself, a projectile's owner when that is
living, else none. With both the damage is
`minecraft:player_explosion`, else `minecraft:explosion`, unless
`settings` names a damage type, and a kill credits the causing entity.
`interaction` says what happens to blocks (`Mob` asks the source's
`entity_mob_griefing`, `Trigger` only works buttons, levers, doors and
the like); `fire` lights some of the air around whatever it is.
`settings` holds the damage calculator, particles and sound, each
vanilla's default when `None`. There is no radius limit, as in
vanilla: a big blast costs the blocks its rays find, and one of 0 or
below finds none. Refused, with nothing exploded and no hook told, as
[`ExplodeError`] says.
handles.signature: fn explode(self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: Option<EntityRef>, _: [f64; 3], _: f32, _: bool, _: ExplosionInteraction, _: ExplosionSettings) -> Result<(), ExplodeError>

handles.doc:
Side: server.
Destroys the blocks at `positions` as the blast `level.explode(host, source, center,
radius, fire, interaction)` would destroy them, without casting its rays, hurting or
pushing entities, or any packet or sound: a mod that casts its own rays breaks what they
found with it, spread over ticks if it likes. A Horizon addition. Each call is one
explosion to the hooks: `explosion_start` first, which may cancel it (then nothing breaks
and the answer is 0), then, for a radius of at least 0.00001, `explosion_detonate` with
the positions as its block list, in the order given, a repeated one once; a listener may
only take positions out (spare them), and one it adds is ignored. Then the block step in
vanilla's order: the positions shuffled with the level's random, and each block hit as
the blast hits one (air skipped; `can_drop_from_explosion`; loot with the radius under
the decay interaction; experience when the causing entity is a player;
`on_block_exploded`, whose default sets air and primes TNT owned by the causing entity),
the drops of the whole call merged and popped after the last block; then, with `fire`, a
third of the cells left air above a solid block catch fire, under `None` too. `None`
breaks nothing else, and `Trigger` only works the blocks it may. Unlike vanilla's rays, a
position in a chunk that isn't loaded is skipped, never loaded and not counted, and so is
one outside the level's height. The number of blocks destroyed: those that were not air
when their turn came. `Err`, with nothing changed, for more than 65,536 positions
(`ExplosionDestroyError::MAX_POSITIONS`), a stale level or `source`, or a centre or
radius that isn't finite or a negative radius.
handles.signature: fn explosion_destroy_blocks(self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &[[i32; 3]], _: Option<EntityRef>, _: [f64; 3], _: f32, _: bool, _: ExplosionInteraction) -> Result<u32, ExplosionDestroyError>

handles.doc:
Side: server.
The resistance the blast `level.explode(host, source, center, radius, fire, interaction)`
would set off would meet in the cell at `pos`, as its rays read it
(`ExplosionDamageCalculator.getBlockExplosionResistance`), without exploding anything. The
larger of the block's answer (its parts' `explosion_resistance` first, then its own value)
and the fluid's (water and lava 100); `NoResistance` for air with no fluid. The blast's
calculator is the one `explode` gives that source, read from the same selection: as
vanilla's `EntityBasedExplosionDamageCalculator` asks the source, a primed TNT minecart's
rails and the blocks under them resist 0 (and the blast spares them), and a dangerous
wither skull caps a block it may destroy at 0.8; any other source has the default one.
A respawn anchor's water cell
belongs to the anchor's own sourceless blast, which no description names, so no read sees
it. The causing entity and damage type come from `source` as for `explode`, and parts are
asked with that `ExplosionStart`. `Unavailable` for a stale level or `source`, a chunk
that isn't loaded (it is never loaded) or a state the game doesn't know; None only from a
host without a game. The level does not change.
handles.signature: fn explosion_resistance(self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: [i32; 3], _: Option<EntityRef>, _: [f64; 3], _: f32, _: bool, _: ExplosionInteraction) -> Option<ExplosionResistance>

handles.doc:
Side: server.
`level_explosion_resistance` for every cell of `cells`, one answer a cell in the order
`cells` gives them. A state is asked once per call only when every part on its block that
answers `explosion_resistance` declares the answer pure
(`BlockPart::explosion_resistance_is_pure`); otherwise its parts are asked once a cell.
Refused, with nothing read, for an inverted area or more than
`ResistanceCells::MAX` (262,144) cells: it runs on the server tick, so read big areas in
pieces.
handles.signature: fn explosion_resistances(self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &ResistanceCells, _: Option<EntityRef>, _: [f64; 3], _: f32, _: bool, _: ExplosionInteraction) -> Result<Vec<ExplosionResistance>, ResistanceCellsError>

Side: server.
`ServerLevel.findClosestBiome3d`: search this level's generator for an id or `#tag`.
The result follows vanilla's sampled spiral and vertical order; it is not a search
through edited biome cells. Does not load resident chunks or switch parked levels.
None for no match, a stale/unavailable level, an unavailable generator, a negative
radius, nonpositive sampling steps, or a potential sample count above
[`BiomeSearch::MAX_SAMPLES`] (see [`BiomeSearch::new`] for the work formula).
Positive vertical steps larger than the build height sample only the clamped origin.

Side: server.
`ServerLevel.findNearestMapStructure` without skipping known starts: the
nearest start of `structure`, an id or a `#tag`, searched in this
level's generator as `/locate structure` does. Random-spread structure
sets are searched in squares of placement cells out to
[`StructureSearch::radius`]; concentric rings (strongholds) check every
ring position whatever the radius. Starts are built as the search needs
them, without loading or generating chunks or switching parked levels.
None for no start, a structure that does not generate in this level,
a world without structures, a stale level, a client, a negative radius,
one above [`StructureSearch::MAX_RADIUS`], and an origin outside the
world's 30,000,000-block bound.

`FluidState.canBeReplacedWith(level, pos, fluid, direction)` for the fluid at `pos`: whether
`fluid` flowing in `direction` takes its place. The empty fluid yields to anything, water
only to a non-water fluid flowing down, lava to water once it stands 4/9 of a block high,
and a mod's world fluid to nothing. False for a `fluid` with no world form. None as for
`fluid_height`.
handles.signature: fn fluid_can_be_replaced_with(self, _: &dyn Host, _: [i32; 3], _: FluidKey, _: Direction) -> Option<bool>

Side: both.
`FluidState.getFlow` at `pos`: the current that pushes an entity there, after the
`fluid_flow` hook, as entities feel it. Zero where no fluid flows. None as for
`block_state`.

Side: both.
`FluidState.getHeight(level, pos)` of the fluid at `pos`: 0 for none, a full block under
the same fluid, else the fluid's own height (`amount / 9`). None as for `block_state`.
An unloaded block above counts as no fluid there.

Side: both.
The surface height of the fluid at `pos` that the camera's immersion test reads: a source
with a block above whose underside is sturdy fills its cell (1), anything else is
`fluid_height`. None as for `fluid_height`.

Side: both.
The fluid's shape at `pos` (`FluidState.getShape`), as block-local boxes: none for no
fluid, else one box from the floor to the fluid's height (`FluidState.getHeight`), a
full block under the same fluid, else the fluid's own height (`amount / 9`). None as for
`block_state`; an unloaded block above counts as no fluid there.

The fluid state at `pos` of the level `level` names (`BlockGetter.getFluidState`). None
for a stale handle, a chunk that isn't loaded or a `y` outside the world: a read never
loads a chunk.

Side: server.
Run the flow step of the fluid at `pos` now (`FluidState.tick`, which `ServerLevel.tickFluid`
calls for a due fluid tick): the fluid levels, spreads and schedules its next step with
the same random draws, hooks and level events as a queued one. Ticking the empty fluid does
nothing. The queue is not read or changed; `schedule_fluid_tick` queues one. False for a
refused write, a stale or parked handle, a client and an unloaded or out-of-height
position.

Side: server.
`Fluid.getTickDelay(level)`: the game ticks between a flow step of `fluid` at `pos` and the
next. Water is 5, lava 30 (10 in the Nether, where it flows fast) and the empty fluid 0; a
flowing form answers as its source. A mod's world fluid answers what it declared, as its
`fluid_rules` parts change it at `pos`, floored at 1. None for a stale handle, a client,
a level parked while the server ticks another, a position that isn't loaded or is outside
the world, and a fluid with no world form.

Side: server.
The level's force-loaded chunks (`/forceload query`), sorted as
the command lists them. None for a stale handle or on a client.

Side: server.
Sends game event `event` (`minecraft:block_change`...) from `at`, as
`Level.gameEvent(event, at, context)` does: sculk sensors, shriekers,
wardens and allays receive the optional source and affected state.
Returns false without emitting for an unknown event, invalid position,
stale or foreign source, unregistered state, client or inactive level.

Game rule `rule` (`minecraft:keep_inventory` or `keep_inventory`), as
`/gamerule` queries it: `Ok(None)` for an unknown rule. A gone/reopened level
returns `Stale`; an unreadable side or phase returns `Unavailable`.

Read a registered boolean game rule.

Side: server.
Read a registered integer game rule (`GameRules.getInt`), always within the range it was
declared with. None for a stale handle, a level the server has not opened, or a client.

Every game rule the world has (`GameRules`) with its current value, by `minecraft:` id

returns `Stale`; an unreadable side or phase returns `Unavailable`.

handles.doc:
Side: both.
The level's game time (`Level.getGameTime`). On clients this is the
synchronized time advanced by the local level tick. API 381.

Side: both.
`Level.getSkyDarken`: the sky-light reduction from dimension, time and weather.
Reads any loaded server level, including parked levels, or the current client level.
None for a stale or unavailable level. Does not load chunks.

Side: server.
Plays level event `id` at `pos` with `data` for every player on the
server, in every level and at any distance (`ServerLevel.globalLevelEvent`).
Vanilla's ids are the wither's spawn (`1023`), the dragon's death
(`1028`) and an End portal opening (`1038`): the client has a sound for
them only through this global form, played two blocks from the camera
towards the position the player is sent. Each player gets a position
of their own: `pos` in this level within 32 blocks of its centre, the
block 32 blocks from them towards that centre further away, and the
block they stand in for a player in another level.
With the `global_sound_events` game rule off it is a plain
[`level_event`](Self::level_level_event), as vanilla falls back: only
the players of this level near `pos` get it. False for the same events
and data `level_event` refuses, a parked level, a stale handle or a
client.

Side: both.
Whether any block collision shape shares volume with `aabb` (`[min_x, min_y, min_z, max_x,
max_y, max_z]`): the block half of `CollisionGetter.noCollision(aabb)`, negated. The same
walk and limits as `collision_boxes`, stopping at the first shape it finds; entities and
the world border are not counted. None as for `collision_boxes`.

Side: server.
Whether any neighbour powers the block at `pos` (`SignalGetter.hasNeighborSignal`),
asking no side past the first that does. False where `signal` is None.

Side: server.
Whether any watered-area ticket covers this block. Minimum bounds are inclusive and
maximum bounds exclusive on all three axes. Reads active and parked levels, loads no
chunks, and calls no mod predicates. False on clients or for a stale/unavailable level.

Side: both.
The lowest block `y` and the height of the level
(`LevelHeightAccessor.getMinY`, `getHeight`). Reads any loaded server level
or the client's current level. None for a stale handle, before client login,
or for a dimension unavailable on this side. Does not load chunks. API 381.

Side: server.
Whether this is the level in place: the one the server ticks now, whose block entities
the game's own capabilities read and write and whose capabilities
`LevelRef::capability` looks up. False for a level parked while the server ticks
another (its blocks can still be read), for a handle of an earlier open, and on a
client.

Side: both.
`Level.isInSpawnableBounds`: 30,000,000 blocks on x and z, 20,000,000 on y. None as for
`native_level_height`. Does not load chunks.

Side: both.
`Level.isInWorldBounds`: `pos` within 30,000,000 blocks on x and z and inside the level's
build height. None as for `native_level_height`. Does not load chunks.

Side: server.
Tells kept capabilities at `pos` that a provider's answer there changed with no change
of block or block entity (NeoForge's `invalidateCapabilities`), such as a machine whose
side configuration changed: the capability generation there moves on
([`LevelRef::capability_generation`]), so a [`BlockCapabilityCache`] there looks again
at its next `get`. Inside a transaction it happens at the root commit, and an aborted
one changes nothing. Block and block entity changes, chunk unloads and mod switches
need no call: the cache sees them itself. False, with nothing changed, off the level in
place, for a stale handle, on a client and for a position that isn't loaded.

Side: both.
Whether `pos` is inside the world's height and its chunk is loaded
(`Level.isLoaded`, which is false outside `isInValidBounds`): a block
read or write there finds the world. False on a client or for a stale
handle: the position is not loaded here. On a client, a chunk it holds is loaded
(`ClientLevel.hasChunkAt`). API 381.

Side: server.
Whether it rains (`Level.isRaining`: a rain level above 0.2).

Side: server.
`Level.isRainingAt(pos)` in the level a handle names, the one in place or a parked one:
it rains there and `pos` is under open sky in a biome that rains. None for a stale
handle, on a client, and where `pos` is not loaded or outside the world's height; a
read never loads a chunk.

Side: server.
`BlockState.isRedstoneConductor(level, pos)` for the block at `pos`: whether it passes
strong power on to its neighbours (stone and soul sand do; glass, single slabs and
leaves don't), answered by the game's redstone engine. The engine reads the state
alone, so today a block entity's live shape is ignored: an open shulker box still
conducts. None for a position that isn't loaded, and as for `signal`.

Side: server.
Whether it thunders (`Level.isThundering`: a thunder level above 0.9).

Side: server.
Plays level event `id` at `pos` with `data` for the players near it
(`Level.levelEvent(null, id, pos, data)`): `1000`s are sounds, `2000`s
particles, as vanilla's `LevelEvent` numbers them (`2001` breaks a
block with state id `data`). No player is left out, the acting one
included. False for an event that carries a block state (2001, 2014,
3008) when `data` isn't one.
handles.signature: fn level_event(self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: i32, _: [i32; 3], _: i32) -> bool

handles.doc:
Side: server.
`ServerLevel.findLightningTargetAround`: the closest lightning rod near the column at
`pos`'s `x` and `z`, else a living entity under open sky within 3 blocks of it, picked
with the level random as vanilla does (so this moves later draws), else the top of the
column. Strikes nothing. None for a refused level, a stale or parked handle, a client and
an unloaded column.

Side: server.
Whether nothing solid lies on the segment `from`..`to`, as
`LivingEntity.hasLineOfSight` clips between two eyes (`ClipContext.Block.COLLIDER`,
`ClipContext.Fluid.NONE`): `clip`'s miss. Fluids, entities and the border don't block it.
None as for `clip`.

Side: both.
Every loaded chunk of an open server level as handles, ordered by chunk x then z. None for
a stale handle or on a client. Loads nothing.

Side: server.
The local difficulty at `pos` (`ServerLevel.getCurrentDifficultyAt`), as mobs spawned
there are finalized with: the world difficulty scaled by the level's age, the chunk's
inhabited time and the moon (both 0 for a chunk that isn't loaded). Its
`special_multiplier` is vanilla's `getSpecialMultiplier`. None for a stale handle, a level
the server has not opened, or a client.

Side: both.
The dimension's logical height (`ServerLevel.getLogicalHeight`), which may differ
from build height. Reads active and parked server levels or the client's current level.
None for a stale or unavailable level. Does not load chunks.

Side: server.
Map `id`'s saved data (`ServerLevel.getMapData(new MapId(id))`): read from memory, or
from `data/minecraft/maps/<id>.dat` when nothing has loaded it yet, without keeping it.
Maps belong to the world, not to a level. None on a client, for a stale handle and for
a map id nothing ever made.

Side: server.
The chunk tickets `controller` holds in the level, as (owner, chunk
position, natural_spawning), in order. None for a stale handle, on a
client, outside a mod's hook and for another mod's controller.
