Side: server.
Tell the block at `pos` that `source`'s block beside it changed (`Level.neighborChanged`),
as a diode tells the block in front of it before updating that block's neighbours.
Typed errors refuse stale/unavailable levels or invalid states; Ok(false) means an
unloaded or out-of-height position. Errors never mutate the level.
handles.signature: fn neighbor_changed(self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: [i32; 3], _: BlockState) -> Result<bool, LevelWriteError>

handles.doc:
Side: server.
`ServerLevel.players`: the online players in this level, parked or in
place, each once under their own UUID, also during a guest's turn. Fake
players are not listed, as vanilla's list leaves out connectionless
players; a player displaced by a nested guest turn is not listed either,
since its handle cannot resolve until that turn ends. None on a client
and for a stale handle.

Side: server.
`BucketPickup.pickupBlock` for a mod's fluid container (NeoForge's
`FluidUtil.tryPickupFluid`): takes the fluid source at `pos` in the level in place, a
waterlogged block's water or a bubble column's, as an empty bucket would, `player`
picking it up when given (only a creative player drains a barrier). What came out, a
bucket of it. None, with nothing done, where the block gives no fluid (a flowing fluid,
powder snow, any other block), in another level, a chunk that isn't loaded, or a
transaction that isn't open.

Kept by transaction `tx`: the block is decided and written at the call, so later reads
in the transaction see it drained and a second pickup there gets nothing; its updates, a
drained block's drops when it no longer survives, and the bucket's fill sound and
`minecraft:fluid_pickup` (from `player`) follow at the outermost commit. An abort leaves
the world as it was, with no drop, sound or event, where NeoForge's may have changed it.
handles.signature: fn pickup_fluid(self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: [i32; 3], _: Option<PlayerRef>, _: &Transaction) -> Option<FluidStack>

`BucketItem.emptyContents` of a bucket of `fluid` for a mod's fluid container (NeoForge's
`FluidUtil.tryPlaceFluid`), with no hit result: at `pos` in the level in place, its source
into air or a block it replaces (broken with its drops), water into a waterloggable
block (a lit campfire or candle put out), or hissing away where water evaporates (the
Nether). `validate` refuses a waterloggable block that won't take it (one waterlogged
already), which a bucket empties into all the same (NeoForge's `validatePlaced`). True
when it was placed or hissed away; false, with nothing done, for a fluid with no world
form, where it can't be placed, in another level, a chunk that isn't loaded, or a
transaction that isn't open.

Kept by transaction `tx` as [`level_pickup_fluid`](Self::level_pickup_fluid) is: the
block written at the call, its updates, the fluid tick, a replaced block's drops, a doused
block's sound and the bucket's empty sound and `minecraft:fluid_place` (from `player`) at
the outermost commit, nothing of it after an abort.
handles.signature: fn place_fluid(self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: [i32; 3], _: FluidKey, _: Option<PlayerRef>, _: bool, _: &Transaction) -> bool

The bucket's sound and game event for `fluid` at the centre of `pos` in the level in
place, as `FluidUtil.triggerSoundAndGameEvent` plays them (`pickup`: the fill sound and
`minecraft:fluid_pickup`, else the empty sound and `minecraft:fluid_place`; a tank-only
fluid has no sound), from `player` when given, at the outermost commit of transaction
`tx`: nothing if it aborts. False, with nothing queued, in another level or for a
transaction that isn't open.

Plays sound event `sound` at `at` for the players in this level
within range (16 blocks, times the volume above 1), as
`ServerLevel.playSound(null, ...)` does, under `source`'s volume
slider. A `minecraft:` event must be registered; a mod's goes by name
and is heard where its resources define it. True means queued, not
heard.

Drops `stack` as a broken block drops it (`Block.popResource`): an
item entity at a random point within a quarter block of the middle of
`pos` (three draws from the level random, made for an empty stack and
with `block_drops` off too), with its own random motion and the
default pickup delay of 10 ticks. None, with nothing spawned, for an
empty stack or an unknown item, with the `block_drops` rule off, on a
client, for a stale handle, a level not in place, once the entity ids run out, or an
item a mod kept out (`entity_join_level`).
Inside a transaction its join waits for the root commit, so a mod keeping the item out is not
known at the call: the handle is returned and reads stale from the commit on.

Side: server.
`Raids.get(id)`: the raid saved under `id` in the requested level, if
`Raids` still holds it (a stopped raid goes at its next tick).

Side: server.
`ServerLevel.getRaidAt(pos)`: the closest active raid whose centre is
less than 96 blocks away (`Raids.getNearbyRaid`, 9216 squared).

Side: server.
Every raid `Raids` holds, in its iteration order, stopped ones
included until their next tick. None for a closed or stale level.

Side: server.
The random of the server level `level` names: vanilla's `Level.random`
(`level.getRandom()`), the one its explosions, block drops and other
level draws use, so a mod's draws move vanilla's later ones as a Java
mod's do. A parked level (the Nether while the server ticks the
Overworld) answers with its own stream. This is a copy of it as it
stands: draw with `LevelRef::with_random`, which stores the stream
back, so the draws move the level's own. `None` on a client of a
server, for a stale handle and for a level not open: the Nether and
the End open when someone first goes there and close after 300 ticks
with nobody in them (`close_idle_levels`).

Side: server.
Every entity the segment from `from` to `to` passes through, nearest first: the test
`ProjectileUtil.getEntityHitResult` makes on each candidate, each entity's box grown by
`margin` on every side and clipped against the segment. A ray that starts inside a box
does not hit that entity, as in vanilla. `exclude` (the shooter) is skipped. Vanilla's
filter (`canHitEntity`, `isPickable`) is the caller's: take the first hit it accepts.
Candidates are those `entities_in` finds, so spectators are not hit and the same kinds
are left out. None for a negative or non-finite margin, a non-finite point, and where
`entities_in` is None (a stale handle, a parked level).
handles.signature: fn ray_trace_entities(self, _: &dyn Host, _: [f64; 3], _: [f64; 3], _: f64, _: Option<EntityRef>) -> Option<Vec<EntityRayHit>>

handles.doc:
Side: server.
Match and assemble through the engine's recipe matcher, without consuming inputs.
Covers minecraft:crafting, smelting, blasting, smoking, campfire_cooking,
stonecutting and smithing, including data-pack recipes of those types.
Registered crafting serializers match through minecraft:crafting. Read-only and unregistered
mod-owned types return RecipeLookupError::NotMatchable; cache recipes_of_type once
per load/reload and match those in mod memory (no per-tick host crossing).
A valid input without a match returns Ok(None); invalid shapes/items and unavailable
levels are typed refusals. Crafting dimensions are 1 through 3, with row-major slots.

Side: server.
Registers `passage` in the level ([`Passage`], arismoko/horizon#3775) and numbers it. The engine
tells it to every Horizon client holding its chunk ([`Passage::chunk`]) at the end of
the server's tick, and to a client that gets the chunk later as the chunk is sent
(`chunk_sent`); a client forgets it with the chunk. Passages are not saved and a
datapack reload does not bring them back: they hold until `remove_passage`, the
level's close or the world's, so a mod registers its own again in `level_load`. An
id is never given again while the game runs. A level holds 256 at most and a chunk 8.
A passage removed before the tick's end is never told. Refused with nothing
registered for a stale handle, a client, a passage that isn't a finite rectangle
with unit axes at a right angle and sides above 0 and at most 32 blocks, one with a
corner past vanilla's position limits, a full level or chunk, and once every id was
given.
handles.signature: fn register_passage(self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: Passage) -> Result<PassageId, PassageRegistrationError>

handles.doc:
Side: server.
Queues the loaded chunks `chunks` (chunk coordinates) of the level in place, and the loaded
chunks around them, to be lit again whole from their blocks, for a mod that wrote blocks by
other means (`edit_blocks` queues the same relight for its own chunks). Accepted at once and
never lit during the call: the light jobs run at the level's next light update, as those of `edit_blocks` and
`level_check_light` do, and a column whose eight
neighbours are not all loaded waits until they are. The light that changed goes to the
players who see that chunk's border, as any relight's does. There is no completion event
and no per-call count of finished chunks: a mod that needs the new light reads it on a
later tick (`level_brightness`), and `chunk_resend` sends the chunk with whatever light has
landed by the end of that tick. Returns how many columns were queued, the ring included; a
column not loaded, or already waiting in the queue, is not counted. The queue is bounded
(4096 columns in all, and 256 chunks a call): a call that would pass either is refused
whole with `TooManyChunks`, whose `max` is how many chunks a call may take now. Each
refusal queues nothing and is named by `ChunkRefusal`: `Stale`, `Client`, `NotInPlace` (a
level that is not the one being ticked) and `TooManyChunks`.
handles.signature: fn relight_chunks(self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &[[i32; 2]]) -> Result<u32, ChunkRefusal>

Remove a block in place (`Level.removeBlock`), preserving its fluid.
handles.signature: fn remove_block(self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: [i32; 3], _: bool) -> bool

handles.doc:
Side: server.
Removes the level's passage `id`: the clients that were told of it are told it is
gone at the end of the server's tick. True when it was registered in this level.
False for another level's or an unknown id, a stale handle and a client.
handles.signature: fn remove_passage(self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: PassageId) -> bool

handles.doc:
Side: server.
Ask for the level to be saved: its level data, chunks and entities, as the autosave and
`/save-all` save a level, with its chunks on disk when it ends. The save runs at the start
of the next server tick, not inside the call, which may be in a hook of the very tick that
is saving; a level asked for twice before then is saved once. True when the request was
taken: the call cannot tell whether the save worked. `level_save` fires with the level's
dimension once it was written; a save that fails fires nothing and is logged. False for a
stale handle and on a client.

Side: server.
The world's respawn data (`LevelData.getRespawnData`): the world spawn and the way a
player appearing there faces, as `/setworldspawn` sets them. Horizon keeps one world
spawn, in the Overworld, so every level of a world answers the same. None on a client,
for a stale handle, and before the world has chosen its spawn.

Side: server.
One roll of the loot table `table` (`mymod:sifting/gravel`, the world's data packs
merged), handed back instead of dropped: `LootTable.getRandomItems(LootParams)` with
`origin` as ORIGIN, `tool` as TOOL when given and `entity` as THIS_ENTITY when given,
the context `/loot … fish <table> <pos> <tool>` gives. The roll draws from the table's
random sequence, else the level random, as vanilla's does, so it moves later draws: that
is why this is a write. The stacks come split to their stack sizes, empties left out.
Mods' loot kinds see `origin` and this level; no `loot_drops` event, since nothing
drops. None for a table that isn't there, a stale or parked handle, a client, and a
stale `entity`.
handles.signature: fn roll_loot(self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &str, _: [f64; 3], _: Option<&item::item_stack::ItemStack>, _: Option<EntityRef>) -> Result<Option<Vec<item::item_stack::ItemStack>>, item::item_stack::StackWriteError>

handles.doc:
Side: server.
`Level.getSeaLevel`: 63 in the Overworld, 32 in the Nether, 0 in the End; for a level of the
noise generator the `sea_level` of its noise settings (a data pack's too, when it replaces
them), for another level the `sea_level` its `DimensionSettings` gave, else 63. It is the sea
level the game uses for the level: terrain and aquifers, mob spawning and mob behaviour, rain
and snow, and maps. None for a stale handle and on a client.

Side: server.
The world's seed (`WorldOptions.seed`), as `/seed` shows it.

Side: server.
Tell the clients the block at `pos` changed (`Level.sendBlockUpdated`): its state and
block entity data are sent again at the end of the tick, without writing anything, for
a mod that changed what a block shows by other means than a block write. False, with
nothing queued, for a stale or parked handle, a client, and an unloaded or out-of-height
position. True with no player to notify (no one is in the level) when the position is
valid: the chunk is marked changed and nothing is sent.
Inside a transaction this waits for the root commit; abort publishes no notice.
Outside a transaction this executes immediately. True means accepted or queued,
not already delivered.

Side: server.
Sends `count` particles around `at` to the players in this level
within 32 blocks, as `ServerLevel.sendParticles` does: each offset is
a Gaussian times `spread`, and `speed` scales their motion (a zero
count sends one particle moving along `spread`). Block particle types
need `state`; item particles need `options.item_stack` (validated against
the item registry and stack limits). Trail and vibration remain unsupported.
True means queued, not drawn.
handles.signature: fn send_particles(self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &ParticleOptions, _: Option<BlockState>, _: [f64; 3], _: [f64; 3], _: f64, _: i32) -> bool

handles.doc:
Side: both.
Set the biome of the 4x4x4 cell holding `pos` to `biome` (`minecraft:plains`), as
`/fillbiome` does for one cell. False for a refused write, a stale or parked handle, a
client, an unknown biome and an unchanged cell.
Tentative reads see the new cells inside a transaction. Abort restores the cells
without publishing. Saving, remeshing and resending wait for the outermost commit,
once per column. Outside a transaction they run immediately.

Side: server.
Set a block (`Level.setBlock`). Stale/unavailable levels and invalid states return
typed errors without mutation. Ok(false) means vanilla refused an unchanged,
unloaded or out-of-height write. Notification follows the supplied update flags.
handles.signature: fn set_block(self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: [i32; 3], _: BlockState, _: BlockUpdateFlags) -> Result<bool, LevelWriteError>

handles.doc:
Side: server.
Send `ServerLevel.destroyBlockProgress` in this level: stages 0..9 show a crack,
any other stage removes it. A machine uses a stable negative breaker id.
Inside a transaction, notices wait for the root commit in call order; abort publishes
no notice. Outside a transaction this executes immediately. True means accepted or
queued, not already delivered.

fn set_client_break_progress(self, _: &mut dyn ClientHost, _: i32, _: [i32; 3], _: i32) -> bool

handles.doc:
Side: server.
Sets the time of the level's own clock (its dimension type's `default_clock`, the one
`level_clock_time` reads) to `time` ticks, as `/time set <time>` run in that level does:
`time_skip` (cause `mod`) fires first and a mod can keep the old time, and the clock's
fraction of a tick restarts. Players see the new time with the next time sync. A time
the clock already shows is true and changes nothing. False for a negative time, a level
without a default clock, a stale handle, a client, and when a mod kept the old time.
handles.signature: fn set_clock_time(self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: i64) -> bool

handles.doc:
Side: server.
Sets game rule `rule` (`minecraft:keep_inventory` or `keep_inventory`) to `value`, as
`/gamerule <rule> <value>` does (`GameRules.set` and `MinecraftServer.onGameRuleChanged`):
the world follows it (`advance_time` freezes the clocks), `game_rule_changed` fires with
no actor, and the players' clients get the rules they show. The rules are the world's,
so any open level's handle sets them. True also when the rule already had the value.
False for an unknown rule, a value of the other kind or outside the rule's range, a
stale handle and a client.
handles.signature: fn set_game_rule(self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &str, _: GameRuleValue) -> bool

handles.doc:
Side: server.
Repaint map `id` with `colors` (128 by 128 colour ids, row by row), pixel by pixel as
`MapItemSavedData.setColor` does: each changed pixel marks the map to save, to redraw and
to send to the players carrying or framing it. True when a pixel changed. False for
another length, a stale handle, a client and a map id nothing made.
handles.signature: fn set_map_data(self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: i32, _: &[u8]) -> bool

handles.doc:
Side: server.
Replace the random of the server level `level` names with `random`,
a stream `native_level_random` gave and the mod drew from. False where
that gives `None`.
handles.signature: fn set_random(self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: LegacyRandom) -> bool

handles.doc:
Side: server.
`LevelData.setRespawnData(RespawnData.of(..))`, as `/setworldspawn` does: the world spawn
moves to `pos`, facing `yaw` (wrapped to -180..180) and `pitch` (clamped to -90..90), a
player whose own respawn point was the old world spawn follows it, and `spawn_change`
fires. Only the Overworld's handle, where Horizon keeps the world spawn. False for
another level, a stale handle, a client, a non-finite angle and a position outside the
spawnable bounds.
handles.signature: fn set_respawn_data(self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: [i32; 3], _: f32, _: f32) -> bool

handles.doc:
Side: server.
Sets which categories the level's natural spawning may spawn
([`SpawnFlags`]), from the next spawn pass on. Kept and refused as
`set_spawn_limits`.
handles.signature: fn set_spawn_flags(self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: SpawnFlags) -> bool

handles.doc:
Side: server.
Sets the level's natural spawning limits ([`SpawnLimits`]), from the next
spawn pass on. They hold until the world closes, while the level is
parked and across its closing and opening again, and are not saved: the
world opens with vanilla's, so a mod sets its own in `level_load`. Mobs
already in the level stay. False, with nothing set, on a client and for
a stale handle or a level that isn't open.
handles.signature: fn set_spawn_limits(self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: SpawnLimits) -> bool

handles.doc:
Side: server.
Sets the weather as `/weather` does (`ServerLevel.setWeatherParameters`): clear for
`clear_ticks`, or raining (and thundering) for `weather_ticks`, after which the
weather cycle goes on as usual. Rain and thunder then fade in or out as vanilla's do;
`set_weather_levels` sets their strength at once. The `weather_change` hook may cancel
all of it and `thunder_change` the thunder. The players see it after the next sync.
False for a negative time, a call from inside `weather_change` or `thunder_change`, a
parked level, a stale handle or a client.
handles.signature: fn set_weather(self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: i32, _: i32, _: bool, _: bool) -> bool

handles.doc:
Side: server.
How strong the rain and thunder are now (`Level.setRainLevel`, `setThunderLevel`),
each clamped to 0 to 1 and set without fading. They still drift toward the weather
the level has (`set_weather`) by 0.01 a tick, as vanilla's do. False for a value that
isn't finite, a parked level, a stale handle or a client.
handles.signature: fn set_weather_levels(self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: f32, _: f32) -> bool

handles.doc:
Side: server.
Moves the world border's centre (`WorldBorder.setCenter`), as `/worldborder center`
does. Horizon keeps one border for every level, so this moves it everywhere; the
players see it after the next sync. The centre it already has is true, with nothing
heard. False for a centre that isn't finite or lies past 2.9999984E7 on x or z, a call
from inside `world_border_center_changed`, a stale handle, a level the server has not
opened or a client.

Side: server.
The world border's damage (`setDamagePerBlock`, `setSafeZone`), as `/worldborder
damage amount` and `buffer`: a player outside the border and past `safe_zone` blocks
takes `per_block` damage for each block beyond it. False for a value that is
negative or not finite, a stale handle, a level the server has not opened or a client.
handles.signature: fn set_world_border_damage(self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: f64, _: f64) -> bool

handles.doc:
Side: server.
Sets the world border's size, as `/worldborder set`: at once when `ticks` is 0
(`setSize`), otherwise growing or shrinking in a straight line over `ticks` game ticks
from its size now (`lerpSizeBetween`). The one border every level shares. A still
border set to the size it has at once is true, with nothing heard. False for a size
outside 1 to 5.9999968E7, a negative `ticks`, a call from inside
`world_border_bounds_changed`, a stale handle, a level the server has not opened or a
client.
handles.signature: fn set_world_border_size(self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: f64, _: i64) -> bool

handles.doc:
Side: server.
The world border's warning (`setWarningBlocks`, `setWarningTime`), as `/worldborder
warning distance` and `time`: a player's screen tints red within `distance` blocks of
the border, or when a shrinking border will reach them within `ticks` game ticks.
False for a negative value, a stale handle, a level the server has not opened or a
client.
handles.signature: fn set_world_border_warning(self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: i32, _: i32) -> bool

handles.doc:
Side: server.
`Some(true)` when scheduled blocks, block events and block entities can tick here:
a resident, in-bounds position with block-ticking tickets and no pending entities.
`Some(false)` for unloaded or out-of-bounds positions, tickets that forbid ticking,
or a chunk waiting for its entities. With no ticket system, resident in-bounds
chunks with no pending entities tick; an active but empty ticket system permits none.
`None` for stale handles, a client or a level not currently in place. Parked
levels cannot answer because the live ticket state belongs to the level in place.
Does not load chunks. Each call shares the ticket map through a reference count
and borrows the pending-entity set without copying it or allocating a memo table.

Side: server.
How strongly the block at `pos` powers the block on its `direction` side, power it
conducts included (`SignalGetter.getSignal(pos, direction)`, as a block reads its
neighbour `pos` that lies `direction` from it), 0 to 15. None for another level, a stale
handle or a client. Takes a shared host and opens no transaction.

Side: server.
Which categories the level's natural spawning may spawn ([`SpawnFlags`]):
both on until a mod turns one off. Reads parked levels. None on a
client and for a stale handle.

Side: server.
Spawns `stack` as an item entity at `x y z` (`new ItemEntity(level, x,
y, z, stack)` and `addFreshEntity`): its own random motion (up 0.2, up
to 0.1 either way across), with `pickup_delay` ticks before it can be
picked up, as `ItemEntity.setPickupDelay` at construction (vanilla
passes 10 for a block's drop, 40 for a player's throw and 32767 for
never). None, with nothing
spawned, for an empty stack or an unknown item, a value that isn't
finite, on a client, for a stale handle, a level not in place, or an
item a mod kept out (`entity_join_level`).
Inside a transaction its join waits for the root commit, so a mod keeping the item out is not
known at the call: the handle is returned and reads stale from the commit on.
handles.signature: fn spawn_item(self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: f64, _: f64, _: f64, _: item::item_stack::ItemStack, _: u32) -> Result<Option<EntityRef>, item::item_stack::StackWriteError>

handles.doc:
Side: server.
`spawn_item` with the item entity's motion set to
`motion` (blocks a tick), as `new ItemEntity(level, x, y, z, stack,
deltaX, deltaY, deltaZ)`, and the same `pickup_delay` ticks before it
can be picked up (`ItemEntity.setPickupDelay`). None in the same
cases, and for a motion that isn't finite.
handles.signature: fn spawn_item_with_motion(self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: f64, _: f64, _: f64, _: item::item_stack::ItemStack, _: [f64; 3], _: u32) -> Result<Option<EntityRef>, item::item_stack::StackWriteError>

handles.doc:
Side: server.
The level's natural spawning limits by category ([`SpawnLimits`]):
[`SpawnLimits::VANILLA`] until a mod sets others. Reads parked levels.
None on a client and for a stale handle.

Side: server.
Spawns a mob of `kind` (`minecraft:zombie`) at `pos` in the level as
`EntityType.spawn` does with `reason`: the entity type creates it (its
Parts and attachments with it, and `entity_constructing`), with a random
yaw from the level random, then `finalize_spawn` and `finalizeSpawn`
with that reason (equipment, variants, jockeys), and it joins the level
(`entity_join_level`), not persistent, as a natural spawn joins. The
level's spawn limits, flags and spawn rules don't apply, as they don't
to `/summon`. The new mob as a handle. None, with nothing spawned, for a
kind that isn't a mob, a position that isn't finite or is outside the
spawnable bounds (`Level.isInSpawnableBounds`), an unloaded chunk, a
stale handle, a level not in place, a client, a `finalize_spawn` that
cancelled the spawn or a mob a mod kept out.
Inside a transaction its join waits for the root commit, so a mod keeping the mob out is not
known at the call: the handle is returned and reads stale from the commit on.
handles.signature: fn spawn_mob(self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &str, _: [f64; 3], _: SpawnReason) -> Option<EntityRef>

handles.doc:
Side: server.
Strikes lightning at `at`, as summoning a `minecraft:lightning_bolt`
does: it sets fire, hurts and converts what it hits (a pig to a
zombified piglin...) and every player hears the thunder. With
`visual_only` it only flashes and sounds (`setVisualOnly`). The
`lightning_strike` hook hears it first with the cause `mod` and may
cancel it. False for a chunk that isn't loaded or a canceled strike.
handles.signature: fn strike_lightning(self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: [f64; 3], _: bool) -> bool

handles.doc:
Side: server.
`StructureManager.getStructureAt` and `getStructureWithPieceAt` in one read: every
structure the chunk at `pos` refers to whose start's box or one of whose pieces, as
placed, holds `pos`, with which of the two (`in_box`, `in_piece`). Reads the level in place or
parked from the starts the generator holds: loads no chunk and builds no start. Empty
for a chunk that refers to no structure there; None on a client, for a stale or
unavailable level, for a chunk that isn't loaded and for one whose references the level
can't resolve now (a level without generated terrain, or starts the generator no longer
holds).

Side: server.
Tell the neighbours of `pos` that a block changed there, as vanilla's own writes do:
`Neighbours` (`Level.updateNeighborsAt`: a lever's or a button's own block, and the one
it is attached to, when the signal it gives changes), `NeighboursExcept(direction)`
(`updateNeighborsAtExceptFromFacing`: a diode's front) or `OutputSignal`
(`updateNeighbourForOutputSignal`: the comparators beside it, when its comparator output
changes without its state changing). `source` is the state whose block vanilla passes as
the one that changed. Typed errors refuse stale/unavailable levels or invalid states
without mutation; Ok(false) means an unloaded or out-of-height position.
handles.signature: fn update_neighbors(self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: [i32; 3], _: BlockState, _: NeighbourUpdate) -> Result<bool, LevelWriteError>

handles.doc:
Side: both.
The rain and thunder levels, each 0.0 to 1.0 (`Level.getRainLevel`,
`getThunderLevel` at partial tick 1.0): both 0 in a level with no weather.
Reads any open server level or the client's current synchronized level;
None for a stale handle, an unavailable level or a client not logged in.

Draw from the level's own random stream (vanilla's `Level.random`), in vanilla's order:
`draw` gets the stream and the level keeps it after. None where `random` is None.
handles.signature: fn with_random<T>(self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: impl FnOnce(&mut LegacyRandom) -> T) -> Option<T>

handles.doc:
Side: server.
The level's world border as [min_x, min_z, max_x, max_z], using the
previous size while it moves. Horizon currently shares one border
across its dimensions. None for a stale handle or a closed level.

Draw from the level's own random stream, in vanilla's order: `draw` gets the
stream and the level keeps it after. None on a non-authoritative level.
handles.signature: fn with_random<T>(&mut self, _: impl FnOnce(&mut LegacyRandom) -> T) -> Option<T>

handles.doc: Both channels at 15.
`block` and `sky` each in `0..=15`, or `None`.
`inner`, limited to `max_insert` in and `max_extract` out per call.
handles.signature: fn new(_: Box<dyn EnergyHandler>, _: u32, _: u32) -> Self

handles.doc: The registered listener's name.
Names a listener key.

Side: both.
The entity's absorption amount (`LivingEntity.getAbsorptionAmount`; Paper's
`Damageable#getAbsorptionAmount`), the extra hearts that take a hit before
health does. Resolves as `living_health` does: during a player's turn only
that player. None for an armor stand and the dragon, which carry none.

Side: server.
Adds an attribute modifier (`AttributeInstance.addTransientModifier`
or `addPermanentModifier`). A permanent one is saved with the entity;
a transient one lasts until it unloads. It goes where `/attribute`
writes (`Game::write_attribute`), so gameplay and the entity's clients
see it. False when the entity already has a modifier with that id on
the attribute (vanilla throws), for an attribute the entity type does
not have, a non-finite amount, the dragon (whose attributes nothing
reads yet), a stale handle, or on a client.
handles.signature: fn add_attribute_modifier(self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &str, _: AttributeModifier, _: ModifierLifetime) -> bool

handles.doc:
Side: server.
`LivingEntity.addEffect(instance)`: gives the living entity the
effect by the game's own path. A player's or a guest's goes through
`add_player_effect` (so `MobEffectInstance.update`'s rules, the
attribute modifiers, absorption and the added-effect hooks of a
content mod's effect all apply); a mob's goes past `canBeAffected`
(a spider shrugs off poison) into its effects with the same hooks.
The amplifier is cut to 0..=255 and the duration is -1 (infinite) or
ticks. False before effect resolution, for a duration below -1, an armor
stand, the dragon, a stale handle or a client, or when the active
instance did not change, as in vanilla's `addEffect`.

Side: server.
Whether the entity is alive (`LivingEntity.isAlive`; Paper's
`Entity#isDead` is its inverse). A dying mob, mid death
animation, is not.

In a mob's goal tick ([`GoalContext::host`](crate::GoalContext::host)) this reads
the active mob or a disjoint live mob when available; player reads use the
game host. Other unsupported reads retain their typed refusal.

Side: server.
Apply one loaded consumable effect without consuming the item.
Mod-defined kinds enter the normal consume_effect hook: Some(true) means
dispatch was entered, not that a listener changed game state. Reapplying
the same kind from its own handler on this call stack returns Some(false)
without recursing; other kinds dispatch normally. None means an unavailable
item/index/target or an unsupported vanilla effect for that target.
handles.signature: fn apply_consume_effect(self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: &item::item_stack::ItemStack, _: usize) -> Result<Option<bool>, item::item_stack::StackWriteError>

handles.doc:
Side: server.
`LivingEntity.getArrowCount`: the arrows stuck in a player or a mob.
None for armor stands and the dragon, which Horizon keeps no count
for, and for a stale handle.

Side: both.
The base value of an attribute, before modifiers
(`AttributeMap.getBaseValue`), read as the effective value is.

In a mob's goal tick ([`GoalContext::host`](crate::GoalContext::host)) this reads
the active mob or a disjoint live mob when available; player reads use the
game host. Other unsupported reads retain their typed refusal.

Side: both.
The modifiers on the entity's attribute `id`
(`AttributeInstance.getModifiers`), in the order they were added: a
mod's transient and permanent ones, the saved list's, and what the
worn and held items grant. An attribute no modifier is on answers an
empty list; None for an attribute the entity type does not have, a
stale handle, or on a client for any entity but the local player,
whose copy of the synced instances it reads.

In a mob's goal tick ([`GoalContext::host`](crate::GoalContext::host)) this reads
the active mob or a disjoint live mob when available; player reads use the
game host. Other unsupported reads retain their typed refusal.

Side: both.
The effective value of an attribute on a living entity
(`AttributeMap.getValue`). None for an unknown or absent attribute, an
unavailable entity, a stale handle, or on a client for any entity but
the local player, whose copy of the synced instances it reads. A mob,
an armor stand and the dragon answer from their live attribute map: the
type's defaults, the saved `attributes`, and the modifiers of what they
wear or hold.

In a mob's goal tick ([`GoalContext::host`](crate::GoalContext::host)) this reads
the active mob or a disjoint live mob when available; player reads use the
game host. Other unsupported reads retain their typed refusal.

Side: both.
The ids of the attributes the entity's type has
(`AttributeMap`'s holder's attribute set), in registry order: the same
set the value and base reads answer for. None for a stale handle or an
unavailable entity; on a client, for any entity but the local player
(the client keeps no attribute map of another entity's, only the few
fields it draws).

In a mob's goal tick ([`GoalContext::host`](crate::GoalContext::host)) this reads
the active mob or a disjoint live mob when available; player reads use the
game host. Other unsupported reads retain their typed refusal.

Side: both.
Whether the entity is a baby (`LivingEntity.isBaby`): a mob answers
from its age, negative until it grows up. A player, an armor stand
and the dragon are never babies.

In a mob's goal tick ([`GoalContext::host`](crate::GoalContext::host)) this reads
the active mob or a disjoint live mob when available; player reads use the
game host. Other unsupported reads retain their typed refusal.

Side: server.
The bed a sleeper lies in, as its block faces
(`LivingEntity.getBedOrientation` over `BedBlock.getBedOrientation`):
the block at the sleeping position, its `facing` where that block is
one of `#minecraft:beds` — one path for every sleeper. None where
the sleeper keeps no position, the block is not a bed, or the handle
is stale.

In a mob's goal tick ([`GoalContext::host`](crate::GoalContext::host)) this reads
the active mob or a disjoint live mob when available; player reads use the
game host. Other unsupported reads retain their typed refusal.

Side: server.
`LivingEntity.canBreatheUnderwater`: the species' own breath —
`is(#can_breathe_under_water)` in vanilla, `breathes_water` here (a
squid's true, a dolphin's false); a player answers false (no player
kind is in the tag). This is the tag read only, not the whole drown
decision: the air tick itself also keeps the air up behind Water
Breathing, the conduit's power and a player's invulnerability,
which this read does not carry. None for a stale handle, an armor
stand or the dragon.

In a mob's goal tick ([`GoalContext::host`](crate::GoalContext::host)) this reads
the active mob or a disjoint live mob when available; player reads use the
game host. Other unsupported reads retain their typed refusal.

Side: server.
`LivingEntity.canFreeze`: the decision the freeze tick itself runs —
a mob's (`ai::can_freeze`: not `#freeze_immune_entity_types`, no
`#freeze_immune_wearables` worn), a player's
(`PlayerMotion::can_freeze`: not a spectator, no immune armor).
None for a stale handle, an armor stand or the dragon.

In a mob's goal tick ([`GoalContext::host`](crate::GoalContext::host)) this reads
the active mob or a disjoint live mob when available; player reads use the
game host. Other unsupported reads retain their typed refusal.

Side: server.
`Entity.canUsePortal`: the engine's one gate for a player,
`player_can_use_portal` (`Entity.canUsePortal(false)`: alive, nobody's
passenger — and not asleep, vanilla `LivingEntity.canUsePortal`'s
`isSleeping` half; a parity fix: the client's portal entry used to
skip it), a guest's the same rule over their body and vehicle, a
mob's walk gate (`mob_can_use_portal`, 's read: not a boss that
never travels, not a creaking bound to its heart, not asleep in its
bed, riding nothing, carrying no one this side holds back). None for
a stale handle, an armor stand or the dragon: the portal walk
carries neither as its own traveller.

In a mob's goal tick ([`GoalContext::host`](crate::GoalContext::host)) this reads
the active mob or a disjoint live mob when available; player reads use the
game host. Other unsupported reads retain their typed refusal.

Side: server.
`LivingEntity.clearSleepingPos`: the player no longer names a bed, so
`is_sleeping` is false and the next entity sync stands them up.
Normal server guests in the level in place are supported; guests in
another level, fake players, mobs, armor stands and the dragon are
refused. This does not run the wake-up animation
or move the player; use `stop_sleeping` to stand beside the bed.

Side: both.
`LivingEntity.getDimensions(Pose)`: the box the living entity has in
`pose` — its width, height and eye height, `minecraft:scale`
included, the fixed 0.2 box of a sleeping pose included. The species'
own state still answers where its `getDefaultDimensions` reads it: a
digging sniffer or an emerging warden is low in every pose. None for
a stale or unavailable handle.

In a mob's goal tick ([`GoalContext::host`](crate::GoalContext::host)) this reads
the active mob or a disjoint live mob when available; player reads use the
game host. Other unsupported reads retain their typed refusal.

Side: server.
Throws `stack`, which the mod holds, from the eyes (`LivingEntity.drop`,
`ServerPlayer.drop`), never through a slot: along the view with a
main-hand swing, or with `throw_randomly` scattered with none, as a
death's drops. `include_thrower_name` sets the thrower, and a player's
throw along the view then counts in its stats and fires `item_toss`.
None for an empty stack, a stand or the dragon, a stale handle, or an
item a mod kept out. Inside a transaction its join waits for the root commit, so a mod
keeping the item out is not known at the call. API @API:living_refs@.
handles.signature: fn drop(self, _: &mut dyn ServerHost, _: item::item_stack::ItemStack, _: bool, _: bool) -> Result<Option<EntityRef>, item::item_stack::StackWriteError>

handles.doc:
Side: both.
The entity's instance of `effect` (`LivingEntity.getEffect`): its id
namespaced as the registry has it, the ticks left (-1 infinite), the
amplifier and the flags. The effect is a registration-slot key resolved at load.
None when it has the effect not, before effect resolution, or for an armor
stand, the dragon or a stale handle; on a client, for any entity but the
local player, whose copy of what the server sent it is read.

In a mob's goal tick ([`GoalContext::host`](crate::GoalContext::host)) this reads
the active mob or a disjoint live mob when available; player reads use the
game host. Other unsupported reads retain their typed refusal.

Side: client.
`LivingEntity.getEffectBlendFactor(effect, partialTick)` on a client:
how far the effect has faded in, from 0 to 1, between the last tick
and the next at `partial`. Darkness fades in and out over 22 ticks and
nausea in over 150 and out over 20 (`MobEffect.setBlendDuration`), the
fades the fog, lightmap and screen spin draw. Other effects start at
0 after a blended add and interpolate to their post-countdown target
during each client tick: 1 while active, 0 once expired. An unblended
add starts at its target immediately; an update preserves the old blend.
`partial` is not clamped. The registration-slot key is resolved at load.
0 when the entity lacks the effect. None before effect resolution, for a stale
handle, or an entity other than the local player: the client keeps no
other entity's effects.
handles.signature: fn effect_blend_factor(self, _: &dyn ClientHost, _: EffectKey, _: f32) -> Option<f32>

handles.doc:
Side: both.
The entity's active effects (`LivingEntity.getActiveEffects`), in the
order their store keeps them, in `Some` even when it has none. None

`LivingEntity.randomTeleport(x, y, z, true, avoid)`: the point `at`
is clamped into the world border and drops to the first block in
`minecraft:entities_can_teleport_to` below it, losing a block of height
per step down. The entity lands there, keeping its motion, unless that
ground or a block in its box at the landing is in the `avoid` block
tag, the box collides or holds a liquid, or the species refuses the
spot (an enderman never lands on ground holding water). A landing
stops a mob's navigation and broadcasts entity event 46 (the portal
particles). Nothing else is played: a chorus fruit's sound and an
enderman's own teleport effects belong to their callers.

True when the entity moved. False when no spot was found, for a
non-finite point, a fake player, a player in another level, an armor
stand or the dragon, a stale handle, or on a client.

way a mod's tick moves the end of the use): at 1 the use completes on
the next tick, at 0 or less it runs until the player lets go, as in
vanilla. It moves the deadline the use-item Tick hook moves, so only
the uses that count it (food, drink, mod items) follow it: shield, bow,
trident, spear, instrument and bundle uses ignore it, and a call from
inside the Tick hook itself is overwritten by that hook's result.

A mob's use never runs out, so the write moves its use counter to
where `ticks` are left: a spear's stabs, a bow's draw and the use
reads follow it on the next ticks, and a time past the item's use
duration is as long as it. False when the entity uses nothing (a
piglin admiring gold and a drinking witch use none), for armor stands
and the dragon, and for a stale handle.

around see the spin. It moves the player not at all: a Riptide launch
adds its own velocity. A `ticks` of 0 or less ends a spin under way
and clears its damage. False for a mob, an armor stand and the dragon
(Horizon runs no spin for them), a dead player, a non-finite `damage`,
a stale handle and a client.

path (`start_sleeping`). Normal server guests in the level in place
are supported; guests in another level, fake players, mobs, armor
stands and the dragon are refused. This only

for armor stands and the dragon, and for a player other than the

one of its buttons does (`MultiPlayerGameMode.handleInventoryButtonClick`,

(`clickMenuButton`, and `menu_button` for a mod's menu). For a client
mod's own input on a menu's screen where `screen_click` doesn't come,

(`AbstractContainerScreen.onClose`, `LocalPlayer.closeContainer`): the

menus, non-client hosts and a menu whose screen is not open, such as

Close a player's open menu as `ServerPlayer.closeContainer` does, running the normal
lifecycle once: the container's lid, a vehicle's or a trade's stand-in, the crafting,
station and mount menus, the carried stack back to the inventory,
`player_container_close`, then the client's window closed (`ContainerClose`). Refuses
stale menus, clients, a player whose state is swapped in for a turn, and the player's own
inventory menu, which is never closed. A client closes its own screen with `close`.

to feet), a block entity's or an entity's slot, the ender chest's, the crafting grid's
or a mod's chest menu's.

by the recipe book. The boxes follow the actual layout, including GUI
scale and the recipe book's horizontal offset.

handles.doc:
`PathNavigation.moveTo(Path, speed)`: follow a path the mod computed.
Each [`PathNode`] is floored to its block, and the engine classifies
the node's [`PathType`] on submit (the mod gives no types); the
classification is information for the follower, never a filter: a node
it calls blocked is not refused, moved or dropped, so the path is
followed as given. As every `moveTo`, this trims the path: a node in a
cauldron is raised onto its rim, and with avoid-sun a ground navigation
cuts at the first node that can see the sky. The path is finished once
its next-node index reaches the node count; [`mob_is_done`](MobsBackend::mob_is_done)
is true when there is no path or it is finished. A supplied path keeps
no recompute target, so a block change on it or the stuck check drops
it and no search is ever run in its place (stricter than vanilla, which
re-searches to the previous target); the per-node timeout drops it as
well. Only non-finite coordinates and speeds are refused; there is no
cap on the node count, and unloaded or out-of-world nodes are neither
refused nor clamped: a finite coordinate at the edge of the `i32` range
saturates when it is floored to its block, and every block step after
it (the classifier's neighbours, the floor under a node, the follower's
waypoint) saturates too, so no mod input panics the engine. As in
vanilla, the mob's own goals may replace the path next tick. Refuses
with a [`MoveToPathError`]: `NotFinite` for such a coordinate or speed,
`Unavailable` for a stale or unavailable mob, a client, and the dragon
(which flies by its phase and keeps no navigation), and `Empty` when
the path has no node left to follow after the trim.

controls, for brain and goal mobs alike. `LivingEntity.aiStep` still
runs with every move input (`xxa`, `yya`, `zza`) and the jump flag

goals and brain memories are kept and resume on the next AI step; the
navigation timeout does not count the pause. `NoAI` is neither read nor
written, and the per-species `isNoAi` checks outside the AI step still
read only `NoAI`. Saved with the entity as an attachment-style value
(`horizon:attachments`, `horizon` / `ai_paused`), never a vanilla key,
and read back on load. Refused, with nothing changed, as

A client's copy loads the tag the server sent (`loadWithComponents`

replace its own of the same names. One it already has as sent is

Replace the one-shot fields the block's next change sends clients; an empty compound
clears them. They go over what `block_entity_update_tag` gives (or alone, without
one) in the single packet every current viewer gets, and are gone. Call
`block_entity_sync` to send them: until a change reaches a viewer they wait, however
many chunks are sent, and they end with the block entity. They are for a one-shot
effect, not state: nothing saves, clones or compares them, and the revision stays.
A client merges them into its copy's `nbt` as any update field, where they stay until
sent again: a changing value, such as a counter, tells one effect from the next.
Fields that would take the packet past what a client reads (2 MiB of network NBT) are
dropped with a warning, and the change goes without them. A transaction that rolls the
block entity back also drops a batch queued before it.

generic, so it can be named:

```
# use mod_api::*;
fn register(r: &mut dyn Registrar) -> ToServer<VarInt> {
    r.payload_handlers()
        .registrar("1")
        .play_to_server_typed::<VarInt>(
            PayloadId("example:counter".into()),
            |value, _| if value.0 >= 0 { Ok(()) } else { Err("negative".into()) },
        )
}
```

generic, so it can be named:

```
# use mod_api::*;
fn register(r: &mut dyn Registrar) -> ToServer<VarInt> {
    r.payload_handlers()
        .registrar("1")
        .play_to_server_typed::<VarInt>(
            PayloadId("example:counter".into()),
            |value, _| if value.0 >= 0 { Ok(()) } else { Err("negative".into()) },
        )
}
```

holding the copy it showed. A [`MenuSlotBackRefusal`], and nothing changes, for a player
not online or a window that is not their open menu, a menu that is not a blockless mod
menu, more places than its container slots, or a place that doesn't resolve now.

`ServerPlayerGameMode.destroyBlock`: breaks the block at `pos` in the player's level as
this player breaks it, as FTB Ultimine does for each block of a vein. The player's own
checks hold: a spectator, an adventure player whose tool can't break it, a held item that
can't break blocks (a sword in creative), a game master block without the permission and
a dedicated server's spawn protection leave it. Then `break_block` hears it and may cancel
it, and the break runs as the player's own: the block's effects, events, particles and
sound, `player_destroyed_block`, the loot rolled for the held item and its enchantments,
`block_drops` with this player as the breaker, the item's wear, the mined statistic and
the exhaustion. A vein miner takes each block's drops and experience in `block_drops` and
sets them down where it wants with `LevelRef::pop_resource` and
`LevelRef::award_experience`; what else the break sets loose (a torch losing its support,
a container's contents) still drops in the world. With `into_inventory`, the drops left
after `block_drops` go to the player's inventory instead, and what doesn't fit drops from
them as `Inventory.placeItemBackInInventory` drops it. The player needn't reach or look at
the block. Breaking from `break_block` or `block_drops` makes them hear these breaks too:
a mod keeps its own guard, and a break started from inside eight others is refused (a
Horizon safeguard that the reference does not have). True when the block was removed; false, with nothing broken, for a stale handle, a player who
isn't here or is dead, air, an unloaded block, a block no survival player can break
(bedrock), a canceled break, and off a server.

Disconnects that player with `reason`, as `/kick` does
(`ServerGamePacketListenerImpl.disconnect`): their client shows it, the log's "lost
connection" line names it, `player_kicked` hears it and a dedicated server records a
`kick` event. The connection closes when the server next polls it, so the calling hook
finishes first; works for the acting player inside their own hook, and without the
world published. A fake (client-less) player leaves through the same removal path:
the leave line is broadcast once and `player_logged_out` fires once at the next poll.

owner) and a player whose disconnect is already pending (a second call, also from

Opens content mod menu type `menu` for a connected player from anywhere, with no
block (`ServerPlayer.openMenu(provider, extraDataWriter)`): an item's use, an entity,
a command. The menu replaces the one they had open. Its container slots show empty
and their clicks go to the mods (`native_menu_clicked`), as `open_menu`'s do. `extra`
(at most 32 KiB) is what the client's `screen_extra_data` reads, and `pos`, when
given, its `screen_pos`. The old menu closes on the server as a close does (its
`removed`, `player_container_close`, the cursor stack and crafting grids back to the
inventory) before the new one is built; `replace` says whether the client is first sent
a close for it, as for `open_menu`. `MenuReplace::InPlace` sends none: the client keeps
its screen and mouse until the new screen replaces it. The window id, or Ok(None) when
a mod cancelled the open. Errors: `NotModMenu`, `PlayerUnavailable` (stale, fake or
vanilla client), `TooLarge`, or `Title` for a title that could not cross; a cancelled or
refused open leaves the old menu as it was.

Opens vanilla workstation menu `menu` for a connected player with no block, as a Java
item does with a `ContainerLevelAccess` at the player: `minecraft:crafting`, `loom`,
`grindstone`, `cartography_table`, `stonecutter`, `smithing` or `anvil`. The station
works where the player stands at each use (its sounds, experience and level events);
its input slots start with `inputs` (the crafting grid's nine, row by row; a station's
in its menu's order). It stays open while the player's inventory holds one of `keep`
(`AbstractContainerMenu.stillValid`) and closes as walking away does once it holds
none, so an empty `keep` closes it on the next tick. An anvil opened this way wears no
block and plays no anvil event: its mod does both after `anvil_craft_post`. Before the
inputs go back to the inventory on closing, `station_closing` lets a mod keep them.
The menu replaces the one the player had open, as `player_open_menu`'s does; a stock
client shows it. The window id, or Ok(None) when a mod cancelled the open. Errors:
`NotStation`, `PlayerUnavailable`, `TooManyInputs`, `Stack` for an input the game
refuses, or `Busy` from a hook the player's station asks while it opens or takes a click;
a refused open leaves the old menu as it was.

protection and the border, then the action. Once it runs, an effect a fake can't take
part in (a menu, sleep, a ride, another dimension) is stopped where it would start, and

vanilla's result) have still happened then. The fake is found once, and its turn

Side: server.
Writes `state` at `pos` in `level` for the player, for a state the mod already chose
(an editor's or a schematic's). It is `level_set_block` with a placement's flags
(`NEIGHBORS | CLIENTS`, plus `KNOWN_SHAPE` when `update_neighbour_shapes` is false; without
it the neighbours' shapes update, so fences, walls and stairs connect), so the block entity
follows that write's rules, and then `Block.setPlacedBy` of the block that stands there, run in
the player's turn (a bed places its head, a door its upper half). Nothing else of vanilla's `BlockItem.place`
or `useOn` runs: no check that the block may be placed there (survival, entity
obstruction, build permission, spawn protection), no `placed_block` advancement trigger or
statistic, no place sound, no game event, no item used or consumed, and `setPlacedBy` is

for `player`: vanilla's

trigger, not yet granted, of an advancement not yet done, is tested
by `test` and then by its `player` predicate; those that pass are
granted, and an advancement they complete is awarded with its toast,
chat line and rewards, as the game's own triggers award.

The acting player is reached inside their hook; another live player
is reached in their own level, including during a guest's turn. An
outer player displaced by a nested turn is unavailable. `Ok(())`
means the player was reached, whether or not anything was granted.
A stale/offline/displaced handle, a remote client, or a `minecraft:`
trigger or empty id is refused with a typed reason.

`test` is lent to this call only. A failed test stops further testing
and reports `Test`; earlier matching criteria may already be granted.
Wasm predicates run synchronously, including callbacks into the group
firing the trigger, within that call's remaining execution and memory limits.

startup: a level whose stem's `biome_source` is `{"type": "mymod:chaos"}`,
or whose [`DimensionSettings`](crate::DimensionSettings) name it in

decoration included, and a mod's chunk generator. Its

the world, an id registered twice and an empty biome list refuse the
mods at startup, naming the mod.

startup: a level whose stem names `mymod:void` then has the terrain of

runs on the worldgen worker threads. The level gets the vanilla stages
its [`vanilla_stages`](crate::ChunkGenerator::vanilla_stages) asks for,
read here, once. The id may use any manifest-owned namespace. An unowned
namespace, an empty name, a name that is no folder of the world and an id

completes that argument with it. A name in an unowned namespace, an empty name, and an
id registered twice refuse the mods at startup, naming the mod.

Register a crafting kind once at startup. Duplicate names, foreign namespaces,
and values without an explicit Wire codec refuse startup, naming the kind.

Register density function type `name` (`plates` or `mymod:plates`) once at startup: any
density JSON, a data pack's density function, noise router or noise settings, can then
use `{"type": "mymod:plates", ...}` as a node, and `density_type` decodes that object.
Every reader of the density graph sees its values: chunk fill, far terrain, structure
heights, climate and biomes, spawn finding, aquifers and ore veins. Its
[`DensityFunction`](crate::DensityFunction)s run on the worldgen worker threads. An
unowned namespace, an empty name, a name with characters an id can't hold and an id
registered twice refuse the mods at startup, naming the mod.

Register dimension `name` (`pocket` or `mymod:pocket`) once at startup:
every world then has the level `mymod:pocket`, shaped and generated by
`settings`, as if a data pack below all the others gave it. A data pack
can replace its level stem or dimension type. The id may use any
manifest-owned namespace; an unowned namespace, an empty name, a name that is no
folder of the world (`../x`, `a//b`, capitals), a vanilla
level, an id registered twice, a build height the dimension type codec
refuses and an unknown generator refuse the mods at startup, naming
the mod.

mod. Names must fit 32767 ASCII bytes. The base is read once here; a panic,
zero limit or tooltip exceeding 32767 UTF-16 units also refuses registration.
Horizon bounds the complete encoded selector metadata to 256 KiB; a token that

NeoForge's `DispenseFluidContainer`: a dispenser's answer for a fluid container, which a
container's [`dispense_item`](crate::ItemPart::dispense_item) part returns (it is no default:
vanilla's buckets keep their own behaviours). `event.stack` runs in a two-slot copy whose
item may change ([`ItemPlace::ScratchSlots`]), reached one item at a time
([`ItemPlace::OneByOne`]): the container's handler sees one container, and an empty one may
become a full one of another item. It picks up from the block in front first
([`try_pickup_fluid`], its `FLUIDS` reached from the dispenser's side), and places a bucket
of what it holds there ([`try_place_fluid`], unvalidated, as a bucket) only where nothing
was picked up; the fluid's sound and game event go out as the transfer commits, before the
dispenser's click and smoke. A single container is replaced in place; from a larger stack
the slot keeps the rest and the changed container goes into the dispenser, else out of its
front with a second click ([`dispense_with_remainder`](crate::prelude::ItemsServerHost::dispense_with_remainder)).
Where neither moves anything, nothing is changed and one container is dispensed as it is
([`dispense_default`](crate::prelude::ItemsServerHost::dispense_default)). None, for vanilla
to decide, only where the dispenser's level isn't open.

`FluidUtil.getFirstStackContained`: what the fluid container at `place` holds at its first
index that holds any ([`ITEM_FLUIDS`]), whatever the count of the stack there; it may not
come out, and the container may hold more. None where nothing there holds a fluid.

`FluidUtil.interactWithFluidHandler` for any handler: fills the fluid container `player`
holds in `hand` ([`ITEM_FLUIDS`] at [`ItemPlace::PlayerHand`]) from `handler` and, when
nothing goes in, empties it into `handler`. Either way it moves the first fluid that moves,
as much of it as fits, in a transaction of its own: a stack of more than one container has
one split off, changed, where the place puts it, and a creative player keeps the hand's
stack, as [`ItemPlace::PlayerHand`] writes. Once something moved it plays the fill or empty
sound and game event at the centre of `pos`, or half a block above the player's feet
where `pos` is none, as
[`trigger_sound_and_game_event`]. True when something moved; false, with nothing changed,
where the hand holds no fluid container or nothing moves either way.

The sound and game event go out as it returns: call it outside a transaction the caller

functions.doc:
`FluidUtil.triggerSoundAndGameEvent`: what a bucket plays as `fluid` goes in or out of a
container at `at` in `level`. `pickup` is true when the fluid came out of the handler into the
container (`minecraft:fluid_pickup` and the fluid's
[`fluid_pickup_sound`](crate::prelude::TagsHost::fluid_pickup_sound)) and false when it went
in (`minecraft:fluid_place` and its
[`fluid_empty_sound`](crate::prelude::TagsHost::fluid_empty_sound)). The sound plays under
the block slider at full volume and pitch for every player near, the acting one included,

functions.doc:
Cube root, fdlibm's `cbrt`.

A first estimate from the high word divided by 3 (5 bits), a rational
correction (23 bits), the estimate chopped to 20 bits and nudged up, then
one Newton step. `cbrt(±0)`, `cbrt(±inf)` and `cbrt(NaN)` return the
argument.
StrictMath-exact cosine, linked into the caller without a host call.
StrictMath-exact exponential, linked into native and wasm guests without host calls.

`sqrt(x^2 + y^2)` without undue overflow or underflow, fdlibm's
`__ieee754_hypot`.

With `a >= b` the magnitudes, compared by high word: `a + b` when `a` is
more than 2^60 times `b`; otherwise both scaled by a power of two when
large or tiny, `a^2 + b^2` summed from parts with the low 32 bits split
off, and the square root scaled back. An infinite argument gives +inf,
even with a NaN; otherwise a NaN gives NaN.

Natural logarithm, fdlibm's `__ieee754_log`.

Writes `x = 2^k * (1 + f)` with `sqrt(2)/2 < 1 + f < sqrt(2)`, then
returns `k * ln 2 + log(1 + f)`, with `log(1 + f)` from a degree-14
polynomial in `s = f / (2 + f)` (or a short series when |f| < 2^-20).
`log(±0)` is -inf, negative arguments give NaN, `log(+inf)` is +inf.

Base-10 logarithm, fdlibm's `__ieee754_log10`.

Writes `x = 2^n * m`, with `m` in [1, 2), or in [1/2, 1) and `n` one
higher when the exponent is negative, and returns
`n * log10_2hi + (n * log10_2lo + log(m) / ln 10)`, with [`log`] for
`log(m)`. Special cases as [`log`].
StrictMath-exact power, linked into native and wasm guests without host calls.
StrictMath-exact sine, linked into the caller without a host call.
StrictMath-exact tangent, linked into the caller without a host call.

`#[wire(crate = ::mod_vocab::wire)]` selects the contract module for

Mark a trait mod and derive its hook subscriptions.

A hook method may carry `#[listener(priority = <i32>, receive_cancelled)]`, both optional:
mods run by descending priority (0 when omitted), then in dependency order, and a mod that
receives cancelled events is still called after an earlier mod cancels, with
`event.cancelled` to read and clear. `receive_cancelled` compiles only on a hook a mod may
cancel.

dependency `other_mod` is installed. A native mod is built with the Cargo feature `other_mod`
only when it is; a wasm mod is built with it and asks the game at the call, since an absent
library's functions trap. One guard for both builds.

Literal words use ASCII letters, digits, `_` and `-`, matched with their case as Brigadier's
(`cu callItemClear`). Only the first word may additionally begin with one `/`: register

A command a native mod adds, as one usage: words, then arguments
`<name:kind>`, optional ones last in brackets `[name:kind]`:
`pay <player:player> <amount:integer>`, `balance [player:player]`,
`eco give <player:player> <amount:integer>`. Kinds: `word`, `text` (the
rest of the line, last), `integer`, `number`, `boolean`, `player`, `players`,
`entity`, `entities`, `item`, `block_pos`, `vec3` (a point, `Vec3Argument.vec3()`; delivered
as `Vec3`), `id` (a free `namespace:path` identifier, delivered as that canonical string),
`mod_id` (a loaded package id, delivered as a
string), `resource:<registry>` (an id that registry holds, delivered as `Id`:
`<kind:resource:minecraft:entity_type>`), or a command argument type a mod registered with
`Registrar::register_command_argument`, named by its namespaced id:
`machine use <machine:mymod:machine>`. Usages of one command share their
words; the server merges them into one tree. Each executable usage keeps its own level:
a public `foo bar` lets everyone traverse `foo`, but does not make an
operator-only `foo` executable. Optional arguments also allow execution at
their preceding prefixes, at that usage's level.

Side: server. Selector arguments use vanilla's source position, permissions,
cardinality and selection order; `player`/`entity` require one result and
`players`/`entities` require a nonempty result. Unresolvable entity handles are
omitted; lists have no extra cap beyond the wire frame limits.

(`entity.position(host)`). It holds the world's epoch and the entity's id: ids
are shared by every server level and never reused while the server world is
open. An entity that changes dimension on its own (a lone mob, a general entity)
is rebuilt under a new id, as in vanilla, so its old handle goes stale; a vehicle a
player rides keeps its id, and its handle still resolves in the new level. Follow
the entity's UUID across a change of level.

of an entity that is gone, or used on a client. `Host::entity` makes a server
handle from an event's entity id; `ClientHost::crosshair_target` supplies a
client handle for an entity hit.

types.doc:
`InsideBlockEffectApplier.StepBasedCollector`: the effects and entity writes of one
block sweep. The walk advances a step per block it reaches; a step's effects flush
once each, in [`InsideEffect`] order, with the writes asked `run_before` an effect
before it and those asked `run_after` after it. Steps flush in the order the walk
reached them, and [`InsideEffects::take_planned`] hands the whole ordered plan to the
entity's own tick, which stops applying at the first item after the entity dies.

A write at the block an entity is inside, asked for when the part is told and applied

state the entity touched. The same contract as a landing write: the complete
requested batch is checked before queuing, and an invalid state refuses all writes
and sibling outputs from that callback.

components, as `StackItemAccess`: what doesn't fit, or is another item, is refused.

The place inside, where an insert goes into that slot only
(`ItemAccess.forHandlerIndexStrict`): around a [`BlockEntity`](Self::BlockEntity),
[`EntitySlot`](Self::EntitySlot) or [`Nested`](Self::Nested) slot, what doesn't fit is
refused instead of spread to the other slots. Around any other place it is that place.

One item at a time of the place inside (`ItemAccess.oneByOne`): its count reads at most
1 and an extract takes at most 1, so a handler acting on the whole stack acts on one.
Inserts go to the place inside as they would.

The place inside, as a player with infinite materials reaches it
(`ItemAccess.forInfiniteMaterials`): while `player` has them (creative's `instabuild`),
an extract gives without taking and an insert is taken whole, one of it going to the
player only if they have none: into their inventory, or dropped at the root commit when
it is full. Inserting nothing gives nothing. Otherwise it is the place inside.

Wrappers may nest to any depth in a mod's own code: reading and writing undo them in a
loop. One crossing the wasm boundary nests at most 15 wrappers deep (the wire's 32
levels, two for each); a deeper one is refused there.

A stack outside the world whose item may change: a private two-slot copy, as
`DispenseFluidContainer` runs a dispensed container, so an empty bucket can become a
full one. [`ItemsServerHost::scratch_slots`](crate::prelude::ItemsServerHost::scratch_slots)
makes one in a transaction with the stack in its first slot, and
[`scratch_take_slots`](crate::prelude::ItemsServerHost::scratch_take_slots) takes both
slots back out. Reads and extracts are the first slot's; an insert fills the first slot
where it is empty or holds the same item and components, and what doesn't fit goes to
the second (`forHandlerIndex`), as a changed item split off a stack does. It lives and
aborts as a [`Scratch`](Self::Scratch) stack does.

types.doc:
A scene's own clock. The scene keeps its live particles from one draw to the next
under `id` and the calling mod (one id per scene a mod's screens show; two mods'
id 1 are two scenes). When `tick` is ahead of the tick the scene last ran, it runs
the ticks in between: the blocks' animate ticks when `animate_blocks` is set
([`SCENE_ANIMATE_PICKS`] picks a tick among the scene's own blocks), then the
particles'. A jump of more than [`SCENE_CATCH_UP`] ticks (a page resumed) starts the
scene over from no particles and runs only the last [`SCENE_CATCH_UP`] ticks. The
same tick again is a paused scene: nothing is added and nothing moves. A tick behind
the last one, or a scene whose blocks or entities changed, starts the scene over with
no particles. Each tick's randomness is seeded from `id` and the tick, so the same
ticks give the same picture.

fields.doc: Which of the calling mod's scenes this is; a screen showing two gives them two ids.

An open transaction, as NeoForge's `TransactionContext`: what every write of a handler or a
place takes. `host.transaction` gets one from the game and lends it to its closure alone.

It lets its holder write in the transaction, not end it: ending one takes its
[`TransactionSeal`], which only whoever opened it holds. The authority is the game's, not
this value's: it names one transaction the game opened by a token that cannot be guessed in
practice (a randomly keyed 64-bit hash), and the game checks it on every write. A write
given a transaction that is not open changes nothing, so a value decoded from bytes or kept
past its closure cannot write outside the journal.

The outermost transaction is closing: on a commit, the game is telling the world of its

the transaction that just ended.

A block's part: code attached through [`Registrar`] to one block, a mod's own or vanilla's.
Its methods are the scoped hooks', asked only for the blocks it is attached to: a scoped
hook has no [`Hooks`] method. They may run on the window's thread or the server thread.
Annotate each part trait implementation with [`horizon_part`] to derive its subscriptions.

An entity type's part (arismoko/horizon#1077): code attached through
`RegistrationContext::entity_part` to one entity type, a mod's own or vanilla's
(`minecraft:zombie`). Its `register_goals` runs at every `Mob` construction of that
type, spawned or loaded, right after the species' own goals — vanilla's `registerGoals`
moment — and the goals it adds join the mob's two selectors beside vanilla's, same
priorities and interruption. Its `register_behaviors` runs wherever a brain-driven
species' brain is built (#824). Its `spawn_cluster_size` answers how large a spawn group of the
type may grow. Its `general_entity_tick` runs for one general entity row's authoritative
tick (#792). Annotate each part trait implementation with
[`horizon_part`] to derive its subscriptions; the goal, behavior and spawn-size methods
are not hooks, so they subscribe nothing whatever they override.

capabilities.doc:
Energy, as NeoForge 26.3's `Capabilities.Energy.BLOCK`: a block entity's energy as one side
reaches it. The game answers it for a mod block entity's buffer (`Registrar::block_energy`, as
`SimpleEnergyHandler`): its capacity, the most one insert and one extract move, and the sides
a fill comes through and a drain leaves by.

An entity's items as automation reaches them, as NeoForge 26.3's
`Capabilities.Item.ENTITY_AUTOMATION`, asked for the side of the entity a hopper reaches it
from. The game answers it for a chest or hopper minecart and a chest boat, the container
entities `EntitySelector.CONTAINER_ENTITY_SELECTOR` picks, with the slots [`ENTITY_ITEMS`]
gives them; a player and a chested mount are not reached by automation.

An entity's energy, as NeoForge 26.3's `Capabilities.Energy.ENTITY`, asked for the side of
the entity a lookup reaches it from, or none for no particular side. Vanilla has no entity
that holds energy, so only mods answer it.

An entity's fluids, as NeoForge 26.3's `Capabilities.Fluid.ENTITY`, asked for the side of
the entity a lookup reaches it from, or none for no particular side. Vanilla has no entity
that holds a fluid, so only mods answer it.

An entity's items, as NeoForge 26.3's `Capabilities.Item.ENTITY`. The game answers it for a
player with their inventory (`PlayerInventoryWrapper`): indices as vanilla's `Inventory`
numbers them, 0..36 the main inventory (0..9 the hotbar), 36..40 the armour from feet to
head, 40 the off hand. For a chest or hopper minecart, a chest boat, or a chested donkey,
mule or llama, it answers with their container's slots ([`ItemPlace::EntitySlot`]).

Fluid tanks, as NeoForge 26.3's `Capabilities.Fluid.BLOCK`: a block's tanks as one side
reaches them, numbered from 0 for that side, as [`ITEMS`](crate::ITEMS)' slots. The game
answers it for a mod block's tanks (`Registrar::block_fluids`) and for a cauldron: one tank
holding the content its block has, vanilla's water (a bucket in thirds) and lava (a bucket
only whole) or a content a mod registered through `register_cauldron_fluid_content`, filled
and drained by whole levels; an empty cauldron takes any fluid that has a content. A
cauldron has no block entity, so it is answered by position. Powder snow is no fluid: its
cauldron has no content and no answer.

Energy held by an item, as NeoForge 26.3's `Capabilities.Energy.ITEM`: a handler for the item at
one place, found with [`ItemPlace::capability`](crate::ItemPlace::capability), whose changes
rewrite the item there with an [`exchange`](crate::ItemPlace::exchange) of one, so from a stack
of more than one the changed item splits off. Vanilla has no energy items, so only mods answer
it.

Fluid held by an item, as NeoForge 26.3's `Capabilities.Fluid.ITEM`: a handler for the item at
one place, whose changes rewrite the item there with an [`exchange`](ItemPlace::exchange) of
one, so from a stack of more than one the changed item splits off. The game answers it for
vanilla's buckets (NeoForge's `BucketResourceHandler`): one tank of a bucket, filled and drained
whole, an empty bucket taking plain water or lava.

Items held by an item, as NeoForge 26.3's `Capabilities.Item.ITEM`: a handler for the item at
one place, whose changes rewrite the item there with an [`exchange`](ItemPlace::exchange) of
one, so from a stack of more than one the changed item splits off. The game answers it for an item with `item_container`
slots, kept in its `minecraft:container`, or `minecraft:bundle_contents`.

Item slots, as NeoForge 26.3's `Capabilities.Item.BLOCK`: container slots as one side
reaches them. The game answers for block entities with slots by their `WorldlyContainer`
sides, including double chests as one container and a mod block's `Registrar::block_container`,
plus composters without block entities. A composter has one input slot from above or without
a side, and one output slot from below; horizontal faces give no game handler. Its input
consumes one compostable item per insertion below level seven, its output holds one bone
meal only at level eight, and feedback waits for the root commit. Its position-local random
stream is also journaled, so aborted retries keep their chance outcome without rewinding
the level's unrelated random draws.

Items by kind: a container's or composter port's [`ItemStorage`] as one side reaches it.
The game answers it for every container or port [`ITEMS`] reaches, from those slots; a mod's
bulk store answers it with a provider of its own (`block_entity_capability(&STORAGE, ..)`).
A block with slots and a store of its own registers its provider `before_game`, or the slots
answer first.
New blocks, items and mob effects from the mod's `data/` (API 0.2).

behaviours.doc: A set, pool or processor list file in a mod's own namespace that holds `horizon:add_to` (an id or a list of ids) adds entries to other sets, pools or lists and is not one of its own. Only structure sets (their `structures`), template pools (their `elements`) and processor lists (their `processors`) take additions. The entries are appended to the list of each target the file names, after the target's own entries and every mod's own files, ordered by `horizon:priority` (an integer, lower first, 1000 when the file has none), and files of equal priority in mod order, then file order. A target nobody defines is skipped.

A mod block with no block entity type of its own (a type that declares the block wins) whose content `template` is a vanilla block with a block entity gets that block entity's class, chosen by the template's block entity class and not by the block's name. A block on a sign or hanging sign template is valid for that block entity as it stands, so a world generation feature that places it gives it that block entity. For any other class (a vault, say) the block is valid for that type once the type's `block_entity_type_add_blocks` event adds it; from then on it creates, ticks and saves as the template's block entity would, and loads back as the same type. Without that event a block with no declared type has no block entity.
